text: Tata Capital Limited - Retail customercare@tatacapital.com Tata Capital Limited - Commercial contactcommercialfinance@tatacapital.com Tata Capital Housing Finance Limited - Home Loans customercare.housing@tatacapital.com AMC AMC shall be levied at 0.25% of the Dropline Amount or INR 1,000, whichever is higher, and shall be computed on the opening balance in the month in which the charge is to be levied. For Loans booked prior to or on the 15th of a month: AMC shall be charged in the 13th month, 25th month, 37th month, 49th month, and every 12 months thereafter during the tenure. For Loans booked after the 15th of the month: AMC shall be charged in the 12th month, 24th month, 36th month, 48th month, and every 12 months thereafter during the tenure. Such AMC shall be collected along with the EPI of the respective month, except for the final EMI month, wherein no AMC shall be levied. Penal Charges For default in payment of interest and/ or principal amounts 3% per month on defaulted amount (Annualized Penal Charge of 36%) AMC (Hybrid Term Loan Facility) This is an annual charge for maintaining your account if you've opted for a flexible funding option such as a Hybrid Term Loan. At Tata Capital, you will be charged: AMC shall be levied at 0.25% of the Dropline Amount or INR 10,000, whichever is higher, and shall be computed on the opening balance in the month in which the charge is to be levied. For Loans booked prior to or on the 15th of a month: AMC shall be charged in the 13th month, 25th month, 37th month, 49th month, and every 12 months thereafter during the tenure. For Loans booked after the 15th of the month: AMC shall be charged in the 12th month, 24th month, 36th month, 48th month, and every 12 months thereafter during the tenure. Such AMC shall be collected along with the EPI of the respective month, except for the final EMI month, wherein no AMC shall be levied. DPD Value Meaning XXX Safe value, meaning no data was provided by lender to CICs. 000 Safe value, meaning on-time payments with no outstanding dues. STD Standard payment where payment is done within 90 days of the due date. SUB Sub-Standard Payment where payment is made more than 90 days after the due date. DBT Sub-Standard Payment where payment is made more than 90 days after the due date. LSS High likelihood that the borrower won't repay the loan amount.

Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund When it comes to buying a home, many people opt for a home loan . However, most people don’t know that home loan repayment can be made in multiple ways. You can choose between pre-EMI and Full EMI options , depending on your preference. If you’re planning on getting a home loan, it’s essential to understand these options to manage your finances efficiently while the property is constructed. In this article, we’ll take a deep dive into what pre-EMI is, its advantages, and how to calculate it. What is Pre-EMI Meaning? A pre-EMI is a repayment scheme banks and financial institutions offer for home loans for under-construction properties. Under this scheme, you’ll only have to pay the interest on the amount disbursed by the lender. This means that during the construction phase of the property, you’ll not have to pay the principal amount of the loan. Instead, you’ll only have to pay the interest portion of the loan as EMIs. This interest-only payment is called pre-EMI. However, since the disbursal is based on completing different project phases, the lender may release the full amount in 3-6 tranches. Once you take possession of the property, your actual repayments start, and you’ll have to pay the full EMI (principal amount + interest). Also, read – Top Things to keep in mind before prepaying your Home Loan Benefits of Pre-EMI Now that you’re aware of what pre-EMI meaning, let’s look at some of its benefits. 1. Lower EMIs During the construction phase of the property, you only have to pay the interest on the disbursed amount. This leads to lower EMIs during the pre-EMI period, which helps you manage your finances effectively. 2. Reduced financial burden The pre-EMI scheme is great for people who are renting a home but want to buy a house. It lets them pay only the interest on their home loan till the property is ready. This makes it easier to afford and plan for the future, as they can expect their income to increase before starting full EMI payments. 3. pre-EMI tax benefit Under the Income Tax Act 24, you can get Pre EMI tax benefits when you choose it as an option for your home loan. However, there’s a catch! You can’t claim a tax deduction on the interest you pay during the construction period. But once you own the property, you can claim the interest paid during construction in five equal installments for a tax deduction, up to a limit of Rs. 2 lakhs per year. Also, read – Importance of NOC After Paying off Your Home Loan Difference Between Full EMI and Pre-EMI 1. Loan disbursal If you select the Full-EMI option, you’ll receive the entire loan amount in one go. However, if you choose the pre-EMI option, the loan amount is disbursed in installments. 2. Interest rate The interest of pre-EMI is calculated on the loan amount disbursed . On the other hand, the full-EMI interest is calculated on the principal loan amount. 3. Repayment period Choosing Full-EMI over pre-EMI leads to faster debt repayment as monthly installments cover a larger portion of the principal amount. 4. Principal Amount The Full-EMI principal loan amount and loan tenure decrease with each monthly payment. However, there is no impact on the loan tenure, principal loan amount, or interest rate under the pre-EMI option. 5. EMI payments The pre-EMI monthly payments commence as soon as construction begins. Whereas full-EMI payments only start once you’ve taken possession of the property after it is completed. Also, read – Renting vs buying a house in India: Pros and cons How to Calculate Pre-EMI? To understand how to calculate pre-EMI, let’s take an example. Let’s assume Rohan avails a loan of INR 20 lakhs for 20 years at an 8% interest rate. He takes this loan for a new under-construction property that’ll be completed within 2 years. So, in the first tranche, the lender disburses Rs 4 lakhs. Here’s what it’ll look like: Disbursement Timeline Disbursed Amount Total Disbursed Amount pre-EMI (Rs) Regular EMIs(start after 24 months) Initial 4,00,000 4,00,000 2,666 16,729 6 months 4,00,000 8,00,000 5,333 16,729 12 months 4,00,000 12,00,000 8,000 16,729 18 months 4,00,000 16,00,000 10,667 16,729 24 months 4,00,000 20,00,000 16,729 16,729 The lender disburses the principal amount in 5 tranches based on the completion of the project, with the final instalment being disbursed upon possession of the house. It’s important to note that pre-EMI isn’t included in the original tenor of the loan, and it extends beyond the loan’s actual term. As a result, Rohan ends up paying more interest than he would otherwise. The stark difference between full EMI and pre-EMI, as per the above example, is that you can repay the loan within 20 years in the former. While in the latter, you’ll repay the loan in 22 years. Also, read – How Home Loan Top-up Work – A Complete Guide Tax Benefits on Pre EMI Interest in Home Loans Pre EMI tax benefits help you save smart on your home loan. Here’s how home loan tax deduction and pre EMI interest deduction work, with key housing loan tax benefits . So what is pre EMI interest? Pre EMI interest is the interest paid during the construction period before full EMIs start. You can claim this pre EMI income tax deduction under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act after the possession of the property. Also, read – Types of Collateral Properties Which Can be Used for a Loan When Should You Opt for Pre EMI? Specific situations help you decide when to choose pre EMI. Pre EMI best time is when you need short-term relief without stopping the loan progress. Here’s pre EMI vs full EMI timing , to help you when opting for pre EMI. What is pre EMI in home loan? Choose pre EMI home loan during property construction when full EMIs start later. It helps manage cash flow by paying only interest initially, delaying principal payments. Ideal if you expect income to rise or want to reduce immediate EMI burden. Pre EMI suitability allows tax benefits on interest paid before possession. Now that you know what is pre EMI in home loan, you can switch to full EMI once your property is ready or your earnings stabilise. Also, read – How to Reduce a Home Loan Tenure Pre EMI in Education Loans and Other Loan Types There are many loan types with pre EMI meaning just like the pre EMI education loan. Here we’ll look at the pre EMI meaning loans: Firstly, what is Pre EMI interest? Pre EMI meaning is paying only interest on the loan amount before full EMIs start. Education loan types with pre EMI allow students to manage cash flow during studies. Applied to home loans, personal loans for construction, and similar long-term loans. Education loan interest pre EMI payments qualify for tax benefits under certain conditions. Pre EMI home loans also help reduce immediate repayment pressure while the loan disbursal progresses. Switch to full EMI after course completion or property possession. Pre EMI other loans options help you plan finances better. Also, read – What Happens When a Home Loan Borrower Passes Away? Using Pre EMI Calculators to Plan Your Finances Smart pre EMI financial planning starts with the right tools. A pre EMI calculator shows your exact costs upfront. Here’s how to calculate pre EMI easily. Enter loan amount, interest rate, and construction tenure into the tool. It works just like a home loan EMI calculator. It computes monthly interest-only payments during the pre-EMI phase. Compare with full EMI to see cash flow impact using a loan interest calculator. You can adjust scenarios to match your budget and avoid surprises. Apply For Home Loan Say Hello to Your New Home with Our Easy Home Loans! The disadvantages of pre-EMI include an extended loan tenure, delayed principal repayment, higher interest outlay and limited ownership over the property. Is pre-EMI a good option? Pre-EMI can be a good option for many as only the interest amount is paid in the pre-construction stage under a pre-EMI home loan. This allows you to manage your financial resources better as compared to a full-EMI option. What is the interest on pre-EMI? The interest on pre-EMI refers to the interest part on the disbursed loan amount that the borrower can pay until the EMI payment cycle begins. Can pre EMI be converted to full EMI anytime? Your pre EMI converts to full EMI after receiving possession. To convert a pre EMI home loan to full EMI before the possession, contact your lender. Is pre EMI compulsory in all home loans? No, pre EMI home loan is not compulsory. It applies mainly to the properties that are under-construction. How does missing pre EMI payment affect my credit score? Missing payments like pre EMI home loan can lower your credit score. It reflects a delayed interest payment, impacting your creditworthiness negatively. What tax benefits are available on pre EMI interest? You can claim a tax deduction on pre EMI interest under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act after the possession of the property. LTV Upto 100% on road funding Type of Fee Applicable Charges Processing fees The fee is charged for processing the loan application. It is payable even if the loan is rejected. Foreclosure charges This is a charge applied if you choose to repay your entire loan before the end of the contracted loan term. a) Within 12 months of the date of first disbursement- 6% of principal outstanding at the time of Foreclosure b) After 12 months of the date of first disbursement- 5% of principal outstanding amount at the time of Foreclosure Statement of Accounts This is a charge applied for providing a physical copy of the Statement of Account – a statement having a list of all transactions made in your loan account during a given period. At Tata Capital, you will be charged Customer portal – Nil Branch walk-in - Rs. 250 Loan Cancellation Charge This is a charge applied if you request loan cancellation after the cooling-off period At Tata Capital, you will be charged, Rs. 6500 Stamp Duty This is a government-mandated fee required for legally registering your loan agreement. It is charged at actuals. NACH / PDC Charges This is a charge applied when you use post-dated cheques (PDCs) or physical NACH forms instead of setting up an electronic mandate for EMI payments. At Tata Capital, you will be charged Rs. 500 Documentation charges This fee covers the cost of verifying your documents, completing necessary compliance checks, and conducting due diligence before your loan is disbursed. At Tata Capital, you are charged Up to Rs. 1999. NOC for conversion of private to commercial registration This is a charge applied for issuing a No Objection Certificate (NOC) required to convert and register your vehicle at RTO from private to commercial use. At Tata Capital, you will be charged Rs. 1999 Charges for Repossession of Vehicle This is a charge applied when an asset is repossessed due to non-repayment of the loan. At Tata Capital, you will be charged Rs. 22000 (as applicable) PDD Charges This charge is applied for managing the Registration Certificate (RC), including document storage, administrative handling, and record management. At Tata Capital, you are charged Rs. 450 Charges for delay in RC hypothecation This is a monthly charge applied when you fail to submit the Registration Certificate (RC) for hypothecation to the Registering Authority within 120 days from the date of loan disbursement. At Tata Capital, you are charged, Rs.1000/-per month till the time of registration/noting with the authority, where RC hypothecation is pending beyond 120 days post disbursement. Part- Prepayment Charges This is a charge applied if you choose to repay part of your loan before the end of your loan tenure. a) Within 12 months of date of first disbursement - 6% of part-prepayment amount b) After 12 months of date of first disbursement - 5% of part-prepayment amount Switch Fee without any Top Up This is a charge applied if you request a change or reduction in the interest rate on your existing Loan. At Tata Capital, you will be charged, (Rate reduction * Principal Outstanding*75%) OR Minimum of Rs. 5000 - whichever is higher

While a perfect score is rare, most lenders consider 750 or above to be an excellent credit score. Making timely repayments, maintaining low credit utilization, and responsible borrowing habits are far more important than trying to achieve a perfect 900. The maximum CIBIL score in India is 900, although a score of 750 or above is generally considered excellent for loan eligibility. Your CIBIL score is one of the first things a lender checks when you apply for a loan or credit card. It reflects how responsibly you have managed your credit over the years and plays a key role in loan approval. But have you ever wondered what is the maximum CIBIL score in India and whether it is actually possible to achieve it? This guide explains the highest possible score, what it means, and the habits that can help you get there. What is the maximum CIBIL score in India? The maximum CIBIL score in India is 900. The CIBIL score range typically runs from 300 to 900. A higher score indicates stronger creditworthiness, and vice versa. Note that if a person has never taken a loan or a credit card , their CIBIL score is not 300. Instead, their credit report mentions NA (Not Applicable) or NH (No History). Is a 900 CIBIL score actually possible? While 900 is the maximum score in CIBIL, it is practically impossible to achieve it. A perfect score requires years of flawless repayments, a long credit history, and a healthy mix of credit accounts. And even then, it is not guaranteed. In practice, a score of 750 or above is considered excellent by most lenders. Also Read – How to Increase CIBIL Score From 600 to 750 What CIBIL score do you actually need for a loan? A high CIBIL score certainly helps, but it is not the only factor lenders consider. Your income, existing EMIs, employment stability, and debt-to-income ratio are also assessed before a loan decision is made. So, there is no fixed maximum CIBIL score for loan approval . The table below depicts the CIBIL score ranges and loan approval chances: CIBIL Score Range Loan Approval Chances 300 – 549 Low 550 – 649 Fair, subject to strict checks 650 – 749 Good 750 or above High What affects your CIBIL score? The following factors typically affect your CIBIL score: Repayment history: Your record of paying EMIs and credit card bills on time; this is the single biggest factor. Credit utilization ratio: The percentage of your available credit that you regularly use. Credit mix: The balance between secured loans and unsecured credit in your profile. Length of credit history: The age of your oldest and active credit accounts. Recent hard inquiries: The number of loan or credit card applications made with lenders in a short period. Also Read – How to Build Credit Score from Zero? How to achieve and maintain a high CIBIL score? Instead of trying to achieve a perfect score of 900, you should aim to reach and maintain your CIBIL score above 750. If you are wondering how to achieve maximum CIBIL score, these practical tips can help: Pay all your loan EMIs and credit card bills on time. Keep your credit utilization ratio below 30%. Do not close old credit accounts unnecessarily. Avoid applying for multiple loans or credit cards within a short period. Maintain a balanced mix of secured and unsecured credit. Check your credit report regularly and raise a dispute if you find any errors. There is no fixed timeline for improving a CIBIL score. Credit bureaus update your records only after lenders report them, which is typically done every month. Thus, changes are not immediate. Borrowers with a short credit history may see their scores change differently from those with a long credit history or past defaults. Also Read – Tips to improve CIBIL score after a payment default What are the common myths about the maximum CIBIL score? Myths Facts Checking your CIBIL score lowers it. Self-checks do not affect your score. A high score guarantees loan approval. Lenders look at several other factors too. Closing old credit cards improves your score. It’s the opposite. You need a 900 CIBIL score for the best loan rates. 900 score is practically impossible. A score of 750 or above will do. Taking no loans results in a perfect score. It only shows NA or NH. Conclusion While 900 is the maximum CIBIL score in India, it is practically impossible to achieve. A score of 750 or above is generally enough to be viewed favorably by most lenders. Consistent repayments and disciplined credit usage matter far more than chasing perfection. You can also check your eligibility for a Tata Capital Personal Loan before applying. property deposits, brokerage, travel, and accommodation. While it offers much-needed support, you should consider borrowing only after checking for any available employer relocation allowances. A personal loan for moving is a standard personal loan that helps manage expenses incurred during relocation. Moving to a new city brings several upfront expenses. Funding these entirely from your pocket may strain your finances, especially in a new environment. This is where a personal loan for relocation can help. This article explains the typical cost of relocating, the expenses a personal loan for moving can cover, alternative ways to fund your move, and the key factors to consider before borrowing. What does relocating to a new city actually cost? The cost of moving depends on factors such as the distance, the destination city, family size, and lifestyle. You can get an indicative estimate of common relocation expenses in India from the table below. Expense Indicative cost Rs. * Packers and movers (intercity) 10,000 to 50,000+ Rental security deposit Two to three months’ rent (may be higher in some metros) Brokerage charges Around one month’s rent Travel expenses for family 2,000 to 30,000+ Temporary accommodation 2,000 to 8,000 per night Basic furniture and appliances 30,000 to 1,50,000+ Vehicle transportation 5,000 to 20,000 School admission or transfer costs Varies by school *Indicative costs only. Actual expenses may differ. What is a personal loan for relocation? A personal loan can be used for a variety of purposes. A personal loan for relocation is not a separate financial product; it is a standard unsecured personal loan that can be used to fund moving-related expenses. It is often suitable for relocation because it requires no collateral, has no end-use restriction, and offers quick disbursal. Also Read – What is a Good Credit Score in India? What relocation expenses can a personal loan cover? Depending on your needs, you may use the loan for expenses such as: Packers and movers charges Security deposit and brokerage Travel and temporary stay expenses for your family Furniture and essential household appliances Vehicle transport costs School admission fees for children Initial living expenses until your first salary is credited in the new city Also Read – What is EMI and How Does it Work What are the benefits of using a personal loan to relocate? A personal loan for relocation can reduce the financial pressure of meeting major moving expenses during the initial stages of your transition. Some of its benefits are: Collateral-free borrowing: No need to pledge a hard-earned asset for a one-time expense. Flexible repayment tenure: Spread the relocation cost across affordable Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs). Quick disbursal: Access funds when you need them the most. No end-use restriction : Use a single loan to cover different relocation expenses. Personal loan vs other ways to fund your move Before opting for a personal loan, it is prudent to compare it with other funding options: Funding option Pros Cons Savings No interest cost Can significantly reduce your emergency savings Employer relocation allowance May fully or partially cover relocation expenses Not offered by all employers and may not cover the entire cost Credit card Quick access to funds High revolving interest if not repaid on time Loan against fixed deposit or gold Lower interest rates Requires pledging an asset Personal loan Collateral-free, predictable EMIs, flexible usage Interest, processing fees, and other applicable charges may apply What are the eligibility criteria and documents required? Eligibility varies across lenders but generally depends on factors such as your age, employment, income, work experience, and credit score . Keep your identity, address, income proof, and bank statements ready to facilitate quicker verification. Tip: Apply before changing your salary account or address to avoid verification delays. Also Read – Documents Required for Personal Loan How to apply for a personal loan for relocation? Here’s how you can apply for a personal loan for relocation: Check your eligibility . Decide the loan amount and use an EMI Calculator to estimate your EMI and choose a suitable tenure. Complete the online application form. Submit the required documents. Receive approval and disbursal after successful verification. What should you consider before borrowing for relocation? A personal loan may support you financially in a new city. That said, it is still a monetary commitment. Before borrowing, keep the following points in mind: Check your employer’s relocation benefits before applying, as they may cover part or all of your moving costs. Borrow only the shortfall after using your savings or employer reimbursement. Keep EMIs affordable, especially if you are relocating for a new job and settling into a new city. Factor in the total borrowing cost, including processing fees and other applicable charges, not just the EMI. Understand the impact on your credit profile, especially if you plan to apply for a home loan or another major loan in the near future. Conclusion Relocation costs can run into lakhs. A personal loan for moving lets you spread these expenses over time without pledging any collateral. Before applying, check whether your employer offers relocation assistance and borrow only the amount you need. machine. The amount charged for carrying out this process is known as franking charges. They are paid to certify that the applicable stamp duty has been paid on legal documents such as loan agreements and sale deeds. Franking charges vary from state to state and are usually a small percentage of the property’s value or the home loan amount. Understanding how franking differs from stamp duty and budgeting for it alongside other closing costs can help you avoid surprises during your home-buying journey. Franking charges are the fees paid for stamping home loan or property documents through an authorized franking machine to certify payment of the applicable stamp duty. You have compared home loan interest rates , arranged your down payment, and are almost ready to complete the paperwork. Then, just before the loan is processed, you notice another item in the list of charges – franking charges. Many homebuyers see this fee for the first time and wonder whether it is another tax or simply an extra cost added by the lender. In reality, franking charges on a home loan are linked to the stamping of certain loan and property documents. They are legally valid under applicable state laws. Although the amount is usually small, understanding why it is charged can help you avoid confusion during the home-buying process. In this article, we’ll explain what franking charges for home loans are, how they differ from stamp duty, the applicable rates, and how the franking process works. Keep reading. What are franking charges? To understand what franking charges are, you must first know the meaning of franking. It is the process of stamping a legal document using a franking machine to confirm that the applicable stamp duty has been paid. This stamping is carried out by an authorized bank or a government-approved franking agent on documents such as a home loan agreement or a property sale deed . The amount charged for carrying out this stamping process is known as franking charges. While franking charges for home loans are usually small, they are part of the overall documentation costs of a property transaction. Why do you pay franking charges on home loans? Franking charges in a home loan are paid because certain loan and property documents must be stamped to show that the applicable stamp duty has been paid. This makes the documents legally valid and acceptable as evidence. Franking is usually completed when the loan and property documents are executed. It helps ensure compliance with stamp duty laws, avoids future legal or revenue-related issues, and allows the home loan process to move forward without delays. Franking charges vs stamp duty: What’s the difference? Many homebuyers assume that franking charges and stamp duty are the same, but they are not. Stamp duty is the tax payable on certain property and loan documents. Whereas franking charges for home loans are generally a small fee for carrying out the franking process and are usually adjusted against the total stamp duty payable. The table below compares franking charges and stamp duty: Basis Stamp Duty Franking Charges Meaning A government tax payable on specified property and loan documents. Charges paid for carrying out a stamping process, known as franking. Purpose Makes the document legally valid after payment of the prescribed duty. Provides proof that the required stamp duty has been paid. Collected By State governments. Authorized banks or government-approved franking agents. Amount Depends on state laws, property value, and transaction type. Usually a small percentage or service charge, adjusted against the applicable stamp duty. Franking charges rate: How much do you pay? The amount payable as franking charges is usually a small percentage of the property’s value or the home loan amount. In many states, it is around 0.1% and is often subject to a cap. However, the exact rate is decided by the respective state government. Thus, it is not the same across India. For example, franking charges for home loans in Maharashtra may differ from those applicable in other states. In most cases, the amount paid through franking is adjusted against the total stamp duty payable on the document. Also Read – Hidden charges in home loan What are the franking charges for home loans in Maharashtra & Mumbai? Franking is widely used for property and loan documents in Maharashtra, including Mumbai. The franking charges for home loans in Mumbai typically range from 0.1% to 0.3% of the loan amount and are adjusted against the applicable stamp duty. Since the applicable rate and maximum limit are determined by the state government and may change over time, always verify the latest charges on the official Maharashtra Inspector General of Registration (IGR) or state stamp authority website before completing your transaction. How to pay franking charges: The process The exact procedure for paying franking charges on a home loan may differ slightly from one state to another. However, the process usually follows these steps: Visit an authorized franking center such as a designated bank, licensed franking agent, or the office of the Sub-Registrar. Submit the document that needs to be franked, such as the home loan agreement or property sale deed. Pay the applicable amount as per the state rules and the document value. Get the document franked using a franking machine. Complete the registration process by submitting the franked document to the relevant registration authority. Franking charges and notary charges: Are they the same? No. Franking and notary charges for home loans are two different expenses. Franking charges are paid to certify that the required stamp duty has been paid on a loan or property document. Notary charges, on the other hand, are the fees paid to a Notary Public for verifying, witnessing, or attesting documents and signatures. Although both may appear among your documentation costs, they serve entirely different legal purposes and are charged separately. What are the other home loan closing costs? Apart from franking charges in home loans, you should also budget for other expenses such as stamp duty, property registration charges, legal and notary fees, and the lender’s home loan processing fee . These costs are usually payable at different stages of the property purchase and can add significantly to your overall purchase price. Planning for them in advance can help avoid last-minute surprises. They help certify that the required stamp duty has been paid and make your property documents legally valid. Since franking charges vary across states, it is always advisable to check the applicable rules in advance. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A machinery loan without collateral helps MSMEs and startups purchase or upgrade equipment without pledging business or personal assets. Other benefits include quick approval, high loan amount, flexible repayment tenure, and minimal documentation. Since these loans are unsecured, lenders mainly evaluate the business’s cash flow, credit profile, and repayment capacity before approving the application. There are several government schemes that also help businesses avail of machinery loans without security. A machinery loan without collateral is an unsecured business loan that helps eligible enterprises finance machinery or equipment without offering any asset as security. For many businesses, growth begins with better machines. Whether you want to expand production, replace outdated equipment, or invest in new technology, buying machinery is often a key part of growing a business. However, the challenge is that many micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and startups struggle to secure the capital needed to purchase machinery. They may not even own valuable assets that can be pledged as collateral. This is where a machinery loan without collateral can come to the rescue. It allows eligible businesses to invest in essential equipment without pledging personal or business assets as security. This guide explains how a machinery loan without security works, who can apply, the eligibility criteria, the required documents, interest rates, and the application process, among other details. Keep reading. What is a machinery loan without collateral? A machinery loan without collateral is a type of business loan that helps you purchase plant, machinery, or equipment without pledging property or other assets as security. It is also known as an unsecured machinery loan. The approval is typically based on factors such as your business’s financial performance, cash flow, repayment capacity, credit profile, and operating history. Many banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) in India offer machinery loans without security to eligible MSMEs and businesses. A machinery loan for startups and MSMEs makes it easier to invest in new equipment without blocking valuable assets. Here are the key features and benefits: No collateral required : You can raise funds for buying machinery without pledging your personal or business assets. Quick approval and disbursal : Machinery loans are often processed faster since they do not have any collateral involved. High loan amount : If you have a good credit profile and repayment capacity, you can qualify for a larger loan amount as well. What are the features and benefits of a machinery loan without collateral? Minimal documentation : You are only required to submit a few basic documents, including your PAN and Aadhaar card, business registration certificate, and equipment quotation. Flexible repayment tenure: You can choose a repayment tenure based on your monthly cash flow. Helps preserve assets : Your existing assets remain available for future business needs and funding. How can new businesses qualify for a machinery loan for startups? Getting a machinery loan for startups can be challenging because of their limited operating history. They also lack ownership of assets that can be pledged as collateral. Here are a few practical tips that can help: Prepare a well-structured business plan that clearly explains your business model, expected revenue, and how the machinery will support growth. Maintain a good personal credit score. Lenders often consider the founder’s credit profile for startups. Keep your financial projections realistic and be ready to explain how you plan to repay the loan. Arrange all business documents, registrations, and licenses in advance to avoid delays. Explore government-backed credit guarantee schemes, such as CGTMSE , wherever applicable, as they can improve your chances of approval. Choose a lender that offers dedicated financing solutions for MSMEs and startups, rather than applying to multiple institutions blindly. What are the eligibility criteria for unsecured machinery loans? The eligibility criteria for a machinery loan without security may vary from lender to lender. However, most lenders consider these common when reviewing applications: Business vintage: A minimum operating history is often preferred. Annual turnover: Businesses must meet the lender’s minimum annual turnover criterion. Credit score: A CIBIL score of 700 or above helps. Entity type: Proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs, private limited companies, and other eligible business entities can apply. Udyam registration: Several lenders require a Udyam registration certificate . It is important to note that approvals for unsecured machinery loans often hinge on the business’s credit profile and cash flow rather than any collateral. What are the documents required for the loan? In most cases, lenders require only a few basic documents for machinery loans without collateral. The list typically includes: KYC documents : Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, and address proof of the applicant. Business registration documents : Business registration certificate, Udyam Registration, or other applicable licenses. Bank statements : Recent bank statements for the period specified by the lender. Income proof : Income Tax Returns (ITRs), audited financial statements, or profit and loss statements, wherever applicable. GST documents : GST registration certificate and recent GST returns, if applicable. Machinery quotation : A quotation or proforma invoice from the supplier for the machinery or equipment you plan to purchase. What are the interest rates and charges for unsecured machinery loans? The interest rate is influenced by factors such as your CIBIL score, loan amount, repayment tenure, business vintage, turnover, and overall repayment capacity. In general, unsecured loans may carry slightly higher interest rates than secured loans because no collateral is offered. It is always advisable to compare offers from different lenders before making a decision. Apart from the interest rate, lenders levy the following charges: Charge Description Processing fee A one-time fee charged to evaluate and process the loan application. Documentation charges Fees, if any, for preparing and verifying loan documents. Foreclosure or prepayment charges Charges that may apply if you repay the loan before the agreed tenure. Penal interest Additional interest charged in case of delayed EMI payments. EMI bounce charge Applicable if your EMI bounces due to insufficient balance in your bank account. Government schemes for collateral-free machinery loans The Government of India has introduced several schemes to offer collateral-free machinery loans for startups. Some of the notable schemes include: CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises) A credit guarantee is provided to authorized lenders under this scheme. It encourages them to offer collateral-free loans to eligible MSMEs. Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) Under this scheme, the government has authorized certain lenders to provide MSME loans at affordable interest rates. The loans are categorized as Shishu , Kishor, Tarun , and Tarun Plus. Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) SIDBI is an apex financial body that provides refinancing facilities and term loans to banks and NBFCs. These lenders then extend credit to MSMEs on a broader scale. How to apply for a machinery loan without collateral? With Tata Capital , you can apply for a machinery loan without security through a simple process: Check your eligibility for the loan. Make sure you meet the lender’s minimum annual turnover, credit score , and other requirements. Arrange your KYC documents, business records, bank statements, financials, and the machinery quotation or proforma invoice. Fill in an online machinery loan application form on Tata Capital’s website. Upload the required documents. Wait for the verification and approval. This may take anywhere from a few hours to a few working days. Once approved, the loan amount is disbursed in accordance with the agreed terms. Conclusion A collateral-free machinery loan can help MSMEs and startups invest in the equipment they need without pledging valuable assets. The approval depends largely on your credit profile, cash flow, and business performance. Choosing the right lender and keeping your documents ready can make the process much smoother. A new business can apply for machinery finance even if it does not have a long track record. Lenders may evaluate the founder's credit history, the business proposal, expected revenues, and the overall viability of the venture before deciding whether to approve the application. What is the interest rate on an unsecured machinery loan? The interest rate is decided after the lender reviews your application. Factors such as your CIBIL score, business turnover, repayment capacity, loan amount, and tenure all play a role. CGTMSE supports eligible MSMEs by providing a credit guarantee to the lending institution. Because part of the lending risk is covered under the scheme, banks may be more willing to sanction collateral-free loans to qualifying businesses that need funds for machinery or equipment. financially during unforeseeable circumstances. But, did you know that LIC policies can also help you get access to loans when required? A loan against LIC policy is a type of secured loan that facilitates the option to avail of a loan by pledging the policy to the lender. This provision ensures that you do not need to liquidate your hard-earned assets such as property or automobiles to the lender, so you can retain their ownership. However, before you apply for a loan against your LIC policy, understanding how it works is essential. To help you make an informed financial decision, this article details the nuances and workings of a loan against LIC policy and how it can help you get the finances you need in times of emergencies. What is a loan against LIC policies? LIC policyholders can avail of loans against LIC policy after the policy acquires a surrender value. The loan can be taken against this surrender value of the policy. The surrender value is the amount of money policyholders will receive if they decide to discontinue the policy before maturity. The key features of loans against LIC policy are: 1 The interest rate on a loan on LIC policy depends on the prevailing rates linked to government bond yields and the applicant’s credit profile. 2. Loans against LIC policy are only available to LIC endowment policyholders. 3. The loan amount sanctioned is an advance against the future surrender value of the LIC endowment policy. 4. The maximum loan amount is usually up to 90% of the surrender value for policies in force. For paid-up policies, the maximum is 85% of the surrender value. 5. The LIC insurance policy is held as collateral by LIC against the loan. LIC can withhold or terminate the policy if the applicant defaults on loan repayments. 6. Not all LIC policies have a loan facility. Policyholders must choose plans that specifically offer the loan feature. 7. If an outstanding loan with interest exceeds the surrender value, LIC has the right to terminate the insurance policy. 8. If the policy matures before full loan repayment, LIC can deduct the outstanding loan amount from the policy proceeds before disbursing the balance to the policyholder. What Types of LIC Policies Are Eligible for Loan Facility? LIC offers customers a wide variety of insurance plans and policies. These can be used for retirement savings, life insurance , education, and other savings. The most common types include term plans, endowment plans, money-back policies, pension schemes, and ULIPs. However, not all can be used for LIC loans against policies. Eligibility for loans against insurance policies varies by lender. However, the most common loan policies are endowment plans and ULIPs. LIC Loan Against Policy: Eligibility Criteria in India Here are the eligibility criteria for availing a loan against LIC policy: 1. The applicant must be a citizen of India. 2. The applicant should be at least 18 years old. 3. The policy must have a guaranteed surrender value. 4. The applicant must have a valid LIC policy. 5. The applicant should have paid at least 3 years’ premium in full for the LIC policy to avail the loan facility. Here are some of the eligible LIC policy plans that can be used as collateral for securing a loan against LIC policy: 1. Jeevan Pragati 2. Jeevan Labh 3. Single-Premium Endowment Plan 4. New Endowment Plan 5. New Jeevan Anand 6. Jeevan Rakshak 7. Limited Premium Endowment Plan 8. Jeevan Lakshya Also,read – Loan Against National Savings Certificates (NSC) How Much Loan Can You Get Against Your LIC Policy? The principal amount for a loan against a policy will vary based on many factors. These include the lender’s policies, the insurance policy’s value, and the borrower’s profile. Most lenders offer loan values up to 90% of the insurance policy’s value. However, this amount will vary by financial institution. It is crucial to research different lenders to find one that aligns with your requirements. Interest Rate & Charges for Loan Against LIC Policy The interest rates and other charges for loans against insurance policies will also vary by lender. Depending on the specific policy, the lower end of the interest range is between 9% and 10%. However, some financial institutions may charge up to 15% interest on loans against policy. Some factors affecting your upfront costs include processing fees and any additional charges your lender levies. Some other factors, such as your income, credit profile and history, credit score , and repayment history, will also affect interest rates. How to Apply for Loan Against LIC Policy? The process is subject to changes by LIC. Here are the key steps to avail a loan against an LIC policy: Offline method To avail of a loan against LIC policy, offline, follow these steps: Step 1: Visit the nearest LIC branch office and obtain the loan application form. Step 2: Fill in the application with your policy details and required information. Attach KYC documents like identity proof and address proof. Step 3: Submit the duly filled application at the branch along with the original policy bond. Step 4: The LIC office will verify your policy details, premium payment status and surrender value to determine your loan eligibility. If approved, LIC will sanction the loan and disburse the amount as per the product terms. The original policy will be retained by LIC until full loan repayment. Online method To avail of a loan on LIC policy online, follow these steps: Step 1: Register for LIC’s e-services and login to your account. Step 2: Check your policy eligibility for a loan and view applicable terms and conditions online. Step 3: Fill out the application form online and submit it along with scanned copies of KYC documents. Step 4: You may need to send original physical documents to the nearest LIC branch for verification. Once verified and approved, the amount is disbursed into your account. Policy documents may be required to be deposited in physical form at the branch. Also,read – Pros & Cons Of Taking Loan Against Shares Loan Repayment, Lapse Risks & Closure: How It Works One of the most important aspects of handling a loan is timely repayment. Delaying or defaulting on your EMI payments may negatively affect your credit score and history. Banks and other institutions may also impose penalties for non-payment. Financial institutions and credit bureaus may also take legal action against long-term defaulters. Additionally, because the insurance policy secures the loan, borrowers may lose access to it. Some lenders could also charge additional fees for foreclosure or prepayments on loans against insurance policies. Terms and conditions to avail of a loan against LIC policies The terms and conditions are subject to change by LIC. Below are some terms and conditions applicable for loans against LIC policies: 1. The minimum tenure of the loan is 6 months. Shorter tenures are not permitted. 2. Prepayment of the loan is allowed only after paying at least 6 EMIs. 3. In case of the unfortunate demise of the policyholder before loan maturity, interest will be charged only until the date of the demise. 4. If the policy matures during the loan tenure, the maturity claim proceeds can be utilised by LIC to first recover the outstanding loan with interest. 5. Only LIC policyholders with eligible endowment, moneyback and whole-life plans can avail of loans after acquiring the stipulated surrender value. 6. The policyholder needs to pay interest regularly as per the schedule to avoid loan foreclosure. 7. LIC reserves the right to terminate the policy if the loan with interest exceeds the surrender value. However, one must repay interest and principal on time to avoid policy termination or loan ballooning beyond surrender value. The key difference is that a loan against an LIC policy is secured. Personal loans can be unsecured, and often lead to higher interest rates and EMIs. Can I apply for loan against insurance policy fully online? Yes, many private and public sector banks, as well as NBFCs , let you see how to apply for a loan on an LIC policy online. Will my policy lapse or benefits be affected if I take an LIC loan and don’t repay? If your loan against LIC policy is unpaid, it may lead to defaults on your account, and you could lose access to the security. Additionally, it might negatively impact your credit score and could lead to legal action. Is CIBIL/credit score required for loan against LIC policy in India? LIC personal loan eligibility varies based on the lender. Some may require your CIBIL or credit score, while others don’t for secured loans. What document proofs are needed to get a loan against LIC policy? Generally, the documents required to obtain a loan against an LIC policy include your KYC documents, bank details, an application form, and your policy documents. However, this may vary by lender. What are the main risks of taking a loan against insurance policy for emergencies? The significant risk associated with loans against insurance policies is that the loan amount and accrued interest may exceed the policy's value. This may cause the policy to lapse. register the mortgage agreement with a sub-registrar’s office. It allows the borrower to obtain a loan against property while officially documenting the loan agreement. A registered mortgage differs significantly from an equitable mortgage, in which a borrower simply deposits the property’s title deed with the lender. The benefits of a registered mortgage include greater transparency, stronger legal clarity, higher security for lenders, and a reduced risk of disputes. As a borrower, it’s crucial to carefully consider the costs involved and long-term implications before entering into a registered mortgage. A registered mortgage is a type of mortgage used for a loan against a property , wherein a borrower needs to register the mortgage agreement at a sub-registrar’s office. A loan against property or a mortgage loan can help you arrange funds for tackling a medical emergency , business expansion, or other major financial requirements. You can mortgage your residential or commercial property with a lender and access high-amount loans at comparatively lower interest rates. But do you know there are two ways to create a mortgage on your property? These are registered mortgages and equitable mortgages. In a registered mortgage, the mortgage agreement is officially registered at the sub-registrar’s office. Whereas an equitable mortgage is created only by depositing a property’s title deed with the lender. Both methods differ in legal formalities, registration processes, and fees involved. In this blog, we will discuss in detail what a registered mortgage is. We will also explain the process for creating a registered mortgage in India, the required documents, the benefits, and the registered mortgage charges. Keep reading. What is a registered mortgage? A registered mortgage is a type of mortgage in which the borrower officially registers the mortgage agreement with the local sub-registrar’s office. In this arrangement, the borrower pledges a property as security for a loan, and the mortgage details are legally recorded through a formal registration process. Under a registered mortgage, the lender gets a legal right over the property until the loan is fully repaid. Registration is done in accordance with the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and other applicable state laws. Since the mortgage is legally registered with the government authority, it creates a stronger legal claim for the lender on the mortgaged property. Also, read – What is the DLC rate? What are the types of mortgages in India? The two most commonly used types of mortgages in India are registered mortgages and equitable mortgages. Although both involve mortgaging a property to secure a loan, they differ in terms of registration, documentation, charges, and legal procedures. The mortgage type primarily determines how the property is pledged for the loan and the legal formalities required during the borrowing process. Different mortgage structures help borrowers and lenders choose a suitable arrangement based on convenience, cost, and legal protection. ● Registered mortgage A registered mortgage is created by executing and registering a formal mortgage agreement at the sub-registrar’s office. The borrower voluntarily transfers all rights in the property to the lender as security for the loan. This type of mortgage involves legal registration, stamp duty , and registration charges. Since the agreement is recorded with the government authority, lenders usually have stronger legal protection in the event of repayment default or property-related disputes. ● Equitable mortgage An equitable mortgage is created by depositing the property’s original title deed with the lender. The document remains with the lender until the borrower has fully repaid the loan. This way, the borrower transfers an equitable interest in the property. The lender returns the title deed upon repayment of the loan. Since no legal procedures or registrations are required, this type of mortgage is less expensive and involves less paperwork. However, the risk involved is higher. Also, read – Margin money in home loan How does a registered mortgage work? A registered mortgage operates through a formal legal process in which the borrower mortgages a property in favor of the lender to secure a loan. The process usually begins after the lender verifies the borrower’s eligibility, property ownership documents, and loan requirements. Once the loan is approved, both the lender and borrower sign a mortgage agreement outlining the loan terms, property details, repayment conditions, and rights of both parties. The mortgage agreement is then officially registered at the local sub-registrar’s office by paying the applicable stamp duty and registered mortgage charges. Once the registration process is completed, the lender disburses the approved loan amount to the borrower. The property remains mortgaged to the lender until the borrower fully repays the loan, along with any applicable interest and charges. If the borrower fails to repay the loan or defaults on EMIs , the lender gets the legal right to take possession of the property and sell it to recover the outstanding dues. Also, read – Tenancy Agreements in India Why is a registered mortgage important? Here’s why a registered mortgage is considered important in property loans: Strong legal validity: Since the mortgage agreement is registered with the government authority, it has a strong legal validity. Transparency : All key loan terms, property details, and both parties’ rights are officially documented. Higher security for lenders : The lender gets a legal claim over the property until the borrower fully repays the loan. Reduces the risk of disputes: Registration creates a formal public record that helps avoid ownership-related confusion or disputes later. Registered vs equitable mortgages: Key differences The table below depicts the difference between registered and equitable mortgages based on key parameters: Basis Registered Mortgage Equitable Mortgage Process Involves registration of a mortgage agreement. Created through the deposit of a title deed to the lender. Legal Standing Stronger legal validity and enforceability. Comparatively lower legal and formal protection. Costs Involved Higher due to stamp duty and registration charges. Lower than a registered mortgage. Lender’s Rights Stronger legal rights over the mortgaged property. Rights mainly based on possession of title documents. Risk Provides security to both parties. Riskier type of mortgage. Suitable For High-value loans. Regular home loans . Who should opt for a registered mortgage? A registered mortgage is more suitable for borrowers who are applying for a high loan amount and seeking maximum legal protection against property fraud. Those taking out a mortgage loan for a long tenure should also opt for this route. In general, the following types of borrowers should go for a registered mortgage: Those applying for high-value mortgage loans Borrowers using commercial properties as collateral Borrowers seeking stronger legal clarity and transparency If the lender required a registered mortgage for loan disbursal If the loan tenure is on the higher side, i.e., 15 years or more Borrowers residing in a city where registered mortgages are mandatory Also, read – Understanding the occupancy certificate What is the process to register a mortgage in India? Creating a registered mortgage in India involves a few straightforward steps: 1. Check your eligibility and apply for a mortgage loan with a lender. Furnish the required documents. 2. The lender then verifies your loan application and the documents submitted. Upon successful verification, your loan is approved. 3. Both the lender and the borrower then prepare a mortgage loan agreement that outlines the loan amount, interest rate, repayment terms, property details, and the rights of both parties. 4. The mortgage agreement is then registered at a sub-registrar’s office by paying stamp duty, registration fee, and other registered mortgage charges. 5. The agreement remains valid until you have fully repaid your loan. Upon full repayment, the lender loses its rights over the property. What are the documents required for a registered mortgage? You may need the following documents when creating a registered mortgage: Proof of identity: PAN card, Aadhaar card, passport, driver’s license, or voter’s ID card. Proof of address: Aadhaar card, passport, voter’s ID card, or rental agreement. Proof of age: PAN card, Aadhaar card, or birth certificate. Property documents: Sale deed, title deed, tax receipts, ownership transfer agreement, etc. Financial documents: Bank statements, Income Tax Returns (ITRs), salary slips, profit-loss statements, etc. Recent passport-sized photographs Note that this list of documents is indicative. You may need to complete additional paperwork at the time of registration. Also, read – What is Mutation of property What are the benefits of choosing a registered mortgage? A registered mortgage offers clear advantages for both borrowers and lenders. It creates a legally recognized and well-documented loan arrangement. Strong legal clarity : The mortgage agreement is registered with a government authority. So, there is a clear legal recognition. Better enforceability : In the event of default, the lender has a legally valid claim to the property. This makes recovery more feasible. Reduced risk of disputes : Official registration lowers the risk of future ownership conflicts or misunderstandings. Improved borrower confidence : Borrowers get a clear and structured agreement that is legally recognized. Key things to consider before registering a mortgage Here are a few factors you must consider before creating a registered mortgage: Creating a registered mortgage entails stamp duty, registration fees, and various other charges. These charges can escalate your overall borrowing costs. The registration process may take longer due to documentation checks and formalities at the sub-registrar’s office. You must plan accordingly to avoid delays in loan disbursal. A registered mortgage creates a legally binding claim on the property. You must understand that the lender gains enforceable rights until the loan is fully repaid. Carefully analyze whether the benefits justify the additional long-term costs compared to other mortgage types. Conclusion A registered mortgage is a safe and legally strong way to take a loan against property. It creates an official record of the mortgage and clearly defines the rights of both the borrower and the lender. This makes the loan process more transparent and secure. However, it also involves registration charges, stamp duty, and some legal formalities. Before choosing a registered mortgage, you must understand the costs, the process, and the legal implications. It is important to compare it with other mortgage types and choose the one that best suits your needs. A careful decision can help avoid future issues and make borrowing more secure and affordable. A registered mortgage is a type of mortgage in which you need to officially register a mortgage agreement at a sub registrar’s office. The lender acquires legal rights to the property until the loan is fully repaid, as per the agreement. A registered mortgage allows you to pledge a property as security for a loan and document all details legally. What is the difference between a registered and an equitable mortgage? In a registered mortgage, the agreement is formally registered with the government office. In an equitable mortgage, the borrower simply deposits property papers with the lender. Registered mortgages follow more legal steps, while equitable mortgages are simpler and usually cheaper to create. Is a registered mortgage mandatory for all loans? No, it is not required for every loan. Banks decide the type of mortgage based on loan amount, risk, and property type. Many loans against property are still granted through an equitable mortgage, depending on the lender’s internal policies and the borrower's profile. However, in some cities or states, registered mortgages are mandatory. What are the charges involved in a registered mortgage? The main costs include stamp duty, registration fee, and processing charges. These registered mortgage charges depend on the state rules and property value. Because of legal registration requirements, the overall cost is usually higher than that of other types of mortgages, such as an equitable mortgage. How long does it take to register a mortgage? The process usually takes a few working days. It depends on how quickly documents are verified and how busy the sub-registrar's office is. If everything is in order, it moves faster. Any missing or incorrect documents can easily delay the process. What documents are required for mortgage registration? You may need a proof of identity, proof of address, proof of age, bank statements, proof of income, and property-related documents for mortgage registration. Sometimes, you may also need additional verification papers. All details must be correct, as incomplete or wrong documents can delay the registration process. Can a registered mortgage be canceled? Yes, a registered mortgage can be canceled. Doing so requires a formal, legal process. Usually, this is done only when the loan is fully repaid at the end of the tenure. In some special cases, you can cancel a registered mortgage earlier if the lender becomes unresponsive or you do not want to continue with the repayment for a valid reason. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund An education loan scheme helps students manage the cost of higher education in India or abroad. These loans usually cover tuition fees, living expenses, and other academic costs. Understanding the eligibility criteria, documents, and application process is important before applying. Choosing the right loan option can help students pursue their education goals with better financial planning. Pursuing higher education is an important step in life, but it often comes with significant expenses. Tuition fees, hostel charges, study materials, and travel costs can make quality education difficult to afford for many families. To cover these expenses, several banks and financial institutions in India offer education loan schemes. An education loan scheme in India allows students to pursue higher education in India or abroad without putting the entire financial burden on their parents. In this blog, you will learn about the education loan in detail, including its key features, benefits, eligibility criteria, and the application process. Continue reading. Overview of education loan schemes in India An education loan scheme in India is designed to help students finance the cost of higher education when their personal savings are insufficient. These loans can cover a range of academic expenses, including tuition fees, examination charges, hostel fees, books, and study materials. In some cases, the loan may also support travel and living expenses for students studying abroad. An education loan can be secured or unsecured. A secured loan is one where the borrower provides collateral, such as property, fixed deposits, or other acceptable assets, as security. Unsecured loans, on the other hand, do not require any collateral and are generally offered for smaller loan amounts. What are the different types of education loan schemes available? Banks and financial institutions in India offer various types of education loan schemes to help students with different study plans and financial needs. The common types include: Domestic education loans : These loans are designed for students who plan to pursue higher education within India. They usually cover tuition fees, hostel charges, books, and other academic expenses. Overseas education loans : These loans are designed for students who wish to study abroad. In addition to tuition fees, accommodation, and other academic costs, these loans also cover travel and visa-related expenses. Government-backed loans : The Government of India has introduced several education loan subsidy schemes for the overall development of eligible students. Common examples include the Vidya Lakshmi Scheme , the Padho Pradesh Scheme, and the Central Scheme of Interest Subsidy for Education Loan. Can you use property as collateral for an education loan? In some cases, lenders may ask for security or collateral to provide an education loan. This usually happens when the loan amount is high or if the course is perceived as risky. You can offer your real estate property, fixed deposit, or gold to avail of financing in such a situation. When you take an education loan by providing your property as collateral, it is known as a loan against property . Offering collateral not only improves your chances of getting a loan but also helps you secure a lower interest rate. What are the key features and benefits of a loan against property for education? Taking a loan against property for education can offer several advantages for students planning higher studies. Since the loan is secured with an asset, lenders may offer a higher loan amount compared to unsecured options. Borrowers may also benefit from competitive interest rates and flexible repayment terms. Other than these benefits, a loan against property for education allows students to get access to finances even if they fail to fulfill the lender’s eligibility criteria for an unsecured education loan . Simple and hassle-free documentation Many lenders follow a simple documentation process when offering a loan against property for education. Applicants generally need to submit identity proof, income details, academic documents, and property-related papers. Once these documents are verified, the loan application moves to the approval stage. Since the loan is secured, lenders do not worry about its repayment. Higher loan eligibility and sanction amount One of the major advantages of pledging property as collateral is the possibility of securing a higher loan amount. Since the loan is backed by a valuable asset, lenders may be more comfortable approving larger funding. This can help cover significant education expenses such as tuition fees, accommodation, travel, and other study-related costs comfortably. Long and flexible repayment tenure A loan against property for education often comes with a longer repayment tenure. You can choose to repay the amount in several years, which helps spread the financial burden over time. Some lenders may even offer a moratorium period before your regular EMIs begin. You can pay only the interest amount during this period. Top-up loan and balance transfer facility Many lenders provide the option of a top-up loan on a loan against property for education. It can come in handy should you need additional funds later for education-related expenses. You may also avail of the balance transfer facility to shift your education loan to another lender offering better repayment terms or a lower interest rate. What are the documents required for an education loan scheme? When you apply for a higher education loan scheme, lenders typically ask for a specific set of documents to check your eligibility and repayment capacity. The exact requirements may slightly vary from one lender to another, but the following documents are commonly required: KYC documents: Identity and address proof such as Aadhaar card, PAN card, or passport. Income proof: Bank statements, salary slips, or Income Tax Return (ITR). Admission letter: A copy of the admission letter from a recognized university/college. Course fee details: A detailed breakdown of the course fee and other expenses. Property documents: Required for a loan against property for education. What are the eligibility criteria for education loan scheme? Several banks and financial institutions offer education loan schemes in India for pursuing graduation, post-graduation, and diploma courses. However, to apply for these schemes, both students and co-applicants must fulfill certain eligibility conditions. The student should be an Indian citizen, aged between 18 and 35 years. They must have secured admission to a recognized college or university through a valid admission process. They must have completed at least 10+2 or a diploma. The university must be listed, recognized, and accredited in India or abroad. The co-applicant can be the student’s parent, sibling, guardian, or spouse. Collateral or security may be required in some cases. Note that these are generic criteria. The exact eligibility criteria may vary from one lending institution to another. Step-by-step application process for the education loan scheme You can apply for an education loan scheme online or offline. To apply offline, you can visit the lender’s branch and get in touch with a representative. For the online application, you can follow these steps: Go to the lender’s website and fill out an online loan application form. Upload the required documents. Wait for the lender to verify your loan application and submitted documents. Upon successful verification, the lender provides approval for the loan. Once approved, the loan amount is sanctioned and disbursed. How to apply for an education loan against property? You can apply for an education loan against property through a similar process. However, it includes a few additional steps. After submitting the loan application and the required documents, you must provide property-related papers to the lender. The lender then carries out a property valuation to determine its market value. This helps them determine the loan amount that can be sanctioned. In addition, legal verification of the property documents is conducted to confirm clear ownership and ensure there are no disputes. Once the property valuation and legal checks are completed, the lender can proceed with loan approval and disbursal. Before applying, it is wise to compare lenders, review the terms carefully, and choose an education loan scheme that suits your precise financial requirements. Add wings to your dream. An education loan scheme is designed to help students pay for the expenses related to their higher education. It typically covers tuition fees, hostel charges, study materials, and travel costs, among other academic-related expenses. The loan is usually repaid in installments after the course is completed. Who is eligible to apply for an education loan? Students who are Indian citizens and have secured admission to a recognized college or university can usually apply for an education loan scheme. Most lenders in India provide an education loan without collateral. In such cases, the loan is approved based on the student’s admission details and the co-applicant’s credit profile. An education loan against property is a secured loan where the borrower pledges a residential or commercial property as collateral. What is the maximum loan amount I can avail? The maximum loan amount under an education loan scheme depends on the lender, the course, and the institution.
