Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Education loans have emerged as one of the most useful financial tools. They help students and parents manage expenses for higher education and cover a range of expenses, including academic fees, admission fees, hostel fees, equipment costs, and travel costs. With flexible repayment options and mandatory moratorium periods, education loans offer immense financial relief. Apart from these benefits, an education loan also provides certain tax benefits to borrowers. These benefits are available under Section 80E of the Income Tax Act of 1969. This section allows a deduction on the interest paid on an education loan. It is particularly useful for salaried individuals and parents who are funding higher education. Keep reading to learn more about Section 80E , including its limit, eligibility, purpose, and other important details. What is Section 80E of the Income Tax Act? Section 80E of the Income Tax Act provides a tax benefit on education loans. It allows you to claim a deduction on the interest paid on a loan taken for higher studies while filing your Income Tax Return (ITR). It is important to note that only the interest component of your education loan’s equated monthly instalment (EMI) is eligible for tax deduction. The principal amount that you repay does not qualify for deduction under Section 80E . Key highlights of Section 80E deduction Section 80E allows you to reduce your taxable income, thus lowering your overall income tax outgo. Here are some important points to note about this section: You can claim only the interest component of your education loan EMIs as a deduction under Section 80E . There is no upper limit on the maximum amount you can claim as a tax deduction under this section. The deduction is allowed only to individual taxpayers. Companies, forms, and HUFs cannot claim a deduction under 80E . The loan must be taken for funding higher education in India or abroad. You can claim the deduction for a maximum of eight years or until the interest is fully repaid, whichever is earlier. The deduction is available only for taxpayers under the old tax regime . Who is eligible to claim the Section 80E deduction? Not everyone can claim a tax deduction under Section 80E. There are certain conditions related to who can apply, why the loan is taken, and where the loan comes from. These rules help ensure that the deduction is used only for genuine education-related expenses. Understanding these basic requirements can help you determine whether you qualify before claiming the deduction. Eligible individuals Only individual taxpayers are allowed to claim a deduction under 80E . It means that companies, firms, groups, trusts, and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) cannot claim this deduction. The loan can be taken for the taxpayer’s own education or for a close family member. This includes their spouse, children, or a student for whom they are a legal guardian. The person claiming the deduction should also be the one repaying the loan. Eligible loan purpose The loan must be taken for higher education in India or abroad. Higher education generally refers to courses pursued after completing senior secondary education. It includes not only conventional academic degrees but also skill-based vocational courses from recognized universities and/or educational institutions. The course should lead to a degree or certification that is accepted by relevant authorities. Approved financial institutions You can claim the deduction on an education loan only if you have taken it from a recognized financial institution like a bank, a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), or an approved charitable organization. Loans taken from friends, relatives, or informal sources do not qualify for this benefit. The lender must be properly registered and authorized in accordance with the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) guidelines. Maximum deduction available under Section 80E One key feature of Section 80E is that there is no upper limit on the maximum amount you can claim as a tax deduction. It means you can claim the full interest paid on an education loan in a financial year. This is unlike Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, which allows a tax deduction of up to Rs. 1.5 lakhs only per financial year. Let’s understand the maximum deduction under Section 80E with an example . Suppose you’ve paid Rs. 2 lakh as interest on your child’s education loan during a financial year and have also made investments worth Rs. 2 lakh in tax-free instruments in the same year. This means you can claim a tax deduction of Rs. 2 lakh under Section 80E, but only Rs. 1.5 lakh under Section 80C. Duration of deduction under Section 80E The deduction under Section 80E is available for a limited period. You can claim it for up to eight consecutive assessment years or until the interest is fully repaid, whichever comes earlier. The deduction begins from the year you start repaying the loan. For example, if you repay the loan in five years, you can claim the deduction only for those five years. If the repayment continues beyond the eighth year, no benefit is available after that year. Hence, repaying within this period can help maximize tax benefits. Documents required to claim the Section 80E benefit To claim a tax deduction under Section 80E, you must maintain proper documentation, which includes: Interest certificate: An interest certificate is the most crucial document required to support your tax deduction claim under 80E. This certificate must clearly show the amount of interest you have paid on an education loan during a financial year. Loan repayment schedule: A loan repayment schedule outlines a detailed timeline for how you plan to repay your education loan amount. It also shows a segregation of the principal and interest components of your EMIs. Loan statement: A loan statement mentions your outstanding loan balance at the beginning and the end of each financial year. What courses qualify as higher education? The tax deduction under Section 80E is available only if you have taken a loan for higher education. It refers to full-time courses taken after completing senior secondary education (Class XII) or its equivalent. This includes both academic and skill-based programs. Professional courses can include bachelor’s or master’s degrees in engineering, medicine, management, or law. Vocational courses may cover fields such as aviation, hospitality, media, advertising, or specialized technical training. The key point is that the course should be recognized and pursued at an approved university or educational institution. It does not matter if the institute is in India or abroad. Also read – Income tax on a 12 lakh salary Can you claim Section 80E deduction on early loan repayment? Under Section 80E , the deduction is available only on the interest amount you actually pay on an education loan. Thus, if you repay your loan early, you won’t be able to claim the full interest that you were initially supposed to pay. If you want to maximize your tax savings, you can continue to pay education loan EMIs and invest extra funds elsewhere. However, if you wish to reduce your overall interest outgo and become debt-free, you can opt for the route of prepayment or foreclosure. The right approach depends on your financial goals and comfort with regular EMI payments. Common mistakes to avoid while claiming 80E deduction While claiming 80E benefits, several taxpayers make some common mistakes that can trigger scrutiny notices from the Income Tax Department. Here’s what you need to avoid: Never claim a deduction on the principal component of your EMIs. Only the interest component is eligible for deductions. Do not claim an incorrect or inflated interest amount. It can lead to serious repercussions. Do not forget to support your claim with valid document proof. Do not claim a deduction for loans taken from friends, family members, or other informal sources. Do not claim multiple deductions on the same interest amount if several family members are repaying the loan. Also read – Can We Get Tax Benefit on Personal Loan Section 80E vs other education-related tax benefits Apart from Section 80E, the government also provides tax benefits on education-related expenses under other sections of the Income Tax Act. These provisions are different in terms of what they cover and how much deduction you can claim. Section 80C: Under Section 80C, you can claim a tax deduction on tuition fees paid for your children. This section also covers tax-free investment instruments, such as the Public Provident Fund (PPF) and life insurance policies. The maximum deduction allowed in a financial year is Rs. 1.5 lakh. Section 10(14): Under Section 10(14), you can claim a tax deduction for tuition fees paid for your children’s full-time education at a school or college in India. However, this benefit is available only for employed taxpayers, and the maximum deduction allowed is Rs. 1,200 per child per financial year. Summary: How to maximize your tax savings under Section 80E? Section 80E offers a useful tax benefit for individuals repaying education loans. It allows deduction on the interest component, with no upper limit, for up to eight years. To maximize your savings, you should plan your repayments wisely. Extending the loan tenure may help you claim deductions for a longer period. Do not forget to maintain proper documentation and file your ITR on time. You can also combine the benefits under Sections 80E and 80C to further reduce your tax outgo. Add wings to your dream. Apply for an Education loan! Section 80E of the Income Tax Act is a provision that allows you to claim a deduction on education loan interest. This benefit is available for loans taken for higher studies. It helps reduce your taxable income during the repayment period and lowers your overall tax burden. Who can claim a deduction under Section 80E? Only individual taxpayers can claim this deduction. You can avail it if the loan is taken for your own education, your spouse, your children, or a student for whom you are a legal guardian. The person claiming the benefit must also be the one repaying the loan. Is there a maximum limit on deduction under Section 80E? There is no upper limit on the amount you can claim under Section 80E. It means you can claim the entire interest amount paid during a financial year. However, the benefit applies only to the interest component of the loan, and not to the principal portion of the EMI. For how many years can I claim the Section 80E tax benefit? You can claim the deduction for a maximum of eight years. The period starts from the year you begin repaying the loan. If the loan is fully repaid earlier, the benefit ends in that year. However, if your repayment extends beyond eight years, no deduction will be allowed after this time frame. Can I claim Section 80E deduction for a loan taken for my child’s education? Yes, you can claim this deduction if the loan is taken out for your child’s higher education. The key condition is that you should be the one repaying the loan. In such cases, the interest paid becomes eligible for tax deductions under Section 80E. Are both principal and interest eligible for deduction under Section 80E? No, Section 80E allows deduction only on the interest paid on the education loan. The principal repayment does not qualify for any tax benefit under this section. You can check your interest certificate to know the exact eligible amount. Can the Section 80E benefit be claimed along with other education-related deductions? Yes, you can claim the Section 80E benefit along with other education-related deductions. For example, you can claim a deduction on tuition fees under Section 80C and interest under Section 80E at the same time. This can help you maximize your tax savings. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund The Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS) scheme is a Government of India program that covers the full interest on an education loan during the moratorium period for students from families with an annual income below ₹4.5 lakh. This blog covers the CSIS full form, who qualifies, what the subsidy covers, how to apply and how to check your CSIS subsidy status. Mr Khanna is 52 and has three bank brochures on the dining table in front of him. His daughter has secured admission to a private MBBS college. He has done the interest calculation twice. The numbers are not comfortable. Then a colleague at work mentions a government scheme that waives the interest entirely during the course period. He looks for his CSIS scheme eligibility. For families in his income bracket, this scheme can make a significant difference to the total cost of an education loan. Here is everything he needs to know. What is the CSIS scheme? CSIS full form: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme. It is a scheme launched by the Government of India under the Ministry of Education. The scheme provides a full interest subsidy on education loans during the moratorium period. The moratorium period is the time during which the student does not repay the loan. It covers the course duration plus one year after completion or six months after getting a job, whichever is earlier. During this period, without any subsidy, interest continues to accrue on the loan. The CSIS scheme covers that interest entirely for eligible students. It applies to loans taken from scheduled banks listed under the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) model education loan scheme . Leading non-banking financial companies such as Tata Capital also offer education loans and can guide applicants through the CSIS process, provided the loan meets the scheme’s criteria. (Source: Ministry of Education, Government of India) CSIS scheme eligibility: who can apply? The CSIS scheme eligibility criteria are defined by the Ministry of Education. Students must meet all of the following conditions: The student must be an Indian national. The annual gross parental or family income must be below ₹4.5 lakh. The student must have secured admission through a recognized selection process to a technical or professional course at an undergraduate level. The institution must be a recognized college or university approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), Medical Council of India (MCI), University Grants Commission (UGC) or other statutory bodies. The course must be a full-time undergraduate program in technical or professional streams. Management and law programs at the postgraduate level are not covered under this scheme. The education loan must be taken from a scheduled bank under the IBA model scheme. Mr Khanna’s daughter’s MBBS program at a Medical Council of India-recognized private college qualifies. The family income check is the key hurdle. For families with an income of ₹4.5 lakh or below annually, the scheme provides complete interest relief during the course. What does the CSIS subsidy cover? The CSIS subsidy covers 100% of the interest on the education loan during the moratorium period. No interest accumulates for the student during the course. When repayment begins, only the principal and interest from that point forward are due. There is a loan amount ceiling. The subsidy applies to loans up to ₹7.5 lakh. For loans above this amount, the interest subsidy applies only to the ₹7.5 lakh portion. Parameter Detail Scheme name Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS) Scheme Applicable to Education loans under the IBA model scheme Income limit Annual family income below ₹4.5 lakh Loan amount covered Up to ₹7.5 lakh Subsidy coverage Full interest during the moratorium period Moratorium period Course duration plus 1 year or 6 months after employment, whichever is earlier Course type Full-time undergraduate technical or professional programs Who runs it Ministry of Education, Government of India How to apply for the CSIS scheme The CSIS application process is handled through the lending bank or NBFC at the time of taking the education loan. The student does not apply directly to the government. Take the education loan from a scheduled bank or an eligible NBFC. The loan must be under the IBA model scheme. Submit the income certificate. The family’s income must be certified by an authorized officer, such as a Tehsildar or BDO. The certificate must confirm that the annual income is below ₹4.5 lakh. Submit the admission proof. Provide documentation confirming admission to an approved institution and course. The lender forwards the claim. The bank or NBFC submits the subsidy claim to Canara Bank, which is the nodal bank for the scheme. Subsidy is credited. The subsidy amount is transferred directly to the borrower’s loan account, reducing the outstanding principal during repayment. Tata Capital’s education loan team can help applicants understand whether their loan structure is compatible with the CSIS scheme. With transparent terms and no hidden charges, leading NBFCs such as Tata Capital make the process easier to manage from application to disbursement. How to check CSIS subsidy status To check your CSIS subsidy status, contact your lending institution directly. The bank or NBFC that processed your loan will have the claim submission records. Ask for: Confirmation that the CSIS claim has been submitted to Canara Bank The claim reference number The date on which the subsidy was or will be credited to your loan account The official portal for the scheme is maintained by Vidya Lakshmi, the government’s education loan portal ( vidyalakshmi.co.in ). Students can log in to check the status of their application and track whether the subsidy has been processed. This is a text reference only; visit the portal directly. CSIS scheme vs other interest subsidy schemes on education loans There are other government interest subsidy schemes for education loans. Knowing the difference helps you apply for the right one. Scheme Who it covers Income limit Subsidy type CSIS (Central Sector Interest Subsidy) Students from families with an income below ₹4.5 lakh, technical and professional UG courses Below ₹4.5 lakh per year Full interest during moratorium Dr. Ambedkar Interest Subsidy Scheme OBC and EBC students pursuing overseas studies OBC: below ₹8 lakh; EBC: below ₹2.5 lakh Full interest during the moratorium for overseas studies Padho Pardesh Scheme Minority community students studying abroad Below ₹6 lakh per year Full interest during the moratorium for overseas studies Mr Khanna’s situation, a domestic MBBS program, family income below ₹4.5 lakh, falls squarely under the CSIS scheme. The other schemes apply to overseas education or specific community categories. Education loans and the CSIS scheme: what to check before applying Before applying for an education loan with the intent to claim the CSIS subsidy, confirm the following with your lender: Is the loan structured under the IBA model education loan scheme? Does the institution and course appear on the approved list of AICTE, UGC or MCI? Is the income certificate from an authorized officer acceptable? Has the bank or NBFC processed CSIS claims before? On the other hand, eligibility for such schemes may not be available to every individual, as they have specific, detailed criteria. In such cases, you can opt for an education loan from Tata Capital. For MBBS and other professional undergraduate programs at recognized Indian institutions, Tata Capital offers loans up to ₹85 lakh without collateral and up to ₹2 crore with security. Interest rates start from 9.50% p.a. Where applicable, the CSIS subsidy can significantly reduce the effective cost of the loan over the course period. Conclusion The Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS) scheme is a practical way for families with an annual income below ₹4.5 lakh to reduce the cost of an education loan. The scheme covers full interest during the moratorium period on loans up to ₹7.5 lakh for eligible undergraduate technical and professional courses. The application goes through the lending bank or NBFC. The income certificate, proof of admission, and loan documentation are the key requirements. Status can be tracked through the Vidya Lakshmi portal or directly with the lender. For families like Mr Khanna’s, combining the CSIS subsidy with an education loan from a transparent lender can make the difference between a loan that feels manageable and one that does not. Who is eligible for the CSIS scheme? Indian students whose family income is below ₹4.5 lakh per year, studying full-time undergraduate technical or professional courses at recognized Indian institutions approved by AICTE, UGC or MCI. The loan must be under the IBA model education loan scheme. What does the CSIS subsidy cover? The CSIS subsidy covers 100% of the interest on education loans during the moratorium period. This applies to the loan amount up to ₹7.5 lakh. No interest accumulates for the student during the course duration plus one year after completion. The lender files the subsidy claim with Canara Bank, the nodal bank for the scheme. How can I check my CSIS subsidy status? Contact your lending institution with your loan account number and ask for the CSIS claim reference. You can also log in to the Vidya Lakshmi portal (vidyalakshmi.co.in) to track the status of your education loan subsidy application. Does the CSIS scheme apply to MBBS courses? Yes. Medical Council of India-recognized MBBS programs qualify under the CSIS scheme, provided the student meets the income eligibility criteria and the loan is under the IBA model scheme. Does Tata Capital offer education loans eligible for the CSIS subsidy? Tata Capital offers education loans for undergraduate professional and technical courses at recognized institutions. Check with Tata Capital's education loan team whether your specific loan structure qualifies under the IBA model scheme for CSIS purposes. Education loans start from 9.50% p.a. Visit tatacapital.com/education-loan.html for details. What is the maximum loan amount covered under the CSIS scheme? The CSIS interest subsidy applies to the loan amount up to ₹7.5 lakh. If the loan exceeds this amount, the subsidy covers only the interest on the ₹7.5 lakh portion. The remaining loan amount accrues interest as normal. Rs 25 lakh education loan without collateral?” And the straight answer – yes, you can! In this comprehensive guide, we will navigate the realm of study abroad loan without collateral, helping you understand the ins and outs of securing a substantial 25 Lakhs for your educational pursuits. Let’s get started. What is a Non Collateral (Unsecured) Education Loan? A non-collateral student loan, often referred to as an unsecured education loan, is a financial boon for students seeking funds for their overseas education without the obligation of providing collateral. Unlike traditional loans that demand assets like property or land as security, non-collateral education loans allow you to borrow without risking your valuable possessions. Maximum Amount One of the key advantages of an education loan for abroad studies without collateral is the flexibility in loan amounts. Students can secure up to Rs 50 Lakhs to fund their education without the burden of collateral. This substantial sum caters to various expenses , including tuition fees, living costs, travel expenses, and study materials, ensuring that financial constraints don’t hinder your educational pursuits. Eligibility Criteria for Education Loan Without Collateral Now, let’s delve into the essential eligibility criteria shaping your journey to securing a Rs 25 Lakhs study abroad loan without collateral: 1. financial profile. The interest rates banks offer are generally lower than those of Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), but the eligibility criteria may be stricter. NBFCs might approve the loan faster with flexible eligibility rules, but NBFC home loan interest rates tend to be higher. NBFCs may give you a loan even if you have a lower credit score and non-standard income documents. However, banks will need you to have stable salaried jobs and a clean credit history. Deciding between a home loan from an NBFC vs a bank home loan requires comparing lending flexibility, interest rates, borrowing costs, and eligibility criteria. When it comes to financing a dream home in India, potential homeowners often find themselves facing the critical decision of choosing between a bank home loan and a non-banking financial company (NBFC) home loan . Both banking institutions and NBFCs offer diverse home loan options, with each having its own set of advantages and disadvantages. This article aims to provide an unbiased comparison between home loan NBFC vs bank loans, highlighting the various aspects that need to be considered before making a decision. NBFC home loans vs bank An NBFC home loan is offered by a non-banking financial company. It may allow more flexibility for borrowers with varied income sources or different financial profiles. Bank home loans generally follow more standardized lending processes, with interest rates, eligibility, and documentation often linked closely to the borrower’s credit profile and income. Comparing home loan from an NBFC vs bank loan based on interest rates, eligibility, flexibility, processing time, and overall costs helps you make a wise financial decision. What are the key differences between banks and NBFC home loans? Traditional bank loans differ from NBFC home loans in various ways, as shown in the table below: Factor Bank home loan NBFC home loan Interest rate Starting from 7.10% The NBFC home loan interest rate varies widely, starting from 7.15% Eligibility Usually stricter income, credit score, and documentation checks NBFC home loan eligibility may be more flexible for some self-employed or non-standard income profiles Processing time Often takes longer due to detailed verification and internal checks Can be faster because of digital processes and flexible assessment. Actual timelines vary by lender Documentation Generally, extensive income, identity, and property documents are required Documentation is required but may be more flexible Best suited for Borrowers with strong credit profiles seeking competitive rates Borrowers who value flexibility, faster processing, or have varied income profiles What are the advantages and disadvantages: Banks vs NBFCs for home loans? Understanding the disadvantages and advantages of home loans by banks and NBFCs helps you make an informed borrowing decision. Make sure you compare interest rates, eligibility, and processing speed before selecting a lender. Advantages and disadvantages of taking a home loan from a bank If you take a traditional bank home loan, you can get competitive interest rates and structured repayment options. However, stricter eligibility rules, lengthy processing, and extensive documentation may be drawbacks. Advantages Disadvantages Lower interest rates: Banks usually offer lower interest rates on home loans than NBFCs, owing to their access to low-cost funds from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and deposits from customers. This can lead to significant savings on interest payments over the loan tenure . Stringent eligibility criteria: Banks generally have stricter eligibility criteria, including higher credit score requirements, which can make it difficult for some borrowers with a lower credit score to qualify for a home loan. Better transparency: Banks are subject to stricter regulations and supervision by the RBI, resulting in better transparency in their operations and loan processes. This makes it easier for borrowers to understand the terms and conditions of their home loan and avoid any hidden charges. Rigid documentation requirements: Banks tend to be inflexible when it comes to documentation, requiring a long list of documents for loan approval, such as income tax returns, bank statements, and property documents. This can be a hassle for borrowers who may not have all the necessary documents readily available. Access to additional services: Banks typically provide a wide range of financial services, such as savings accounts, credit cards , and investment options . Opting for a home loan from a bank can make it convenient for borrowers to access and manage these services under one roof. Advantages and disadvantages of taking a home loan from an NBFC An NBFC home loan can be advantageous in different ways, such as faster processing, flexible eligibility, and convenient services. However, there may also be drawbacks, such as higher interest rates and fees than those charged by banks. Advantages Disadvantages Flexible eligibility criteria: NBFCs are known for their flexible eligibility criteria and are more willing to cater to borrowers with lower credit scores or unconventional income sources, making it relatively easier for many applicants to qualify for a home loan. Higher interest rates: NBFCs tend to charge higher interest rates on home loans than banks, as they source their funds from the market at higher costs. This can increase the overall cost of borrowing. However, the rate difference is not large compared to banks. Faster processing and disbursal: NBFCs generally have quicker loan processing and disbursal times than banks, as they are not subject to the same level of regulatory oversight. This can be advantageous for borrowers who need funds urgently. Limited range of services: Unlike banks, NBFCs may not offer a wide range of additional financial services, such as savings accounts or investment options, which could be a disadvantage for borrowers seeking a comprehensive financial solution. Customized loan products: NBFCs often offer specialized home loan products tailored to the specific needs of different customer segments, such as self-employed individuals, salaried professionals, or non-resident Indians (NRIs). What are the different types of home loans available from banks and NBFCs? Banks and NBFCs offer different home loan options to meet varied customer needs such as buying, constructing, renovating, or expanding a residential property. Here are the types of home loans offered by banks and NBFCs: Type of loan Description Home purchase loan This helps you buy ready or under-construction properties easily. Home construction loan This loan funds building your dream house on your land. Home renovation loan This loan helps finance renovations, repairs, and home improvements. Land purchase loan This is useful to purchase a residential plot. Balance transfer loan With this loan, you can shift your existing loans to a different lender for better rates. NRI home loans To support overseas Indians in property deals. What are the NBFC home loan interest rates? Comparing NBFC home loan interest rates helps you choose wisely in today’s market. Here are some latest NBFC loan rate trends: NBFCs often offer competitive rates, slightly higher than banks but with flexible terms. The NBFC current home loan rates start at 7.75% per year, depending on your credit profile and loan amount. NBFCs focus on faster approvals despite slightly higher rates. You can expect variable rates to follow market movements. Keep an eye on special offers or NBFC home loan interest rate cuts targeting specific borrower segments from time to time. What are the NBFC home loan eligibility criteria? The NBFC home loan eligibility criteria are as follows: The age specifications defined by the lenders. A proof of stable income criteria for NBFC loans with salary slips, ITR, or employment profiles. A good CIBIL score above 750 for better chances of approval. Valid ID proofs like Aadhaar and PAN cards. Your bank statements, to show sufficient repayment capacity via debt-to-income ratio. Salaried or self-employed both qualify for an NBFC home loan under the NBFC home loan eligibility criteria with proper financial proofs. What is the role of NBFCs in India’s financial inclusion & home loan sector? In growing India’s economy, there’s a big role for NBFCs. They serve people that banks often ignore, like self-employed or rural borrowers. NBFC financial inclusion works through quick approval of home loans with flexible rules in the NBFC home loan sector. NBFCs also make use of digital platforms and mobile banking facilities. This offers faster loan disbursements for different customer segments. This inclusive approach of NBFCs supports economic development and provides faster approvals compared to banks. Which is the best NBFC for home loans in India? While various top NBFCs offer flexible home loans to borrowers, Tata Capital is a leading NBFC for home loans in India. With Tata Capital , borrowers can apply for a customized home loan online and enjoy a quick approval and disbursal process. What are the features of Tata Capital NBFC home loans? Multipurpose loan Tata Capital home loans are multipurpose. You can use the funds for various purposes such as house construction, extension, purchase of under-construction property, home renovation, etc. Easy eligibility criteria Many NBFCs, such as Tata Capital, have simple eligibility criteria to cater to a wide range of borrowers. The standard eligibility factors include age specifications, credit history, employment profiles, and stable income requirements. Quick online application process You can quickly apply for a home loan online. All you need to do is access the home loan application form from the website, fill in your information, and upload the necessary documents. The experts will verify your documents and inspect the property. Once verified, your loan will be approved and disbursed within a few days. Conclusion In conclusion, the decision between taking a home loan NBFC vs bank loan ultimately depends on the specific needs and circumstances of the borrower. To make the best choice, borrowers should compare the interest rates, processing fees, loan features, and customer service quality of different banks and NBFCs before deciding on a home loan provider. They should also evaluate their financial situation, credit score, and long-term financial goals to determine which institution will best meet their needs. By carefully considering all of these factors, borrowers can make a well-informed decision that will help them secure their dream home and achieve their financial objectives. Further, NBFCs may have specific eligibility criteria for salaried employees and self-employed professionals. As a result, you must check specific requirements with your preferred lender before applying. Are NBFCs better than banks? NBFCs and banks each have their advantages when it comes to applying for a loan. NBFCs may offer quicker loan processing and more flexible eligibility criteria, while banks typically provide better transparency in processes, lower interest rates, and access to additional services such as savings accounts or investment options. The choice ultimately depends on the individual preferences and financial needs of the borrowers. How does Tata Capital simplify NBFC home loan processing? Tata Capital offers a quick approval and disbursal process. Our digital verification and minimal documentation requirements make NFBC home loan processing simple. Can NRIs apply for NBFC home loans? Yes, NRIs can apply for NBFC home loans. They just need to meet the eligibility criteria, such as a valid passport, age, and income proof. What are the repayment options available for NBFC home loans? NBFC home loans usually offer repayment options primarily as EMIs with flexible plans like step-up or step-down EMIs, and part-payments. Contact your lender to learn about the repayment options they provide. How to calculate EMIs for NBFC home loans? You can use Tata Capital’s online EMI calculator for calculating EMIs for NBFC home loans. EMIs for this loan are calculated in the same way as that of a bank home loan. Are interest rates lower in banks or NBFCs for home loans? The home loan interest rates banks offer may be lower, especially for borrowers with strong credit profiles. On the other hand, NBFC rates can vary based on the borrower, loan amount, and financial profile. You must compare the annual interest rate, processing fees, and other charges before choosing. How do eligibility criteria differ between banks and NBFCs? The eligibility criteria for banks are stricter than for NBFCs. Bank rules depend on income, credit score, and existing debts. When it comes to NBFCs, they may accept a wider range of borrowers. This is because their assessment methods are more flexible. Which offers faster home loan approval: Banks or NBFCs? NBFCs may offer faster home loan approvals because their processes can be more flexible and digital. But the process with banks may be longer due to internal procedures and extensive verification. The actual time taken to process your loan application also depends on your credit profile, income, and completeness of documents. Are NBFCs more flexible than banks in approving home loans? NBFCs can be more flexible than banks when assessing borrowers with varied income sources, self-employment, or non-standard financial profiles. However, this does not mean approval is guaranteed. NBFCs also assess income, credit history, repayment capacity, and property-related documents. What is the difference in loan processing time between banks and NBFCs? The processing time for a loan varies across lenders. Sometimes, NBFCs may process applications faster because of digital systems and flexible procedures. On the other hand, banks can take longer because of detailed checks and documentation. A complete application with accurate documents can help either lender process the loan faster. Why are leading NBFCS better for home loans? Leading NBFCs can offer convenient digital applications, faster processing, and flexible eligibility options. They may also provide personalized assistance throughout the application process. However, you should compare interest rates, fees, loan terms, customer service, and other charges before selecting an NBFC. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary A home loan sanction letter is an official document that lenders or financial institutions issue confirming loan approval. It mentions the key loan terms, including the loan amount, interest rate (fixed or floating), loan tenure, repayment terms, processing fees, prepayment charges, and more. No funds are released during this phase. A home loan disbursement letter confirms that the lender has completed all verification formalities and has subsequently transferred the funds to your bank account or that of the property builder or seller. Home loan sanction and disbursement are two steps in the loan process. The former involves loan approval after checking your borrower profile. The latter involves releasing the funds. If you’ve applied for a home loan and are waiting for its approval, you’re waiting for a loan sanction. A bank or financial institution provides this through a home loan sanction letter. The document is an official confirmation of the approval of your loan application . After you receive the sanction letter, the next phase is loan disbursement. It refers to the release and transfer of funds directly into your bank account. The home loan disbursement letter lets you initiate the process of purchasing a home. It is the stage from which your dream of owning a home is actually realized, and your bank account has the funds required to secure your new home. This article explains loan sanction meaning and the differences between a home loan sanction letter vs disbursement. What is a home loan sanction letter? A home loan sanction letter is the official document a bank or financial institution issues, confirming that your home loan application has been approved after thorough verification. It is a statement given by the lender regarding their willingness to grant a specific loan amount. To understand the loan sanction meaning, you need to go through the details covered in the sanction letter, including key information, such as the sanctioned amount, loan tenure, interest rate, EMI , and terms and conditions related to repayment and processing. To obtain it, you must submit necessary documents like property papers, income proof such as ITRs, salary slips, and KYC documents such as ID and address proof. These documents help the lender assess your repayment capacity, verify your identity, and ensure the property’s legality. A sanction letter is essential for loan disbursal. What is a home loan disbursement letter? The lender issues a home loan disbursement letter after the borrower accepts the loan offer and completes all documentation. It marks the stage when the sanctioned loan amount is ready to be released. The bank verifies property documents, legal clearances, and borrower details to ensure compliance with loan terms before disbursement. The disbursement process involves signing the final loan agreement, submitting post-dated cheques or ECS details, and completing any pending formalities. Funds are then released either in installments for under-construction properties or as a lump sum for ready-to-move homes or resale properties. The letter specifies the disbursed amount, payment schedule, and recipient details, the builder or the seller. It ensures full transparency between the borrower and lender, confirming that the loan has been officially released for the intended property purchase. What are the key differences between home loan sanction letter and disbursement? A sanction letter and a disbursement serve different purposes. The sanction letter signifies loan approval, while the disbursement marks fund release. The following table entails a quick comparison of the sanction letter vs the disbursement letter. Aspect Sanction letter Disbursement Meaning Official approval of your loan application by the lender Actual release of approved loan funds Stage Given by the lender after verifying eligibility Done after the sanction is accepted Purpose States the approval of the lender to grant a specific loan amount Transfers funds for property purchase or construction Documents required Income proof, KYC, credit report, property papers Signed loan agreement, property registration, NOC , builder’s demand letter Timing Early stage, before the loan amount is given Final stage, when funds are paid out Impact Builds borrowing ability Creates financial liability (EMIs start post-disbursement) To conclude, the sanction letter represents approval, while disbursement completes the funding process. Both are legally and financially crucial for home buyers. What are the home loan disbursement stages? Home loan disbursement stages begin after the loan is sanctioned. Before releasing funds, lenders verify the borrower’s eligibility and validate all submitted documents. Below are the key steps involved in the home loan sanction and disbursement process: Application stage: The borrower submits the loan application along with required documents, completes the KYC process, and pays the processing fee if applicable. The lender verifies the details and checks the borrower’s credit score and repayment capacity. Sanction stage: After successful verification, the lender approves the loan and issues a sanction letter outlining the approved amount, interest rate, tenure, and terms. The borrower must sign and accept this offer to proceed further. Legalities fulfillment: The borrower submits property-related documents for legal scrutiny. The lender conducts technical evaluation and title verification, including a property visit to assess location, ownership, and construction quality. Disbursement: This is the final stage of the home loan disbursement timeline. Once all conditions are fulfilled, the lender releases the loan amount and issues a home loan disbursement letter confirming the release. What is the loan agreement, and what are the essential documents for sanction and disbursement? A loan agreement is an official contract between the borrower and the lender, mentioning the terms and conditions of the approved loan. It includes key details such as the loan amount, interest rate, tenure, repayment schedule, EMI amount, penalties, and rights and obligations of both parties. Having a loan agreement is vital because it provides a clear understanding of the repayment responsibilities and applicable charges. It outlines what happens if you miss a payment. As a legal document, it protects both parties in case of disputes. It also helps maintain transparency, avoid unexpected costs, and misunderstandings. What are the key clauses that typically comprise a standard loan agreement? A loan agreement may contain several clauses that define the lender’s rights and your responsibilities. You must understand these clauses to know what you are agreeing to and avoid surprises during the loan tenure. Security cover clause: The loan must remain adequately secured throughout the tenure. If the value of the property falls or the security is damaged, the lender may ask for additional security. Setting off other balances: If you make any payment, it must first be used to clear other outstanding dues, such as penalties, fees or charges. The remaining amount is then adjusted towards the EMI or principal. Assignment to third parties: The lender has the right to transfer the loan to another party, such as another lender. The loan terms and borrower’s obligations continue to remain the same even after the transfer. Prepayment clause: This clause explains how the borrower can repay a part or all of the outstanding principal before the agreed loan tenure ends. It also mentions if there are any applicable charges. Notification clause: This clause highlights the borrower’s responsibility to inform the lender about important changes. These include changes in address, employment, income, or residential status. Definition of default: This clause explains what constitutes a default. Failure to make repayments on time is one such example. It also outlines the possible consequences. Amendment clause: It specifies how changes to the loan agreement can be made, including the process, timing, and rights of both parties. What are the documents required at the home loan sanction stage? You will need to submit certain documents at the sanction stage. These allow lenders to check your financial health, credit score , and eligibility before giving their formal approval and issuing a home loan sanction letter. The list includes: Income proof (salary slips, ITRs, Form 16) KYC documents (ID and address proof) Property documents (sale agreement, ownership proof) Bank statements and credit report What are the documents required at the disbursement stage? You also need to submit some documents at the disbursement stage. At this point, your loan is approved. However, the bank or lender requires final paperwork proving the property or purchase is ready and that all legal requirements are met. The list of documents includes: Signed loan agreement Property registration papers and NOC Builder’s demand letter or seller’s payment request Post-dated cheques or ECS mandate Together, these documents ensure financial authenticity and smooth loan processing. Also Read – When does a home loan balance transfer Why is a sanction letter important in a bank loan process? A home loan sanction letter is an important document that confirms that the lender has approved your loan application based on the stated terms and conditions. It gives you a clear picture of what the lender is offering before the loan is disbursed. Here’s why it is important to have a sanction letter: Confirms loan approval: The letter shows that the lender has sanctioned the loan. Details loan terms: It clearly states the loan amount, interest rate, tenure, EMI, and other conditions. Helps with planning: It allows you to assess whether the loan and EMIs fit your budget. Lists important conditions: It highlights the documents you must submit, the fees you need to pay, or other requirements to be completed before disbursement. Provides clarity: The letter creates a written record of the agreed terms so that there are no misunderstandings in the future. Also Read – When does a home loan balance transfer In conclusion A sanction letter indicates loan approval, while a disbursement indicates funds release. Since there are various steps involved in the loan disbursement process, you must be careful throughout. Read all the fine print and reach out to your lender in case of any queries. Check the validity of the home loan sanction letter before proceeding. If you want to apply for a home loan, Tata Capital is here for you. If a loan is sanctioned but not disbursed, it means that while the loan application has been approved, the funds have not yet been released to the borrower. The time between the loan sanction and disbursement can differ from one lender to another, and the borrower can contact the lender in case of delays. Is EMI based on the sanctioned amount or the disbursed amount? EMI (Equated Monthly Instalment) is calculated based on the disbursed amount, not the sanctioned amount. The sanctioned amount is the approved loan limit, but the EMI payments are determined by the amount disbursed to the borrower​. How much time does it take to disburse a home loan after sanction? The time taken to disburse a home loan after sanction varies but typically ranges from a few days to a few weeks. The duration depends on the lender's internal processes​ and may vary if they require additional documents from the borrower. What is the difference between sanction and disbursement? The sanction of a loan refers to the lender's approval of the loan application and the agreed loan amount. Disbursement, on the other hand, is the actual release of funds to the borrower after meeting all required conditions and documentation​. Can a bank cancel a home loan after disbursement? Generally, a bank cannot cancel a home loan after disbursement. They might, however, reject the loan application even after the sanction letter if there is a drop in the credit score or job instability. What is the difference between sanction and disbursed? Sanction refers to the approval of a loan or credit facility by a bank or financial institution for a specific amount of funds under pre-determined conditions. This sanction is based on your documents and eligibility. However, it doesn’t mean that the funds have been transferred to your account or released. Disbursement refers to the actual release or transfer of the approved funds. It is the step after loan sanction when the approved amount comes into your bank account. In simple words, a sanction relates to loan approval, while a disbursement relates to funds transfer. What is the purpose of a sanction letter? The sanction letter’s purpose is to officially confirm the bank’s acceptance and approval of your loan application. It is the lender’s formal offer, specifying all the necessary details of the loan, such as the sanctioned loan amount, tenure, interest rate, EMIs, repayment terms, and other conditions. The sanction letter serves as proof of loan eligibility. It is often required for processing home loan and education loan applications. It provides the borrower with financial backing proof, essential for planning their budget and for using as a negotiating tool with sellers or for visa applications. Borrowers can use the sanction letter to understand the approved offer before final disbursal. What is the personal loan disbursement and process for sanctioning? Personal loan disbursement is the process of transferring the approved loan amount to the borrower’s account after the loan has been sanctioned. The process for sanctioning begins with the submission of an application, followed by credit evaluation, document verification, and approval. The final loan agreement is signed after the bank issues the sanction letter and the borrower accepts the terms. The lender then disburses the loan amount directly into the borrower’s bank account. The disbursement timeline for personal loans is 24 to 48 hours. Is EMI calculated on the sanctioned amount or the disbursed amount? Equated Monthly Installment (EMI) is calculated on the disbursed amount, not the sanctioned amount. The sanctioned amount represents the maximum loan approved. However, when it comes to loan disbursement, the amount may change. Some fees or charges, such as insurance premiums or processing fees, may be deducted upfront at the time of disbursement. Hence, you cannot calculate EMI on the sanctioned amount because it is the disbursed amount that you’re liable to repay to the lender. The calculation of EMI depends on the amount disbursed, the applicable interest rate, and the repayment period. Do I get my sanction money back? No, there is no refund for the sanctioned money because sanctions are approvals and not the actual transfer of funds. The money is released into your account after loan disbursement, and the amount may vary from the sanctioned amount, as it also includes deductions for processing fees, insurance premiums, etc. If you don’t want to proceed with the loan after reviewing the details on the sanction letter, you can cancel the loan before disbursement. In this case, you do not owe the bank or lender any money, except the minimal processing fees charged by the lender for certain types of loans. Can a bank cancel a loan after it is disbursed? Generally, banks cannot cancel a loan after its disbursal, as it has been transferred to the borrower’s account, and the borrower is legally bound to repay. However, the borrower can request early closure to treat cancellation as an early repayment. This process involves repaying the full principal amount along with any applicable interest and fees. Sometimes, there may be fraudulent or misrepresented disbursements. If that happens, the bank has the right to take legal action. Normally, cancellation is possible only before disbursement, not after. How long does home loan disbursement take after sanction? Home loan disbursement process can take around 3 to 7 working days after sanction for ready properties. Under-construction properties disbursement can take slightly longer time due to stage-wise verification. Can a sanctioned loan be cancelled before disbursement? Yes. A sanctioned loan can be cancelled without any penalty before home loan disbursement stages as the sanction letter is an offer, not the final agreement. What documents are required at disbursement stage specifically? Signed copies of sanction letter, loan agreement, property documents like sale deed, allotment letter, payment receipts, bank account details, identity and address proofs are required at disbursement stage. How is EMI calculated if loan is disbursed in installments? The regular EMI (principal + interest) starts after the full disbursement or possession if the loan is disbursed in installments. You only have to pay pre-EMIs (interest-only) on the amounts drawn until then. What if property documents are found unsatisfactory during disbursement? If any of the required documents are found unsatisfactory, the home loan sanction and disbursement process is halted until the discrepancies or missing paperwork are resolved. The loan may even be rejected if the issues cannot be fixed. Who pays margin money and when? have a regular income. In most cases, the loan is approved with the support of a parent or guardian as a co-applicant or by taking the loan in the parent’s name. Understanding the eligibility criteria, required documents, repayment terms, and costs can make the borrowing process much smoother. It’s also important to borrow only what you need and repay the loan on time to maintain a healthy credit profile for future financial needs. A two-wheeler loan for students without income is a financing option that usually allows students to buy a bike or scooter with the support of a parent or guardian who meets the lender’s income requirements. Many students dream of owning a bike or scooter because it makes daily travel to college, coaching classes, internships, or part-time jobs much easier. It saves time, reduces dependence on public transport, and offers greater flexibility in managing a busy schedule. However, funding a two-wheeler may come across as a hurdle for most of them. A two-wheeler loan for students without income becomes the best bet here. But most students do not have a regular source of income or salary slips, making it difficult to qualify for a loan on their own. However, it is important to know that some lenders approve bike loan for students with the support of a parent or guardian as a co-applicant or guarantor. In this guide, we have explained how a two-wheeler loan for students without income works and how to apply for it. We have also explained the eligibility criteria, the required documents, and other requirements for the loan. Keep reading. Can a student get a two-wheeler loan without income proof? In most cases, a student cannot get a two-wheeler loan without income proof entirely on their own. Since lenders need confidence that the loan will be repaid, they usually require a co-applicant or guarantor. They can be anyone, such as a parent, sibling, or guardian, with a stable source of income. The loan can also be approved in the parent’s name, while the student uses the vehicle. Some lenders may also consider alternative financial profiles or additional supporting documents, depending on their lending policy. So, if you are looking for a two-wheeler loan for students without income, having a financially strong co-applicant can significantly improve your chances of getting the loan approved. Also Read – Zero-down payment bike loan How does a bike loan for students work? Lending institutions in India offer bike loan for students through several routes. The most suitable route depends on your personal choice and the availability of financial support from the family. Route 1 – Co-applicant or guarantor model This is the most common option. A parent, sibling, or guardian with a stable income becomes a co-applicant or guarantor for the loan. Route 2 – Loan in the parent’s name The loan can be sanctioned in the parent’s name, and the parent will be responsible for the repayment. However, the student uses the two-wheeler for college, coaching, or daily travel. Route 3 – Secured loan option If no one is available to become a co-applicant or guarantor, the student can secure the two-wheeler loan by offering a Fixed Deposit (FD) or any such asset as collateral. It’s also important to note that the two-wheeler itself is usually hypothecated to the lender as security until the loan is fully repaid. What are the eligibility criteria for a bike loan for students? The eligibility criteria for a two-wheeler loan for students without income may differ from one lender to another. However, most lenders look for the following parameters: The student should usually be 18 years or older. A parent or guardian with a stable income should apply as a co-applicant or guarantor. Valid KYC documents of both the student and the co-applicant must be submitted. Some lenders may ask for a minimum down payment. The co-applicant should satisfy the lender’s income and credit requirements. Read More – Common two-wheeler loan mistakes new borrowers should avoid What are the documents required? The following documents are usually required for a two-wheeler loan without income proof: Student’s documents KYC documents (Aadhaar card, PAN card, Voter ID card, or Passport) A valid driving license College ID card or admission letter Address proof (if different from the KYC document) Passport-size photographs Co-applicant’s documents KYC documents (Aadhaar card, PAN card, Voter ID card, or Passport) Income proof, such as salary slips or Income Tax Returns (ITRs) Recent bank statements Address proof (if different from the KYC document) Passport-size photographs What are the tips to improve approval chances? Here are a few practical tips that can help you improve your chances of getting a two-wheeler loan for students without income: Add a co-applicant with a strong credit profile and income. Adding someone with a poor credit history or low income can further jeopardize your chances of loan approval. Pay a higher down payment. Doing so reduces the lender’s risk and thus improves the likelihood of loan approval. Choose an affordable two-wheeler. Select a bike or scooter that matches the co-applicant’s repayment capacity instead of opting for a high-priced model. Keep all documents ready. Submit complete KYC, college, income, and address documents to avoid delays during verification. Also Read – Two-Wheeler Loan Checklist How to apply for a student two-wheeler loan? Several banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) in India offer two-wheeler loans for students without income. You can apply online or offline in the following steps: Choose the two-wheeler you want to purchase and check its on-road price with the dealer. Identify the co-applicant or guarantor for your loan. It can be your parent, sibling, or guardian. Fill out an online loan application on the lender’s website or mobile app. To apply offline, visit the lender’s nearest branch. Submit the required documents. Upon approval, the funds are disbursed directly to the lender. The process can take a few hours to a few working days. What are the things to keep in mind when applying for a loan? Even if it is a bike loan for students, it involves a financial commitment. You must keep the following in mind when borrowing: Borrow only what can be comfortably repaid. Avoid taking a bigger loan than your parent’s repayment capacity. Understand the EMI and total borrowing cost. Check the interest rate, tenure, processing fee, and other charges before accepting the loan. Remember that the co-applicant is equally responsible. If the EMIs are missed, it can affect the co-applicant’s credit score as well. It’s important to pay the EMIs on time. Timely repayment helps build a good credit history for future loans. Read the loan terms carefully. Make sure you understand the repayment schedule, charges, and conditions before signing the agreement. Conclusion A two-wheeler loan without income proof is generally possible when a parent or guardian joins as a co-applicant or guarantor. This makes it easier for students to finance a bike while ensuring the lender has a reliable repayment source. However, it’s important to compare loan offers, understand the repayment terms, and borrow only what your parents can comfortably repay. Can a student get a two-wheeler loan in their parent's name? Yes. Many students choose to take the loan in their parents’ name, especially when they have no income. The parent becomes the borrower and repays the loan, while the student uses the two-wheeler. This is a common option offered by many lenders. What is the minimum age for a two-wheeler loan? Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund We, as individuals, have a general tendency to plan for almost everything. Education, marriage, holidays, work and our future are what we plan for. Some of us plan to study further in a renowned university, while some plan to get married at a certain age. Holidays and vacations are something we all want and the most common thing we want in life is a secured future. While planning is easy, the actual hard part is saving up for those plans. Now, if you have any kind of savings or financial nest somewhere, you are set to carry out your plans. However, what if you come across a financial roadblock on your way to make your dreams come true? You would not and should not give up on your dreams. How about a little help instead? Help comes to you in the form of personal loans. Be it for education, marriage or travel- a personal loan is an unsecured loan that you can avail in time of your financial crunch. While you would not need to keep any security or collateral, there are few things you will need. One of them is a good CIBIL score . What is CIBIL Score? Before you open your web browser and try to understand what exactly a CIBIL score is, here is a gist of it. This is your credit information report and the three digit number defines your credit history. It is as simple as that. Credit score ranges from 300 to 900 and better the credit history, higher the score. Your CIBIL score defines how good you have been with your payments and credit exposure. While calculating your CIBIL score, your credit card utilisation, repayment of credit card bills, number of loans, repayment of those loans are taken into consideration. Once you apply and hand over the information to the agency, they calculate your CIBIL score and formulate a credit report which explains how much your creditworthiness is. This score is what you submit while you apply for a personal loan. If you have never defaulted on payments and have good credit exposure, chances are you can get a score of 750 or above. Your high personal loan CIBIL score can not only help you avail a personal loan but also give you better interest rates and fast disbursal of the personal loan. Also Read – 800-Plus Credit Score Steps to get a Personal Loan with a Low CIBIL Score Just because a few things did not work in your favor does not mean you feel hopeless. If you are applying for a personal loan and your CIBIL score is low, you shouldn’t lose heart. There are a few things you can still do that can work in your favour while applying for a personal loan. 1. Opt for a lower loan amount Applying for a high loan amount with a poor credit score can affect your chances of approval. The higher the amount you apply for, the riskier you appear to the lender. Consider applying for a lower loan amount if you meet other eligibility criteria. The lender might be willing to offer you a lower amount. What’s more, this will also make repayment easier for you. 2. Stable Income Another way to get a low credit score personal loan is by proving your financial capability to the lender. If you have received a salary hike recently or have an additional source of income, the lender may consider your application despite a low score. You can offer evidence of a stable job and income source, which can increase the likelihood of loan approval as it indicates higher repayment capacity. However, you may have to pay a higher rate of interest on the loan. 3. Get a co-applicant If you have a poor credit score, you can also consider applying for a loan with a co-applicant or a guarantor. You can apply for a joint loan with your spouse, close relative, or a friend with a healthy credit score, thus leveraging their score for approval. Moreover, with the permission of your guarantor or co-applicant, you need to provide a few signatures and fulfill KYC formalities for the loan. Getting a co-applicant is more likely to increase your chances of loan approval and can even fetch you affordable personal loan interest rates. 4. Pledge a collateral While personal loans are an unsecured form of finance, you can still check if there is a provision for collateral. You can ask your lender and consider pledging security against your loan to improve your loan application. The lender might re-consider and offer a personal loan for a low CIBIL score if you can offer collateral as a security. 5. Leverage Alternative Lenders Traditional banks often rely heavily on credit scores when evaluating loan applications. At Tata Capital, we consider multiple factors, including your income stability, banking behaviour, repayment capacity, and overall financial profile. This broader assessment may help eligible borrowers access financing even if they have faced challenges obtaining credit through conventional lending channels. How is the CIBIL Score Calculated? The CIBIL score is calculated as Payment history : Accounts for 35% of the score. Ensuring timely EMI payments positively impact the score. Credit utilisation : Makes up 30% of the score. A lower credit utilisation rate, less than 30%, is preferable. Credit type and duration : Contributes 25% to the score. You must avoid having numerous credit lines and have a diverse mix of credit types (loans, credit cards ) to maintain a good credit score. Credit report inquiries : Factors like credit report inquiries and number of credit lines account for 20% of the score. Credit mix : Older accounts with clean records improve the score. New credit and inquiries : Each hard inquiry from a fresh loan application temporarily reduces your score. Applying to multiple lenders in a short window causes a bigger drop. Your CIBIL report will include your credit score, personal and contact information, credit summary, credit history of inquiries, and financial status according to employment. What are the Different CIBIL Score Ranges? Your CIBIL score is grouped into different ranges that indicate your creditworthiness. Understanding these ranges can help you assess your chances of loan approval and identify areas where you may need to improve your credit profile. CIBIL Score Creditworthiness Probability of Approval <600 Needs attention Low 600-649 Uncertain Difficult 650-699 Satisfactory Possible 700-749 Good Good 750-900 Excellent Very high Eligibility to get a Personal Loan for a low CIBIL score Here are the various eligibility factors that you must consider to apply for a loan, even with a low CIBIL score- Income – To avail of a loan with a low CIBIL score, you must be able to show the lender that you have a high income and repayment capacity. For this, you must provide proof of income. Employment – Salaried individuals working in public or private organisations can apply. Employment proof – Lenders also require a stable employment history and income to determine financial stability. To be eligible for a personal loan for CIBIL defaulter , provide documents like salary slips and employment certificates as required by the lender. Age – Applicants need to fall within the lender’s prescribed age criteria. Meeting the minimum and maximum age requirements is an important part of the eligibility assessment. Existing Debt Burden – Lenders also consider your current financial obligations, including EMIs and other outstanding loans. A manageable debt burden and a healthy repayment capacity can improve your chances of loan approval. Factors that Affect Your CIBIL Score Applying for a CIBIL score is like tossing a coin. Either you get a high score or a low score. If your score is high, you can rejoice as you know your chances of getting your personal loan approved is high with better interest rates. However, what if you are in for a rude awakening when you find out that you have a low CIBIL score? Well, before you lose hope let’s consider a few factors that got you the low score in the first place: 1. Your application: You know the saying “try, try till you succeed…” In this context, the multiple loan applications that you have been sending out to banks and financial institutions; be it for a personal loan, a secured loan or credit card can get you a low CIBIL Score. 2. A high number of unsecured loans: Too much of a good thing is, sometimes, bad enough. If you have too many loans against your name, this would be another factor that can lower your CIBIL score. 3. Delaying and defaulting payments: Any missed payment or part-payment, be it for your credit card or your loan EMI, will give you a negative mark on your CIBIL score. There is a reason why your EMI structure is explained while availing a personal loan. This is so that you know how much your monthly outflow would be against your loan and you plan your finances accordingly. 4. Someone else defaulting on payments: Yes, you read it right. If you are a guarantor for someone else and if that person has delayed or defaulted on their payments, it will affect your CIBIL score as well. 5. Payment History The 35% weight of your score. Every EMI paid on time strengthens it; every delay hurts it. Set up auto-debit to remove human error from this. 6. Credit Mix & Age A varied credit history (mix of loans and cards) built over years reflects better management than a thin history with one product. Do not close old, well-managed credit cards; they contribute positively to credit age. 7. New Enquiries Hard inquiries stay on your report for 24 months and briefly reduce the score. Soft inquiries (like checking your own report) do not affect it. Only apply for new credit when necessary. Importance of CIBIL Score for Personal Loans Your CIBIL score indicates your creditworthiness and is crucial in ensuring loan eligibility. Here’s how a high CIBIL score is important for you- Increase your chances of approval : A higher credit score can increase the likelihood of loan approval. Fetch competitive interest rates : A good score can help fetch lower interest rates, reducing overall loan costs. Apply for a high loan amount : With a high credit score, you may also qualify for higher loan amounts. Get better repayment terms : Strong credit scores can also help you secure more favourable loan and repayment terms. Enjoy high negotiation power : Borrowers with high scores have better leverage to negotiate loan terms and interest rates based on their financial needs. There are means and ways to everything. All you need to do is work around it. If you have a low CIBIL score and are applying for a personal loan, speak to NBFC like Tata Capital and you will find a way out. Conclusion Getting a personal loan with a low CIBIL score may seem challenging, but it is not impossible. What matters most is how you present your overall financial profile to the lender. By focusing on factors like stable income, responsible borrowing, and choosing the right loan amount, you can improve your chances of approval even with a lower score. At the same time, working on improving your credit habits will benefit you in the long run by helping you access better loan terms and lower interest rates. With the right approach and careful planning, a personal loan can still support your financial needs without putting undue pressure on your finances. It may be possible to get a personal loan without a CIBIL score. To determine eligibility, lenders may consider alternative factors such as high income, employment stability, and repayment capacity. Can I Get a Loan with a 550 CIBIL Score? Depending on the lender’s eligibility criteria, you may get a loan with a 550 CIBIL score, but it may come with higher interest rates and stringent terms. What is the lowest CIBIL Score for a personal loan? Typically, the lowest CIBIL score accepted for personal loans is around 600. However, each lender has different criteria, and some may consider scores below this threshold, especially if other factors like income are strong. Which loan is easiest to qualify for? Secured loans are often the easiest to qualify for. These loans require collateral, reducing the lender’s risk and making approval more likely even if the applicant’s credit score is low. To improve your CIBIL score, it is important to make timely payments on all credit accounts, reduce outstanding debt, and maintain a low credit utilisation ratio.
