Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Your credit score reflects your financial behavior. A number between 300 and 900 tells lenders how well you manage your credit. Higher scores indicate good debt repayment, which can lead to lower rates and higher limits on loans and credit cards. The credit scores are based on different models that are determined by the credit bureaus, of which the most commonly recognized one for the country is the average CIBIL Score. Other equally popular credit scoring models include Equifax and Experian. They all follow the same basic principles. What is the Average CIBIL Score/Average Credit Score in India? Examining your credit score may make you compare yourself to others. Comprehending the typical credit score within the nation can provide insight into your position. A 700 score is good, indicating responsible credit management in India. A score over 750 indicates good credit. But a score under 650 could raise interest rates and make credit harder to get. Typical Ranges for Credit Scores (CIBIL Score): Substandard: 300–499 Moderate: 500–649 Excellent: 650–749 Excellent: 750–799 Great: 800–900 Credit scores vary depending on age, income, and credit history. Individuals who are younger or new to credit usage may exhibit lower credit scores compared to those with an established and stable borrowing history. Credit Score Chart: Ranges & Loan Approval Odds in India A credit score helps lenders decide how risky it is to give you a loan . In India, a CIBIL score ranges from 300 to 900. Higher scores mean better loan approval chances. 1. Below 600 This score shows poor credit health. It usually means missed payments or high debt. Most lenders avoid approving loans in this range. 2. 600–649 This range signals weak credit behaviour. Loan approval is possible but difficult, and interest rates may be high. 3. 650–699 A fair score that shows average credit management. Some lenders may approve loans, but the terms may not be very attractive. 4. 700–749 This score reflects good credit habits. Loan approval chances are strong, with better interest rates. 5. 750–900 An excellent score showing high trustworthiness. Loans are easily approved with the best rates and flexible terms. Why is a Normal Credit Score Important in India? The credit score plays a crucial role in an individual’s financial status. It influences the acquisition of loans, credit cards, mortgages, and certain employment opportunities. Your score is used by almost all banks, lending institutions, and credit card companies to figure out how risky you are. What are the Benefits of a High or Good Credit Score? Low interest rates: A normal credit score makes you a more attractive borrower, lowering loan, credit card, and mortgage rates. Increased loan approval qualifications: A normal credit score makes it easier to get personal or home loans . Enhanced credit limits: A normal credit score frequently results in elevated credit limits, providing greater latitude in financial management. Disadvantages Associated with a Low Credit Score Elevated interest rates: One might encounter increased interest rates, resulting in a more costly borrowing experience. Restricted availability of financial instruments: The range of premium credit cards and loans with advantageous conditions may be constrained. An individual seeks such housing or employment when landlords or employers use his credit records in the course of the application. A normal credit score may qualify a borrower for a lower home loan interest rate , saving them a lot of money over the decades. Low scores usually mean higher loan repayments and a lower chance of getting loans or credit cards. Factors Affecting Your Average or CIBIL Credit Score Several factors play a huge role in determining the scores that you may get. Although the specific algorithms may vary among different scoring models, they all examine comparable elements of your financial history. Here is an analysis of the most significant elements: Payment History (35%): Credit account repayment timelines affect credit scores. Delinquent payments, defaults, and bankruptcies can severely damage your credit score. Your debt (30%): Total debt, especially the ratio of your outstanding balance to your credit limit, affects your score. Using a lot of credit can hurt your score. Try to keep your credit utilization ratio below 30%. Credit history duration (15%): A longer credit history boosts your score. Keeping older accounts in good standing shows stable borrowing. New credit (10%): A hard inquiry may lower your score when you apply for new credit. Credit inquiries in a short time may indicate financial instability. Credit cards, auto loans , and home loans can boost your score. Creating new accounts without a need may lower your score in the short term. How Does an Average Credit Score in India Affect Loans and Credit Card Approval? Average credit scores can open doors, but they may not get the best terms. Your borrowing capacity and financial options are greatly affected by your average credit score. Benefits: Facilitated authorization for a majority of loans and credit card applications. Access to superior interest rates and credit terms compared to those with less favorable scores. Drawbacks: Elevated interest rates, in contrast to those possessing exemplary credit ratings. Restricted availability of exclusive rewards programs and financial offerings. Consider a scenario in which two individuals seek to obtain a personal loan amounting to ₹5,00,000. The individual possessing an average credit score is projected to incur approximately ₹66,000 in interest over a span of 12 months, given an APR of 23.74%. With an exemplary credit rating (APR: 15.74%), the individual will incur a mere ₹43,600 in interest for the identical loan sum. The disparity in interest payments underscores the potential for substantial savings over time that can be achieved through an improved credit score. Common Reasons for a Low Average CIBIL Score and How to Fix Them A low average CIBIL score usually happens due to poor credit habits or unnoticed mistakes. Here are common reasons and simple ways to fix them: 1. Late or missed payments Even one delayed payment can lower your score. Always pay EMIs and credit card bills on time, and set reminders or auto-debit to avoid delays. 2. High credit card usage Using too much of your credit limit signals risk. Try to keep card spending below 30% of the total limit to maintain a healthy score. 3. Too many credit applications Applying for many cards or loans creates multiple credit checks. Apply only when needed and space out applications. 4. Multiple active loans Having too many loans increases your debt burden. Focus on closing small or high-interest loans before taking new ones. 5. Errors in credit reports Incorrect details or fraud can reduce your score. Check your report regularly and raise disputes immediately. How to Check Average Credit Score or CIBIL Score in India To manage your finances well, you must monitor your credit score. Here’s how you can check your average credit score in India: Credit Reports: You get one free credit report from CIBIL, Experian, and Equifax annually. Many financial institutions offer free credit score assessments. Credit Card Companies: Many Indian credit card companies offer free credit score reports. Digital Platforms: CRED and BankBazaar offer free credit score checks. How to Improve Your Average Credit Score in India If your credit score is average, you can improve it. Pay bills on time: Your credit score is your payment history. Establishing an autopay system or using reminders may help avoid missing due dates. Reduce credit card balances to keep your credit utilization ratio under 30%. This will improve your score. Maintain Existing Accounts: Closing longstanding accounts reduces your credit history. Instead, it increases your credit utilization ratio. This can lower your credit score. Reduce the number of hard inquiries: Having several credit cards or loans raised in a limited period can dampen the credit score. Addressing Credit Report Inaccuracies: To avoid credit score damage, dispute credit report errors. Through persistent endeavors, enhancing your score and realizing financial aspirations becomes increasingly feasible. Conclusion An average credit score in India can unlock financial products, and with diligence, one can improve one’s score and economic prospects. Recognizing that even small credit practices like timely bill payments and credit utilization reduction can improve credit scores is crucial.Commence the management of your credit today, thereby asserting control over your financial future. For an in-depth examination of financial products that may assist you in enhancing your credit profile, consider visiting Tata Capital’s website or downloading the Tata Capital app. FAQs What is the average credit score in India for 2024? The average credit score in India typically falls around 620–700. This range is seen as common and shows moderate credit behaviour, but higher scores still improve loan approval chances and better terms. What is considered a normal or good credit score for loans in India? A good credit score in India is generally 700 and above. Scores above this make it easier to get loans with better interest rates, while scores of 750+ are seen as excellent. Can I get a personal loan with an average credit score? Yes, you may get a personal loan with an average score (around 650–699), but approval is less certain and interest rates may be higher than for those with better scores. How does the average credit score affect home loan interest rates? An average credit score can still get a home loan, but lenders may charge higher interest rates and offer less attractive terms compared to borrowers with scores above 750. Does a higher income automatically mean a higher CIBIL score? No. A higher income does not automatically improve your CIBIL score. Your score depends mainly on credit behaviour, such as payments, credit use, and history. How fast can I improve my average credit score to a good score? You can begin to see improvement in 3–6 months by paying bills on time and lowering credit use, but reaching a good score may take longer, depending on your credit habits and history. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary A legal heir certificate helps establish the lawful heirs of a deceased person and is commonly used during property mutation, transfer, and other administrative processes. Although it is not mandatory for every property transfer, it often becomes necessary when the owner dies without leaving a valid will or when authorities ask for proof of succession. It is also important to understand how it differs from a succession certificate, the documents needed to obtain it, and the application process. Knowing when this document is required can help heirs complete property-related formalities with fewer delays. Losing a loved one is very difficult. The last thing any family would want is confusion over paperwork when it comes to transferring the deceased person’s property. One document that is frequently mentioned during this process is a legal heir certificate. Many people wonder, “Is a legal heir certificate mandatory for property transfer?” The short answer is no. It is not compulsory in every situation. However, it becomes an important document in many cases, particularly when the deceased has not left behind a valid will. Understanding what a legal heir certificate is and when it is required can save time and prevent unnecessary delays. This article explains the meaning of a legal heir certificate, when it is required, the documents needed to obtain it, and how it differs from a succession certificate. Keep reading. What is a legal heir certificate? Let’s start with the meaning of a legal heir certificate. A legal heir certificate is an official document issued by the competent local authority, such as the Tehsildar, Revenue Officer, or Municipal Corporation, to identify the surviving legal heirs of a deceased person. It helps establish the legal relationship between the deceased and their heirs for certain administrative and financial purposes. A legal heir document is typically required when transferring property, claiming insurance proceeds, accessing bank accounts, or settling other assets of a deceased person. This document is governed by state laws and is also known as a Varisu Certificate, Waris Certificate, or Family Member Certificate in different states. Also Read – Possession certificate: Meaning, importance Is a legal heir certificate mandatory for property transfer? Now that you know what a legal heir certificate is, it’s time to address the elephant in the room: is a legal heir certificate mandatory for property transfer? The answer depends on the circumstances. While this document becomes important in many situations, especially when there is no clear proof of succession, it is not always required for property transfers. Learning about these situations in advance can help heirs avoid unnecessary paperwork and delays during the transfer process. When do you need a legal heir certificate? Here are the common situations in which a legal heir certificate is typically required: When the property owner dies without leaving a valid will (intestate). For property mutation in municipal or revenue records after the owner’s death. When government departments, banks, housing authorities, or other financial institutions require proof of the deceased person’s legal heirs before processing the transfer or releasing assets. When is a legal heir certificate not required? On the other hand, a legal heir document may not be necessary in certain cases. If the deceased has left behind a registered will (or probate), the property can usually be transferred based on that document. In cases of joint ownership with survivorship rights. If the family has executed a registered family settlement. What is the difference between a legal heir certificate and a succession certificate? Many people use the terms legal heir certificate and succession certificate interchangeably. Both these documents are issued after a person’s death. However, they serve different purposes. The table below explains the difference between a legal heir certificate and a succession certificate to help you apply for the right document and avoid delays in settling property or financial assets. Basis Legal heir certificate Succession certificate Issuing authority Tehsildar, Revenue Officer, Municipal Corporation, or other competent local authority. Competent civil courts. Purpose Identifies the legal heirs of the deceased for property mutation, government benefits, insurance claims, and similar purposes. Primarily used to claim movable financial assets such as bank deposits, shares, securities, debentures, and other investments. Governing law Governed by the applicable state rules and procedures. Issued under the Indian Succession Act, 1925. Time taken For issuance Usually around 15-30 days (may vary by state). Commonly takes 3-6 months, depending on court procedures. What are the documents required for a legal heir certificate? The exact documents required for a legal heir certificate may differ slightly from one state to another. However, most authorities ask applicants to submit the following papers: Death certificate of the deceased. Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, or other identity and address proof of the applicant. Identity and address proof of the other legal heirs (if any). Proof of relationship with the deceased. For example, a birth certificate, family register, etc. Ration card or family card, if applicable. Self-declaration or affidavit on the prescribed stamp paper. Identity and address proof of the deceased. Also Read – What is a Commencement Certificate? How to apply for a legal heir certificate? The process to apply for a legal heir certificate is fairly straightforward. Although the exact method may vary slightly from one state to another, it usually involves the following steps: Go to the Tehsildar or Taluk Office, or access your state’s e-District or other official online portal. Fill in the application form by entering the required details of the deceased, the applicant, and all the legal heirs. Attach or upload the supporting documents required for a legal heir certificate. Make sure the documents are accurate and complete. Submit the duly filled application form at the designated office or upload it through the official portal. Pay the application fee (if any). Wait for the revenue official or other local authority to verify the details. Upon successful verification, a legal heir certificate will be issued. The process may take around 15 to 30 days. Why does a legal heir certificate matter for property and home loans? A legal heir certificate plays an important role when ownership of a property has to be updated after the owner’s death. It is commonly used during property mutation to establish who the lawful heirs are. If the inherited property has an outstanding home loan , lenders also need clarity on the legal heirs before processing requests related to repayment, transfer, or ownership changes. For inherited or jointly owned properties, Tata Capital (HFL) may require relevant legal documents as part of its verification process before considering any home loan-related request. Also Read – Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC): Meaning, process & how to apply online Conclusion Whether you are a property owner or a legal heir seeking to transfer property after the loss of a family member, learning the meaning of a legal heir certificate can make a big difference. If you are wondering, “Is a legal heir certificate mandatory for property transfer?”, the answer is not always. It may be required if the owner dies without leaving a will, or when a property mutation needs to be completed. Since the rules can vary across states and individual situations, it is advisable to consult the concerned authority or a legal professional before proceeding. This article is meant for general information and should not be treated as legal advice. No, not in every case. Some property transfers happen without it. For example, a registered will may be enough. But if the owner dies without a will, the local authority may ask for a legal heir certificate before updating the property records. The requirement depends on the facts of the case. What is a legal heir certificate? A legal heir certificate is a document issued by the local authority after a person's death. It lists the surviving legal heirs of the deceased. Families often need it while updating property records or dealing with banks, insurance companies, and government offices after the death of a family member. What documents are required for a legal heir certificate? The exact list differs from one state to another. In most cases, you will need the death certificate, identity proof of the applicant, documents showing the relationship with the deceased, and address proof. Some states may also ask for an affidavit or other supporting documents. What is the difference between a legal heir certificate and a succession certificate? People often confuse these two documents, but they are used for different purposes. A legal heir certificate identifies the legal heirs of the deceased. A succession certificate is usually needed when someone wants to claim financial assets such as bank deposits, shares, or securities through the court. Who can apply for a legal heir certificate? A family member who is legally recognized as an heir can apply. This could be the spouse, a son, a daughter, a parent, or another eligible heir, depending on the applicable law. The application is normally submitted to the local revenue office or through the state's online portal. How long does it take to get a legal heir certificate? There is no fixed timeline because every state follows its own procedure. In many places, the certificate is issued within 15 to 30 days if all the documents are in order. If the authorities need further verification, it may take a little more time. Can property be transferred without a legal heir certificate? Yes, that is possible in some situations. If there is a registered will, joint ownership with survivorship rights, or another legally accepted document, the transfer may go ahead without a legal heir certificate. operations, is calculated by estimating the difference between current assets and current liabilities. Current assets include cash, inventory, and money owed by customers. Current liabilities include bills and short-term debts due within a year. The significance of working capital monitoring lies in its ability to measure your short-term financial health and day-to-day operational liquidity. It tracks liquidity to determine if short-term assets can cover short-term debts like salaries and vendor bills. Working capital is the money a business has to continue its day-to-day operations. It is calculated by subtracting current liabilities from current assets. Want to know what working capital meaning is and what the working capital definition is? Let us explain the concept of working capital. Working capital and cash flow are two important financial metrics that every business keeps a close watch on. The importance of working capital and cash flow cannot be overstated. These two financial metrics help businesses evaluate whether they can withstand a market downturn or not. In simple terms, working capital is defined as the liquidity level of a company to meet its day-to-day and short-term expenses. There are various benefits of working capital for a company, from paying employees and vendors to planning for future needs. The importance of working capital for a business is remarkably high. As such, working capital meaning is related to the lifeblood of a business. The need for working capital is evident in its role in helping businesses manage daily expenses, maintain cash flow, and support smooth operations and growth. This article explores working capital, its importance, and explains the working capital management meaning for businesses. Working capital is a crucial financial metric that measures a company’s ability to meet its short-term obligations, such as paying bills and covering operational expenses. It is calculated by subtracting current liabilities from current assets. In simpler terms, working capital represents a company’s liquidity, indicating its capacity to generate cash and effectively manage its day-to-day operations. Also Read – Working capital loan vs term loan What is the need for working capital in a business? Working capital is essential in a business because it helps you manage daily operations without financial stress. It ensures you have adequate funds to pay short-term expenses, keep your business running smoothly, and handle unexpected costs. When a company has sufficient working capital, its financial stability improves, and it can take advantage of new business opportunities. The need for working capital can be seen in the following cases: Pay daily expenses: It helps cover salaries, rent, utility bills, and other operating costs. Maintain cash flow: It helps manage payment delays from customers. Buy inventory: It helps maintain sufficient stock to meet customer demand. Handle emergencies: You can use working capital to manage unexpected expenses. Support growth: It helps you expand operations and invest in new opportunities. What is the working capital formula? Working capital is a crucial financial metric representing the difference between a company’s assets and liabilities. The need of working capital is to measure a company’s short-term liquidity to meet its everyday business expenses. The formula for calculating working capital is straightforward: Working Capital = Current Assets − Current Liabilities Where, Current assets include cash, bank balance, inventory, accounts receivable, and other assets that can be converted into cash within one year. Current liabilities include accounts payable, short-term loans, outstanding bills, and other obligations due within one year. To understand the importance of working capital, let’s take this example. If a company has Rs. 5,00,000 in current assets and Rs. 3,00,000 in current liabilities, the working capital would be: Rs. 5,00,000 – Rs. 3,00,000 = Rs. 2,00,000 A positive working capital indicates that a company can cover its short-term liabilities with its short-term assets, reflecting good financial health and operational efficiency. Conversely, a negative working capital suggests potential liquidity problems, indicating that the company may struggle to meet its day-to-day and short-term expenses. The working capital formula also serves as the foundation of working capital management. If you calculate and monitor working capital regularly, you can identify cash flow gaps, manage inventory efficiently, collect receivables on time, and control short-term liabilities. This helps avoid financial stress. It also helps ensure smooth day-to-day operations and maintain adequate liquidity. Proper working capital management ensures a company maintains adequate cash flow to meet its operational needs and financial commitments. It involves optimizing current assets and liabilities to ensure smooth business operations without unnecessary financial strain. Also Read – Types of Working Capital What are the components of working capital? Now that the working capital’s definition is clear, it is vital to understand its components. The key components of working capital include current assets and current liabilities. Together, they help measure a business’s ability to meet its short-term financial obligations. Here’s a brief description of each component. 1. Current assets (Inflows) These are resources that can be converted to cash or used within one year. Cash and cash equivalents: This includes cash on hand, bank balances, and short-term investments readily available for daily business expenses. Accounts receivable: It includes money that customers owe your business for goods or services sold on credit. Inventory: It covers raw materials, work in progress, and finished goods that are held for production or sale. Prepaid expenses: It includes payments made in advance for future expenses, such as rent, insurance, or software subscriptions. 2. Current liabilities (Outflows) These include short-term debts and obligations that must be paid within one year. Accounts payable: It is the money your business owes to suppliers or vendors for purchases made on credit. Short-term debt: It includes loans, overdrafts, or other borrowings due for repayment within one year. Accrued expenses: These are the expenses that have been incurred but are yet to be paid, such as taxes, salaries, or utility bills. Also Read – Key factors determining working capital requirements What are the types of working capital in India? Working capital is broadly classified based on its financial concept and the period for which it is needed. This classification helps businesses understand their funding requirements. 1. By value and liquidity This classification divides working capital based on asset value and how quickly you can convert it into cash. It helps assess a business’s ability to meet its short-term financial obligations. Gross working capital: The total value of all current assets, such as cash, inventory, and accounts receivable. Net Working Capital (NWC): The difference between current assets and current liabilities. It shows a company’s ability to meet short-term obligations. Negative working capital: It occurs when current liabilities exceed current assets, which may lead to cash flow challenges. 2. By time and need This classification divides working capital based on how long funds are required and the nature of the business need. It helps businesses plan funds for regular operations as well as changing or seasonal requirements. Permanent (fixed) working capital: The minimum amount of working capital required to run daily business operations throughout the year. Temporary (variable) working capital: The additional working capital needed during seasonal demand, business expansion, or unexpected expenses. Seasonal working capital: It refers to the extra funds a business needs during busy seasons when sales, production, or operating expenses increase temporarily. What are the advantages of working capital? To understand the significance of working capital, you must understand its advantages. Liquidity: If you have adequate working capital, it ensures your business can meet short-term financial obligations. It also ensures you can maintain healthy cash flow and continue daily operations without facing cash shortages. Operational efficiency: Proper working capital helps you pay suppliers, employees, and other expenses on time. It ensures smooth operations and avoids disruptions in business activities. Flexibility: Sufficient working capital enables your business to manage unexpected expenses and respond to market changes. It also helps you seize growth opportunities without financial strain. Creditworthiness: If you have positive working capital, it indicates good financial health. It improves your chances of securing loans and better credit terms. It helps you gain the trust of lenders and suppliers. Cost management: Healthy working capital reduces the need for costly short-term borrowing. It helps your business save on interest costs and manage finances more efficiently. What are the limitations of working capital? While the advantages help you understand the importance of working capital, there are also certain limitations that you need to understand. Idle assets: Excess working capital may leave cash or inventory unused. This can reduce returns and limit the business’s ability to use resources more productively. Opportunity cost: If there’s money tied up in working capital, it cannot be invested in expansion, technology, or other opportunities that could generate higher returns. Seasonal variations: Working capital needs may increase or decrease during different seasons. This can make it challenging to manage cash flow throughout the year. Dependency on external factors: Economic slowdowns, inflation, supply chain disruptions, or changing customer demand can affect working capital requirements and overall business operations. Static snapshot vs. fluid reality: Working capital indicates the financial position at a specific time. This means that it may not reflect daily changes. Often, it does not consider day-to-day cash flows, sales, or expenses. Ignores asset quality: A high working capital figure may look positive, but some assets may be difficult to sell or collect, reducing their actual value. Risk of overspending: Having excess working capital may encourage businesses to spend more than necessary, leading to inefficient use of funds and lower returns. Mixing short-term and long-term funds: Working capital figures may not clearly show whether short-term assets are being financed through suitable short-term or long-term sources. Does not reflect long-term health: Working capital mainly focuses on short-term finances. It does not fully show profitability, debt levels, growth potential, or the business’s long-term financial strength. Working capital cycle: How does it impact Indian businesses? The working capital cycle is the time required by a business to transform its current net liabilities and assets into cash. The cycle basically tracks how long cash is tied up in inventory and as customer payments, and how quickly they can turn it back into available funds. The working capital cycle has a direct relationship with liquidity. This means that the shorter a working capital cycle is, the faster it will be for a business to access blocked cash. Businesses typically aim to keep the working capital cycle short. It’s because the longer the money remains blocked, the more difficult it will be for you to take advantage of opportunities or cover other necessary costs. For Indian businesses: A shorter working capital cycle means faster cash recovery, helping businesses pay salaries, vendors, and bills on time. Such businesses can reinvest faster and scale without constant funding stress. Long cycles lock money in inventory and customer dues, increasing dependence on loans and overdrafts. Delayed payments and excess inventory increase bad-debt risk and operational instability. What is the importance of working capital management strategies for Indian SMEs? Working capital management is the process of managing a company’s current assets and current liabilities to maintain healthy cash flow and ensure smooth day-to-day business operations. Here are some reasons why working capital management matters: Prevents insolvency: Proper working capital management helps businesses meet short-term financial obligations and reduces the risk of running out of cash. Ensures uninterrupted operations: It ensures timely payments to employees, suppliers, and service providers, allowing business operations to continue without disruptions. Improves creditworthiness: Maintaining healthy working capital strengthens your financial position, making it easier to obtain loans and negotiate better credit terms. Helps navigate market volatility: Adequate working capital helps businesses handle unexpected expenses, seasonal demand, and economic uncertainty with greater confidence. The core strategies Indian SMEs can adopt for working capital management are: 1. Accelerate accounts receivable The strategy focuses on collecting customer payments on time. It helps to improve cash flow and reduce outstanding dues. 2. Optimize inventory levels SMEs must focus on maintaining sufficient inventory to meet demand without locking up excess funds in unsold stock. 3. Extend accounts payable Businesses must negotiate longer payment terms with suppliers while ensuring payments are made on time. 4. Utilize supply chain financing The strategy focuses on using financing solutions to improve cash flow and pay suppliers without affecting daily operations. 5. Know your working capital position It is advisable to regularly track cash, inventory, receivables, and payables. It helps you understand how much working capital your SME needs. As a result, you can avoid cash shortages and unnecessary borrowing. 6. Manage inventory and customer payments better You must maintain the right inventory levels and follow up on outstanding customer payments. Faster collections and efficient inventory management can improve cash flow and reduce funding needs. 7. Build strong supplier relationships It is essential to pay suppliers on time and have clear communication with them. When you have strong supplier relationships, you can negotiate better credit periods, flexible payment terms, and obtain reliable supplies. How are digital payments changing working capital needs? With the emergence of payment methods like UPI, digital wallets, and online payment gateways, money now reaches businesses faster, and digital payments have become the norm. Using these digital payment methods, businesses can now receive due payments instantly, reducing the wait time for funds. Instant settlements mean less money is locked up, freeing up working capital previously tied up in receivables. This also leads to fewer liquidity gaps, enabling quicker supplier payments, inventory restocking, and reduced reliance on short-term loans. The different ways in which digital payments are changing working capital needs include: 1. Accelerated cash conversion cycle Digital payments help businesses receive customer payments faster. This reduces the time between selling goods and receiving cash. It improves liquidity and reduces short-term funding needs. 2. Enhanced cash flow visibility & automation With digital payment systems, you have real-time transaction records and cash flow information. Consequently, SMEs can track payments, reconcile accounts, and manage working capital more efficiently. 3. Lower operational costs & improved margins Digital payments can reduce paperwork, manual reconciliation, and cash-handling costs. This saves time and resources. It helps businesses improve operational efficiency and margins. 4. Unlocking formal credit & working capital financing Through digital payment systems, SMEs have a clearer financial record. Lenders can use this data to assess business activity, making formal credit and working capital financing easier to access. What are working capital challenges? Businesses often face several challenges in managing working capital effectively. The common issues include: External disruptions: Economic downturns, inflation, supply chain issues, or changing customer demand can affect cash flow and increase working capital needs. Poor cash flow management: If customer payments are delayed and there are uncontrolled expenses, it may lead to cash shortages. Substandard lender practices: Working capital financing can become more expensive due to high interest rates or restrictive loan terms. Inaccurate forecasting: Poor financial planning can result in either excess or insufficient working capital. Ineffective inventory management: If there is overstocking or stock shortages, it can increase costs and disrupt business operations. How does working capital affect business loans? Working capital affects business loans in various ways. These include: Loan eligibility: Healthy working capital shows lenders that your business can manage short-term expenses and repay loans on time. Loan amount: Your chances of getting a higher loan amount are improved if you have a strong cash flow and working capital. Interest rates: Better financial health can help you access more favorable borrowing terms. Repayment ability: Adequate working capital ensures you can manage EMIs without disrupting daily operations. Creditworthiness: Consistent working capital management builds lender confidence and strengthens your overall credit profile. What are the common mistakes in working capital management? Some of the common mistakes you can make and must avoid during working capital management are: Poor cash flow planning: Not forecasting cash needs can lead to sudden shortages and payment delays. Excess inventory: Holding too much stock locks money that could be used elsewhere. Delayed collections: Allowing customers to delay payments can weaken cash flow. Ignoring supplier terms: Poorly managed supplier payments may affect business relationships. Over-borrowing: Taking more short-term debt than needed can increase interest costs and repayment pressure. Conclusion Working capital is essential for keeping your business running smoothly and meeting everyday financial needs. It helps you pay expenses on time, maintain healthy cash flow, and prepare for unexpected situations. However, having working capital alone is not enough. Effective working capital management ensures your funds are used wisely by balancing current assets and liabilities. If you understand the need for working capital and manage it efficiently, you can improve financial stability, support business growth, and build a stronger foundation for long-term success. The working capital life cycle refers to the time it takes for a company to convert its current assets and liabilities into cash through regular business operations. What are the 4 types of working capital? The four types of working capital are gross working capital, net working capital, permanent working capital, and variable working capital. Is working capital a profit? No, working capital is not a profit. It represents the difference between current assets and current liabilities, indicating the business’s liquidity to manage its short-term expenses. What is working capital turnover? Working capital turnover measures how efficiently a company uses its working capital to generate sales. It is calculated as net sales divided by average working capital. Can a business have too much working capital? Excess working capital can signal resource inefficiency. Idle cash may reflect missed investment opportunities, while holding too much inventory can tie up funds that could be used for more productive ventures. What should be excluded from working capital? Exclude items like property, equipment, long-term loans, shares, and patents. These are not short-term assets or liabilities and don’t directly affect a business’s day-to-day cash flow. How does working capital affect business loan approvals in India? Lenders assess working capital to evaluate cash flow management and the repayment capacity of borrowers. Positive working capital improves loan approval chances, while a negative one often leads to rejection or higher interest rates. What is the ideal working capital ratio for Indian startups? An ideal working capital ratio for Indian startups is generally between 1.2-2.0. Below 1.2 indicates potential cash flow problems and above 2.0 suggests poor asset utilization with too much idle cash. Can working capital be negative for growing Indian businesses? Yes, working capital can be negative for growing Indian businesses if they don’t have enough cash to meet their short-term requirements, leading cash flow issues. How do seasonal businesses manage working capital fluctuations? Seasonal businesses manage working capital fluctuations by forecasting demand accurately, building cash reserves during peak seasons, adjusting inventory levels based on sales cycles, and negotiating flexible payment terms with suppliers. What role does working capital play in inventory management? The need of working capital is to buy and store inventory. Adequate working capital ensures you can keep products in stock to sell, while avoiding buying too much that locks up cash you need for other business expenses. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund As India is moving towards self-reliance by promoting a startup ecosystem, more and more entrepreneurs are seeking funds to realise their dreams. Startup ventures need funding to start the business and turn it into a profitable enterprise. There could be multiple reasons why startup loans are required, depending upon the nature and purpose of the business. Personal loans for business startups are one of the most feasible options for entrepreneurs to get much-needed capital without having to give up ownership or control of their venture. Startup loans are also offered to businesses with very limited or no credit history at all. What is a Startup Business Loan? A startup business loan is credit specifically designed to help new ventures fund their launch and early operations. Unlike traditional business loans that assume years of financial history, startup loans are structured for businesses with limited revenue records, often relying on the founder’s credit profile and a solid business plan . These loans cover working capital, equipment, marketing, hiring, and other early-stage costs, allowing entrepreneurs to build their businesses without giving up equity. Advantages and disadvantages of Startup Business Loans A startup business loan can give a new venture the capital it needs without giving up equity, but it also brings obligations worth weighing. Understanding both sides first helps you decide whether this route fits your stage and cash flow. Advantages Retain full ownership: A loan is debt, not equity, so you keep complete control of your business and its future profits. No investor gets a share or a say in your decisions. Build business credit: Repaying a loan on time strengthens your business credit profile, which can help you secure larger funding on better terms later. Potential tax deductions: The interest paid on a business loan is generally treated as a deductible business expense, which can lower your taxable profit. Confirm the current rules with your tax advisor. Fast access to capital: Compared with raising equity, a loan can be arranged quickly, giving you funds to act on time-sensitive needs like inventory, equipment, or a new order. Disadvantages Strict eligibility requirements: Lenders assess your credit score , business plan, and financials before approving. A new venture with limited history may find it harder to qualify. High interest rates and fees: Startups carry more risk, loans can come with higher interest rates and added charges than established businesses receive. Read the full cost before signing. Cash flow strain: Fixed monthly repayments begin whether or not the business is profitable yet, which can pressure cash flow in the early months. Personal liability risk: Many startup loans need a personal guarantee, so your personal assets may be at risk if the business cannot repay. Eligibility Criteria for Startup Business Loan A startup must meet certain eligibility requirements to avail of a small loan to start a business. A startup loan for a new business can be availed of either by an individual or a group of individuals. Some common eligibility requirements and documentation required for a startup loan include – Age Criteria: The minimum age for applicants is 21 years, and the maximum age limit is 65 years. Citizenship: The applicant should be a citizen of India with a valid PAN. Valid Identity Proof: The applicant needs to provide proof of identity in the form of either an Aadhaar card or a valid driving licence or a passport. Bank Statements: The applicant has to submit bank statements for the last six months. Business Ownership Documents and Business Plan: The applicant also needs to provide proof of ownership of the business along with a business plan. These requirements help the lender verify the credibility of applicants seeking startup loans. Additionally, the credit score or credit standing of the entrepreneur is linked to the startup venture. Documents Required for a Startup Business Loan Documentation is what separates a smooth application from a stalled one. Prepare these before you start: KYC: Aadhaar and PAN for the founder or all partners Business registration: Certificate of incorporation, LLP registration, GST certificate, or Udyam registration Business plan: Purpose of the loan, projected revenues, cost breakdown, and repayment plan Bank statements: Last 6 months of the primary business account, or personal account if the business is new Income proof: ITR of the founder for the last 1 to 2 years Address proof: For business premises and applicant Steps for Getting a Startup Loan for New Business Startup loans are a form of personal loans for business purposes. However, entrepreneurs are expected to fulfil certain requirements before applying for a startup loan. Business plan : First of all, entrepreneurs need to prepare a business plan as it helps outline the purpose of the business and its plan. The business plan provides an overview of the business idea, its objective, potential returns, and the expected growth trajectory of the enterprise. Lending to a completely new business involves significant risks. In the absence of detailed financial records, lenders rely on the business plan to judge the repaying capacity of a business. This document gives the lender an idea of the future cash flows of a business. Thus, banks and financial institutions need a business plan to lend even a small loan to start a business as it helps them better understand the viability and sustainability of a startup venture. Costs and finances: Next, entrepreneurs should review the cost of setting up and running their startup and the finances available to them. This will help determine the amount of loan required from a startup loan for a new business. Personal credit scores and reports: Before submitting a startup business loan application, one needs to ensure that they have their credit scores and other necessary documents in place. As it is a personal loan for business, lenders require these documents to understand the repayment ability and to determine potential interest rates. Other necessary documents include personal tax returns and bank statements. Business licences, registrations, and legal documents: Entrepreneurs need a business licence, registrations, and other legal documents as lenders may ask for these documents. Apart from these documents, lenders may also require a startup’s bank statements and financial records. Evaluate various lenders: Once all the necessary documents are in place, one needs to evaluate and compare various lenders in terms of the interest rate and loan amount offered, and other loan conditions. Evaluating deals offered by multiple lenders will help in getting the best deal. Submit the loan application: After shortlisting the lender, entrepreneurs should review their startup loan application process and compile the necessary paperwork. Nowadays, most lenders accept online loan applications. Once the application and documentation are completed, the applicant will be contacted by a representative of the lender. Also,read – 10 Small Business Ideas Under Rs. 50,000 Interest Rates and Charges Startup loans are offered at interest rates that vary between 16% and 27% per annum. The rate of interest depends upon various factors, including – CIBIL Score: ACIBIL score is an important factor in determining startup loan interest rates. A healthy CIBIL score reflects the strong financial capability of a borrower, and loans to such applicants are considered a low-risk option for the lender. Thus, a healthy CIBIL score will help you get a startup loan at a comparatively lower interest rate. Company prospects: In the case of startups, very little credit history is available, due to which the lender has to judge the borrower’s repayment capacity based on the prospects of the company. If the company has strong prospects, then a lower rate of interest could be charged. Collateral: In case an asset is offered as collateral, a lower interest rate could be charged as it reduces the risk for the lender.Apart from the rate of interest, you need to pay a one-time charge called a processing fee. It covers the cost of processing the documents and other administrative costs associated with the loan approval process. This fee is non-refundable and is calculated as a percentage of the loan amount. Conclusion Startup loans can support you in realising your entrepreneurial aspirations. They offer numerous advantages over other sources of finance, especially for a startup. Getting a startup business loan from Tata Capital is easy and convenient. Get in touch for more details. Tata Capital offers unsecured business loans with easy eligibility criteria, attractive interest rates, flexible tenures, minimum documentation, quick approvals, and fast disbursals. What is the amount of startup loan? You can get a startup loan of up to Rs 90 Lakhs with Tata Capital. What’s more, you can get one without pledging collateral, at an attractive interest rate and with a flexible loan tenure that fits your financial plans. Which loan is best to start a business? The best loan to start a business is a business loan from Tata Capital. Specially designed to meet the needs of a commercial establishment, this loan helps you finance a variety of business needs, from day-to-day expenses to business expansion. Is it possible to secure a business loan without any revenue? Securing a business loan without revenue can be difficult because revenue is crucial to judging a business's creditworthiness and loan repayment capabilities. However, with the country's growing startup culture, startups can find select investors who might extend finance. Can I get a startup business loan without any revenue proof? It is difficult but not impossible. Lenders assess the founder's credit profile, business plan, and personal financials in such cases. Government schemes like MUDRA and Stand-Up India are more accommodating for zero-revenue startups. What are the chances of loan approval for a newly registered startup? Approval depends on the founder's CIBIL score, quality of the business plan, and the loan amount requested. A strong personal credit profile and a realistic ask improve approval odds significantly. How does a lender evaluate a startup's business plan for a loan? Lenders look at market size, revenue model, projected cash flows, and how the loan amount will be deployed. A clear repayment plan tied to specific revenue milestones works better than optimistic top-line projections. Are there specific loan options available for first-time entrepreneurs? MUDRA (Shishu, Kishor, Tarun), Stand-Up India for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs, and NBFC-driven unsecured business loans like Tata Capital's are designed for first-time founders. Can I apply for a startup loan with a low or no CIBIL score? With no CIBIL score (first-time borrower), lenders may consider the application based on the business plan and other financials. With a low score, options narrow. Improving the score before applying opens better rates and higher amounts. What documents are mandatory for an unsecured startup business loan? KYC (Aadhaar, PAN), business registration proof, ITR for 1-2 years, bank statements for 6 months, business plan, and address proof. Some lenders may additionally ask for GST returns or a promoter's personal ITR. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund If a person owns shares in the open market, they can apply for a loan against shares. There are several benefits attached to availing of such loans . The article describes what is loan against shares’ meaning, how the loans against shares process works, and how it benefits people by allowing them to borrow conveniently. Loan Against Shares: Meaning & Overview The loans against shares process are loans taken against financial assets like shares, mutual funds or life insurance policies . The financial assets act as collateral or surety to the bank. A loan against shares helps people use their financial assets more efficiently. It prevents people from hastily selling their shares. The limit of loan they can pledge on their shares is based on the number of shares they own and the bank where they are availing the loan. Loan Against Shares Process: Step-by-Step Guide Market Shares are a vital financial asset. They are instrumental in times of unprecedented need. After they pledge their shares, the bank gives them a hybrid term loan facility, from which they can withdraw any money out of their total loan amount. The applicant will be liable to pay interest only on the amount they withdraw. The following example helps explain the loan against shares process better: Suppose an applicant receives a loan of Rs. 2 lakhs . The applicant only withdraws Rs. 1.5 lakhs with a repayment tenure of five months. As per the bank’s hybrid term loan policy, they will charge interest only on Rs. 1.5 lakhs (amount withdrawn) and not Rs. 2 lakhs. Besides, people can also pledge shares of their relatives, including their spouse, parents, and siblings, who are above the age of 18 years. But in this case, the relative has to play the part of being a co-applicant and should sign the hybrid term loan agreement. Benefits of Loan Against Shares Now that you know what is loan against shares’ meaning and how does loan against shares work, let’s move on to the benefits. The main benefits are as below: A loan against shares in India is a secure loan. The loan is not dependent on the borrower’s creditworthiness but on the security of the shares he has submitted. Loans against shares are given only to shares which are readily marketable and which are free from disabilities. Loans against shares have a lower interest rate than personal loans. Interest Rate is very important for any person pledging a loan. Interest rates vary for all kinds of loans. Secured loans have a lower interest rate compared to unsecured ones. The borrower can use the loan against shares for any purpose of their wish. The lenders will not ask about the meaning of the loan during the approval process. Hence, borrowers have complete freedom in the usage of their loans. You can smoothly switch pledge between the securities within your financial portfolio. It depends on the stock market assessment performed by the applicant. It allows them to enjoy the benefits of bonuses, rights and dividends, etc. Since the ownership of the financial products remains with the borrower, the idea of a loan proves to be lucrative for them. Other advantages of loan against shares in India include: The loan pledged on shares can be processed quickly. Loans against shares are determined based on the current market value of the shares. One can quickly evaluate these market values. People can extend the repayment of these loans. Fall within the age bracket of 18 to 70 years. Be a salaried or self-employed individual, or represent a partnership firm, proprietorship, trust, or public/private company. Hold approved securities in a valid Demat or mutual fund account. Ensure the securities are maintained with recognised depositories such as NSDL or CDSL, or authorised transfer agents like CAMS or KFIN. You also need to provide the following documents with the loan application if applying online: PAN card Aadhar card and the mobile number linked to it. If you’re applying offline, submit the following: PAN card Address and identity proof: Aadhaar Card / Passport / Driving Licence/ Voter ID Signature These are the documents that are generally required for loan against stocks in India. However, you may need to provide additional documents depending on which category of borrower you are. How is the Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio Calculated for LAS? LTV plays a major role in how does loan against shares work, as it determines the maximum loan amount you can borrow. The Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio for loan against stocks in India is calculated by dividing the loan amount by the current market value of the pledged securities, expressed as a percentage: LTV = (Loan Amount / Market Value of Shares) × 100. For example, if your shares are worth ₹10 lakhs and the lender offers ₹7.5 lakhs, the LTV is 75%. The LTV ratio protects lenders from market volatility while determining your maximum borrowing capacity for loan against stocks in India. Conclusion To summarize, loan against shares in India is a convenient way to secure funds for your requirements. With flexibility in swapping securities and another benefit such as zero foreclosure charges, you can reap many benefits. Moreover, the process of application is smooth and hassle-free. Tata Capital also provides an online application process where you can easily apply and get your loan. Looking for more information on the subject? A loan against stocks in India is a secured loan where you pledge your equity shares as collateral to borrow funds. Shares remain in your demat account but are marked as pledged until full repayment. What are the risks involved in availing a loan against shares? The main risks include forced liquidation of shares upon default, margin calls if share prices drop, loss of dividend rights during pledge, market volatility affecting collateral value, and potential credit score damage from non-repayment. What is the typical loan-to-value ratio for loan against shares? The typical loan-to-value (LTV) ratio for loan against shares in India ranges from 50% to 60% of the share's market value, varying based on stock volatility, liquidity, company fundamentals, and lender's risk assessment policies. What documents are required for a loan against shares application? Documents required include PAN card, identity and address proof like Aadhaar Card / Passport / Driving Licence/ Voter ID, and your signature. Are there alternatives to loans against shares for getting urgent funds? Yes, alternatives include personal loans, credit cards, gold loans, loan against property, loan against bonds, overdraft facilities, and emergency funds from provident funds or insurance policies. What happens if I default on my loan against shares? If you default on your loan against stocks in India, the lender will sell your pledged shares to recover dues. You lose your investment permanently, face credit score damage or legal action. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Availing loans against properties, be the property is residential or commercial, is one of the oldest forms of credit. When a person can’t get a personal loan or business loan , keeping his existing property can get him credit from a financial institute. As the loan is availed against property, there are certain tax benefits that one can enjoy for the same. This article will give insight into the tax benefits on loans against property that are available in India and how one can make use of the same. What is a Loan Against Property? A loan against property is a secured loan where one keeps the property as collateral security for availing a loan. The value of the loan is derived as per the current valuation of the property. A certain percentage, say, for instance, 70% or 80% of the value of the property is disbursed as a loan amount to the applicant. The borrower can get a loan against property income tax benefits as well, unlike other types of loans. Many people confuse mortgage loan income tax benefits with tax benefits for home entity loans. These two are not the same. The two loans are only different. A home entity loan is a home loan that one avails for building a home. At the same time, tax benefits on loans against property can be availed against loans taken by pledging the property which is already existing. Tax Benefits under Income Tax Act for Loan Against Property Tax provision Income tax implication on a Loan Against Property Tax Exemptions Under Section 24(B) Tax deduction of up to Rs. 2 lakhs on the interest paid Tax Exemptions Under Section 37(1) Rebate on the processing fee, documentation fee, and interest if the loan is used to meet business expenses – Section 24(B) Under this section, salaried borrowers can enjoy tax exemptions of up to Rs. 2 lakhs if they use the loan against property to buy a new residential property. To avail of this tax benefit, the loan must have been taken for the purpose of purchase, construction, or repair of a residential property. If you use the loan to purchase or construct a property, you can claim the deduction if the acquisition or construction is completed within 5 years of taking the loan. – Section 37(1) Under Section 37(1), you can claim tax benefits if you’ve taken the loan to meet business expenses. Borrowers can claim rebates on the processing fee, documentation fee, and even the interest paid on the loan amount. These amounts can be claimed as business expenses during the time of filing the claim. However, it’s important that the loan amount is exclusively used for the purpose of the business. Eligibility criteria for availing tax benefits on Loan Against Property To understand tax benefits on loan against property and determine how to save tax on loan against property , it is important to review the eligibility conditions that must be met, which include: The loan must be availed from a recognised financial institution or lender operating in India Loan against property tax exemption is available only on the interest paid, not on the principal repayment The borrowed amount should be used for eligible purposes such as business expansion, property purchase, construction, or renovation Interest paid on a loan used for business or professional purposes can be claimed as a deductible expense For personal use, interest deduction is allowed under Section 24(b) only if the funds are used for acquiring or improving a residential property The borrower must be the legal owner or co-owner of the mortgaged property Proper loan statements and proof of end-use must be maintained to claim tax benefits The loan must be actively serviced during the relevant financial year Documentation required to claim tax exemptions on Loan Against Property To successfully claim tax benefits on loan against property and understand how to save tax on loan against property , keeping the correct documents in place is essential, which include: Loan sanction letter issued by the lender Loan account statement showing interest paid during the financial year Interest certificate from the lender to support loan against property tax exemption claims Proof of end-use of funds, such as bills, invoices, or business expense records Ownership documents of the mortgaged property, including sale deed or title deed Construction, renovation, or property purchase receipts, if applicable Business financial statements when claiming interest as a deductible expense Income tax returns and computation statements reflecting the loan against property tax exemption claim Also, read – Step By Step Loan Against Property Process Section 37(1) vs Section 24(b): Detailed comparison for taxpayers Depending on whether a loan supports business activities or residential property ownership, interest deductions fall under different sections, compared as follows: Basis of comparison Section 37(1) Section 24(b) Applicable to Business owners and professionals Individual taxpayers owning house property Purpose of loan Loan used for business or professional activities Loan used to acquire, construct, repair, or renovate residential property Nature of deduction Business expense deduction Income from house property deduction Eligible amount Entire interest amount, if wholly for business use Up to ₹2 lakh for self-occupied property Principal deduction Not applicable Not applicable under this section Proof required Business expense records and loan statements Interest certificate and property ownership proof Income head Profits and Gains of Business or Profession Income from House Property Suitability Ideal for business-funded loan against property Suitable for personal residential property loans Also, read – Home loan vs loan against property: What’s the difference? Situations where Loan Against Property offers no tax exemption While a loan against property comes with flexible usage, not all uses qualify for tax exemptions. Here are some situations that don’t qualify for tax exemptions: -Loan used for non-housing purposes If you use a loan against property for purposes other than purchasing, constructing, or repairing a residential property, the interest paid does not qualify for tax deductions under the Income Tax Act. The only exception is using the funds for business purposes, for which you can claim rebates by proving the funds were used to meet business expenses. -Non-qualifying expenses Although you can use the loan against property funds to meet various financial needs, expenses related to education, marriage, travel, or medical bills do not qualify for tax benefits. Therefore, it’s important to carefully understand the tax benefits and implications to select the best strategy for your situation and make informed decisions. Mistakes to avoid when claiming tax benefits on Loan Against Property While claiming tax benefits on loan against property can be an effective way to reduce liability and understand how to save tax on loan against property , certain common errors may lead to rejection of claims, making it important to avoid the following mistakes: Claiming principal repayment as a deduction, even though only interest qualifies for loan against property tax exemption Failing to maintain proper loan statements and interest certificates from the lender Using loan funds for ineligible purposes while still claiming tax deductions Claiming deductions under the incorrect section of the Income Tax Act Not retaining proof of end-use, especially for business-related claims Assuming unlimited deductions for personal use without checking applicable caps Claiming tax benefits without being the legal owner or co-owner of the property Missing or delaying loan repayments during the relevant financial year Also, read – Can I get a 100% Loan Against Property? Summary: Key tax and financial benefits of Loan Against Property While an income tax rebate on a loan against property is one of the most important benefits of a loan against property, there are many other benefits that one can consider. -Large sanction: As a loan against property is a secured loan, the amount one can avail as a loan is quite large as around 70% to 75% of the property value can be sanctioned as a loan. So, if someone is looking for a loan for business growth or building a new residential property and is short of cash, then applying for a loan against property will help them get a fast loan along with income tax benefits for a loan against property. -Lower interest rate: Since the borrower keeps property as collateral, the risk of the lender reduces if the borrower defaults on repaying the loan. This is why the interest rate is also lower for loans against property. So, one can not only enjoy tax benefits for loans against property. So, a loan against property can be used as a two-way sword that helps in saving interest as well as providing tax benefits. The borrower can save a lot compared to other types of loans where large amounts are sanctioned. -Longer repayment tenure: Another benefit of availing of a loan against property is the longer repayment tenure. These loans can be paid over many years as per the borrower’s preference. Usually, no personal loans or business loans have much longer tenure. Since it is a secured loan, the tenure can be decided at per convenience of the borrower and stretched over many years. Also, read – Why NBFCs are the Best Choice for Loan Against Property? Conclusion So, a loan against property can be used for tax savings as there are different tax rebates on loans against property. That said, the borrower must consider the use of the funds as that would determine his eligiblity for a loan against property for availing of the tax benefits. No, the loan amount received from a loan against property is not considered taxable income. It is a secured loan and is not subject to income tax. However, if you generate any income using the loan amount (such as investment returns), it might be taxable. Does a loan against property come under 80C? No, a loan against property does not come under 80C. Section 80C provides tax deductions for principal repayment of a home loan, life insurance premiums, and other specified investments. How much interest is paid on a loan against property? The interest rate on a loan against property varies depending on the lender, loan amount, tenure, and your credit profile. Generally, interest rates for loans against property range between 8% and 15% per annum. How much ITR is required for a loan against property? Most lenders require borrowers to submit their ITRs for the past 2-3 years to process a loan against property application. This helps the lender assess the borrower’s income stability and repayment capacity. Can a loan against property be converted to a home loan? No, it is not possible to convert a loan against property to a home loan. However, you can close the existing loan and take a new home loan if you wish to buy or construct a house. Can salaried individuals claim tax benefits on a loan against property in India? No, it is not possible to convert a loan against property to a home loan. However, you can close the existing loan and take a new home loan if you wish to buy or construct a house. Can salaried individuals claim tax benefits on a loan against property in India? Yes, salaried individuals can claim tax benefits on loan against property if interest is used for eligible purposes, helping understand how to save tax on loan against property. Is the principal repayment on a loan against property eligible for income tax deduction? no, principal repayment is not deductible. loan against property tax exemption applies only to interest paid, subject to usage and applicable income tax provisions. What documents are necessary to claim tax benefits for loan against property under Section 24(b) or 37(1)? Loan statements, interest certificate, proof of end-use, property ownership documents, and business records are required to claim tax benefits on loan against property correctly. Is there a difference in tax exemption between using the loan for business vs. personal use? Yes, business use allows broader deductions under Section 37(1), while personal use has limits under Section 24(b). What are the most common reasons for rejection of a tax benefit claim on loan against property? Incorrect section claims, missing documents, ineligible fund usage, ownership issues, or claiming principal repayment often lead to rejection when learning how to save tax on loan against property. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Congratulations on receiving an acceptance letter from your dream university! Now, to finance your tuition fee, living costs, and other expenses, you can consider opting for education finance. It is a ray of hope for students who aspire to study in premier institutes and are looking to manage their educational expenses. Loans for education come with a pretty simple application process. But, first things first, you must write a loan application letter to the lender requesting them to sanction your loan. Read on to understand how to write an application for education loan. How to Write an Application for Education Loan After you have selected a lender, you must write a loan application letter to them explaining your academic and financial situation. Here’s what you should include in your letter. Recipient’s address : First, you must mention the Manager’s name you are writing the letter to, the name of the lending institution, branch details, and the branch address. Applicant address : Next, include your name and address. Date : Once you have mentioned the address details, write the date. This doubles up as the date of application when the lender approves your letter. Subject : After the date, write the subject line or the purpose of the letter. So, make sure it is to the point and conveys the intent of writing the letter. Salutation : Once you mention the email subject, address the authority directly in the salutation. Body : Now comes the meat of the application. This section must include all the details required by the lender to grant you a loan. So, introduce yourself, talk about the institute you have been accepted into and the degree you wish to pursue and mention why you need the loan. Make sure to include your academic records, entrance/foreign exam scorecard, acceptance letter, and other relevant documents to make a convincing case for why you deserve the opportunity. Lastly, assure the lender that you will complete your studies and fetch a good job and close the letter. Here’s a sample letter to make things clear for you. Also, read – Step-by-Step Guide to the Education Loan Procedure 2026 Format of Loan Application Letter for Education Loan (with Template) Before starting your loan application letter , it’s crucial to be aware of the correct format. Below, we list the proper format for your application letter for an education loan and include a template to follow. Your loan application letter must start by following the format below: Recipient’s Address Sender’s Address Date Subject Greeting or salutation Body Regards Here is a template to follow: To The Bank Manager XYZ Bank XYZ Branch Address, City From ABC Address, City Date: DD/MM/YYYY Subject Line: Application for an education loan for college Dear ma’am/sir, [Body of the letter] Thank you Regards, ABC Sample Loan Application Letter for Education Loan To The Bank Manager ABC Bank XYZ Branch Address City From Anita Address City Date: XX/X/20XX Subject: Application for the education loan Sir/Madam I am writing this letter to apply for a student loan to pursue higher education in English Literature. I recently completed my Bachelor’s in English Literature from the University of Delhi with a 9.7 CGPA. Besides, I scored 85% marks in the All India Senior School Certificate Examination (AISSCE) with a Science background. I applied to the University of Pennsylvania for a full-time Master’s degree in English and have been selected for the programme. The total hostel fee, cost of education accessories, tuition fee, and boarding expenses in the United States is approximately Rs. 20 lakhs. Due to my humble family background, I’m unable to afford the cost and require financial assistance. I request you to grant me a personal loan for higher education at this prestigious university. I will repay the loan amount on time. I have attached my academic records, credentials, acceptance letter and other relevant documents with the letter. I am looking forward to your response. Additionally, if an applicant has lower academic scores, they can still strengthen their application by demonstrating strong results on entrance exams, providing credible reasoning for their scores, providing collateral for the loan , and more. How Should I Address The Education Loan Application Letter? Address the loan letter to the bank manager or the appropriate official at the branch where you’re applying for the loan.
