With multi-year completion times, higher education can get expensive. This is especially true for high-demand professional courses like an MBA. Paying for a two, three or four-year degree out-of-pocket often becomes difficult. Several banks and financial institutions provide education loans to eligible students to help them complete their education without undue financial strain. If you’re a parent considering financing your child’s education via an education loan or a student, you must first ensure whether the opted lies on the list of courses eligible for education loans. Confused where to get started? Worry not. This article covers the nitty-gritty of courses eligible for education loans in India. Courses Eligible for Education Loan in India To avail of education finance, you must be well informed about student loan approved courses, loan amount, loan process , interest rates, security, services, processing fees, documentation, and few other details. To answer the question education loan available for which courses, here’s a list of eligible courses for education loan: Type of Course Name of course Undergraduate degree and diploma BA, BCom, BE, BEd, BSc, BBA, MBBS, B Tech, LLB. and others Postgraduate degree or diploma MA, M Com, MSc, M Res, LLM, MFA, M Ed, M Phil, MBA, MD, and others Doctoral courses PhD Certificate courses In Computers, Nursing, Teaching, job-oriented course, etc. Diploma In Engineering, Agriculture, Veterinary courses, any job-oriented course, etc. Degree/Diploma In Army, Navy or Air-Force training courses, Aeronautics or any other relevant Pilot Training courses Miscellaneous Other courses run by the State Skill Mission or National Skill Development Corporation Nowadays, owing to the increased popularity of short-term courses for soft skills, animation, English learning, catering, spoken English, data science, Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital marketing, event management etc., are also eligible for loans . However, it is advisable to check with the lender if they offer an education loan for short term courses. Benefits of Education Loans Besides providing you with affordable access to top-class education in premier institutes, education loans in India offer tons of perks. With Tata Capital , you can comfortably borrow a higher loan amount along with swift and hassle-free loan sanctions at minimal fast-track documentation. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Girl’s education is one of the major factors in the promotion of gender equality, economic growth, and social progress. Education not only gives young women the tools to achieve their goals, but it also has a significant impact on how future leaders get shaped. In an attempt to reduce the academic disparity, the Indian government has collaborated with non-profits and financial institutions to introduce a number of education loan programmes aimed at empowering female students. Understanding the diverse range of education loan options available is essential for building a more equitable future for women in India. So in this article we will explore different types of education loans for girl students available in India and their eligibility criteria. Advantages of Education Loans for Women: Lower Rates, Subsidies & Offers Understand the key advantages of education loan for girl students in India: Lower Interest Rates Many lenders offer a concessional interest rate on an education loan for women . This directly reduces the total repayment burden over the loan tenure. Interest Subsidy Schemes Under select government-backed schemes, education loans for girl students in India may qualify for interest subsidies during the study and moratorium period, easing financial pressure on families with limited income. Reduced Processing Charges Some banks and NBFCs waive or lower processing fees for education loans for girls , helping cut upfront costs at the time of loan sanction. Flexible Repayment Structure Extended moratorium periods and longer repayment tenures allow women borrowers to start repayment only after completing education and securing employment. Encourages Financial Independence An education loan for girl students enables women to invest in higher studies independently, supporting long-term career growth and financial confidence. Types of Education Loans for Girl Students in India The Indian government, in collaboration with non-profit organisations and financial institutions, provides a range of education loan schemes expressly intended to benefit female students. Here is a list of a few education loans for girls in India: 1. Pragati Scholarship Scheme The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) launched this scheme to empower female students pursuing technical education. It offers financial support to enable students to pursue further education in management, technology, and engineering-related sectors. Eligibility criteria: – Accessible to female students at AICTE-approved universities who are enrolled in their first year of diploma or degree programs, as well as those who are lateral entering in their second year. – Candidates must be citizens of India. – The family’s annual income shouldn’t be more than Rs. 8 lakh. For married candidates, the higher income of parents or in-laws will be taken into account. 2. Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Yojana This flagship initiative by the Government of India is focused on promoting the welfare of girl children across the country. The program’s objectives are to advance education, increase knowledge of girls’ rights, and enhance the effectiveness of welfare services for girls. Eligibility criteria: – Targeted at districts with low Child Sex Ratios (CSR). – All girl children born in these districts are eligible for benefits. – Parents and guardians of girls in these districts are encouraged to participate and avail themselves of the scheme’s benefits. 3. Corp Vidya Scheme This loan is provided by Corporation Bank, which helps women pay for their education at low interest rates and offers extra perks for studying overseas. Eligibility criteria: – Graduate and postgraduate degree programs, certificates, and authorised professional courses from approved Indian and international universities are eligible for loans. – Programs offered by prestigious institutions such as IIMs, IITs, and other government-approved universities qualify for financial support. – Research courses (PhD) and non-degree programs, including correspondence and certificate courses, are not eligible for loans under this scheme. 4. Vidya Lakshmi Loan This collaborative initiative by the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, and Indian Banks Association aims to support students financially, especially those from lower-income families. Eligibility criteria: – The applicant must be an Indian citizen. – The loan can be availed only once for either undergraduate (UG), postgraduate (PG), or integrated courses. – The candidate must be accepted into an accredited school, domestically or internationally. The institution should be authorised or recognised by a government agency. 5. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) A government-backed savings program called the SSY encourages parents to invest in their daughter’s future. It provides favourable tax advantages and interest rates. Eligibility criteria: – Up until the age of ten, a girl child’s parents or legal guardians can open an account on her behalf. – A family may open up to two accounts, one for each girl child. A third account is permitted in cases of twins or triplets. – A minimum deposit of Rs. 250 is required to open the account, and a maximum deposit of Rs. 1.5 lakh is permitted each financial year. 6. Cent Vidyarthi The Central Bank of India offers loans up to Rs. 10 lakh for education within the country and Rs. 20 lakh for education overseas. Low interest rates are maintained to guarantee student accessibility. Eligibility criteria: – The applicant must be an Indian citizen. – The student must have been accepted into a reputable university in India or overseas for a higher education programme. – Selection to this program must be gained through an entrance exam or merit-based selection process. 7. Vidhya Jyoti This education loan, by the Indian Overseas Bank, is open to all female students. It includes a flexible repayment duration and a loan limit of Rs. 30 lakh for studies in India and Rs. 40 lakh for education abroad. Eligibility criteria: – The applicant must be a Person of Indian Origin (PIO), an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI), or a Non-Resident Indian (NRI). – The student must have been accepted into a reputable university in India or overseas for a higher education programme. – Applicants are selected based on merit through an entrance exam or other merit-based system. Also, read – Step-by-Step Guide to the Education Loan Procedure 2026 Eligibility Criteria for Education Loan for Girl Students in India Nationality The applicant must be an Indian citizen to qualify for an education loan for girl students in India. Age Requirement Female students are generally eligible between 18 to 35 years, ensuring support during key higher-education years. Educational Qualification Completion of 10+2 or a recognised diploma is mandatory before applying for the loan. Course Eligibility The loan is available for graduation, postgraduate degrees, or PG diplomas in professional and recognised courses. Institute Recognition Admission must be secured in a listed, recognised, and accredited institution in India or abroad. From administering medication and monitoring patient vitals to assisting in surgeries and managing day-to-day patient needs, nurses do it all. And the first step towards this promising career is applying for a Bachelor’s of Science in Nursing. This four-year undergraduate course puts you on the track to a successful nursing career. What’s more, you can apply for an education loan for BSc nursing to finance your education conveniently and without financial burden. Here, we discuss everything you need to know about an education loan for BSc nursing, from the eligibility criteria to its application process. Why Take an Education Loan for BSc Nursing? While many institutions today offer scholarships and grants which can provide financial support, education loans for nursing students remain one of the best options for those looking to finance their education. Here’s why: 1. Convenient Financing for Education: An education loan for nursing students allows you to fund your course without jeopardising your financial stability. 2. Significant Loan Amount: You can get high loan amounts through education loans to help you cover all direct and indirect expenses of education. 3. Flexible Repayment Schedules: Education loans allow you to start repayment after completing your education . This allows you to concentrate on your studies without any financial burden. 4. Extensive Loan Coverage: An education loan for nursing students covers all facets of pursuing an educational course, not just the tuition fees. With this loan, you can meet living expenses such as the cost of food, groceries, local conveyance, rent, etc., and other expenses such as the cost of the laptop, books, laboratory fees, etc. Interest Rates and Loan Amounts Available for BSc Nursing If you’re exploring an education loan for BSc Nursing in India, Tata Capital offers competitive financing options to help cover tuition, accommodation, books and living costs. Loan Amounts: Tata Capital provides unsecured education loan for nursing up to ₹85 lakh and secured loans up to ₹2 crore, depending on your course fees and co-applicant’s financial profile. Interest Rates: Tata Capital offers competitive interest rates starting at 9.50%, which vary based on tenure, loan structure, and credit profile. Loan Tenure: You can choose repayment tenures up to 13 years, including a moratorium period of one year. With Tata Capital’s flexible loan options for nurses in India, pursuing BSc Nursing is financially feasible for applicants. Eligibility Criteria for Education Loan for BSc Nursing The eligibility criteria for an education loan for nursing students can differ with the lender. Here are some general criteria you should meet for a successful application: You should have completed 10+2/diploma You should be between the ages of 18 and 35 years You should require the loan to pursue education from a listed, recognised and accredited institution in the country or abroad You must be able to provide a pre-admission sanction document, scores on entrance tests such as GRE, GMAT, etc., 12 th /HSC results, or a document confirming your admission Your parents, siblings, spouse, grandparents, parents-in-law or maternal/paternal uncle must be a co-borrower Be sure to check your chosen lender’s eligibility criteria thoroughly before applying. Tata Capital offers education loans for nursing students with easy eligibility criteria. Documents Required for Education Loan for BSc Nursing While the documents required for a successful education loan application vary with lenders, here are some of the documents you might have to submit: Proof of Identity: PAN Card, Passport Academic Documents: The lender might require your 10th mark sheet, 12th mark sheet, available semester mark sheet/transcript, degree, exam scores (GRE, IELTS, TOEFL, GMAT, other) Financial Documents: The lender might require salary slips for the past three months, Form 16 of the previous two years, ITRs of the last three years, business proof, P&L accounts, balance sheet, bank statements for the last six months. Collateral vs. Non-Collateral Loans for Nursing Students For students, understanding the difference between collateral and non-collateral funding is key when choosing an education loan for BSc Nursing. Non-Collateral Loans Do not require property or asset security Suitable for students applying for a BSc nursing education loan without access to collateral Loan amounts are limited and depend on academic profile and co-applicant income Processing is usually faster, but interest rates may be slightly higher Collateral Loans Require security such as residential property, fixed deposits, or other acceptable assets Allows for higher loan amounts, useful when total course costs are higher Interest rates are generally lower compared to unsecured options Longer repayment tenures may be available Preferred when exploring larger loan options for nurses in India Both types are valid loan options for nurses in India, and the choice often depends on financial background, loan amount needed and long-term repayment plans. Tata Capital offers unsecured loans of up to ₹85 lakh and secured loans up to ₹2 crore. Top Banks and NBFCs Offering Education Loans for BSc Nursing in India Several banks and NBFCs in India offer tailored education loans for BSc Nursing, designed to cover tuition fees, accommodation, study materials, and other related expenses. These lenders provide both secured and unsecured options, flexible repayment tenures, and moratorium periods aligned with the course duration. Among leading NBFCs, Tata Capital offers competitive BSc nursing education loan solutions with high loan limits, transparent interest rates, and a streamlined application process. Its flexible structures make it a preferred choice for students seeking reliable loan options for nurses in India. Before applying, students should compare loan amounts, interest rates, collateral requirements, and repayment terms to choose an education loan for nursing that best supports their academic and financial goals. Application Process for BSc Nursing Education Loan Every lender will have their own application process. However, here are some general steps to follow: Offline Process Step 1: Visit your chosen lender’s nearest branch Step 2: Complete the process as per the direction of the executive Step 3: Once your application is verified, you will receive the loan amount Online Application Process Step 1: Navigate to your chosen lender’s official website Step 2: Fill the form online and upload all necessary documents Step 3: Once your application is verified, the loan amount will be sanctioned Tips to Improve Your BSc Nursing Loan Eligibility Strong Academic Record: Good marks and admission into a recognised nursing college show seriousness and can strengthen your application. Secure a Co-Applicant with Stable Income: A co-applicant (usually a parent or guardian) with a steady job or business enhances your profile and increases approval chances. Maintain a Healthy Credit Score: Lenders prefer applicants and co-applicants with good credit histories, which reflects repayment discipline. Provide Comprehensive Documentation: Submit clear admission letters, fee structure, identity proofs, income documents and bank statements to speed up verification. Prepare a Clear Loan Requirement Plan: Showing how the funds will be used (tuition, hostel fees, books) helps lenders assess risk and boosts your education loan for BSc nursing application. Conclusion: Secure Your Future with a BSc Nursing Education Loan Pursuing a Bachelor’s in Nursing can be an extremely gratifying and fulfilling career option. Equipping you with all the training you need to offer sound medical treatment, this four-year undergraduate course can help prepare you for a successful career in the medical field. However, it can put a strain on your finances as well. Fortunately, you can apply for an education loan with Tata Capital. Offering high loan amounts, attractive interest rates, pre-admission sanction, easy disbursal, and without any collateral, Tata Capital’s education loan helps you achieve your professional dreams without any financial burden. If so, it’s important to understand the concept of margin money. But, what is margin amount in education loan? The term “margin money” refers to the portion of the educational expenses that you, as the borrower, need to fund on your own. To illustrate what is margin money in education in a better way, let’s consider an example. Suppose the total cost of your education is Rs. 10,00,000 and the margin money requirement is 5%. In this case, you would be required to contribute Rs. 50,000 from your own funds, and the education loan would cover the remaining Rs. 9,50,000. It’s essential for students and their families to be aware of what is margin money in education loan and the requirements when applying for education loans. Margin money in education loan: Meaning & how it works Now that we have a basic knowledge on what is margin amount in education loan, let’s delve into its role in loan disbursement. Here’s how it typically works: Calculation of total cost: Before applying for an education loan, you need to determine the total cost of your educational program. This includes tuition fees, accommodation charges, books, and other related expenses. Determination of margin money: The lending institution specifies a margin money percentage that you must contribute from your own funds. This percentage can vary based on factors such as the loan amount and the institution’s policies. Loan amount calculation: The loan amount is calculated by subtracting the margin money from the total cost of education. Disbursement process: The education loan is disbursed based on the approved loan amount. The funds are either released directly to the educational institution or provided to you, depending on the terms of the loan. Use of margin money: The margin money contributed by you is typically used to cover initial expenses or as a security deposit, depending on the requirements of the educational institution. Repayment structure: The repayment structure of the education loan is based on the disbursed loan amount. You are required to repay the loan amount along with applicable interest over an agreed-upon repayment period. How to calculate margin in education loan: Formula & example After what is margin money in education loan, now let’s explore what is margin in education loan example and its calculation. The formula for calculating margin money is straightforward: Margin Money = Total Cost of Education × (Margin Money Percentage/100) Let’s go through an example to illustrate this calculation. Suppose the total cost of education is Rs. 3,00,000, and the lending institution requires a margin money contribution of 15%. Using the formula: Margin Money = Rs. 3,00,000 × (15/100) Margin Money = Rs. 3,00,000 × 0.15 Margin Money = Rs. 45,000 Here, what is margin in education loan example would be Rs. 45,000. You would need to provide this amount from your funds, while the education loan would cover the remaining Rs. 2,55,000 (Rs. 3,00,000 – Rs. 45,000) based on the margin money in education loan and total cost of education. Margin money policies by banks vs NBFCs: India comparison When comparing margin money in education loan requirements among different banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) , there are a few factors to consider: Loan amount vs. Margin money percentage: Evaluate how the margin money percentage influences the loan amount. Different institutions may have varying percentages. Total cost of education: Check if there are any restrictions on the types of expenses considered in the total cost of education. Flexibility and terms: Assess the flexibility offered by each institution in terms of margin money payment and any variations based on the course or program. Interest rates and repayment terms: Consider the overall terms of the education loan, including interest rates and repayment periods, in addition to the margin money requirement. Eligibility criteria: Understand any specific eligibility criteria associated with margin money, such as the applicant’s income, credit history, or collateral requirements. Margin money requirements: Public Sector Banks vs. Private Sector Banks The margin money policies of public sector banks (PSBs) and private sector banks differ based on their respective approaches, ownership structures, and government regulations. Here’s a general comparison: Public Sector Banks (PSBs): Government Influence: PSBs often have margin money policies influenced by government guidelines and regulatory frameworks. Flexible for Social Objectives: Some PSBs may have more flexibility in margin money requirements for courses that align with national priorities or social objectives. Government-Sponsored Schemes: PSBs may participate in government-sponsored education loan schemes with reduced or no margin money for economically disadvantaged students. Interest Rate Subsidies: In some cases, PSBs may offer interest rate subsidies or concessions to certain categories of students, impacting the overall financial burden. Private Sector Banks: Market-Driven Approach: Private sector banks often adopt a market-driven approach, setting margin money policies based on their assessment of risk and profitability. Varied Margin Requirements: Margin money requirements in private banks may vary widely based on the loan amount, course type, and the borrower’s creditworthiness. Focus on Risk Management: Private banks may emphasize risk management, adjusting margin money requirements to mitigate potential loan default risks. Customer-Centric Solutions: Some private banks may offer customized margin money solutions, considering the unique circumstances and financial capabilities of individual borrowers. Strategies for minimising margin money To minimise the margin money you need to contribute, consider implementing the following strategies: Scholarships and grants: Explore scholarships and grants that can help cover educational expenses and reduce the amount of margin money required. Part-time work: Consider taking up part-time work opportunities to earn extra income and contribute to your education expenses. Negotiate with lenders: Discuss flexible repayment plans with lenders that can help reduce the financial burden and margin money requirement. Cost-saving options to lower education loan margin Opt for cost-saving measures such as community college or online courses to reduce overall educational expenses. Conclusion In conclusion, understanding what is margin in education loan and how it influences education loans is essential to students and their families. By being aware of what is margin in education loan example and its requirements, you can plan your finances accordingly and ensure a smooth disbursement and repayment process. Remember to research different banks’ policies, consider government schemes , and explore strategies for minimizing the margin money required. Margin money is the portion of education costs you pay yourself, while the lender funds the rest. If you’re wondering what is margin money in education loan, it’s essentially your contribution toward total expenses, as defined under education loan margin in India. How is margin calculated in an education loan? Margin is calculated as a percentage of the total course cost. For clarity, what is margin in education loan example: if fees are ₹10 lakhs and margin is 10%, you contribute ₹1 lakh, and the loan covers ₹9 lakhs. Is margin required in all education loans in India? No. Margin money in education loan applies mainly to higher loan amounts or overseas studies. Under education loan margin in India, many government-backed schemes waive margin for smaller loans or specific categories like female students or SC/ST applicants. Can private banks or NBFCs offer 0% margin loans? Certain lenders may provide loans requiring minimal margin money in education loan, though conditions differ. It’s essential to understand education loan margin in India and how it influences eligibility, repayment, and your overall financial planning. Does margin money have to be paid upfront or in instalments? Usually, margin money is paid proportionately as fees are disbursed, not entirely upfront. Understanding what is margin money in education loan helps students plan cash flow, since contributions align with each semester’s expense schedule. Can scholarships/waivers replace margin money? Yes, approved scholarships, fee waivers, or grants can often be adjusted against margin money in education loan. Under education loan margin in India, lenders may accept documented funding sources as the student’s contribution, reducing out-of-pocket costs. Is margin money refunded after loan closure? No. Margin money is not refundable because it’s your share of the education cost, not a deposit. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Pursuing a Doctor of Philosophy or PhD is a significant step towards career advancement and gaining expert knowledge in your chosen field. However, the financial burden of a long-duration course like a PhD can be challenging. Many students opt for education loans for PhD programs to overcome this hurdle. This blog post is a handy guide to applying for an education loan for PhD students. Benefits of an Education Loan for PhD An education loan tailored for PhD programs offers several advantages that can help you achieve your academic goals without financial constraints. Here are some key benefits: Access to Quality Education: An education loan covers various expenses such as tuition fees, accommodation costs, research materials, and travel expenses. It ensures that finance is not a barrier to pursuing your higher education dreams. Independence in Financing: It also allows you to become financially self-reliant during your doctoral journey without exhausting your family’s savings or relying on scholarships/grants. Building a Credit Score: Your education loan will be your first debt obligation. Timely repayments build a good credit score, which is essential for future financial endeavours, such as buying a house or starting a business. Types of Student Loans for a Doctorate Degree Financial institutions generally offer two types of education loans specifically tailored for PhD programs based on collateral: Secured Loan: A secured education loan requires a borrower to pledge an asset as collateral, such as residential property or non-agricultural land. This type of loan generally offers lower interest rates due to the collateral provided. Unsecured Loan: Borrowers do not need to provide any collateral for an unsecured education loan. However, these loans usually have higher interest rates than secured loans. Education Loan for PhD Students: Eligibility Criteria Before applying for an education loan for a PhD program, you need to meet certain eligibility criteria. The primary borrower must: – Be an Indian citizen aged 18 years or older. – Have a confirmed admission offer from a recognized institution before the final loan disbursal. – Include a co-borrower who earns in India. If you have a co-borrower, the person must: – Be an Indian citizen, legal guardian, parent, sibling, or other blood relative. – Hold a bank account in India capable of signing cheques. – Be the primary debtor responsible for repayment. Documents Required to Apply for an Education Loan for PhD To complete your education loan application process smoothly, ensure you have the necessary documents ready. Below is a list of essential documents required for education loan . For the Borrower: 1. Academic Documents: Provide all relevant academic certificates and mark sheets. 2. Proof of Admission: Submit your admission offer letter from the respective institution. 3. Fee Structure: Include a detailed breakdown of tuition fees and other expenses. 4. Photo ID Proof: Attach a copy of your valid photo identification document (such as an Aadhaar card or passport). 5. Passport-sized Photographs: Provide two recent colour passport-sized photographs. 6. Residence Proof: Submit documents such as electricity bills or rental agreements as proof of your residence address. 7. Date of Birth Proof: Attach any valid document indicating your date of birth. 8. Signature Verification Document: Submit a document that verifies your signature, such as a copy of your PAN card or passport. For the Co-borrower: 1. Photo ID Proof: Attach a copy of the co-borrower’s valid photo identification document. 2. Passport-sized Photographs: Provide two recent colour passport-sized photographs of the co-borrower. 3. Residence Proof: Submit documents proving the co-borrower’s residence address. 4. Date of Birth Proof: Attach any valid document indicating the co-borrower’s date of birth. 5. Signature Verification Document: Submit a document that verifies the co-borrower’s signature. 6. It is advisable to consult with your lender to understand their specific document requirements before initiating the loan application process. Application Process to Get an Education Loan for PhD Students To apply for PhD student loans, follow these steps: 1. Fill out the student loan application form accurately, ensuring all required information is provided. 2. Attach all necessary documents for the student and co-borrower, including KYC documents. 3. Submit the completed form and supporting documents either online or by visiting the financier’s office. PhD Student Loan Repayment Method Repaying your education loan for a PhD can be done in two primary ways: – Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs): Most borrowers choose this popular repayment method, where fixed EMI amounts are paid each month. EMIs consist of both principal and interest components, helping you gradually repay the loan over time. – Interest Servicing During the Course: Some borrowers opt to pay simple or partial interest during the moratorium period when they are not required to make full EMI payments. However, it is important to note that interest continues to accrue during this period, increasing the overall repayment cost of student loans. Conclusion Opting for an education loan allows you to access quality education without financial constraints and build a strong credit score while pursuing your academic aspirations. Remember to choose the loan type that suits your needs and understand all terms and conditions before signing the agreement. What is the maximum loan amount available for a PhD education loan in India? Tata Capital offers unsecured PhD education loans up to around ₹85 lakh and secured loans up to about ₹2 crore, depending on your requirements and security provided. What documents are required for a PhD education loan in India? You must submit identity and address proofs, academic records, admission confirmation (such as offer letter), income proofs of co-applicant and recent photographs as part of the documentation. How are interest rates and repayment terms decided for PhD student loans? Interest rates are based on loan type (secured/unsecured), your and your co-applicant’s financial profile, chosen tenure and prevailing rate guidelines. Repayment terms, including tenure, are agreed at sanction. Is a co-applicant mandatory for a PhD education loan? Yes, a co-applicant (such as parent, spouse or sibling) is typically mandatory for eligibility and to strengthen repayment assurance. What is the moratorium period for PhD education loans in India? After your PhD course ends, you usually get a moratorium (repayment holiday) that covers course duration plus a period of about 6 months to 1 year before EMI repayment begins. boon! -Wordsworth In the above lines, the great poet William Wordsworth indirectly laments the loss of humanities and arts in the increasingly materialistic world of his time. Ever since the Industrial Revolution, people have realized the role of arts in shaping our lives over centuries. While the fields of science and commerce study material things, studying the arts means examining what it means to be human. If you often find yourself grappling with the same concerns, a bachelor of arts from a reputed university will give you a perfect opportunity to indulge your interests while building a stellar career. What’s more? You can even choose from many subjects (literature, history, philosophy, psychology, etc.) to major in. The biggest concern when enrolling for a multi-year education degree is consistent funding. Education loans can provide all the necessary financing for the entire duration of your education. Need help figuring out where to start with education loans ? Here’s a complete guide on education loan for bachelor of arts for you. What is a bachelor of arts? A bachelor of arts is a three-year undergraduate degree program in various subjects such as economics, literature, philosophy, social science, psychology, etc. Top universities that offer a bachelor of arts include Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), Delhi University (DU), Ashoka University, Presidency College and Indraprastha University (IPU). To be eligible for a bachelor of arts, you should have completed senior secondary studies (10+2) from a recognized board with more than 50 %. Additionally, you must also clear one of the following exams: 1. Common University Entrance Test (CUET): The CUET exam, held in May/June every year, is for studying in central universities like the JNU and Delhi University. Some private universities can also consider CUET scores for admission. 2. Indraprastha University Common Entrance Test (IPU CET): The Indraprastha University conducts IPU CET in April/May every year for entry into its bachelor of arts program. Cost of BA course in India A bachelor of arts in any subject will cost you Rs. 3000-10000 annually on average from public universities. The fees for a bachelor of arts from private universities like Ashoka University are higher and can vary from Rs. 60000 to Rs. 300000 annually. Career opportunities after BA in India With a bachelor of arts from a good university, you can expect to earn Rs. 4-7 LPA in government or private sectors. Some job profiles open to you after a bachelor of arts include: 1. Psychologist: With a BA in psychology, you can choose to be a psychologist and assist people with mental issues through counselling. A starting salary for a psychologist is around Rs. 4.2 LPA. 2. Teacher: A bachelor of arts also prepares you to be an excellent teacher who can effectively guide students in a particular subject. You will have various options as a teacher, from schools and colleges to coaching centres with attractive salaries. 3. Political consultant: Newspapers, online news outlets, and political think tanks always look for brilliant bachelor of arts graduates in political science. The starting salary for this job profile is Rs. 7.5 LPA. Eligibility criteria for education loan for BA students in India Applicants must fulfill the following conditions to secure an education loan for BA in India: Age limit: Typically 18–35 years. Admission proof: Confirmed admission in a recognised college/university in India. Academic records: Good past academic performance. Co-applicant : Parent/guardian usually required as a co-applicant. Nationality: Indian citizen. Income criteria: Family should have a stable income to repay the loan. Collateral: Required for loans above a certain amount (varies by lenders). Documentation: ID proof, address proof, and admission letter mandatory. Interest rates, processing fees, and margin for BA student loan When considering an education loan for bachelor of arts students, it’s helpful to understand the typical costs involved: Interest rates: Loans carry an interest rate , which can be fixed or floating, and may vary depending on the financial institution and loan type. Processing fees: A small one-time fee is usually charged to process the loan application. This varies across lenders and schemes. Margin/Contribution: Lenders may require a portion of the course cost to be paid by the student or family upfront, known as the margin. These aspects can differ depending on the financial institution and the specific loan scheme chosen. How to apply for an education loan for BA in India? To apply for an education loan for bachelor of arts, you can follow the steps given here: 1. Select the best education loan lender for BA Several financial institutions provide education loans for a bachelor of arts. Before deciding on a lender, you should compare the interest rate, repayment period and loan coverage. 2. Prepare the required education loan documents Before applying for an education loan, you should have the required documents ready to avoid last-minute hassle. Some standard education loan documents include identity proof, academic documents and financial documents. 3. Obtain and fill the loan application form You can get the education loan application form from the financial institution’s website or by visiting their office. 4. Submit the application and documents Take care while filling out the form and attaching the required documents. Remember to read any guidelines or disclaimers. Once you’re satisfied, go ahead and submit the loan application. The lender will contact you once your application is approved. Tips for quick education loan approval for BA To secure quick approval for an education loan for BA undergraduate students in India: Complete documentation: Submit all required documents, including admission letter, ID, address proof, and academic records. Strong co-applicant: Include a co-applicant with a stable income to boost credibility. Clear repayment plan: Show the lender your plan to repay the loan on time . Maintain good credit: Ensure your or your co-applicant’s credit history is clean. Apply early: Submit the loan application well before course commencement. These steps can speed up the loan approval process. Concluding thoughts A bachelor of arts degree is intellectually satisfying and provides a prestigious career with steady growth. While reputed universities offer an excellent education, a three-year degree can be expensive. For a hassle-free education experience, securing funding before admission is paramount. Instead of dipping into your savings, consider an education loan for BA. Tata Capital provides student finance facilities with attractive interest rates, pre-admission sanction and zero margin. Tata Capital’s versatile education loans cover every necessary education expense so that you can devote yourself entirely to learning without worry. Add wings to your dream. Submission of required documents: Your chosen lender will need you to submit certain documents to process your loan. Here’s a general list of documents to keep ready for the purpose: Admission letter: Proof of admission to the educational institution. KYC documents : Proof of address and identity, such as passport or Aadhar card. Academic transcripts: Certificates of qualification awarded earlier. Co-applicant’s financial details: Income proof, as may be demonstrated through salary slips or tax returns. Collateral documents: Where applicable, documents concerning assets pledged against collateral. c. Verification process: The lender typically verifies your application and documents after submission. Depending upon the institution, the process can take a few days to a couple of weeks. d. Disbursement of loan: After sanctioning, the amount so approved is disbursed. Repayment periods will also depend on the borrower’s profile and lender policies. While an education loan provides financial support, securing one can be challenging, especially if the primary applicant lacks a strong credit history or sufficient income. This is where a co-applicant plays a key role in improving loan eligibility . With a co-applicant, students can improve their chances of loan approval, get better interest rates, and access higher loan amounts. This article explores a co-applicant’s role in an education loan , its impact on eligibility, and key borrower considerations. What is a Co-applicant in an Education Loan? A co-applicant in an education loan is someone who shares financial responsibility for repaying the loan alongside the primary borrower. Co-applicants, also known as co-borrowers, strengthen the loan application by offering an extra source of income and financial stability. Types of Co-Applicants in Education Loans: Primary & Financial In an education loan, a co-applicant plays an important role in supporting the student’s loan application . There are two main types of co-applicants: Primary co-applicant Financial co-applicant Usually parents of the student. When a student cannot appoint a primary co-applicant with a permanent source of income, a financial co-applicant is appointed. A primary co-applicant is selected regardless of their financial condition. In the case of secured education loans, government banks may even allow retired parents or individuals without a regular income to act as primary co-applicants. Individuals such as first cousins, other close family members, or paternal and maternal uncles or aunts can become financial co-applicants, as long as they have a stable income. Difference Between Co-Applicant and Guarantor in Education Loan While both co-applicants and guarantors provide financial backing, they have distinct roles: Aspect Co-applicant Guarantor Loan liability Shares equal responsibility for repayment Liable only if borrower defaults Impact on credit score Affects both the borrower’s and co-applicant’s credit score Affects credit score only if repayment is missed Income consideration Lender assesses co-applicant’s income for eligibility Guarantor’s income is not considered Who Can Be a Co-Applicant for an Education Loan? Typically, lenders allow the following individuals as co-applicants: Parents or legal guardians (most common). Spouse or siblings (in some cases). Other close family members as per lender guidelines. Note: Friends are generally not allowed as co-applicants. Co-Applicant Eligibility Criteria for Education Loan To qualify as a co-applicant, individuals must meet certain financial requirements: Stable income: Lenders verify that the co-applicant has a consistent income to ensure smooth loan repayment. A lack of steady earnings may affect approval chances. Good credit score: A high credit score indicates financial credibility and enhances the chances of securing a loan. Employment status: Co-applicants should be salaried or self-employed with verifiable income sources. Lenders prefer individuals with a stable job or business for financial security. Income Tax Returns (ITR): Lenders require recent ITR documents for income verification. Existing liabilities: Ongoing loans or debts are checked to determine repayment capacity and overall financial stability. Documents Required from Co-Applicant for Education Loan Lenders require different documents based on whether the co-applicant is salaried or self-employed. Here’s a breakdown: Document type Salaried co-applicant Self-employed co-applicant Recent salary slips Last three months Not applicable Business address proof Not required GST certificate, MSME certificate, or utility bill Income Tax Returns (ITR) Form 16 or IT returns for the last two years IT returns for the last two years (max 6-month gap) TDS certificate (Form 16A) Required, along with balance sheet, and profit and loss statement Required, along with balance sheet, and profit and loss statement Bank statements Last six months Last six months Statement of assets and liabilities Mandatory Mandatory Professional qualification certificate Required for professionals like C.A., doctors Required for professionals like C.A., doctors These documents help lenders evaluate the financial standing of the co-applicant and ensure they meet the loan eligibility requirements. How Co-Applicant Improves Education Loan Approval and Interest Rates Applying with a co-borrower for an education loan improves loan approval chances. Here’s how: Better creditworthiness: Lenders assess both the student and co-applicant’s financial profiles. A co-applicant with a stable income and a strong credit score increases approval chances. Higher loan amounts: With a financially strong co-applicant, students may qualify for a higher loan amount, covering tuition fees, accommodation, and other expenses. Lower interest rates: A well-qualified co-applicant can secure lower loan interest rates, reducing repayment costs Faster loan approval: A strong co-applicant in education loans leads to quicker loan processing and approval. Impact of Co-Applicant’s CIBIL Score & Income On Loan Approval A co-applicant must be the primary debtor and should have an Indian bank account. Along with basic eligibility, lenders carefully look through the co-applicant’s financial profile before approving an education loan. CIBIL Score It reflects the creditworthiness of the co-applicant. It is based on their credit and repayment history. Scores range from 300 to 850. A higher score improves loan approval chances. Income Lenders assess the co-applicant’s annual income, which must meet the lender’s minimum requirement. Income Tax Returns (ITR) are essential, as they help lenders review financial details. Salaried co-applicants must submit salary slips from the last 6–8 months as salary proof. How to Apply for an Education Loan with a Co-Applicant The educational loan process with a co-applicant involves these steps: 1. Online application Fill the loan application form online with your details and those of your co-applicant. Provide basic information about your course, institution, and loan amount required. 2. Document submission Submit the required documents of both the student and the co-applicant . The same can include proof of income, bank statements, ID proofs, and the letter of admission issued by the educational institution. 3. Verification The financial position of the applicant and the co-applicant is scrutinised by the lender. The credit score, stability of income, and ability to repay is evaluated to sanction the loan. 4. Approval and sanction After being verified, the loan is approved. A sanction letter with the amount of the loan, interest rate, tenure, and repayment schedule is given. 5. Disbursal After agreeing to the terms of the loan, the amount is disbursed directly to the school in accordance with the fee structure. When Should You Apply with a Co-Applicant for Education Loan? Here are some individuals who may benefit from applying with a co-applicant: Students without a credit history: Most students do not have a financial track record, so a co-applicant strengthens their loan application. Borrowers needing higher loan amounts: A stable co-applicant can secure a larger loan for tuition and living expenses. Applicants with low credit scores: A co-applicant with a good credit score increases approval chances if the primary borrower has a weak credit profile. Common Co-Applicant Mistakes That Lead to Loan Rejection Choosing the right education loan co-applicant is important. Being aware of potential mistakes can help students make a better decision when choosing. Some common co-applicant mistakes that can occur are mentioned below: Selecting a co-applicant without a stable income or strong credit history. Submitting incomplete, incorrect, or missing documents such as income or financial statements. Ignoring the legal responsibility of repayment if the student defaults. Overlooking the impact of default on the co-applicant’s credit score. Tips to Choose the Right Co-Applicant for Maximum Success Choosing the right person to be a co-applicant is a difficult but important task. Some tips to choose the right co-applicant are listed below:. Relationship: A parent, legal guardian, sibling, or any blood relative can be an education loan co-applicant. Primary Debtor: The co-applicant must act as the primary debtor and have an Indian bank account with cheque-signing authority. CIBIL Score: A higher CIBIL score (300–850) shows strong creditworthiness and improves loan approval chances. ITR Records: Income Tax Returns are essential, as lenders use them to review financial details. Salaried Proof: Salaried co-applicants must submit salary slips from the last 6-8 months. Business Proof: Self-employed co-applicants need documents such as GST registration, incorporation papers, and recent financial statements. Income Level: Lenders also assess annual income, which must meet their minimum requirement. Can You Get an Education Loan Without a Co-Applicant? A co-applicant is important because many students do not have a steady income or credit history. This gives lenders confidence that the loan will be repaid if the student faces financial problems. However, a co-applicant is not always required and depends on the lender’s rules and the borrower’s financial profile. Conclusion A co-applicant in an education loan plays a vital role in improving loan eligibility, securing better terms, and ensuring successful repayment. By adding a financially stable co-borrower, students can easily access the funds they need for higher education. Add wings to your dream. Apply for an Education loan! This blog will offer guidance on comprehending education loan eligibility and equip readers with the information necessary to utilise an education loan eligibility calculator. Readers, whether students or parents, can begin an exciting journey of exploring education loan eligibility and securing their future. What is an education loan? An education loan is a financing option that helps students cover the cost of higher education. These loans are offered by financial institutions and cover expenses like tuition, books, living expenses, and other academic fees. An education loan typically comes with flexible repayment terms and may include a grace period until the student completes their education. What are the key features of education loans? Here are some key features of education loans: The moratorium period Education loans are designed with the constraints of students in mind, which is why they include a moratorium period. This period can last anywhere from 6 to 12 months after you complete your course. It offers you a break from repaying the loan through EMIs while you get settled. Flexible repayment Education loans allow you to make flexible repayments that suit your income and other financial needs. You can extend the repayment period over several years after completing your course. This allows you to gradually repay the loan while also building your life and career. Secured vs. Unsecured Education loans can either be secured or unsecured, and you can choose the option that best fits your needs. Secured loans require collateral, whereas unsecured loans do not. You can make this decision based on what works best for your financial situation. What are the different types of education loans? Domestic, abroad, secured & unsecured Education loans can be of different types. You can choose them depending on whether you study in India or abroad, whether you pledge collateral or not, and other similar factors. Here are the different types of education loans available: Domestic education loan : This type of loan is for students who plan to study within the country. The loan can be used to cover expenses such as tuition fees, books, accommodation, equipment, etc. Abroad (overseas) education loans : This loan is for students who plan to study in foreign universities. These loans help cover various education-related expenses such as tuition fees, travel, accommodation, and study materials. Graduate education loan : Students who want to pursue a postgraduate course can apply for this type of loan. Undergraduate education loan : This type of loan is for students who want to pursue an undergraduate course. They may offer loan amounts ranging from Rs 85 lakh up to Rs. 2 crore. Professional education loan : Working professionals who want to enhance their employment skills can apply for this type of loan. These loans offer quick disbursals, allowing working professionals to pursue their dreams without hassles. Secured education loans (with collateral): This loan requires deposits, property or securities to be used as collateral. Since these loans are secured, they may offer a high loan amount of up to Rs. 2 crore. Unsecured education loans (collateral-free) : This type of loan does not require collateral. However, they may also offer relatively lower loan amounts, depending on several factors. By understanding education loan eligibility and exploring the different types of education loans available, students can find the financial support they need to achieve their educational goals. Institution Affiliation University Grants Commission (UGC)/All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)/Govt., etc. Co-applicant Parent/guardian or spouse/parent-in-law (for married candidates). What is the student loan age limit and maximum loan amount in India? They take into account various factors before approving a loan. Some of the factors that can improve one’s education loan eligibility are: Obtaining high grades/ranking in the qualifying exams. Having an excellent academic record. Achieving admission to a reputed/top-ranked institute or university. Having strong financial support from parents/guardians/co-borrower. Having positive potential for future employment/income generation. Personal loan for education vs education loan: Which one should you choose? While you can use both an education loan and a personal loan to fund education expenses, their flexibility and benefits may differ. Let’s understand this in detail: Interest rates : Education loans are designed for funding education, so lenders may offer them at relatively lower interest rates, especially when backed by collateral or a co-applicant. Personal loans, on the other hand, are usually unsecured and not tied to any specific purpose. As a result, lenders may quote higher interest rates to cover the risk associated with lending. Moratorium period : Education loans come with a moratorium period, making it easier to manage repayment. Personal loans generally do not offer a moratorium period, so you may need to start repaying almost immediately. Collateral and guarantor : The educational loan eligibility criteria may differ from personal loans. For example, some education loans, though not all, may require collateral or a guarantor. This may make it harder for some people to qualify for them. Personal loans, in most cases, do not require either, which makes it easier to acquire them. Highlight Relevant Experience: If you used the gap period for internships, training, workshops, or relevant practical work, include certificates to show continued learning and commitment. Choose a Strong Co-Applicant: A co-applicant (often a parent/guardian) with stable income, good credit history, and strong repayment capacity can offset academic weaknesses when assessing education loan eligibility. Students applying for MBBS should have Physics/Biology/Chemistry as their primary subjects in 12th standard and must have secured at least 50% in the examinations. The university/institute must be recognised by the National Medical Commission (NMC), World Health Organization (WHO) and United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). In this article, we will delve into the intricacies of education loan repayment rules in India, shedding light on the significance of understanding these rules for effective planning. Moratorium Period Understanding the moratorium period is fundamental to crafting a successful education loan repayment strategy. The moratorium period acts as a crucial phase where students are granted a repayment holiday, delaying the start of Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs) . Typically, this period spans the course duration plus an additional 6 months to a year. For instance, if your academic program extends over 2 years, the moratorium period could extend up to 3 years. However, variations exist among banks. In Government banks, students may opt to start EMIs during the moratorium, while in Private banks and NBFCs , this is usually not the case. During the moratorium period, Government banks often offer a no-payment option, relieving students from any financial obligation. In contrast, Private banks and NBFCs might require students to pay either full or partial interest during this period. Education Loan Repayment Rules During Moratorium Navigating through the moratorium period involves understanding whether repayments are mandatory during this financial respite. Ideally, the moratorium period is designed to offer students a financial breather after completing their studies. During this phase, students are not obliged to make any payments. However, the scenario varies across banks. Some offer a zero-payment moratorium, allowing students to complete financial relief during this period. In contrast, others may calculate and expect partial or full interest payments. This distinction in policies between banks underscores the importance of knowing your lender’s terms. Differences Between Repayment in Government Banks and NBFCs Comparing the education loan repayment processes between Government banks and Non-Banking Financial Corporations (NBFCs) is vital for students making informed decisions. Government banks often stand out due to their student-friendly repayment policies, offering a broader repayment tenure of 12 to 15 years after the moratorium period concludes. This extended tenure provides students with a significant repayment holiday, allowing them to settle into their careers before beginning EMIs. In contrast, NBFCs present a different approach. While they do offer a moratorium period akin to Government banks, students might be required to pay interest during this phase. Additionally, the total loan tenure in NBFCs is often capped at 10 years, including the moratorium period. Choosing between Government banks and NBFCs involves careful consideration. Opting for a Government bank with collateral can yield better offers, as the loan tenure includes the moratorium period. This choice is crucial, as it can impact the overall duration of your loan and, subsequently, your financial burden. When to Start Repaying an Education Loan in India Choosing the right time to initiate education loan repayments is a pivotal decision that significantly impacts your financial trajectory. Most students find the optimal window for repayment between 5 to 7 years post-education. While the moratorium period offers a payment-free window, it’s crucial to recognize that it’s not interest-free. Simple interest accrues during this period, especially considering the relatively high-interest rates in Private banks and NBFCs. Starting repayments early is advised to prevent the accumulation of substantial interest and alleviate the overall cost of the loan. Delaying repayment can inadvertently amplify the financial burden. As the moratorium is a grace period for EMIs but not interest, planning becomes imperative. Education Loan EMI: Calculation and Repayment Modes Education loan EMIs are Equated Monthly Instalments you pay each month to clear your student loan repayment over the chosen tenure. The EMI is calculated using the standard formula: EMI = [P × R × (1+R)ⁿ] / [(1+R)ⁿ–1], where P is the principal loan amount, R is the monthly interest rate and n is the total number of monthly payments. This helps you plan how much you need to repay every month. In India, education loan repayment normally starts after the moratorium period which includes your course duration plus 6–12 months after completion or 6 months after getting a job, whichever comes earlier. The full repayment period can extend up to several years, depending on the lender’s policies. Popular repayment modes include auto-debit via NACH/ECS, UPI and online banking, which make paying your EMIs convenient. Timely repayment improves your credit score and avoids penalties. Popular Methods to Pay Education Loan in India (NACH, ECS, Cheques) Here are popular methods for education loan repayment in India using different repayment modes: NACH (National Automated Clearing House): Under the NACH mandate , your education loan EMI is automatically debited from your bank account on the due date. This method is widely preferred for education loan repayment as it ensures timely payments, avoids missed EMIs, and helps maintain a good credit score. ECS (Electronic Clearance Service): ECS works in a similar way by enabling automatic student loan repayment from your account every month. It suits borrowers who want a structured and hassle-free way to repay their education loan, provided sufficient balance is maintained. Cheques: Some lenders still allow repayment through cheques, especially for borrowers who prefer offline methods. While reliable, this option requires manual tracking and timely submission to avoid delays or penalties. RTGS/NEFT: These netbanking modes are suitable for student loan repayment, wherein funds are transferred instantly from your bank account to the lender. They are suitable for lump-sum payments, part-prepayments, or closing the loan, but are usually available only during bank working hours. How to Calculate Your Student Loan Repayment Using Calculators To calculate your student loan repayment using an online EMI calculator , follow these simple steps: Enter the loan amount: Type in the total education loan repayment amount you plan to borrow. Input the interest rate: Add the annual interest rate charged by the bank; the calculator converts this to a monthly rate for accurate results. Select loan tenure: Choose how long you want to take to repay the loan (in years or months). Click “Calculate”: The tool instantly shows your monthly EMI, the total interest payable, and the full repayment amount over the tenure. Using these calculators makes it easy to plan how to pay your education loan and understand your obligations in an instant. How to Repay Your Education Loan: Step-by-Step Process Here’s a step-by-step guide if you’re wondering how to pay education loan in India: Know your repayment start date: Repayment typically begins after your moratorium period (course duration plus about 6–12 months) or after securing a job, whichever comes earlier. Review your loan agreement: Check details like interest rates, EMI amount, tenure, and education loan repayment rules so you know when to repay education loan and what’s expected. Plan your budget: Use a student loan repayment calculator to estimate your monthly EMIs and budget your post-graduation income accordingly. Choose a repayment mode: Set up auto-debit (NACH/ECS), NEFT/RTGS, or cheques for regular EMIs. Start EMIs on time: Make your monthly education loan repayment through the chosen mode to avoid penalties and protect your credit score. Managing Repayment During Financial Emergencies & Deferment Here’s how you can manage your student loan repayment during financial emergencies and unforeseen circumstances: Communicate with your lender early: If you face financial difficulties, reach out to your lender as soon as possible. Lenders may offer options such as loan restructuring or temporary relief to avoid defaults and legal consequences. Request repayment flexibility: Some lenders allow you to restructure the repayment schedule so you pay a smaller amount during hard times or adjust EMIs temporarily. This can help manage education loan repayment without hitting defaults. Deferment or moratorium extension: Beyond the standard moratorium (course duration + 6–12 months), you may be able to negotiate extensions or defer additional payments if employment or income is delayed, easing pressure on how to repay education loan. Make partial payments: During challenging periods, making smaller payments toward interest or principal can reduce the total burden and help maintain your student loan repayment schedule. Staying proactive and informed helps you manage repayment more smoothly and protects your credit health during emergencies. Education Loan Repayment Strategies and Tips Navigating the complex terrain of education loan repayment requires a strategic approach. Here are key tips to optimize your repayment journey: How to Use Education Loan Features and Benefits 1. Capitalize on bank features such as interest rate discounts for female candidates, loan insurance benefits, and schemes like Rinn Raksha. 2. Explore subsidy schemes tailored for differently-abled individuals or those from economically weaker sections. 2. Opt for Fixed Rates: – 1. Consider opting for fixed interest rates over floating rates for stability. 2. Understand the impact of interest rate fluctuations, especially for those with floating interest rates. 3. Take Loan Amount Whenever Required: 1. Utilize your loan amount judiciously; interest is calculated on the amount utilized, not the sanctioned amount. 2. Seek clarification from TATA Capital if you face challenges understanding this concept. How to Budget for Your Student Loan Repayment 1. Repayment demands meticulous planning and budgeting. 2. Prioritize repaying the loan, cutting down on unnecessary expenses. 3. Create a detailed budget considering monthly EMIs and interest. 5. Utilize Tax Benefits: – 1. Indian bank borrowers can benefit from Section 80E for tax deductions on education loan interest payments. 2. Understand that the deduction is applicable only for the interest component of the EMI, with a maximum tax benefit period of 8 years. Conclusion Navigating the landscape of education loan repayment in India demands meticulous planning and a nuanced understanding of policies. From comprehending the intricacies of the moratorium period to making informed choices between Government banks and NBFCs, each decision significantly impacts your financial journey. Starting repayments at the right time and implementing strategic tips, such as optimizing available features and utilizing tax benefits, can pave the way for a smoother repayment process. As you embark on your education loan repayment journey, remember that TATA Capital is here to guide you. Your student loan repayment generally begins once your moratorium ends, i.e. after you complete your course and the additional grace period (often 6–12 months) is over. How can I pay my education loan EMI if I am abroad? If you are abroad, you can usually pay your education loan EMIs using online banking (NEFT/RTGS), international bank transfers, or auto-debit arrangements through NACH/standing instructions set up before departure. Most lenders support digital payment options to manage student loan repayment from overseas. Is it beneficial to pay interest during the moratorium period? Yes. Paying interest during the moratorium, even if only simple interest, prevents interest from being added to the principal later, which can reduce the total repayment burden. Can I change my education loan repayment schedule or defer payments? Many lenders allow you to request changes to your repayment schedule or defer payments in cases of financial hardship, subject to their terms and approval. This helps manage repayment during tough times without defaulting. higher education. However, different financial institutions have different loan features to offer which can make it challenging to shortlist the one tailored to your financial needs. To solve this problem, the Government of India established the Vidya Lakshmi Portal to democratise access to education loans. This national portal has brought all major education loan schemes offered by different financial institutions under a unified platform. Students now have easy access to multiple financing options on customised terms through a simplified online process. This article will explain the features and the process of availing of an education loan through the Vidyalakshmi portal. What is the Vidya Lakshmi Portal for education loan? The Vidya Lakshmi education loan portal is a government initiative to provide a single-window electronic platform for students to access education loans and scholarships provided by financial institutions. The portal allows students to explore tailored education financing products from various financial institutions based on parameters such as loan amount, interest rates, moratorium period and repayment schedules. Vidya Laxmi Education loan interest rate The interest rates available under Vidya Laxmi Education Loan differs on the basis of financial institution that provide. These interest rates are typically linked to the RBI’s prevailing repo rate. Interest can also depend on the amount of fee charged in Quality Higher Education Institutions (QHEI) or Higher Education Institution. Students must keep the following details in mind while applying for Vidya Laxmi Education loan: Interest rates are capped at individual lender’s Externally Benchmarked Lending Rate (EBLR) + 0.5%. At present, the interest rates range between 8.1% and 18% for loans of up to ₹10 lakh. Interest rates under the scheme must always be less than what is usually charged by lenders on an education loan Students with annual family income of up to 4.5 lakhs get full interest subvention. Students with annual family income of up to 8 lakhs get 3% interest subvention on loans up to 10 lakhs. Features of the Vidya Lakshmi portal for education loan Below are the main features of the Vidyalakshmi education loan portal: Unified education loan platform: The Vidya Lakshmi portal brings over 100 education loan schemes offered by 38 leading financial institutions under one unified platform. This provides students with a single window to compare customised financing options from different institutions as per their specific needs. Applicants can access tailored loan products for various academic disciplines and apply through a common national education loan application form accessible online. This eliminates the need to approach financial institutions individually, saving time. Loan amount flexibility: Students can identify and apply for education loans as per their requirements under the Vidya Lakshmi scheme. This flexibility in financing can help students pursue any academic programme from short-term diplomas to doctorate degrees from reputed national or overseas universities. The portal allows scheme-wise comparison from various lenders. Students can analyse the varied education loans to choose their ideal financing solution. Streamlined application: Vidya Lakshmi portal allows submission of the unified Common Education Loan Application Form (CELAF) online providing speed and convenience. Applicants also need to upload required academic credentials and income proofs in digitised formats for loan application processing. The single form allows students to apply to multiple appropriate loan schemes from different partner financial institutions simultaneously. The Portal further enables tracking application status in real-time. Also, read – Facts you need to know about Education Loan Benefits of applying via Vidya Lakshmi portal The Vidya Lakshmi portal offers numerous benefits to students and parents: Easy loan discovery: The Vidya Lakshmi portal eliminates the need to manually evaluate numerous complex loan schemes by bringing customised education financing from 100+ options offered by 38 financial institutions under one roof. Students can conveniently compare interest rates, fees, repayment schedules and other parameters digitally to determine loans that suit their unique needs. This helps in saving time and also reduces confusion. Simplified documentation: The national Common Education Loan Application for Vidya Lakshmi portal considerably simplifies documentation while raising financing requests. Applicants need to digitally submit it only once for three loan applications. The status tracking feature further enables students to monitor application progress online securely. Multiple scheme applications: The single loan application form at the Vidyalakshmi portal allows students to apply to potentially 3 different education loan schemes from partner institutions simultaneously if eligibility criteria are met. This expands the probability of loan approval within the application processing timeline. Direct grievance assistance: Students facing any application-related queries or complaints can register them directly with the financial institutions on the Vidya Lakshmi portal. Vidya Lakshmi education loan eligibility criteria Here is the Vidyalakshmi education loan eligibility: Indian citizenship Completed 10+2 level schooling or equivalent with a minimum 50% aggregate marks Secured admission to the chosen institute via merit or entrance exam Annual family income between INR 4-5 lakhs In addition to the Vidyalakshmi loan eligibility, specific eligibility norms may vary as per respective partner financial institutions’ policies. Documents required for Vidya Lakshmi education loans After checking the Vidyalakshmi loan eligibility, students need to have scanned versions of the following key documents handy before initiating an online application for education loans under the Vidya Lakshmi portal: Identity proof like Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport Age proof that includes Birth Certificate, 10th Pass Certificate Academic credentials like marksheets, Admission letters, and fee structure Income proof in the form of IT Returns, Salary Slips, Assets Proof Bank statements Additional documents may be requested by respective financial institutions during later processing stages as relevant. Keeping the prerequisites ready helps expedite loan approval. Also, read – Step-by-Step Guide to the Education Loan Procedure 2026 How to apply for an education loan on Vidya Lakshmi portal? At the heart of the scheme is the Vidya Lakshmi portal education loan , a single-window digital platform that allows students to explore, compare, and apply for loans from multiple lenders at once. One of the major advantages of the scheme is transparency. Students can view lender-specific terms, including the Vidya Lakshmi education loan interest rate , which varies by financial institution, course, and applicant profile. The portal also supports interest subsidy benefits under applicable central government schemes for eligible students, especially those from economically weaker sections. Understanding how to apply education loan in Vidya Lakshmi portal is straightforward. Students register, fill a Common Education Loan Application Form (CELAF), upload documents, and track application status online. Overall, the Vidya Lakshmi scheme makes education financing more accessible, structured, and student-friendly. Also, read – How is Interest Calculated on Education Loans? Loan limit, tenure & expenses covered under Vidya Lakshmi scheme The Vidya Lakshmi scheme offers flexible education loan options to support students pursuing higher studies in India and abroad. Through the Vidya Lakshmi portal education loan , applicants can access loans starting from modest amounts to higher limits, depending on the course, institution, and lender guidelines. Loan tenures are generally long, allowing students sufficient time to complete their studies and repay comfortably after the moratorium period. Expenses covered under the scheme typically include tuition fees, hostel charges, examination fees, books, equipment, and reasonable living expenses. Some financial institutions may also finance travel costs for overseas education. While the Vidya Lakshmi education loan interest rate is not fixed under the scheme, the portal enables students to compare lender-specific rates and repayment terms before applying. This transparency helps applicants choose a loan aligned with their financial capacity and academic goals. Common Education Loan Application Form (CELAF): Step-by-step guide The Common Education Loan Application Form (CELAF) streamlines the education loan application process through a single, standardised form. Here’s how to complete it step by step: Step 1: Register on the Vidya Lakshmi portal using your basic personal details. Step 2: Log in and select the Common Education Loan Application Form (CELAF). Step 3: Enter academic details, course information, institution name, and required loan amount. Step 4: Fill in co-applicant and financial details as requested. Step 5: Upload mandatory documents such as admission letter, academic records, ID proof, and income documents. Step 6: Review the form carefully and submit it online. Step 7: Choose preferred lenders and track your application status through the portal dashboard. This structured process ensures faster, transparent, and hassle-free loan applications.
