Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund The Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) play a vital role in the Indian economy. However, these enterprises often need help accessing credit due to weak credit history and collateral. This Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) addresses this issue by providing credit guarantees to financial institutions, enabling them to extend collateral-free credit to MSEs. In fact, during FY 2023, the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) has issued guarantees amounting to ₹1,04,781 crore. Whether you’re a startup enthusiast or a seasoned business leader, understanding the role of CGTMSE could be pivotal for your entrepreneurial journey. In this blog post, we cover various CGTMSE scheme details. Let’s find out how CGTMSE can support your business goals. What is CGTMSE? (Full Form, Purpose & How Credit Guarantee Works) CGTMSE’s full form is Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises. This scheme was initiated in 2000 by the Government of India and SIDBI. It aims to foster the growth of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs). The CGTMSE scheme serves as a vital resource for MSEs, addressing the challenge of accessing financial support from traditional lenders. Under this scheme, MSEs can secure credit facilities without the burden of providing tangible collateral or third-party guarantees. Instead, the scheme offers a guarantee cover to lending institutions, reducing their risk in case of borrower default. This reduces the lending risk for financial institutions and enhances the creditworthiness of MSEs. The CGTMSE scheme is inclusive, catering to MSEs across diverse manufacturing, services, and retail sectors. It prioritises inclusivity by empowering economically weaker sections, women entrepreneurs, and those in rural or underserved areas. CGTMSE Scheme Eligibility Criteria (Who Can Apply?) The eligibility criteria for the CGTMSE loan and scheme are as follows: Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs): Both existing and new MSEs operating in various sectors, including manufacturing and services, are eligible. Size of enterprises: MSEs of all sizes are eligible, ensuring accessibility for budding entrepreneurs and established businesses. Lending institutions: Participation is open to a wide range of lending institutions, including National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), Non- Banking Financial Companies (NBFC), North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd (NEDFi), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), and Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI). Special provisions: Special provisions are made for specific categories, such as women entrepreneurs and businesses in the Northeast Region (NER), offering enhanced guarantee cover and tailored credit facilities. CGTMSE Scheme Features (Guarantee Coverage, Maximum Loan, No-Collateral) The CGTMSE scheme offers several key features that make it attractive for MSEs: The scheme operates within the framework of RBI guidelines, ensuring transparency and consistency in CGTMSE loan interest rate. MSEs engaged in manufacturing and services, excluding specific sectors like educational institutions and agriculture-related activities, are eligible for coverage. The CGTMSE loan amount is between Rs. 50 lakhs to Rs. 5 crores, depending on the type of lending institution. CGTMSE provides guarantee coverage ranging from 75% to 85%, reducing the risk for lenders and encouraging them to extend credit to MSEs without requiring collateral or third-party guarantees. One of the most significant advantages of the CGTMSE scheme is that it eliminates the need for collateral or third-party guarantees, making credit more accessible to MSEs. CGTMSE Benefits for MSME Owners & Startups The CGTMSE scheme offers several benefits for MSEs: Financial inclusion: By providing collateral-free credit, the scheme promotes financial inclusion, enabling MSEs, especially those from marginalised sections, to access formal credit facilities. Risk mitigation: The guarantee provided by CGTMSE mitigates the risk for lenders, encouraging them to extend credit to MSEs that may otherwise be deemed too risky. Business growth: Access to credit under the scheme facilitates business growth, allowing MSEs to invest in expansion, technology adoption, and market diversification. Empowerment: The scheme empowers MSEs to fulfil their potential, driving entrepreneurship, innovation, and job creation. How Does the CGTMSE Loan/Guarantee Scheme Work? Here’s a breakdown of how the CGTMSE loan works: Step 1: MSEs must meet the eligibility criteria and gather all required documents. Step 2: Choose a suitable Member Lending Institution (MLI) under the CGTMSE scheme based on their offerings and terms. Step 3: Submit the business loan application and the required documents to the chosen MLI. Step 4: The MLI reviews the application, conducts due diligence, and assesses the viability of the business proposal. Step 5: If the application meets the MLI’s criteria, they sanction the loan amount per their internal policies and the CGTMSE scheme guidelines. Step 6: The MLI applies to CGTMSE for guarantee cover on behalf of the borrower. Step 7: The borrower pays the applicable guarantee fee and service charges to CGTMSE registration as per the approved rates. Step 8: The MLI disburses the sanctioned loan amount to the borrower’s account upon approval of the guarantee cover. Step 9: The borrower repays the loan per the agreed schedule, including principal and interest payments. The borrower must comply with all terms and conditions of the loan agreement and ensure timely repayment throughout the loan tenure. Also,read: Mudra Business Loan: How to Apply, Eligibility & Documents CGTMSE Scheme: Stepwise Loan Application & Approval Process The following steps explain how MSMEs can smoothly move from application to disbursal under the CGTMSE framework. Lender Selection: Choose an eligible Lender, participating in the Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSME , and discuss your funding requirement, and business profile. Documentation Readiness: Compile essential documents, including KYC, Udyam registration, financial statements, and the CGTMSE loan application form , for accurate submission. Loan Application: Submission Submit the completed application to the Lender, for preliminary verification and processing. Credit Assessment: The Lender evaluates business viability, repayment capacity, and overall creditworthiness. Guarantee Coverage: Request Upon approval, the Lender applies to CGTMSE, for guarantee cover, on your behalf. Loan Sanction and Disbursal: After guarantee confirmation, funds are sanctioned, and disbursed, for business use. Also,read: What Are the Types of Business Loans? Documents Required for CGTMSE Loan Application Looking to benefit from a CGTMSE loan for a new business? Copy of loan approval from the bank CGTMSE Guarantee Fees, Coverage Table & Renewal Guarantee Fee Structure: The guarantee fee is charged annually, on the outstanding loan amount, and varies based on loan size, borrower category, and risk profile under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSME . Coverage Levels: The guarantee typically covers 75 per cent to 85 per cent of the sanctioned amount, offering meaningful risk protection to the Lender. Concessional Benefits: Women entrepreneurs and select priority segments may receive higher coverage, improving overall credit access. Validity and Renewal: Guarantee cover remains active for the loan tenure, and renewal is required annually, subject to timely fee payment. Application Compliance: Accurate submission of the CGTMSE loan application form , along with supporting documents, ensures uninterrupted guarantee coverage. Incomplete Documentation: Missing or inaccurate business records, and financials, often lead to rejection, so ensure your paperwork is complete, and up to date. Weak Financials: Poor cash flow, and low profitability, increase risk perception at the Lender, so maintain clear accounts, and realistic projections. Credit History Issues: A low credit score, or past defaults, reduce repayment confidence, so clear outstanding dues, and build consistent credit behaviour. Unconvincing Business: Plan An unclear strategy, or weak market understanding, affects approval, so present a focused plan, showing growth, and repayment capacity. Who is eligible for a loan or guarantee under the CGTMSE scheme? Can new and existing MSMEs apply for CGTMSE loans? Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A home loan helps individuals buy their dream home by providing the necessary funds while allowing them to repay it over time. This makes owning a home more accessible for many. However, in the past few years, home loans have become more expensive, impacting both new borrowers and those with existing loans. Higher interest rates have increased the financial strain, either by raising monthly EMIs or extending the loan tenure . To ease this burden, borrowers can opt for a loan conversion by paying a small conversion fee. Many financial institutions allow you to switch from your current higher interest rate to their lower, prevailing rates. This reduction in interest rates helps lower your EMIs, making it easier to manage monthly payments and save on the total loan cost. In this article, we explain what conversion charges in home loans are, how they work, and the benefits they offer. We also cover the critical factors to consider before choosing this option so you can make the best financial decision for your home loan. Fixed vs Floating Home Loan Interest Rates Explained Before understanding home loan conversion charges, it’s important to know the two main types of interest rates- floating and fixed. Fixed interest rates stay constant throughout the loan’s tenure. They are not affected by economic policies, giving borrowers the assurance of a stable EMI. However, these rates are typically higher than floating rates, as financial institutions charge more to cover the risk of interest rate fluctuations. In contrast, floating interest rates change based on market conditions. They are tied to a benchmark rate, currently the Repo Linked Lending Rate (RLLR), which is adjusted by the government. As a result, borrowers’ interest rates may vary when these benchmarks change. What are Conversion Charges for Home Loans? Conversion charges in a home loan are fees that a borrower must pay when switching from their existing interest rate to a lower one offered by their lender. Some financial institutions allow their current borrowers to opt for this switch in order to benefit from reduced interest rates, which can help lower monthly EMIs and the total loan cost. The conversion fee typically ranges between 0.25% and 0.5% of the outstanding loan amount , depending on the lender’s policies. Additionally, there may be a minimum fee, often around Rs. 5,000, along with applicable taxes. How Home Loan Conversion Charges Work: A Step-by-Step Guide Let us say you took out a home loan two years ago at a 10% interest rate. Now that the market rate has dropped to 8.75%, you can request your lender to switch your loan to the lower rate. In exchange, the lender will charge a conversion fee to process this switch. Once the conversion is done, your EMIs may reduce, helping you manage monthly payments more easily. Alternatively, you could keep the EMIs the same and shorten your loan tenure. While the conversion fee is an upfront cost, the potential savings from paying lower interest over time make it a beneficial move. Why do Lenders Charge a Conversion Fee? Conversion charges for home loans help lenders recover administrative costs related to recalculating loan terms and updating loan agreements. These fees also help offset potential revenue loss from lowering interest rates. Additionally, financial institutions want to maintain a balance between retaining existing ones and attracting new customers. While offering competitive interest rates to new borrowers helps them grow their market, the conversion facility ensures they don’t lose existing borrowers to competitors. Key Benefits of Converting Your Home Loan Though you have to pay an upfront conversion fee, switching your home loan can offer several benefits. – A reduced interest rate directly lowers your monthly EMIs, helping you manage your finances better. – You can maintain the same EMI amount while reducing your loan tenure, allowing you to repay the loan faster. – Over time, the savings from lower interest payments often outweigh the conversion fees, making this option cost-effective. – Since you are not transferring your loan to another bank, you don’t have to go through the documentation and legal formalities for a new loan. Critical Factors to Evaluate Before Loan Conversion While paying a small conversion fee can lead to lower interest rates, there are some factors you should consider. 1. Check the fee structure Conversion charges vary among lenders. Some financial institutions charge a flat fee, while others calculate it as a percentage of the outstanding loan. It’s crucial to determine whether the savings on interest justify the conversion cost. 2. Compare new offers Before opting for conversion, compare the new rate offered by your lender with those from other financial institutions. In some cases, transferring your loan to another lender may yield better savings, even after considering processing fees. 3. Impact on loan tenure A conversion can either reduce your EMI or shorten the loan tenure. Ensure you understand the implications of both options and choose the one that aligns with your financial goals. 4. Market trends Interest rates fluctuate based on economic factors. If you anticipate further drops in rates, consider waiting before converting. Conversely, if rates are on the rise, acting quickly can help you lock in a lower rate. How to Apply for Home Loan Conversion: Step-by-Step Process When interest rates fall, converting your existing home loan is one of the simplest ways to reduce your EMI without changing lenders. Since the process happens within the same financial institution, it is quicker and involves minimal paperwork. Here’s how you can apply for a home loan conversion: 1. Submit a conversion request: Start by placing a formal request with your existing lender. You can usually do this through a branch visit, customer portal, or email. 2. Lender assessment: The lender reviews your repayment history, credit score , and the difference between your current rate and the new prevailing rate. 3. Approval and fee intimation: If approved, the lender communicates the applicable conversion charges and revised loan terms. 4. Pay the conversion fee: Once you pay the one-time fee, the lender initiates the switch. 5. Receive revised loan schedule: You will get a new repayment schedule showing either reduced EMIs or a shorter tenure at the revised interest rate. Comparing Conversion Fees Across Top Lenders in India Conversion fees vary across lenders and depend on the loan type , benchmark, and rate structure. While some lenders charge a fixed fee, others calculate it as a percentage of the outstanding principal. Lender Floating Rate Conversion Fee Fixed to Floating Conversion Fee Tata Capital 0.25% of outstanding amount (or as per your loan terms) 1.50% of outstanding amount (for fixed-to-floating conversions) SBI Up to ₹5,000 (fixed fee) ₹5,000 (fixed fee) HDFC Bank 0.25% of outstanding amount 1.75% of outstanding amount ICICI Bank 0.50% of outstanding amount 1.75% of outstanding amount HSBC ₹2,500 (fixed fee) ₹5,000 (fixed fee) Loan Conversion vs Balance Transfer: Which Saves More? Both loan conversion and balance transfer aim to reduce your interest burden, but they differ in cost, effort, and potential savings. Loan conversion is usually faster and cheaper. You stay with the same lender, avoid legal and valuation charges, and only pay a small conversion fee. This option works well if your lender is offering a competitive rate and your remaining tenure is limited. A balance transfer, on the other hand, involves switching to a new lender. While this option includes higher upfront costs such as processing fees and legal charges, the interest rate reduction is often larger. If your existing lender offers only a marginal rate cut, a balance transfer can generate greater long-term savings. However, if the rate difference is small or your loan is nearing completion, conversion is usually the more practical choice. Calculation Example: Saving ₹X with Conversion vs Balance Transfer Let’s assume the following scenario: Outstanding loan amount: ₹50,00,000 Remaining tenure: 15 years Current interest rate: 9.00% Option New Rate One-time Cost Total Interest Outgo Net Savings No change 9.00% ₹0 ₹42,57,363 — Conversion 8.75% ₹5,000 ₹40,30,816 ₹2,21,547 Balance Transfer 8.50% ₹35,000 ₹38,06,256 ₹4,16,107 Although balance transfer involves higher upfront costs, the deeper rate cut results in higher overall savings over the loan tenure. Documents Required for Home Loan Conversion Application Since the conversion happens with your existing lender, documentation requirements are minimal. You may need to submit: – A formal request letter asking for interest rate or benchmark conversion – Loan account details, including outstanding amount and remaining tenure – Updated KYC documents such as Aadhaar and PAN, if required – Latest income proof, if the lender reassesses eligibility – Payment receipt for the conversion fee Wrapping up Converting your home loan interest rates is an excellent way to lower your interest and ease financial pressure. Although you’ll need to pay a conversion fee for a home loan, the long-term savings from reduced interest often outweigh the initial cost. However, before deciding, carefully evaluate your current loan terms, compare offers from different financial institutions, and understand the fee structure. With the right approach, you can make the most of your home loan and reduce your overall borrowing costs. Can I negotiate the conversion fee with my lender? If you have a strong credit profile and repayment history, lenders may reduce or waive conversion fees to retain you as a borrower. Well, then, you must learn about the home loan processing fee. Know that your lending institution charges this as a one-time fee for facilitating your loan application. Certain lending institutions and NBFCs also term this an administrative fee, which they don’t deduct from your EMIs . This means you must pay the home loan processing fee upfront and out of your pocket. What is Home Loan Processing Fee? A loan processing fee is a standard feature on most loans , and housing finance is no different. You typically pay a home loan processing fee to your lending institution or NBFC to facilitate your borrowing process. This includes various administrative tasks such as: Paperwork verification Site inspection Legal documentation And other such operations. Typically, most lending institutions charge this fee one time, but they may split it into two parts. You may pay the first half of the fee at the time of application, and the final instalment, if your loan is approved. Other institutions may levy the loan processing fee only once your application is approved. Therefore, it is prudent to ask your lending institution about the loan processing fee payment plan in advance. What is the Processing Fee for Loan for Homes? Your processing fee depends on your lending institution. However, a general rule of thumb with this fee is that it depends on the mortgage charges for a home loan. Simply speaking, your processing fee is a percentage of your total housing loan. This percentage figure can change with different lenders, but usually, it goes up to 1% of the total loan amount. In a few cases, you may find a new lender willing to charge zero processing fee for a home loan in a bid to acquire customers quickly. Since the mortgage charges for a home loan have a significant role to play in processing fees, choose this number wisely. What Other Charges Can I Expect on Home Loans? In addition to the processing fee, a lending institution may levy the following home loan charges: Default Penalty Timely repaying your home loan EMIs has a positive impact on your CIBIL score. This makes it easier for you to get more loans in the future. On the other hand, defaulting or delaying your loan repayments will lead to a penalty. Depending on your lending institution, this number can go up to 2% of the total amount borrowed. Therefore, be sure to check your lender’s default penalty policy. To easily avoid this home loan charge , provide standing instructions to your primary account, which will always carry ample funds. Prepayment Charges Borrowers may want to foreclose their home loan before the tenure is up. Or, they may pay off a big chunk of their EMI earlier than is stipulated in their loan contract. This is called loan prepayment, for which a lender may charge a fee. Therefore, check the prepayment charges mentioned in your contract before signing above the dotted line. You may also encounter certain lending institutions that don’t have a prepayment penalty. Certain lenders term this fee pre-closure or foreclosure charges. Try finding a loan deal where you can avoid this home loan charge. Insurance Against Property This is an optional processing charge for a home loan, as not all buyers want to insure their property. The ones who do can request their lending institutions to insure their property. For this, the lending institution deducts the required amount along with the EMI. Conversion Fee Another optional processing charge for a home loan is the conversion fee. Suppose home loan interest rates in the market have come down. Naturally, you would want to avail those rates. You can do this by transferring your existing loan to the same lending institution. For this, your lender will levy a conversion fee, depending on the difference between the old and new interest rates. You can also switch lenders if you find a lower interest rate elsewhere. In that case, you will escape the conversion fee altogether. However, bear in mind the new lender may charge you the processing fee of the home loan. Current Home Loan Processing Fees by Bank Home loan processing fees in 2026 vary by lender. Currently, home loan bank processing charges levied by major lenders typically range from 0.25% to 1% of the loan amount. These amounts are also usually capped at Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 50,000. Some financial institutions use a flat-fee structure, while others charge a percentage of the sanctioned amount. These fees typically cover administrative checks, credit appraisal, legal verification, and technical valuation. To secure the best offer, remember to check with different financial institutions. Conduct online research to identify the best home loan fee comparison and current loan processing fees . How to Negotiate or Reduce Home Loan Processing Fees While they are usually fixed and unavoidable, there are steps one can take to reduce home loan fees . Let’s take a look at some tips to save on loan fees : 1. High credit score : A higher CIBIL score gives borrowers a stronger chance to negotiate loan processing charges . 2. Applying during festive periods : Many lenders may offer discounts of up to 50% lower on home loan processing fees . 3. Apply to known financial institutions : It’s also smart to approach financial institutions where you already have an account or sizable deposits, since existing customers typically receive preferential treatment. State-wise Stamp Duty & Registration Charges Impacting Total Costs Stamp duty varies by state , as do registration charges on home loans . Depending on the state, these amounts can materially increase your home loan’s total cost . State-wise loan fees generally range from 4% to 8% of the total property value, and registration charges sometimes add around 1%. Additionally, some states may offer lower rates for women buyers or affordable housing segments. It’s important to note that most lenders do not finance these charges, so buyers must pay them out of pocket. Processing Fee Waiver Offers from Top Banks In many circumstances, financial institutions may roll out home loan fee waivers . Top banks offer loan waivers or bank processing fee offers in order to attract new borrowers. This is especially true during festive seasons or special campaigns. These waived loan charges could include zero processing fees or capped charges for specific borrower categories, such as first-time buyers or women applicants. It’s important to remember that while such waivers reduce upfront costs, borrowers should assess the complete loan package and long-term costs. A fee waiver is beneficial only if the overall cost of borrowing remains competitive. Impact of GST on Home Loan Processing Fees Lenders must charge GST on home loan fees . The current home loan processing GST is 18%. While the loan fee tax impact won’t affect the principal loan amount, it will increase your upfront costs. For instance, a processing fee of ₹10,000 attracts an additional ₹1,800 as GST. Since the GST effect on processing charges is mandatory and non-negotiable, you must factor it into your initial cash outflow when estimating the total cost of availing a home loan. Home loan processing fees are usually non-refundable. Even if the application is rejected, they will cover verification and administrative costs. Home loan processing fee refunds may apply under specific, documented promotional offers. Can I negotiate the processing fee with my bank? Usually, processing charges for home loans are non-negotiable. However, sometimes, they may be negotiable if you have a strong credit score, an existing relationship with the lender, or competing offers. How does the processing fee differ for salaried vs self-employed applicants? Mortgage loan processing fees may vary based on the borrower's profile. For example, salaried applicants often pay lower rates because their income is stable, while self-employed borrowers face higher fees. Are home loan processing fees taxable under income tax? Under Section 80C, home loan processing fees, principal repayment, and stamp duty are deductible up to ₹1.5 lakh. This is subject to a five-year holding period. What is the average processing fee percentage across Indian banks? In India, what is the processing fee for home loans varies by lender. This amount usually ranges from 0.25% to 3%, depending on loan type and customer profile. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Many homebuyers focus only on one thing when taking a home loan – the interest rate. But the interest rate is not the only cost you pay. In reality, a home loan often comes with several hidden charges that you may not notice at first. These extra costs can appear at different stages of the loan process. Some are charged at the loan approval stage, while others may be applied later during repayment or loan closure. If you are not aware of these home loan extra charges, they can increase the overall cost of your home loan. Understanding these charges in advance can help you plan better and avoid unpleasant surprises later. In this blog, we will look at the hidden charges in home loans that every borrower should know before signing the loan agreement. What are the hidden charges in a home loan? When you apply for a home loan , the lender levies certain extra charges apart from the interest rate. These charges are often referred to as hidden charges in home loans. They may include processing fees, legal charges, documentation costs, valuation charges, and administrative fees. Hidden fees in home loans are collected at various stages of the loan process. For example, legal and valuation charges are levied even before loan approval, during the property valuation. In contrast, the processing fee is levied at the time of disbursal. Understanding what the hidden charges in a home loan are can help you estimate the true cost of borrowing and avoid surprises later. Why is it important to understand home loan charges before applying? As a borrower, it’s crucial to understand the hidden costs of a mortgage when applying for a home loan. These charges may increase your overall borrowing costs and affect long-term affordability. They can even disrupt your entire financial planning. To understand the hidden fees in home loans, you can review the loan documents and read the fine print carefully. Do not hesitate to ask your lender to explain anything that is unclear. Instead of going with the lender offering the lowest interest rate, it is better to opt for the one that levies the fewest hidden charges. Explained below are the various home loan extra charges one by one: Processing fees and applicable GST A processing fee is one of the most common hidden charges in home loans. The lender levies this fee to cover the cost of reviewing your application, checking documents, and assessing your eligibility. Most lenders charge a small percentage of the loan amount as processing fees. This percentage may range between 0.5% to 2%. Some lenders may charge a flat fee as a home loan processing fee . Additionally, a Goods and Services Tax (GST) is levied on the processing fee. Property valuation, legal, and technical charges Lenders need to conduct several checks related to the property before approving a home loan application. These checks include valuation, legal verification, and technical inspection of the property. For these, the lender may need to take the help of professional experts. To cover the fees of these experts, the lender collects property valuation, legal, and technical charges from the borrower. In most cases, the lender collects these charges as a flat fee at the home loan application stage. Although the charge may not be very high, it still adds to the total cost of the loan. Stamp duty and registration expenses When you buy a property, you must pay stamp duty and registration charges to the government. These charges are required to legally register the property in your name. They are paid at the time of property registration. The exact amount depends on the state where the property is located and the property value. Although you do not pay these charges to the lender, they are still considered part of the hidden costs of a mortgage because they increase the total cost of buying a home. Prepayment and foreclosure charges When you decide to repay a part of your home loan during its tenure, it is known as home loan prepayment . It helps in reducing the outstanding principal amount. And thus, it results in lower EMIs and interest outgo. If you choose to close your loan account by paying the total outstanding balance , this is known as loan foreclosure. Most lenders charge a fee for early repayment, known as the prepayment and foreclosure charge. This charge is levied as a fixed percentage of the outstanding home loan balance at the time of prepayment. Late EMI penalty and bounce charges You must pay your home loan EMIs on the scheduled date every month. If the EMI payment is delayed, the lender may charge a late payment penalty. It is usually a small percentage of the overdue amount. In some cases, it is charged as a flat fee. If the EMI fails due to insufficient funds in the bank account, an EMI bounce charge may also be levied. Over time, these penalties can significantly increase your home loan cost. Repeated instances of missed or delayed EMI payments may also affect your credit score. Memorandum of Deposit of Title (MODT) deed charges When a homebuyer avails of a home loan, they are required to deposit the property’s title deed as collateral with the lender. In many states, a document called the Memorandum of Deposit of Title Deed (MODT) is created to record this transaction. Registering this document may require paying certain charges. The exact cost depends on the state rules and the loan amount. Most home loan borrowers are unaware of these mortgage hidden fees. Administrative, documentation, and statement charges Some lenders levy several nominal charges to cover administrative costs. These can include documentation charges, loan agreement copy charges, and account statement fees. Usually, such charges are not levied by default. Instead, they are charged as an extra fee when you request certain services, such as the issuance of a duplicate loan agreement copy, physical loan account statements, etc. These are usually small amounts, ranging between Rs. 50 to Rs. 500 in most cases. Charges for loan modification or tenure change Sometimes, home loan borrowers may want to make changes to their loan terms during the loan tenure. For example, they may request a change in loan tenure or the applicable interest rate. Lenders usually charge a nominal loan modification fee to facilitate such changes. This fee is levied only if the borrower submits an application for a modification in the original loan terms. The authority of whether or not to accept the loan modification request lies solely with the lender. Recovery and legal action charges in the case of default If a borrower defaults on their home loan or stops paying EMIs for an extended period, the lender may initiate the recovery process. This may include sending legal notices or starting legal proceedings against the borrower to recover the loan amount. For this, the lender may have to make payments to attorneys and recovery agents. Even in such cases, the lender collects the incurred expenses from the borrower. The recovery and legal action charges are added to the total outstanding dues. Checklist: What to review before signing the home loan agreement? Before signing a home loan agreement, it is important to carefully review all the terms and conditions mentioned in the document. Doing so can help you avoid unexpected hidden charges in home loan agreements later. Look out for these clauses specifically: Fee schedule: Check the complete list of charges, including processing fees, verification fees, and other home loan extra charges. Penalty clauses: Look for details about late EMI penalties, bounce charges, and foreclosure conditions. GST impact: Confirm whether the GST is applicable to different fees. It can increase the total payable amount. Written confirmation: Ask the lender for a written breakdown of all hidden fees in the home loan terms before signing the agreement. Commonly overlooked home loan charges Apart from the home loan hidden charges already mentioned in the blog post, there are several other minor costs that borrowers often overlook. These may include loan conversion charges, loan cancellation charges, loan revalidation charges, duplicate amortization schedule fees, and fees for issuing a No Objection Certificate (NOC) upon loan closure. Individually, these costs may appear small. But together, they can increase the overall borrowing cost. That is why it’s essential to read the loan agreement thoroughly and understand all potential hidden charges before signing. Remember, awareness helps avoid surprises. Summary – Know the true cost of your home loan A home loan can help you buy the house of your dreams and pay for it in EMIs over a convenient tenure. But before you apply for a home loan, it’s crucial to understand all hidden charges and fees. Apart from the interest rate, charges such as processing fees, property valuation fees, legal fees, stamp duty, and documentation costs can escalate your total borrowing cost. You can find these charges in the loan agreement or fine print. Besides, you must compare home loan offers from several lenders, check the applicable interest rate and fee structure, and seek clarifications from the lender wherever required. Doing so may help you avoid surprises and make a well-informed borrowing decision. Say Hello to Your New Home with Our Easy Home Loans! Common hidden charges in home loans include processing fees, property valuation charges, legal verification fees, and documentation costs. Borrowers may also pay stamp duty, MODT charges, or administrative fees. Some lenders may also charge penalties for late EMI payments or early loan closure. Are processing fees refundable if the loan is not approved? In most cases, processing fees are non-refundable, even if the loan is not approved. Lenders charge this fee to review the application, check documents, and verify details. However, policies may vary between lenders. So, it is always better to confirm the terms before applying. What is MODT, and why is it charged in a home loan? MODT stands for Memorandum of Deposits of Title Deed. It is a legal document that proves the borrower has deposited the original property papers with the lender as collateral for a home loan. To cover the cost of registering this document, lenders charge an MODT fee on home loans. Do banks charge penalties for home loan prepayment or foreclosure? When a borrower decides to repay a portion of the home loan, it is known as prepayment or foreclosure. Some banks may charge penalties for prepayment on a home loan or for foreclosure. It’s because they lose out on the interest income. It is always advisable to check the loan agreement for specific terms. Are legal and technical verification charges mandatory? Yes, legal and technical verification charges are usually required during the home loan process. The lender uses these checks to confirm that the property documents are valid and the construction is acceptable. These charges are generally collected during the loan approval stage as part of the verification process. What happens if I miss a home loan EMI payment? If you miss your home loan EMI payment, your lender may charge a late payment penalty or penal interest on the overdue amount. If the EMI payment fails due to insufficient funds in your bank account, a bounce charge may also apply. Repeated delays can affect your credit score and impact your chances of getting another loan in the future. How can I avoid hidden charges while applying for a home loan? Are you confused with questions like what is a sale deed, why do you need a sale deed, what is the sale deed of a property, what is the sale deed of a flat, etc.? Well, buying a house isn’t easy and requires you to carefully go through a lot of important paperwork. One such essential document is the property sale deed. When you’re applying for a home loan, you have to submit the property sale deed, among other relevant documents, to the lender. The lender will have possession of the deed throughout the loan duration. What is a sale deed? If you’re new to real estate investments, you’d probably be wondering about sale deed’s meaning. A property sale deed is a legal document that serves as evidence of the transfer of property ownership from the seller to the buyer. The transfer is legally complete only after both parties sign the sale deed. When talking about what is a sale deed, many people confuse it with an agreement of sale. However, both these documents are different. While a sale deed is evidence of transferring ownership of the property, an agreement of sale indicates the contract between the buyer and seller to transfer property ownership in the future. A sale deed includes all details of the transaction, like – Details of the buyer and seller Details of the property Financial details and mode of payment Details of property possession Indemnity clause, etc. Benefits of a sale deed A sale deed is an important legal document when buying a house. To further understand what a sale deed document is, let’s look at some of its benefits. It protects the interests of the parties involved and guards them against legal disputes It helps the buyer get all relevant details of the property, like its location, construction area, etc. It is a legally enforceable document that recognizes the property transaction It serves as legal evidence in case of a property dispute What is a sale deed in a home loan? When you buy a house, it is important to understand what the sale deed of a property is, or what is the sale deed of a flat. You get legal ownership of the house only after you and the seller sign the property sale deed. The lender will keep the original document until the repayment of the loan and will return it within 15 days of repayment. Documents required for a sale deed If you’re wondering what the sale deed documentation requirement is, here is a list to get you sorted: The extract General power of attorney Copy of the building plan No objection certificates Allotment letter Agreement of sale Possession letter Receipt of payment Receipt of property tax Encumbrance certificate Completion certificate Occupancy certificate What is the sale deed registration process? Now that you know sale deed’s meaning and the required documents, let’s understand what the sale deed registration process is. To register for the sale deed, you can either visit the office of the sub-registrar or book an appointment online. The parties involved in the transaction will have to visit the facilitation centre for document verification. After all formalities are done, the sub-registrar will inspect the documents for any discrepancies. Once the sub-registrar accepts the documents and you complete all required formalities, you will receive a receipt. You can obtain the sale deed from the sub registrar’s office within 15 days of the process. Things to consider while registering for the sale deed Here are a few things you must keep in mind while registering: The property must be free from financial or legal liabilities Make sure you obtain a non-encumbrance certificate to ensure the property is not under any liabilities. You will also have to produce this document while applying for a home loan . The seller must complete all payments before transferring the ownership Before registering for the sales deed, make sure there are no outstanding payments for the property, like electricity bills, water bills, maintenance expenses, property tax, etc. The seller must complete all payments before transferring the ownership of the property. You must also understand what the sale deed of a property is and what is the sale deed of a flat, along with the documents required for each. Difference between a sale deed and an agreement of sale Most homebuyers confuse a sale deed with a sale agreement. However, it is vital to learn the difference between the two. Both documents are indispensable yet serve distinct purposes. The following pointers will help you learn the difference between a sale deed vs agreement of sale: A sale agreement reflects the terms of the asset’s sale. It is a basic document and does not legally confirm the transfer of ownership. A sale deed legally records the transfer of the property’s possession. You will need it while applying for a home loan. Legal importance of a sale deed in property transactions The legal importance of a sale deed is crucial. It serves as proof of property ownership. So, if there is any dispute related to the ownership of a property, a sale deed can help with the resolution. However, a sale deed is considered legally binding only after registration. Registration involves recording the deed at the local sub-registrar’s office. The sale deed’s significance is more for the buyer as it is conclusive evidence of ownership. It comprises details about the current and past owners and any legal encumbrances. You must check the information on the sale deed to avoid potential legal complications. Also,Read- Home Loan from Bank vs NBFC: Which is better? Common mistakes to avoid when registering a sale deed Registering a sale deed is necessary. However, many individuals make errors in the sale deed registration, which can lead to legal or financial complications in the future. All property details mentioned in the sale deed must be accurate and should match the official records. Moreover, you must never underpay stamp duty, as it can attract penalties. One of the other sale deed registration mistakes you must avoid is signing documents without reading every clause carefully. If a clause doesn’t suit your interest, you must negotiate it or get it rectified. You must also ensure that all parties and witnesses are present during registration. How does a sale deed ensure risk mitigation for home loan buyers? A sale deed legally establishes property ownership. It confirms that the seller has transferred all rights, title, and interest to the buyer. As a result, your risks are mitigated as you have proof of ownership. You must also recognize the sale deed’s importance for a home loan. When you apply for the loan, you must submit the registered document for banks to verify a clear title. Lenders also need to check that the property details are accurate and all legal requirements are fulfilled. A registered sale deed is part of the public property records and safeguards the borrower and the lender from legal and financial risks in the future. How does a sale deed affect home loan approval? A sale deed is crucial for home loan approval because it proves legal ownership of the property. Lenders review the registered sale deed to ensure the seller has a clear title. Your loan will not be approved if the transaction isn’t legal. What is the step-by-step process for sale deed registration? The process for sale deed registration includes the following steps: Drafting the sale deed Paying stamp duty and registration charges Scheduling an appointment at the sub-registrar’s office Signing of the deed by the buyer and seller in the presence of witnesses Completing biometric verification and registration Can the sale deed be transferred if the home loan is still active? No, it isn’t easy to transfer the sale deed if the home loan is still active. You need to have the lender’s consent. The property is mortgaged; thus, you must either close the loan or formally transfer it. You also need the bank’s no-objection certificate. What happens if the sale deed is not registered? If a sale deed is not registered, the property transfer is not legally valid. You may not get legal ownership rights, face difficulties in selling or mortgaging the property, and encounter issues during disputes or loan applications. How to verify the authenticity of a sale deed? You can verify a sale deed’s authenticity by checking its registration details at the local sub-registrar’s office. You can also go through the online land records portal. Make sure you check the stamp duty payment, signatures, property details, and chain of ownership to ensure the deed is genuine. What role does the sale deed number play in property ownership? The sale deed number is a unique registration reference that helps identify the property transaction in government records. It is essential for tracking ownership history, verifying documents, applying for loans, and resolving legal or property-related disputes. or collateral. The difference between secured and unsecured loans lies in the applicable interest rates, loan limits, processing speeds, and eligibility criteria. While unsecured loans offer quick and flexible access to funds, they usually come with higher interest rates and lower borrowing limits than secured loans. Comparing lenders can help you make a better financial decision. An unsecured loan is a loan that is approved without collateral and is granted based on the borrower’s creditworthiness, income, and repayment capacity. Rohit wanted to expand his small business and needed additional funds. He approached a few lenders, but there was one problem. He did not own a property, vehicle, or any other asset that he could offer as collateral. Just when he thought borrowing money would be difficult, a friend told him about unsecured loans. The idea seemed surprising at first. How could a lender approve a loan without any security? But when Rohit applied and received approval, he realized that such loans do exist. If you are also wondering what an unsecured loan is, you are at the right place. In this guide, we have explained the unsecured loan meaning, how unsecured loans work, their common types, examples, eligibility criteria, interest rates, and more. We have also explained the differences between secured and unsecured loans to help you make a better choice. Keep reading. What is an unsecured loan? The unsecured loan meaning is quite simple. It refers to a loan that does not require any collateral or security. In other words, you do not have to pledge your house, car, gold, investments, or any other assets to qualify for financing. Instead, the lender approves your loan application based on your income, credit score , employment stability, and existing financial obligations , among other factors. This is different from a secured loan, which is usually backed by an asset or collateral. For example, a home loan is secured by the property being purchased. Similarly, a gold loan is backed by gold jewelry. Some common features of unsecured loans include: No collateral is required. Approval is based on factors such as credit score and income. Processing and disbursal are generally quick. Loans can be used for multiple purposes. Loan amounts are usually smaller than secured loans. Repayment tenures are typically shorter. The interest rates are generally higher. How does an unsecured loan work? Unsecured loans work differently from secured loans. Since no collateral is involved, lenders focus on the borrower’s credit and financial profile before approving loan applications. They carefully review factors such as CIBIL score , income, employment stability, existing loans, and repayment history, based on the documents and information submitted by the borrower. If the lender is satisfied with the borrower’s creditworthiness, the loan is sanctioned. Since the risk is higher due to the lack of collateral, interest rates on unsecured loans are generally higher than those on secured loans. Once the loan is disbursed, the borrower begins the repayment through Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs) . In the case of a default, the lender may initiate recovery proceedings as permitted by the law. However, unlike secured loans, there are no specific assets that can be automatically seized. Secured vs unsecured loans: What are the differences? As mentioned, the basic difference between secured and unsecured loans is the involvement of collateral. Apart from this, they also differ in factors such as applicable interest rates, loan amount or limit, approval speed, and eligibility criteria. The table below depicts a detailed comparison of secured vs unsecured loans: Basis Secured Loans Unsecured Loans Collateral Backed by collateral, which can be a house, car, gold, etc. No collateral or asset is required. Interest Rate Usually lower because the lender has security. Higher than secured loans because of greater risk. Loan Amount/Limit Depends on the collateral’s market value. Determined by the lender based on the borrower’s credit profile. Approval Speed May take time due to asset valuation. Processed faster because no asset valuation is required. Eligibility Criteria Lenient; based on the collateral’s value and the borrower’s profile. Strict; based on the borrower’s income, CIBIL score, and the overall financial profile. Risk for the Lender Low High Examples Secured loans’ examples include home loans, auto loans , and gold loans. Unsecured loans’ examples include personal loans, education loans, etc. What are the different types of unsecured loans? Lending institutions in India offer several types of unsecured loans. While their purpose and features may vary, they all have one thing in common: they do not require collateral. Here is the list of unsecured loans commonly available in India: Personal loans : These are multipurpose loans that can be used for various personal and business needs. Credit cards : A revolving line of credit that allows you to make purchases and pay later. Many credit cards even offer EMI facilities. Education loans : These loans allow you to fund your higher education expenses. Several lenders offer unsecured education loans up to a specific limit. Consumer durable loans: These are short-term loans used specifically to purchase products like smartphones, laptops, refrigerators, televisions, and other large appliances. Business loans : These loans are given exclusively to self-employed borrowers to help them manage working capital needs and cash flow gaps. What are the eligibility criteria for unsecured loans? Since unsecured loans are not backed by collateral, lenders closely review the borrower’s financial profile before approving an application. The stronger your profile, the better your chances of getting approved and securing a favorable interest rate. While the exact requirements vary from one lender to another, the common eligibility criteria include: A good CIBIL score : A healthy CIBIL score (preferably above 700) is one of the most basic requirements to qualify for an unsecured loan. It can also help you get a lower interest rate. Stable income : You must have a stable and sufficient income from a fixed source. Both self-employed and salaried individuals can apply. Work experience : Some lenders may need a minimum period of work experience or business vintage. The exact criterion may vary, but can range from 2 to 4 years. Age band : Most lenders have minimum and maximum age limits for borrowers. The most typical age band is between 18 and 65 years. Residency : You must be an Indian resident with a valid identity and address proof. How much can you borrow? Unsecured loan limit The amount you can borrow through an unsecured loan depends mainly on your income, CIBIL score, existing financial obligations, and the lender’s internal policy. Since there is no collateral involved, lenders are generally more cautious when deciding the loan amount. As a result, the unsecured loan limit is usually lower than what the same borrower may qualify for under a secured loan. Depending on the lender and loan type , unsecured loan amounts can range from a few thousand rupees to several lakhs. However, the actual limit varies from one lender to another. What are the interest rates on unsecured loans? Interest rates on unsecured loans are usually higher than those on secured loans because the lender has no collateral. The rate offered depends largely on the borrower’s credit score, income, repayment history, and overall financial profile. Borrowers with strong credit profiles often qualify for lower rates. While comparing loan offers, it is advisable to look beyond the headline interest rate and check the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) , as it reflects the overall cost of borrowing. How to apply for an unsecured loan online? Several banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) in India allow you to apply for an unsecured loan online from the comforts of your home/office. Here are a few basic steps you need to follow: Check whether you meet the lender’s eligibility criteria for an unsecured loan. Fill out an online loan application form on the lender’s website. Upload the required documents. These may include KYC documents, proof of income, and proof of employment. Wait for the lender to verify the details and the documents submitted. Accept the terms and conditions to receive disbursal in your bank account. What are the advantages and disadvantages of unsecured loans? Unsecured loans have both pros and cons. Comparing them can help you make a better financial decision: Pros : You do not need to pledge your valuable assets as collateral. Loans are often processed and disbursed quickly. There are different types of unsecured loans for different financial needs. Your personal assets are not at risk of being seized by the lender. Cons: Interest rates are usually higher than those of secured loans. The approved loan limit is also lower in most cases. A good CIBIL score is strictly required to qualify for the loan. Borrowers with weak credit profiles may face higher interest rates or limited loan options. Conclusion Unsecured loans offer quick and flexible access to funds without requiring collateral. This makes them suitable for a variety of personal and business purposes. However, they usually come with higher interest rates and depend heavily on your credit profile. Before applying, make sure the EMI fits comfortably within your repayment capacity. It is also a good idea to compare multiple options and read the terms and conditions carefully before making a decision. Get an Instant Personal Loan for all your needs ! loan you can get. Lenders assess several factors, including your monthly income, existing EMIs, credit score, employment stability, and repayment capacity, before deciding on the loan amount. While a lower salary may reduce the eligible loan amount, maintaining a good credit history and stable income can improve your chances of approval. Understanding these factors can help you estimate your borrowing capacity and apply for a loan that fits your financial situation. Personal Loan on ₹15000 Salary Borrowers from various salary brackets have routinely accepted personal loans. The qualifying conditions are simplified with a minimum wage slab so that all those with modest incomes can benefit from personal loans . The confirmation of monthly salary is done primarily to assess the applicant’s ability to repay. Borrowers with a salary of Rs. 15,000 can readily obtain modest cash loans starting from Rs. 50,000 – Rs. 1,50,000, depending on the vendor. When split down into EMIs, this is simple to repay. The loan amount, however, might differ from bank to bank. Calculate your personal loan EMI here. Expected Loan Amount & Interest Rates The loan amount you may qualify for on a ₹15,000 monthly salary depends on your repayment capacity, existing financial obligations, credit score , and the lender’s eligibility criteria. While eligibility varies, lenders generally assess whether the EMI fits comfortably within your monthly income before approving the loan. Interest rates also differ based on your credit profile, employment stability, and loan tenure , making it important to compare lenders before applying. How to Get a Personal Loan on a Rs. 15000 Salary To request a personal loan for a minimum salary of 15000, customers must first complete the following steps: Examine the Eligibility Conditions : Check the lender’s eligibility conditions and utilize the personal loan on Rs 15000 salary eligibility tools. Determine the Interest Rate & Other Charges : Customers will be charged interest on their loan based on their wage, loan amount, loan period, credit history, and other criteria. They must additionally pay a registration fee in order to acquire the loan. Gather the Required Documents : Customers must provide all of the bank’s required paperwork for the loan to be approved. Complete the Application Form : Users must go to the lender’s webpage to finish the loan request form. To complete the loan request form, users must provide personal information such as their name, email address, contact information, loan amount, and so on. Features and Benefits of an Instant Personal Loan for Rs. 15000 Salary An instant personal loan can help salaried individuals manage planned and unexpected expenses without lengthy paperwork. 1. Core Features Collateral-Free: No assets or securities are required to apply for the loan. Flexible Tenure: Choose a repayment tenure that suits your budget and repayment capacity. Digital Documentation: Complete the application and document submission process online with minimal paperwork. Instant Disbursal: Eligible applicants may receive loan approval and disbursal quickly, subject to verification. 2. Key Benefits Emergency Assistance: Access funds for urgent expenses such as medical emergencies, repairs, or other unforeseen needs. End-Use Freedom: Use the loan for education, travel, home improvement, debt consolidation, or other personal requirements. Credit Score Improvement: Timely EMI payments can help build and maintain a healthy credit score. Is ₹50,000 personal loan secured or unsecured? A ₹50,000 personal loan is unsecured, meaning you don't need to pledge any asset or property against it. Lenders instead rely on your credit score, income, and repayment history to decide approval; even a 50000 loan urgent without CIBIL score consideration is possible with some lenders, though it may come with a higher interest rate. What is the interest rate for a ₹50,000 loan? Interest rates on a personal loan up to 50000 vary by lender, generally in the 9-15% per annum range, though at Tata Capital rates start from 10.99% per annum. Your final rate depends on your credit score, income, and repayment capacity, so it's worth comparing a couple of lenders before applying. How quickly can I get a ₹50,000 loan? Most digital lenders, Tata Capital included, can disburse a ₹50,000 loan within a few hours of approval, sometimes the same day. It helps to understand how personal loan disbursement works beforehand, since the exact timeline depends on how quickly your KYC and income documents get verified. Can I prepay a ₹50,000 loan early? Yes, most lenders allow you to prepay or foreclose a ₹50,000 loan without much hassle, though it's worth checking if any prepayment charges apply, especially within the first few months. Clearing it early, when you can afford to, usually saves you on the total interest paid. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund If you’re hesitating to plan that long-awaited family holiday, renovate your house or are stressing about how you will meet your medical expenditure, it’s time to take a sigh of relief. Because there is a way, you can do all that without dipping into your savings. State Bank of India (SBI) offers the Xpress credit loan scheme. This scheme allows you to take out a loan for any big-ticket purchase and keep your savings away for a rainy day. Whatever your need, this personal loan can help you with it. And so, here we’ll discuss everything you need to know about this government personal loan scheme. Let’s begin! Understanding the Meaning of Xpress Credit Loan Xpress Credit Loan is a personal loan scheme offered by the State Bank of India for salaried individuals, including government employees. Under this scheme, salaried individuals can get instant loans to meet their financial needs. Loans ranging from Rs 25,000 to Rs 20 Lakh, and up to Rs 35 Lakh in some cases, can be availed under this scheme, with loan tenures of six months to six years. Xpress Credit Loan, meaning SBI’s quick, paperless personal loan specifically designed for salaried individuals, has features like attractive interest rates, minimal documentation and low processing fees. The application process is easy and fully digitised, ensuring quick sanction and disbursement of funds. Eligibility Criteria The Xpress credit loan can be applied for by individuals meeting the following eligibility criteria: Individuals with an SBI salary account and a minimum salary of Rs 15,000 Individuals working with central, state, quasi-government, public sector undertakings (PSUs), reputed educational institutions, and selected corporates. Individuals with an EMI/NMI ratio of less than 50% Also, read – Top Government Schemes for Startups and MSMEs in India How to apply If you meet the eligibility criteria, the next step is filling up the application form. You can download this from SBI’s official website or collect it from your nearest SBI bank branch. The application form requires details like name, age, address, income, work profile and the like. Ensure all details are correct and legibly written to get your loan application approved quickly. To benefit from this govt. personal loan scheme, you will need to accompany your application form with the required documents. Salaried employees need to submit the following documents with the application form: Passport-size photographs As proof of identity- Aadhaar card, PAN card, driving licence, voter identity card, passport As proof of income- bank account statement, salary slips, ITR, Form 16 As proof of address- Aadhaar card, ration card, passport, bank account statement, driving licence, electricity bill, telephone bill, sales deed/ property purchase agreement Letter of authority addressed to disbursing authority Copy of identity card issued by the employer organisation Letter of authority from the authority responsible for disbursing salary Individuals with a Defence Salary Package (DSP), Paramilitary Salary Package (PMSP) and Indian Coast Guard Salary Package (ICGSP) the following documents are to be submitted: Passport-size photographs AS proof of identity- Aadhaar card, PAN card, voter identity card, driving licence As proof of address- passport, telephone bill, voter identity card, electricity bills Copy of salary slip for the preceding six months Bank statement for the preceding six months for the account where the salary has been credited. Also, read – Government Schemes for Women Entrepreneurs in India Documents Required for Xpress Credit Loan For the Xpress Credit loan, a person needs to submit a set of documents that generally include identity proof, address proof, income proof, and other verification documents, along with an application form. In case of salaried employees, the Xpress Credit Loan documents required are: Proof of identity Proof of address Latest salary slips (at least 3 months) Bank account statement showing salary credit Copy of ID card issued by employer Proof of income: Form 16, recent Income Tax Returns (ITR) Letter of authority (where applicable, as per employer/organisation norms) Additional documents required in case of individuals with special salary packages (DSP, PMSP, ICGSP) are salary slips for last 6 months and bank statement of account where salary is credited for the same duration. This is a slightly altered set with emphasis on longer salary/bank statement histories. Xpress Credit Loan Interest Rates and Tenure The Xpress credit loan tenure ranges from six months to six years (or until retirement, whichever is earlier). The Xpress Credit Loan interest rates vary based on your employment category. Look at the table below for a better understanding. Applicant Category Interest Rate (p.a.) Maximum Loan Amount Defense and Central Armed Police 11.15% – 12.65% Up to Rs 35 lakh Central/State Govt and PSU 11.55% – 14.05% Up to Rs 20 lakh Corporate Salaried 12.55% – 14.55% Up to Rs 20 lakh Additional charges When applying for an Xpress credit loan, certain additional fees are also levied by SBI. These are as follows. Processing fees SBI charges 1% of the loan amount and the applicable service tax as a processing fee under the instant credit scheme. Penal interest There is no penal interest for loans amounting to Rs 25,000 and below. However, for loan amounts more than Rs 25,000, individuals will be charged a penal interest where the discrepancy exceeds the EMI amount and for more than a month. The penal interest will be 2% p.a., in addition to the interest rate charged for the loan. However, the penal interest will not be levied where a portion of the instalment or EMI remains overdue. Foreclosure charges In case the borrower wants to close the account before the term ends, they will have to pay 3% as repayment charges. It will be charged on the prepaid, irrespective of whether the borrower repays the EMI in part or complete before the end of the term. However, this charge can be avoided if the borrower uses the proceeds of a new loan granted under this scheme. Comparing Xpress Credit with Other Personal Loan Options Since borrowers often evaluate multiple lenders before applying for a personal loan , here’s a side-by-side comparison of Xpress Credit loan vs personal loan alternatives for better clarity: Feature SBI Xpress Credit HDFC Bank Personal Loan Tata Capital Personal Loan Interest Rate 11.15% to 14.55% (depending on employment type) 10.85% to 24% 10.99% to 29.99% p.a Loan Amount Range Rs 25,000 to Rs 20 lakh Rs 50,000 to Rs 40 lakh Rs 40,000 to Rs 35 lakh Loan Tenure / Repayment Period 6 months to 72 months 12 to 60 months 12 to 72 months Processing Fee / Charges 1% of the loan amount + taxes. Up to Rs 6,500 + GST Up to 3.5% of loan amount + GST Pre-closure / Foreclosure Penalty 3% of prepaid amount (varies by category) 2% to 4% of outstanding principal (after first 12 EMIs) Part Prepayment : No charge up to 25% disproportioned principal; 6.5% (first 12 months), 4.5% (after) Foreclosure : 6.5% (within 12 months), 4.5% (after 12 months) Managing Your Xpress Credit Loan Effectively: Tips and Best Practices Learning how to manage Xpress Credit loan can seem overwhelming at first, but with better financial planning it can become easier. Some practical ways in which you can avoid Xpress Credit loan mistakes are: Affordable repayment : Choose a tenure that keeps monthly payments affordable and set up automatic debits to avoid missed instalments. Regular review of loan statements: Keep a track of the repayment on SBI’s digital platforms to check progress or spot any discrepancies. Part-payments: When you have surplus income, use it to make part-payments which will help to reduce interest and shorten the loan term. However, keep in mind the prepayment charges applicable. Keep an emergency fund: It can be used to cover a few EMIs in case of financial uncertainty. Avoid taking on multiple loans: Multiple loans at once can strain your budget. To sum up The Xpress credit loan’s meaning is an instant loan to meet your financial needs immediately. By following the application procedure and submitting the required documents, you can receive your personal loans within days. Xpress credit loan is a personal loan that SBI offers to eligible salaried customers maintaining a salary account with the bank. It involves quick approval, minimal paperwork, attractive interest rates and flexible repayment options. Who is eligible for Xpress Credit Loan? Eligibility criteria for Xpress Credit Loan mainly includes salaried individuals with a minimum salary of Rs 15000, having a regular salary account in SBI. This covers Central and State Government employees, defence personnel, PSU staff, and corporate employees. Applicants must also have an EMI/NMI ratio less than 50%. What are the typical interest rates for Xpress Credit Loan? Interest rates generally fall within a competitive range and vary by employer category, income, and credit profile. Government and PSU employees usually receive more favourable rates, while corporate salaried individuals may be charged slightly higher. Can I apply for Xpress Credit Loan online? Yes. Eligible customers can apply through SBI’s YONO app, net banking portal, or the bank’s official website. The online process is quick, paper-light, and allows instant eligibility checks, making it convenient for existing salary account holders. What documents are required for Xpress Credit Loan application? The applicants can download the application form from SBI’s official website and attach the required documents, which usually include identity proof, address proof, recent salary slips, bank statements, and employment details. Is Xpress Credit Loan a government scheme? Xpress Credit Loan is a personal loan product offered by the State Bank of India to its eligible salaried customers. However, government employees are offered better interest rates. How does Xpress Credit Loan work? SBI evaluates your salary account and creditworthiness, sanctions the loan, and disburses the amount. You repay through monthly EMIs over 6 months to 6 years. What is the maximum loan amount and tenure for Xpress Credit Loan? The maximum loan amount for an Xpress credit loan is Rs 20 Lakh, and the maximum tenure is 6 years. What are the key benefits of Xpress Credit Loan for government employees? Xpress Credit Loan is extremely beneficial for government employees, as it offers personal loans at more favourable interest rates, given the stability of their income, without the need for security or a guarantor. What are the charges involved in Xpress Credit Loan? The charges involved in Xpress Credit loan are: Processing fee: 1% of the loan amount + GST. Penal interest: 2% per month on overdue amount. Foreclosure: 3% on the prepaid amount. You are typically allowed to borrow between 75% and 95% of your investment value, depending on the lender’s policy. The loan can be taken for different purposes and usually comes with lower interest rates compared to unsecured personal loans. A loan against fixed deposit is a loan you can take by pledging your fixed deposit with the lender while allowing your investment to continue earning interest throughout the tenure. If you have ever wondered, “Can I take a loan against my fixed deposit?”, the answer is yes. A loan against fixed deposit allows you to access funds in times of need without breaking your investment. This guide explains what a loan against a fixed deposit is, how it works, the loan against fixed deposit interest rate, the loan amount you can get, its benefits and disadvantages, and the different types of loans you can avail of against your fixed deposit. What is a loan against fixed deposit and how does it work? A loan against fixed deposit is a secured loan where your fixed deposit acts as collateral with the lender. Instead of breaking your fixed deposit, you pledge it to borrow some percentage of the deposit value. The lender places a lien on your fixed deposit until you repay the outstanding loan amount, while your investment continues to earn interest as per its original terms. You can repay the loan through Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs) or by using the overdraft facility , if available. Once done, the lien is lifted, and you regain full access to your fixed deposit. Learn More – Loan Against Securities What is the loan against fixed deposit interest rate? The loan against fixed deposit interest rate is generally lower than the interest rate charged by unsecured personal loans because your fixed deposit serves as collateral. Most lenders typically charge an interest rate that is 1% to 2% higher than your fixed deposit interest rate, although the exact rate varies across lenders and the type of fixed deposit. For instance, if your fixed deposit earns 5% interest per annum, you can typically obtain a loan at 6% to 7% per annum. Check – Loan Against Securities Interest Rates & Charges Loan amount against fixed deposit: How much can you get? If you are wondering, “ Can I take a loan against my fixed deposit,and how much can I get? “, the loan amount typically depends on the value of your fixed deposit and the lender’s policy. Most banks and financial institutions offer 75% to 90% of the fixed deposit value as the loan amount. Some lenders may also sanction up to 95%, depending on their Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio. These figures are indicative and vary across lenders. However, the loan amount cannot exceed the value of your fixed deposit in any case. What are the benefits of a loan against fixed deposit? A loan against fixed deposit offers several benefits, such as: Lower interest rates compared to unsecured loans. No need to break your investment to access funds. Continued interest earnings on your fixed deposit until it matures. Quick approval and disbursal with minimal documentation and relaxed eligibility criteria. Flexible end use, as the funds can be used for almost any purpose, unlike a car or home loan. Can you take different types of loans against a fixed deposit? Yes. Fixed deposits can help you access different types of loans. However, not every fixed deposit qualifies as collateral. Some common loan options and exclusions include: Personal loan against fixed deposit Education loan against fixed deposit Car loan against fixed deposit Home loan against fixed deposit: Suitable for smaller funding needs. For larger home purchases, a traditional home loan such as Tata Capital Home Loan may be a better option. Loan against tax saver fixed deposit: Not permitted, as tax-saving fixed deposits have a mandatory five-year lock-in period and cannot be pledged as collateral. Learn More – Documents Required for Loan Against Securities Loan against fixed deposit vs personal loan: Which is better? The better choice depends on individual needs.
