Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A question that often occurs in the minds of Indian citizens is: Should I rent or buy a home? While there is no fixed answer because it varies based on one’s condition, there are pros and cons of each that must be evaluated before arriving at a decision. Renting doesn’t require large upfront costs, but it also doesn’t help you acquire a long-term asset. Similarly, buying gives you ownership rights, but it doesn’t allow you to move too frequently. This article explores the concept of buying vs renting a house, enabling you to arrive at an informed decision on: is it better to rent or buy a home. Renting vs buying a house: The key difference Renting a house means paying a landlord monthly rent to live in their property without ownership rights. Buying a house, on the other hand, involves purchasing property and gaining complete ownership after paying its full value or through home loan EMIs. Let’s understand the key differences. Basis Renting a house Buying a house Ownership No ownership, temporary stay Full ownership after purchase Upfront cost Low, includes security deposit and rent High, includes registration, down payment, EMIs Flexibility Easy to relocate anytime Difficult to move, as selling takes time Maintenance Managed by the landlord The owner bears all costs Long-term value No asset creation Builds equity and long-term wealth Tax benefits Limited or none Tax deductions on a home loan Ideal for Young couples who need to relocate frequently Those who need a long-term stay Advantages of renting a home If you often question yourself: Should I rent a home?, take a look at the following advantages of renting a home: Low initial cost: Renting requires only a security deposit and monthly rent, avoiding large upfront expenses like down payment, stamp duty, or registration charges. Flexibility to move: Ideal for people who frequently relocate for work or personal reasons, as tenants can easily change homes without long-term commitment. No maintenance burden: Generally, it is the responsibility of the landlord to handle maintenance costs and major repairs. Freedom from property taxes: Renters do not have to pay annual property taxes or society maintenance fees. Access to better locations: Renting allows individuals to live in prime or expensive areas that may be unaffordable to buy. Easier financial management: Rent is often lower than EMIs. As a result, tenants can manage monthly expenses and also save. Protection from market risks: There is no effect of property market fluctuations or interest rate changes on tenants. Short-term convenience: Renting is suitable for students, professionals, or newly married couples who may not yet be ready for homeownership. No long-term liability: Tenants don’t need to worry about long-term debt or the sale of property when they wish to relocate, upgrade, or downgrade. Disadvantages of renting a house The various disadvantages of renting a house are: No ownership benefits: Monthly rent payments do not build any equity or long-term assets for the tenant. Lack of stability: Renters may have to move frequently if landlords increase rent, sell the property, or terminate the agreement. Regular rent hikes: Rent often increases annually, burdening the tenant more without the benefit of ownership. Limited control: Tenants cannot make structural changes, renovations, or significant decor modifications without the landlord’s approval. Uncertain tenure: Lease agreements are typically short-term. As a result, renters are uncertain about where they’ll live for long. No tax benefits: Unlike homeowners, tenants cannot claim tax deductions on rent paid, except under certain allowances for salaried individuals. Advantages of buying a home Buyers must understand the advantages of buying a home in India before taking the plunge. Long-term financial stability: Owning a home eliminates the uncertainty of rising rents and provides lifelong security, especially after the loan is fully repaid. Asset and wealth creation: Every EMI paid builds ownership in a tangible asset that typically appreciates over time, helping you accumulate long-term wealth. Appreciation in property value: Real estate often increases in value due to urban development, better infrastructure, and rising demand. It lets you earn significant returns in the long run. Tax benefits: Home buyers can avail deductions on home loan interest under Section 24(b) and principal repayment under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, reducing overall tax liability. Collateral for loans: Property can be used as security to obtain personal, business, or education loans, improving financial flexibility. Rental income potential: A second home or a portion of your property can be rented out to generate steady passive income. Family security and legacy: A home ensures long-term comfort for your family and can be passed down as a valuable inheritance. Disadvantages of buying a home The drawbacks of buying a home are as follows: High upfront costs: Buying a home requires a significant down payment, registration fees, and stamp duty. Long-term financial commitment: A home purchase requires paying monthly installments. It also requires handling property taxes and other expenses. Reduced flexibility: When you own a home, it is difficult to relocate quickly due to the long selling process and market dependency. Market risks: Property values can fluctuate based on economic or location factors, affecting the resale potential of your asset. Liquidity concerns: It is not easy to convert a home into cash quickly. The asset is not easily liquidated. Maintenance expenses: You will have to pay for the repairs and society charges for a home you own. Interest burden: Long-term home loans result in substantial interest payments over time. In most Indian cities, renting a home is usually cheaper than buying one, if you take it for the short term. Renters only pay monthly rent and a small deposit, whereas buyers face large upfront costs like down payments, registration fees, and EMIs. However, buying becomes more cost-effective in the long run as property values appreciate and EMIs build ownership equity. The answer also depends on the city. In metros, property prices are higher, whereas in smaller cities, real estate costs are low. Thus, renting is more suited in metros, leaving buying for the smaller cities. Should I rent or buy a home if I move cities frequently? If you relocate frequently due to work or lifestyle, renting is a more practical and cost-effective choice. There is no worry of selling property, paying EMIs, or managing vacant homes. Buying, on the other hand, ties you to a location and involves high transaction costs, maintenance expenses, and potential losses if property prices stagnate. Unless you plan to settle in one city for at least 7–10 years, renting helps maintain liquidity, avoid long-term commitments, and reduce the financial strain associated with property ownership. What are the financial benefits of buying vs renting a house? Buying a house provides long-term financial stability, asset appreciation, and tax benefits on home loan interest and principal repayments. It helps build equity over time, securing ownership and future wealth creation. Renting, however, offers flexibility and lower upfront costs, allowing savings to be invested elsewhere for potentially higher returns. Renters also avoid property taxes, maintenance charges, and loan interest. Buying is financially more beneficial for long-term residents seeking stability and capital growth, while renting suits those who prioritize mobility, lower risk, and short-term affordability. Your salary looks good, your credit score is decent, and you expect quick approval. But the lender still rejects your application. The reason might be something many borrowers often overlook: you do not meet the lender’s criterion of debt-to-income ratio for personal loans. Many borrowers focus only on their monthly income and credit score when applying for a personal loan . However, lenders also look at how much of that income is already committed to existing loan EMIs and regular financial obligations. If a large portion of your income is already tied up in repayments, the lender may hesitate to offer a new loan. In this blog, you will learn in detail about the meaning of the Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio, how it affects your personal loan eligibility, and what can be the ideal DTI ratio for loan approval. Keep reading. What is the Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio? The debt-to-income ratio shows how much of your monthly income goes towards the repayment of your existing debt. A high DTI ratio means a significant portion of your income is already being used to service loan EMIs. In contrast, a lower DTI ratio indicates that you have a strong ability to manage debt and repay loans. In other words, your DTI ratio compares your total monthly debt payments with your gross monthly income. Gross income means your earnings before taxes and deductions. Debt payments may include EMIs for personal loans, home loans , car loans , or credit card dues. That is why this ratio is sometimes known as the EMI-to-income ratio. Here’s the basic formula to calculate the DTI ratio: DTI Ratio = (Total monthly debt payments / Gross monthly income) x 100 Why does the debt-to-income ratio matter for personal loans? Your debt-to-income ratio plays a crucial role in determining your personal loan eligibility. Lenders often use this ratio to assess your repayment capacity and financial stability. It helps them understand what portion of your monthly income is going towards existing debts and financial obligations, and whether you can comfortably handle another EMI. If the ratio is too high, the lender may refrain from approving your personal loan application . Basically, analyzing borrowers’ debt-to-income ratio for personal loan applications helps the lender with risk assessment. A lower ratio usually suggests lower risk, while a higher ratio may increase the chances of loan rejection or stricter loan terms. How does the DTI ratio impact your personal loan approval? We have already discussed how the debt-to-income ratio for personal loan applications can influence a lender’s decision to approve or reject a loan. However, its role does not end there. This ratio can also affect the loan amount, repayment tenure, and interest rate offered to the borrower. If your DTI ratio is lower, lenders may feel more confident about your repayment capacity. In such cases, they may offer you a higher loan amount or a flexible repayment tenure. You can also secure a lower interest rate. On the other hand, if the ratio is high, the lender may reduce the loan amount or offer a shorter tenure. Also,read – What Is FOIR? Calculation Of FOIR On Personal Loan How to calculate your debt-to-income ratio? You can calculate your DTI ratio using the simple formula mentioned above. Here are the steps for the same: 1. Evaluate your gross monthly income. This is your total monthly income before taxes and deductions. Make sure to consider income from all sources, including salary, freelance work, rent, and short-term gains from investments. 2. Add your monthly debt payments. Include all loan EMIs, credit card payments, and other regular debt obligations. 3. Divide your total monthly debt payments by your gross monthly income. 4. Multiply the result obtained in step 3 by 100 to calculate your debt-to-income ratio percentage. DTI calculation example by numbers Let’s consider a practical example to understand how to calculate the DTI ratio. Suppose your monthly salary is Rs. 60,000 and you earn Rs. 20,000 from rent and other sources. It means that your gross monthly income is Rs. 80,000 (60,000 + 20,000). If you are paying Rs. 15,000 as your home loan EMI and Rs. 5,000 as your car loan EMI, your total monthly debt payments amount to Rs. 20,000 (15,000 + 5,000). Using the formula, your DTI ratio is [(20,000 / 80,000) x 100], i.e., 25%. Also,read – Personal loan limits in India: What’s the maximum you can borrow? What is the ideal debt-to-income ratio for a personal loan? Lenders usually prefer borrowers with a lower debt-to-income ratio for personal loan applications. In most cases, the ideal EMI-to-income ratio is considered to be around 20% to 40%. A DTI ratio of less than 20% reflects an excellent financial position, whereas a DTI ratio above 40% reflects high debt levels. Such borrowers may find it difficult to get personal loan approval. However, the exact limit can vary depending on the lender, your credit score, income stability, and overall financial profile. Eligibility criteria linked to the debt-to-income ratio Your debt-to-income ratio is one of the most crucial factors that determine your personal loan eligibility . However, this ratio is not the only factor lenders consider in their decision-making process. They also evaluate other aspects such as your income stability, employment type, and credit score before approving a loan. In most cases, the final decision is based on a combination of these factors. For example, a lender may still approve a loan application even if the DTI ratio is slightly high, provided the borrower has an excellent credit score and a stable income. Practical ways to improve your debt-to-income ratios You can improve your DTI ratio by following a few simple tips. One such step is to repay small loans or credit card dues to reduce your total monthly debt payments. You can also try to increase your gross monthly income through bonuses, side work, or additional income sources. Another useful step is to avoid taking new credit frequently. This helps you maintain your overall debt position. You may also consider refinancing high-interest loans to reduce your monthly EMI burden. Avoiding or postponing a big-ticket purchase, such as a car, TV, or furniture, may also indirectly help you improve your DTI ratio. It’s because you’ll use less credit, and your overall monthly financial obligations will stay within manageable levels. Common mistakes that increase your DTI ratio Here are some common mistakes that can unknowingly increase your DTI ratio: Taking multiple short-term loans: Multiple small-ticket loans can increase your overall debt obligations. This, in turn, can swell your fixed obligation to income ratio. Excessive credit card usage: Higher credit card usage can increase your debt obligations as well as your credit utilization ratio. Thus, it impacts both your DTI ratio and credit score. Ignoring hidden liabilities: Small liabilities, such as minor credit card bills, BNPL (Buy Now Pay Later) purchases, etc., are often overlooked. But they can also increase your DTI ratio. Not closing unused loan accounts: Even inactive credit accounts can affect your overall financial profile and the DTI ratio. Here are a few points to keep in mind: A lower DTI ratio indicates better repayment capability, and vice versa. An ideal debt-to-income ratio for personal loans is around 20% to 40%. It means the maximum EMI percentage of salary should hover around 40%. Lenders also consider your credit score, income stability, and employment type while determining personal loan eligibility. If your DTI ratio is above the acceptable level, it’s better to first improve it before applying for a new loan. Maintaining a healthy DTI ratio can make it easier to qualify for a loan and manage repayments comfortably. Get an Instant Personal Loan for all your needs ! specialized financial institutions allow you to extend it to 32 years. The actual maximum tenure for a home loan depends on your age when you apply for the loan, your retirement age, and the lender’s specific rules. Opting for a long home loan tenure helps you get lower monthly Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs), but the total interest you have to pay over the loan lifecycle is substantially higher. The typical home loan tenure in India ranges from a minimum tenure of 1 to 5 years to a maximum tenure of 20 to 30 years. Buying a home is one of the biggest financial milestones for most people. And a home loan has increased the chances of achieving this goal. When taking a home loan , the first question a borrower asks the lender is: What is the home loan tenure I can get? Home loan tenure refers to the number of years a lender offers you to repay the loan. It varies from lender to lender, ranging from 5 to 30 years. The EMI payment and the interest outgo depend on the loan tenure. What is home loan tenure? Home loan tenure refers to the total period over which you repay your home loan, including both the principal amount and the interest. Lenders in India typically offer a range, from the minimum tenure for a home loan, which is usually around 5 years, to the home loan maximum tenure that can extend up to 30 years, depending on factors like the borrower’s age, income, and the lender’s policies. Choosing the best tenure for a home loan is an important decision. A shorter tenure means higher EMIs but lower overall interest, helping you clear the loan faster. On the other hand, a longer tenure lowers your monthly EMIs, making repayments more manageable, but increases the total interest paid over the life of the loan. Ultimately, the ideal home loan tenure balances your current financial capacity with long-term financial goals, ensuring that EMIs are affordable while minimizing interest costs. What are the home loan tenure options in India – 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 years? When applying for a home loan in India, choosing the right tenure matters. Home loan tenure is the period over which you repay the loan, including the principal and interest. Banks and housing finance companies generally offer tenures ranging from a minimum tenure of a home loan of 5 years to a maximum of 30 years. The most popular options include 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 years. Shorter tenure: 5 to 10 years Pros: Faster repayment and significant savings on total interest. Cons: Higher EMIs can put pressure on your monthly budget. Medium tenure: 15 to 20 years Pros: Balances affordable EMIs with lower overall interest costs. Cons: You may pay more interest than with a shorter tenure. This can be a suitable option for many first-time homebuyers. Long tenure: 25 to 30 years Pros: Lower EMIs provide greater monthly financial flexibility. Cons: The longer repayment period results in higher total interest costs. The best tenure for a home loan depends on factors such as your age, income stability, career plans, and other financial commitments. Make sure you assess your current and future finances before choosing a tenure. Aim for an EMI that is comfortable to manage while keeping your overall interest cost as low as possible. Also Read – Types of interest rates What is the minimum home loan tenure? The minimum tenure for a home loan in India is usually around 5 years, although it can vary between lenders. When the tenure is short, you repay the loan in fewer years. The monthly EMI is higher as the principal is divided over a shorter period. However, the interest you pay is also for a shorter time, which can significantly lower your total interest cost. You should opt for a shorter tenure if you have a stable income and enough monthly surplus to manage higher EMIs. However, before you choose it, ensure that you can comfortably pay the monthly EMI. What is the maximum home loan tenure? When planning to buy a home, understanding your loan tenure is crucial. The home loan maximum tenure in India is generally 30 years, offering borrowers the flexibility to spread repayments over a long period. On the other hand, the minimum tenure of a home loan usually starts at 5 years. This wide range allows you to choose the best tenure for a home loan depending on your income, financial goals, and repayment capacity. Longer tenures, like 25 or 30 years, reduce your monthly EMIs, making it easier to manage your budget without straining other expenses. However, they come with the trade-off of higher total interest paid over the loan’s life. Shorter tenures, such as 5 or 10 years, require higher EMIs, which can be challenging for some borrowers, but they allow you to clear the loan faster and save significantly on interest costs. Minimum home loan tenure vs. maximum home loan tenure: What are the differences? Tenure plays a vital role when selecting a home loan. It determines your EMI burden, interest outgo, and overall financial planning. The following table compares the home loan maximum tenure against the home loan minimum tenure to help you decide which one best suits your needs. Criteria Minimum home loan tenure Maximum home loan tenure Typical range 5 to 10 years 25 to 30 years Monthly EMI payment Higher EMIs Lower EMIs Total interest payment Lower overall interest Significantly higher interest due to a greater number of EMI payments Financial burden Heavy in the short term Spread over a longer period Loan repayment speed Quick repayment, debt-free sooner Longer repayment period, the debt continues Eligibility Requires higher income stability Easier eligibility with lower EMI Impact on savings Reduces the ability to save in the short term Allows more savings and liquidity Flexibility Limited flexibility due to high EMI Greater flexibility in managing expenses Ideal for High-income earners desiring early closure Young borrowers seeking affordable EMIs How does home loan tenure affect your EMI and total interest? Your home loan tenure directly impacts your EMIs and the total interest you pay over the life of the loan. Here’s how different tenures make a difference: Loan tenure Monthly EMI Total interest Suitable for Shorter (10-15 years) Higher EMI Much lower Borrowers with higher income who can afford higher EMIs Medium (15-20 years) Moderate EMI Moderate Borrowers looking for a balance between EMI and interest cost Longer (25-30 years) Lower EMI Much higher Borrowers who want lower monthly financial burden What are the factors affecting home loan tenure? Many factors affect the home loan tenure, including your age, income, repayment capacity, loan amount, interest rate , and financial commitments. These factors can influence the tenure that best suits your budget and repayment goals. Borrower’s age A more extended loan tenure is ideal for young borrowers who are expected to have more working years to repay the loan. The loan tenure you’re eligible for will depend on the remaining years of service. Salaried individuals can apply for a home loan up to the age of 60 years, while self-employed individuals can apply up to the age of 65 years. Property’s age When you avail of a home loan, the property you intend to buy is pledged as collateral. If you fail to pay your dues, the lender can sell the property to recover the remaining debt. So, you cannot have a loan tenure that’s longer than the property’s residual life. Income and financial stability Lenders sanction a higher loan amount and a longer loan tenure to borrowers earning a higher income. It is because the chances of default are lower. Ensure that you have a steady and reliable source of income and a stable financial situation. Individuals nearing retirement are generally not eligible for a home loan unless they can prove that they have another regular income source. Leasehold properties If you take a home loan to buy a property on leasehold land, the lender can sell the property to recover your defaulted loan only until the end of the leasehold period. Thus, in this case, you are eligible for a tenure equal to or shorter than the remaining leasehold period. What is the impact of credit score on home loan tenure eligibility? Your credit score can influence the home loan terms offered by a lender, including the tenure. A good score shows a strong repayment history and may improve your chances of getting favorable loan terms. A lower score may lead to stricter conditions or a higher interest rate, which can affect the overall cost of a longer tenure. Good credit score: It may help you access better interest rates and flexible tenure options. Lower credit score: It may result in higher rates or stricter loan terms. Longer tenure: A higher interest rate can increase the total interest paid. Better score: It can make it easier to choose a tenure that balances affordable EMIs with lower interest costs. How does home loan tenure affect tax benefits? Home loan tenure affects the period over which you can claim eligible tax deductions. If you opt for a longer tenure, you may have eligible interest payments spread over more years. Section 24(b): Eligible borrowers can claim a deduction for interest paid on a home loan if they fulfill applicable conditions and limits. Section 80C : You can claim deductions on principal repayment if the overall limit and applicable tax rules are met. Note that the tax benefits depend on factors such as property type, possession status, and the tax regime you choose. How to choose the best home loan tenure for your needs? Choosing the best tenure for home loan involves evaluating both your current finances and long-term plans. With many options, the right choice depends on the following factors: Loan amount The loan amount is one of the most important factors determining the repayment tenure. If you apply for a higher loan amount, choosing a shorter loan tenure will translate to higher EMIs and interest payments, which can be difficult to repay for the average income borrower. A longer home loan tenure is suggested, especially if the loan amount is large. EMI payment capacity The size of EMI payments also depends on the loan tenure, making it essential for you to assess the EMI amount you can pay comfortably. A home loan EMI calculator can help in picking the ideal combination of home loan tenure and EMI payment amount to ensure smooth repayment. Your monthly affordability Your EMI should fit comfortably within your monthly budget after accounting for regular expenses and savings. While shorter tenures reduce interest, they come with higher EMIs that may strain cash flow if not planned carefully. Total interest outgo A shorter tenure results in lower total interest paid over the loan’s life, whereas longer tenures increase the overall interest cost. Income stability and future growth If you have a stable job or expect steady income growth, a shorter tenure may be manageable. Borrowers with variable or uncertain income may prefer longer tenures for repayment flexibility. Life stage and financial responsibilities Younger borrowers may opt for longer tenures to keep EMIs low, with plans to prepay later. Those with family responsibilities or nearing retirement often benefit from shorter tenures to reduce long-term liability. Flexibility and prepayment options Choosing a slightly longer tenure with the option to make prepayments can offer the best of both worlds: manageable EMIs and reduced interest over time. If you’ve chosen the home loan maximum tenure, with the right approach, you can move closer to the best tenure for home loan. Here are a few simple ways to do that: Make regular prepayments. Even small, periodic prepayments directly reduce the principal, helping you move closer to the minimum tenure for a home loan while cutting down total interest. Salary hikes or additional income can be used to increase EMIs. This reduces the outstanding balance faster and shortens the loan tenure without major lifestyle changes. Use annual bonuses or incentives to make lump-sum payments. These one-time contributions can significantly reduce tenure and interest burden. When lenders allow EMI increases instead of tenure extensions, choosing higher EMIs helps prevent the loan from stretching toward the home loan maximum tenure. Switching to a lower-rate loan and keeping the EMI unchanged can automatically reduce the loan tenure and bring you closer to the best tenure for a home loan. Conclusion Choosing the right home loan tenure is a crucial part of your homeownership journey. Try to pick a tenure based on your income, financial condition, and lifestyle. If it is challenging for you to pay a high EMI amount due to a tight budget, opt for the home loan with the maximum tenure. Similarly, if you have a steady income, choose a shorter home loan tenure. interest rate, buying a house has become easier. However, repaying a home loan is still a big responsibility to shoulder. A regular payment of EMIs, without disrupting your monthly obligations, can be difficult in tough times. Therefore, with the use of an online housing loan calculator , you can tailor a loan plan according to your needs. What Is an NOC? A No Objection Certificate (NOC) is a legal document stating that an organisation or individual does not object to the details mentioned therein. It is also referred to as a “No Dues Certificate” and can be obtained directly from your lender. The document also contains crucial information regarding your housing loan payment history which is vital for your credit score. An NOC acts as a legal proof for the completion of your debt i.e., the home loan. This is why obtaining an NOC from your lender is extremely important. Here is why you must procure an NOC after paying off your house loan. Why You Must Obtain an NOC After Repaying Your Home Loan Even after clearing all your EMIs , obtaining a No Objection Certificate (NOC) is essential. It acts as official proof that your home loan has been fully repaid, safeguards your property rights, and ensures that your credit records are accurately updated. Here are some key aspects to consider: To secure loan closure proof Once your home loan repayment is complete, getting a loan closure should be the next step. An NOC issued by your lender acts as a proof that there is no outstanding amount left on your house loan. It is taken, essentially, to safeguard your property rights from the lender. When you check for a home loan online, ensure that your tenure and EMIs will compliment your financial health. An easy method to do this is by using a free online home loan EMI calculator. For a flawless credit history Your home loan eligibility is directly affected by your CIBIL score . Therefore, your CIBIL report is a database that must be updated once your entire home loan has been repaid. A bad credit score will reflect poorly on your ability to repay a loan. In such a scenario, chances are that your application for any future loans will be rejected. An NOC helps you to clear off any pending dues in your CIBIL report and even enhances your credit score. Preventing disputes with lienholder Even if you have been consistent in paying off the EMIs on your housing loan, it has to reflect in your credit history. With the absence of an NOC from the lender, you will be unable to claim your rights on the lien, which in the case of a home loan, is your house. An NOC will also prevent the lender from making any false claims against you, thus protecting your actual housing loan repayment history. Step-by-Step Process to Obtain Your Home Loan NOC Obtaining a Home Loan NOC after closing your loan is an essential final step to ensure complete financial and legal closure. Here is a clear step by step process to help you secure your home loan NOC certificate smoothly. Step 1: Confirm full loan repayment Ensure all EMIs outstanding interest and applicable charges are fully cleared with the Lender. This confirms that no dues remain against your loan account. Step 2: Submit a NOC request Place a formal request for an NOC for a housing loan through the Lender’s branch customer service portal or official communication channel. Some Lenders may auto initiate the process after closure. Step 3: Collect key closure documents Along with the NOC request, ensure you receive your loan closure statement, the original property documents, and confirmation of lien removal, if applicable. Step 4: Verify credit record updates Check that the Lender has updated your loan status as closed with the credit bureaus. This protects your credit profile from future discrepancies. Step 5: Safely store the NOC Once issued, carefully preserve the NOC for home loan, as it is required for property sale transfer or future financing. Also, read – What is Home Loan Prepayment and How Does it Work? NOC for Registered vs Unregistered Properties A No Objection Certificate plays a critical role once a loan is fully repaid, but its importance varies depending on whether the property is registered or unregistered. For a registered property, the NOC acts as formal confirmation from the Lender that there are no outstanding dues. This document helps clear the charge marked on the property records and safeguards the owner during resale or transfer. In such cases, obtaining a home credit NOC also ensures that credit records reflect proper loan closure. For unregistered properties, the relevance of an NOC becomes even more significant. Since ownership records are not formally updated with local authorities, the NOC serves as primary proof that the Lender no longer has a financial claim. Without an NOC for a housing loan, future registration or sale of the property may face legal and verification challenges. In both scenarios, an NOC for a home loan protects the borrower from disputes, prevents future liability claims and confirms complete loan closure. While the documentation process may differ slightly, obtaining an NOC is essential regardless of property status. It provides financial clarity, legal security and long term peace of mind for homeowners who have successfully repaid their loan. Also, read – Home Credit Loan Settlement Process What to Do If You Lose Your NOC Certificate Losing your NOC after closing a home loan can feel stressful, but the situation is manageable with the right steps. The NOC is official proof that the Lender has no remaining claim on your property and that the loan account is fully closed. If it is misplaced, act promptly to protect your ownership rights and credit records. Notify the Lender promptly: Inform your Lender as soon as the NOC is lost and submit a formal written request for a duplicate certificate to initiate the reissue process without delays. Follow the prescribed procedure: Adhere to the standard housing loan NOC process, as Lenders typically reissue the document only after completing their internal verification checks. Submit supporting documents: Provide identity proof, loan account details, and a written declaration clearly explaining how and when the NOC was misplaced. Complete additional formalities if required: Some Lenders may ask for an indemnity bond or a nominal processing fee to safeguard against future disputes. Verify the reissued NOC carefully: Ensure the duplicate certificate clearly confirms full loan closure and states that the charge on the property has been fully released. Store the document securely: Maintain both digital and physical copies of your home credit NOC to support future property transactions and ensure long term legal and financial security. How Long Does It Take to Receive Your NOC? Once your home loan is fully repaid, the time taken to receive your NOC depends on how efficiently your Lender completes the housing loan NOC process. In most cases, Lenders issue the certificate within 7 to 15 working days after confirming that all dues are cleared and there are no pending charges. This period allows the Lender to verify loan closure records and complete internal checks. If the request is submitted digitally and all documents are in order, the process may be faster. Offline requests or discrepancies in account details can slightly extend the timeline. The NOC for a housing loan is a critical document, as it confirms that the Lender has released all rights over the property and enables updates with registration authorities and credit bureaus. Following up with your Lender and retaining acknowledgement of your request can help ensure timely issuance and avoid future property related complications. A home loan NOC certificate is an official document issued by the lender confirming that the borrower has fully repaid the home loan. It is mandatory because it legally discharges the property from any loan obligations and ensures that ownership rights are fully transferred to the borrower. How does NOC affect my CIBIL score? Obtaining a home loan NOC positively reflects on your credit history. It confirms that the loan has been fully repaid and no outstanding dues remain, which helps maintain a healthy CIBIL score. A delay in securing the NOC for a housing loan may temporarily indicate unsettled accounts, potentially affecting creditworthiness. Can I sell my property without a NOC? Selling a property without an NOC for home loan is not advisable. The document confirms that the property is free from any loan obligations. Without it, the buyer cannot verify clear ownership, which can lead to legal issues. The importance of home loan NOC ensures safe and smooth property transfers. What documents are required to apply for NOC? To apply for a home loan NOC, you must submit the loan account statement, identity proof, property papers, and a written request to the lender. Additional documents may include repayment receipts or PAN proof. Providing complete documentation ensures the timely processing of the NOC for home loan. Is there a validity period for a Home Loan NOC? A home loan NOC certificate generally does not have a fixed expiry date. However, it is advisable to use it promptly for property sale or registration purposes. Keeping the document up to date and safely stored ensures smooth legal and financial transactions in the future. The NOC for housing loan serves as permanent proof of loan closure. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Receiving extra money is always a good thing. There may come a time when you may receive some lump sum amount such as a bonus or incentive payment. You could also come across some family inheritance or make a windfall profit if you are a businessperson. However, your conundrum comes when you need to decide how to spend it. If you have loans including home loans , you are in two minds whether to use the lump sum amount to prepay your housing loan or other loans or probably put to use elsewhere. “To prepay or not to prepay,” the classic Shakespearian dilemma will bother you. Well, prepayment is a facility offered by financial institutions like Tata Capital , whereby you as a home loan borrower can prepay your home loan or other loans fully and complete the formalities of discharging your loan obligation to the lender. Lenders can also offer you part prepayment facility. Intuitively, it makes a lot of sense to use the money to prepay and become debt free. But, is it as simple as that? Let’s find out from the following 7 factors that are before you, as well as what is prepayment of home loan and how to plan it effectively. 7 Factors to Know Before Opting for Prepayment 1. Prepayment comes with conditions: Financial institutions like Tata Capital, imposes some conditions for prepayment home loan which could include charges and the number of times you can make the prepayment. For instance, it charges 2% plus taxes for prepayment on home loan balance transfer . 2. Effect of part prepayment on your loan: If your lump sum amount is insufficient to foreclose your home loan you could consider making a part prepayment as per conditions. The advantage of part prepayment is to reduce your interest burden. For instance, if your principal outstanding is Rs 15 lakh and you want to part prepay Rs 8 lakh, your lender recasts the housing loan with Rs 7 lakh as the principal to be repaid and charges interest accordingly which would also cause a change in the EMI. In fact, part prepayment could be more advantageous if the prospects of an increase in interest rates in the future are high. 3. Which loan to close first? If you are a person who has more than one type of loan – education loan , car loan , business loan or personal loan – you should try to use the lump sum amount to pay off the loan with the highest interest rate. Typically, personal loans and business loans, being unsecured loans, carry higher interest rates than secured loans such as car loans and home loans. So, it makes sense to clear off the personal loan first and if anything is left over you could consider part prepayment of your housing loan. You can check Home Loan interest rates on the Tata Capital website. 4. Effect on credit score: Remember that the banks and financial institutions sends details of your home loan to the credit bureau, which uses the data to prepare a credit score for you. Since repayment history is an important factor for credit score part prepayment augurs well for your credit score. Ensure that this fact reflects in the credit score as sometimes delay in feeding information can be detrimental to you. 5. Alternate use of lump sum amount: Making investment decisions is tricky and with the myriad possibilities for the investment, you find it difficult to choose. You could take the advice of finance professionals to help you make the decisions. One simple rule of thumb is to consider the possible return of your intended investments. If that return is higher than the interest rate you are paying on your home loan it may be better to invest in that instrument. 6. Tax benefits: This is another area which may require the help of finance professionals. It works both ways. You could get tax benefits or you could lose tax benefits depending on the way you have structured your housing loan. You need to consult a tax professional and use the inputs to make a proper decision. 7. Timing: Timing is a factor that affects your decision to prepay or not to repay. Another thumb rule is that in the initial part of the loan tenure, a prepayment is a good option. This is because you will pay a much lower interest amount on the reduced principal outstanding after prepayment. This also reduces home loan EMI . However, if you receive your lump sum amount during the later part of the loan tenure it may be better to use the funds elsewhere and allow the loan repayment to be discharged in the normal tenure. Make sure you check and choose the best EMI option. There could be other factors besides the seven described above that could affect your decision to prepay or not to prepay. Tata Capital and other housing finance companies create their own conditions in accordance with RBI guidelines in respect to the prepayment. You should consider all of them and consult with finance and tax professionals before you make a decision one way or the other. How to Calculate Prepayment Savings: A Step-by-Step Guide To calculate savings through loan prepayment, a prepay home loan calculator is a convenient option. A home loan prepayment calculator is an online tool that helps you check whether making a prepayment on the loan is worthwhile. It can demonstrate how prepayment can reduce your loan burden. If you are thinking of choosing the prepayment option, these calculators help you understand how your loan changes in the following aspects: The percentage or amount of EMI saved The due EMI amount The revised EMI after prepayment The revised loan tenure To use an online house loan prepayment calculator, you will need to enter a few details: Prepayment home loan amount Outstanding loan amount Remaining loan tenure Rate of interest Once you enter this information, the calculator will show your total savings and how prepayment impacts your EMIs (for the remaining tenure). It also helps track the total prepayment made, empowering you to pick the right prepayment option. Prepayment vs Investment: Comparing Returns A common dilemma for a home loan borrower is whether to prepay the loan or consider other investment opportunities. Here is a list of things to consider, to make the decision: Long Term Finances Start by thinking about your long-term finances and goals. Expenses like children’s education, family responsibilities, or retirement planning may require more liquidity going ahead. If you’re planning on prepayment home loan for the extra security, make sure your long-term finances are not significantly affected. Otherwise, investments can help you build wealth. Inflation and Tax Benefits Inflation affects the value of your loan over time. Investments can offer returns that outgrow inflation. On the other hand, home loans offer tax deductions (under Section 24 of the Income Tax Act, India). Consider whether your home loan can reduce your tax burden substantially. Prepayment Charges Some lenders charge a fee for prepayment. Always review these costs before deciding. Investment Returns Consider the trade-off: evaluate if investments can offer higher long-term returns than the interest saved through prepay home loan. In many cases, a balanced mix of partial prepayment and investing works best. Step-by-Step Process to Prepay Your Home Loan If you have assessed your financial situation, long-term goals, disadvantages and advantages of prepayment of home loan, and considered all options available at hand – and decided to prepay your home loan, here’s a simple guide to help you through it. Step 1: Review loan agreement Start by checking your loan documents for prepayment rules. Look for details on minimum prepayment amounts and applicable charges. Some lenders offer partial and full prepayment options too. Step 2: Arrange funds Ensure that you have funds available for the prepayment as well as emergency funds. Include all upcoming expenses like medical bills, education fees, and general living expenses. Step 3: Contact lender Next, contact your home loan lender about your intention to prepay home loan. Most lenders will have prepayment clauses for penalties, limits, and the final impact on EMI and loan tenure. Your lender will explain the procedure, including any prepayment charges involved. Step 4: Submit documents Submit the required documents (identity proof, loan account details) as requested by your lender. Step 5: Make the payment Pay the prepayment amount using the approved payment mode. Afterwards, remember to collect an acknowledgement and updated loan statement with the revised EMI or loan tenure. Conclusion Prepaying your home loan can be a practical way to reduce loan burden, and get closer to a debt-free status. The final decision will depend on the interest rate of your home loan, the remaining tenure, prepayment home loan charges, and other related factors. Carefully thinking through your options and their ripple effects can help you make the right decision for your situation. With Tata Capital’s flexible repayment options and competitive interest rates, planning your home loan becomes easier. Prepayment charges are usually not applicable on floating-rate home loans, as per RBI guidelines. For fixed-rate loans, lenders may charge a fee, which varies by bank and loan terms. It is best to check directly with your lender for exact charges and conditions. Can I prepay my home loan without reducing my EMI tenure? Yes, one of the advantages of prepayment of home loan is lenders allow you to either reduce your EMI or shorten the loan tenure. Reducing EMI helps with monthly cash flow. On the flip side reducing tenure leads to higher interest savings, and faster loan closure. How much can I save in interest by prepaying my home loan? Prepay home loan reduces the outstanding principal, which lowers the interest charged over time. Even small prepayments, especially in the early years, can result in savings on your home loan. To estimate exact savings, you can use an online home loan prepayment calculator with your loan details. Is prepaying a home loan better than investing the surplus amount? Deciding between prepayment home loan and investment can have nuance. If your loan interest rate is higher than expected investment returns, prepayment may be better. However, if investments offer higher returns and you value that wealth growth, investing could be more suitable for your situation. What documents are required to prepay a home loan? To prepay home loan, you typically need your loan account details, valid identity proof, and a prepayment request form. Some lenders may also ask for updated bank statements or additional documents, depending on their internal policies. Check with your lender to get the exact list. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund When you avail of a loan, the common terms you come across are loan tenure, interest rate, and EMI. The EMI, or Equated Monthly Installment, is the amount you must return to the bank every month to repay the loan amount. Understanding what EMI is, its types, calculation, and working is beneficial for the smooth repayment of a loan. What is EMI? EMI’s full form is Equated Monthly Installment. It refers to the fixed amount you must pay every month to repay a loan within a specified tenure. It includes both the principal amount and the interest charged by the lender, divided equally across the repayment period. EMIs are a convenient and structured way to manage loan repayments, making large financial commitments, such as home loans, car loans, or personal loans, affordable over time. In India, EMIs play a vital role in financial planning. They enable you to achieve a balance between borrowing and monthly expenses. Factors like loan amount, interest rate, and tenure influence the amount of EMI you are obligated to pay. If you choose a shorter duration, your EMIs will rise. But your EMIs will fall in case the duration opted for is longer. Knowledge about EMIs helps you make informed financial decisions and avoid defaults. Understanding the EMI full form and how it works You will often come across the term EMI when you’re speaking to a loan agent or when you’re buying something costly. Most e-commerce websites allow you to pay for smartphones, kitchen appliances, travel tickets, etc., via an EMI plan. EMI’s full form in banking is Equated Monthly Installments, and it is a convenient way to pay off loans over time through regular, manageable installments rather than a single lump sum payment. For instance, if you’re purchasing a smartphone worth Rs. 80,000, you can either pay the entire amount upfront as a lump sum or choose to repay it through an EMI plan over 12 months. The EMI plan divides the smartphone’s cost price (Rs. 80,000) into 12 equal installments while charging an additional interest on these payments. Thus, under the EMI plan, you will be required to pay around Rs. 7,200 per month, considering the store charges an interest of 8%. Each EMI consists of two main components: the principal and the interest. The principal is the original amount borrowed, while the interest is the cost charged by the lender for providing the loan. Initially, a larger portion of the EMI goes toward interest. However, the share of principal increases as the loan progresses. The distribution of payments is handled by the amortization schedule to ensure that you repay both parts evenly over the tenure. The loan tenure, which can range from a few months to several years, directly affects the EMI amount. If the tenure is longer, the EMI is spread across a longer period, making the installment amount smaller. However, if the tenure is shorter, the EMI is higher. EMIs are typically paid on a fixed date each month, making them predictable and easy to include in financial planning. You can pay EMIs through various methods, such as auto-debit, post-dated cheques, or online transfers. You must know how EMI works for different types of interest rates. The EMI amount remains constant throughout the loan tenure in a fixed interest rate loan. However, the EMI may change depending on market fluctuations in the case of floating interest rates. EMI calculation: Formula with examples Calculating an EMI helps borrowers understand their monthly repayment obligation before taking a loan. The standard EMI formula is: EMI = [P × R × (1 + R)ⁿ] / [(1 + R)ⁿ – 1] where, P refers to the principal loan amount R refers to the monthly interest rate N stands for loan tenure in months This formula ensures that borrowers can evenly repay both the principal and interest over the entire tenure. The interest portion is higher during the early stages of repayment, gradually reducing as the principal balance decreases. Example: Suppose you take a home loan of Rs. 10,00,000 at an annual interest rate of 10% for a tenure of 10 years (120 months). Step 1: Convert the annual rate to a monthly rate. R = 10 / 12 / 100 = 0.00833 Step 2: Substitute in the formula. EMI = [10,00,000 × 0.00833 × (1 + 0.00833)¹²⁰] / [(1 + 0.00833)¹²⁰ – 1] Step 3: Calculate accordingly. EMI = Rs. 13,215 per month So, you will be able to clear off the loan as per schedule if you pay an EMI of Rs. 13,215 every month. You will pay a total of Rs. 15,85,800 over 120 months (Rs. 13,215 x 120). Since the principal loan amount was Rs. 10,00,000, the additional Rs. 5,85,800 is the interest payout. Using this formula, you can estimate EMIs for different loan amounts, interest rates, and tenures, helping you choose affordable repayment options and plan your finances more effectively. Types of EMI & calculation methods When taking a loan in India , understanding EMI calculation can significantly impact your repayment strategy and total cost. In a fixed-rate EMI, the interest is calculated on the entire loan amount throughout the tenure, and the EMI remains constant from the beginning to the end. Those who prefer to have a fixed monthly payment that they know in advance should opt for this method. However, since interest doesn’t reduce as the principal is repaid, the overall interest cost tends to be higher. In contrast, a reducing balance EMI, also known as diminishing balance, recalculates interest each month on the outstanding principal. As the principal decreases with each payment, the interest component also reduces over time. This method ensures you pay interest only on the remaining loan amount, resulting in lower total interest outgo. However, EMIs may fluctuate slightly with changing rates, and initial payments are typically higher. The following table compares the two types of EMIs: Aspect Fixed-rate EMI Reducing balance EMI Interest calculation On the entire loan amount On the remaining principal balance EMI amount Constant throughout tenure Gradually decreases over time Total interest paid Higher Lower Best for Short-term or small loans Long-term or high-value loans Flexibility Less flexible More dynamic and cost-effective Types of EMI Generally, Indian lenders offer two types of EMIs: fixed EMIs and flexible EMIs. Fixed EMIs remain the same throughout the loan tenure, as both the principal and interest components are predetermined. Consequently, this EMI option provides predictability and makes monthly budgeting easier, ideal for borrowers who prefer stability and consistent payments. However, you may have to pay a higher interest component in the fixed EMI option if market rates decline during the loan period. Flexible EMIs, on the other hand, allow adjustments in repayment schedules based on changing financial situations. Borrowers can increase or decrease EMI amounts, make part-prepayments, or even pause payments under specific conditions. This option provides greater control and convenience. It is ideal for those with an unstable income. Choosing between the two depends on your financial discipline, income stability, and comfort with market-linked rate variations. How is EMI calculated? EMI is calculated based on three key components: the loan amount (principal), the interest rate, and the loan tenure. Banks and financial institutions use a mathematical EMI formula to calculate your monthly installment. It ensures systematic repayment of both the principal and interest. Fixed-rate method In the fixed-rate EMI system, the interest is calculated on the entire loan amount throughout the repayment period. The EMI calculation remains constant for the full tenure, making it easier for borrowers to plan their budgets. However, since the interest portion does not reduce as the principal is repaid, the overall cost of borrowing tends to be slightly higher. Reducing balance method In the reducing balance method, the interest is charged only on the outstanding principal each month. As borrowers make payments, the principal decreases, leading to a gradual reduction in the interest portion. This method results in lower total interest outgo compared to fixed-rate EMIs and is commonly used for home, car, and business loans in India. Most banks and NBFCs in India use the reducing balance method for transparency and cost efficiency. How to use EMI calculators? An online EMI calculator is one of the easiest ways to estimate your monthly loan payments before applying. Tata Capital offers a user-friendly EMI calculator on its website for different loan types, including personal, home, car, and business loans. Simply enter three key details: the loan amount, interest rate, and tenure. The calculations with accurate amounts will appear within seconds. Apart from the monthly EMI, you can view the total interest payable and total repayment amount on your screen. You can even adjust the values to compare different scenarios and find a repayment plan that fits your budget. This tool helps borrowers make informed decisions by understanding how small changes in tenure or interest rate can affect their EMI calculation. It saves time during financial planning and does not leave any chance for manual error. You can confidently choose the most affordable and convenient loan option with Tata Capital. EMI in different types of loans in India Whether it’s buying a home, upgrading a car, expanding a business, or funding education, every financial goal comes with distinct borrowing needs. However, EMI is common to all. There may be a difference in the structure and other terms across different loan types. Understanding how EMI works for personal, home, car, education, and business loans can help you align repayments with your financial priorities. To suit the requirements of different customers, Tata Capital offers customized and flexible EMI plans. Personal loans Personal loan EMIs are ideal for meeting immediate financial needs such as weddings, medical expenses, or travel. With a Tata Capital personal loan , you can choose loan amounts of up to Rs. 35 lakh at affordable interest rates starting at 11.50%, with a flexible tenure of up to 6 years. Home loans The tenure for home loans is typically longer, up to 30 years, making them more affordable despite the large loan amount. Tata Capital offers home loans of up to Rs. 7.5 crore at interest rates of 7.75% for a tenure of up to 30 years. You can use the EMI calculator to plan your repayment schedule. You can also opt for part-pre-payment to shorten the tenure or reduce future EMIs. Car loans Car loans let individuals purchase new or used vehicles with EMIs structured according to the down payment, interest rate, and tenure. Tata Capital offers flexible car loans with quick approvals, loan amounts up to Rs. 50 lakh, and repayment tenures of up to 84 months, making vehicle ownership easier for salaried and self-employed individuals. Education loans Education loan EMIs often begin after a moratorium period, typically six months to one year after completing studies. Tata Capital’s education loans of up to Rs. 2 crore* help parents and students fund higher education in India or abroad. You can opt for secured or unsecured loan options based on your preference. Business loans Business loans are designed to support working capital needs, expansion, or machinery purchase. Tata Capital offers unsecured business loans of up to Rs. 90 lakhs at interest rates starting from 12% with a tenure of up to 60 months. Factors affecting your EMI amount The Equated Monthly Installment (EMI) you pay on a loan depends on several financial factors that determine the overall cost of borrowing. Understanding what affects EMI helps you make better financial decisions and manage repayments efficiently. Loan amount The principal amount you borrow has a direct impact on your EMI. A higher loan amount means larger monthly installments. For example, the EMI for a home loan worth Rs. 20 lakh will be higher than the EMI for a loan worth Rs. 10 lakh, even at the same interest rate and tenure. Interest rate The rate of interest, fixed or floating, is one of the most crucial factors. Even a small change in interest rate can significantly alter the EMI value. In India, lenders like banks and NBFCs set rates based on your credit profile, loan type, and market trends. Loan tenure A longer tenure lowers the EMI amount, but the total interest paid over time increases. Conversely, a shorter tenure raises your monthly EMI but helps you save on interest costs. Down payment Making a higher down payment reduces the loan amount, thereby lowering your EMI. This is common in car and home loans, where you can decide how much to pay up front. Credit score Your credit score influences the interest rate offered. If you have a higher score of 750 or above, you can get lower interest rates. On the other hand, a poor score results in costlier loans, increasing the EMI burden. Benefits of EMI for borrowers There are numerous benefits of EMI for borrowers, which make borrowing more convenient and manageable for individuals. Let’s check out the most important ones: Convenience You can repay loans conveniently with the option of EMI as you distribute fixed payments each month. Large financial commitments like car loans, home loans, and education loans are simplified. For example, instead of paying Rs. 10 lakh upfront for a car, you can spread it over 5 years in affordable monthly payments. Affordability EMIs make expensive purchases accessible by breaking the repayment down into smaller installments. Due to this flexibility, middle-income borrowers can fulfill goals without suffering from the problems of financial strain. Predictable budgeting Since EMI amounts remain constant (in fixed-rate loans), you can plan your monthly budgets effectively. Knowing exactly how much to set aside each month ensures financial discipline and stability. Credit score improvement A borrower’s credit score improves with regular and timely EMI payments. A strong credit score increases eligibility for future loans and helps secure better interest rates. Overall, EMIs promote responsible borrowing by making large purchases achievable while encouraging timely repayment and disciplined financial planning. Tips for efficient EMI management Managing EMIs efficiently is essential for maintaining financial stability and a good credit score. Here are some important dos and don’ts on how to manage EMI in the best possible manner: Dos Create a monthly budget Track your income, expenses, and EMIs to ensure timely payments without straining your finances. Set up auto-debit or reminders If you don’t want to miss due dates, set payment reminders or enable the auto-debit facility. Maintain an emergency fund You can experience financial issues like medical emergencies or job loss at any time. Remember to create an emergency fund and keep EMI payments for 3 to 6 months. Consider pre-payment when possible Use bonuses or extra income to prepay your loan, reducing the outstanding principal and future EMIs. Keep a watch on your loan statements If you want to be sure that the right EMI amount is deducted from your account each month, you must review your loan statement frequently. Don’ts Don’t miss or delay payments Late or missed EMIs attract penalties and can negatively impact your credit score. Don’t take multiple loans simultaneously If you have secured multiple loans, it can increase your financial stress. The risk of defaults may also increase. Don’t ignore interest rate changes For floating-rate loans, monitor rate fluctuations and consider refinancing if rates drop significantly. Don’t depend on minimum payments alone Instead of making the minimum payment, pay the full EMI to avoid increasing the repayment timeline or accumulating interest. EMI stands for Equated Monthly Installment. It’s a fixed monthly payment that helps you repay loans in manageable portions over time. EMIs are important because they simplify loan repayment, maintain financial discipline, and make big expenses like homes, cars, or education affordable through structured payments. How is EMI calculated, and can I calculate it myself? EMI is calculated using the formula: EMI = [P × R × (1+R)ⁿ] / [(1+R)ⁿ–1], where P is the loan amount, R is the monthly interest rate, and N is the tenure in months. You can easily calculate EMI yourself using this formula or an online EMI calculator provided by lenders. What happens if I miss an EMI payment? Missing an EMI payment can lead to penalties, late fees, and a negative impact on your credit score. If you default continuously, it can also result in legal action or repossession of the financed asset. It’s advisable to inform your lender in advance and seek a grace period or restructuring option if needed. Can I pay my EMI online with Tata Capital? Yes, Tata Capital allows convenient online EMI payments through its website, mobile app, or auto-debit facilities. Customers can also use methods like NetBanking, UPI, debit cards, or e-wallets to ensure timely and hassle-free EMI payments each month. Is there a difference between EMI and SIP? Yes. An EMI (Equated Monthly Installment) is a repayment made toward a loan, while an SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) is a regular investment made in mutual funds. EMIs reduce debt, whereas SIPs help build wealth over time through disciplined monthly investments. What is No Cost EMI, and is it really free of interest? A No Cost EMI allows you to pay for a product in installments without extra interest. However, the cost may be adjusted by offering discounts or removing upfront benefits. It’s not always entirely interest-free, so checking the total payable amount before purchase is important. Are EMI payments eligible for tax benefits in India? Yes, certain EMI payments qualify for tax benefits. For instance, home loan EMIs allow tax deductions under Sections 80C (principal) and 24(b) (interest) of the Income Tax Act. However, EMIs for personal, car, or consumer loans generally do not offer tax benefits. How can I reduce my EMI amount? You can reduce your EMI by opting for a longer tenure, bargaining for a lower interest rate, making a larger down payment, or transferring your loan to another lender offering better terms. Regular pre-payments also reduce the principal amount, helping lower future EMIs. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Housing market prices have skyrocketed in the last few months. However, it hasn’t led to a steep decline in either demand or sales. Instead, a majority of new home buyers, even young and first-time buyers, have set their hearts on mid-end (Rs. 40 – Rs. 80 lakhs) and high-end (Rs. 80 – Rs. 1.5 crores) properties. One of the factors behind this has been the simplicity of getting a home loan : It begins with interested property buyers applying for a housing loan. The loan is then sanctioned by the lender (bank or other financial institutions) after thorough verification of the borrower’s background, documents, CIBIL score , etc. Finally, the loan is disbursed. In this article, we will go through the home loan sanction and disbursement process in detail for the benefit of individuals who might be interested in taking a home loan. What is a Home Loan Sanction Letter? A home loan sanction letter is the formal document that confirms the lender has approved your loan application. It is the lender’s official commitment, in principle, to fund you, issued after your eligibility, credit history, and documents have cleared appraisal. It is not the release of money; it is the approval that makes the release possible. The letter records every key term of the approval. What is a Home Loan Disbursement Letter? A home loan disbursement letter is the document the lender issues when the approved loan amount is actually released. Where the sanction letter records the approval, the disbursement letter records the payment. It typically states the amount disbursed, the date of disbursement, the mode of payment, and the beneficiary, usually the seller or builder rather than the borrower. For under-construction properties funded in tranches, a disbursement letter accompanies each release, stating the installment amount and the cumulative amount disbursed so far. The letter also anchors your repayment: pre-EMI interest or EMIs are calculated with reference to the disbursed amount and date it records. Keep every disbursement letter safely filed, as they serve as proof of payment during property registration, tax filing, and any future dispute or balance transfer. How does the home loan sanction and disbursement process work? As already mentioned, it’s up to the bank to approve any loan application after verifying the applicant’s background, required documents , and CIBIL score. The “quantum of loan” that can be approved also depends on these factors. Once the application is sanctioned, the bank will issue a home loan sanction letter, which will include details regarding the loan amount, tenure, and interest rate, and other relevant information regarding the loan for the rest of the home loan disbursement process. Application & Credit Appraisal : You submit the loan application along with KYC, income, and property documents. The lender then evaluates your CIBIL score, income stability, and existing liabilities to assess repayment capacity and decide the loan amount you qualify for. Loan Sanctioning : If the appraisal clears, the lender issues a sanction letter stating the approved loan amount, interest rate, tenure, and terms. You review, sign, and return the acceptance copy within the letter’s validity period. Legal & Technical Verification : The lender’s legal team examines the property’s ownership chain, title documents, and encumbrance status, while the technical team inspects the property’s construction quality and assigns a market valuation. Down Payment & Agreement : You pay your own contribution, typically 10 to 20% of the property cost, directly to the seller or builder, and sign the final loan and mortgage agreements along with any pre-disbursement formalities. Fund Disbursement : The lender releases the funds as a lump sum for ready-to-move or resale properties, or in stage-wise tranches linked to construction progress for under-construction properties. Also, read – Home loan sanction letter vs disbursement explained Housing loan sanction process When the bank approves a loan, it indicates that the borrower can now confirm the booking of the property and make the down payment. Sanctioning of the home loan depends on the applicant’s income. Banks usually sanction 80 to 90% of the property value as a loan, depending on the loan size and the lender’s loan-to-value policy. Documents Required for Home Loan Sanction Documentation is where sanction timelines are won or lost. The lender uses these documents to verify your identity, confirm your income, and validate the property, so a complete set submitted upfront moves the application through appraisal in one pass. Keep the following ready: Applicant’s photograph Legal certificates pertaining to purchasing the property Identity proof Residence proof The latest salary slip, validated by the office and attested by the applicant himself Six months’ bank statement Form 16/ income tax return Also, read – Personal Loan Sanction Letter: Meaning, Format, Importance & Validity Home loan process after sanction After the home loan has been sanctioned, the housing loan disbursement process takes place. The actual disbursement is done through the home loan cheque disbursement process. The cheque is issued in favor of the seller of the property, which is handed over after the actual process of registration. Step-by-step home loan disbursement process The housing loan disbursement steps are as follows: Issuance of the loan sanction letter: The lender approves the loan after evaluating eligibility, credit score, and documents. Acceptance of the sanction letter: You sign and accept the loan terms and conditions. Legal and technical verification: The lender verifies property documents and construction status. Agreement execution: You sign the loan and mortgage agreements. Fulfillment of pre-disbursement conditions: You submit the required documents and pay applicable charges, such as processing fees and other administrative charges. Disbursement of loan amount: The funds are released in a lump sum or stages, based on property type and construction progress. Home loan disbursement stages There are multiple stages (usually three) in the home loan disbursement when the lender disburses loans in installments. Disbursement in installments is usually done when the property being purchased is an under-constructed one. The payments are made depending on the stage of construction of the property. The full journey to disbursement runs in two phases: 1. The Pre-Disbursement Stages Application : You submit the loan application with KYC, income, and property documents, giving the lender everything needed to begin appraisal. Sanctioning : The lender evaluates your profile and issues the sanction letter, which you accept within its validity period. Legal and Technical Verification : The property’s title, approvals, and construction status are verified, and its value is assessed. Disbursement cannot begin until both checks are clear. 2. The Disbursement Process Stages Agreement Execution : You sign the loan and mortgage agreements, legally binding both sides to the sanctioned terms. Own Contribution : You pay your margin money to the seller or builder and submit proof of payment, since lenders release their share only after yours is in. Release of Funds : The lender disburses the amount, in full for ready properties or in construction-linked tranches for under-construction ones, and repayment begins as per the schedule. Home loan disbursement criteria A bank-appointed architect should certify that the proposed construction is in strict adherence to the sanctioned plan. No upfront disbursal of loan should be made to incomplete/ under-construction projects. Disbursement will only depend on the stages of construction of the property. However, projects sponsored by the government or statutory authorities shall enjoy disbursal of loans as deemed fit by any such authorities. Interest Rate Options During Disbursement (Fixed vs Floating) Home loan interest rates come in two types: fixed and floating. A fixed rate stays constant for the agreed period, keeping your EMI fully predictable. It suits borrowers who value certainty and want protection if market rates rise, though fixed rates are typically priced higher at the outset and may carry prepayment charges. A floating rate moves with the lender’s benchmark, so your EMI or tenure adjusts as market rates change. Floating rates usually start lower than fixed rates, benefit you when rates fall, and generally carry no prepayment penalty for individual borrowers, which makes early repayment easier. Tata Capital offers home loans at competitive interest rates with flexible repayment options; check the current rates on the Tata Capital home loan rates and charges page before applying, and match the rate type to how long you plan to hold the loan.
