It reflects your repayment behavior and overall creditworthiness, and plays a crucial role in loan approvals, credit card eligibility, and overall financial credibility. It is imperative to understand how credit scores work, how long it may take to improve them, and the different phases of credit score recovery. Learn the practical ways to improve a low score, factors that affect score updates, and tips for maintaining healthy credit habits. While small improvements may occur within a few weeks, a major recovery usually requires consistent repayment discipline and responsible credit use over time. Regular monitoring and careful financial planning can gradually help build a stronger credit profile. A credit score is a three-digit number ranging from 300 to 900 that reflects your repayment behavior and overall creditworthiness. A low credit score can make borrowing difficult. Whenever you apply for a new loan or credit card , the lender carefully checks your credit report before approving the application. If your credit score is above the required level, you may find it easy to qualify for loans and other credit offerings. Additionally, a high credit score can help you negotiate a lower interest rate and more favorable repayment terms. But what if your credit score isn’t up to the mark? Well, you can always take steps to improve it before re-applying for a loan. The question is, how many days will it take to increase the CIBIL score? The answer is not always the same for everyone. The improvement timeline can depend on factors such as repayment behavior, pending loans, credit utilization, and dispute resolution updates. In this blog, we will explain how much time it takes to improve the CIBIL score and what steps you can take to do so faster. What is a credit score? A credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment behavior. It helps lenders understand how responsibly you have handled debt in the past. In India, a credit score can range between 300 and 900. A higher score means you have repaid your dues on time and have a clean credit history. It improves your chances of getting loans and credit cards at favorable terms. Several credit bureaus in India calculate credit scores based on your credit history and repayment records shared by banks and other financial institutions. Since TransUnion CIBIL is one of the most widely known credit bureaus in the country, people sometimes refer to a credit score as a “ CIBIL score .” Why does your credit score matter? Your credit score is considered one of the most important financial indicators because it reflects your repayment behavior and overall credit discipline. Banks and financial institutions in India typically review this score before approving loans, credit cards, or other credit products. A good credit score may improve your chances of faster approvals and better borrowing terms, while a low score may become a hurdle in availing credit facilities. Furthermore, a healthy credit score can help you secure loans at lower interest rates and favorable repayment terms. Most lenders are willing to provide credit to financially credible individuals, even if it means relaxing certain lending conditions. Also, read – 800 Credit Score Benefits 7 Ways To Improve Credit Score in 30 Days Boosting your credit score in such a short time seems may seem like a tall order. However, with the right amount of financial discipline and commitment, you will be able to see improvements in your score. 1. Never Delay Another Bill Payment The first and foremost answer to how to improve credit score in 30 days is by paying your credit card, loan EMIs or any other bills on time. Even better would be to clear these bills a couple of days before the due date. Doing this will have a twofold effect. Firstly, it will prove solvency, which is key in quickly improving the credit score. Secondly, it will make you eligible for higher credit limits, which in turn boosts your credit score. Therefore, be it your utility payments, credit card bills, or monthly installments , never delay, or worse, default on a bill payment. 2. Get a Credit Card It’s simple! How to improve credit score fast is irrelevant, if you don’t have any credit history – means you are a fresher. No credit history equals no high/low credit score. This may initially sound like a good thing, but it can be detrimental when the time comes to take any type of loan . Having a credit history is not a bad thing. In fact, it works like a report card of your creditworthiness and lets future lenders trust you with high loan amounts at low-interest rates. Therefore, get a credit card, regardless of whether you will use it or not. It is anyway a mode to secure interest-free credit for often 45 days, if not more. And, allows you to, first, receive a credit score and, secondly, improve it. If you are a first-timer who wants to get a credit card, refer to tip number five in this article. 3. Bring Down Credit Utilization Ratio This expert tip on how to improve credit score in 30 days also works for individuals who have a relatively high score and want to ensure it stays that way, even if they end up delaying one or two bill payments. One of the hidden secrets to improving credit score in 30 days is to keep your credit utilization below 30%. So, suppose your credit limit is Rs. 1 lakh, and you want to boost it quickly; avoid spending more than Rs. 30,000 on your card – just until your CIBIL score goes up. By doing this, not only will you raise your CIBIL score fast, but you will also end up repaying your bills on time and practicing financial discipline. 4. Request to Increase Credit Card Limit Once you have managed to keep your credit utilization below or up to 30%, play your second move, which is to request a higher credit limit. Getting approved for a higher credit card limit signifies you as a responsible user, which is a great way to improve credit score quickly. If you have been repaying your bills on time and keeping your utilization under 30%, most lenders will happily bump your credit limit. Some issuers even allow you to increase your credit limit online. However, keep in mind that just because the issuer has increased your credit limit, you must continue using only 30% of the total limit and not get tempted by the raise. 5. Opt for a Cash-Backed Credit Card Perhaps the easiest reply to how to improve credit score fast is by opting for a cash-backed credit card. You can do this by depositing a one-time amount which is the same as your credit limit or slightly lower. This provides a bulletproof guarantee of repayment, which is an excellent way to improve credit score fast. Opting for a secured credit card is also a great way to get a credit card for first-time users with no credit history and, therefore, may not get one quickly. 6. Don’t Buy Multiple Credit Cards/Loans A key strategy to improve credit score fast is not to have multiple credit cards or loans simultaneously. Though numerous credit cards or loans could help borrowers tide over their financial needs, it is not prudent to have various debts together. Lenders consider borrowers with multiple obligations short on credit, which could hamper their potential repaying capability. If a borrower fails to repay numerous debts on time, this could negatively impact their credit score. So, avoid having multiple credit cards or loans at one time or maintain a time gap between various debts. It will help improve their credit score. 7. Track Credit Report Credit score forms part of the comprehensive credit report issued by India’s four authorized credit bureaus: CIBIL Equifax, Highmark™ and Experian. Regular tracking of the credit report will bring any inconsistencies or errors to the notice of the concerned bureau or authority. Getting the same rectified immediately is another way to improve credit score in 30 days. Otherwise, errors or mistakes in credit reports negatively impact the credit score. How long does it take to improve a CIBIL score? There is no fixed answer to how much time it takes to improve a CIBIL score, as it may vary from person to person. The CIBIL score increase time usually depends on factors such as repayment history, pending dues, credit utilization, loan defaults, and overall credit behavior. For some individuals, noticeable improvement may happen within a few weeks or months after clearing outstanding dues and maintaining disciplined repayments. In more serious cases involving defaults or settlements, complete improvement may take much longer. In general, it may take anywhere from 30 days to 12 months to significantly improve a credit score. Also, read – How To Improve Credit Score In 30 Days? CIBIL score improvement timeline Banks and financial institutions usually report your loan and credit card activity to TransUnion CIBIL once every month. Because of this, any changes in your credit behavior may not reflect immediately in your credit report. In most cases, changes in the CIBIL score may take around 30 to 45 days to appear after the latest reporting cycle. However, major credit score improvement usually occurs gradually in phases, depending on the severity of the issue and the corrective steps the borrower takes. ● Quick improvement (1-2 months) Minor credit issues may sometimes be corrected quickly. For example, paying a pending credit card bill, clearing a missed EMI, reducing your credit utilization ratio, or correcting an error in the credit report may result in noticeable improvement within one or two months. Since lenders update credit activity monthly, positive changes may start reflecting after the next credit score update date. ● Moderate improvement (3-6 months) If the credit score has been affected by repeated missed EMIs or delayed payments over several months, improvement may take longer. During this phase, borrowers usually need to maintain regular repayments, reduce outstanding dues, avoid delays, and consistently build a stable repayment track record. Gradual improvement may become visible over three to six months with disciplined credit behavior. ● Long-term growth (6-12 months) Severe credit issues such as loan defaults, settlements, write-offs, or bankruptcy can take much longer to recover from. In such situations, the timeline to improve the score may range from six months to one year, or even longer in some cases. During this period, borrowers should focus on clearing outstanding dues, paying EMIs on time, maintaining low credit utilization, and avoiding frequent loan or credit card applications. Also, read – What Does a 777 Credit Score Mean? What are the key factors that affect your credit score? Several factors go into the calculation of your credit score. These include: Repayment history : It is the most crucial factor that impacts your credit score. Missed or late EMI/credit card bill payments can severely damage your credit score. Credit utilization ratio : It is the ratio of credit used to total available credit. A high credit utilization ratio indicates dependency on debt and can hurt your credit score. Credit mix : Maintaining a healthy mix of different credit types, including personal loans , auto loans , home loans , and credit cards, can actually improve your credit score. Credit inquiries : Whenever you apply for a new loan or a credit card, the lender conducts a hard inquiry on your credit report. It can temporarily lower your credit score. Age of credit : The age of your credit account shows how long you have been a responsible borrower. The longer the age, the better it reflects on your credit score. How to improve your CIBIL score faster? If your credit score is low and lenders are rejecting your loan or credit card applications , it does not mean your financial journey has come to an end. You can actually improve a damaged credit score with disciplined financial habits and consistent repayment behavior. While the process may take time, consistently following a few practical steps can gradually strengthen your credit profile and improve your chances of getting loans in the future. Here are a few tips you can follow: ● Pay EMIs and bills on time This is very important. Make it a habit to pay all your loan EMIs and credit card bills on time. If you tend to forget the due dates, you can set reminders on your smartphone. You can also sign up for auto-payment of EMIs and bills directly from your bank account through NACH mandate . Even a single instance of missed or delayed payment can severely hurt your CIBIL score. ● Reduce credit card usage As mentioned, a high credit utilization ratio reflects your dependency on debt. It, in turn, hurts your credit score. Thus, you should always aim to keep your credit utilization ratio at or below 30%. One of the best ways to do this is to reduce your credit card usage. Make payments from your savings bank account or debit card instead. If you have multiple credit cards, use all of them judiciously. ● Maintain a balanced credit mix Too much dependency on unsecured borrowing may have a negative impact on your CIBIL score. On the other hand, having a balanced mix of secured and unsecured credits can help improve your credit score significantly. So, if you have already opted for unsecured loans, such as personal loans and credit cards, consider availing secured credit options if needed in future, such as an FD-backed credit card or a loan against gold. ● Keep old accounts active The length of your credit history also influences your CIBIL score. Closing old credit cards or long-standing loan accounts may unnecessarily reduce the score. On the flip side, keeping such accounts active and using them responsibly may help strengthen your credit profile. It demonstrates long-term repayment discipline to credit bureaus. ● Check your credit reports frequently Sometimes, your CIBIL score might get hurt due to no fault of yours. It might happen due to incorrect entries or because the credit bureau confused you with someone with a similar name or address. Frequently checking your credit reports can help you identify such discrepancies and report them to the bureau immediately. In most cases, the CIBIL dispute resolution time ranges from a few days to a month. ● Avoid too many loan applications Each time you apply for a new loan or a credit card, the lender pulls your credit report for a hard inquiry. This, in turn, lowers your CIBIL score. Although the drop is temporary, it’s better to avoid applying for too many loans unless you genuinely need them. Frequent loan or credit card applications may also make you appear credit-hungry in the eyes of the bureaus. ● Use credit responsibly Responsible credit behavior plays a major role in the long-term improvement of your CIBIL score. Borrow only what you can comfortably repay. Avoid unnecessary debt accumulation. If you are using credit cards or overdraft loans, avoid maxing out the limits. Financial discipline, along with timely repayment of debts, helps in building a lender’s confidence in you. ● Manage credit limits smartly If you have a higher available credit limit, it does not mean you should use it unnecessarily. Doing so can not only hurt your CIBIL score but also lead to needless spending. It, in turn, derails your overall financial planning. On the other hand, controlled usage of credit limits may positively influence your CIBL score in the long run. Also, read – Personal loan for CIBIL score of 550 How long does it take to get your CIBIL report? You can get your CIBIL report through a quick and simple process. The simplest option is to visit the official TransUnion CIBIL website and request a CIBIL report. This report consists of your credit score, active credit accounts, credit utilization ratio, repayment history, and the overall status of your financial health. You may have to pay a nominal fee, and the report becomes available for download within a few minutes. Some popular online platforms and mobile applications even allow you to access your credit reports for free. The timeline to get your reports may range from a few minutes to a few days, depending on the platform. Additional tips to maintain a healthy credit score Here are a few additional tips that can help you maintain a healthy CIBIL score: Always pay your loan EMIs and credit card bills before the due date. Do not wait for the last minute. Avoid using your credit cards up to their limits. Distribute your spending across multiple cards. Keep checking your credit report for errors or suspicious activity. If you have reported an error, check again when the CIBIL score is updated. Maintain a proper balance between income, expenses, and debt obligations. Set aside a portion of your earnings for debt repayments. Build an emergency fund to avoid missing payments during financial difficulties. Use credit only when necessary and borrow within your repayment capacity. Final thoughts on improving your credit score Your credit score is one of the most crucial financial parameters. It reflects your creditworthiness in the lender’s eyes and determines whether you can avail of loans. A low credit score can result in the rejection of your application, whereas a good credit score can help you secure financing at favorable terms. If your credit score is not up to the mark, you can take steps to improve it gradually. These may include paying your outstanding dues on time, maintaining a low credit utilization ratio, keeping old credit accounts active, and using credit limits responsibly. But remember, the process may take time, and the exact timeline to rebuild your credit score depends on the extent of the damage and the corrective steps you take. The time required to reach a 750 CIBIL score depends on your current credit profile and repayment history. For some people, it may take a few months, while for others with major defaults or missed payments, it may take much longer with regular financial discipline and timely repayments. How much can a CIBIL score improve in one month? A CIBIL score may improve slightly within one month if you clear pending dues, reduce credit card usage, or correct errors in the credit report. However, large improvements usually take more time because banks generally update credit activity once every month. Can I improve my CIBIL score in 30 days? Yes, small improvements may happen within 30 days if you make timely payments, lower outstanding balances, and avoid missing EMIs. However, complete recovery from a poor credit history usually takes longer and requires consistent financial discipline over several months. How often is the CIBIL score updated? Banks and financial institutions generally report your credit activity to credit bureaus once every month. Because of this, your CIBIL score is usually updated monthly, although the exact timing may vary depending on the lender and reporting cycle. What is the fastest way to improve a credit score? The fastest way to improve a credit score is to pay EMIs and credit card bills on time, reduce credit utilization, and clear pending dues. Regular repayments and responsible credit usage can gradually help improve the score over the next few update cycles. Does checking my CIBIL score affect it? No, checking your own CIBIL score does not negatively affect it. This is known as a soft inquiry and is only meant for personal review. However, repeated loan or credit card applications may result in hard inquiries that can slightly affect the score. What is a good CIBIL score for loan approval? It depends on the lender. A CIBIL score of around 750 or above is generally considered good by many lenders in India. A higher score may improve the chances of faster loan approval, lower interest rates, and better repayment terms. However, the approval chances also depend on income and repayment capacity. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund ELSS mutual funds, meaning Equity Linked Savings Schemes, are equity mutual funds that allocate at least 80% of their assets to stocks. They have the potential for long-term wealth creation. Moreover, ELSS mutual funds offer tax deductions of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, provided you opt for the old tax regime. There is a 3-year lock-in period, which is the shortest among all other tax-saving options. ELSS mutual funds allocate a major part of the money into equity and equity-related instruments and offer tax-saving benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. ELSS mutual funds’ full form is Equity Linked Savings Scheme. The equity mutual fund offers a deduction of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh under Section 80C and has a 3-year lock-in period. However, this tax benefit is available only under the old tax regime. What is ELSS? If you are wondering what an ELSS mutual fund is, it is an Equity Linked Savings Scheme. As per SEBI guidelines, it requires an allocation of at least 80% in equity and equity-related instruments. Also Read – Old vs New Tax Regime Explained Does ELSS still save tax in 2026? Yes, but only for some taxpayers. The ELSS tax deduction is available only under the old tax regime. However, since the new tax regime is now the default, many taxpayers cannot claim this benefit. Additionally, from 1 April 2026, under the Income Tax Act, 2025, the old Section 80C has been renumbered as Section 123 (read with Schedule XV). This does not change the deduction limit of Rs. 1.5 lakh, but the section number has changed. How ELSS saves tax: A worked example Here’s an example to understand how an ELSS mutual fund saves taxes. Old tax regime New tax regime ELSS investment: Rs. 1,50,000 ELSS investment: Rs. 1,50,000 Section 123 deduction: Rs. 1,50,000 Deduction: NIL Tax slab: 30% Tax slab: 30% Tax saved: Rs. 45,000 Tax saved: 0 Health and education cess saving : Rs. 1,800 (4% of 45,000) Health and education cess saving :0 Total tax saving: Rs. 46,800 Total tax saving: Rs. 0 How much tax do you pay when you exit ELSS? ELSS returns are not tax-free upon redemption. After the 3-year lock-in period, all gains are Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG). As of FY 2026-2027, the LTCG taxation rate is 12.5% on gains above Rs. 1.25 lakh in a financial year. This Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption applies to your total equity gains, not each fund. Thus, it is advisable that you spread redemptions across different financial years to help keep gains within the exemption limit. Read More – How to Save Income Tax in India What is the ELSS lock-in period of 3 years? ELSS has a 3-year lock-in period. However, if you invest through an SIP, each installment has its own 3-year lock-in from its investment date. So, if your first installment was made in January 2026 and the second in July 2026, you can redeem the first after January 2029 and the second after July 2029. What are the ELSS vs other Section 80C options? Feature Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) Public Provident Fund (PPF) Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) 5-Year tax-saving Fixed Deposit National Savings Certificate (NSC) Lock-in 3 years 15 years Till retirement/withdrawal rules 5 years 5 years Returns Market-linked Government-backed, fixed Government-declared Fixed Fixed Risk High – capital value can rise or fall Very low Very low Low Low Capital safety Not guaranteed Guaranteed by the government Backed by EPF rules Principal protected Principal protected Taxation on exit LTCG tax applies as per prevailing rules Generally tax-free Generally tax-free if conditions are met Interest is taxable Interest is taxable Who should consider ELSS – and who should not? An ELSS mutual fund may be suitable for: Taxpayers who opted for the old tax regime. Investors with a moderate-to-high risk appetite. People who can stay invested for more than 3 years. An ELSS mutual fund may NOT be suitable for: Anyone who has opted for the new tax regime. Anyone who may need the money within 3 years, since there is no premature withdrawal. Anyone investing only to save tax without considering their overall equity allocation and the associated risk. How to invest in ELSS? After understanding ELSS mutual funds’ meaning, you need to learn how to invest in it. Here’s the required step-by-step process: Complete your KYC and choose the best ELSS mutual fund, suiting your financial goals and risk appetite. Invest through an SIP or lump sum. Most ELSS funds let you start with Rs. 500. A year-round SIP reduces market timing risk compared with making a lump-sum investment just before the tax-saving deadline. Track your investment using the Moneyfy ELSS Calculator and compare options on the Moneyfy Tax Saver (ELSS) Funds page before investing. Conclusion ELSS can help you build long-term wealth while offering tax savings under Section 123 of the Income Tax Act. Before investing, check your tax regime, risk appetite, investment horizon, and overall financial goals. Don’t choose ELSS only for tax benefits, as its returns after the 3-year lock-in period still attract taxes at 12.5%. Build Your Wealth with Expert Guidance from Tata Capital! The old tax regime allows a deduction of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh under Section 80C every financial year. This reduces your taxable income and the resulting payable taxes. Can I claim ELSS under the new tax regime? No. There are no applicable deductions for ELSS mutual funds under the new tax regime. Is ELSS tax-free on redemption? No. ELSS returns are subject to Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) as per the tax rules applicable at the time of redemption. How does the 3-year lock-in work for an ELSS SIP? The 3-year lock-in period applies to every ELSS installment individually. So, if you make an SIP investment in July 2026, you can only redeem it after July 2029. Is ELSS still valid after the Income Tax Act 2025? The Income Tax Act 2025 has renumbered Section 80C as Section 123. However, deductions on ELSS mutual funds still apply under the old tax regime. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Wondering how home loan repayment works? Read on. As a home buyer, you know how housing loans have benefits manifold. Whether you want to purchase a property, construct one, buy a plot, or extend your existing home, housing finance can help. However, equally important is making timely EMI payments and closing the loan on time. So, here’s a guide to home finance repayment . How Home Loan Repayment Works After you apply for a loan, you start repayment in the form of Equated Monthly Instalments (EMIs) . An EMI is a sum you pay back to the lender monthly. The monthly instalment comprises two components- the principal amount and interest applicable divided monthly across the loan tenure you choose. Here, an extended loan tenure translates into smaller EMIs. However, the longer the loan term, the higher your interest payable. Hence, it’s important to consider your monthly repayment capacity while applying for a loan . For comfortably repaying the home loan , here are a few repayment options available. Also, read – How to repay your home loan faster Home Loan Repayment Options in India: EMI, Step-Up & Flexible Plans Choosing the right repayment for home loan style can make your journey far more comfortable. Lenders offer flexible home loan repayment options designed to suit different income patterns and life stages. The most common choice is the standard EMI method, where monthly payments remain consistent and predictable, helping you plan home loan repayments with ease. If you are early in your career and expect your income to grow, a step-up repayment plan lets you start with lower EMIs and increase them gradually. If you earn more now but expect income to reduce later, a step-down repayment plan allows higher EMIs initially and lower payments in the future. Understanding these housing loan repayment options gives clarity on how home loan repayment works and ensures your chosen method aligns well with the overall home loan repayment process and your financial status. Every home loan gives you more than one way to structure your EMI, and picking the right one comes down to how your income is likely to move over the loan tenure. Here is a closer look at the seven repayment structures you are most likely to come across. 1. Standard EMI (Equated Monthly Installment) This is the default option on almost every home loan. You pay the same EMI every month for the entire tenure, with the principal and interest split recalculated internally as the loan ages. It suits salaried borrowers with a steady, predictable income, since budgeting stays simple from the first EMI to the last. 2. Step-Up Repayment Scheme Under Tata Capital’s Step-Up Flexi EMI Plan, you start with a lower EMI and it increases at set intervals over the tenure. For example, a starting EMI of ₹25,000 may step up to ₹30,000 after two years and ₹35,000 after four. This suits borrowers early in their career who expect their income to rise, and it can also help you qualify for a higher loan amount at the outset, since the initial outflow is lower. 3. Step-Down Repayment Scheme A step-down plan works the other way round. EMIs start higher and reduce at intervals through the tenure. It suits borrowers closer to retirement, or a loan where a parent and child combine incomes and the parent’s contribution is expected to taper off. Note that this option is less commonly advertised among lenders’ current standard offerings compared to step-up plans, so it’s worth confirming availability with your lender before you apply. 4. Pre-EMI Option For an under-construction property, the loan is usually disbursed in three to six tranches as construction progresses. Under the Pre-EMI option, you pay interest only on the amount disbursed so far, not the full sanctioned loan. Once the property is complete and the full amount is disbursed, regular EMIs covering both principal and interest begin. This keeps outflow low during construction, though it does mean paying interest for longer overall, since pre-EMI months sit outside the loan’s regular tenure. 5. Full EMI Option (Tranche-Based EMI) This is the alternative to Pre-EMI on the same tranche-based disbursement. Instead of paying interest only, you start paying full EMIs, principal and interest, on each tranche as soon as it is disbursed, even before the property is complete. Your total interest cost over the loan is lower than with Pre-EMI, since principal repayment begins earlier, though your monthly outflow during construction is higher. 6. Home Loan Overdraft / Smart Saver Tata Capital’s home loan overdraft facility links your loan to an overdraft account. Any surplus you park in that account reduces the loan balance that interest is calculated on, while remaining withdrawable whenever you need it. For example, parking a ₹2 lakh surplus against a ₹20 lakh outstanding loan means interest is charged only on ₹18 lakh. The trade-off is that overdraft-linked home loans typically carry a slightly higher interest rate than a standard loan, so it suits borrowers who can consistently maintain a surplus rather than an occasional one. 7. Accelerated Repayment / Prepayment Strategy This involves paying more than your scheduled EMI, whether as a lump sum or a part-prepayment, to bring down the principal faster. Since floating-rate home loans in India carry no prepayment penalty for individual borrowers, this is one of the more accessible ways to cut both tenure and total interest, especially when done in the earlier years of the loan. Factors Affecting Home Loan Repayment Amount Several factors decide how much you end up paying each month and over the life of the loan. Loan amount and down payment : A larger down payment means a smaller principal to borrow, which directly lowers your EMI and the total interest paid over the tenure. Interest rate: Even a small difference in rate compounds significantly over a 15-30 year tenure, so it’s worth comparing lenders before you commit. Loan tenure: A longer tenure lowers the EMI but increases the total interest paid, while a shorter tenure does the opposite. This is one of the biggest levers on affordability, so it’s worth comparing a few tenure lengths on an EMI calculator before you choose the right home loan tenure for yourself. Credit score: A stronger score can help you secure a lower interest rate on home loan , which lowers your EMI for the same loan amount. Repayment plan chosen: Standard, step-up, step-down, or overdraft-linked loans all produce a different EMI pattern for the same principal. Home Loan Prepayment and Foreclosure Options You also have the option to repay your loan partly through loan prepayment. With this, you essentially make partial loan repayments with incentives or bonuses you receive at work or any extra funds to lower your overall principal amount. Additionally, check for the part-prepayment charges with your lender beforehand. Besides, in your initial years of repayment, the interest component repaid is higher as opposed to the latter years of repayment when the principal component is higher. By prepaying a sizeable amount, you save significantly on your repayment costs. How to Access Your Home Loan Repayment Details Online You do not need to call your lender or visit a branch to check your repayment status. Tata Capital’s retail customer portal gives existing borrowers direct access to their loan account. Go to the Retail Customer Login section on tatacapital.com. Log in with your registered User ID or mobile number, then complete OTP verification. Once logged in, you can view your loan account, check your outstanding balance, and see your repayment schedule. You can also download your loan statement or interest certificate directly from the portal, which is useful when filing taxes or applying for another loan. If you need a revised repayment schedule after a part-prepayment or EMI date change, the updated version is also available for download once your request is processed. Complete Home Loan Repayment Process Step-by-Step Understanding how does loan repayment work helps you stay confident and in control from day one. Here’s a step-by-step overview of the home loan repayment process, so you always know what to expect and how home loan repayment works in practice. Step 1: After disbursement, your bank sets a repayment schedule based on tenure, interest rate, and EMI amount. This step marks the formal start of the home loan repayment process. Step 2: EMIs must be paid monthly, covering both principal and interest. These payments are usually auto-debited from your bank account to ensure timely home loan repayments, explaining how home loan repayment works overtime. Step 3: As tenure progresses, interest reduces and principal repayment increases. You must keep reviewing your loan statement regularly for any outstanding dues, the interest charged, and repayment progress. Step 4: On full repayment of housing loan, the lender usually issues a No-Dues Certificate (NDC) or a No Objection Certificate (NOC) , signifying the completion of the home loan repayment process smoothly. Also, read – Pay Home Loan EMIs If You Lose Your Job How to Choose the Best Home Loan Repayment Method for You When deciding how to repay a home loan, first look at how stable your income is today and how it may change in the future. If your salary is steady, regular EMIs usually work best. If you expect income growth, flexible options can reduce early pressure. Also consider existing expenses, future plans, and emergency savings so home loan repayments stay manageable. Choosing a method that fits your lifestyle makes the entire home loan repayment process smoother and less stressful. Also, read – Home Loan Prepayment Calculator Guide Tips to Manage Home Loan Repayment Managing your loan smartly can significantly reduce interest burden over time. One of the most effective strategies to manage home loan repayment is making part-prepayments whenever possible, as this directly lowers the principal and speeds up repayment of housing loan. Keeping EMIs aligned with income hikes helps stabilise home loan repayments without lifestyle compromises. Regularly reviewing interest rates offered by your bank can also uncover savings opportunities. Most importantly, maintaining consistency and financial discipline ensures the repayment of housing loan stays smooth, predictable, and far less stressful across the entire loan tenure. These habits fall into three broad groups, depending on what you’re optimising for. Fast-Track Repayment Strategies Paying one extra EMI a year, using a bonus or tax refund, can shave several years off a long tenure without disrupting your monthly budget. Rounding your EMI up to the nearest thousand, or increasing it in line with each salary hike, compounds the same way over time. Smart Interest Optimization Since interest is front-loaded in the early years of a loan, prepaying while the outstanding principal is still high saves more than the same amount prepaid later. It’s also worth periodically comparing your rate against what other lenders offer. If you can lower the interest rate on your home loan by even half a percentage point through negotiation or a balance transfer, the savings compound over the remaining tenure. Financial Safety Nets Don’t use all your spare money for loan prepayments. Keep some aside for emergencies, such as a job loss or unexpected medical expense. That way, you can keep paying your EMIs even when something goes wrong. Paying off the loan faster only helps if you can keep up with your regular payments. Conclusion After understanding how home loan repayment works, it’s important to look for a lender with flexible repayment facilities. With Tata Capital , you can avail of a loan that works for you. The home loan repayment process begins after loan disbursement. You repay the loan through monthly EMIs comprising principal and interest. Payments continue for the chosen tenure until full closure, after which the bank issues a loan completion certificate. What are the different home loan repayment options available? Common home loan repayment options include standard EMIs, step-up plans, step-down plans, and flexible repayment structures. These options help borrowers align home loan repayments with income patterns and long-term financial goals. How does home loan prepayment work and is there a penalty? Prepayment allows partial or full repayment of housing loan before tenure completion. Most lenders do not charge penalties on floating-rate loans. Prepayments reduce interest burden and help you understand better how home loan repayment works in your favour. Does increasing EMI repayment reduce the tenure of my loan? Yes. Increasing your EMI usually reduces the loan tenure rather than the EMI amount. This shortens the home loan repayment process and lowers total interest, making it an effective way to close your loan faster. Which home loan repayment option is best for first-time buyers? For first-time buyers, regular EMIs or step-up plans are usually suitable. These options simplify how home loan repayment works, keep early payments manageable, and provide stability while adjusting to long-term financial commitments. What is the 2% rule in repaying home loans? This is a common personal finance rule. It suggests increasing your EMI by about 2% every year instead of keeping it fixed throughout the loan. The small increase can help you repay the loan faster and reduce the total interest you pay. Can I reduce my home loan tenure without prepayment? Yes, by increasing your EMI amount whenever your income rises, even without a lump-sum prepayment. A higher EMI applies more towards the principal each month, which shortens the tenure. Switching to a shorter tenure at the same EMI level, if your lender permits it, has a similar effect. Is part-prepayment better than EMI increase? Both can lower the interest you pay over the loan term. With part-prepayment, you pay a lump sum toward the principal. Increasing your EMI, on the other hand, means paying more every month. Choose part-prepayment if you have occasional extra funds, or a higher EMI if your income allows you to pay more each month. Can I switch repayment plans during tenure? Some lenders let you change your repayment plan, such as switching from a step-up plan to a standard EMI, if you meet their requirements. Check with your lender, as you may need to submit documents or go through another eligibility check. banks, telecom operators, and fintech companies use to verify your identity. It is remote and paperless. This means that the customer does not need to visit the branch and submit physical paperwork. e-KYC in India is heavily dependent on the Aadhaar system. You can complete Aadhaar-based e-KYC by verifying your identity using the OTP sent to your registered mobile number or through biometric authentication. The process is convenient, with the benefits of enhanced security and instant verification. e-KYC is a modern approach to the traditional KYC process. The digitized process verifies a customer’s identity and address without requiring paper documents. The digital age has modernized many vital services we use daily, upgrading them to be faster and more cost-effective. Among these is e-KYC, or Electronic Know Your Customer. E-KYC is the digital version of the Know Your Customer (KYC) process used in financial institutions. This highly secure and efficient process lets you verify your identity for financial transactions using your Aadhaar number. This article will explore eKYC’s meaning, its types, and the application process. What is e-KYC? Full form & meaning The e-KYC full form is Electronic Know Your Customer. It is a digital service that verifies your identity via Aadhaar authentication. Banks and financial institutions can use e-KYC to verify your identity online. It replaces physical document submission with secure digital verification, making the process faster and more convenient. The e-KYC mechanism is provided by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) and allows instant verification of the Aadhaar number holder’s identity. It is the modern, paperless version of the Know Your Customer protocol mandated for all financial institutions by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). With e-KYC, you can: Verify your identity online Complete KYC with minimal paperwork Get faster access to financial services Enjoy secure digital verification Since e-KYC is a paperless process, it significantly reduces the costs associated with the traditional Know Your Customer process. e-KYC plays an important role in banking. It helps customers quickly and securely verify their identity. The key points of its role in banking are: Speeds up account opening and loan processing Supports paperless banking services Helps prevent fraud and identity theft Ensures compliance with RBI’s KYC regulations eKYC meaning in banking: Why do financial institutions need eKYC? eKYC’s meaning in banking is digitally verifying a customer’s identity without physical documents. Financial institutions need eKYC to speed up account opening, prevent fraud, reduce paperwork, and comply with RBI and government regulations. It also improves customer convenience and security. What are the advantages and benefits of e-KYC in India? After having a clear understanding of e-KYC’s meaning and role in banking, you must learn about e-KYC benefits. The process makes identity verification faster, simpler, and more secure for both customers and service providers. The key benefits of e-KYC in India are: Instant onboarding: e-KYC helps you open bank accounts, apply for loans, buy insurance, or invest in financial products within minutes. There is no need to wait for manual document verification. Paperless convenience: You do not have to fill out lengthy forms or submit physical copies of documents. The entire verification process can be completed online, saving time and effort. Cost-effective: Since e-KYC reduces paperwork, printing, storage, and manual verification, it lowers operational costs for banks and financial institutions. These savings can also improve customer service. Heightened security and fraud reduction: e-KYC uses secure digital verification methods. These include Aadhaar authentication and OTP verification to confirm your identity. This helps reduce identity theft, fake documents, and fraudulent transactions. Strict user consent: Your Aadhaar or personal information can only be accessed after you provide your explicit consent. This gives you greater control over your data and ensures your information is shared only with your approval. What are the types of e-KYC processes in India? There are several types of e-KYC methods used in India to verify a person’s or an organization’s identity. These e-KYC types include: OTP-based e-KYC In this method, you provide your Aadhaar number to get an OTP to your registered mobile number. You then use this OTP to complete the verification process. This type of Aadhaar-based e-KYC is the most convenient type for most people as it requires no biometric data or physical interactions. Biometric-based e-KYC In this method, you provide your Aadhaar number along with biometric data like fingerprints. The provided data is used for verification by matching it with the data stored in the UIDAI database. This type of Aadhaar-based e-KYC ensures high security due to the unique biometric data requirements. Offline e-KYC This method is unique due to its offline nature. You download a digitally signed XML with your demographic details from the official UIDAI website. This XML file can then be provided wherever KYC is required. This method allows you to ensure your privacy without revealing your UID number. Video KYC Video KYC is a digital verification method where your identity is confirmed through a live video call with an authorized representative. You may need to show your original identity documents, answer a few questions, and complete a live photo or signature check. It offers a quick, secure, and paperless KYC experience. Also Read – CKYC: Full form, meaning, process, and key benefits Video KYC: What is it and how does it work? Video KYC (VKYC) is a paperless process that lets you verify your identity through a live video call. It is commonly used by banks, NBFCs , and other financial institutions to complete remote customer verification. During the call, you may be asked to show your Aadhaar, PAN card, or another valid ID. The executive may also ask you to answer a few questions, take a live photo, or display your signature. Once your details are verified, your KYC is completed. Video KYC saves time, reduces paperwork, and lets you complete the verification process from the comfort of your home. What is Aadhaar-based e-KYC: Eligibility, safety & government norms? Aadhaar-based e-KYC allows banks and financial institutions to quickly verify a customer’s identity using their Aadhaar number. It is regulated by UIDAI and follows strict government and RBI guidelines to ensure data security. Individuals who are eligible for eKYC with Aadhaar include Indian residents with a valid Aadhaar number linked to their mobile number. The government ensures that Aadhaar-based e-KYC is a secure system through the following norms: It uses encrypted OTP or biometric authentication. It follows UIDAI consent-based data-sharing rules. It complies with RBI and data privacy guidelines. e-KYC with Aadhaar is a safe and efficient process. It is commonly used by many financial institutions. What are the eligibility criteria for e-KYC registration? Before you learn how to do e-KYC online, make sure you meet the basic eligibility requirements. Most banks, NBFCs, telecom companies, and financial institutions follow these common criteria: You must be an Indian resident. You should have a valid Aadhaar number. Your mobile number must be linked to your Aadhaar. You should have valid identity details. You must give the service provider your consent to access your Aadhaar details for verification. You should meet the provider’s requirements, such as providing additional details like the PAN card or a live selfie. What documents are required for e-KYC in India? As e-KYC is an entirely digital and paperless mechanism, it requires no documentation. You only require your Aadhaar number to get your KYC done online. You will be asked to upload a self-attested copy of your e-Aadhaar to the KYC registration agency (KRA) of your choice. Any other document requirements will be mentioned on the KRA’s portal. Additionally, you may have to provide a passport photograph to avail e-KYC services. How to do e-KYC online: Step-by-step process It is easy to apply for an e-KYC online. Follow the steps given below for a hassle-free e-KYC registration process: Visit any SEBI-licensed KRA’s official website (Know Your Customer Registration Agency). Create your personal account by filling in the required details. Provide your personal details, including your Aadhaar number and registered mobile number. Enter the provided OTP and complete the verification process. Submit a self-attested copy of your Aadhaar card. Visit the KRA’s web portal and input your PAN number to keep up with your application status. e-KYC status: How to check & track your application? Follow the straightforward steps given below to check your e-KYC status: Visit the official Central Depository Service Limited (CDSL) website. Click on ‘Inquire Your KYC.’ Fill in the required details, including your PAN or Aadhaar number. Enter the provided captcha. Click ‘Submit’. After completing this process, your e-KYC verification status will appear. If your application is verified, your status will show as ‘Verified by NDML.’ Otherwise, your status will appear as ‘Pending’. What are the key differences between e-KYC vs regular KYC? Regular and e-KYC in India are both methods to verify customer identity. However, their process and speeds vary. The following table highlights the differences between e-KYC and regular KYC. Parameter eKYC Regular KYC Process Fully digital and paperless Physical documents are required Time taken A few minutes Takes days to process Verification Aadhaar OTP, biometrics, or video In-person or document submission Convenience Higher, can be done online Lower, a branch visit is needed Cost Lower for banks Higher due to manual handling In a nutshell, e-KYC is faster and more convenient, while regular KYC is used when digital verification is not possible. Conclusion The fast, paperless, and secure services provided by e-KYC make it an invaluable mechanism for both customers and organizations. Understanding the meaning of e-KYC will help you benefit from this modern and efficient way to easily verify your identity during financial transactions. E-KYC of Aadhar is an electronic service that verifies your identity using your Aadhar card. This mechanism is provided by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) and provides authenticated instant verification of the Aadhar number holder’s identity. Who is eligible for eKYC? All resident Indian citizens are eligible for e-KYC. The e-KYC process requires an Aadhar card and a linked mobile number. Non-resident Indians and foreigners can also be eligible for e-KYC if they qualify for Aadhar (living in India for 182 days in the twelve months before applying for an Aadhar card). What is the cost of eKYC? The authentication process does not charge any fees. Each e-KYC transaction that involves sharing the e-KYC information of the Aadhar number holder is charged Rs. 20. The 2024 Economic Survey showed that companies have experienced increased ease in the e-KYC process by using Aadhar card services, lowering the cost from Rs. 1,000 to less than six rupees. Is eKYC safe? E-KYC is perfectly safe as it requires customers to go through biometric authentication, including checking for the customer’s photograph, fingerprint, or iris scan. In most cases, customers are asked to submit a selfie, and its authenticity is verified via the latest technology like live facial recognition. What is the eKYC full form and its meaning in banking? eKYC stands for Electronic Know Your Customer. In banking, its purpose is to digitally verify a customer’s identity using Aadhaar or other approved documents without physical paperwork. How to do eKYC online using Aadhaar for a bank account? You can complete eKYC online by entering your Aadhaar number on the bank’s website or app. Verify it through an OTP received on your registered mobile number. Is eKYC through Aadhaar safe? Yes, Aadhaar-based eKYC is generally safe as it uses encrypted systems, OTP or biometric authentication, and follows UIDAI and RBI security guidelines. What are the documents required for eKYC registration in India? Mostly, the Aadhaar is all you need for eKYC registration in India. However, in some cases, you may need to provide your PAN card, Voter’s ID, and mobile number. Can NRIs and foreigners complete Aadhaar-based eKYC in India? NRIs with a valid Aadhaar can use Aadhaar-based eKYC. Foreigners without Aadhaar must complete physical KYC or video KYC as per RBI rules. What is offline eKYC, and how is it different from Aadhaar OTP? Offline eKYC uses a downloaded Aadhaar XML or QR code without sharing Aadhaar details. But Aadhaar OTP eKYC requires real-time OTP verification. Does eKYC require biometric authentication every time? No, eKYC does not always need biometrics. It can be completed using OTP, video KYC, or offline methods, depending on the service provider. What if my eKYC is pending or failed? If your eKYC fails or remains pending, you should check the details and retry the process. You can also contact the bank, which may ask you to complete physical or video KYC. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund If you are eyeing a residential property and contemplating how much home loan you will get on it, you are subconsciously assessing your LTV (Loan-to-Value) ratio. Not sure what we mean? The following section will make things clearer. What is an LTV ratio? The percentage of loan extended by the lender to the borrower against a fixed property value is the housing loan LTV ratio. Lenders typically assess the LTV ratio for home loan to determine the risk of lending a loan to a borrower. The LTV full form is Loan to Value, and your LTV ratio for housing loan will depend on the kind of financial stability you can show to the lender. Housing finance usually covers anywhere between 75% to 90% of the total property cost, while the borrower puts down the rest as a down payment. So, if you are planning on financing a large portion of the property value with the help of housing finance, a higher housing loan LTV ratio will be ideal and vice versa. Remember, a higher LTV ratio for home loan means a bigger loan amount, favourable loan terms, and lower down payment. In contrast, a lower LTV for housing loan indicates a smaller loan amount, with usually a higher down payment. Also, read – What is the OCR amount in a Home Loan? How do LTV ratios work when it comes to housing finance? Multiple factors determine your housing finance eligibility . The most prominent ones are: Stable income High credit score Previous and ongoing debts Let’s look at each of them in detail and figure out where LTV ratio home loan fits in the picture. The higher your income, the better your chances of getting a higher LTV ratio. Meaning, if you make enough money, lenders will be more willing to extend a bigger loan amount, thus boosting your LTV for housing loan. If you have a high CIBIL score , ideally above 750, your chances of getting a loan at a higher LTV ratio also goes up. This doesn’t mean you have to take a large loan. It simply means you are eligible for one. Lenders will calculate the value of your ongoing debt, if any, against the amount of money you earn to approve an LTV ratio for a housing loan. Also, read – What is a Leave and License Agreement? How to Calculate Your Home Loan LTV Ratio (With Example) The Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio shows how much the property’s value is being paid using a home loan. Using this ratio, lenders can judge their risk on the loan. Then they can decide how much loan they can offer, the interest rate, and the down payment. The formula to calculate LTV for home loan is: LTV Ratio (%) = (Loan Amount ÷ Property Value) × 100 Let’s demonstrate how to calculate your home loan LTV ratio using an example. Suppose you are buying a house worth ₹50 lakh, and the bank approves a home loan of ₹35 lakh. The LTV ratio home loan would be: LTV Ratio = (35,00,000 ÷ 50,00,000) × 100 = 70% This means the bank is funding 70% of the property’s value. You must pay the remaining 30% from your own savings as a down payment. In general, a lower LTV ratio is better because it reduces the lender’s risk. Consequently, you could secure the loan on better terms. To make this calculation easier, you can also employ an online LTV calculator. Within the calculator, you can enter the property value and the loan amount you want, and the calculator will instantly show your LTV ratio. Also, read – What is EBLR and Its Impact on Loan Interest Rate? 5 Proven Tips to Improve Your LTV Ratio & Secure Better Loan Terms Improving your LTV in home loan can help you get better home loan terms, such as lower interest rates. Here are five practical ways to improve your LTV ratio home loan: Increase your down payment Paying more money upfront reduces the loan amount compared to the property value. A lower loan amount directly improves your LTV for home loan and makes you a safer borrower in the eyes of lenders. Choose appropriate property Properties in well-developed areas with steady demand are considered less risky. A stable or appreciating property value helps maintain a healthier LTV ratio for housing loan. Pay off existing loans Clearing personal loans or credit card dues improves your financial profile. This can allow you to improve your LTV for housing loan. Check the property valuation carefully If a property is undervalued by the lender, your LTV in home loan ratio may increase. Research the market price properly before applying to avoid approval or interest rate issues. Improve your credit score A good repayment history and strong credit score can help you negotiate better interest rates, even if your LTV ratio is slightly on the higher side. Also, read – What is the Annual Value of House Property? Slabs and upper ceiling for Loan to Value ratio The LTV for housing loan slabs and ceilings for housing finance fall under the purview of the Reserve Bank of India. As per the RBI guidelines: A lending institution can only approve up to 90% LTV if the loan amount goes up to Rs. 30 lakhs. If the total loan amount falls between Rs. 30 lakhs and Rs. 75 lakhs, the LTV ratio for home loan can go up to 80%. For a loan amount higher than Rs. 75 lakhs, the LTV ratio home loan cannot exceed 75%. Also, read – What are Conversion Charges for Home Loans? How LTV Impacts Interest Rates & Loan Tenure LTV for home loan plays an important role in deciding your home loan interest rate and tenure. Lenders use the LTV ratio home loan to measure risk by comparing the loan amount to the property’s value. A higher LTV means the lender is funding a larger portion of the loan. Interest Rates Borrowers with a lower ratio of LTV in home loan are seen as financially stable because they invest more of their own money. So banks often offer lower interest rates and more flexible loan terms to such borrowers. In contrast, a higher LTV ratio for housing loan may lead to slightly higher interest rates. Loan Tenures With a lower housing loan LTV, lenders may be more willing to approve longer repayment periods. Overall, maintaining a good LTV ratio for home loan can help you secure better interest rates, longer tenures, and make loan repayments affordable. The RBI has set some maximum LTV for home loan limits based on property value. For homes costing up to ₹30 lakh, lenders can offer up to 90% LTV, for properties between ₹30–75 lakh, the limit is 80%, and for properties above ₹75 lakh, it is at 75%. How does a higher LTV ratio affect my home loan interest rate? A higher LTV ratio for housing loan means the lender is financing a larger portion of the property value, which increases their risk. Then, due to this added risk, lenders often charge slightly higher interest rates. Lower housing loan LTV ratios make loan interest rates more favourable. Can I get a home loan with an LTV ratio above 90%? LTV for housing loan above 90% is rare. Some banks may allow it for low-value properties or specific schemes, but even in these cases, approval is limited and usually comes with higher interest rates. It’s a good idea to work on your LTV ratio home loan. What documents prove property value for LTV calculation? Lenders use some documents to assess property value for LTV in home loan calculation. These include the sale or title deed, approved building plans, property tax receipts, occupancy or completion certificate, encumbrance certificate, utility bills, and identity and address proof of the borrower. How does LTV differ for under-construction vs ready-to-move properties? RBI housing loan LTV limits are the same for both under-construction and ready-to-move homes. However, lenders often offer lower LTV in home loan for under-construction properties. This is due to delay and completion risks, and applies especially if the project lacks some compliance criteria, or has weak developer credibility. Loans available in India are categorized into different types based on their usage and whether they require collateral. If a loan requires collateral, it is a secured loan; if it doesn’t, it is an unsecured loan. Banks classify loans by purpose into personal loans, home loans, vehicle loans, education loans, business loans, loans against property, loans against securities, etc. When you understand the different types of loans available in India, you can make a wise borrowing decision by choosing the right financing option. Factors influencing your decision include your needs, interest rates, and repayment abilities. There are different types of loans available in India. You must understand these types to be able to secure the financing solution that suits your requirements. The Indian lending market is busier than ever. Today, several banks and NBFC s are eager to offer loans to individuals and businesses who need financial resources. In tandem, people are keen to take advantage of loan schemes as well. Loans provide financial flexibility in managing personal and business finances while retaining existing savings and investments. They help you overcome financial constraints and grab opportunities that may otherwise be out of reach. And thanks to technology, loans are more accessible than ever. Instant online loans can be helpful in several situations, like expanding your business, buying a home or a car, funding higher education, or dealing with unexpected expenses. What’s more, loan schemes also offer tax benefits on the repayment amount. And by repaying your loan in a disciplined manner, you can also increase your credit score, which further boosts your eligibility for future loans. If you need funds to achieve a goal and are wondering if an appropriate loan scheme can help, this article is for you. We have categorized them into secured loans (those that require collateral) and unsecured loans (those that don’t require collateral). Here is your guide to the different types of loans available in India. What is a loan? Definition, features, and how it works A loan is an amount of money you borrow from a bank, lender, or financial institution. You are bound to repay the borrowed amount over time. An interest is also charged on the money that has been lent. Loans help you fulfill goals and purchase what you wouldn’t have otherwise been able to due to financial constraints. For example, you can use a loan to buy a house or vehicle, fund education, or handle emergencies. The key features of a loan are: The borrowed amount is called the principal. Lenders charge interest on the borrowed amount. Loan repayments are made through Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs). Loans have a fixed tenure or repayment period. Loan approval depends on factors such as your credit score and income. When you apply for a loan, the lender reviews your application and approves it after verification. The money is then disbursed into your account. You can start repaying the principal and interest as per the agreed schedule. Continue reading this guide to loans in India to understand the different types and make a smart borrowing decision. What are secured loans in India? A loan where the lender asks you for collateral is a secured loan. The collateral offers the lender security and reduces their risk. When you avail of a secured loan, you get benefits such as lower interest rates, a higher loan amount, easier approval, and longer repayment terms. What are the types of secured loans? Home loans Home loans are ideal if you want to build or purchase a house without compromising on your savings. For this loan, the collateral is the house you are building or buying, and the repayment duration is typically 10 to 30 years from when you build or buy your home. A stable income, a good credit score, and the ability to make the down payment for the house will ensure that you are eligible for a home loan. Another benefit of taking a home loan is that you can claim tax deductions on both the principal amount and the interest payments, as per Section 80C and Section 24B of the Income Tax Act. Loan against property A loan against property is a type of loan where you use a property registered in your name as collateral. This may be a commercial or a residential property. To qualify for a loan against property, the property must meet the valuation criteria set by the lender. The repayment duration for this type of loan is generally 5 to 20 years. You can use a commercial property registered in your or your business’s name as collateral for a loan against commercial property. This type of loan works best for entrepreneurs as it helps them finance and grow their business venture. Vehicle loans A vehicle loan allows immediate access to your dream vehicle while spreading its cost over time. These loans have shorter repayment terms compared to home loans, and the vehicle you purchase is your collateral. To be considered eligible for a vehicle loan, you must have a driver’s license, a stable income with income proof, and a good credit history. Loan against fixed deposits If you hold a fixed deposit, you can use it as collateral for a secured loan. The repayment duration corresponds with the deposit’s tenure. This type of loan is perfect if you need funds in the short term without breaking your fixed deposit prematurely. Gold loan As the name suggests, you can avail of a gold loan by pledging physical gold as collateral. In this case, the loan amount depends on the value and purity of the gold you wish to pledge, and the repayment duration can be anywhere between a few months and a few years. This type of loan allows you to gain access to funds instantly without selling your gold assets. Loan against securities If you have invested in financial securities, you can use them as collateral to avail a loan. You may use mutual funds, bonds, and stocks for this purpose. To be eligible for this loan, the securities must meet the requirements defined by the lender, and the repayment duration also depends on the type of security pledged. This loan gives you liquidity without having to forego the benefits of future securities market growth. Loan against insurance policies You can also use your life insurance or endowment policy to obtain a loan by placing the policy as your collateral. The repayment criteria for a loan against insurance depend on the type of insurance pledged. This loan allows you to retain the benefits of your insurance policy while also procuring funds urgently. Working capital loans A working capital loan is a secured loan that helps businesses manage daily operating expenses. These include salaries, rent, equipment purchases, and utility bills. To obtain the loan, businesses will need to pledge collateral like inventory, equipment, or property. Working capital loans improve cash flow and ensure smooth business operations during periods of low revenue or seasonal fluctuations. What are unsecured loans in India? An unsecured loan is a loan you can avail of without any collateral. The lender considers your creditworthiness to assess if you can repay the loan. They use your credit score and history to determine whether to approve your loan request. The application process for unsecured loans is relatively simple and more accessible. However, with unsecured loans, the lender subjects you to stricter eligibility criteria and charges higher interest rates. What are the different types of unsecured loans available in India? Personal loans Personal loans provide you with funds for various uses. You may use it to pay for an event, a medical emergency, higher education, travel, debt repayment, or home improvement. The eligibility for this loan depends on your credit score, employment status, and income. Credit card loans If you have a credit card, your card provider may offer instant loans against your card. The loan amount depends on your credit limit, while the interest rates and repayment duration are specific to the terms of your credit card provider. Since you are an existing customer, these loans are pre-approved, and there is no need for any paperwork. Short-term business loans A short-term business loan helps businesses meet immediate financial needs. These include managing cash flow, purchasing inventory, or covering operating expenses. Since it is an unsecured loan, you don’t need to provide any collateral. This makes the approval even faster. The repayment period of these loans usually ranges from a few months to a few years and may carry higher interest rates. Education loans An education loan helps students pay for tuition fees, books, accommodation, and other study-related expenses. In many cases, this type of unsecured loan doesn’t require collateral, especially if it involves a smaller loan amount. Loan repayment usually begins after you have completed the course or after a specific moratorium period . This feature of education loans gives students time to find employment and become capable of repaying the loan. What are the key differences between secured and unsecured loans? The following table highlights the differences between secured and unsecured loans : Basis Secured loan Unsecured loan Collateral Requires an asset such as property, gold, or a vehicle as security Does not require any collateral or security Risk for the lender Lower risk because the lender can recover dues from the pledged asset Higher risk since there is no asset backing the loan Interest rate Usually lower due to reduced lender risk Usually higher because of greater lender risk Loan amount Higher loan amounts are generally available Loan amounts are usually lower Approval Depends on the value of the collateral and the borrower’s profile Depends mainly on income, credit score, and repayment capacity What are flexi loans, and how do they work? Flexi loans are one of the different types of loans in India. It gives borrowers access to a pre-approved credit limit. Under this loan type, instead of taking the entire loan amount at once, you can withdraw funds as needed and repay them when you have surplus funds. Lenders charge interest only on the amount used rather than the full limit. This makes flexi loans a flexible and cost-effective option for managing personal or business financial needs while maintaining better control over borrowing costs. What are the key benefits of flexi loans for borrowers? Flexi loans offer several benefits to borrowers by providing greater control over how they use and repay borrowed funds. The key benefits include: Withdraw funds as needed: Borrowers can access money from the approved loan limit whenever required, instead of taking the entire amount at once. Pay interest only on the used amount: Lenders charge interest only on the amount withdrawn, helping reduce borrowing costs. Flexible repayment: You can repay the borrowed amount and withdraw it again, depending on the lender’s terms. Better cash flow management: Flexi loans help manage unexpected expenses and cash shortages without applying for a new loan each time. Quick access to funds: Once a flexi loan is approved, you can access funds quickly, making them an ideal choice during emergencies. Which type of loan has the lowest interest rate in India? In India, you will get the lowest interest rates on secured loans, especially home loans and loans against property. Since these loans are backed by collateral, lenders face less risk and can offer lower rates. You may qualify for even better rates if you have a good credit score , stable income, and strong repayment history. Before applying, you must compare offers from different lenders to find the most affordable loan option for your needs. What are the key factors to consider before taking a loan in India? What is the purpose of the loan? Defining the purpose for which you need a loan is the first step when you start thinking about taking a loan. This way, you know exactly how to use your loan amount and borrow only what you need. Do I have the collateral or eligibility required? Understanding the collateral requirements for a loan is an essential step to choosing the right loan. This clarity helps you determine if you should opt for a secured or an unsecured loan. What repayment tenure and EMI can I comfortably afford? Your tenure, interest rates, and loan amount are based on your financial credibility, availability of collateral, type of collateral, and type of loan. Before you commit, make sure you understand all your loan terms completely. If you find that you cannot afford to repay your loan as per the given loan terms, it is best to wait a while and assess your options. You can compare interest rates among different lenders and ask for longer tenures to reduce the burden of EMI. Are you ready to apply? Find the right loan with Tata Capital Turn to the Tata Capital loan app. We offer a variety of loan schemes for individuals and businesses so that you can fulfill your dreams and achieve your goals with ease. Tata Capital offers competitive interest rates, flexible EMI options, and multi-purpose secured and unsecured loans with minimal documentation. To plan your loan repayment journey, you can use our EMI calculator to estimate your EMI amount and make an informed borrowing decision. Visit the Tata Capital website to learn more, check your eligibility, and apply online. Bottom line To choose from among the various loan types in India, you must consider your financial goals, repayment capacity, and the purpose of borrowing. Secured loans are usually suitable when you need a larger amount at lower interest rates and can provide collateral. Unsecured loans offer faster access to funds without requiring any collateral. Flexi loans can be helpful if you need ongoing access to money with flexible withdrawals and repayments. Before applying, you must compare interest rates, fees, eligibility criteria, and repayment terms. If you choose a loan wisely, it can be easier for you to meet your financial needs while keeping borrowing costs manageable. A term loan provides a lump sum amount that you can repay through fixed EMIs. On the other hand, an overdraft facility lets you withdraw funds as per your requirement up to a pre-approved limit. Which type of loan is best for a medical emergency in India? A personal loan is most commonly used for a medical emergency in India. It offers quick approval, fast disbursal, and usually does not require collateral. Can I get a loan without a salary slip or ITR in India? Yes, some lenders approve a loan application without a salary slip or Income Tax Return (ITR) in India. You will need to provide bank statements, business income, or alternative income proofs. The eligibility requirements will vary. What is the maximum loan amount I can get against my property in India? Under a loan against property, most lenders offer up to 60% to 80% of the property’s market value. The final loan amount will depend on the property’s type and your repayment capacity. What is the minimum CIBIL score required to get a personal loan in India? Many lenders prefer a CIBIL score of 700 or above to give you a personal loan in India. Some may approve loans with lower scores, but the interest rates could be higher. Can I prepay or foreclose a loan early, and are there charges? Yes, many lenders allow you to prepay or foreclose a loan. However, some may charge a fee. It depends on the loan type and terms. What is the difference between a loan and a line of credit? A loan provides a fixed amount up front. On the other hand, if you take a line of credit, there is a borrowing limit that you can use, repay, and reuse as needed. How does taking multiple loans affect my CIBIL score? If you take multiple loans, it increases your debt burden. Your CIBIL score also gets lowered with frequent loan applications and missed payments. It also affects future loan approvals.
