Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Home loan foreclosure allows borrowers to repay their outstanding loan before the tenure ends, potentially reducing the total interest burden and freeing up future cash flow. Foreclosure charges depend on factors such as the lender, loan type, interest structure and borrower category. Proper closure also involves collecting the foreclosure letter, No Dues Certificate and original property documents. Borrowers should also consider the impact on credit records and tax benefits before deciding to foreclose. Home loan foreclosure charges are levied by the lender when a borrower repays the outstanding home loan amount before the agreed tenure ends. Home loans help us finance our dream of providing our loved ones with a comfortable and secure living space. However, home loans are long-term commitments and require you to pledge the home you build as collateral to the lender. These long-term loans often have a repayment tenure lasting 15-20 years and sometimes even more. Long tenures come with high interest, so foreclosing your home loan is a wise decision as it gives you flexibility in future financial planning. Lifting off the burden of monthly mortgage payments will enable you to direct your cash flow towards other investments and focus on other financial goals. Closing a loan within the predetermined tenure will also improve your credit score. Additionally, you can enjoy debt-free home ownership as there are no financial obligations to your lender. While foreclosing your home loan can offer numerous benefits, understanding the intricacies of loan foreclosure can help you make informed financial decisions. This blog will cover everything you need to know about foreclosing your home loan, from home loan foreclosure charges offered by different lenders to points to remember while foreclosing your loan. What are home loan foreclosure charges? The lender imposes foreclosure charges on home loans when you repay your loan before the decided repayment tenure. Foreclosure charges for home loans intend to compensate the lender for the potential income they may have incurred from the interest. These charges vary from lender to lender, so read all the documents carefully and closely analyze the loan terms and costs. The lender calculates home loan foreclosure charges based on payment penalty percentage, interest on the amount you have prepaid, the tenure of your loan and whether they have fixed or floating interest rate. Reviewing your loan agreement to understand these charges and comparing different lenders is prudent. Home loan closure charges also depend on whether the borrower repays the loan with their funds or through another funding source. Some borrowers may consider refinancing with a different lender because of attractive Home Loan interest rates . Here is how this works: The borrower will get loan approval from their desired lender. The lender will then close the home loan by repaying the loan amount to the existing lender. The borrower has to repay the loan to their new lender at the new interest rate. Financial institutions have different loan foreclosure charges for individuals and non-individuals. It is prudent to shop around and understand your financial needs and repayment ability before committing to a loan. Foreclosure charges: Fixed vs floating rate loans Several borrowers remain confused about how foreclosure charges are levied on fixed-rate and floating-rate loans. As per the latest Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines , lenders are not permitted to levy foreclosure charges on loans with floating interest rates. However, they can continue to charge foreclosure or pre-payment fees on loans with fixed interest rates. It means that foreclosing a floating-rate loan is usually cheaper than foreclosing a fixed-rate loan. Home loan foreclosure charges of different lenders Home loan foreclosure charges apply when the borrower repays the entire loan amount. Pre-payment charges are applied if the borrower repays a part of the total loan amount. Some financial institutions do not have any home loan foreclosure charges, while others base it on whether the borrower is an individual or non-individual. Below are the home loan foreclosure and pre-payment charges by different financial institutions: Financial institutions Home loan foreclosure charges Home loan pre-payment charges TATA Capital Nil if paid using own funds Nil if paid using own funds HDFC Nil Nil Indiabulls Nil Nil Sundaram Home Finance Limited Nil Nil Aditya Birla Housing Finance Limited Nil for individual borrowers 2% of outstanding principal for non-individual borrowers Nil Gruh Finance Limited Nil Nil DHFL Nil for individual borrowers 2% of outstanding principal for non-individual borrowers Nil for individual borrowers 3% of the outstanding principal for non-individual borrowers LIC Housing Finance Limited Nil to 2% of the prepaid amount Nil to 2% of the prepaid amount Federal Bank Nil to 3% of the outstanding amount Nil to 3% of the outstanding amount State Bank of India Nil Nil Axis Bank Nil Nil India Shelter Finance Corporation Nil Nil Reliance Home Finance Limited 2% – 5% of the outstanding amount 2% – 5% of the outstanding amount Kotak Mahindra Bank Nil Nil Central Bank of India Nil Nil AAVAS Finances Limited Nil Nil Yes Bank Nil for floating interest rates 4% of the outstanding amount for fixed interest rates Nil for floating interest rates 4% of the outstanding amount for fixed interest rates Indian Overseas Bank Nil Nil Bank of India Nil Nil Dhanlaxmi Bank Nil Nil Andhra Bank Nil Nil Bank of Baroda Nil Nil IDBI Bank Nil Nil Bank of Maharashtra Nil Nil Dena Bank Nil Nil PNB Housing Finance Limited Nil Nil for individual borrowers 2% of prepaid amount for non-individual borrowers Types of home loan closure procedures Here is a look at the various types of home loan closure procedures: Preclosure: This refers to when you choose to pay off your entire loan before the end of your loan tenure . In other words, you decide to close your loan obligations by paying the outstanding amount earlier and saving on the interest that you would have to pay if you decided to complete the tenure. Regular closure: This involves repaying your home loan according to the decided schedule throughout the loan tenure. Inadequate home loan closure: If the borrower faces financial setbacks that affect their ability to repay the loan as scheduled, lenders may consider waiving the fees. Settled home loan closure: In case the borrower is unable to repay the entire loan amount, the lender might offer a discounted rate to settle the overdue amount of the loan while waiving the remaining amount. Steps for home loan foreclosure After analysing different home loan foreclosure charges, here are the steps you can follow to close your loan before the repayment term ends: Step 1: Visit your lending institution. Step 2: Submit all the loan-related documents. Step 3: Pay the loan amount and the home loan foreclosure charges. Step 4: Collect your home loan foreclosure letter Documents required after home loan foreclosure Once you have paid home loan foreclosure charges, ensure to collect the following documents from the lender: Mandatory documents to collect No Dues Certificate or No Objection Certificate: This certificate proves that you have repaid your home loan and there are no dues. Original property papers: Once you have closed your home loan, you can ask the lender to return the original property papers. These may include the Title Deed and other documents. Loan closure statement: This document reflects the date and other details related to the home loan closure or repayment. Security and post-dated cheques: If you have submitted any security or post-dated cheques to the lender, you can collect them after home loan foreclosure. Post-closure administrative steps You must take the following steps after the foreclosure of your home loan: Lien removal: The property is marked as a lien in the name of the lender until you have fully repaid your home loan. Updated encumbrance certificate: An Encumbrance Certificate (EC) is an official legal document from the government’s registration department that proves a property is free from any legal and financial liabilities. Credit score update: Keep checking your credit reports after loan closure. Make sure the updated records reflect the current status. Points to remember during home loan foreclosure Following the process of closing a loan properly is just as crucial as following the process of borrowing a loan. Here are some points to remember while foreclosing your home loan: Collecting all the documents is necessary. While availing of a home loan, the original property documents are given to the lender. Ensure to collect those documents after foreclosing your loan. The No Objection Certificate proves you have closed your loan. It is an essential document as it helps you with future loans. Closing a loan on time adds to your credit score . Remember to ask the lender to update your credit score to boost your creditworthiness. Carry your government ID proof, as it is necessary to close your loan. Also, carry your chequebook to pay the final settlement and home loan foreclosure charges of the home loan. Collect the acknowledgement of the final payment from the lender. Ensure that it is duly stamped and signed by the official. Home loan foreclosure charges calculator Calculating foreclosure charges helps you estimate the fees a lender may charge if you repay your loan before the agreed-upon tenure. This allows you to plan your prepayment effectively and understand the potential costs involved. The amount varies depending on factors such as the payment penalty percentage, interest on the prepaid amount, loan tenure, and whether the loan has a fixed or floating interest rate. Using a foreclosure charges calculator or a prepayment charges calculator can help you estimate these costs accurately. Additionally, a home loan calculator can help you plan your finances and make informed decisions before prepaying your loan. How to avoid or reduce home loan foreclosure charges? If you plan early, you can easily avoid foreclosure charges and reduce your home loan costs. Here are some simple ways to manage your repayment better. Understand Your Lender’s Policies: Know the terms related to early repayment so you can identify ways to lower foreclosure fees and save on loan closure. Make Regular Part-Payments: Use any surplus income to reduce the principal amount. This is one of the most effective home loan prepayment tips. Choose a Flexible Loan Structure: Opt for a loan plan that allows early repayment without heavy penalties to help you avoid foreclosure charges. Maintain Strong Repayment Discipline: Consistent repayment often encourages the lender to offer relaxed terms, helping you further reduce home loan charges. Impact of home loan foreclosure on credit score and tax benefits A home loan foreclosure can impact both your credit score and tax benefits. Here’s what to keep in mind: 1. Impact on credit score Voluntary Foreclosure (Pre-closure): Paying the full outstanding amount without defaults is usually seen positively. Potential Minor Dip: Closing a long-term loan may cause a brief score dip due to a shorter credit history and changed credit mix. Long-term Benefit: A responsible closure history can improve creditworthiness over time. 2. Impact on tax benefits Loss of Deductions: You lose the loan closure tax benefits for the remaining loan tenure. Section 80C: Deduction on principal repayment up to ₹1.5 lakh per year. Section 24(b): Deduction on interest paid up to ₹2 lakh per year for self-occupied properties; higher limits may apply for let-out properties. By understanding the home loan foreclosure effect, including credit score after foreclosure and the tax implications of loan closure, you can decide wisely, weighing repayment benefits against long-term goals. Foreclosure letter for home loan: What is it and how to obtain it? A foreclosure letter is an official document issued by a lender when a borrower wants to repay the outstanding home loan before the agreed tenure ends. The foreclosure letterincludes details such as the outstanding principal, applicable interest, foreclosure charges, and the total amount required to close the loan. You can usually obtain a foreclosure letter by following these steps: Contact the lender: Submit a foreclosure request through the lender’s branch, website, mobile app, or customer service channel. Provide loan details: Share your loan account number and required identification or account-related documents. Get the amount payable details: The lender calculates the amount payable, including the principal, interest and any applicable charges. Check the letter: Review the foreclosure amount, validity period, payment instructions and other details mentioned in the document. Make the payment: Pay the stated amount within the specified period to close the loan. Collect closure documents: After payment, obtain the loan closure letter, No Dues Certificate and other relevant property documents from the lender. In a nutshell Understanding the foreclosure charges of home loans is essential to making wise financial decisions. Understanding all the costs, interests and fees associated with the loan from your chosen lender is prudent so that you can plan your finances seamlessly. You can easily achieve your long-term financial goals by carefully analyzing your lender. Home loan foreclosure can help lift the weight of long EMIs and save interest, improving the overall cash flow. However, ensure that you read and discuss all the loan-related terms with your lender in advance. Before foreclosing on your home loan, consult your lender, assess your financial situation and talk to an expert. Forecasting the potential long-term impacts on your finances can help you achieve your future aspirations. While financing your dreams, visiting different lenders and examining their services is crucial. Home loan foreclosure charges are the fees imposed by the lender on the borrower if the borrower decides to repay the loan amount before the end of the predetermined repayment tenure. Why do lenders impose foreclosure charges on home loans? Lenders impose home loan foreclosure charges in home loans to compensate the income they may have earned from the interest if the borrower repaid the loan amount according to the decided repayment tenure. How are home loan foreclosure charges calculated? Foreclosure home loan charges are calculated based on factors like fixed or floating interest rates, prepayment penalty percentage, loan repayment tenure, and other additional charges, if applicable. What are the rbi guidelines on foreclosure charges on home loan? According to the RBI, lenders cannot levy foreclosure charges or penalties for prepayments on home loans for loans with floating interest rates. How can I avoid the foreclosure charges on my house loan? You can avoid foreclosure charges by opting for a house loan with a floating interest rate, as the RBI restricts lenders from levying foreclosure and prepayment charges on such loans. Does foreclosure home loan reduce interest rate? The foreclosure of your home loan can help you save on the interest you would have had to pay during the remaining loan tenure. However, preclosure of your home loan doesn’t reduce interest rates. What are the benefits of home loan foreclosure? The benefits of home loan foreclosure include improving your credit score, saving on interest payments, and decreasing your financial obligations. Is it a good idea to foreclose on a home loan? Yes. Foreclosing a home loan is beneficial in several ways, provided the borrower is comfortable in repaying the outstanding debt without burdening their finances. It shortens the loan tenure, thereby enabling the borrower to save on interest expenses. It also increases monthly cash flow by eliminating EMIs. What are the differences between home loan pre-payment & home loan foreclosure? The key difference between home loan pre-payment and home loan foreclosure lies in the amount paid. Pre-payment refers to paying an amount greater than the EMI or a partial amount of the loan principal. On the other hand, foreclosure involves paying the entire outstanding loan amount before the end of the loan tenure. What is a foreclosure letter for a home loan and how do I get it? A foreclosure letter for a home loan is an official document from your lender confirming that your loan is fully repaid. You can request it after completing the pre-closure of your home loan by submitting your repayment proof. The lender then verifies your account and issues the letter for your records. What is the home loan closure procedure after foreclosure? Once you repay the entire outstanding amount, the lender completes the home loan closure procedure by updating your loan status and returning your original documents. They also issue a No Dues Certificate and a closure statement, which confirm that your property is free from any financial obligation. How can I avoid home loan foreclosure charges? You can reduce or avoid foreclosure charges by choosing a lender that offers flexible repayment terms, planning early part-payments and checking fee policies before applying. Comparing options helps you find lower costs, especially if you’re considering pre-closure of a home loan to shorten your tenure and save interest. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Is buying a home a good investment? This is a common question that arises in the minds of many potential homebuyers. Investing in a home has its pros and cons, and not considering them before buying a house can be a recipe for disaster. Generally, buying a house is considered a wise decision, but is buying property a good investment or not requires a very individualistic evaluation. You must evaluate your current situation, including financials, family size, phase of life, income source, etc., and the implications of the decision before buying a house. Important factors to consider in home value Buying-related costs The overall expense of purchasing a home increases with costs such as stamp duty, registration fees, property taxes, and legal charges. These impact affordability and, in turn, influence a property’s value perception in the market. Location Location is one of the most vital factors in determining home value. Properties in well-connected areas with access to schools, hospitals, transport, and commercial markets tend to appreciate more than those in remote or underdeveloped locations. Market conditions Fluctuations in real estate demand, interest rates, and overall economic trends have a significant impact on property values. Prices increase faster in a rising market, while downturns result in depreciation. Property’s condition The price for well-maintained homes with strong construction quality, modern amenities, and updated interiors is typically higher than that of poorly maintained ones. Demand and supply The balance between demand and supply of properties impacts value. If demand is high and supply is low, prices rise, whereas oversupply results in a price decrease. Key benefits of buying a house as an investment If you’re wondering is buying a flat a good investment, here are some benefits to help you decide. Equity building: Paying monthly EMIs helps build equity in the property, which increases your ownership stake over time. If property values rise, this can help in building a significant financial asset. Financial stability: When you own a house, your financial stability improves. And, generally, a property’s value increases over time. So, buying a property is a promising investment in the long run. Rental income: If you own a property, you can choose to rent it out and earn a steady income, which can help you cover your EMI payments and generate an additional income to meet monthly expenses. Comparing home ownership vs. renting Parameter Home ownership Renting Upfront costs Down payment, registration charges, and other fees Security deposit, advance rent Maintenance expenses The owner must pay all repair and upkeep costs Typically, the landlord takes care of maintenance expenses Monthly payments EMI payments (interest + principal) Rent payments, which can increase periodically Equity building Property value may rise in the long term, offering wealth creation No wealth accumulation; rent payments are only an expense Flexibility Less flexible – tougher to move due to the selling process High flexibility – easier to relocate by not renewing or ending the lease Tax benefits Eligible for home loan tax deductions No tax benefits Long-term vs. short-term investment in a house Your investment horizon is a key factor to consider when determining: ‘Is buying a house a good investment?’ Long-term investment: Appreciation in real estate occurs in the long term. If you’re interested in retaining the property for several years, you can reap the benefits of significant appreciation and equity buildup. Short-term investment: Property values can undergo fluctuations in the short term, which makes real estate a less reliable short-term investment. Market volatility may not let you gain the expected profits if you want to sell the property quickly. Tax benefits and deductions related to home ownership Many tax benefits are available to Indian homeowners to help them reduce the financial burden of buying and owning property. Individuals availing of a home loan must educate themselves on these benefits to maximize savings: Section 80C: This section allows you to claim a deduction of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh on the principal repayment of a home loan. You can also claim deductions on other eligible investments, including ULIP premiums, life insurance premiums, and PPF. Section 24(b): In the case of self-occupied properties, homeowners are eligible for a claim of up to Rs. 2 lakh every year against interest paid on home loans. Stamp duty and registration fees: You can claim deductions on the fee payments under Section 80C. However, the deduction qualifies only for the purchase year. The brand fulfills the borrowing needs of individual, retail, and corporate customers. Tata Capital offers home loan solutions at competitive interest rates, starting from 7.75% per annum. The loan repayment terms are friendly and flexible, with the option of choosing a tenure of up to 30 years. Conclusion After carefully considering the multiple aspects of buying property, you can decide if buying a home fits your current financial aspirations. While buying a fully-approved house in a happening locality can be a good idea, only you can choose if it’s the right call for you in your current situation. So, don’t hesitate to examine your means and needs to answer the question honestly. If buying a home is on the cards for you, consider getting a home loan to finance it conveniently and enjoy tax benefits. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund When dealing with debt management, individuals often face complex concepts and confusing terms, such as loan write off vs waive off. When an individual is unable to repay their loan, lenders label it a “ Non-Performing Asset ” or bad loan. Lenders can deal with NPAs in one of two ways, they can either be written off or waived off. While these terms may sound similar, they often refer to two distinct processes with different outcomes for lenders and borrowers. Put briefly, with a loan write-off, the lender believes the loan cannot be recovered and removes it from their books, marking it as a loss. With loan waive-offs, the lender forgives the loan, and the borrower is not required to repay it. In this article, we take an in-depth look at the difference between write-offs and waive-offs in loans. Loan Write-off Vs Loan Waive-Off Now that you know what they are, it’s time to understand the difference between the loan write-offs and waive-offs. Differentiating Parameter Loan Write-Off Loan Waive-Off Repayment A lender writes off a loan to equalise their balance sheets. It does not mean the loan is cancelled. The loan account is active, and lenders hope to make a recovery at a later date. Here, a lender gives up all claims to a loan amount. It is a complete cancellation of a loan. This means the borrower is free from their debt. Recovery What happens when a loan is written off is that lenders may pursue recovery with the help of a legal entity. They can do this since the loan is not closed. Lenders cannot pursue the loan amount once it’s waived off. They cannot seek assistance from any legal entities or third-party recovery agents to collect outstanding funds. In this case, the loan is closed. Collateral A lender has the legal right to retain any collateral pledged by the buyer. They are allowed to auction the collateral to recover the outstanding loan amount. A waived-off loan means that the lender must return any collateral pledged by the borrower at the time of taking the loan. Eligibility Financial institutions write off loans to clean up their balance sheets and optimise tax liabilities. Hence, all borrowers come under its purview. A loan waive-off facility is mainly provided to farmers to help them during natural calamities that are impossible to deal with. Compulsion It’s mandatory for financial institutions to write off loans to keep their books and ledgers balanced and in check. Borrowers cannot submit requests to waive-off loans. This is a voluntary activity from the lender’s end with the government’s support. Key Differences: Loan Write-Off vs Loan Waive-Off The key difference between loan write-off and waive off is that write-offs keep the borrower liable, whereas waive-offs release them from the debt. In addition to the loan write-off vs loan waive-off comparison given in the table above, another practical way to distinguish a loan write-off from a loan waive-off is to look at each through the lens of intent and outcome. A write-off is fundamentally an accounting treatment: The loan is classified as a Non-Performing Asset and is derecognised from the books, improving portfolio clarity, while the borrower’s liability and the lender’s recovery rights remain intact. A waive-off is a policy or relief decision: The lender gives up the legal right to collect the loan, the borrower’s obligation ends, and the loan ceases to exist. What is a Loan Write-Off? A loan write-off refers to any amount a lending institution “writes off,” even if the whole loan isn’t cleared. This helps lenders balance their books. For example, Mr. Mehta takes a loan of Rs. 10 lakhs for 3 years from Institution A. After 8 months of timely EMIs, he suddenly stops paying. Despite follow-ups and legal attempts, he doesn’t repay. Institution A then reduces the loan’s value, hoping he’ll repay at least part of it. This reduction in value is called a loan write-off. Benefits of a Loan Write-Off for Lenders A loan write-off benefits the lender in the following ways- Lenders can reduce their tax obligation on the total loan value after it is written off. Lenders can remove non-performing assets and maintain a clean balance sheet. In many cases, borrowers do not use their entire credit limit. They only borrow the required amount and pay interest on it. After the loan write-off, lenders can use the funds initially blocked for the borrower for their own business operations and expansion. A loan write-off does not mean borrowers don’t need to repay the loan. Lenders can continue pursuing the loan repayment , which, if received after the write-off, can be considered a profit in the year of repayment. Also, read – What is Personal Loan? Reasons for the Loan Write-Off There are many reasons for a loan write-off, such as: If an individual doesn’t make timely repayments If a borrower declares bankruptcy If a borrower passes away, and their estate cannot cover the debt If the value of the collateral provided drops below the loan amount Impact of a Loan Write-Off (on Lender and Borrower CIBIL) A loan write-off can have significant impacts. Being written off means the loan can no longer be an asset, and the lending institution can reduce its NPAs on its records. A loan write-off can also lessen the lending institution’s tax liability. What is a Loan Waive-Off? To understand the difference between a write-off vs. a waive-off, it is first essential to understand what a waive-off is. A loan waive-off is when a lender forgives a part or the entirety of the borrower’s loan. For example, Mr Chaudhary borrowed a personal loan of Rs 5 lakhs for 2 years. However, he ultimately had to declare bankruptcy. His inability to repay the loan leads the lending institution to waive off his loan, meaning his debt is forgiven. However, this only happens in exceptional circumstances. Benefits of a Loan Waive-Off for Borrowers A loan waive-off can have significant impacts on the lender and borrower. While the lender faces substantial losses, it greatly benefits the borrower in many ways. These include: Financial respite: When a loan is waived, the borrower is no longer required to pay off their debt. This can offer them enormous financial respite. It allows the borrower to focus their spending on necessities (whether that is housing, medical expenses, or other reasons). Impact on credit score: When a lending institution waives off a borrower’s loan, it can positively impact their credit score, improving their future creditworthiness. Farmers and other individuals in the agricultural sector are often offered this provision. Reasons for Loan Waive-Off There are many reasons why a lending institution may offer a loan waive-off, including: Financial difficulties Natural calamities Loss of or decrease in the value of collateral Alterations in loan terms Government policies Impact of a Loan Waive-Off (on Borrower’s Credit & Liability) The impacts of a loan waive-off include: The account is closed Lenders cannot take legal measures to get the loan amount back It minimises tax liabilities The borrower’s credit score improves How Loan Write-Off and Waive-Off Affect Your Credit Score A credit score is a numerical indicator of one’s creditworthiness and financial discipline. It reflects your credit usage and how reliably you can repay the debt. Both loan write-off and loan waive-off can affect your credit score. Loan write-off credit score impact: A loan write-off harms your credit score because it signals that the lender considers your loan doubtful for recovery. It can be harder for you to obtain loans in the future and if approved, it may have higher interest rates. Loan waive-off credit score impact: A loan waive-off, meaning relinquishing of the legal right to collect a loan, may affect credit negatively when it’s caused by financial difficulties. It may affect it positively if the borrower later rebuilds credit through consistent timely repayments on other active accounts Get a Personal Loan at Tata Capital Are you looking for a personal loan ? This includes travel, wedding expenses, higher education, home renovations, and more! No security or collateral required: Tata Capital’s personal loan is unsecured, meaning borrowers are not required to pledge assets or provide securities. Hybrid loan term options: With the Personal Loan Hybrid Loan Term option, users can withdraw money up to a predetermined limit, and interest is only charged on the amount used. Zero pre-payment charges: You can partially prepay up to 25% of the loan at any point after 12 months without availing of any penalties or additional charges. Flexible tenure: We offer repayment tenures of up to 6 years, allowing borrowers control over their EMI options. Conclusion Loan write-offs vs. waive-offs take place under different circumstances. While the former is a mandatory practice, the latter is at the discretion of the government and the lender. A loan write-off simply means the lender considers the loan a loss and accepts that it is unlikely to recover the loan. They write it off from the balance sheet to equalise it. However, it does not mean the loan is cancelled, and you are still obligated to repay it. How does a loan write-off affect my credit score? A loan write-off negatively impacts your credit score, indicating non-repayment, which can affect future loan approvals. What are the common reasons for a loan waiver? Loan waivers are usually granted due to economic hardships, natural disasters, or government policies aimed at easing borrowers' financial burdens. What are the tax implications of a loan write-off or waiver? Loan waivers and write-offs reduce the tax liabilities of the lender. Can a loan be written off and waived at the same time? No, loans cannot be written off and waived off at the same time. A loan write-off removes the loan from the lending institution’s balance sheets. On the other hand, a loan waive-off is when the lender decides to forgive the loan partially or entirely, meaning the borrower’s debt is cleared. Can a borrower request a loan waiver? Borrowers do have the option to request a loan waiver. However, approval is usually granted only under specific circumstances. This includes financial struggles, natural disasters, or government programs meant to offer relief to specific sectors. What is the loan write-off meaning? Loan write-off meaning is an accounting action, when a lender removes a loan from his books upon realising that its recovery is doubtful. However, the borrower is still legally liable to repay it. What is the main difference between loan write-off and loan waive-off? Loan write-off meaning is when the lender removes the loan from its books but still retains the right to collect it from the borrower. A loan waive-off on the other hand fully cancels repayment, stops recovery, returns collateral, and usually applies under specific government-supported schemes. How does a loan write-off affect my credit score in India? A loan write-off negatively impacts your credit score because it signals that the lender considers your loan doubtful for recovery. It can be harder for you to obtain loans in the future and if approved, it may have higher interest rates. What is the loan waive-off meaning? Loan waive-off meaning is when the lender gives up the legal right to recover a loan. From the point of view of a borrower, they no longer need to pay the loan back. typically the default option for most people. And why not? Personal loans are convenient to apply for, require minimal documentation, feature simple eligibility criteria, and offer you access to funds quickly. However, what happens when you don’t have a CIBIL score? Your credit score is a crucial eligibility requirement when applying for a loan, as it helps lenders assess your borrowing history and repayment habits. While getting a loan without a credit score can be challenging, it is not impossible. Many lenders are open to alternative methods to assess your creditworthiness and allow you to borrow funds with low or no CIBIL score without undergoing a hard credit inquiry. Here are five practical ways to access a loan without relying on your CIBIL score. How to Get a Loan without a Credit Score? Even with no CIBIL Score, there are various ways to get an instant loan. Here are five ways to do it: Apply with a guarantor Request a smaller loan amount Provide income proof Offer collateral Explain credit inactivity 1. Apply with a guarantor If you don’t have a credit score , applying with a guarantor with a strong credit history can greatly improve your chances of getting the loan. A guarantor acts as a financial backer who vouches for your repayment ability. Essentially, their credibility offsets your lack of credit history. A guarantor can be anyone – your parent, spouse, sibling, or any close relative with reliable proof of income and a good credit score. However, it’s important to note that a guarantor is legally responsible for repaying the loan in case of default. So, you must ensure timely repayment of EMIs to enjoy a smooth repayment process. 2. Apply for a small loan amount If you’re new to borrowing a loan and don’t have a credit score, requesting a smaller loan amount based on your income is the best bet. This is because, with a small loan, you can better demonstrate your repayment capability. Lenders are more likely to approve modest sums because the risk involved is lower. If they are sure that you can afford the EMIs with your income, they are more likely to approve the loan. Not to mention, timely repayments will show that you are a responsible borrower, so you can gradually build trust with lenders. Over time, this track record can even help you access larger loan amounts. Think of it as building your financial credibility, one step at a time. 3. Apply with income proof When you apply for a loan, Apply with income proofthe lender also requires you to provide proof of income to determine your financial stability. In the absence of a credit score, proof of income is essential to show that you have a steady cash flow to meet your loan obligations. Based on your lender’s documentation requirements for salaried and self-employed individuals, you will have to submit salary slips, bank statements, IT returns, and so on to highlight your income stability. 4. Apply for a collateral-based loan Typically personal loans are collateral-free loans. However, if you’re applying for a loan without a credit score, consider pledging an asset as security. This reduces the lender’s risk because the collateral can be liquidated in case of default to recover the loan amount. A collateral can be any valuable asset, including property, fixed deposits, gold, or other assets. Since the loan is secured against the collateral, lenders may be more willing to approve the application, even if you lack a credit score. For example, a gold loan is often easier to obtain because the pledged gold serves as a reliable security. 5. Get an NH or HN on your credit report If you’ve been financially inactive, it’s crucial to address this with lenders. A no-credit history (NH) remark on your credit report simply highlights that you’ve never taken a loan or used a credit card before. An “NH” score doesn’t mean you’re a risky borrower or have a negative financial status. So, when applying for a loan, provide a detailed explanation of your financial history and the reasons behind your lack of credit activity. This could include highlighting stable income, consistent savings, or past instances where you managed finances responsibly without borrowing. Lenders appreciate honesty, and being upfront about your situation can build the trust necessary to secure approval. Is it Possible to Get a Small Loan in India without a CIBIL Check? While most lenders require the applicant’s credit information and CIBIL score to assess their creditworthiness, getting a small instant loan without a CIBIL check in India is still possible. Most lenders allow you to apply for an instant loan without a CIBIL score in the following ways- 1. Apply with a guarantor, in which case the guarantor’s credit history will be considered before loan approval. 2. Apply for a small loan amount to ensure easy repayment per your financial capacity. 3. You can also consider pledging collateral that mitigates the lender’s risk without the credit score. 4. Furnish income proof documents to assure the lender of your repayment capacity. If you have a low or no CIBIL score, you can easily apply for a personal loan for CIBIL defaulter through these methods and receive the funds quickly without undergoing a hard inquiry or CIBIL check on your credit report. Conclusion Although a no-credit-check loan can be sanctioned without a CIBIL score, you’ll be charged a high rate of interest. Therefore, if you need urgent access to funds, turn to Tata Capital. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Imagine the scenario: You walk into your local bank or visit an online financial institution, such as TATA Capital, ready to apply for a loan. You have your documents, your identification and everything in order, but then the dreaded word appears – CIBIL score. It falls just short of the preferred range, sitting at 600, and suddenly, your financial plans are on hold. If this scenario seems familiar, it’s time to learn how to increase CIBIL score from 600 to 750. How Does the CIBIL Score Work? The Cibil score is calculated based on the information in one’s credit report, which is a record of their credit history. This information includes data on the types of credit they have (credit cards, loans, etc.), their payment history, the amount of debt they have and their credit utilisation ratio, among other factors. Payment History : One’s repayment behaviour plays a crucial role in determining their Cibil score . Regularly paying off the credit dues indicates responsible credit behaviour, which in turn improves one’s score. Conversely, late payments, defaults and settlements can harm one’s chances of landing a better mark on how to improve cibil score after settlement. Credit Utilisation : This refers to the ratio of one’s credit usage to their credit limit. A high credit utilisation ratio may imply dependency on credit, which can negatively impact their score. It is recommended to maintain a ratio of 30% or less. Credit Mix and Duration : The type of credit (secured and unsecured) and the duration of one’s credit history also factor into their Cibil score. A balanced mix of secured (such as home loans ) and unsecured loans (such as credit cards) and a longer credit history can enhance one’s score. Credit Enquiries : Each time one applies for a new line of credit, a ‘hard enquiry’ is made, which can temporarily lower their Cibil score. Hence, too many credit applications within a short period can negatively affect your score. Public Records : Records such as bankruptcies and tax liens can severely harm one’s Cibil score. Understanding these factors can provide clear insights into how to improve one’s Cibil score. By managing these aspects of one’s financial behaviour, one can begin to work towards enhancing their creditworthiness. Also, read – How to Build Credit Score from Zero & Improve CIBIL Score Common Reasons Your CIBIL Score May Be at 600 The majority of the CIBIL score 600 reasons stem from a low credit score caused by missed payments or a high credit utilisation ratio. Another example of a low credit score causes is the frequent hard inquiries from multiple loan applications that can hurt credit score. Some more factors affecting CIBIL are unbalanced credit mix, short history from closing old accounts, report errors, partial EMI payments, and defaults. To know why CIBIL score is low, keep a check on the above factors. More importantly, always pay your existing debt obligations on time. Also, read – How To Improve Credit Score In 30 Days? Tips to Increase Cibil Score Timely Bill Payments Paying one’s bills on time is the cornerstone of a healthy credit profile. This is more than just meeting the deadline for one’s credit card payments; it extends to all forms of bills that might be associated with their name. These can include household utility bills, loan EMIs and even mobile phone bills. Each missed payment is a mark against their credit health, lowering their Cibil score. When contemplating how to improve cibil score immediately, it is essential to prioritise timely bill payments. Automating payments or setting reminders can be beneficial strategies to ensure not to miss a deadline. Lower Credit Utilisation Credit utilisation refers to the proportion of one’s available credit that they are currently using. If one is regularly nearing their credit limit, it can be an indicator to lenders that they are heavily reliant on credit, which can negatively impact their Cibil score. If you’re exploring how to increase your Cibil score, aim to maintain a credit utilisation ratio of no more than 30% of your available credit limit. This indicates to lenders that you’re using credit responsibly and not living beyond your means. Eliminating Debt Debt can be a significant factor in determining one’s Cibil score. The more debt one has, the more it can decrease their score. It’s not uncommon for individuals to wonder how to improve their cibil score after settlement. The answer lies in eliminating their outstanding debt. Regular payments towards their debt, coupled with strategies to reduce the total debt amount, can gradually improve their Cibil score. Debt consolidation loans , for instance, can be a viable option to manage high-interest debt effectively. Diversifying Credit Another aspect of understanding how to increase one’s Cibil score is diversifying their credit. A mix of secured loans (such as home loans and car loans ) and unsecured loans (such as credit cards and personal loans ) can positively impact their Cibil score. Lenders view this credit mix as an indication of responsible credit management. It suggests that they can handle different types of credit products and that they are more likely to handle repayments responsibly. Regular Monitoring In the journey of increasing one’s Cibil score, regular monitoring is a crucial but often overlooked step. Regular checks of your Cibil score and report help you understand your credit standing, track your progress and identify any inaccuracies or fraudulent activities in the credit report. Errors in the credit report can pull down your score; hence, it’s essential to get them rectified to get a better hit on how to improve cibil score immediately. Monitoring services provide timely updates and can be a valuable tool in understanding how to increase your Cibil score. Also, read – 800-Plus Credit Score: How to Make the Most of It Maintain a Healthy Credit Mix A diverse credit mix shows financial institutions that you can manage different types of credit responsibly. It indicates lower credit risk, as handling various credit accounts requires financial discipline and organisation. A healthy credit mix includes secured loans like auto or home loans and unsecured loans like credit cards or personal loans. Having this mix of credit shows that you are not overly reliant on one type of credit, thus improving your creditworthiness. However, avoid opening multiple new accounts at once, as it can signal financial distress. Instead, gradually diversify your credit types over time. Remember, the key is to manage all your accounts well, make timely payments, and keep your credit utilisation low. This way, you can build a robust credit profile, boosting your credit score. How Long Does It Take to Increase CIBIL Score from 600 to 750? In India, moving a CIBIL score from 600 to 750 usually takes 6 to 12 months, depending on your credit behaviour. This timeline varies based on how consistently you pay EMIs, clear outstanding dues, lower credit card utilisation, and avoid new hard inquiries. If you are wondering how to improve your CIBIL score from 600 to 750, keep in mind that it requires consistent financial discipline. You can improve your credit score timeline by making timely EMI payments and by keeping your credit utilisation ratio under 30%. Next, avoid multiple inquiries and fix errors in your credit report to increase CIBIL score from 600 to 750. Also, read – Personal loan for CIBIL score of 550 Conclusion In conclusion, mastering the art of improving your Cibil score unlocks a world of financial opportunities, from securing a mortgage to achieving lower interest rates on loans. This journey, though demanding, is a worthwhile investment in your financial health. As you embark on this mission, remember, every step you take towards improving your Cibil score brings you one step closer to your financial dreams. Maintain a good CIBIL score by paying dues on time, keeping credit utilisation below 30%, avoiding multiple loan applications, and regularly monitoring your credit report for errors. A balanced mix of unsecured and secured loans helps, too. How can I increase my CIBIL score quickly? To increase your CIBIL score, pay off debts, minimize inquiries for hard loans, and reduce your credit card balance. How to increase CIBIL score from 600 to 750 in 30 days? To increase your CIBIL score, pay your loan EMIs, credit card bills, and other dues on time, preferably a few days before the due date. Timely payments can significantly improve your credit score. Can I Increase My CIBIL Score From 600 to 750 Immediately? No, you cannot boost your CIBIL score from 600 to 750 instantly. Improving your score takes time and consistent financial habits. You can focus on repaying your debts, making timely payments and reducing your credit utilisation rate. Does having more credit cards improve your credit score? Having more credit cards does not automatically improve your credit score. Your score improves only when you use credit responsibly, i.e. by paying bills on time, keeping utilisation low, and avoiding frequent hard inquiries. Too many cards can actually harm your score if they lead to higher spending or missed payments. What role does credit utilisation play in CIBIL scoring? Credit utilisation plays a major role in CIBIL scoring because it shows how much of your available credit you are using. Keeping utilisation below 30% signals disciplined spending and helps maintain a healthy score. High utilisation suggests credit stress, which can lower your CIBIL score even if payments are on time. Is it possible to get a personal loan with a CIBIL score of 600? It is possible to get a personal loan with a CIBIL score of 600, but approval is more difficult. Most lenders in India prefer scores above 700. With a score of 600, you may still qualify if you have stable income, low existing debt, or a strong banking relationship, but the interest rate is usually higher and loan amounts may be restricted. What factors lead to sudden drops in CIBIL score? Missed or delayed payments, high credit card utilisation, or multiple hard inquiries within a short time are some factors that can cause sudden drops in your CIBIL scores. You should regularly monitor your credit report and address these issues to avoid drops in your CIBIL score. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Everyone may not have the same taste when it comes to building a house of their own. Some may prefer a ready home while others may want to buy a plot of land to build a house. With loans now easily offered by most lenders for both residential property and plot purchases, buyers can easily make their choice. A plot loan implies a loan provided by a lender to a borrower to buy a piece of land (plot) to build their home. A plot loan is a type of home loan that can be availed only for constructing a residential property. While finalising any loan, borrowers look at the tax benefit offered by such loans. However, while purchasing a plot with a plot loan, many buyers often wonder whether they can avail of a plot plus construction loan tax benefits. The income tax benefit on a plot purchase loan would depend on what a borrower intends to do with the purchased plot. Keep reading this article to know whether a plot loan is eligible for tax exemption, how much tax rebate on a plot loan is possible, or in other words, the plot loan tax benefits. What Is a Plot Loan and How Is It Different? A plot loan or a land loan is disbursed for the sole purpose of purchasing a piece of land, which can be used for building a home or a real estate portfolio in the future. Unlike a standard home loan, which is taken for under-construction or ready-to-occupy residential property, a plot loan is designed only for purchasing a vacant plot of land, usually found within the limits of a municipality or corporation, giving you the flexibility to build later. Plot loans usually come with shorter repayment tenures and slightly higher interest rates than home loans. This is because buying a plot without building on it is seen as riskier by lenders. If construction doesn’t happen, the property’s value may not grow as expected. Also, read – Token money: Meaning, purpose & important things to know Plot Loan Tax Benefits: Know How It Works Tax benefits come in handy when availing of home loans. So, borrowers expect an income tax rebate on plot loans, also. The question of whether plot loan tax exemption is available is dependent on what purpose the plot purchased is meant to be used for. A buyer may purchase a plot as an investment with no intention to build a house, villa, etc. They may have invested from a long-term perspective and are expecting appreciation in the plot value over time. So, they wish to keep it vacant and sell it later for a profit when the plot value increases. In such a scenario, they are not eligible for plot loan tax benefits. If a buyer buys a plot to build a home, villa, or any other building, then they can claim income tax benefits on the plot loan. Both the plot plus construction loan tax benefits can be availed by the purchaser. It means they get the benefit of a plot loan taken to buy the plot plus the home loan for plot tax benefit to build a home on the plot. So, a borrower gets a twin tax exemption. Tips to Help You Enjoy the Benefits of the Plot Loan Here are some smart tips to help you make the most of your plot loan and enjoy its full benefits: 1. Make sure whatever construction you are going to do on the plot is completed within 5 years so that you can enjoy tax benefits. 2. If you buy the property with a family member and take a joint loan, both of you can claim tax deductions. This means double the total tax savings for your household. 3. Keep proper records of your EMI slips, sanction letters, and completion certificates. These documents are essential proof for tax deductions and future verifications. 4. You can claim any interest paid during the plot purchase or construction period after the construction is finished. 5. Lastly, you can also consult a tax advisor to ensure you are not missing out on any eligible benefits. Also, read – Pledge vs hypothecation vs mortgage: Key differences Who Can Avail of Plot Loan Tax Benefits Your eligibility to claim plot loan tax benefits depends on a few key conditions related to ownership, construction timelines, and how the loan is used. Here is what you must be aware of: The loan must be used only to buy a residential plot, not agricultural or commercial land. The land should fall within a municipal or corporation area. Construction on the plot must be completed within 5 years of the loan being sanctioned. If you live in the property yourself, you may qualify for higher tax deductions than if you rent it out. You must be the legal owner of the plot, and all documents, including construction proofs, payment receipts, and financial records, must be properly maintained. Also, read – Can you claim home loan interest tax benefits before possession? How to avail tax benefits on a plot purchase loan Now, let’s see how you can get any tax benefit on plot purchase loan . The above example shows that a plot loan income tax benefit can be claimed only when a house is constructed on the same plot. Also, the plot loan tax exemption becomes eligible in the year when the construction gets completed. Post completion of house or building construction, the plot owner can claim the below plot loan income tax benefits. 1. Plot Loan Tax Benefits under Section 80C Section 80C of the Income Tax Act 1961 states a plot owner can claim a tax rebate on a plot loan up to Rs.1.50 lakhs on the principal component of the plot loan plus a home loan that gets repaid in a fiscal year. The principal amount is the original amount of the loan and does not include the interest portion. However, fees related to registration and plot title transfer form part of Section 80 C deduction, provided their payment is made during the year when home construction activity is completed. 2. Plot Loan Tax Benefit under Section 24 Section 24 of the Income Tax Act 1961 allows for plot loan income tax benefits on the interest component. To claim the plot loan tax exemption under Section 24, the construction of the house much be completed and the borrower should occupy the house. Then, they can claim a plot loan income tax benefit on interest up to Rs. 2 lakhs annually. This deduction cannot be availed if you do not reside in the house post its completion and give it on rent. The plot loan can be easily converted to a home loan by submitting a completion and occupancy certificate to the lender. Then, you can avail of tax benefit on plot purchase loan on interest. 3. Additional Plot Loan Income Tax Benefits Deduction on Interest Rate As per the Income Tax Act 1961, if anyone purchases a plot to build a home, they can get plot loans at a low rate of interest. This is beneficial to the borrower as they get a plot loan at a lower rate of interest which results in lower EMIs. Low Pre-construction Interest Rate The Income Tax Act 1961 allows for additional tax benefit on plot purchase loan through a reduced pre-construction rate of interest. When a borrower begins building activity at the start of a fiscal year, they get a deduction of the pre-construction rate of interest. This deduction is from the same year and can be claimed in 5 installments. It is available up to Rs. 2 lakhs provided the borrower resides in the property. Also, read – What is Home Loan Prepayment and How Does it Work? Example to understand the tax benefits Now that you have understood when an income tax rebate on plot loans is possible, let’s see an example. Meera decides to buy a land plot for Rs. 25 lakhs. She approaches a bank to avail of a loan of Rs. 25 lakhs. After one year, Meera plans to build a house on the same plot. The estimated cost of construction is Rs. 40 lakhs. She further decides to avail of a home loan for Rs. 40 lakhs. Combining the plot loan and the home loan, the total loan availed by Meera is Rs. 65 lakhs. So, can Meera claim an income tax rebate on a plot loan? Yes and no. For the first year of plot purchase, Meera cannot claim plot loan tax exemption. It is because there is no construction of a house on the plot. However, Meera can claim the plot plus construction loan tax benefit on the combined loan amount of Rs. 65 lakhs from the time of construction of the house to its completion. Best Cities to buy a plot in India Now that you understand the plot loan tax exemption , let’s see where it is recommended to buy plots. Below is the list of best cities where a plot can be purchased and you can claim plot loan income tax benefits: Bengaluru Ahmedabad Gurugram New Delhi Chennai Hyderabad Noida Pune Thane Ghaziabad Faridabad Conclusion A borrower can claim plot loan tax exemption provided they complete the construction of the house. Plot loan tax benefits become available only after you finish building a house on the land. Once the plot is developed for residential purposes, you can claim deductions on the interest you pay and certain related costs. To qualify for plot loan tax exemption , the construction must be completed within five years from the end of the financial year in which the loan was sanctioned. Which papers do I have to provide to receive tax benefits on my plot loan? To claim tax benefits on a plot loan, you’ll need to provide your loan sanction letter, interest certificates, and a completion or occupancy certificate. Once the construction is finished within the five-year limit, you can use these documents to claim deductions under Sections 24 and 80C of the Income Tax Act when filing your ITR. Is it possible to deduct pre-construction interest on plot loans from tax? Yes, you can claim pre-construction interest deductions on your plot loan, but only after the house is fully constructed. Beginning from the year the construction is completed, the total interest can be claimed in five equal yearly instalments. Bear in mind that this benefit applies only if you or your immediate family uses the property. Do both co-owners of a plot of land have the right to claim tax benefits? Yes, co-owners also have the right to claim plot loan income tax benefits , but only if they are also co-borrowers and each pays their share of the loan. According to Section 24 of the Income Tax Act, each co-owner can deduct their portion of the interest, while Section 80C lets them claim principal repayment. How can I own land and not pay taxes? Although you can't completely avoid taxes legally, it's possible to reduce your tax burden through exemptions and deductions. For instance, you can claim plot loan income tax benefits when the loan is used to build a residential house on the plot. The interest you pay on the loan can be deducted under Section 24, and principal repayments under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A home loan is a bridge that transforms the dream of homeownership into a reality. But while the benefits of a home loan are undeniable, understanding its implications on your income tax can be complicated. From understanding the tax benefits to decoding the various components of your home loan declaration, there are multiple aspects that you must consider. In this blog, we’ll guide you through the different sections in the Income Tax Act that allow tax deductions on home loans and how to declare home loans in Income Tax Returns. Section-wise tax benefits on home loan Before understanding how to declare home loan interest in Income Tax returns, it is crucial to understand the different sections of the IT Act that allow you to claim tax benefits on home loans . Sections of the Income Tax Act Nature of tax benefits Deduction limit Section 80C Deduction on repayment of the principal amount Up to ₹ 1.5 lakhs Section 24b Deduction on the interest provided that the construction or acquisition of the house completed within 5 years Up to ₹ 2 lakhs Section 80EE Additional deductions for loans taken to build the first property between April 2016 to March 2017, with a maximum loan amount of ₹ 35 lakhs and a maximum property value of ₹ 50 lakhs Up to ₹ 50,000 Section 80EEA Deductions for interest payments and section 24b Up to ₹ 1.5 lakhs + ₹ 2 lakhs (under section 24b) If you have taken a joint home loan, each borrower can claim a deduction of up to ₹ 2 lakhs on the loan interest under section 24b. Moreover, you can claim a deduction of up to ₹ 1.5 lakhs on the principal repayment amount for a joint home loan under section 80C. This section also allows a deduction of ₹ 1.5 lakhs on stamp duty and registration charges. Step-by-step guide to declare home loan in ITR Here is a step-by-step guide on how to declare home loans in income tax: Step 1: Ensure you have all your property ownership documents, certificates of construction and home loan approval with the interests and payments made, municipal taxes receipt and your identity proof. Step 2: Submit the documents to your employer. Step 3: Calculate the deductions you can claim on your home loan. Step 4: Visit the official Income Tax website to complete the submission of your home loan tax. After following all the mentioned steps, download your tax statement for verification. Documents required for home loan tax declaration When making a home loan tax declaration , submitting the correct documents helps ensure smooth and accurate deduction claims. Employers and tax authorities generally require the following: A duly filled home loan declaration form Interest certificate issued by the lender Principal repayment statement Loan sanction letter Possession or completion certificate Additionally, a valid home loan statement for income tax is essential to verify the breakup of principal and interest. These home loan documents for tax exemption support accurate calculations during ITR filing for home loan and help avoid discrepancies or delays. Common mistakes to avoid when declaring home loan in ITR Many taxpayers make avoidable errors during ITR filing for home loan , which may result in reduced deductions, delayed refunds, or tax notices. Common mistakes include: Claiming deductions before possession of the property, as tax benefits are allowed only after possession is completed Submitting incomplete or incorrect home loan documents for tax exemption , such as missing interest certificates or repayment proofs Using an outdated home loan statement for income tax that does not reflect the current financial year Exceeding eligible deduction limits under Section 80C or Section 24(b), which can lead to disallowed claims Mismatch between employer declarations and actual ITR entries , especially for salaried individuals Incorrect claims in joint home loans , such as claiming the full deduction instead of proportionate ownership share Making an accurate home loan tax declaration and verifying all documents before ITR filing for home loan helps avoid scrutiny and ensures a smoother tax filing experience. Home loan tax benefits for joint loan applicants Joint home loan applicants can significantly increase their overall tax savings when deductions are claimed correctly and in line with income tax rules. To ensure smooth ITR filing for home loan , the following points should be considered: Each applicant must be both a co-owner of the property and a co-borrower of the home loan to be eligible for tax deductions Separate home loan declaration forms must be submitted by each borrower, particularly when declaring investments to employers Individual home loan documents for tax exemption , including interest certificates and principal repayment statements, are mandatory for each applicant Tax benefits on principal repayment under Section 80C and interest under Section 24(b) can be claimed based on the ownership and repayment share During ITR filing for home loan , deductions should reflect the actual contribution made by each co-borrower Claiming the full deduction by one applicant, despite shared ownership, may lead to partial disallowance or tax scrutiny Proper documentation helps avoid mismatches between lender records, employer declarations, and income tax returns A well-prepared home loan tax declaration , supported by accurate documents, ensures that joint applicants can claim their rightful benefits without complications. Section 80C: Deduction on principal repayment Section 80C of the Income Tax Act allows taxpayers to claim a deduction of up to ₹1.5 lakh per financial year on the principal repayment of a home loan. This benefit is available only after the possession of the residential property and does not apply to commercial properties. For a valid home loan tax declaration , taxpayers must submit proof of principal repayment, usually reflected in the home loan statement for income tax issued by the lender. This document helps confirm the exact amount eligible for deduction. During ITR filing for home loan , it is important to ensure that the principal amount claimed under Section 80C is within the overall limit and does not overlap with other eligible investments such as PPF, ELSS, or life insurance premiums. Proper documentation and accurate reporting help avoid disallowance of deductions and ensure compliance with tax regulations. Section 24(b): Deduction on home loan interest Section 24(b) allows taxpayers to claim a deduction on the interest paid on a home loan, up to ₹2 lakh per financial year for a self-occupied residential property. For a let-out property, the entire interest paid may be claimed, subject to applicable income tax limits. In the case of under-construction properties, the deduction can be claimed only after possession. The interest paid during the construction period is allowed as a deduction in five equal instalments , starting from the year of possession. For an accurate home loan tax declaration , a lender-issued home loan statement for income tax or interest certificate is mandatory. During ITR filing for home loan , correctly reporting the interest amount ensures maximum eligible benefits while remaining fully compliant with income tax regulations. In a nutshell Home loans are a great way to fund your homeownership dreams. By understanding how to declare a home loan for income tax and arming yourself with knowledge, you not only enjoy the comforts of your home but also make the most of the financial advantages it brings. Under which sections can I claim tax benefits on a home loan? You can claim tax benefits on a home loan under sections 80C, 24b, 80EE and 80EEA. Can I claim tax benefits on a second home loan? Can I claim deductions on both principal and interest for my home loan? Yes. You can claim principal repayment under Section 80C and interest under Section 24(b). Ensure proper home loan tax declaration and submit valid home loan documents for tax exemption during ITR filing for home loan . What documents do I need to submit for home loan tax deductions? Separate home loan declaration forms and individual home loan documents for tax exemption are required while ITR filing for home loan . Can I claim tax benefits on a second home loan? Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Applying for a home loan is the first step towards owning the house of your dreams. While the application process is quick and easy to follow, not everyone is familiar with it. If you are a potential homebuyer looking for a home loan, it is imperative to be well-versed in the lender’s home loan eligibility criteria and the disbursal process for hassle-free loan approval. Here are the steps involved in obtaining a home loan. Filling out your home loan application form The process begins with applying to the lender either online or offline. They require you to fill in information such as personal details, residential address, employment, annual income, property details, and so on. Home loan eligibility criteria in India Before proceeding with the home loan application process​, you must understand whether you’re eligible for it. All lenders have set specific home loan eligibility criteria, and if you meet the requirements, your chances of loan approval are higher. The most common eligibility factors are: Age: You must be between 21 and 65 years of age. Employment status: You can either apply as a salaried individual with a stable job or a self-employed individual with a steady income source. Income: You must earn at least Rs. 30,000 per month. Credit score: Your credit score must be 750+, reflecting your ability to repay the loan. Documents required for a home loan application Once you have filled out the application form correctly, the lender will ask you to submit a list of documents along with it. This includes: Identity proof Income proof Address proof Employment details Proof of income Bank account statements Property details (if the loan is finalized) Payment of the processing fee Payment of processing fee After successful submission of the application and the required paperwork, you will have to pay a non-refundable processing fee to the lender. Most lenders charge a fee between 0.25% to 0.5% of the loan amount for the home loan application process. However, you can also negotiate to waive off this charge. Verification and credit check in the home loan process The lender will then assess your application and authenticate your documents. They will get in touch with you at your residence or your workplace to validate the information and credentials you have provided. Moreover, they will also run a credit inquiry and check your CIBIL score to determine your financial stability and repayment capacity. Issuance of home loan sanction letter and terms After the lender finds your application satisfactory, they will move forward with the home loan process and offer you the sanction letter. It contains the following details: Loan amount Rate of interest Type of interest rate- fixed or floating Repayment tenure Other terms and conditions associated with the loan Make sure that the letter mentions the home loan interest rate and other terms as discussed. You have to sign a copy of the sanction letter and revert to the lender with your acceptance. Property verification and valuation process Before disbursing the loan, the lender will check the property you intend to purchase. You will have to submit the original copy of the property-related documents. They will legally inspect the site to determine that the title is clear of any dispute. Similarly, they will run a technical valuation in case the property is under construction. Final loan disbursal and agreement signing Once all the aforementioned formalities are successfully carried out and you agree with the loan terms, the lender prepares the documentation and begins with the loan registration. Home loan processing time can take up to 2-3 weeks, depending upon the lender. After you sign the final agreement, the lender will disburse the loan as per the terms. Online home loan application process: How to apply digitally? Understanding the online home loan application process, step by step, is essential to ensure that you make no mistakes and have your loan sanctioned as early as possible. The online process eliminates the need to visit a branch physically. Check out the online home loan process step-by-step below: Visit the lender’s official website. Navigate to the dedicated Home Loan page. Press ‘Apply’. Enter your mobile number and verify with the OTP. Fill out the loan application form with basic details such as name, address, contact, employment details, etc. Upload the necessary documents. These include proof of identity, address, and income. Submit the form once you’ve completed it with accurate details. Await the lender’s home loan verification process and approval. Once approved, you will receive the loan amount in your account. Home loan processing time and approval timelines There are many steps in the home loan application process for both the borrower and the lender. It is not a one-day process. When you apply for a home loan online in India, it starts with you submitting your loan application and required documents, followed by the lender’s verification and assessment before disbursal. Any confusion at any step can make the process longer. To minimize their risks, lenders ensure that the information you’ve provided is correct and that you are capable of repaying their loan. They study your profile and the property details. If all documents are valid and accurate, the processing time and approval timeline for salaried professionals is about 4 to 5 working days. On the other hand, self-employed applicants can expect approval in 7 to 10 working days. Tips to avoid home loan application rejection A home loan application can be rejected due to various reasons, including low credit score, incomplete documentation, income instability, and property issues. You must eliminate all such challenges before initiating the home loan process. Here are some tips that can help avoid home loan application rejection: Improve your credit score : Pay all your dues on time to achieve a high credit score and increase the likelihood of loan approval. Make sure your credit report is updated: Review your credit report periodically – annually or bi-annually – to ensure there are no errors and it is accurately updated. Keep all documents ready: Check the list of documents the lender requires and arrange them beforehand. Do not change jobs frequently: Job hopping reflects income instability, reducing your chances of loan approval. Benefits of applying for a home loan in India Many people consider a home loan a financial burden. However, it has plenty of benefits.
