Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Introduction: It is not uncommon for borrowers to face financial difficulties during their loan term. The reasons can include job loss, medical emergencies, death of a family member, etc. In such times, the facility of loan modification can be a lifeline. Understanding what loan modification is, how it works, and its pros and cons can help you navigate financial challenges without defaulting. What is a loan modification? A loan modification refers to any permanent change made to the terms of an existing loan, often after a mutual agreement between the lender and the borrower. The modifications can include reducing the interest rate, extending the repayment tenure, changing the EMI plan, or allowing a different repayment structure. A loan modification is usually done to make repayment easier for the borrower without taking out a new loan. In simple terms, the lender alters the existing loan terms instead of replacing the loan itself. A loan modification is thus different from loan refinancing, which involves the borrower taking out a new loan (often with better repayment terms and interest rates) to pay off the existing one. Once you can define loan modification , it should not be a challenging task to understand what a modified loan is. To make it clear, a modified loan is a loan whose original terms have been officially altered after an agreement between the lender and the borrower. It can be any type of loan, including a home loan , personal loan , business loan , or car loan . A loan modification offers a lifeline to borrowers under financial stress while ensuring lenders continue to recover dues systematically. It can be of great relevance in the following scenarios: Job loss or reduced income Medical or family emergencies Business slowdown Natural disasters or economic disruptions Wars, riots, burglary, and other man-made disasters Rising interest burden Death or disability How does loan modification work? The loan modification process starts when the borrower requests that the lender alter the loan terms. However, the modifications are strictly subject to the lender’s discretion. The lender is not obligated to approve the loan modification request, but may do so if the borrower can demonstrate financial hardship and ensure repayment if the modification is approved. The lender may also assess the borrower’s credit history, other debts, income, and the overall financial scenario before agreeing to loan modification(s). Once the lender and the borrower reach a mutual agreement, they can proceed with the formalities for the modification. Below are the ways in which a loan can be modified: 1 Reduction in interest rate The lender may choose to reduce the loan interest rate temporarily or permanently. This can help in lowering the borrower’s EMI burden significantly without altering other loan parameters. 2 Extension of loan tenure The lender can also approve an extension of the loan tenure. Although it can lower the EMI amount by spreading the repayments over a longer duration, the overall interest outgo would increase. 3 Restructuring of the EMI schedul e The lender may offer to restructure the EMI schedule. For example, the borrower can choose to pay lower EMIs at present and gradually increase them in the future. This is a good option when there is a temporary slowdown in income. 4 Principal forbearance Principal forbearance involves the temporary suspension or deferment of the repayment of the principal amount. The borrower can continue to pay only the interest until they recover from the financial crunch. 5 EMI moratorium The lender may grant a temporary pause on EMIs, maybe for six to twelve months, without declaring the loan as defaulted. Benefits of loan modification in India Loan modification offers several financial and emotional advantages for borrowers facing temporary hardships. The most obvious advantage is that it helps them to regain financial stability without defaulting. Other notable loan modification benefits include: Improved cash flow A reduction in the interest rate or an extension of the loan tenure can help borrowers manage their monthly expenses more comfortably. For example, a salaried individual facing pay cuts can request a tenure extension to reduce the monthly financial burden. Avoiding foreclosure or asset loss One of the most crucial loan modification advantages is that it can help borrowers avoid foreclosure or loss of valuable assets, including cars, real estate properties, etc. By making repayments more affordable and convenient, the lender ensures the borrower continues repayment without defaulting. Credit score protection Defaulting on a loan can cause irreparable damage to your credit score. Timely loan modification can help borrowers repay under revised terms. This safeguards their credit history and their ability to apply for loans in the future. Peace of mind Financial hardships can take an emotional toll on anyone. The additional burden of loan repayment can add fuel to the fire. However, with the option of loan modification, the borrower can enjoy some peace of mind and focus on regaining financial strength. Avoiding legal action Loan modifications can help a borrower escape financial penalties as well as any legal action by the lender. Additionally, it helps the lender avoid the lengthy and costly process of loan recovery under the SARFAESI Act or court proceedings. Why do people opt for loan modification? While trying to understand the loan modification meaning , you must realize the reasons why borrowers seek it in the first place. It provides them with a lifeline during times of financial hardship. Here are some common reasons why people apply for a loan modification: Job loss or income reduction A sudden loss of employment or income reduction makes it difficult for anyone to keep up with the EMI payments. Applying for a loan modification can offer relief by lowering monthly payments. Business slowdown Self-employed individuals and small business owners often experience irregular cash flows. Opting for a loan modification can help manage repayments during such times. Medical emergencies A medical emergency at your home can quickly drain your savings. Opting for a loan modification can ease your financial burden, allowing you to focus on recovery rather than repayments. Death of a family member The sudden death of a family member can bring emotional as well as financial distress. Asking the lender to restructure loan repayments can bring relief in such a scenario. Natural disasters Natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods, or cyclones can damage property and livelihood. Loan modification or moratorium can provide financial breathing space during such circumstances. Unexpected life expenses Major life events such as a wedding, higher education, or home renovation can bring short-term financial distress. Opting for a loan modification can help you overcome without defaulting. Also, read – Understanding Debt Restructuring: Process & Benefits Types of loan modifications Loan modification can be of several types, depending on the modification made and its impact on the borrower. Let’s have a look at the common types of loan modifications and how they work for different loan products in India: Interest rate reduction Reducing the applicable interest rate either for the entire loan tenure or for a part of it helps in lowering the EMI amount and the total interest outgo. This type of loan modification works best for high-value loans, such as home loans and loans against properties. For example, a home loan of Rs. 50 lakhs at 10.5% per annum for 20 years requires you to pay approximately Rs. 49,919 as EMIs and Rs. 69,80,559 as interest. However, if your lender reduces the interest rate to 9.5%, your EMIs will drop to Rs. 46,607, and your total interest outgo will be Rs. 61,85,574. Tenure extension Increasing the repayment tenure spreads your EMIs over a longer period, thereby reducing monthly payments. This type of loan modification works best for short-term loans, such as personal loans and car loans. For example, if you take a personal loan of Rs. 10 lakhs for five years at 12% per annum interest rate, your EMIs would be Rs. 22,444. Extending the tenure to eight years can reduce your EMIs to Rs. 16,253. Principal forbearance Principal forbearance involves temporarily deferring a portion of the principal repayment. It can be paid at a later date or at the end of the loan term. This reduces the immediate financial burden on the borrower by lowering the EMI amount. Repayment structuring It involves an alteration of the original payment structure. For example, a lender can allow the borrower struggling after a salary cut to switch to step-up EMIs from fixed EMIs. This arrangement allows them to pay lower EMIs in the beginning, and gradually increase them as their income increases. How to qualify for a loan modification in India? There isn’t a defined criterion to qualify for a loan modification in India. It typically depends on the borrower’s ability to demonstrate financial hardship and prove an inability to pay current EMIs. However, the final decision of whether or not to approve a loan modification request rests solely with the lending institution. Here are some basic factors that can determine your loan modification eligibility: Existing loan type The loan type matters a lot. Most banks and Non-Banking Financial Corporations (NBFCs) in India accept loan modification requests for long-term loans, including home loans and loans against properties. It’s because these loans often entail prolonged repayment tenures, and a borrower may go through tough phases in between. Financial hardship The borrower’s ability to demonstrate financial hardship and the reason behind it can have a significant impact. You must be able to explain why you are seeking a loan modification and how it can help you repay your loan more conveniently. Provide documents to support your claim of a job loss or income reduction, medical emergency, etc. Income documents Any evidence of income loss, such as a pay-cut notice, an Income Tax Return (ITR), profit-loss statements, bank statements, etc., can help you support your request for a loan modification. Clear and accurate documents boost approval chances. Lender’s policies Different lenders may have different policies regarding loan modifications. While lenders have a lenient approach and happily accommodate loan modification requests, some do not. Review your loan agreement or contact your relationship manager to understand your lender’s policy before applying. Pros and cons of loan modification in India Loan modification offers both advantages as well as disadvantages for lenders and borrowers. Understanding the loan modification pros and cons can help you make the right financial decision. Let’s have a look at them: Advantages: Improved cash flow A loan modification can reduce the borrower’s monthly financial burden. Subsequently, it improves their cash flow and helps them manage day-to-day expenses more comfortably. Foreclosure avoidance For home/car loan borrowers, loan default can result in foreclosure of the asset. A modification in loan terms can help them avoid such a situation. Credit score protection Missed or delayed EMIs payments can severely hamper your credit score. A loan default can even cause irreparable damage. Timely loan modification can prevent such circumstances. Avoid legal fees By allowing simple loan modifications, lenders can avoid costly lawsuits and loan recovery expenses. They can accept gradual repayments from financially struggling borrowers. Disadvantages Higher interest outgo While an extended loan tenure can decrease your monthly EMI payments , you may end up with a higher interest outgo. Potential fees Some lenders charge a nominal processing fee for loan modifications. This can increase your overall borrowing costs. Future risk Although a loan modification can provide temporary relief, it may expose you to greater risks in the future. If your financial situation doesn’t improve, you might struggle even with the modified repayment terms. No guarantee of approval A lender is not obligated to accept loan modification requests. The approval depends on the lender’s policy and several other factors. How to apply for a loan modification? The loan modification process in India involves a few key steps and transparent communication with the lender. Here’s how you can apply for a loan modification : 1. Understand the eligibility Start by researching and understanding the lender’s policies and other factors that can influence your loan modification eligibility. Gather information on the types of loan modifications available, reasons accepted, and the documents required. 2. Gather the required documents Start collecting the required documents to support your loan modification request. These may include pay-cut notices, emergency hospitalization bills, bank statements, ITRs, and other documents that can demonstrate your financial hardship. 3. Approach the lender Once you have all the documents ready, you can approach your lender and submit a formal request for a loan modification. Be transparent and clearly state the reason why you are seeking a loan modification in your application. Submit all the documents to validate your claim. 4. Wait for the approval The lender may take some time to verify and approve your loan modification request. Be patient and wait for the process. You may be asked to make trial payments to demonstrate your ability to meet modified payment terms. 5. Agreement and implementation After careful evaluation, the lender may agree to modify your loan repayment terms. It will send you a formal agreement outlining the revised loan terms. Carefully review and accept it to activate the changes. Alternatives to loan modification in India Even after all your efforts, it may happen that the lender denies your loan modification request. What to do in such a case? What are the other options to modify a loan ? Here are some loan modification alternatives you can explore: Loan refinancing Loan refinancing is probably the best loan modification alternative you can consider. It involves taking a new loan with the same or a different lender at a lower interest rate and using it to pay off your existing loan. It can help you reduce your EMI burden and the total interest cost significantly. However, you may require a good credit score to avail of a new loan, and it may involve a processing fee and other one-time charges. Balance transfer You can even choose to transfer your existing loan balance to a different lender offering better interest rates and repayment terms. Doing so can significantly reduce your financial burden and ease your repayment headache. Debt consolidation Debt consolidation refers to the process of combining multiple existing loans into a single loan with one EMI. If you are struggling to pay separate EMIs for personal loans, car loans, home loans, etc., you can take a single, larger loan and foreclose others. It can streamline your repayments, but your overall tenure and the total repayment amount might increase. Partial settlement If you are unable to continue with your loan repayment , you can negotiate with your lender for a partial settlement. The lender may accept a reduced amount and close your loan account. However, this can damage your credit score and hurt your chances of taking a loan in the future. Yes. A loan modification can affect your credit score both positively and negatively, depending on the circumstances. If you have missed your EMIs and seek a loan modification, it can hurt your credit score. On the flip side, regular repayments with modified terms can help build your credit score. How long does it take to get a loan modification approval? The time taken for loan modification approval varies from lender to lender. It may also depend on your ability to demonstrate financial hardship and the authenticity of the documents submitted by you. Your lender may take up to three months to accept or deny your request. Is there a fee for applying for a loan modification with Tata Capital? Yes. You may have to pay a nominal processing fee for a loan modification with Tata Capital. The exact amount depends on the type of loan and the modification requested. For more details, visit our Loan Charges page or get in touch with our customer care executive. Will my EMI always reduce after modification? Your EMIs might reduce if you are applying for an interest rate reduction or loan tenure extension. However, if you choose to repay faster or add missed EMIs to the balance, your EMI could remain the same or even increase slightly, depending on the revised terms. Can I get a loan modification for a home loan/business loan/personal loan? Yes. You can request a loan modification for most loans, including home loans, business loans, and personal loans. However, your eligibility to get your loan modified depends on your ability to demonstrate financial hardship. What happens if my loan modification request is rejected? If your lender rejects your loan modification request, you can consider other alternatives to reduce your financial burden. These include loan refinancing, balance transfer, debt consolidation, and partial settlement. It is the annualized rate of return used to measure the growth of a mutual fund from its initial to its final value over a definite period. The calculation assumes that profits, including dividends and gains, are reinvested. You can use CAGR to directly compare the performance of different mutual fund schemes across varying time periods. Its best use is to evaluate the performance of lump sum investments over a holding period of 1 year or more. The CAGR formula reflects the snowball effect of reinvested profits in mutual fund schemes . It helps you project future growth and determine if your long-term goals are on track. Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) is the smoothed yearly growth rate of an investment over a specific period. So, if you have ever wanted to calculate your mutual fund investment’s growth each year on average, CAGR is what you need to use. It does not show the ups and downs from year to year, but presents growth as a steady annual rate. As a result, it makes it easier for you to compare different investments. CAGR helps you understand at what pace your money is growing over time, enabling you to efficiently plan financial goals like buying a home, a child’s education, or building a retirement corpus. In this article, you will learn CAGR’s full form, CAGR’s meaning, CAGR’s formula with an example, and how it is used in mutual funds. What is CAGR? Full form and meaning CAGR stands for Compound Annual Growth Rate. It is the constant yearly rate at which your investment would have grown, compounding steadily over time. It smooths out year-to-year ups and downs. In other words, it indicates the average yearly growth of your investment from the beginning value to the ending value. You can use the calculation method regardless of whether the investment is a mutual fund, fixed-income product, stock, real estate, or any other asset . Generally, investors use CAGR to compare performance and understand an investment’s long-term growth more clearly. Also, read – Venture capital market in India What is the CAGR formula, and how to calculate it? The formula for calculating CAGR is: ((Ending value/Beginning value) ^ (1/n)) – 1 where, Ending value refers to the final investment value Beginning value refers to the initial investment value n stands for the number of years To get the CAGR percentage, you must multiply the result by 100. Let us look at the following example to learn how to calculate CAGR in a mutual fund. Suppose the starting value of a mutual fund investment was Rs. 1,00,000, while the ending value was Rs. 2,00,000. The time period was 5 years. Ending value / starting value = 200000/100000 = 2 2 ^ (1/5) – 1 = 0.1487 0.1487 X 100 = 14.87% So, the investment’s growth was at a CAGR of around 14.87% per year over 5 years. Also, read – Where should NRIs invest their money in India? What is CAGR in mutual funds? After you’ve grasped CAGR’s generic meaning and formula, it is vital to understand the meaning of CAGR in a mutual fund specifically. The numeric value indicates the annualized return of a fund over a period of 1, 3, 5, or 10 years. It shows how much a lump-sum investment would have grown each year on average if it had compounded at a steady rate. You can find the CAGR value in mutual fund fact sheets. It helps you compare different funds on a like-for-like basis. However, it reflects the point-to-point growth of a lump-sum investment and does not account for regular Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) contributions. Also, read – Private credit vs private equity vs public debt How to calculate CAGR for a mutual fund? Learning how to calculate the CAGR for a mutual fund is vital to making the most of your investments. Here is an illustration to help with the same. Suppose your initial investment amount in a mutual fund is Rs. 1,00,000, and its final value grows to Rs. 1,90,000 after 5 years. CAGR = ((190000 / 100000) ^ (1/5)) – 1 The calculation estimates a CAGR of approximately 13.7% per year. This means your lump-sum mutual fund investment grew at an average compounded rate of 13.7% over 5 years. You can also calculate CAGR using the fund’s starting and ending Net Asset Values (NAVs) over a specific period. What is the difference between CAGR and absolute return? Absolute return estimates the total percentage gain or loss on an investment. It does not consider the holding period. On the other hand, CAGR converts the total return into an annualized growth rate. As a result, it becomes easier to compare investments held for different periods. For example, if a mutual fund investment grows from Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 1,90,000 in 5 years, its absolute return is calculated as follows: Absolute return = (Final value – Initial value) / (Initial value) X 100 Absolute return = (190000 – 100000) / (100000) X 100 = 90% However, the CAGR is only approximately 13.7% per year. The CAGR shows the average annual compounded growth rate over the 5-year period. Also, read – How many mutual funds should you hold? CAGR vs XIRR: Which should you use for mutual funds? The key differentiator between CAGR and Extended Internal Rate of Return (XIRR) is its suitability. CAGR is for a single lump-sum investment, and XIRR is for SIPs or multiple investments. Here’s a table to help you differentiate between the two: Basis CAGR XIRR Full form Compound Annual Growth Rate Extended Internal Rate of Return Best used for Single lump-sum investment SIPs and multiple investments Considers the timing of cash flows No Yes Suitable for regular SIPs No Yes Calculation method Uses beginning value, ending value, and time period Uses all investment and redemption dates Accuracy for SIP returns Can be misleading More accurate Common use Point-to-point mutual fund returns are shown in the fact sheets Actual investor returns from SIPs and staggered investments In a nutshell, if you invested once and held the fund, check the CAGR. If you invested through SIPs or made multiple transactions, use XIRR to understand your real returns. What are the limitations of CAGR? The limitations of CAGR are as follows: 1. Assumes smooth growth: CAGR assumes investments grow at a smooth, steady rate, which rarely happens in real markets. 2. Hides volatility and drawdowns: CAGR only looks at the starting and ending values. It hides volatility and does not show interim gains, losses, or market crashes. 3. Depends on the start and end dates: CAGR is highly sensitive to the chosen start and end dates, as it measures only point-to-point performance. 4. Ignores immediate cash flows: It does not account for intermediate cash flows, such as additional investments or withdrawals. 5. Not suited for SIPs: SIPs involve multiple investments over time. Thus, CAGR cannot accurately measure returns. Why does CAGR matter to mutual fund investors? If investors know what a CAGR is in mutual funds, they can compare the long-term performance of different funds. The method is simple and consistent. It helps set realistic expectations by showing the average annual growth rate of a lump-sum investment over time. However, you must not view CAGR in isolation. For a complete evaluation, you must also consider rolling returns, risk levels, and the fund’s volatility before making investment decisions. Conclusion Compound Annual Growth Rate, or CAGR, is a useful metric for understanding the average annual growth rate of a lump-sum mutual fund investment over a period of time. It smooths out year-to-year fluctuations and makes it easier to compare fund performance. The formula relies on a fund’s beginning value and ending value and assumes that the profits are reinvested. However, if you are looking at SIPs or investments with multiple cash flows, XIRR is the more appropriate measure. To get a balanced view, you should also evaluate CAGR alongside risk, volatility, and rolling returns. Build Your Wealth with Expert Guidance from Tata Capital! Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Almost every year, RBI puts out guidelines that every home loan provider and lending institutions must mandatorily follow. This is done to maintain uniformity amongst different providers and act in the customers’ best interests. In 2019, RBI has made changes that make home loans easier for borrowers to pay. These guidelines include: Know More There are to be no pre-payment charges across all banks and lenders in the case of floating interest loans. External benchmarks for interest rates have been established to which all floating rate loans have to be linked. The 3 external benchmarks include RBI’s policy repo rate, the Government’s 3-month and 6-month treasury bill yields, and any other benchmark rates that have been or will be published by Financial Benchmarks India Private Limited. Borrowers who have already taken out home loans can switch to these benchmark-associated loans at no additional cost. Borrowers can get funding of up to 90% of the property value through a home loan if this 90% comes out to be less than or equal to Rs. 30 lakhs. Borrowers can get funding of up to 80% of the property value through a home loan if this 80% comes out to be more than Rs. 30 lakhs but up to Rs. 75 lakhs. For all other loans, the maximum funding stands at 75% of the property value. Borrowers are not mandated to purchase insurance from home loan lenders. Registration charges, stamp duty, and other charges related to documentation are not to be included when the loan-to-value ratio is being calculated. There will be no foreclosure charges on home loans. Up to Rs. 35 lakhs, loans in metro cities will be regarded as priority sector loans. If a borrower switches his loan to one linked with the external benchmark, the interest rate they incur will be the same as that of a new loan. Banks have to adhere to a uniform external benchmark within one particular loan category. The interest rate of home loans has to be reset at least every 3 months according to the external benchmark. The credit risk premium can be changed only in the case of a borrower’s credit assessment undergoing a noticeable change. The flexibility in terms of this change is specified in the loan contract. Banks and lenders can decide the spread over the external benchmark independently, and this spread can be altered once in every 3 years. The home loan interest rates start at a low 9.25% and the amount goes from Rs. 2 lakhs right up to Rs. 5 crores. With a Tata Capital housing loan, you never have to wait to own your dream house – apply for home loan today! RBI Rules For Home Loan The Reserve Bank of India sets the rules within which every bank and housing finance company in the country lends for housing. These rules decide how much of a property’s value can be financed, how interest rates are set and revised, and what protections you are entitled to as a borrower. Understanding them helps you know what a lender can and cannot do at every stage of your loan. Role of RBI in Housing Finance The RBI regulates housing credit across the financial system. It directly supervises scheduled commercial banks and, since 2019, has also regulated housing finance companies, which were previously overseen by the National Housing Bank. Through its guidelines, the RBI sets lending caps such as the loan-to-value ratio, prescribes how floating interest rates must be benchmarked and reset, defines fair practice standards for loan servicing and recovery, and uses the repo rate to influence the cost of housing credit across the economy. Why RBI Regulations Are Important for Borrowers RBI regulations exist to keep the lending relationship fair. They ensure you receive a Key Facts Statement disclosing the total cost of your loan before you sign, that your floating rate moves with a transparent external benchmark rather than an internal rate the lender controls, that you can prepay a floating rate loan without penalty, and that your original property documents are returned within 30 days of full repayment. Without these rules, each lender could set its own terms on every one of these points. RBI Guidelines For Home Loan Documents The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has set forth specific guidelines for the documentation required when applying for a home loan, aiming to streamline the process and ensure transparency. These guidelines include: 1 – Identity Proof : A government-issued photo ID such as a passport, PAN card, or Aadhar card. 2- Address Proof : Documents like utility bills, Aadhar card, or passport to verify the applicant’s current residence. 3 – Income Proof : Salary slips, income tax returns, and bank statements are required to ascertain the borrower’s repayment capacity. 4 – Property Documents : Legal documents related to the property being purchased, including the sale deed, NOC from the builder or society, and property tax receipts. 5 – Credit History : A report detailing the applicant’s credit scores and past loan repayment records to assess creditworthiness. Key RBI Guidelines for Home Loans in India Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio Norms The LTV ratio caps how much of the property’s value a lender can finance. The remainder is your down payment. The RBI’s LTV slabs for individual housing loans are: Loan Amount Maximum LTV Minimum Down Payment Up to ₹30 lakh 90% 10% Above ₹30 lakh and up to ₹75 lakh 80% 20% Above ₹75 lakh 75% 25% Stamp duty and registration charges are excluded from the LTV calculation, except for properties costing up to ₹10 lakh, so budget for these costs separately. Repo Rate and Its Impact on Home Loan Interest Rates The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks. Since October 2019, financial institutions have been required to link floating-rate retail loans to an external benchmark, most commonly the repo rate, under the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) system. When the RBI cuts the repo rate, your EBLR-linked home loan rate falls at the next reset, and when the RBI raises it, your rate rises. This makes rate transmission faster and more transparent than the older internal benchmark systems. Floating vs Fixed Interest Rate Rules Under the RBI’s guidelines for floating rate loans, lenders must inform borrowers when benchmark rate changes affect their EMI or tenure. They must also offer a switch to a fixed rate as per board-approved policy, allow EMI or tenure adjustments where applicable, and permit part-prepayment or full prepayment as per the loan terms. Any switching charges must be disclosed upfront. Factor Floating Rate Fixed Rate Rate Movement Changes with the external benchmark Constant for the fixed period EMI Predictability Varies at reset Stable Prepayment Charges Not permitted for individual borrowers May apply as per loan terms Suitable For Borrowers expecting rates to fall or hold Borrowers who want payment certainty Risk Weight on Housing Loans Risk weight decides how much capital a lender must set aside against a loan. The RBI links risk weights on individual housing loans to the LTV ratio: the lower your LTV, the lower the risk weight and the cheaper the loan is for the lender to carry. This is one reason a larger down payment often earns you a better interest rate. It also keeps the housing finance system stable by requiring more capital against riskier, higher-LTV lending. Prepayment and Foreclosure Charges Rules Under the RBI’s Pre-payment Charges on Loans Directions, 2025, lenders cannot charge prepayment or foreclosure fees on floating rate loans taken by individuals for non-business purposes. This applies to loans sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026, and covers both partial prepayments and full foreclosure, with no minimum lock-in period. Fixed rate loans may still attract prepayment charges, but these must be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and the Key Facts Statement. Latest RBI Guidelines For Home Loan Moratoriums and Restructuring The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced guidelines for home loan moratoriums and restructuring to provide relief to borrowers facing financial difficulties. Here are the key points: 1 – Financial Hardship Consideration : The guidelines allow banks to offer moratoriums or restructuring options to borrowers demonstrating financial hardship due to unforeseen circumstances. 2 – Moratorium Period : Borrowers can avail of a temporary suspension of EMI payments, with specific terms and duration as determined by the lender based on RBI directives. 3 – Restructuring Options : Includes altering the repayment schedule, extending the loan tenure, or changing the interest rate to make the loan more manageable for the borrower. 4 – Application Process : Borrowers must apply for these relief measures within a specified timeframe, providing necessary documentation to prove their financial distress. 5 – Impact on Credit Score : The RBI has provided provisions that ensure such restructuring or moratoriums, when granted, do not adversely affect the borrower’s credit score. Eligibility Criteria as per RBI Guidelines The RBI does not prescribe a single eligibility checklist for home loans. Instead, it sets the framework within which lenders build their own criteria. RBI rules require lenders to verify KYC, assess repayment capacity through documented income, report repayment behaviour to credit bureaus, and stay within the LTV caps for the loan size. Age: Most lenders accept applicants between 21 and 65 years, with the loan expected to close before or around retirement. Income and Stability: Salaried and self-employed applicants both qualify, with income assessed through salary slips, bank statements, or income tax returns. Credit Score : The RBI does not mandate a minimum score, but lenders use it as a primary filter. A higher score improves both approval chances and the rate offered. Existing Obligations: Current EMIs reduce the income available for a new loan, so lenders assess your total debt relative to your income before deciding on the loan amount. RBI Guidelines on Prepayment and Foreclosure Prepayment reduces your outstanding principal ahead of schedule, and foreclosure closes the loan entirely before the tenure ends. The RBI’s rules on both depend on your interest rate type. For floating rate home loans taken by individuals, no prepayment or foreclosure charges can be levied. The 2025 Directions extend this protection to all loans sanctioned or renewed from January 1, 2026, regardless of whether a co-borrower is on the loan, and prohibit lenders from imposing any lock-in period before you can prepay. For fixed-rate loans, lenders may charge a prepayment fee as specified in the loan agreement. The charge must be disclosed in the sanction letter and Key Facts Statement and cannot be introduced or increased later. After full repayment, the lender must return your original property documents within 30 days and remove charges registered against the property. If the lender delays beyond this, RBI rules require it to compensate you for each day of delay. RBI Guidelines for Home Loan Balance Transfer A balance transfer moves your outstanding loan to a new lender, and RBI rules govern each step. Since floating rate home loans carry no foreclosure charges for individual borrowers, your existing lender cannot penalise you for switching. It must issue the foreclosure letter and the statement of account upon request and hand over your original property documents within 30 days of closure. The new lender treats the transfer as a fresh loan. It conducts its own credit appraisal, verifies the property, and must provide you with a Key Facts Statement that shows the total cost of the new loan, including processing fees and the annual percentage rate. Compare this against your remaining interest on the existing loan before deciding. The RBI’s rate transparency rules work in your favour here: as both lenders price off external benchmarks, you can compare spreads directly rather than decoding two different internal rate systems. Borrower Rights Under RBI Home Loan Rules RBI regulations give home loan borrowers a defined set of rights that apply across all banks and housing finance companies: Right to Transparent Pricing: You must receive a Key Facts Statement before signing, showing the interest rate, all fees, and the annual percentage rate in a standard format. Right to Rate Reset Options: At each floating rate reset, you can choose between a revised EMI and a revised tenure and ask to switch to a fixed rate as per the lender’s policy. Right to Penalty-Free Prepayment: On floating-rate loans, you can prepay or foreclose at any time without charges. Right to Your Documents: Original property documents must be returned within 30 days of full repayment, with compensation payable for delays. Right to Fair Recovery Practices: Lenders and their recovery agents must follow the RBI’s fair practices code, which prohibits harassment and requires proper notice before action. Right to Grievance Redressal: Every lender must have a grievance mechanism. If your complaint is not resolved within 30 days, you can escalate it to the RBI’s Integrated Ombudsman at no cost. How RBI Guidelines Impact Home Loan Borrowers Loan-to-Value (LTV) Limits : RBI’s LTV norms determine the minimum down payment you need based on the loan amount. Since stamp duty and registration charges are generally excluded from the LTV calculation, you should budget for these expenses separately. No Prepayment Charges on Floating Rate Loans : Individual borrowers with floating rate home loans can make part or full prepayments without prepayment charges. Paying off a portion of the loan early can reduce your interest burden and may shorten the loan tenure. Flexibility During Interest Rate Resets : When interest rates change, lenders must inform you of the impact on your EMI or tenure. Depending on the loan terms, you may have the option to increase your EMI, extend the tenure, or switch to a fixed interest rate. Credit Score Matters More : Lenders regularly review your credit history during loan assessment. Maintaining a good repayment record and paying EMIs and credit card bills on time can improve your eligibility for better loan terms. Protection of Original Property Documents : Lenders are responsible for safeguarding your original property documents during the loan tenure. After the loan is closed, they must return the documents within the applicable regulatory timeline. Greater Transparency in Digital Lending : RBI’s digital lending guidelines require lenders to disclose all applicable charges upfront, identify the regulated lending entity, and provide a grievance redressal mechanism, helping borrowers make informed decisions. Home Loan Interest Rate RBI Guidelines Interest rates are a significant factor for borrowers, influencing the overall cost of the loan and monthly repayments. The RBI has introduced several guidelines to ensure fairness and transparency in how interest rates are determined: 1 – Adoption of External Benchmarks : The RBI mandates that banks link the interest rates of home loans to an external benchmark, such as the repo rate. This move ensures that borrowers benefit directly from any changes in the monetary policy. 2 – Review and Reset Period : Lenders are required to have a clear review and reset period for interest rates, typically once every three months, providing timely reflection of changes in the benchmark rates. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary A savings scheme for a girl child is a special savings plan dedicated to keeping daughters financially secure. It helps you build a corpus for your girl child’s future, such as higher education or marriage. You can opt for government-backed savings schemes or those offered by private institutions. The best investment plan for a girl child in India is the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY). It is a government initiative focusing on wealth generation to secure the future of your girl child. A savings scheme for a girl childis designed exclusively for young girls. It promotes early saving and often comes with guaranteed interest and tax benefits. If your goal is to build a tax-efficient corpus for your daughter’s future goals, it is essential to choose the right savings and investment plan. These goals can include schooling, higher education, marriage, or other milestones. In India, there are several investment plans for a girl child, including government-backed schemes , Public Provident Fund (PPF), mutual funds , child insurance plans , and fixed deposits. Each option offers different returns, risks, tax benefits, flexibility, and investment horizons, making it difficult for you to choose the best scheme for a girl child. This guide outlines the features, benefits, and limitations of popular investment options so you can choose the most suitable plan for your daughter’s long-term financial security. Why should you start investing early for your girl child? When you start investing early, your investments have more time to benefit from compounding, in which returns earn additional returns over the years. Using the power of compounding, you can grow even small, regular investments into a significant corpus by the time your daughter reaches important milestones such as higher education or marriage. Moreover, if you begin early, you will need a lower monthly or annual contribution to reach your goal. For example, if you make a Rs. 25,000 annual investment for a girl child, starting from her birth until she turns 18, you can build a sizeable corpus. The wealth generated and growth will depend on the actual returns earned. You can use the savings to cover future educational expenses without financial stress. Also, read – Multi Asset Funds Explained What are the best saving and investment options for a girl child? India offers many savings and investment options to help you build a financial corpus for your daughter’s future. Some of these plans focus on safety and guaranteed returns, while others aim for higher long-term growth. To choose the best investment plan for a girl child in India, you will need to understand your goals, investment horizon, and risk appetite. In the sections below, you will find details on the best schemes for a girl child in India, helping you understand safer, lower-risk options and growth-oriented investments with higher return potential. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY): The flagship scheme Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is the government-backed flagship savings scheme for a girl child. It is often viewed as the best scheme for a girl child as it is risk-free and helps fulfill long-term goals. It offers attractive returns, strong tax benefits, and a structured investment period. The scheme matures exactly 21 years from the date of account opening. However, you need to make deposits only for the first 15 years. The government reviews the interest rate quarterly and revises it as needed. Interest rate 8.2% p.a., as of June 16, 2026 (Q1 FY2026-27) Tax benefit Deductions of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh under Section 80C Tax status Exempt-Exempt-Exempt (EEE) – investment, interest, and maturity amounts are tax-free Eligibility The account must be opened before the girl turns 10. Minimum deposit Rs. 250 Maximum deposit Rs. 1.5 lakh per year Deposit period 15 years from account opening Maturity 21 years from account opening or at marriage after 18 years of age Withdrawal Partially, up to 50% at the age of 18 for higher education Public Provident Fund (PPF) The Public Provident Fund (PPF) is another safe, government-backed savings scheme for a girl child. It currently offers around 7.1% annual interest (as of June 16, 2026). However, the interest rate is not fixed, and the government reviews it every quarter. Like SSY, PPF also enjoys EEE tax status. This means your investment, gains, and maturity amounts are tax-free. You can open a PPF account in a child’s name under a guardian’s supervision. The deposits into PPF are also deductible under Section 80C. However, the total deductions for SSY and PPF investments can together be up to Rs. 1.5 lakh of the Section 80C limit. Thus, PPF is a good complement to SSY because it offers greater flexibility. Mutual funds and SIPs for a girl child If you have a long investment horizon of 10 to 18 years, equity mutual funds through Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) can be the best investment plan for your girl child in India. Their growth potential is higher than fixed-rate schemes such as SSY or PPF. However, they also carry market risks. Under this category of savings scheme for a girl child, you can consider children’s funds, gift funds, or diversified equity mutual funds . But you must know that there are no guaranteed returns, and you may face ups and downs. You can adopt a balanced approach that uses SSY and PPF as a safe foundation, with mutual funds for long-term growth. Child insurance and ULIP plans Most insurance companies offer child-focused plans, including child endowment plans, Unit-Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs), and money-back policies. These products combine insurance and investment. However, before proceeding, you must understand the purposes of both. A child has no income to insure. Thus, your first priority must be having adequate term insurance for the earning parent. Many bundled child plans may have higher premiums and lower return potential than buying term insurance separately and investing through SSY, PPF, or mutual funds. You must carefully compare costs, benefits, and returns before deciding which is the best policy for a girl child. Fixed deposits and recurring deposits Fixed Deposits (FDs) and Recurring Deposits (RDs) are safe and predictable savings options offered by banks and post offices. They provide fixed returns and are the ideal choice if you prefer stability over growth. However, the interest earned on these deposits is taxable, which can reduce post-tax returns compared with tax-efficient options such as SSY and PPF. FDs and RDs are best used for short-term goals or as a small, stable portion of your overall investment plan for your daughter. Also, read – Understanding global investments What are the government schemes for the girl child in India? In addition to the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), there are several other government schemes designed to support the education, welfare, and financial security of girl children in India. SSY is a central government scheme available nationwide. However, many states offer their own programs with different eligibility conditions and benefits. Some examples are Ladli, Bhagyashree, Kanyashree, and Bhagyalakshmi schemes. The rules of these savings schemes for a girl child can change over time. Therefore, you must check your state government’s official portal for the latest details. How to choose the right plan for your daughter? Choosing the right plan for your daughter becomes easier when you match each investment to your daughter’s future goals, time horizon, and your risk appetite. The framework you can adopt is as follows: Build a safe foundation with SSY and, if suitable, PPF. Add equity mutual funds through SIPs. Focus on long-term growth for over 10 to 18 years. Secure the earning parent with adequate term insurance. Use safer options for near-term goals and growth-oriented investments for long-term goals. Review your plan periodically and adjust as per your goals. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary An HUF home loan is a housing loan that a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) can secure to purchase a home. For this type of home loan, the family’s Karta acts as the primary applicant. Families can use the funds to jointly purchase residential property, build ancestral assets, and share the tax burden. To check the eligibility for granting a loan to an HUF, lenders evaluate the income generated from HUF assets, including rent, interest, and capital gains, along with the Karta’s personal income. Banks offer loans to HUF, or Hindu Undivided Family, as a credit facility in the name of the family unit. Under this system, the Karta acts as the authorized applicant. A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) is a separate legal and tax entity under Indian law. Just like an individual, an HUF can also own property, earn income, and even borrow money from banks and housing finance companies. This makes opening an HUF a useful concept for families looking to buy a house and manage assets collectively. However, the HUF home loan process is slightly different from that of an individual borrower. It requires specific eligibility conditions, documentation, and legal requirements. If you are planning to apply for an HUF loan for buying a property, understanding the process in advance can make things much easier. This page explains how an HUF can apply for a home loan, the eligibility criteria, required documents, application process, and available tax benefits. What is a HUF? HUF’s full form is Hindu Undivided Family. It is a family-based legal and tax entity recognized under Hindu law. It comprises a Karta for managing the HUF. There are coparceners, who are family members with rights in the family property. An HUF can have its own Permanent Account Number (PAN) and assets. It can earn income through rent, interest, and capital gains and file Income Tax Returns (ITRs) independently of its members. Due to this separate status, an HUF can hold property and apply for different types of loans if it fulfills the lender’s rules. Can an HUF take a home loan? Many individuals wonder, “Can an HUF take a home loan?” The answer is yes, an HUF can take a home loan. HUF is a separate legal and tax entity. Thus, it can buy residential property and borrow funds for the purchase. Generally, the Karta makes the loan application, who acts on behalf of the HUF. It is important to understand that not all banks and housing finance companies offer home loans to HUFs. The lending policies differ across institutions. As a result, eligibility criteria , documentation requirements , and loan availability may vary from one lender to another. What is the role of the Karta and coparceners in an HUF home loan? In an HUF home loan, the Karta plays the central role as the primary applicant and authorized signatory. The Karta represents the HUF in all lender communications and signs the loan documents on its behalf. Coparceners are members of the HUF. According to Hindu law, both sons and daughters are coparceners and have equal rights in HUF property. They can be added as co-applicants if the lender requires. Generally, their consent is needed for major property and borrowing decisions. The responsibility of repaying the loan is generally of the HUF and the Karta. Also, read – Understanding Declaration Deeds for Property Ownership What are the eligibility criteria for an HUF home loan? Banks approve loans to HUF if they fulfill the following eligibility criteria: The HUF is a valid entity with its own PAN. The HUF has a stable and verifiable income or cash flow. The HUF and the Karta’s credit profile should be acceptable. The property being purchased should be held in the HUF’s name. The HUF must meet the lender’s specific eligibility and documentation requirements. Before sanctioning a loan, lenders evaluate the HUF’s income and repayment capacity. Eligibility is not restricted to the Karta’s personal income. What are the documents required for an HUF home loan? You must submit the following documents when you apply for an HUF loan. HUF PAN Card HUF deed or declaration document KYC documents of the Karta for identity and address proof Details and KYC documents of coparceners, if required HUF income proof and recent bank statements Income Tax Returns (ITRs) of the HUF Property-related documents, such as the sale agreement and title papers Note: The documentation requirements for an HUF loan may differ from one lender to another. Thus, you must check the lender’s specific list before applying. Also, read – What Are the Pros and Cons of Starting a HUF Business? What is the step-by-step home loan application process for an HUF? The steps you need to follow to apply for a loan for an HUF are as follows: 1. Verify HUF status and PAN: The HUF must be properly constituted and have its own PAN Card. Most lenders require proof that the HUF exists as a separate legal and tax entity. 2. Select a suitable lender: Prepare a list of banks and housing finance companies that offer HUF home loans , as the facility is not offered by all lenders. 3. Submit the home loan application: Apply for the loan with the Karta acting as the authorized representative and primary signatory of the HUF. 4. Submit the required documents: Check the lender’s specific list and submit clear, accurate copies. Generally, these include HUF documents, Karta’s KYC papers, income proof, bank statements, and property-related documents. 5. Complete income and credit verification: The lender evaluates the HUF’s income, cash flows, repayment capacity, and overall credit profile. 6. Property legal and technical assessment: The lender verifies the property’s legal ownership, title, and market value before approving the loan. 7. Receive the loan sanction: The lender issues a sanction letter mentioning the approved loan amount and terms if the application meets the lender’s requirements. 8. Complete formalities and get disbursal: Sign the final loan documents and fulfill any remaining conditions. The lender then disburses the loan amount according to the agreed process. What are the tax benefits of an HUF home loan? One of the key advantages of an HUF home loan is the potential tax benefit. Since an HUF is a separate tax entity, it can claim eligible home loan deductions in its own income tax return, independent of the claims made by individual family members. The HUF may claim deductions on principal repayment under Section 80C and on home loan interest under Section 24(b). The actual benefit depends on the applicable limits and the chosen tax regime. You must consult a qualified Chartered Accountant (CA) for personalized tax advice. What are the key considerations and challenges of an HUF home loan? You must keep the following points in mind before applying for an HUF loan for a home: Fewer lenders offer home loans to HUFs compared to individual borrowers. Consent may be required from relevant coparceners. The property’s ownership and title should be clear and legally valid. A change in the Karta due to succession can create additional administrative requirements. The property purchased through the loan should continue to remain an asset of the HUF. If you understand these factors, it can help avoid future complications. Conclusion A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) can be a practical way to access home loan financing to buy a property. The Karta applies on behalf of the HUF, and obtaining a home loan is easy with the right documentation, a stable income, and lender approval. The HUF can also enjoy separate tax benefits in its own income tax return. However, HUF home loans are not offered by all lenders. The eligibility requirements may also vary. Before applying, carefully review the lender’s policies and verify the latest terms, documentation requirements, and tax implications. Say Hello to Your New Home with Our Easy Home Loans! The Karta usually applies for the home loan on behalf of an HUF. It is the Karta’s responsibility to manage the dealings of the HUF. Thus, it is the Karta only who signs the loan documents. product. The premium paid is split into two parts. The first part is used to provide life insurance coverage, whereas the second part is invested across equity, debt, and hybrid funds. ULIPs can be categorized into various types based on the type of fund and the financial goal they are designed to address. However, they also entail certain charges and a mandatory 5-year lock-in period. Whether to invest in a ULIP depends on your financial goals, investment horizon, and risk appetite. A ULIP (Unit-Linked Insurance Plan) is a financial product that combines the benefits of life insurance protection and market-linked investment. When it comes to financial planning, life insurance and investment are often considered the two crucial pillars. Life insurance helps you ensure the financial security of your loved ones in your absence. Investments allow you to grow your wealth and support long-term goals, such as retirement, a child’s education, etc. A ULIP is a unique financial product that combines the benefits of both life insurance and investment. It allows you to work towards wealth creation while also providing financial protection for your family. This guide explains in depth what is ULIP plan , how it works, its key features, benefits, types, charges, and the latest taxation rules. There is also a comparison between ULIP and mutual funds to help you choose the right instrument. Keep reading. What is a ULIP? Full form and meaning The ULIP full form is Unit-Linked Insurance Plan. As mentioned earlier, it is a financial product that combines the benefits of both life insurance and investment. A common ULIP definition is that it is a long-term financial product designed to help individuals build wealth while also protecting their family’s financial future. The returns are market-linked, which means that there is a potential for significant capital appreciation over time. You also have the flexibility to invest as per your risk appetite and financial goals. ULIPs are offered as insurance-cum-investment products by life insurance providers in India. Read More – Endowment policy: Meaning, types, and benefits How does a ULIP work? As with any other insurance product , you must pay a premium to purchase a ULIP plan. This premium is then split into two parts. The first part is used to provide you with a life insurance cover, which remains valid until the policy term. The second part is invested across equity, debt, and hybrid mutual funds as per the ratio you choose. These funds are managed by professional fund managers. Once your premium is invested in your chosen funds, you are assigned units as per the prevailing Net Asset Value (NAV). The value of the fund moves with the market. You can choose and switch between funds during the policy term. In case something happens to you during the policy term, your nominee stands to receive the death benefits along with the accumulated fund value. What are the key features of a ULIP? Here are the key features of a ULIP plan that make it different from traditional insurance plans: Life cover and investment : With a ULIP plan, you get to enjoy the dual benefits of life insurance coverage and investment. Choice of funds : You can choose to allocate your investments between equity, debt, and hybrid funds based on your financial goals and risk tolerance. Free switches : Most ULIP providers in India allow a limited number of free switches between funds during the policy term. 5-year lock-in period : A ULIP plan typically comes with a mandatory 5-year lock-in period. Withdrawals are not permitted during this time. Partial withdrawals after lock-in : You can make partial withdrawals once the lock-in period is over. Investment allocation : A defined percentage of every premium goes towards investment after charges are deducted, and you can typically choose how this is split across your selected funds. Top-ups : Beyond your regular premium, most ULIPs let you make additional lump-sum investments, called top-ups, to increase your fund value when you have surplus funds available. Tax-saving instrument : Premiums qualify for deduction under Section 80C, making a ULIP one of the few products that combines insurance, market-linked growth, and tax planning in one policy. Multiple premium payment options : You can typically choose to pay premiums monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annually, depending on what suits your cash flow. Read More – Money back policy What are the different types of ULIPs? To fully understand the ULIP meaning, it’s important to know the types of ULIPs available. They can be broadly classified based on the type of investment fund and the financial goal they are designed to serve. The risk and return potential vary depending on the type of ULIP chosen. If you’re still working out the ULIP plan’s meaning before picking a type, it comes down to where your money is invested and which goal it’s tied to. Types of ULIPs based on fund type: 1. Equity ULIPs: These ULIPs invest primarily in equities or stocks of companies. 2. Debt ULIPs: These ULIPs mainly invest in fixed-income instruments. 3. Hybrid or balanced ULIPs: These ULIPs invest in a mix of equity and debt instruments. 4. Liquid Funds: These ULIPs invest in short-term, low-risk money market instruments, and are typically used as a temporary parking option when switching out of equity or debt funds during volatile markets. Types of ULIPs based on goals: 1. Wealth creation ULIP: These ULIPs help create wealth for long-term financial goals. 2. Child education ULIP: These ULIPs are designed for parents looking to create a corpus for their child’s higher education. 3. Retirement ULIP: These ULIPs help investors accumulate wealth for their retirement. What are the benefits of a ULIP? These are the core advantages of unit linked insurance plan structures that keep drawing investors in. ULIP plans have become a highly popular choice over traditional insurance or investment products. Here are some key advantages of unit-linked insurance plans: Dual benefit of protection and growth : ULIPs provide life insurance coverage while also giving you an opportunity to grow your wealth. Flexibility to switch funds : You can easily switch between equity, debt, and hybrid funds based on your financial goals and risk appetite. Potential tax benefits : Premiums paid towards a ULIP plan are eligible for tax deductions under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. Maturity benefits are also tax-free under Section 10 (10D). Goal-based investing : Different ULIP plans are designed to support different life goals. You can select a plan according to your specific financial goal. Transparency : You can transparently view your returns through fluctuations in the NAV. What are the ULIP charges you should know? It is important to understand the charges involved before investing in a ULIP plan. These charges can impact your overall returns. Here are the common ULIP charges: Premium allocation charge : Deducted from the premium before it is invested in the chosen funds. Fund management charge: Charged as a percentage of the investment amount. This charge is capped at 1.35% per annum. Mortality charge: This is the cost of providing the actual life insurance cover. It depends on your age, health condition, and sum assured. Policy administration charge : Levied as a small percentage for maintaining and servicing the policy. Surrender charge: Levied when you choose to terminate or stop your policy before the mandatory 5-year lock-in period. ULIP taxation in India (2026 update) ULIPs offer multiple tax benefits under various sections of the Income Tax Act. Premiums paid towards a ULIP policy are eligible for tax deductions under section 80C, provided that the taxpayer has opted for the old tax regime. For ULIPs issued on or after 1 February 2021 with an aggregate annual premium up to Rs. 2.5 lakhs, maturity benefits are tax-free under section 10 (10D). If the aggregate annual premium exceeds Rs. 2.5 lakhs, maturity gains are taxed as per the capital gains taxation rules. Effective 1 April 2026, long-term capital gains (for units held for more than 12 months) exceeding Rs. 1.25 lakh in a financial year are taxed at 12.5%. Short-term capital gains are taxed at 20%. The amount received by the nominee upon the policyholder’s death continues to remain tax-free. It is advisable to consult a qualified tax advisor or financial planner before making investment decisions based on tax benefits. ULIP vs mutual funds Many investors who understand a ULIP plan in insurance often compare it with mutual funds . While both offer market-linked investment opportunities, they serve different purposes. A ULIP plan combines insurance and investment in a single product, whereas a mutual fund is purely an investment vehicle. The table below depicts a comparison between ULIPs and mutual funds: Basis ULIP Mutual Funds Purpose An insurance-cum-investment product. A pure investment product. Life insurance cover Included Not included Lock-in period Mandatory 5-year lock-in Depends on the scheme. Usually, there is no lock-in period. Taxation Both premiums and maturity benefits are tax-free. Returns are taxable, depending on the type of mutual fund. Charges Higher due to the insurance component. Very nominal. Costs Includes insurance charges, fund management, and administration fees on top of investment. Only fund management and expense ratio; generally lower overall cost. Fund Switching A limited number of free switches between funds are usually allowed each year. Switching between schemes may attract exit load or capital gains tax, depending on the fund and holding period. Read More – Thumb rule of investment: Key SIP rules Who should invest in a ULIP? A unit-linked insurance plan may be suitable for investors with long-term financial goals and who are comfortable staying invested for several years. It can work well for those who want life insurance protection and market-linked investments through a single product. The mandatory lock-in period also encourages disciplined investing and long-term wealth creation. However, investors looking for pure insurance protection and low-cost investment options may find a combination of a term insurance plan and mutual funds more suitable. More specifically, a ULIP tends to suit a few kinds of investors particularly well. Long-Term Planners: Investors who are comfortable staying invested for 10-15 years or more, since ULIPs are built for long horizons rather than short-term gains. Goal-Oriented Savers: Those saving towards a specific milestone, such as a child’s education or retirement, and want a plan structured around that goal. Tax-Conscious Earners: Investors under the old tax regime who want to combine Section 80C deductions with market-linked growth in a single product. Balanced Risk Takers: Those who want equity-linked growth potential but also value the fund-switching flexibility to move towards debt when markets turn volatile. Beginners Seeking Structure: New investors who prefer the discipline of a mandatory lock-in and regular premiums over managing separate insurance and investment products themselves. Conclusion A ULIP plan can be a useful option for investors seeking insurance protection and wealth creation in a single product. However, it is important to understand the lock-in period, the charges involved, the fund options, and the tax rules before investing. Comparing ULIPs with alternatives such as mutual funds and term insurance can help. Choose a product that aligns with your financial goals, investment horizon, and risk appetite. The full form of ULIP is Unit-Linked Insurance Plan. As the name suggests, it combines the benefits of market-linked investment with life insurance coverage. A portion of the premium paid is used to provide life insurance, while the remaining amount is invested in mutual funds of your choice. What is a ULIP plan in simple words? A ULIP plan is a financial product that helps you invest for your long-term financial goals while also providing financial security to your loved ones. When you invest in a ULIP, a part of the premium goes towards life insurance, while the rest is invested in equity, debt, and hybrid funds as per the chosen ratio. Is ULIP a good investment? A ULIP can be suitable for investors who have long-term financial goals and want insurance and investment in one product. It may work well for goals such as retirement or wealth creation. However, whether it is a good investment depends on your risk appetite, goals, and investment horizon. Are ULIP returns tax-free in 2026? The tax treatment depends on the premium amount and policy conditions. For ULIPs issued on or after 1 February 2021 with an aggregate annual premium up to Rs. 2.5 lakhs, maturity benefits are tax-free under section 10 (10D). If the aggregate annual premium exceeds Rs. 2.5 lakhs, maturity gains are taxed as per the capital gains taxation rules. What is the lock-in period for a ULIP? A ULIP comes with a mandatory lock-in period of five years. During this period, withdrawals are generally not allowed. After the lock-in period ends, investors can usually make partial withdrawals, subject to the policy's terms and conditions. What is the difference between a ULIP and a mutual fund? A ULIP combines life insurance and investment in a single product. A mutual fund is purely an investment product and does not provide insurance coverage. ULIPs have a five-year lock-in period, while many mutual funds offer greater liquidity and generally involve lower overall costs. The tax rules for both products also differ. What are the main charges in a ULIP? Common ULIP charges include the premium allocation charge, fund management charge, mortality charge, policy administration charge, and surrender or discontinuance charges. These costs can affect your overall returns, which is why it is important to review the charge structure before investing.
