with extremely low credit scores may need to avail of urgent CIBIL defaulter loans. To obtain an urgent loan for CIBIL defaulters, individuals must take steps such as applying with a co-signer, using collateral to secure the loan, improving their credit scores , and exploring alternative options. While loans for individuals with low credit scores can sometimes seem challenging to obtain, it is still possible to secure them. In this article, we will go over what CIBIL is, who CIBIL defaulters are, and what challenges they may face. We also cover the steps one must take to avail of personal loans for CIBIL defaulters. So if you are looking for an instant loan , why not try Tata Capital ? We offer loans at competitive interest rates with minimal documentation. What are CIBIL defaulters? In some cases, individuals may not be able to repay loans they have availed of. In such a situation, they may be labelled as CIBIL (The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited) defaulters. However, it is essential to note that there is no standardized definition for CIBIL defaulters, and CIBIL does not maintain any lists or data specifically regarding defaulters. Instead, lenders usually review your credit/CIBIL score, to estimate your creditworthiness and approve your loan. Who is considered to be a credit defaulter? When you are unable to meet your loan repayment commitments, there is a risk of being labelled a credit defaulter. Credit rating agencies don’t keep an official list of defaulters. Instead, they assess your creditworthiness based on your credit score , which influences your loan approvals. A credit report reflects your financial discipline, which lenders use to measure your creditworthiness. Late payments can seriously hurt your credit score. Defaulting on loans lands you on the credit defaulter list, indicating a low credit score. As a result, you could face ongoing challenges such as lenders declining future credit applications which can restrict your financial freedom over an extended period. Available loan types for CIBIL defaulters in India Finding a loan for defaulters in India can be challenging, but there are options available: Gold loan: A gold loan can be a viable option when seeking a loan for CIBIL defaulters. You can pledge gold jewelry, coins, or bars as collateral. Lenders usually do not check your CIBIL score, which makes this a quick option. Loans with a co-applicant: Some lenders provide a loan for CIBIL defaulters if you have a trustworthy co-applicant. This increases your chances of approval despite a poor credit history. Loan Against Property (LAP): Residential or commercial property can be used as collateral to get a loan for CIBIL defaulters. LAP offers higher loan amounts and longer repayment tenures. Loan against securities: Investments in mutual funds, stocks, insurance policies, or other similar assets can be leveraged to obtain a loan for CIBIL defaulters. How to secure an urgent loan with low or bad CIBIL score in India? Lenders might be apprehensive about offering urgent loans to CIBIL defaulters, so you must consider a few options to increase your chances of getting a loan. These options include: Apply with a co-signer: When you apply with a co-signer or guarantor with a high credit score, your chances of getting loan approval increases. It’s because they have a higher credit score which minimizes the risk of your application being rejected. Borrow at higher rates of interest: As you have a poor CIBIL score, lenders will not entertain your loan application easily. However, taking a loan at higher interest rates may offset the risk. Use collateral to apply for loans: If you have any physical asset to use as collateral, lenders can be more open to offering loans. However, keep in mind that they may seize the property in case of non-repayment of loan. Try to improve your credit score: If you have existing debt, focus on making timely repayments. Consistent on-time payments can boost your credit score, improving your chances of securing loan approvals in the future. Explore other alternative options: If other options haven’t worked out well, consider taking a more traditional route such as peer-to-peer lending, where you can borrow money from acquaintances or friends through informal agreements Step-by-step guide to applying for instant loan for CIBIL defaulters online Here’s a step-by-step process of how to get urgent loans for CIBIL defaulters online. Identify Lenders for CIBIL Defaulters: Due to low credit scores, certain lenders may not offer urgent loans to CIBIL defaulters. But that doesn’t mean that every lender is against providing loans to them. That’s why you must research properly to see which lenders offer loans and which don’t. Eligibility Criteria: To apply for a personal loan with a low credit score, you’ll have to meet the following eligibility criteria- The applicant must be between 21 and 58 years of age The applicant must have a minimum monthly income of Rs. 15,000 The applicant must have a minimum of one year of work experience. Additionally, don’t forget to check for the interest rate, tenure, and other loan terms offered by the lender. Once you know the lenders offering loans for low credit scores, the next step is to see what criteria they have set. But be aware that since you are applying as a CIBIL defaulter, there may also be other criteria, so look carefully. Also, check their personal loan interest rates , tenures, and other important terms and conditions you find necessary. Required Documents: The lender will require you to submit a set of required documents. Make sure to collect the following documents and keep them updated- ID proof (Aadhaar card/ Passport/ Driving license/ Voter ID) Address proof (Aadhaar card/ Passport/ Voter ID/ Driving license) A copy of your salary slips for the last two months A copy of your bank statement for the last two months A certificate stating one year of continuous employment Apply Online: Once you have all the required documents, go to the lender’s website and fill out the application form. You will be required to fill in details like your name, address, loan needs, etc. Wait for Verification: Upon filling out the application, upload your documents. After this, the lender will verify your application and submitted documents. Once they are satisfied, they will approve your loan application. If not, you’ll have a list of reasons to check for resubmission. Alternatives to a personal loan for a low CIBIL score Here are some alternatives to a personal loan for CIBIL defaulters: Loan against Fixed Deposits (FDs): You can get a low credit score loan by pledging your FD. Your deposit will continue to earn interest, while the loan will offer you funds upfront. Loan against insurance policies: Certain l ife insurance policies allow you to borrow against them. This is a practical alternative to a personal loan for CIBIL defaulters. Gold loan: Gold jewelry, coins, or bars can be pledged for a quick, low credit score loan. The loan amount depends on gold purity and weight. Loan against shares: Banks may offer a personal loan for CIBIL defaulters by accepting listed shares as collateral, based on their market value. Loan against a Public Provident Fund (PPF): A PPF loan lets you raise money without breaking your PPF account. This is another useful low credit score loan option. Challenges for securing a loan for CIBIL defaulters While it is not impossible for individuals to secure loans for low credit scores, those with a poor credit history often encounter multiple hurdles when applying for loans. Here are some common problems faced by CIBIL defaulters: Higher rates of interest: A poor credit score often leads to higher interest rates. Lenders consider those who have defaulted in past repayments as risky borrowers. As a safeguard against risk, financial institutions typically charge extra interest to offset the possibility of default. This makes borrowing money more expensive and difficult for defaulters. Strict loan terms: In addition to increased interest rates, lending to CIBIL defaulters typically comes with more stringent loan conditions. These include shorter loan tenure, smaller principal amount, and limitations regarding its use. These terms are designed to minimize the lender’s risk but often restrict the flexibility and affordability of credit options for borrowers. Fewer lender options: Limited borrowing options can be discouraging for individuals struggling with low credit scores. Most lenders avoid offering loans to clients with low or poor credit ratings. As a result, they may have to rely on alternative sources that come with higher costs and stricter loan terms, further complicating their finances. Security requirement: In some cases, offering significant collateral can convince financial institutions to approve a loan for CIBIL defaulters. Collateral can include assets like houses, cars, or other valuables, which the lender can seize if you default on repayment. Such conditions exclude many defaulters from obtaining loans, especially those without significant assets to pledge. Effects on future financial opportunities: For individuals flagged as CIBIL defaulters, obtaining a loan doesn’t mean their challenges are over. It may also impact your ability to secure future loans, obtain credit cards, and access favorable terms on other financial products. CIBIL score ranges and loan approval chances CIBIL score Creditworthiness Probability of approval <600 Requires attention Low 600-649 Uncertain Challenging 650-699 Satisfactory Possible 700-749 Good High 750-900 Excellent Very high How to increase CIBIL score fast for urgent loan eligibility? Getting a loan can be challenging if you have a low CIBIL score. However, there are few steps you can take to improve your credit score and boost your chances of loan approval. These include: Monitor your credit report frequently: Start by requesting and reviewing your credit report regularly. It gives you crucial insights into the factors that influence your score and helps you spot and fix any mistakes which can boost your rating quickly. Clear your outstanding dues: These may include outstanding credit card bills or existing loans. Make timely payments by setting regular reminders. If you are a defaulter, consolidating your debts can make repayments more manageable. Maintain a low credit utilization: Aim to keep your credit utilization below 30% of your total limit. Using less of your available credit makes you look financially stable and responsible in the eyes of lenders. Avoid acquiring multiple loans: When you apply for a loan, lenders perform a hard inquiry on your credit report, which can temporarily lower your credit score. Do thorough research before applying for new loans to check your eligibility for them. Diversify your credit: Having a diversified mix of loans, such as home loans , and unsecured loans, such as personal loans, can help you boost your credit score. A mixture of loans shows the lenders your ability to responsibly manage different types of credit, thereby making you a potentially low-risk borrower. Boost your credit history: Maintaining a long and consistent credit history reflects positively on your credit score. If you have older credit accounts that are duly paid off, do not close them as they reflect your long-term track record of handling credit responsibly. Seek professional debt counselling: If you’re struggling to handle your debts, consider getting help from a professional debt counsellor. They offer practical plans and strategies to help you manage your debts and gradually improve your credit score . Key factors affecting your CIBIL score in India Applying for your CIBIL score can be an anxiety-inducing process- you don’t know if you will receive a high or low score. If you receive a high score, you can rejoice since your chances of getting approval for loans are high. But what if you receive a low score? The first step is to understand the factors that may have contributed to this low score to begin with: Your application: If you have sent multiple loan applications to lending institutions, it could negatively impact your CIBIL score. A high number of unsecured loans: If you have borrowed multiple loans against your name, it could be another factor that lowers your CIBIL score. Delaying and defaulting payments: If you have defaulted on payments for your loan EMIs or credit cards, this will negatively impact your credit score. Someone else defaulting on payments: In case you have agreed to be a guarantor for someone else, it could affect your credit score. If they default on their loan EMI payments, it will negatively impact your credit score. Tips for urgent loan approval when you have a bad credit report Here are some tips on how to get a personal loan for CIBIL defaulters quickly: Apply for a smaller amount: Requesting a lower amount reduces risk for lenders and improves approval odds for a personal loan for a CIBIL defaulter. Use mobile apps or NBFC platforms: Digital lenders and NBFCs may be more flexible, which makes them a good option for an urgent loan for CIBIL defaulters. Apply with a co-applicant: A co-applicant with a good credit score can boost eligibility for a loan for CIBIL defaulters. Offer collateral: Pledging gold, stocks, FDs, or property strengthens your case for a personal loan for a CIBIL defaulter. Show regular income proof: Salary slips or business income help lenders trust your repayment ability and speed up approval. Risks and precautions for CIBIL defaulters seeking a loan While applying for an offline or online loan for CIBIL defaulters, it is important to proceed carefully. A major risk you can run is irregular income. So, try to maintain and show steady earnings to the lender to improve your chances of approval for a low credit score loan. Make sure to keep your credit utilization below 30% of your total limit. This shows financial discipline and makes you appear more reliable to lenders offering an online loan for CIBIL defaulters. It is also important to avoid applying for multiple loans at once. Each application triggers a hard inquiry, which can temporarily reduce your credit score and affect eligibility for an instant loan for CIBIL defaulters. Also, try to clear existing debts, including credit card dues, before taking a low credit score loan, as this can strengthen your credit profile. How NBFCs and FinTechs evaluate loans for defaulters NBFCs and FinTech lenders assess credit history and credit scores when reviewing a loan for CIBIL defaulters. They evaluate the borrower’s financial status, existing debts, and past repayment behavior. Lenders also verify income proof, bank statements, financial records, and identity documents. In some cases, personal guarantees may be required to reduce risk. For those seeking an urgent loan for a low CIBIL score, showing stable income and a clear repayment capacity can improve approval chances, even with a weak credit profile. Impact of settled loans and written-off accounts If an account shows the status, settled, it means you negotiated with the lender to close the dues for less than the full amount. Lenders consider this risky, which can affect your chances of getting a loan as a CIBIL defaulter. A written-off status appears when dues remain unpaid for around 180 days or more, and the lender marks the amount as uncollectible. This severely damages your credit profile and makes approval for an instant loan for CIBIL defaulters much harder. Conclusion CIBIL scores are a crucial aspect of modern finance. Lenders depend on this number to ascertain an applicant’s creditworthiness. While urgent loans for CIBIL defaulters are still attainable, boosting your score is always a good idea. Basic steps to increase your CIBIL scores, such as paying your loans on time and avoiding taking more than you need, can help immensely. This will also help you get an instant loan online without much trouble. So if you are looking for an instant loan, why not try Tata Capital ? We offer loans at competitive interest rates with minimal documentation. Furthermore, within four simple steps, you will get the necessary funds in no time. Can I get a loan with a 500 credit score? While a credit score of 500 is extremely low, making it challenging to get approved, it may still be possible to obtain a loan. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Most Indian lenders require borrowers to have a minimum CIBIL score for a home loan. It varies by lender, but a credit score of 700 to 750 is generally ideal to get the best interest rates and faster approval. A CIBIL score below 650 is considered high risk and often leads to rejection. Hence, it is advised that you apply with a co-applicant or strong income proof if you want a home loan for a low CIBIL score. Some banks do offer a home loan for a CIBIL score of 550, but it carries higher interest rates and may require additional verification. Banks approve your loan faster if you meet their requirement of the minimum CIBIL score for a home loan. You can also get more favorable loan terms. Are you planning on taking a home loan ? Well, then you should know that you need a good CIBIL score for home loan eligibility. A home loan is an excellent way to finance your dream home. However, home loans are normally hefty amounts and last for years, sometimes even decades. Therefore, when lenders consider loan applications, they need to be extra cautious. To ensure repayment, they determine your capacity using several parameters. CIBIL score is one such, in fact, the primary determiner of your home loan eligibility . So, what is a good CIBIL score for a home loan? In this article, we will outline what a CIBIL score means, the minimum CIBIL score for a home loan, and how you can increase your CIBIL score. Let’s dive in! What is a CIBIL score? Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited (CIBIL) is one of the four credit bureaus authorized by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to keep a credit record of every Indian citizen. You can check your CIBIL or credit score for a home loan once a year for free and multiple times a year at a nominal fee. So, how can you check your CIBIL or credit score for a home loan? It is a simple process. To get your CIBIL score, you need to visit the CIBIL website, fill in the form, make the payment (if you are subscribing to multiple credit scores a year), and your score will be sent to your registered email ID within 24 hours. A CIBIL score is a three-digit number between 300 and 900. CIBIL determines your score based on your credit history and other financial information provided by you while filling out the form. Let us now look at what is the minimum CIBIL score for a home loan in India. What is the minimum CIBIL score required for a home loan? The minimum CIBIL score required for home loans differs from lender to lender. Usually: A CIBIL score of 750 or higher is considered to be excellent A score between 650 and 750 is considered to be a good CIBIL score for a home loan The 550 – 650 bracket is considered to be average A score below 550 is considered bad A score of 650 and above gives you a good chance of getting your loan application approved. Typically, this is considered the minimum CIBIL score for a home loan. However, having a lower CIBIL score does not nullify your chances. It just means you will have less room to negotiate, the lender will have to look at more financial documents, and you might have to do more in terms of convincing them that you will be able to repay the loan, such as including a creditworthy guarantor. What is a good CIBIL score for a home loan? A CIBIL score of 750 or higher is generally ideal for a home loan. It indicates strong credit health, increasing your chances for approval and better loan terms. What are the factors that influence your CIBIL score for a home loan? Your credit score for a home loan is influenced by several factors, including: Repayment history: Paying your EMIs and credit card dues on time impacts your CIBIL score positively, while delays or defaults reduce it. Credit utilization: Using a high percentage of your available credit limit can lower your score. On the other hand, lower utilization can show that you are financially more disciplined, thereby increasing your score. Credit mix: A healthy balance of secured and unsecured loans improves your score and reflects responsible credit behavior. Credit inquiries: If you make frequent loan or credit card applications, it can negatively affect your CIBIL score. How to check the credit score offered by CIBIL? Follow the steps below to check your CIBIL score: Visit CIBIL’s official website. Choose the option to check your credit score. Fill in personal details (DOB, ID, etc.). Complete identity verification steps. View your credit score on the dashboard after submission. What are the benefits of a high CIBIL score for home loan approval? A high CIBIL score for home loan applications has several benefits, including: Substantially lower interest rates (Risk-based pricing): A high CIBIL score shows that you are a low-risk borrower. Lenders may offer lower interest rates, helping you save on total interest costs. Faster approval & “express” sanction: A strong credit history can make lenders more confident about your repayment ability. This may result in quicker loan processing and approval. Higher loan amount & better LTV ratio: A high CIBIL score may improve your chances of getting a higher loan amount. Some lenders may also offer more favorable Loan-to-Value (LTV) terms. Waiver or discounts on processing & legal charges: Some lenders may offer reduced or waived processing fees and other charges to borrowers with strong credit profiles. Extended tenure options (up to 30 years): A good credit score may help you qualify for longer repayment tenures, which can make your monthly EMIs more manageable. Greater leverage to negotiate between lenders: A high score strengthens your bargaining position. You may be able to compare offers and negotiate better interest rates, fees, or loan terms. What are the common mistakes that reduce your CIBIL score? Your CIBIL score reflects how responsibly you manage credit. A few common mistakes can lower your score and make future loans or credit cards harder to get. These include: Missing EMI or credit card payments: Late or missed payments can negatively affect your repayment history. Using too much available credit: A high credit utilization ratio may signal financial stress. Applying for multiple loans: If you make several loan applications within a short period, it can lead to multiple hard inquiries. Closing old credit accounts: This may reduce your overall credit history length. Ignoring errors in your credit report: If you don’t report incorrect information in your credit report, it can affect your score. Make sure you promptly get it corrected. You must check your CIBIL report regularly and make timely payments to maintain a healthy credit profile. How to improve a low CIBIL score for home loan approval? What if you do not meet the criteria of the credit score required for home loans? Well, the good news is that you can increase it over time. Your CIBIL score can be low for many reasons. Here are some common ones: Delay in the repayment of your existing loans Using your credit card to its credit limit Frequently exceeding your credit limit Late or missed payment of credit card bills Having a high debt-to-income ratio . This means that you have more debt obligations than your net monthly income. The different ways in which you can improve your CIBIL score are: Clear past dues: Always pay any pending EMIs, credit card bills, or other dues as soon as possible. If you make payments on time, it shows responsible credit behavior. Limit credit use: Do not use a large part of your available credit limit. A low credit utilization can help maintain a healthy CIBIL score. Fix mistakes in the report: Check your CIBIL report regularly for incorrect details, such as wrongly reported late payments or closed accounts. If there are errors, raise a dispute immediately. Avoid new applications: Avoid applying for several loans or credit cards at the same time. Many credit inquiries in a short timeframe can affect your credit profile negatively. Keep old accounts open: Older credit accounts contribute to your credit history. If they have no ongoing issues, keep them open to indicate that you have a stable credit profile. Conclusion A low CIBIL score increases the chances of your loan application being rejected. If rejected, you should avoid applying repeatedly since that could further hurt your score. Instead, you should work towards improving your CIBIL score by paying your existing EMI dues promptly, keeping credit usage to a minimum, and decreasing other debts. Does my CIBIL score affect my home loan eligibility? Yes, your CIBIL score directly impacts eligibility. A higher score shows responsible credit usage, which improves the chances of approval and could provide access to competitive loan terms. How often should I check my CIBIL score when applying for a home loan? Checking your CIBIL score monthly during the application process helps monitor any changes and ensures it remains favourable for loan approval. Can I get a home loan with a CIBIL score of 550? While it is possible to get a home loan with a low CIBIL score, you may face higher interest rates and stricter conditions. Focus on improving your credit by settling debts and making payments promptly to increase your chances. How much CIBIL score is required for a home loan? Most lenders look for a minimum score of 750 for home loan applications. A higher score typically results in easier approval and access to better interest rates. What CIBIL score is required for a home loan? Most lenders look for a minimum score of 750 for home loan applications. A higher score typically results in easier approval and access to better interest rates. Does a high CIBIL score guarantee home loan approval? No, a high CIBIL score does not guarantee home loan approval. Lenders also assess your income stability, employment history, age, existing liabilities, and repayment capacity. The property’s legal and technical aspects are also considered. What happens if my CIBIL score is below the minimum required? If your CIBIL score is below the minimum required, lenders may reject your loan application. They may also offer the loan at a higher interest rate. In some cases, you may receive a lower loan amount or be asked to add a co-applicant. Can multiple loan applications affect my CIBIL score? Yes, your CIBIL score is negatively affected by multiple loan applications. Each application leads to a hard inquiry. Frequent inquiries indicate your credit hunger, making lenders view you as a higher-risk borrower. Is there a difference between a CIBIL score and a credit score? Yes. A CIBIL score is a type of credit score provided by TransUnion CIBIL in India. A credit score, on the other hand, is a general term that may also include scores from other bureaus like Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark . Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A home is more than just a roof on the head. It’s a place you live your best memories in and a habitat you look up to every day to unwind after a tiring day at work. And this is what makes owning a home a dream for many. If you have decided to turn this dream into a reality, note that your housing finance needs will differ depending on what part of the country you are planning to buy your dream home in. With expensive real estate in metros and megacities, high rises and building complexes are the only affordable option. However; in smaller cities and semi-urban areas, standalone houses and multi-storey bungalows are common. Even though you are buying a property in both instances, there is a difference in how financing works for an apartment/ home loan and a land/ plot loan . Here is a quick look at the differences between the two: Home Loan Plot Loan Purpose To purchase an under construction or built-up home. To purchase a plot of land for residential use. Categories Can be a loan for an apartment, bungalow or any residential unit. Exclusively for a piece of land. Loan to value ratio Housing loans range from 70% – 95% of the property value. Loans capped at 70% of the land value. Fixed income eligibility Usually between 40% to 55% of the your (borrower’s) income. Does not go beyond 30% to 40% of the your (borrower’s) income. Interest rate Home loan interest rates start from 8.25% onward. Plot loan interest rates start from 8.95% onward. Loan tenure Can go up to 30 years. Capped at 15 years, except loans from some NBFCs available for 20 years. Risk assessment of loan Medium High Tax benefit Tax benefits available on both repayment of principal and interest. Tax benefit available only on loan for construction. Availability of tax benefit Every financial year until the loan is repaid. Only after the entire construction is complete. Plot loans are considered to be riskier than standard home loan; therefore, the loan value tends to be marginally lower and interest a little higher. If you want to assess your budget accurately, you can use an EMI calculator for home loan to see which property fits your pocket better. Whatever your investment needs are, Tata Capital has a loan for you. Whether you are looking to buy an apartment, plot of land, extend your home, get construction done or transfer the property, Tata Capital offers easy to secure loans at attractive interest rates. The scale-up EMI option allows you to pay more as your income grows. A host of tools and home loan EMI calculator make it easy and transparent for you to plan for the future. Although there are certain differences between the two, the procedure for application, required documents, criteria for plot loan and home loan eligibility are the same. Understand your eligibility better with the home loan calculator and make your dream home a reality. How to Choose Between a Plot Loan and Home Loan Choosing between a plot loan and a home loan depends primarily on your immediate housing goal. While both help you invest in property, they serve very different purposes and come with distinct financial implications. Here’s what you should keep in mind before deciding: 1. Purpose of purchase: A plot loan is suitable if you want to buy land for future construction or long-term holding. A home loan works better if you want a ready home or plan to start construction immediately. 2. Loan tenure and affordability: Plot loans usually come with shorter tenures and higher EMIs, while home loans offer longer repayment periods , making monthly outgo more manageable. 3. Loan amount eligibility: You generally receive a lower loan amount for land compared to a built property due to higher risk perception. 4. Tax benefits: Home loans offer immediate tax deductions, while plot loans provide tax benefits only after construction is completed. 5. Location restrictions: Plot loans are typically approved only for residential plots within municipal or development authority limits. Plot Loan vs Home Loan: Eligibility Comparison While both plot loans and home loans assess your income, age, and credit profile, lenders apply stricter norms to plot loans. This is mainly because undeveloped land carries higher risk compared to a completed residential property. However, property-related documentation differs significantly because lenders assess risk differently for land and built properties. Documents required for plot loan To approve a plot loan, lenders verify that the land is legally eligible for residential construction. You are typically required to submit: – Sale deed or title deed showing clear ownership – Non-encumbrance certificate confirming no legal dues or disputes – Approved layout or zoning plan from the local authority – Proof that the plot falls within municipal or development authority limits – Non-agricultural (NA) conversion certificate, where applicable Documents required for home loan For a home loan, lenders assess the status and legality of the residential structure. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Purchasing your dream home is a huge financial investment. If you are funding the expenses with a loan, you can consider taking a joint home loan for couples to improve your repayment capacity. Let us look at the pros and cons of joint home loan options. What is a joint home loan? A joint home loan for married couples is a housing loan taken jointly by a husband and wife to purchase or construct a residential property. Both spouses share the responsibility of repaying the loan, and the lender assesses their combined income while determining eligibility. This arrangement can help couples qualify for a higher loan amount, access competitive interest rates, and claim tax benefits individually, subject to ownership share and applicable tax laws. In simple terms, this answers what is joint home loan financing most couples ask about: two people, usually spouses, borrowing together and sharing both the repayment and the ownership. Some also call this a home loan joint account, since the EMI is typically debited from a shared or linked bank account. Whether a joint home loan is a husband-wife pairing or another family combination, the same core principle applies. Combined income, shared liability. Also Read – Home Loan Insurance Benefits for New Home Buyers Benefits of Joint Home Loan for Married Couples Taking a joint home loan with wife or husband brings together two incomes and two credit profiles, and that combination unlocks several advantages of joint home loan borrowing that a single applicant doesn’t get. 1. Rebate on interest rates and easy repayment Most lenders offer lowered interest rates for women co-borrowers. Besides, in a joint loan, you can easily share the repayment burden with your co-applicant. So, your EMI obligations weigh less on your individual incomes. But that’s not all! With two people repaying the loan, you can pay higher EMIs and close the loan over a shorter tenure. 2. Higher loan amount Taking a joint loan also means fulfilling home loan eligibility terms for a bulkier loan amount. How? In a joint loan application, you and your spouse pool your incomes together, increasing your EMI affordability and making you eligible for an extended tenure and higher budget. With a higher loan amount, you can buy a house aligning with your housing desires. 3. Tax benefits The best thing about a home loan for married couple applicants is that you receive tax benefits for both the principal amount and the interest paid. Why, yes! Thanks to Sections 24 and Section 80C of the Income Tax Act. And since two borrowers share the loan, you get double benefits and double savings. But how much can you save? Section 80C enables you to claim a tax deduction of Rs. 1.5 lakhs in a financial year. Moreover, Section 24 allows you to claim an additional rebate of Rs. 2 lakhs on the interest paid. So, as a couple co-owning the property and co-borrowing the loan, you can claim Rs. 4 lakhs under Section 24 and Rs. 3 lakhs under section 80C. That’s a whopping total of Rs. 7 lakhs! Also Read – What is Home Loan Prepayment and How Does it Work? Shared Financial Responsibility & Credit Building Splitting the EMI between two incomes means neither partner carries the full weight alone, which keeps monthly finances more comfortable. It also works in your favour long term: consistent, on-time payments on a joint loan build credit history for both borrowers simultaneously, not just one. Compensating for Weak Credit Profiles If one partner has a limited credit history or a lower score, applying jointly lets the stronger applicant’s profile help carry the application. Lenders assess the combined picture, so a joint home loan husband-wife application can succeed where either partner alone might have struggled to qualify. Disadvantages of Joint Home Loan for Married Couples Now that you know the advantages of joint home loans, let us look at their disadvantages. While the benefits are real, a joint loan also ties both partners’ finances together for the entire tenure, and that comes with its own set of trade-offs worth understanding upfront. 1. Transfer of burden If one of the co-borrowers loses their job or faces a financial emergency, the repayment burden automatically falls upon the other partner. This can put an intense financial strain, which may lead to EMI defaults. Not repaying your EMIs on time will also hurt your credit score. 2. Death of spouse If unfortunately, one of the spouses passes away, the burden of clearing the housing loan again falls entirely on the surviving partner. 3. Separation If a couple decides to part ways in the future or a co-borrower opts out of repaying the loan, the responsibility to pay the loan rests with one applicant. Inability to repay can lead to legal repercussions for both borrowers. To avoid this, you can sign an agreement mentioning each partner’s share in loan liability beforehand. Also Read – What Happens When a Home Loan Borrower Passes Away 4. Credit Score Interdependence A joint loan links both credit histories to the same account. Every on-time EMI helps both scores, but every missed payment damages both equally, regardless of which partner was actually responsible for that month’s payment. One partner’s job loss or financial trouble becomes a shared credit problem, which is one of the less obvious disadvantages of co applicant in home loan arrangements. 5. Reduced Future Borrowing Capacity As long as the joint loan is active, both partners’ individual borrowing capacity for other needs, a car loan, a personal loan, or a second property, is reduced, since lenders factor in the existing joint liability when assessing either partner’s fresh application. 6. Inheritance and Property Ownership Disputes When ownership shares aren’t clearly documented at the outset, disputes can surface later among heirs, particularly if the couple has children from different marriages or if the property was meant to pass to specific family members. A clear co-ownership agreement, decided when the loan is taken, helps avoid this. Joint home loan eligibility criteria in India For married couples planning to buy a home together, understanding the eligibility norms is essential before applying. Joint home loan eligibility for married couples is primarily evaluated based on shared financial strength, ownership structure, and individual credit profiles, as outlined below: Spousal relationship : Both applicants must be legally married, with proof such as a marriage certificate if required by the lender Co-ownership of property : Husband and wife must be co-owners of the property being financed Combined income consideration : The lender considers the combined income of both spouses, one of the key benefits of joint home loanapplications, as it can increase the eligible loan amount Credit score requirement : Each spouse must meet the minimum credit score criteria set by the lender Age eligibility : Both applicants should fall within the lender’s specified age limits at loan maturity Employment stability : Salaried or self-employed spouses must show stable and verifiable income sources Joint repayment capacity : The loan is sanctioned based on the couple’s combined ability to repay EMIs comfortably How to apply for a joint home loan: Step-by-step guide Once you meet the joint home loan eligibility criteria, applying for a joint home loan is a fairly straightforward process. Following these steps can help married couples maximise the benefits of joint home loan applications and ensure a smooth approval journey: Check eligibility of both spouses Review age, income, employment stability, and credit scores of both applicants to confirm joint home loan eligibility. Decide ownership share Finalise the property ownership ratio between husband and wife, as this impacts loan approval and tax benefits. Compare lenders and loan options Evaluate interest rates, processing fees, tenure, and repayment flexibility to make the most of the benefits of joint home loan offerings. Submit the joint loan application Fill out a single application form with details of both spouses and submit it to the chosen lender. Provide required documents Submit KYC documents, income proof, property papers, and bank statements for both applicants. Property verification and credit assessment The lender conducts legal, technical, and credit checks to assess risk and confirm eligibility. Loan approval and disbursal Once approved, the loan is sanctioned and disbursed as per the agreed terms and construction or purchase stage. Joint Home Loan vs Single Home Loan The two routes suit different situations, so it helps to see how they compare directly. Loan amount : A joint home loan draws on combined income, so it typically supports a higher loan amount than a single applicant would qualify for on their own. Tax benefits : Both co-owners can claim deductions individually on a joint loan, effectively doubling the tax benefit compared to a single home loan. Liability : A single home loan puts full repayment responsibility on one person, while a joint loan splits it, but also means each borrower is liable for the other’s share if they default. Credit impact : A single loan affects only one credit profile, while a joint loan links both partners’ scores to the same repayment record for the home loan tenure you choose. Future borrowing : Taking a loan singly leaves the other partner’s borrowing capacity untouched, while a joint loan reduces both partners’ capacity to take on fresh debt until it’s repaid. Documentation : A single application needs one applicant’s paperwork, while a joint application needs KYC, income, and property documents for both, along with clarity on the difference between co-borrower, co-applicant and co-owner roles each person is taking on. Risks to Consider Before Taking a Joint Home Loan Beyond the specific disadvantages already covered, a few broader risks are worth weighing before you commit to a joint loan. Relationship risk : The loan outlasts the relationship’s ups and downs; a joint loan taken during a stable period can become a source of conflict if the relationship changes. Exit complexity : Removing a co-applicant in home loan arrangements, whether through separation, refinancing, or a buyout, usually requires the remaining borrower to be reassessed for eligibility on their own. Unequal contribution disputes : If one partner pays a larger share of the EMI without clear documentation, disagreements can arise later over ownership and entitlement. Joint liability exposure : Both borrowers remain liable for the full loan, not just their agreed share, if the lender is unable to recover dues from one party. Ongoing cooperation : A can two person take home loan for same property arrangement assumes continued cooperation between both parties; a breakdown in that cooperation can complicate everything from EMI payments to eventual resale. Conclusion Joint housing loans are pretty attractive, considering the host of benefits they offer, and they consistently rank among the more practical joint home loan India options for couples buying together. Joint home loan eligibility is assessed based on the combined income, age, credit score, and repayment capacity of all co-applicants. One of the key benefits of joint home loan applications is higher loan eligibility due to shared financial strength. Can joint home loans be taken by family members other than spouses? Yes, joint home loans can be taken with parents, children, or siblings, depending on lender policies. All co-applicants must meet joint home loan eligibility norms and be co-owners of the property. What are the risks of applying for a joint home loan? All borrowers are jointly liable for repayment. If one applicant defaults, the others must cover EMIs, which can affect credit scores despite the benefits of joint home loan arrangements. How to claim tax benefits on joint home loan interest and principal repayment? Each co-owner can claim tax benefits individually based on ownership and repayment share, subject to joint home loan eligibility and applicable income tax limits. Is it possible to convert an individual home loan into a joint home loan? Yes, some lenders allow conversion by adding a co-applicant, provided the revised joint home loan eligibility criteria are met and documentation is updated. What happens to the joint home loan if one borrower passes away? The surviving co-borrower becomes responsible for repayment. A loan protection insurance can help manage this risk while preserving the benefits of joint home loan commitments. Can home loan be taken jointly by family members other than spouses Yes, joint home loans can be taken with parents, children, or siblings, depending on lender policies. All co-applicants must meet joint home loan eligibility norms and be co-owners of the property. Does joint home loan reduce tax? Yes, significantly. Each co-owner who is also a co-borrower can individually claim up to Rs. 1.5 lakh under Section 80C on principal repayment and up to Rs. 2 lakh under Section 24 on interest, meaning a couple can together claim substantially more than a single applicant would. What happens if one borrower stops paying? The other co-borrower becomes responsible for the full EMI, since both parties are jointly and severally liable for the entire loan, not just their agreed share. Missed payments hurt both borrowers' credit scores equally, regardless of who stopped contributing. Is joint home loan good for married couples? For most married couples with two incomes, yes: it improves eligibility, unlocks a higher loan amount, and doubles the available tax benefit. The trade-off is shared liability, so it works best when both partners have stable income and a clear agreement on ownership share. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Affordable housing has been a key objective that the central government and various state governments have been promoting passionately. The affordable housing schemes that state governments run are designed to promote urban development and empower the general populace to own property. If you are a resident of Haryana and want to realize your dream of becoming a homeowner, then the HUDA housing scheme is definitely something you should explore. Here are all the things you should know about Haryana’s HUDA housing scheme: What is HUDA Housing Scheme? The Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA), also known as the Haryana Shahari Vikas Pradhikaran (HSVP), is the body behind the HUDA housing scheme. The scheme was launched in 1962 to give the members of different income categories an opportunity to own real estate at affordable prices. At the same time, the scheme was intended to promote infrastructure development in a structured manner and develop multiple urban estates across the state. Also, read: Home Loan in Gurgaon Based on upcoming and ongoing development, HUDA announces plot allotments every few years and opens up a window for registration. Interested applicants can register for the upcoming HUDA plot scheme on the official HUDA website by paying a nominal fee. Applicants are selected for plot allotment based on a lottery system with a fair and equitable chance of selection. Every plot is opened for an auction upon allotment, and the selected applicant must pay the EDM (Earnest Money Deposit) in the specified time. The applicants must then pay 25% of the total cost of the HUDA plot within 30 days. The remaining amount can be paid within six months or 180 days of allotment. If the applicant is unable to make the payments within the specified time frame, their right to the plot is revoked, and the same allotment is offered to another candidate. While both commercial and residential plots are allocated in the new sectors being developed by Haryana state, the scheme is most famous for its affordable housing options . Also, read – Affordable Housing in India: Know about the Measures Taken By RBI Why Invest in HUDA Upcoming Plot Scheme? Investing in an upcoming HUDA (now HSVP) plot scheme offers a combination of affordability, security, and long-term value. Since plots are allotted directly by a government authority, you benefit from regulated pricing, clear ownership, and planned development. These schemes are particularly attractive if you are a first-time buyer or someone looking to invest in a growing urban area. Key reasons to consider investing include: 1. Affordable entry pricing: Plot prices are generally lower than comparable private developments in the same city. 2. Government-backed assurance: Allotments are made by HSVP, reducing risks related to title disputes or unauthorised development. 3. High appreciation potential: Plots are usually located in emerging sectors that see steady value growth as infrastructure develops. 4. Freedom to build: Buying a plot allows you to design and construct your home based on your preferences and budget. 5. Strong resale demand: HSVP plots often command good resale value due to location and planned infrastructure. Key Benefits of HUDA Plot Schemes HUDA plot schemes are structured to support organised urban expansion while giving buyers access to essential infrastructure from the outset. Whether you plan to build a home or hold the plot as an investment , these schemes offer long-term utility. Some of the benefits you get to enjoy are: – Plots are located in well-laid-out sectors with proper roads, drainage, and civic planning. – Selection is done through a draw of lots or e-auction, ensuring fairness and equal opportunity. – Schemes offer a wide range of plot sizes, catering to different budgets and housing needs. – Water supply, electricity, sewerage, and road connectivity are planned as part of sector development. – Government-led development reduces uncertainty and supports gradual capital appreciation. HUDA Upcoming Plot Scheme 2025 The most recent announcements were made under the upcoming HUDA plot scheme of 2021-22. Under this, the HSVP announced the auction of 1000 industrial and residential plots. Plots can be of the following standard sizes: 2 Kanal (10890 sq. ft.) 1 Kanal (5445 sq. ft.) 10 Marla (2722.5 sq. ft.) 8 Marla (2178 sq. ft.) 6 Marla (1633 sq. ft.) Once the plot auction opens, bidders can select the location, plot and size and bid against the asking price. The auction is managed online, and all applicants have complete visibility of the proceedings. Areas Covered Under HUDA Residential Scheme Under the HUDA current residential scheme, different zones are identified for potential development. High potential zones include Gurgaon, Faridabad, and Panchkula. Medium potential zones include Panipat, Karnal, and Bahadurgarh. Rest of the urban estates across Haryana fall under low potential zones. Under the HUDA new housing scheme, plots will be auctioned in the following regions: Panchkula Ambala Sector 27 Palwal Sector 12 Panipat Nuh Sector 1, 2, 9 Pinjore Mahendragarh Sector 9 and 10 Bahadurgarh Sector 10 Sonipat Sector 5 and 19 Rewari Sector 5 and 7 Tarawadi Sector 1 Jind Sector 9 Jagadhri Sector 22 and 24 Agroha Sector 6 Dadari sector 9 Bhiwani Safidon Sector 7, 8, 9 Karnal sector 32, 33 Fatehabad Sector 9, 11, 56, 56A, 80 Eligibility for HUDA Affordable Housing Scheme The eligibility criteria for the HUDA housing scheme 2022 are very straightforward and have been designed to encourage the participation of first-time home buyers: – The applicant’s annual household income must be equal to or less than Rs. 3 lakhs. – Only Haryana state residents can register and apply for plot allotments. – Rural migrants with no prior property owned in urban developments can apply. – Urban residents who don’t own any residential or industrial plots can apply. – Haryana Government employees belonging to Group D can apply. – Certain organizations and members of co-operative societies can apply, provided they have proof of their nature of work. Applicants only need a copy of their Aadhar Card, a copy of their PAN card, and their birth certificate to prove their Haryana residency. In addition to this, income proof is also needed to apply for the HUDA housing scheme. Members of a co-operative society also need to provide a certified copy of the co-operative society’s resolution and copies of the bylaws when applying. Step-by-Step Guide to Applying for HUDA Upcoming Plot Scheme Applying for the HUDA (HSVP) upcoming plot scheme is a fully online process designed to be transparent and user-friendly. Before applying, you should confirm that you meet the eligibility conditions, especially residency and non-ownership requirements. Step 1: Visit the official HSVP website Go to the Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran portal and look for active or upcoming plot schemes. Step 2: Access the application link Click on the “Booking Open” or relevant scheme notification to begin registration. Step 3: Fill in the online application Enter accurate personal, residential, and income details as required. Step 4: Upload supporting documents Submit scanned copies of ID proof, income proof, and other mandatory documents in the prescribed format. Step 5: Pay the application fee or EMD Complete the payment online using the available payment options. Step 6: Submit and save acknowledgement Submit the form and keep the application number and receipt for future reference. Conclusion Finally, interested applicants can avail the benefits of the HUDA housing scheme 2022by directly registering at the www.hsvphry.org site. The entire process takes a few months – from the auction till the allotments are completed. This makes it possible for applicants to raise the required capital to pay for the plot. Prospective homeowners can use the 180-day period after the allotment to apply for cost-effective home loans. Tata Capital’s affordable home loans start from Rs. 5 lakhs and go up to Rs. 5 crores. With an easy repayment structure, long tenure of up to 30 years, and quick home loan processing, you can fulfil your dream of home ownership as soon as your HUDA plot allotment is done. The HUDA upcoming plot scheme is a government-initiated program by the Haryana Urban Development Authority (now HSVP) to offer residential and commercial plots in planned urban sectors across Haryana. It aims to make property ownership more attainable through transparent e-auctions or lottery-based allotments. Plots are released in identified sectors with civic infrastructure like roads, water, and electricity in place or planned for development. Successful applicants secure legal ownership under HSVP guidelines, often with structured payment timelines designed to support middle-income buyers. How can I apply for the HUDA upcoming plot scheme? You apply by visiting the official HSVP website, registering on the online portal, filling the application form with accurate details, uploading required documents, paying the fee/EMD, and submitting before the deadline. What are the eligibility criteria for the HUDA plot scheme? You must be an Indian citizen and generally a Haryana resident or eligible category. You and your family should not own a HUDA/HSVP-allotted plot in the same urban area. What documents are required for HUDA plot scheme application? You need valid ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID), PAN, Haryana residency proof, income proof, birth certificate, and sometimes an affidavit confirming no prior allotment. When will the HUDA upcoming plot scheme open for registration? Registration dates vary by scheme announcement. You should check the official HSVP website or leading newspaper notifications for opening and closing dates. Can NRIs apply for the HUDA plot scheme? Yes, NRIs and PIOs can usually apply, subject to FEMA compliance and payment through permitted NRE or NRO accounts. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Understanding Repo and Reverse Repo Rates Commercial banks borrow from the Reserve Bank of India at the Repo rate; RBI borrows from commercial banks at the Reverse repo rate. A repurchase agreement or repurchase option or repo, for short, refers to an arrangement where banks provide such securities as treasury bills or gold to borrow money from the central bank for overnight credit when the banks are short of liquidity. The money that commercial banks borrow from the central bank is meant to extend loans to their customers. Typically, customer deposits are also used to meet a bank’s liquidity needs. Banks borrow from the RBI at the prevailing repo rate when that is insufficient. Securing credit for banks is not the only function of the repurchase agreements or repos. Say, during inflation, the banking regulator or the RBI increases the repo rate. This signals to commercial banks that the RBI discourages borrowing for credit creation, which increases the supply of money or liquidity in the economy (a cause for further price rise). In the case of inflation indicators falling below a threshold, the reverse technique of reducing repo rates to encourage borrowing by commercial banks is followed. This would cause increased credit creation, which would increase the money supply and investment activity in the economy. The credit received by banks from RBI is only for an overnight duration. The securities deposited by the banks are released at a predetermined price on payback of the borrowings by the banks. Similar liquidity needs of the RBI and their fulfilment by the commercial banks are done at the prevailing reverse repo rate. The RBI uses the reverse repo rate as an alternative method to maintain the determined inflation levels. The RBI does this by absorbing the money supply from the market at the reverse repo rate. When the reverse repo rate increases, it signals to the banks that the banking regulator wants them to lend money to the RBI, thus sucking up the credit and the liquidity in the market. The opposite happens when the RBI reduces the reverse repo rate. It signals to commercial banks that credit creation and investment activities are encouraged. What is a Repo Rate Linked Home Loan? The concept behind repo-linked home loans is that banks and financial institutions pass on the changes in the repo rate to the borrowers. As the bank’s borrowing cost goes down, home loans become cheaper or vice versa. For instance, during the pandemic, the RBI had brought down the repo rate to 4%, and the banks, on their part, also lowered their lending rate. Banks are quicker in passing on repo rate-related hikes in home loan interest rates to borrowers than a drop in repo rates, which causes their lending rates to drop. Earlier, banks charged the PLR, Prime Lending Rate , but the RBI felt it wasn’t transparent enough and introduced the Base Rate concept. The Base Rate specifies a minimum rate below which the regulator forbids the banks from lending, even to their preferred clients. This provided the transparency the RBI wanted to see. It also ensured that any reduction in the repo rate would be passed on to the customers. Benefits of Repo Linked Home Loans Whether one is switching to a repo-linked rate or taking a new home loan, the following observations might be helpful: Movements in the repo rate get factored into the EMI quicker than any rate benchmarked against banks’ internal cost of funds. There is greater transparency in the rate-setting process EMIs can increase if the repo rate increases. Eventually, the lender or the bank settles on the final rate. The repo rate might be 4%, but the market rate for a home loan is 7%. It can fall or rise a few points based on the movement of the repo rate. RBI wants all banks to adopt the linking of new loans to the repo rate, which is an external benchmark for greater transparency. The State Bank of India (SBI) has already adopted the repo-linked lending rate (RLLR) for its home loan, and so have the Bank of Baroda (BoB) and Syndicate Bank. The others are considering the switch. RLLR will bring a change in the banks’ reluctance to reduce rates. According to some estimates, RLLR rates are 25-45 basis points cheaper than MCLR-linked rates (Margin Cost of Funds Lending Rate). Steps to Switch to a Repo Rate Linked Home Loan Switching to a repo-linked loan is about scrutinizing the costs involved: Switching to RLLR within a bank is a straightforward proposition: the conversion fee paid by a borrower upfront versus the savings on interest is to be watched. Switching to another institution typically happens when a borrower is unhappy with the existing institution’s rates, processing charges, valuation charges, or legal fees. More significantly, studying the spread that the other bank is charging over and above the RRLLR will be important in making the decision. Choose the bank which has the narrowest spread. That spread will mirror the RBI’s recommended rates more closely – the higher the loan’s value, the closer the fit. Comparison: Repo Linked Home Loan vs MCLR and Base Rate Loans A Repo Linked Home Loan is directly tied to the RBI’s repo rate, making it more transparent and responsive to policy changes. Under the repo-linked lending rate, any cut or hike in the repo rate is passed on to borrowers faster. Hence the repo rate impact on home loan EMIs is clearly visible. In contrast, MCLR and Base Rate loans depend on banks’ internal benchmarks, which adjust slowly and reduce the immediate benefit of rate cuts. Base Rate loans are the least transparent, while MCLR offers limited clarity. Because repo-linked loans adjust faster, they are generally more transparent and borrower-friendly than MCLR and Base Rate loans. Common Charges and Hidden Costs in Switching Repo Linked Loans Switching to repo-linked home loan often involves a one-time conversion fee charged by the lender. This fee may be a fixed amount or a small percentage of the outstanding loan balance. It is meant to cover administrative work and discourage frequent changes between different home loan interest rate benchmarks. Before approving the switch, lenders may reassess repo rate home loan eligibility. They often review the repayment history and remaining tenure, and not the income or credit score again. In some cases, the loan tenure or EMI structure may be adjusted to align with the new benchmark-linked rate. Despite these costs, switching can still be beneficial in the long run. Repo-linked loans reflect rate cuts faster, which can reduce overall interest costs. Borrowers should do a cost-benefit analysis to ensure that the savings from lower interest rates outweigh the conversion charges involved. Conclusion A word of caution. Let’s assume that the discussions have started with a bank, and the borrower feels that the initial rate looks attractively low. However, the factors that increase the interest rate, namely the loan-to-value ratio, the borrower’s credit score, and the number of other house properties the borrowers own (two or more), could quickly increase the rate. It is therefore suggested that the difference between the bank’s RLLR and the net interest rate should be watched carefully before deciding on the switch. A repo linked home loan is a housing loan where the interest rate is directly tied to the RBI’s repo rate. When the repo rate changes, the loan interest adjusts accordingly, usually at regular intervals, making rate movements more transparent for borrowers. How is repo rate linked home loan different from MCLR linked loan? A repo rate linked home loan responds faster to RBI rate changes, as it is externally benchmarked. MCLR-linked loans depend on internal benchmarks set by lenders, which may delay rate transmission, meaning borrowers feel the impact of rate cuts much later. What are the benefits of switching to a repo linked home loan? Switching to a repo linked home loan can lead to quicker interest rate reductions when the repo rate falls. It offers better transparency, potentially lower interest costs over time, and clearer understanding of how policy rate changes affect your loan. How does the repo rate affect my home loan EMI? When the RBI reduces the repo rate, the interest on a repo-linked loan usually falls, lowering your EMI or loan tenure. If the repo rate rises, EMIs may increase. The key advantage is faster and clearer transmission of rate changes. Are there any costs in switching to a repo linked home loan? Yes, lenders may charge a small conversion or administrative fee when you switch. There could also be minor documentation costs. These charges are usually one-time and often outweighed by long-term interest savings. Can I switch back if I’m unhappy with the new loan terms? Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund When the moratorium period ends, many borrowers struggle to restart EMI payments, making personal loan restructuring an important option to consider. Lenders in India offer flexible solutions to help customers regain financial stability without defaulting. Understanding how to restructure personal loan repayments through options such as extended tenure or revised EMIs can ease monthly obligations and protect credit scores. The restructuring of personal loan terms varies across lenders, but most require proof of financial stress and a formal request. Knowing these options is important to choose the most suitable plan and manage your finances more confidently after the moratorium. Understanding Loan Moratoriums: A Brief History Let’s go back to the 1st of March 2020. A time of financial hardship caused by the pandemic was beginning the world over. The Reserve Bank of India came to the rescue of Indian borrowers by declaring a loan moratorium or an EMI holiday. With proof of financial stress, a borrower could choose not to pay their loan EMIs during the announced period. This brought stability to credit flows, providing borrowers with much-needed financial relief. The loan moratorium period initially spanned three months, between March and May, 2020. On May 22, 2020, the moratorium window was extended to August. The program was implemented by banks and non-banking finance companies across the country, covering various retail loan types. Personal Loan fell into the moratorium category of standard term loans , along with Auto Loan , Education Loan , Home Loan , and Loan against Property . This EMI holiday came to an end on 31st August 2020. After the end of the moratorium window, regular repayment schedules were back in place. Interest was accrued over this period, and loans were adjusted with extended tenures and altered EMIs. Also, read – Loan Restructuring 2.0: All You Need to Know What is Personal Loan Restructuring? Personal loan restructuring is a relief measure that helps borrowers modify their existing loan terms when they face financial stress. Instead of defaulting, borrowers can request changes such as extending the tenure, reducing EMIs, or opting for temporary payment breaks. This process allows individuals to regain control over repayments without damaging their credit profile. The restructuring is typically offered to borrowers who can prove a drop in income or financial hardship. By adjusting the original loan agreement, lenders make repayment more manageable, giving borrowers time to stabilise their finances while keeping the loan active and compliant. Also, read – Key Points to Consider While Applying for Loan Restructuring Key Benefits of Personal Loan Restructuring Providing financial relief is the primary advantage of restructuring a personal loan. Let’s look at a few more benefits of loan restructuring: Personal loan restructuring makes repayment easier. This is implemented by extending the tenure of the loan or lowering the interest rate. By making the repayment manageable, the borrower can avoid loan defaults. Loan restructuring can thus protect the borrower’s credit score from long-term damage. Restructuring helps the borrower avoid legal actions and heavy penalties. When facing the financial pressure of job loss, reduced income, or a medical crisis, personal loan restructuring can provide quick financial relief. Loan restructuring is beneficial for the lender’s interests as well, letting them recover outstanding dues. Step-by-Step Process for Restructuring Your Personal Loan Understanding how to apply for loan restructuring can be helpful for achieving financial stability. Follow these steps to restructure a personal loan: Assess Financial Situation Begin with a review of your income, expenses, and debts. Contact Your Lender Reach out to your lender and provide an overview of your financial situation. Ask about their personal loan restructuring process . Submit a Restructuring Request Provide the lender with a restructuring request, including supporting documents such as salary slips, bank statements, or tax returns. Review and Finalise Clarify your options with the lender. They may provide interest rate reductions and tenure extensions. Determine which option fits your situation the best.Formalise the agreement, and follow the repayment plan diligently. Also, read – Understanding Debt Restructuring: Process & Benefits Loan Restructuring vs. Moratorium: Key Differences A loan moratorium is not only a time when EMIs do not have to be paid. It is also when unpaid EMIs accrue, to become payable later. It implies that the payable interest amount on the initial principle continues to pile up during the period of the EMI holiday. Then the EMIs become payable with the usual terms after the moratorium. In other words, it’s business as usual after the moratorium. However, it may not be business as usual for the borrower. He may still be facing a financial crunch. That’s where loan restructuring becomes useful as it allows some modification in terms of the personal loan, agreeable to both borrower and lender. It spells relief for the borrowers continuing to experience financial stress. After restructuring, EMIs continue to be paid as before with some allowances, such as a reduction of interest burden or an increase in the tenure of the loan. The whole purpose behind this is that the borrower, under no circumstances, should not struggle to make ends meet on account of paying the EMI. In a way, loan restructuring arrives before the borrower as the logical next step after a loan moratorium. It’s a win-win for the borrower as well as the lender. While the borrower ends up negotiating an EMI manageable for them to pay, restructuring loans allows banks to keep NPAs or non-performing assets in check. Loan Restructuring: Options and Alternatives When RBI introduced the loan moratorium it was specifically mentioned that for those opting for the EMI holiday, the interest amount on the principal would continue to accrue during the scheme’s life. The applicable type of payments that could be deferred were bullet payments, credit card payments, principal and interest payments, and EMIs. The RBI further stated that the deferred payments would neither be considered a criminal offence nor would they affect the borrower’s CIBIL ratings. But during non-payment, their interest charges would increase, thus, in some cases, necessitating the restructuring of their loans. Alternatives to Loan Restructuring The borrower may opt to pay the accumulated interest via a bulk payment. The borrower may want to increase the amount of EMI payments. That can be done by keeping the tenure constant and adding the unpaid EMIs to the outstanding loan amount The borrower may want to keep the EMI unchanged but increase the tenure by adding the due EMI to the due loan amount. How Personal Loan Restructuring Makes Loans Affordable This is accomplished in one or more of the following ways: When the repayment term is extended, increasing the tenure would reduce the borrower’s month-to-month burden and ensure he can make his ends meet despite the EMI payments. Reducing the interest rate: this reduces the interest component of the payback to the lender, spelling a relief to the borrower. Reducing the remaining balance: in this case, computation of interest is done based on the monthly reducing balance method – where there is a reduction of the principal portion and interest is calculated based on the reduced outstanding. The past due amounts are added to the unpaid principal, and then either the interest rate, tenure, or the EMI is altered. Eligibility Criteria for Personal Loan Restructuring Understanding personal loan restructuring eligibility is important for borrowers facing genuine financial stress. Lenders allow restructuring only when the borrower can demonstrate a clear loss of income, job disruption, medical emergency, or any situation that affects repayment capacity. To determine who can restructure personal loan terms, lenders typically review recent bank statements, income documents, and credit history. Borrowers must also have a good repayment record before the hardship began, as past defaults may reduce approval chances. Those meeting these conditions can request revised EMIs, extended tenure, or temporary relief, helping them manage repayments more comfortably during challenging periods. Also, read – Pros And Cons Of Home Loan Restructuring Impact of Personal Loan Restructuring on Your Credit Score Loan restructuring can provide financial relief, but it does affect your loan restructuring credit score. Here is how restructuring affects CIBIL score. Lenders and credit bureaus may flag restructured loans on credit reports, which can lead to a temporary drop in the score. Restructured loans may be labelled “restructured” or “settled,” by credit bureaus, which can imply financial instability to future lenders. The negative impact of loan restructuring is less than that of a loan default, however. Making timely repayments after restructuring your loan can rebuild your credit score over time. Common Mistakes to Avoid When Restructuring Your Loan Let’s look at the most common loan restructuring mistakes: Waiting too long before restructuring of personal loan​ can both harm your CIBIL score and limit restructuring options. Not assessing your repayment capacity before the restructuring can damage your long-term finances. Restructuring without accounting for additional charges can hurt your ability to make repayments. Not being aware of the impact on your credit score can affect your borrowing capacity in the future. Missing payments after restructuring can create further financial stress. Knowing what not to do in loan restructuring will help you manage your finances effectively. Is Personal Loan Restructuring Right for You? If you’re wondering “should I restructure my personal loan”, here are situations where you should consider restructuring: If financial pressures are making regular repayments towards the loan difficult. If rising interest rates and cash flow problems are affecting your repayment ability. If you are at risk of a loan default. If you have experienced sudden job loss, reduced income, or unexpected expenses such as medical bills. If your business is expanding and needs repayment flexibility. Restructuring at the right time can help you deal with economic uncertainty and short-term financial stressors. Knowing when to restructure a personal loan allows you to work towards financial stability effectively. To Summarize It was to identify the stressed loans and help out the borrowers of such loans that the Reserve Bank of India introduced the moratorium on term loans. However, after the moratorium ended, some borrowers still felt distressed. For them, the need was to restructure the loan post the moratorium period, which the RBI recommended, again to help borrowers and keep banks’ NPAs, or non-performing assets, in check. During the moratorium, the borrower is on an EMI holiday, but the loan interest continues accumulating and is added to the principal. Therefore, for the situation after the moratorium, the RBI introduced the loan restructuring scheme for the still stressed borrowers. In the case of loan restructuring, the objective is to make the loan affordable for the borrower by reworking the terms: increase the tenure of the loan to reduce the EMI; charge interest for fewer than applicable months; or reduce the interest component of the loan.
