NOC is typically a legal document that confirms that the issuing authority has no objections to the specific actions mentioned in the document. It can be issued at loan closures, property transfers, immigration of employees or students, or vehicle transfer to a different state. Why is NOC mandatory? NOC is generally optional in a majority of cases unless it is explicitly stated as a required document. It is to demonstrate that the issuing authority has no objections to the undertakings mentioned in the NOC. What if NOC is not given? If NOC is not given, reach out to the issuing authorities to understand the reason behind it, and try to address the concerns that they raise by providing necessary documents or completing the specified actions. When should we apply for NOC? You should apply for NOC when you need official permission from an organization, entity, or individual to perform a specific action. How to check the NOC of a bike online? You can check your bike’s NOC status online through the official Parivahan Sewa website. Visit the “Vehicle Related Services” section, select your state, enter the registration number, and check under “Status” or “NOC Details” to verify if the NOC has been issued. What to do if I lose my NOC certificate? If you lose your NOC certificate, file a police FIR for the lost document. Then, visit your RTO or bank, if it’s a loan-related NOC, with the FIR copy and request a duplicate NOC by submitting the required forms and ID proof. What is a duplicate NOC for two-wheelers? If your original NOC is lost, damaged, or misplaced, a copy of the original NOC will be issued by the lender or RTO. This reissued copy is known as duplicate NOC. It is necessary to prove that no legal or financial obligations exist on the vehicle. Why is NOC required for company registration? An NOC is required for company registration when the business premises are rented or owned by someone else. It confirms the property owner’s consent for using their premises as the company’s registered office address, helping avoid future ownership or legal disputes. Is NOC required for building construction? Yes, an NOC is required before starting any building construction. It must be obtained from authorities like the Fire Department, Pollution Control Board, and local municipal body. These approvals ensure the construction meets safety, environmental, and legal regulations. How to apply for an NOC for car re-registration in another state? To apply for an NOC, visit your original RTO with Form 28, RC, insurance, and pollution certificate. Pay the applicable fee. Once verified, the RTO issues the NOC, allowing you to re-register the car in the new state’s RTO. Do we get NOC after the loan settlement? Yes, once you’ve fully repaid your loan, the lender issues an NOC confirming loan closure and releasing rights over the asset. This document serves as proof that no dues remain and should be collected immediately after final settlement. Where can I obtain a Loan NOC Letter? You can obtain your Loan NOC Letter from the lender’s branch or through their online portal. After the final EMI payment and verification, the bank issues this letter confirming that the loan account is closed and there are no pending dues. What information does a Loan NOC Letter contain? A Loan NOC Letter includes the borrower’s name, loan account number, lender’s details, loan type, closure date, and a statement confirming no outstanding dues. It also mentions the release of rights over the asset, like a house, car, or bike. Is a Loan NOC Letter the same as a Loan Closure Letter? Yes, both documents serve the same purpose. A Loan NOC Letter or Loan Closure Letter confirms the successful repayment of the loan and releases the lender’s claim on the asset. It’s an essential document for future financial or legal references. What details should a Loan NOC include? A Loan NOC should include the borrower’s and lender’s names, loan account number, repayment completion statement, date of loan closure, asset details, and the official signature or stamp of the lender. These details verify that the borrower has no outstanding obligations. How long does it take to receive an NOC? Generally, it takes 7 to 15 working days to receive an NOC after loan closure or RTO application. The timeline may vary based on lender processing time, accuracy of documents, and verification procedures at the respective authority. Is NOC required for all types of loans? Yes, an NOC is essential for secured loans like home, car, or bike loans. It confirms the lender has released ownership rights. However, for unsecured loans like personal loans, the NOC serves as proof of full repayment but is not mandatory. What happens if I don’t obtain an NOC? If you don’t obtain an NOC after loan repayment, the asset remains legally tied to the lender. This can create problems in ownership transfer, resale, or re-registration. Always collect the NOC promptly to avoid future financial or legal complications. Can an NOC be used as legal proof? Yes, an NOC is a valid legal proof confirming there are no pending dues or objections from the issuing authority or lender. It is often required for ownership transfer, loan closure verification, or government documentation purposes. Do I need to submit my NOC anywhere after receiving it? Yes. For vehicle NOCs, submit the certificate to the new RTO for re-registration. For loan-related NOCs, you may submit the letter to the registrar or keep it for future ownership or credit verification purposes. Is there any fee for obtaining an NOC? Yes, a nominal fee is charged for issuing an NOC. For vehicle-related NOCs, it’s paid at the RTO, while banks may charge a small processing fee for loan NOCs. The amount varies by institution and location. Can an NOC be rejected? Yes, an NOC can be rejected if there are pending dues, legal disputes, incorrect documentation, or unpaid challans. Remember to check that all liabilities are cleared and accurate documents are submitted to avoid rejection by the RTO or lender. How should I store my NOC safely? You can store your NOC in a safe place, along with your other important financial or vehicle documents. You can also scan and keep a digital copy securely in cloud storage for easy access during future transactions or verifications. What should I do if my lender refuses to issue an NOC? If your lender refuses to issue an NOC after full repayment, submit a written request or complaint to their branch. If unresolved, escalate the issue to the bank’s grievance redressal officer or file a complaint with the RBI Ombudsman. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Introduction Running a business often means dealing with unpredictable cash flow. One month you’re flush with funds, the next you’re struggling to meet even day-to-day expenses. That’s where external financing avenues, such as cash credit loans, come into the picture. They help you manage short-term working capital requirements without disrupting daily operations or depleting long-term reserves. Excited to know more about the cc loan? Keep reading. What is a cash credit loan? A cash credit loan, also known as a cc loan, refers to a short-term working capital facility offered by banks and Non-Banking Financial Corporations (NBFCs) to businesses in India. Unlike a term loan, where a specific amount is disbursed and repaid over a pre-determined period, a cc loan allows you to withdraw funds multiple times up to a sanctioned loan limit. Interest is charged only on the amount utilized and not on the entire loan limit. A cash credit loan is designed to help business owners tackle urgent cash requirements without taking a fresh loan every time. You can borrow funds from a cash credit loan limit and use it for a variety of purposes, including business expansion, staff payments, rent payments, inventory purchases, technology upgradation, and debt reduction. This limit is decided by the lender based on your business’s annual turnover, credit history , and financial stability. The initial validity of a cash credit loan limit is usually 12 months, after which it can be renewed for another 12 months, and so on. Understanding the cash credit meaning and the advantages it offers over other business financing options, such as term loans and overdrafts (ODs), can help you make the right financial decision. For instance, a term loan allows you to borrow a fixed amount of money and repay it over a specified tenure, along with the applicable interest. Similarly, the OD facility allows individuals and businesses to use more funds than their account balance, up to a pre-approved limit. How does a cash credit loan work? Understanding how cash credit works is crucial for businesses that need recurring access to funds without repeated loan applications. Here’s a step-by-step breakdown of the cash credit loan process, from application to withdrawals to repayment to closure: Application You can start by applying for a cash credit loan with a bank or an NBFC offering this facility. Lenders like Tata Capital allow you to apply digitally from the comfort of your home or office. You can simply visit our website or download the mobile app, fill out an online application form, and upload the required documents . Eligibility check After receiving your application, the lender initiates a process to check your eligibility for a cash credit loan. It usually assesses your business’s financial statements, annual turnover, credit history, and collateral value (total inventory, receivables, fixed assets, etc.) to determine cc loan eligibility. Sanction and limit determination After carefully evaluating your business’s financial stability and collateral value, the lender sanctions a cash credit loan limit. This limit determines the maximum amount you can withdraw at a time. Withdrawals Now you are ready to withdraw funds from your cash credit account, as and when needed. This flexibility makes the facility ideal for managing fluctuating business cash flows. However, the maximum amount you can withdraw depends on the sanctioned loan limit. For example, if you have a sanctioned cc loan limit of Rs. 30 lakhs and you’ve already withdrawn Rs. 20 lakhs from it, you won’t be able to withdraw more than Rs. 10 lakhs now. Interest calculation and repayment You can repay the loan amount at any time during the loan tenure by depositing money into your cc account. The interest will be charged only on the amount you’ve utilized. Renewal or closure A cc loan limit usually has an initial validity of one year, after which you can choose between renewal or closure. Key features of a cash credit loan A cash credit loan is a powerful financing tool that allows you to manage your short-term working capital requirements efficiently. Its structure, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness make it a preferred option for Indian business owners with fluctuating cash flows. Let’s have a look at the key cash credit loan features that distinguish it from other business financing instruments: Flexible credit limit In a cc loan, the lender sanctions a flexible credit limit based on your business turnover, creditworthiness, and collateral value, among several other factors. You can withdraw funds from this limit multiple times during your cc loan tenure. Such a facility helps you tackle evolving financial requirements easily. Interest is charged only on the utilized amount Another standout feature of a cash credit loan is that the interest is charged only on the amount you utilize or withdraw, and not on the entire loan limit. For example, if you have a sanctioned loan limit of Rs. 30 lakhs and have utilized Rs. 10 lakhs till now, the interest will be calculated on Rs. 10 lakhs only. Collateral/security requirement A cash credit loan is typically secured by business assets such as stock, raw materials, finished goods, or receivables. The collateral assures the lender of repayment and helps the borrower access a higher credit limit at competitive interest rates . Short-term tenure and renewals A cash credit loan generally comes with a short tenure of up to 12 months. It is ideal for meeting short-term liquidity requirements. However, once the initial tenure of 12 months is over, you can choose to renew your cash credit loan limit by paying a nominal renewal fee. If unsatisfied, you can even choose to close your cc loan account. Multiple withdrawals and repayments A cash credit loan account allows multiple withdrawals and repayments during the loan tenure. It means that you can withdraw and repay as many times as you want, subject to the sanctioned loan limit. This feature helps you manage cash flow cycles, fund inventory purchases, or handle delayed customer payments without disruption. Tax benefits on interest paid Another feature of a cash credit loan is that the interest paid on the borrowed amount is treated as a business expense. It means that it can be claimed as a tax deduction under Section 37 of the Income Tax Act of 1961. This helps in reducing the overall cost of borrowing and enhances profitability for businesses. Benefits of cash credit loans for businesses A cash credit loan offers immense flexibility and liquidity for businesses. Whether it’s for paying suppliers, meeting payroll, or handling seasonal demand, a cc loan allows you to withdraw funds as and when you need. Here are the key advantages of cash credit loans for businesses: Improved working capital management A cash credit loan allows you to access funds instantly whenever working capital needs arise. It ensures smooth day-to-day operations by bridging the gap between payables and receivables. You can withdraw money as many times as required from the sanctioned loan limit. Boosts liquidity during off-seasons Businesses often face uneven cash flows due to seasonal fluctuations and/or delayed payments. A cc loan limit acts as a financial cushion and provides immediate liquidity to help you sail through the choppy waters. Continuous access to funds helps you maintain a steady performance even during low-revenue periods. Flexibility in withdrawals and repayments One of the major cash credit loan benefits is the flexibility it offers in withdrawals and repayments. It acts like a revolving credit line from which you can withdraw funds, repay them, and then again withdraw, as per your developing financial requirements. This flexibility ensures you won’t have to apply for a new loan every time you go through a cash crunch. Supports business growth By providing easy access to working capital, cash credit loans empower businesses to seize growth opportunities. For example, you can take bulk orders from your customers without worrying about the cash flow shortage. You can even scale your production without any financial stress. Seamless business operations With uninterrupted access to funds, cash credit loans allow you to manage your day-to-day business operations without any hindrance. It ensures that you stay focused on growing your business rather than worrying about the cash in hand. Eligibility criteria to avail a cash credit loan It’s crucial to check your cash credit loan eligibility before applying for it. Getting your loan application rejected by a lender can not only harm your credit score but also damage your business’s reputation. Although the exact eligibility criteria vary from one lending institution to another, here are some common parameters that they check: Business type and registration Lenders offer cash credit loans to businesses registered as sole proprietorships, partnership firms, private limited companies, LLPs (Limited Liability Partnerships), or MSMEs (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises). Additionally, the business must be registered in India. Minimum business vintage Lenders also check on the business’s vintage, i.e., the age of the business, before approving cash credit loan applications. Usually, they require a minimum business vintage of two to three years; however, this criterion may vary from lender to lender. Minimum annual turnover A few lenders may also require a minimum annual turnover for providing cash credit loans. A higher turnover can help you get approval for an enhanced loan limit. CIBIL score The borrower’s CIBIL score, ranging between 300 and 900, reflects their creditworthiness. Lenders usually ask for a CIBIL score of 700 or more to approve your eligibility for a cc loan. A higher CIBIL score can also help you secure a lower interest rate and an improved loan limit. Age limit The borrower’s age can also determine who can apply for a cash credit loan. Usually, this facility is offered to entrepreneurs aged between 24 and 80 years. However, this range is decided by the lender and is not fixed for all. Documents required for a cash credit loan Merely fulfilling the eligibility criteria mentioned above isn’t enough. You must submit the essential cc loan documents to get your loan limit approved. Incorrect or incomplete documentation may lead to the rejection of your loan application. Below is the list of the documents required for a cash credit loan: Identity proof – A government-approved identity proof is required. It may include your PAN card, Aadhaar card, Voter’s ID card, Passport, etc. Address proof – A valid proof of your current address. It can be your Aadhaar card, Passport, rental agreement, property ownership papers, or utility bills. Business registration proof – A business registration proof can be your UDYAM certificate, GST registration certificate, or a certificate of incorporation. Financial statements – These may include your latest Income Tax Returns (ITRs), audited balance sheet, profit-loss statements, etc. Bank statements – Last six-month bank statements may be required to evaluate cash flow and repayment capacity. GST returns – Latest GST filings are required to validate your business’s turnover and sales records. Collateral documents – If you are applying for a cc loan against an asset, such as a real estate property or a fixed deposit, you must submit collateral documents. These may include property papers, asset valuation reports, etc. Apart from the documents mentioned here, you may also need certain additional documents at the time of loan processing. It’s best to get in touch with your lender for more accurate details. Cash credit loan interest rates and charges The applicable cash credit loan interest rate plays a crucial role in determining your overall cost of borrowing. In India, these rates vary across lenders and depend on several key factors such as the applicant’s credit score, business profile, financial stability, and loan tenure. The borrower’s relationship with the lender may also play a part. Businesses with a strong credit history, consistent cash flow, and a good repayment track record often qualify for lower cc loan interest rates in India. On the other hand, start-ups or businesses with fluctuating revenues may be charged slightly higher rates to balance lending risk. Apart from the interest rate, lenders may also levy the following charges on cc loans: Processing fee: A one-time fee charged for covering the administrative costs incurred by the lender. It’s usually 1% to 3% of the sanctioned loan limit. Renewal fee: This is an annual fee for extending or reviewing the cash credit limit. It is usually charged as a flat fee by lenders. Documentation or legal fees: It covers the costs of verifying and registering collateral documents. Foreclosure charges: Charged as a percentage of the outstanding loan amount for foreclosing the loan account before the end of its tenure. At Tata Capital, we offer cash credit loans at highly competitive interest rates. You can even avail of the exclusive pre-approved offer to get the best rate. Common uses of a cash credit loan in business A cash credit loan is one of the most versatile financing tools for businesses. It provides instant access to working capital and helps manage day-to-day operations smoothly, without interrupting business continuity. The benefits of cc loans for businesses range from improved liquidity to flexibility in withdrawals and repayments to hassle-free expansion. Here are some practical cash credit loan uses in daily business operations: Purchasing raw materials Manufacturing businesses can use cash credit loans to buy raw materials in bulk. They ensure uninterrupted production even when receivables are delayed. Paying rent and salaries Even basic expenses, such as paying rent and salaries, seem difficult when there is a cash flow shortage. With a cash credit loan, you can manage these expenses without any hassles. Maintaining inventory If you are a retailer or a wholesaler, you can borrow from your cc loan limit to buy advance inventory during high-demand seasons. It helps you bridge the gap between receivables and payables. Meeting short-term financial requirements You can use cc loans to pay suppliers, clear invoices, and handle other short-term business expenses without waiting for customer payments. Marketing and promotions You can use funds from your cash credit loan to finance marketing campaigns, trade fairs, or product launch events. Business expansion A cash credit loan facility can also help you pay for your business expansion. You can use it to invest in new projects, upgrade your business infrastructure, procure new equipment, and do much more. Things to consider while applying for a cash credit loan A cash credit facility is highly beneficial for managing working capital, but borrowing without proper planning can lead to unnecessary financial strain. Here are some important things to consider before applying for a cash credit loan: Assess your working capital needs: Estimate how much short-term funding your business actually requires. Borrowing an unnecessarily high limit can increase interest costs. Maintain a good credit history: Lenders check your credit score and repayment history before approval. A high CIBIL score improves your cash credit loan eligibility and helps secure better interest rates. Provide adequate collateral: You can consider providing adequate collateral for your cash credit loan. Doing so enhances your chances of loan approval and also helps you secure a higher loan limit. Understand the associated charges: Read the fine print carefully to understand all applicable charges along with the interest rate. Compare between lenders before finalizing. Review repayment flexibility: Check the repayment terms and renewal policies to ensure they align with your business cash flow cycle. How to apply for a cash credit loan? You can apply for a cash credit loan through a straightforward process if you meet the eligibility criteria of the lender. Below are the steps involved in the cash credit loan application process : Research your options Several banks and NBFCs provide cash credit loans in India. Research and compare your options based on the interest rate offered, collateral requirements, annual renewal charge, repayment terms, and other factors to choose the most suitable lender. Check eligibility criteria Once you have zeroed in on a lender, go through its eligibility criteria carefully. Ensure your business meets basic requirements such as valid registration in India, minimum business vintage, stable annual turnover, and a satisfactory CIBIL score. Also, check the collateral requirements. Gather required documents Keep all necessary documents ready, including identity proof, business registration certificates, financial statements, bank statements, GST returns, and collateral documents. Submit your application Submit your cc loan application to the lender online or offline. For an online application, you can visit your lender’s official website or download the mobile app. For an offline application, you can go to the lender’s nearest branch office. Wait for the verification process Upon receiving your application, the lender will evaluate your credit profile, financial health, and collateral value. This stage determines your sanctioned limit and applicable interest rate. Approval and disbursement Upon successful verification, the lender approves your loan application and sanctions a cc loan limit. Accept the terms and conditions of the loan agreement and start borrowing from the sanctioned limit. The full form of cc loan is a cash credit loan. It is a short-term working capital facility offered by banks and NBFCs that allows businesses to borrow funds up to a pre-approved limit. Interest is charged only on the amount utilized or borrowed. How is interest calculated on a cash credit loan? In a cash credit loan, the interest is charged only on the amount utilized or borrowed, not on the sanctioned loan limit. It’s usually computed on a daily reducing balance basis. Can a start-up apply for a cash credit loan? Yes. A start-up can apply for a cash credit loan, provided it meets the lender’s eligibility criteria, such as valid business registration, minimum operational history, and sufficient financial records. However, a few lenders ask for additional collateral or a guarantor to provide cc loans to start-ups. What happens if I do not repay the cash credit loan on time? A cash credit loan offers flexibility in terms of withdrawals and repayments. It means that you can withdraw and repay at any time during the loan tenure. However, if you still fail to repay the loan amount, the lender may impose penalty interest or late payment charges. In severe cases, the lender may seize pledged collateral or take legal recovery actions. Is a cash credit loan tax-deductible? Yes. A cash credit loan offers tax deduction benefits. Under Section 37 of the Income Tax Act of 1961, interest paid towards a cash credit loan is considered a business expense and can be claimed as a tax-deductible. Can a cash credit loan be used for non-business purposes? No. A cash credit loan is specifically designed to help businesses meet short-term working capital requirements. Using it for personal or non-business purposes violates loan terms and can lead to penalties or cancellation. Bhu-Naksha maps online for free. Check the RoR to verify ownership, land classification and revenue details, but use an Encumbrance Certificate and legal title check before buying property or applying for a home loan. Bhulekh Odisha is the official online Odisha land record portal (bhulekh.ori.nic.in), on which you can see and download your Record of Rights (RoR/Khatiyan), details of your plot, and the Bhu-Naksha map free of cost, without the need to go to the tehsil office. The records are important not only for a simple inspection but also as necessary documents that a lender looks at, before approving your loan against property . Understanding Your Land Record: RoR, Khatiyan and Key Terms You should look at the various key terms of the land records before taking a loan on it. The RoR (Record of Rights), also known as the Khatiyan or Patta in Odisha, is the official document held by the government and shows who has the rights to a piece of land and on what terms. A few important terms you may come across include: Khatiyan Number : It is a unique account number under which one or more plots owned by a person (or family) are recorded. Plot/Khesra Number : The plot or Khesra number is the identification number assigned to an individual piece of land within a village. Tenant: The tenant refers to the individual who holds rights over the land. It is not necessarily a renter, but the registered landholder. Kisam (Land Classification): If the land is designated as agricultural, residential, commercial, or another category, then it affects how it can be used and how revenue is calculated. Area and Revenue Details: It refers to the recorded size of the plot and the land revenue (tax) assessed on it. A lender or buyer may examine the Bhulekh land record to check the tenant’s name (to make sure it matches that of the seller), Kisam (to verify that the land is legally usable for the purpose intended), or any other notes on the back page, because it may flag disputes, if any. What is Bhulekh Odisha? Bhulekh Odisha is a digital land portal operated by the Revenue and Disaster Management Department of the Government of Odisha. It allows citizens to check the information relating to the RoR, Khatiyan, plot details, tenant data, and the cadastral (Bhu-Naksha) maps for land throughout the state, without the need to visit the tehsil or revenue office in person. How to Check Odisha Land Records (RoR) Online – Step by Step It is easy to check your Bhulekh Odisha land records from a phone or computer on the official website. Here’s how to do it: Step 1: Go to the Official Portal: Visit the official website to check the bhulekh Orissa land record. Do not trust any third-party website. Step 2: Select Your Location: Navigate to section ‘Select Location for RoR’, and select your District, Tahasil, Village, and RI Circle. Note that location names on the portal are typically listed in Odia. Step 3: Choose your Search Type: Choose the search type, including Khatiyan Number, Plot Number, Tenant Name, or Unique Plot ID, based on information you currently have. Step 4: Enter the details : Enter the Khatiyan number, the plot number, or the tenant/owner’s name as required, then submit the search. Step 5: View the RoR : The Odisha Bhulekh land record will appear in the list. To see details regarding ownership, area, and land classification, open the front page of the RoR. For any remarks such as disputes, government restrictions, or bank encumbrances, you can check the RoR back page. Step 6: Print or save as PDF : Use your browser’s Print function and select the “Save as PDF” option to keep digital Bhulekh Odisha land records. How to Download and Print Your RoR Here is how you can download and print your RoR: Go to the RoR Front Page or the RoR Back Page, depending on what details you require. Use the browser Print function and select the ‘Save as PDF’ option (or print directly if you have a printer connected). Requirements may change, so it is suggested to check the current procedure on the Bhulekh portal or with the tehsil office. How to View the Bhu-Naksha (Land Map) of a Plot RoR can tell who owns the plot, but if you want to know where it is located or what shape it takes, then you can view the land map. Here is how you can view the Bhu-Naksha of a plot: Step1: Open the bhunakshaodisha.nic.in website or click on the ‘Map View’ link from the main Bhulekh portal. Step 2: Select your District, Tahasil, RI Circle, and Village. Step 3: Click on the particular plot you want to view. The map shows the plot’s boundaries, shape, and dimensions. Step 4: Select the Map Report option to generate a PDF. You can choose between a single plot report or a report covering all plots recorded under one owner. Odisha uses modern digital survey technologies, including GNSS (RTK), for cadastral mapping and land-record modernisation. When a person is buying a property or applying for a home loan, the map helps to check the recorded boundaries of the plot and compare them with the sale deed and the actual property. If the boundaries or the position of the plot do not meet, it is suggested to sort out the matter with the relevant revenue authority. However, the map should be treated as one part of property due diligence, along with the RoR, title documents, encumbrance certificate, and legal verification. Bhulekh Odisha Land Valuation and Land Revenue It is easy to assume that a search for “land valuation” is the same as one for “land record”. However, it is not. The land classification and the land revenue amount for the property are shown in your Bhulekh RoR, whereas the government valuation used for stamp duty is verified by the Inspector General of Registration (IGR) Odisha system. You can check the benchmark/circle-rate valuation used for stamp duty by using the valuation or stamp duty calculator tool on the IGR Odisha portal. You can pay outstanding land revenue (Khajana) by using the e-Pauti service on odishalandrevenue.nic.in. You need to enter your district, tahasil, village, and Khata number to see outstanding rent, cess, or arrears and pay online. Keeping land revenue payments up to date can help you maintain your revenue records and avoid outstanding dues. Checking Land Records Before a Home Loan: What to Verify Before buying property with a home loan, you should check the Odisha Bhulekh land record. As a lender, you may review the RoR and other land records as part of property and legal due diligence. As a buyer, you should independently verify the title and boundaries. However, RoR does not prove that the property has a completely clear title. It is useful as evidence of the recorded ownership and rights, but it may not indicate every mortgage, legal claim, or other charge against the property. Check the following before applying for a home loan: Get an Encumbrance Certificate : It allows you to check whether there are any registered mortgages, charges, or other legal claims over the property. Get the Title Checked : Hire a qualified lawyer to check the ownership history of the property and the associated documents. Check Mutation Status : Ensure that the land record has been updated with the new owner’s name after a sale or inheritance. Compare Property Boundaries : Check the Bhu-Naksha map against the sale deed and the actual property to identify any discrepancies. You should obtain a home loan only after having checked these details. The lender’s verification is primarily concerned with evaluating the property and the loan risk. Therefore, it should not replace your own due diligence. When your property documents are accurate, you can explore Tata Capital Home Loan options and use an EMI calculator to plan your repayments. Common Problems and How to Fix Them Some users may encounter problems while trying to search or interpret the Odisha land record. Below are the common problems with solutions to fix them: Record Not Found: If the property details are correct but no online record is available, it means records are not digitised yet.You should recheck the District, Tahasil, Village, RI Circle, and Khatiyan or Plot number. The Bhulekh FAQ confirms that these details are used for finding Odisha Bhulekh land record. Name Does Not Match: If the seller name does not match with name appearing in revenue records, it may indicate that mutation has not been completed. You should ask the concerned revenue authority to clarify the status before proceeding. Boundary Discrepancy: Compare the Bhulekh RoR with the Bhu-Naksha, registered documents, and physical property. If you find any discrepancy, you should investigate it at the relevant Tahasil or revenue office rather than ignoring it. Conclusion bhulekh.ori.nic.in is the website where you can check all Bhulekh Odisha land records. You can check ownership, plot, and revenue details (RoR) on bhulekh.ori.nic.in and view the plot map on bhunakshaodisha.nic.in . These records may support you while purchasing property or applying for a home loan. After due diligence is complete, you can finance the purchase by exploring the different Tata Capital home loan options. Simply choose your District, Tahasil, Village, and RI Circle, and then check records by using the Khatiyan, Plot, or Tenant information. What is RoR in Odisha land records? RoR is the Record of Rights, which is also known as Khatiyan or Patta in Odisha. It is the official document that shows who has the rights to a piece of land, together with the area, the classification of the land, and the revenue details. Bhulekh RoR is treated as prima facie evidence of possession, but not guarantee of clear marketable title. How do I download my RoR from Bhulekh Odisha? Once you have looked at your record on the portal, open either the RoR Front Page or the Back Page and use your browser's printing function to save it as a PDF. The PDF version of Bhulekh Orissa land record is for reference only. You should obtain a certified copy for official purposes from your tehsil office. Is the Bhulekh Odisha RoR accepted by banks for a home loan? Lenders may ask for the RoR to verify ownership. They generally also ask for additional documents such as an Encumbrance Certificate and proof that mutation has been completed. How do I check the Bhu-Naksha map of my plot? Go to bhunakshaodisha.nic.in, choose your District, Tahasil, RI Circle and Village, and then click on your plot to see the boundaries and shape. You can use the Map Report feature to download a PDF of the map for one plot or all plots under one owner. How is land valuation checked in Odisha? You can check the Odisha land valuation through the IGR Odisha portal's valuation calculator, not on Bhulekh. Bhulekh's RoR only shows the land revenues and land classification, which is a separate figure from stamp duty valuation. Is a Bhulekh land record enough to confirm a clear property title? No. RoR serves as prima facie evidence of possession but does not show any encumbrance or bank charge on the property. It is suggested to obtain an Encumbrance Certificate and have a lawyer do a title search before making a purchase or applying for a loan. Is there an official Bhulekh Odisha mobile app? The Government of Odisha has not launched any Bhulekh Odisha land records official mobile application. The Bhulekh website itself is compatible with mobile browsers and does not require an additional app to find land records. GST filings, or mistakes in your commercial report can all lead to a bad business credit history or a low CIBIL MSME Rank. Keeping an eye on your business credit profile can help you catch these issues, correct any inaccurate information and build up your standing with disciplined financial habits before you apply for funding. Most business owners do not realise a crucial fact when they first approach lenders, i.e., our business has its own business credit history and credit report, completely separate from your personal CIBIL score, and commercial lenders check both before approving a business loan . A strong business credit history means easier approvals, higher credit limits, and lower interest rates, whereas a weak profile can lead to costly terms or outright rejections. This guide covers what a business credit report is, how to check it, how the CIBIL MSME Rank works, how it affects your borrowing capacity, and how you can improve it. What is Business Credit History? Business credit history is the official record of your business’s borrowing and repayment activity over time. It includes term loans, working capital credit lines and trade credit built from data that lenders report to commercial credit bureaus. This is separate from your personal credit history although for smaller proprietorships, the two are often considered together by lenders. A clean record helps your business be perceived as a borrower that can handle its own financial obligations and can be trusted. Business Credit Report and CIBIL MSME Rank (CMR): The Basics To evaluate your company’s borrowing track record, lenders rely on the CIBIL Company Credit Report (CCR), the comprehensive document detailing your business credit report, and the CIBIL MSME Rank (CMR) that summarises it. The CMR scale runs from 1 to 10, where CMR-1 represents the best possible standing and CMR-10 represents the worst. This is the exact opposite direction of the familiar 300 to 900 personal credit score range. Note that this ranking is typically available for commercial credit exposures up to Rs 50 crore. CIBIL MSME Rank Band What It Signals Likely Loan Outcome CMR-1 to CMR-3 Low credit risk and strong repayment discipline Easiest approvals, highest credit limits, and preferential risk-based interest rates CMR-4 to CMR-6 Moderate credit risk with occasional delays Standard approvals subject to additional verification or moderate terms CMR-7 to CMR-10 High credit risk or severe past defaults Likely loan rejection or restrictive, costly borrowing terms Note : CIBIL MSME Ranks and commercial credit parameters are issued by credit bureaus and are subject to periodic updates. How Business Credit History Affects Your Loan Approval and Rate When you apply for financing, your business credit history directly impacts your business loan outcomes at every single stage of the evaluation process. A poor CMR can lead to outright rejection while a good rank can open the door to higher loan amounts, competitive interest rates through risk-based pricing and faster turnaround times. To see how this works in real life, consider this anonymised scenario of a wholesale trader seeking funding: The Initial Hurdle: A wholesale trader with a high overdraft utilisation and past missed EMIs applies for a business expansion loan, only to face rejection due to a weak credit rank. The Turnaround Phase: Over the next 12 months, the trader systematically clears overdue payments, lowers credit line utilisation, and files tax returns diligently. The Successful Result: On the subsequent application, the updated business credit report accurately reflects these disciplined financial habits, resulting in a smooth approval at standard market rates. What Lenders Actually Look At Financial institutions will scrutinize your commercial data to assess overall risk, financial discipline and stability before they agree to fund your application. Lenders look at a number of underlying factors when they assess a company’s commercial credit profile: Repayment Track Record: Your track record of timely payments on current term loans and credit lines is the most important factor impacting your rank. Credit Utilisation: High sustained utilisation of overdraft or cash credit facilities signals tight cash flow and acts as an immediate red flag. Age and Depth of Credit: A longer, well-maintained history of handling commercial credit responsibly inspires greater lender confidence. Derogatory Marks: Any history of write-offs, bounced cheques, legal suits filed, or NCLT cases will severely damage your credit standing. GST Filing Behavior: In the modern Indian lending ecosystem, frequent delays in GST filing or mismatches in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B raise questions on business stability. Personal CIBIL Score : For proprietorships and small partnerships, besides the commercial report, the personal credit score of the proprietor is also checked. How to Check Your Business Credit Report Check on your commercial credit health early to prevent surprises during the loan process. You can directly obtain your CIBIL Company Credit Report from the official cibil.com commercial report section or subscription portal. Step 1: Go to the official website of the commercial credit bureau Step 2: Select the company credit report or subscription option. Step 3: Provide essential details, including your business PAN, GST details, and registered entity information. Step 4: Complete the required OTP verification process. Step 5: Access and review your detailed business credit report. Unlike personal credit reports, which offer a free annual summary, commercial credit reports are typically paid subscription products. Business owners are encouraged to review these reports well before applying for capital. How to Build and Improve Your Business Credit History Building robust creditworthiness before you actually need urgent capital is a smart financial strategy. You can strengthen your business credit history and business credit report using these practical steps: Separate Finances: Maintain dedicated business bank accounts and commercial credit lines separate from personal finances. Never Miss a Due Date: Pay every business loan EMI and vendor credit line on time, opting for auto-debit where possible. Keep Utilisation Low: Maintain your overdraft and cash credit utilisation ideally under 30% of your sanctioned limit. File Taxes Accurately: Ensure your GST returns are filed accurately and on time without persistent delays. Clear Derogatives: Pay off any overdue EMIs or old marks, and let a clean repayment track record build over time. Dispute Mistakes: Regularly check your commercial report for errors and raise disputes immediately if you spot discrepancies. Start Small: Build an initial positive track record with a smaller credit line before applying for large-scale enterprise financing. Business Credit vs Personal Credit: What’s the Difference? The study of the difference between individual credit standing and commercial reporting frameworks helps to understand what parameters control different kinds of borrowing. Knowing the difference between personal and commercial credit helps you manage both sides of your financial profile well. Compare the evaluation framework below to highlight the key differences between individual and enterprise reporting standards. Feature Personal CIBIL Score Commercial CIBIL MSME Rank (CMR) Primary Focus Evaluates you as an individual borrower Evaluates your registered business entity Score Scale 300 to 900 (Higher score is better) 1 to 10 (Lower rank number is better) Data Sources Individual credit cards, personal loans, consumer debt Company loans, trade credit, working capital, GST data Relevance Essential for all loans, heavily impacts small business approvals Essential for corporate and MSME business loans For large corporations, personal and business records remain strictly separate, but for small businesses and proprietorships, lenders examine both. A weak personal CIBIL score range can still sink a business loan application even if your commercial record looks decent. Conclusion Your business maintains its own credit report and a CIBIL MSME Rank, where 1 is best and 10 represents the highest credit risk that lenders use to evaluate approvals, credit limits, and interest rates. Your eligibility is determined by commercial records, GST filing behavior and personal scores. So, it is important to maintain disciplined repayments and low credit utilisation. The credit bureaus independently produce credit scores and reports and the ultimate decision to lend is made solely by the relevant financial institution. A business credit history is the official record of how well a business entity pays back money that it has borrowed in the past on loans, credit lines and trade credit. It is a sign of financial reliability to commercial lenders. What is a CIBIL MSME Rank (CMR)? A CIBIL MSME Rank (CMR) is a one-line score given to companies based on their commercial credit report, reflecting their overall credit profile and risk for loans up to ₹50 crore. Is a lower or higher CMR better? Lower CMR is better. The CIBIL MSME Rank ranges from 1 to 10. CMR-1 indicates the lowest credit risk and best financial standing, whereas CMR-10 denotes the highest credit risk. How does business credit history affect a business loan? A good credit history of the business makes for faster loan approvals, higher sanction limits and lower rates of interest. However, a bad history can increase the cost of borrowing or lead to rejection of loans. How do I check my business credit report? To check your business credit report visit the official CIBIL.com commercial report portal, enter your business PAN and entity details and complete the OTP verification process for the paid subscription report. Does my personal CIBIL affect my business loan? Yes. Businesses keep their commercial records separately. Lenders, especially of proprietorships and small partnerships, typically take into account the proprietor's personal CIBIL score in addition to the business credit report. How can I improve my business credit score? You can improve your score by keeping your credit utilisation low, paying all business loan EMIs and vendor dues on time, filing your GST returns on time and monitoring your commercial report for errors regularly. year through the official TransUnion CIBIL website. Log in or register, complete verification, open your Credit Report, and save it as a PDF. Check your personal details, loan and credit card accounts, payment history, and enquiries for errors or unfamiliar activity. Checking your own CIBIL report does not lower your credit score. To download your CIBIL report online, visit the official TransUnion CIBIL website, log in to your myCIBIL account and open your credit report. You can then print the report and save it as a PDF. CIBIL provides one free CIBIL score and report in each calendar year. The report includes your CIBIL score along with the loans, credit cards , repayment history and credit enquiries reported in your name. This helps you see the details used to build your credit profile. The free annual Score and Report is different from paid subscription access, which lets you refresh your Score and Report more frequently. The steps below show how to download your CIBIL report online, save it as a PDF, open it if it is password-protected, and check it for errors or unfamiliar accounts. CIBIL Score vs CIBIL Report: What You’re Downloading A CIBIL score is a three-digit number ranging from 300 to 900. It is calculated using information in the Accounts and Enquiries sections of your CIBIL Report. The CIBIL report, also called a Credit Information Report or CIR, contains the credit information reported by lenders. It includes your personal details, loans, credit cards, outstanding balances, account status, payment history and enquiries. The Account Information section can show up to 36 months of monthly payment history. When you complete a credit score report download, you can review both the score and the credit information behind it. In simple terms, the score is the number, while the report is the detailed record behind that number. If you are not sure what the score means, make sure you understand the CIBIL score range thoroughly. How to Download Your Free CIBIL Report: Step by Step Wondering how to take CIBIL report online? Log in to the official TransUnion CIBIL website and follow the steps given below: 1. Go to the Official CIBIL Website Visit the official TransUnion CIBIL website and select the option for your Free CIBIL Score and Report. If you already have a myCIBIL account, log in and go to the “My Account” section, where CIBIL provides a “Get your Free Report” option when you are eligible. 2. Enter Your Details For a new account, provide the information requested on the enrolment form. This generally includes: Email address Mobile number First and last name ID type and ID number Date of birth PIN code and state The identity options can include PAN and other specific identifiers. Enter your details exactly as they appear on your identification documents, especially your PAN or other identity number. CIBIL uses these details to identify and verify your credit profile. If you use PAN as your ID, enter the number and other personal details accurately. A mismatch can prevent the system from identifying the correct credit profile. 3. Complete Authentication CIBIL verifies the email address and mobile number through OTP authentication during enrolment. Depending on the process, you may also be asked to complete additional identity verification. CIBIL may ask you to keep details of a credit card or loan account handy if additional verification is required. Never share your OTP with another person. 4. Open Your CIBIL Report Once authentication is complete, log in to your myCIBIL account. Your dashboard gives you access to your CIBIL Score and detailed credit report. If you are accessing your free annual report, CIBIL says it should be available instantly after successful authentication. 5. Save the Report as a PDF CIBIL’s current support instructions state that you can: Open the Credit Report section. Select Print the report. Wait for the report to open in printable format. Select Print. Choose Save as PDF on your device. The exact screen labels may change as CIBIL updates its portal, so follow the options shown in your account if they differ slightly. Also Read – Experian vs CIBIL: Which Credit Score Is Better How to Open Your Password-Protected CIBIL Report PDF CIBIL’s current public support instructions do not specify a universal password format for every downloaded CIBIL report PDF. If the PDF you receive is password-protected, use the password instructions provided when the report is generated or in the accompanying communication from CIBIL. Do not rely on password formats published on third-party websites. If you still cannot open the file, log in to myCIBIL and use CIBIL’s official support options. Do not share the PDF, OTP or account credentials with anyone offering to unlock it for you. Free vs Paid CIBIL Report: What to Know You can get CIBIL report online free once in every calendar year. If you want updated access more frequently, CIBIL also offers paid subscription plans. CIBIL’s standard subscription information lists: Option Access Listed Price 1-month plan Regular Score and Report refreshes during the subscription ₹699 6-month plan Regular Score and Report refreshes during the subscription ₹999 12-month plan Regular Score and Report refreshes during the subscription ₹1,499 Note : Prices listed above are as of August 2026 and may change. Check the latest subscription prices on the official CIBIL website before purchasing. What to Check in Your CIBIL Report After the CIBIL report download, check the report for incorrect or unfamiliar information. This involves: Personal information: Confirm your name, date of birth, PAN and contact details. Account information: Review every loan and credit card, including account status, balance, payment history and overdue amounts. Enquiry information: Check whether recent lender enquiries match credit applications you made. Account status: Look for closed accounts still showing as open, incorrect balances or wrong Days Past Due (DPD) entries. Unfamiliar activity: Flag loans, cards or enquiries you do not recognise. If you find incorrect information, you can raise a dispute through CIBIL’s official process. CIBIL allows consumers to dispute inaccuracies, account ownership issues and duplicate information through myCIBIL. If your report contains little or no account information, it may indicate that there is little or no credit history reported in your name. This does not necessarily mean there is an error. If you have existing or previous credit accounts that are missing, check your details and raise a dispute if required. You can also know the ins and outs of credit mix to understand how different types of credit form part of your overall credit profile. How to Spot Fake ‘Free CIBIL Report’ Websites Use caution when you download a CIBIL report online. Watch for these warning signs: A lookalike domain pretending to be CIBIL Requests for your card PIN, CVV, UPI PIN or net-banking password Requests to share an OTP over a call, message or email No clear privacy policy or data-handling information Requests to send your complete report through WhatsApp or unsolicited email Charges for a “free annual CIBIL report” without clearly explaining the service being sold Use cibil.com or an authorised financial channel for the official report. Never share your OTP, PIN, CVV or net-banking password to obtain or download your report. Suspected financial cyber fraud can be reported through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal or by calling 1930. Also Read – What is a credit rating? How Often Should You Download Your CIBIL Report? Use your free annual CIBIL report download to review your credit information at least once a year. Checking your report every six months can also help you spot errors or unfamiliar activity earlier. You may also want to check it before applying for credit, after closing a loan or card, or if you notice activity you do not recognise. Conclusion A CIBIL report download helps you review the credit information recorded in your name. You can get one free CIBIL Score and Report each calendar year through CIBIL, save the report as a PDF, and review your accounts, repayment history and enquiries for errors or activity you do not recognise. If the PDF is password-protected, use the password instructions provided by CIBIL rather than relying on an old password format found online. Use only official or authorised channels to access your report. If you are considering borrowing, you can also check the eligibility requirements and applicable terms for a Tata Capital Personal Loan through the Tata Capital website or app. Disclaimer : This article is for general information only. CIBIL Scores and Reports are issued by TransUnion CIBIL. Processes, features and prices may change. Use official or authorised channels and report suspected cyber fraud through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. FAQs How do I download my CIBIL report? To complete a CIBIL report download, visit the official CIBIL website, register or log in and complete the required authentication. Open your Credit Report, select “Print the report,” and choose “Save as PDF” on your device. If you are unsure how to take CIBIL report, follow the current instructions shown inside myCIBIL. Is downloading a CIBIL report free? Yes. CIBIL provides one free CIBIL Score and Report in every calendar year. After using the free annual access, you can choose a paid subscription if you want more frequent updates. Check the latest subscription price directly on the official CIBIL platform before making a payment. How many times can I get a free CIBIL report? You can get a CIBIL report online free once in each calendar year through CIBIL. If you need refreshed access more often, paid subscription options are available. Some banks and authorised financial platforms may also provide separate credit-score services, but these should not be confused with CIBIL's free annual Score and Report. What is the password for the CIBIL report PDF? CIBIL's current public support instructions do not specify one universal password format for every CIBIL report PDF. If your PDF is password-protected, follow the password instructions displayed when the report is generated or sent to you. Avoid using old password formulas published on third-party websites. Why is my CIBIL report blank? A blank or very limited report can mean that little or no credit history has been reported to CIBIL for your profile. It is not necessarily an error. If you have existing or previous credit accounts that are missing, check your personal details and raise a dispute if required. What's the difference between a CIBIL score and a CIBIL report? A CIBIL Score is a three-digit number ranging from 300 to 900 that summarises your credit history. A CIBIL Report contains the underlying details, including loans, credit cards, repayment history and lender enquiries. A credit score report download therefore provides more information than the score alone. Does downloading my report affect my score? No. Checking your own CIBIL Score and Report does not lower your CIBIL Score. A lender's credit enquiry while assessing a loan or credit application is different from accessing your own report. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary: Understanding your CIBIL report becomes easier by reviewing your score, account details, repayment history and enquiries. You should learn what the STD, SUB, DBT, LSS and DPD indicate, and how these codes affect your credit profile. Learn what steps to take ahead if you identify the negative or inaccurate entries. A CIBIL report provides a detailed account of your credit history, including your loans, credit cards, repayment history and recent credit enquiries. If you understand how to read a CIBIL report, you will be able to spot any errors and understand how lenders view your credit profile. Terms such as LSS in CIBIL, STD, SUB, DBT and DPD may at first appear confusing, but each of them has a specific meaning. STD generally indicates a Standard account, while SUB, DBT and LSS represent progressively more serious account classifications. The Sections of a CIBIL Report A CIBIL report may look complicated, but it involves several key sections. Once you know what each section is, you can easily scan your report within minutes. Score: Your score ranges from 300 to 900 , with a higher score indicating that your credit profile is stronger. Personal Information: This includes details such as your name, date of birth, and other information that may be used to identify you. Ensure that the details are correct. Contact Information: The section contains your current addresses with your contact numbers and email information you provided. Account Information: It is one of the important sections because it provides a list of your loans and credit cards with your account status, outstanding amounts, payment history and other details. This is the section where you will see STD, DBT, LSS, DPD and SUB in CIBIL. Enquiry Information: It shows the record of every lender who has checked your credit record. Employment Information: This section contains employment-related information reported by credit institutions. If you are wondering how to read a CIBIL report , you can start checking your score and personal details, then review every account and its repayment history. Also, carefully check the account section because it shows how your credit has been managed over time. See a Sample CIBIL Report (Annotated) A CIBIL report sample can make the different fields easier to identify. It contains: CIBIL Score Personal Information Contact Information Account Information Account Line Account Status DPD grid Enquiry Information Account Status Codes Explained: STD, SUB, DBT, LSS Account-status codes help you understand how a lender has classified an account. The table below explains STD, SUB, DBT, LSS and other entries you may encounter. Status Full Form What It Means Good or Bad? What You Can Do STD Standard Payments are being made within 90 days. Any account overdue by more than 90 days is classified as an NPA by banks. Good Make the repayments on time to maintain this status. SUB Sub-Standard An account that has remained an NPA for up to 12 months. Warning Clear your overdue amount as soon as possible and resume regular payments. DBT Doubtful The account has remained a Sub-Standard account for a period of 12 months. Serious Contact your lender about a resolution plan and clear the outstanding dues urgently. LSS Loss An account where loss has been identified and remains uncollectible. Most negative Contact the lender to understand the account status and repayment/settlement options, then maintain timely payments on other accounts. 000 Not a full-form/status code Payment was made as per the due date, with no deviation or late payment. Good Continue paying on or before the due date. XXX Not a full-form/status code The bank/lender has not reported information for those months. Neither inherently good nor bad Check with the lender if the reporting gap persists or if the account details are inaccurate. SMA Special Mention Account A special account classification used for reporting a Standard account that is moving towards Sub-Standard. Warning Review the overdue amount and make payments promptly to prevent further deterioration. Important : LSS stands for “Loss” in CIBIL’s official glossary. It should not be expanded as “Lender Settled Status.” “Settled” is a separate account-status concept and should not be conflated with LSS. Also Read – How to Check Your CIBIL Score Online Without a PAN Card What is DPD (Days Past Due)? DPD is Days Past Due and is displayed as a monthly grid alongside each account. Each entry tells you how many days late that particular payment was: 000 or STD : Paid on time. XXX : No data was reported for that month. A DPD figure of 000 is a good sign because it shows that there has been no reported delay in payment. The more days overdue the figure becomes, the more lenders will be concerned about the borrower’s repayment behaviour. The DPD grid may also display asset-classification codes such as STD, DBT, LSS and SUB in CIBIL. These codes are different from numerical DPD values such as 000, 030 or 060. CIBIL’s current guidance indicates that payment history can be reported for up to 36 months. An account that becomes overdue by more than 90 days can be classified as an NPA, after which the relevant asset classification may become SUB. Which Statuses Are Good and Which Are Warnings? A quick way to read your CIBIL report is: Good: STD status, DPD of 000. Warning: SUB status, or DPD numbers that are climbing month over month. Serious: DBT, LSS, or any account marked written-off or settled. Any negative entry can have an impact on your chances of loan approval and on the interest rate given on future loans. However, lenders consider multiple factors when assessing a credit application, so a negative entry does not by itself determine whether a loan will be approved or what rate you will receive. If you want to improve your situation, you should know exactly where you currently stand. To get more ideas on how to rebuild your profile, make sure you understand the maximum CIBIL score to improve your credit mix. Also Read – What is credit review and how does it work? I See a Negative Status — What Should I Do? Identifying the DBT, LSS or SUB in CIBIL report can be unsettling, but there is a clear path forward. Check that it’s correct: Reporting errors may happen, a payment that was actually made on time, or an account that isn’t yours. If the information is inaccurate, you can raise a dispute through CIBIL’s official dispute process or through your myCIBIL account. CIBIL verifies the dispute with the concerned credit institution, and any correction is made based on the lender’s confirmation. If it’s a real delay: If the delay is genuine, pay the overdue amount and then make the next payment on time. The information may remain in your credit history for a period of time. Building a consistent record of on-time repayments can help strengthen your overall credit profile over time. If it’s a settlement or write-off (LSS): Settlement or write-off should not be described as LSS itself. LSS means Loss in CIBIL’s asset-classification terminology. These are serious statuses that future lenders may consider when assessing a credit application. Work with the lender to understand the status and resolve outstanding issues where possible. Additionally, do not fall for “instant CIBIL fix” scams. It is impossible for anyone to erase an accurate default or settlement from your report overnight. Be aware of anyone who claims this for a fee. The only real route is verified dispute resolution or time, along with your good repayment behaviour. Read More – How to build a credit score from scratch Conclusion Reading the CIBIL report will enable you to get a better understanding of your credit score, account details, payment history and the credit enquiries that have been made. STD is a Standard classification, while SUB, DBT and LSS indicate increasingly serious asset classifications. DPD shows how many days a payment was reported late, while 000 indicates payment as per the due date and XXX means information was not reported for that period. Check every entry for errors and raise a dispute through official channels if you find inaccurate information. If a negative entry is accurate, its impact can reduce over time through consistent, on-time repayments rather than shortcuts. Before applying for a personal loan, you can check your eligibility with Tata Capital and explore suitable personal loan options. Disclaimer: This content is for general informational purposes only. Credit status and repayment information are reported to TransUnion CIBIL by lenders. Always verify the details in your specific CIBIL report and raise disputes through official channels if you identify an error. FAQs What does STD mean in a CIBIL report? STD in CIBIL means "Standard" and indicates that payments are being made within 90 days. It should not be interpreted as meaning that a payment was necessarily delayed by less than 90 days. It is a positive sign of repayment behaviour and may work in your favour while applying to lenders. What does SUB mean in a CIBIL report? The SUB full form in CIBIL is 'Sub-Standard'. CIBIL describes a SUB account as one that has remained an NPA for up to 12 months. It is a warning signal that may negatively affect how lenders assess your creditworthiness until the underlying repayment issues are addressed. What is the full form of LSS in CIBIL? LSS stands for the "Loss" asset classification in CIBIL. It refers to an account where loss has been identified and remains uncollectible. It should not be expanded as "Lender Settled Status", and it should not be confused with a separate "Settled" account status. What does DPD mean in a CIBIL report? DPD means "Days Past Due". It is a month-by-month figure that shows how many days each payment was late. 000 indicates that the payment was made on time, whereas an increasing figure shows a growing repayment risk to lenders. XXX means that information was not reported for that month. How do I read my CIBIL report? To read your CIBIL report, start by looking at your score, then go on to the account information section, which gives a list of each loan or card together with its status (STD, SUB, DBT, LSS) and its DPD grid. You can also check your personal details and the enquiry records in the report. Review your contact and employment information as well, and check each section for errors or unfamiliar entries. Can I remove a SUB or LSS status from my report? No. You cannot remove an accurate status instantly, and no legitimate service can do this. If the entry is a genuine reporting error, you may dispute it for free with CIBIL. However, if it reflects a real delay or an accurate adverse classification, its impact may reduce over time with consistent, on-time repayments. Is STD good or bad in a CIBIL report? STD is good. It reflects a Standard account classification where payments are being made within 90 days and is generally viewed more positively than accounts with serious adverse classifications. Checking your own score does not lower it. Learn how to identify the cause, correct inaccurate information and improve your score through consistent repayment habits. Checking your own CIBIL score does not reduce it, as that is a soft enquiry with zero impact. If your CIBIL score has fallen, the reason is usually linked to your borrowing or repayment history, such as missed payments, high credit utilisation or recent credit enquiries. Once you clear up the misconception that checking CIBIL score will reduce score, you realise that scores only dip because of real-world borrowing patterns, and they can always be built back up over time. That said, understanding what changed can help you take the right steps to improve your credit profile over time. Does Checking Your CIBIL Score Reduce It? No. Many people believe that checking their own credit score will cause it to drop. It does not. Accessing your own report through official channels or authorised banking apps always registers as a soft pull, meaning it leaves your score completely untouched. Enquiry Type Who Initiates It? Impact on CIBIL Score Visibility on Report Soft Enquiry You’re checking your own score, or banks are checking pre-approved offers Zero impact (Does not lower your score) Visible only to you Hard Enquiry A lender reviews your report after you formally apply for credit Small temporary drop Visible to all lenders Similarly, if you are shopping around for a major loan and submit multiple applications within a tight 14 to 45-day window for the exact same category, such as a home or personal loan, credit bureaus typically group them together as a single hard enquiry. Moreover, multiple applications for credit within a short period can result in several hard enquiries, eventually affecting your score. Making regular self-checks part of your routine is a smart way to catch reporting errors or signs of fraud early. Why Did My CIBIL Score Decrease? Your credit score is constantly changing rather than being fixed. It fluctuates whenever financial institutions send fresh updates to the bureaus, which typically happens every 15 days. If you notice an unexpected dip out of nowhere, it almost always points to a recent change on your account statement. Usually, this happens because of a delayed EMI payment that just got logged, a sudden spike in your credit card balances, a fresh hard pull from a newly approved credit line, or even closing down an old account that threw off your credit mix. An error in your credit report can also cause an unexpected drop. Pulling up your detailed report and understanding CIBIL score range is the quickest way to figure out precisely why the score decrease patterns happen in your specific case. The Main Reasons for A Low CIBIL Score Isolating the root cause makes it much easier to fix. Your credit health is built by various behavioral and financial markers tracked across your financial profile. To help you analyse and mend your credit health effectively, here is a complete breakdown mapping out each core factor alongside its precise solution: Reason / Cause Impact on Profile Immediate Fix Late or Missed Payments Heavily damages payment history and records severe DPD markers. Automate your bill payments and EMIs so you never miss a due date. High Credit Utilisation Maxing out your credit cards signals heavy reliance on revolving debt. Try to keep your utilisation under 30% of your total card limit. Too Many Hard Enquiries Firing off multiple credit applications all at once signals credit hunger. Space out your credit applications and check your eligibility beforehand. Defaults, Settlements, or Write-offs Choosing to settle a debt rather than paying it off leaves a long-term scar. Clear dues in full whenever possible instead of opting for settlements. Poor Credit Mix Relying only on unsecured lines can stall your score’s long-term growth. Maintain a balanced mix of secured and unsecured credit where appropriate, without taking on unnecessary debt. Short or Thin Credit History Lenders prefer a long, proven, and reliable repayment track record. Keep your oldest credit accounts open and active to anchor your credit age. Errors on the Report Clerical banking mistakes pull your score down unfairly through no fault of yours. Check your reports periodically and log a formal dispute if you spot an error. Being a Guarantor or Co-applicant If someone you co-signed for defaults, it drags your profile down with theirs. Only sign on as a co-applicant if you trust the borrower’s payment habits completely. What Does Not Lower Your Score (Common Myths) To help you take charge of your money with total confidence, let us separate fact from fiction. Here are a few widespread misconceptions worth clearing up: Checking Your Own Score Is Risk-Free: Pulling your own report counts as a soft check, which completely debunks the fear that checking CIBIL score will reduce score. Pre-Approved Offers Don’t Count: A bank quietly reviewing your profile for a pre-approved facility has zero impact on your rating. Income Isn’t a Factor: Having a high salary does not automatically boost your score because income is never part of the calculation. Closing Old Cards Can Backfire: Closing an old credit card can affect your score, particularly if it reduces your available credit or changes your credit history. How to Fix a Low CIBIL Score Improving a lagging credit score requires steady habits rather than an overnight miracle. You can easily increase your CIBIL score from 600 to 750 by following certain habits. To get your numbers moving upward again, keep these strategies in your corner: Pay Every EMI and Credit-Card Bill on Time: Build a consistent repayment record by making all your payments by their due dates. Clear Past Overdues: Pay off previous dues and make sure every upcoming bill is paid well ahead of time. Manage Your Credit Utilisation: Keep your card utilisation comfortably below the 30% ceiling. Preserve Your Credit Age: Leave older credit accounts open to anchor your credit history’s length. Limit New Applications: Avoid unnecessary credit inquiries so you never have to wonder “does checking CIBIL score reduce it?” when making financial moves. Fix Reporting Errors: Dispute errors right away through official bureau portals if you ever find yourself wondering why CIBIL score decrease notifications show up unexpectedly. There is no instant way to repair an accurately reported low score. But sticking to these routines over several months will steadily pull your credit health back into shape. Conclusion To sum up, checking your own score is completely safe and never lowers it. Usually, sudden drops happen because of missed payments, maxed-out cards, too many hard inquiries, defaults, thin credit histories, or reporting errors. Bouncing back takes time and consistency rather than an overnight fix, leaning heavily on on-time payment habits and clearing up errors. Make it a regular habit to keep tabs on your credit health. Additionally, to keep your paperwork sorted and track your financial progress on the go, you can easily grab the Tata Capital App . Disclaimer : The details shared here are for general informational use. CIBIL Scores are issued by TransUnion CIBIL. Use official channels for your credit report, disputes and other credit-related queries. FAQs Does checking the CIBIL score reduce it? No, self-checks register as soft enquiries, which carry zero impact on your score and remain visible only to you. Furthermore, the rumour that checking CIBIL score will reduce your score is entirely false. What is the difference between a soft and a hard enquiry? A soft enquiry happens when you look up your own score or a bank evaluates you for a pre-approved deal, leaving your rating untouched. A hard enquiry happens when a lender pulls your report after a formal credit application, causing a minor, temporary dip. Why did my CIBIL score suddenly drop? Your score can drop unexpectedly due to a newly posted late payment, a sudden jump in credit utilisation, a fresh hard loan pull, or a reporting mistake. Reviewing your report helps you understand exactly why CIBIL score decrease situations happen. How many times can I check my CIBIL score? You can check your CIBIL score as often as you like. Personal checks count as soft inquiries and looking up your score repeatedly will never harm your standing. Do multiple loan applications hurt my score? Yes, multiple loan applications can result in multiple hard enquiries, which may eventually affect your score. Avoid unnecessary applications and consider spacing out applications when possible. Does closing a credit card lower my score? Closing a credit card can affect your score, particularly if it reduces your available credit and increases your utilisation or changes the length of your credit history. The impact depends on your overall credit profile. How long does it take to fix a low CIBIL score? Fixing a low CIBIL score takes time. Improvement can take several months or longer, depending on the reasons for the low score, the severity of past negative information and your repayment behaviour going forward. Consistent and disciplined credit behaviour is key.
