No. HRA exemption is not available under the new tax regime. If you remain in the new regime, the HRA received from your employer becomes taxable as part of your salary income. To claim an HRA exemption, you must opt for the old tax regime and satisfy the prescribed conditions. How do I claim the HRA exemption while filing ITR? To claim HRA exemption, calculate the eligible exemption amount, report the correct salary details in your ITR, and ensure the exempt HRA is reflected in the relevant section. Keep rent receipts, rent agreement, and proof of payment safely, as these documents may be required if your return is selected for verification. Where do I show HRA in ITR-1? In ITR-1 (Sahaj), HRA exemption is reported under the salary section. Go to the schedule relating to exempt allowances under Section 10 and enter the eligible amount under Section 10(13A). After entering the details, verify that your taxable salary has been calculated correctly before submitting the return. Is the landlord PAN mandatory to claim HRA? The landlord's PAN may be required when the annual rent paid exceeds Rs. 1 lakh. If the landlord does not have a PAN, certain declarations may be needed. Taxpayers should maintain proper records and follow the latest income tax requirements while claiming the HRA exemption. Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my parents? Yes. Paying rent to parents can qualify for an HRA exemption if the arrangement is genuine. There should be actual rent payments, proper documentation, and supporting evidence such as rent receipts. The transaction should not be merely a paper arrangement created only for claiming a tax benefit. Can I claim both HRA and home loan benefits? Yes, in certain situations. For example, you may own a house in one city but live in rented accommodation in another city because of your job. In such cases, both HRA exemption and eligible home loan tax benefits may be claimed, subject to the applicable tax provisions and conditions. What if my employer did not consider my HRA? If your employer did not consider the HRA exemption while calculating TDS, you can still claim it while filing your income tax return. You will need to calculate the eligible exemption yourself, enter the correct details in the ITR, and keep all supporting rent-related documents for future reference. Which cities qualify for the 50% HRA limit? For FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai qualify for the 50% HRA limit. Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Ahmedabad have been added to the metro list from FY 2026-27. However, the expanded 8-metro classification applies only from FY 2026-27 onwards. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary The Record of Rights (ROR) is one of the most important land records used to verify details of a property. It contains information about the landholder, survey details, land classification, and other rights recorded by the revenue department. Buyers, lenders, and government authorities rely on this document during property transactions, mutation, and legal verification. Checking the ROR before purchasing a property can help you make a more informed decision and avoid unnecessary complications later. A Record of Rights (ROR) is an official revenue record that contains details about a parcel of land, including the rights recorded against it, the landholder’s details, and other important property information. Not too long ago, verifying land ownership meant going through piles of records and visiting multiple government offices. Today, much of that process has become simpler, thanks to the Record of Rights (ROR). It brings together important details about a piece of land in a single official record, making it easier to verify ownership and other property-related information. Understanding the ROR full form in land records is essential whether you are buying property, applying for a home loan , or simply checking land details. In this guide, you’ll learn the ROR meaning in land, what it contains, why it matters for property transactions and home loans, and how you can check it online. What is the full form and meaning of ROR? The ROR full form in land is Record of Rights. In simple terms, an ROR is an official land record maintained by the state revenue department for a particular parcel of land. It contains details such as the owner’s name, survey number, land area, and land type. It also records the nature and extent of the owner’s or occupant’s rights, along with any revenue, land tax, or rent payable in respect of the property. Understanding the ROR meaning in land is important because it helps establish ownership and verify key land details during property transactions. What is the Record of Rights (ROR)? The Record of Rights is a government-maintained land record that identifies who holds legal rights over a particular piece of land and describes the nature of those rights. Prepared and updated by the state revenue authorities, it plays an important role in maintaining accurate land records and supporting property administration. In the context of the record of rights in land law, the document helps establish the lawful possession and use of a property. Although it may not, by itself, be conclusive proof of title. The ROR in land is known by different names across states. For example, it is known as the 7/12 Extract in Maharashtra, RTC (Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops) or Pahani in Karnataka, Jamabandi in several northern states, and Patta/Chitta in Tamil Nadu. What does an ROR contain? A Record of Rights brings together several important details relating to a land parcel. While the exact format may differ across states, an ROR in land typically includes: Name and details of the person having rights over the land. Survey number or plot number for unique identification of the property. Land area and classification, such as agricultural, residential, or commercial land. Cultivation details, including the name of the cultivator and crop information, where applicable. Encumbrances or liabilities, such as mortgages, loans, or other claims against the land. Tenancy details, if the land has been leased or cultivated by a tenant. Mutation history, showing changes in ownership due to sale, inheritance, gift, or other transfers. What is the importance of ROR in property and home loans? Understanding the ROR meaning is important because this document helps establish who has recognized rights over a piece of land. While an ROR may not be the sole proof of ownership, it is one of the first documents checked during property transactions. The ROR in land records also plays a key role when applying for a home loan or a loan against property , as lenders review the ROR information during legal and title verification. Its importance includes: Helps verify land ownership and the rights associated with the property. Supports title verification before purchasing land or property. Acts as an important record during mutation after a sale, inheritance, or gift. Assists in resolving land disputes by providing official revenue records. Enables lenders to verify the property’s legal status before approving a home loan or a loan against property. A clear and updated ROR can make the legal verification process smoother and may help speed up loan processing. Reduces the risk of fraud by allowing lenders to cross-check important land details before approving a loan application. Also read – What Is Khasra Number How ROR is known across states: Different names Although the Record of Rights serves the same purpose across India, it is known by different names in different states. The terminology and online portals may also vary depending on the state government’s land records system. State Common Name for ROR Maharashtra 7/12 Extract (Satbara) Karnataka RTC (Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops) / Pahani Gujarat 7/12 Utara Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and other North Indian states Jamabandi / Fard West Bengal Khatian Madhya Pradesh Khatauni Tamil Nadu Patta / Chitta Telangana and Andhra Pradesh Adangal / Pahani How to check ROR/Land records online? Today, most state governments provide ROR information through their official land-records portals, making it easier for citizens to access property details without visiting revenue offices. Depending on the state, you can use portals such as Bhulekh, MahaBhulekh, Bhoomi (Karnataka), Dharani (Telangana), and other official land-record websites to view the ROR in land records. Here are the general steps you may need to follow: Visit your state’s official land-records portal. Select the district, taluk/tehsil, village, or other required location details. Enter the survey number, plot number, or owner’s name, depending on the available search options. Verify the details and submit the request. View the relevant ROR information on the screen. You can even download or print it for future reference. Also read – Land survey number: Meaning, importance ROR vs other land documents Just like a Record of Rights in land law, each document serves a specific purpose. Here’s how an ROR differs from other land documents, such as a sale deed and a mutation: Document Purpose What it contains? Record of Rights Revenue record of the land Details of the land, the person holding rights over it, land classification, liabilities, tenancy, and other revenue-related information. Sale Deed Legal transfer of ownership A registered document that records the transfer of ownership from the seller to the buyer. It is a primary title document. Mutation Update of government land records Reflects changes in ownership after a sale, inheritance, gift, or other transfer for revenue and tax purposes. Conclusion The Record of Rights (ROR) is an important document that helps verify ownership, rights, and other key details relating to the land. It is widely used in property transactions and is also reviewed by lenders when processing home loans and loans against property. Before purchasing any land or property, it is always advisable to review the ROR through the relevant state land-records portal . The ROR full form in land records is Record of Rights . It is an official land record maintained by the revenue department that contains details about a specific piece of land. A Record of Rights is a government-maintained document that captures details of a land parcel and the rights associated with it. It generally includes information about the landholder, survey number, land area, and other revenue-related details. Different states may use different names for this record. What does an ROR contain? An ROR usually contains the owner's or landholder's name, survey or plot number, land area, land classification, cultivation details, tenancy information, and any liabilities linked to the property. It may also show changes in ownership through mutation entries recorded by the revenue authorities. Why is ROR important for a home loan? When you apply for a home loan, lenders often review the ROR as part of the property's legal verification process. The document helps them understand who holds rights over the land and whether there are any recorded issues. A clear and updated ROR can make verification easier. What is ROR called in different states? The same land record is known by different names across India. income tax you may save on your home loan during a financial year. These benefits are available under Sections 24(B), 80C, and 80EEA (if applicable). The tool also makes it easier to compare the old and new tax regimes for better financial planning. To use a home loan tax calculator, you will need details such as home loan amount, interest rate, tenure, your annual income, and tax regime, among others. A home loan tax benefit calculator is an online tool that estimates the income tax savings you may receive on your home loan based on your loan details, income, and applicable tax regime. A home loan not only helps you buy your dream home but can also reduce your income tax liability. However, the tax benefits are spread across different sections of the Income Tax Act, with separate limits and conditions for interest and principal repayment. Calculating these savings manually can become confusing very quickly, especially if you’re unsure which tax regime applies to you. This is where a home loan tax benefit calculator becomes useful. It estimates your potential tax savings in just a few clicks, making financial planning much easier. In this guide, we’ll explain how you can calculate the tax benefit on a home loan calculator, what information it provides, and the benefits of using this calculator. What is a home loan tax benefit calculator? A home loan tax benefit calculator is a free online tool that estimates how much income tax you may save on your home loan during a financial year. It works by using details such as your loan amount, interest paid, principal repaid, annual income, and the tax regime you have chosen. A home loan tax calculator helps you understand your likely tax benefits quickly, without having to calculate the deductions manually. What are the tax benefits that a home loan tax calculator helps you estimate? A home loan tax benefit calculator helps you estimate the total amount you can claim as a tax deduction on your home loan in a given financial year under various sections of the Income Tax Act. You can calculate the following tax benefits on a home loan calculator: Section Benefit covered Maximum deduction allowed Section 24(B) Deduction on home loan interest for a self-occupied property. Up to Rs. 2 lakh Section 80C Deduction on principal repayment of the home loan. Up to Rs. 1.5 lakh Section 80EEA Additional deduction on interest for eligible affordable housing loans. Up to Rs. 1.5 lakh Important: The deduction limits, eligibility conditions, and tax regime rules may change through amendments in the Income Tax Act. Always verify the latest provisions before relying on any calculation. Old vs new tax regime: Why does it matter for the calculator? The tax regime you choose has a direct impact on your home loan tax savings. Most deductions related to a self-occupied home, including those under Sections 24(b), 80C, and 80EEA, are generally available only under the old tax regime. The new tax regime largely does not allow deductions, except on the full interest paid on a rental property. A good home loan tax saving calculator also compares your estimated tax liability under both regimes so you understand which option offers greater overall tax savings. Also Read – Tax Benefits on Home Loan What are the details you need before using the calculator? You must keep the following details ready before you begin using a home loan tax benefit calculator: Home loan amount Interest rate on the loan Loan tenure Annual interest paid during the financial year Annual principal repaid (available in your loan interest certificate or amortization schedule) Gross annual income Tax regime selected (old or new) Whether the property is self-occupied or rented Entering the correct details helps the calculator provide a more reliable estimate of your potential tax savings. How to use a home loan tax benefit calculator: Step-by-step A home loan tax calculator is a simple-to-use, online tool. All you have to do is enter a few values, choose your tax regime, and click on the “Calculate” button. Your estimated tax savings will be displayed within a few seconds. Here’s a step-by-step guide to calculate the tax benefit on a home loan calculator: Open the house loan tax benefit calculator page. Fill in your home loan details. These include the loan amount, applicable interest rate, and tenure. Enter your gross annual income so the calculator can estimate your tax liability more accurately. Select whether you have opted for the old tax regime or the new tax regime. The deductions are available only under the old tax regime. Specify whether the property is self-occupied or rented. Click on the “Calculate” button. Your estimated home loan tax benefits under the applicable sections (24(B), 80C, and 80EEA) will be displayed on your screen. Also Read – Home Loan Disbursement Process How to understand your calculator results? Once the calculation is complete, the results are fairly easy to interpret. A house loan tax benefit calculator usually shows the deduction available on your home loan interest under Section 24(B), the deduction on principal repayment under Section 80C, and any additional benefit available under Section 80EEA (if applicable). It also displays the total reduction in your taxable income and the estimated tax savings based on your income tax slab. Remember, these figures are only indicative estimates and should not be treated as your final tax computation for your income tax return. How to calculate home loan tax savings? Explained through an example Let’s understand the calculation of home loan tax savings through an illustrative example. Suppose a home loan borrower has the following details: Annual home loan interest paid – Rs. 2.5 lakh Annual home loan principal repaid – Rs. 4 lakh Tax regime – Old tax regime Income tax slab – 30% Under Section 24(B), the maximum deduction allowed on home loan interest for a self-occupied property is Rs. 2 lakh. Since the borrower paid Rs. 2.5 lakh in interest, only Rs. 2 lakh of it can be claimed as a deduction, even though the actual interest paid was higher. Under Section 80C, the maximum deduction allowed is Rs. 1.5 lakh, and this limit is shared across all eligible investments under the section, not just home loan principal repayment. So even though the borrower repaid Rs. 4 lakh in principal, only Rs. 1.5 lakh of it can be claimed (assuming no other 80C investments exist). Adding these together, the borrower’s total tax deduction for the year is Rs. 2 lakh (Section 24(B)) + Rs. 1.5 lakh (Section 80C) = Rs. 3.5 lakh. Considering the 30% tax slab, a deduction of Rs. 3.5 lakh could translate into an approximate tax saving of Rs. 1.05 lakh, excluding surcharge and cess. Note: This is only an illustrative example to explain the calculation. For a more accurate estimate, use a home loan tax benefit calculator, and consult a tax professional if required. What are the benefits of using a home loan tax benefit calculator? A home loan tax saving calculator allows you to estimate your home loan tax benefits without delving into complex mathematical calculations. Here are the advantages of using this tool: Provides instant estimates of your home loan tax savings. Eliminates the chances of manual calculation errors. Helps you compare tax benefits under the old and new tax regimes. Makes tax and financial planning easier. The calculator is available online for free. You can use it as many times as you want. Conclusion A home loan tax benefit calculator is an easy-to-use, online tool that can help you estimate your potential tax savings before filing your income tax return. It can even help you plan your finances more effectively and maximize available deductions. You can explore the Tata Capital Home Loan solutions and Home Loan Calculators to simplify your planning. Always remember: calculator results are only estimates. Always verify the latest tax provisions and consult a qualified tax advisor before making financial decisions. How do I use a home loan tax benefit calculator? Using the calculator is simple. The calculator then provides an estimate of the deductions and possible tax savings based on the information you entered. What tax benefits can I claim on a home loan? Eligible home loan borrowers may claim deductions on the interest paid, principal repaid, and, in certain cases, additional interest for affordable housing. The exact benefit depends on your eligibility, the type of property, and the tax regime you have selected for that financial year. Is the home loan tax benefit available under the new tax regime? Since tax rules may change over time, it is always advisable to check the latest provisions before making your tax calculations. Is the calculator result the exact tax I will save? No. A home loan tax benefit calculator only provides an estimate based on the details you enter. Your actual tax savings may vary based on your overall financial situation, applicable deductions, and the latest income tax rules. Your final tax liability is determined when you file your income tax return. Can co-borrowers each claim home loan tax benefits? Yes, co-borrowers may claim home loan tax benefits if they are also co-owners of the property and have actually contributed towards repaying the loan. Each person's deduction depends on their share in the loan repayment and the conditions laid down under the Income Tax Act. Does the calculator include Section 80EEA benefits? Many home loan tax benefit calculators also consider Section 80EEA if you enter details that meet the required conditions. However, the deduction is available only for eligible borrowers and properties. The calculator usually applies it only when the relevant eligibility criteria are satisfied. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A construction-perm loan is a single loan that funds home construction in stages and then converts into a long-term mortgage once the construction is complete, without a second application or closing. Building a home usually means juggling two separate loans: one to fund construction and another to pay it off once the house is complete. A construction-perm loan removes that extra step by combining both stages into a single loan that converts automatically into a standard mortgage once the construction is finished. This structure affects everything from the number of closings you go through to how construction-to-perm loan rates are set and locked in. Understanding what a construction-perm loan is, how it works, and how it differs from other construction financing options helps you judge it fairly before you commit to a builder or a lender. How does a construction-to-permanent loan work? A construction-perm loan moves through two distinct stages before it starts to behave like a typical home loan . Construction phase Funds are released in stages, known as draws, tied to milestones such as the foundation, framing, and interior work. Each draw is paid directly to the builder, and you typically make interest-only payments on the amount drawn so far rather than on the full loan. Conversion phase Once construction is complete, the loan converts automatically into a standard mortgage, often referred to simply as a perm loan, with a fixed or adjustable-rate principal-and-interest structure and no second application or closing to go through. This single-close structure is one reason construction-to-perm loan rates are often locked in earlier than they would be with two separate loans. Also Read – What are the documents required for a home loan? Construction-to-permanent loan rates Construction-to-permanent loan rates are often slightly higher than those for a standard home purchase mortgage because the lender takes on additional risk during the construction phase. Depending on the lender, the rate may be locked in at closing or remain adjustable until the loan converts into a permanent mortgage. The rate you receive also depends on factors such as the lender’s policies, your credit profile, and the loan-to-cost ratio. Comparing offers from multiple lenders is important, since rates and terms can vary considerably rather than following a single standard. Construction-to-permanent loan vs. mini-perm loan The terms construction-to-permanent loan and mini-perm loan often surface in the same search results, but they describe two different products built for two different types of borrowers. Feature Construction-perm loan Mini-perm loan Borrower type Individual homebuyers Owners or developers of commercial property Purpose Finances the build of a single-family home Bridges construction financing on an income-producing property Term Converts directly into a long-term mortgage Medium term, typically two to five years End goal Long-term residential mortgage Refinance into a full permanent commercial loan Pros and cons of a construction-to-permanent loan Weighing this loan type against separate construction and mortgage financing comes down to a short list of trade-offs. Pros: A single closing saves time and reduces closing costs compared to two separate loans. The rate can often be locked in before construction even starts. There is no need to re-qualify for a mortgage once building is complete. Cons: Rates tend to be higher than those on a standard mortgage. Qualification requirements tend to be stricter, including a higher credit score , a larger down payment, and an approved builder or contractor with finalized building plans. These loans are typically limited to single-family primary residences rather than multi-family or investment properties. Who should consider a construction-to-permanent loan? A construction-perm loan tends to suit a fairly specific type of borrower rather than every homebuilder. You are building a single-family home that will be your primary residence. You already have a clear construction plan and an approved builder or contractor. You have completed, or can complete, an appraisal and per test before applying. You want financing certainty settled upfront instead of reapplying for a mortgage after construction ends. Also Read – When should you avoid taking a loan against property Conclusion To recap what is a construction-perm loan: it combines construction financing and the eventual mortgage into one loan and one closing. This makes it worth comparing against separate construction and perm loan financing based on rate, closing costs, and qualification requirements before you decide. Speak with a lender to understand your eligibility. Rates, terms, and eligibility criteria vary by lender and are subject to change. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Section 80C of the Income Tax Act lets individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) lower their taxable income with a deduction of Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year under the old tax regime. The 80C deduction list includes investments and expenses such as Equity-Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS), Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP), Public Provident Fund (PPF), life insurance premiums, and home loan principal repayment. Section 80C is a tax-saving provision under the Income Tax Act, 1961. It allows you to claim deductions of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh every financial year. If your goal is to save taxes, you must understand the provisions of Section 80C. It lets you claim a deduction of up to Rs 1.5 lakh in a tax year under the old tax regime. This blog explains the limit, eligible investments, who can claim deductions, and whether you must choose it. What is Section 80C? Section 80C is a tax deduction under the old tax regime that allows individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) to reduce their taxable income by up to Rs 1.5 lakh in a tax year through eligible investments and expenses. It reduces the gross total income. However, it is not a tax credit or a tax refund. Also Read – Income tax slabs & rates in India for FY 2026-27 Section 80C deduction list: What qualifies? The qualifying 80C deduction list is given in the table below: Eligible investment/expense Type Key conditions/lock-in Public Provident Fund (PPF) Investment 15-year maturity (partial withdrawals allowed as per rules) Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) Investment Eligible employee contribution; subject to EPF rules Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) Investment 3-year lock-in Life insurance premium Investment Premium must meet Income Tax Act conditions National Savings Certificate (NSC) Investment 5-year lock-in Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) Investment Account must meet scheme rules; long-term lock-in until maturity/eligible withdrawal Senior Citizens’ Savings Scheme (SCSS) Investment 5-year maturity (extendable as per scheme rules) 5-year tax-saving fixed deposit Investment 5-year lock-in Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP) Investment Subject to prescribed tax conditions and policy rules National Pension System (NPS) – Section 80CCD(1) Investment Counts within the combined Rs 1.5 lakh limit Children’s tuition fees Expense Tuition fees for up to two children, subject to prescribed conditions Home loan principal repayment Expense Eligible for a self-occupied or let-out residential house, subject to conditions Stamp duty and registration charges Expense Allowed in the year paid, within the overall deduction limit and subject to conditions Is Section 80C still available in 2026? Section 80C is still available in 2026 under the old tax regime. However, since the new tax regime is the default, many taxpayers cannot claim this deduction. Under the Income Tax Act 2025, effective 1 April 2026, Section 80C is now Section 123 read with Schedule XV. The Rs. 1.5 lakh limit and eligible investments remain the same. Also Read – FD vs. mutual funds Old regime vs New regime: Is Section 80C still worth it? The following table compares the tax treatment under the old and new regimes for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27). Gross annual income New tax regime (with standard deduction) Old tax regime (with full Rs. 1.5 lakh Section 80C deduction and standard deduction) Which is lower? Rs. 10 lakh Nil (after standard deduction and rebate, if eligible) Nil Both are the same Rs. 15 lakh ~Rs. 97,500 ~Rs. 2,10,600 New regime Rs. 20 lakh ~Rs. 1,92,400 ~Rs. 3,66,600 New regime The new tax regime now gives a lower tax bill for many taxpayers even if they fully use the Rs 1.5 lakh Section 80C deduction under the old regime. Thus, before investing in a 5-year tax-saving FD or an insurance policy only to save tax, compare your tax under both regimes. You must calculate your own numbers or consult a Chartered Accountant. Also Read – Difference between tax deduction and tax exemption What is Section 80C under the new Income Tax Act 2025 (Now Section 123)? From 1 April 2026, several tax deduction sections have been renumbered under the Income Tax Act 2025. However, this is only a structural change. The deduction limits, eligibility rules, and old-regime-only condition remain the same. Tax forms, notices, and calculation tools will now use the new section numbers given below. Old Section New Section (Income Tax Act 2025) Section 80C Section 123 Section 80CCD Section 124 Section 80D Section 126 Section 80E Section 129 Section 80G Section 133 Section 87A Section 156 How to claim deduction under Section 80C? The step-by-step process to claim income tax Section 80C deductions is as follows: Confirm that you have chosen the old tax regime. Gather proofs such as your PPF passbook, LIC premium receipts, ELSS statements, and home loan principal certificate from your lender. Declare eligible investments to your employer for TDS or claim them while filing your ITR. Keep all documents safely for future verification, if required. Also Read – How to save tax for a salary above 50 lakhs What are the common mistakes when claiming 80C deductions? Assuming Rs. 1.5 lakh is a separate limit for Sections 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1). Confusing home loan principal (Section 80C) with home loan interest (Section 24(b)). Claiming Section 80C deductions under the new tax regime. Buying insurance only to save tax. Ignoring the five-year property-sale reversal rule. Forgetting that EPF contributions already use part of the Rs. 1.5 lakh limit. Conclusion Section 80C can help you save tax, but only if you choose the old tax regime. Before investing, compare your tax under both regimes, understand the eligible deductions, and invest based on your financial goals and not just to save tax. Section 80C is a tax deduction that lets eligible individuals and HUFs reduce their taxable income by up to Rs 1.5 lakh under the old tax regime. What is the maximum deduction under Section 80C? The maximum deduction under 80C is Rs 1.5 lakh in a tax year. What is included in the 80C deduction list? The list of eligible deductions under 80C includes PPF, EPF, ELSS, life insurance premiums, NSC, SSY, SCSS, 5-year tax-saving FDs, ULIPs, NPS under Section 80CCD(1), children’s tuition fees, home loan principal repayment, and stamp duty and registration charges. Can I claim 80C under the new tax regime? No. Section 80C is available only under the old tax regime. Is Section 80C still valid after the Income Tax Act 2025? Yes. The Income Tax Act 2025, effective 1 April 2026, has renumbered Section 80C as Section 123. However, the deduction limit and eligible investments remain the same. Does home loan principal repayment qualify under 80C? Yes. Home loan principal repayment qualifies if you fulfill the conditions of the Income Tax Act. Who is eligible to claim a deduction under Section 80C? Individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who opt for the old tax regime can claim the deduction for eligible investments. Is the Rs 1.5 lakh limit separate for 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD? No. Rs 1.5 lakh is the combined limit for Sections 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1). It is not a separate limit for each section. High Mark. Lenders evaluate the credit reports from one or more of these bureaus before approving your loan. The Equifax credit score, Experian, and CIBIL score usually range from 300 to 900. However, they differ based on levels of trust, update speeds, and data rules. TransUnion CIBIL is the oldest and most trusted credit bureau, Experian is a major global bureau, while Equifax is known for data analytics. Experian, CIBIL, CRIF High Mark, and Equifax credit scores are important factors lenders consider for loan approval. These scores are generated by collecting financial data. India has four RBI-licensed credit bureaus: Experian, CIBIL (TransUnion), Equifax, and CRIF High Mark. Each bureau generates its own credit score , which often confuses borrowers. This guide explains the Experian Credit score , Equifax credit score, why scores differ across bureaus, and which one matters most to lenders. Which are India’s four credit bureaus? An overview CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and High Mark (CRIF) collect credit data from lenders to generate credit reports and scores under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005. Credit bureau Brief introduction TransUnion CIBIL India’s oldest and most widely used credit bureau. Experian India A global credit bureau offering credit reports and scores. Equifax India It provides credit information and credit scores. CRIF High Mark It offers credit reports for individuals and businesses. What is the CIBIL score? CIBIL (TransUnion CIBIL) is the oldest credit bureau in India and most widely used by lenders. Its CIBIL score ranges from 300 to 900 , wherein a score of 750 or above is generally considered good. Since most lenders check this score, “CIBIL score” is often used as a general term for credit scores in India. What is the Experian credit score? Experian India also provides a credit score ranging from 300 to 900. Like the TransUnion CIBIL score, the Experian CIBIL score is based on your credit history. However, Experian may use a different scoring model and receive data from some lenders that CIBIL does not, and vice versa. What is the Equifax credit score? The Equifax credit score is provided by Equifax India and ranges from 1 to 999. This range is the primary difference between Equifax and Experian. Some banks and NBFCs use the Equifax credit score as an alternative or additional check when assessing loan applications. Also Read – CIBIL score vs. credit score CIBIL vs Experian vs Equifax: What are the key differences? The following table highlights the differences between CIBIL and Experian and the differences between Equifax and Experian. Feature TransUnion CIBIL Experian India Equifax India CRIF High Mark Parent company TransUnion Experian plc Equifax Inc. CRIF S.p.A. Score range 300-900 300-900 1-999 300-900 Data sources Varies by lender reporting Varies by lender reporting Varies by lender reporting Varies by lender reporting Lender preference Most widely used by banks and NBFCs Used by some lenders Used by some lenders Used by some lenders Why are your CIBIL and Experian scores different? If you are wondering why Experian and CIBIL scores are different for you, here are the simple reasons: Different lender reporting: Not all lenders report to every bureau. Different scoring models: Each bureau uses its own scoring method. Update timing: Credit information may be updated on different dates. Dispute status: A corrected error may appear in one bureau before another. Also Read – Credit Rating vs. Credit Score Which credit score do lenders check? Most banks and NBFCs in India commonly check the CIBIL score when evaluating a loan application. However, some lenders use Experian, Equifax, or CRIF High Mark as their primary bureau or as an additional check. To improve your loan approval chances, you must maintain a healthy credit score across all four credit bureaus , not just CIBIL. How to check your credit score across all bureaus? You can check your credit score on the official websites of the different bureaus. Each bureau offers one free credit report every year, as per the RBI mandate. Check all four reports periodically to spot errors or score differences and raise disputes if needed. What are the tips to improve your credit score across all bureaus? If you want to improve your credit score across all bureaus, here are some tips to follow: Pay bills and dues on time: Never miss EMI or credit card payments. Keep usage low: Use less than 30% of your credit limit. Limit applications: Avoid multiple loan inquiries within a short time. Check reports: Review all bureau reports and dispute errors promptly. Maintain balance: Keep a healthy mix of secured and unsecured credit. Eligible borrowers can opt for Tata Capital Personal Loans and Business Loans to meet funding needs responsibly. Conclusion CIBIL is India’s most widely used credit bureau. However, the others, such as Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark, also matter. The scores of different bureaus vary because of data coverage and scoring methods. You must try to maintain a healthy score across all bureaus. Khasra numbers. A Khasra number is an essential term related to land records in India. A person planning to invest in a plot of land in India should therefore be aware of – what is a Khasra numberand other critical terms associated with it. For instance, what is a Khata number? This article will help land buyers get information about Khasra numbers, key related aspects, and how to obtain them. What is Khasra Number? Meaning & Definition Khasra is a Persian term that implies a unique number assigned to a plot or a piece of land in a rural area. It is also called a DAG number. A plot or survey number is assigned to identify land in urban India. Likewise, an identification number gets assigned to a plot or a piece of land in rural areas across the country. This unique identification number is the Khasra number. The local revenue department authorities allocate the Khasra number to the relevant rural area. Also, read – Can you claim home loan interest tax benefits before possession? How does a buyer know what is the Khasra number of lands? The buyer can get the information about the Khasra number from a document called ‘Sharja.’ A Sharja is a complete map of the entire land in a village. It is an important document, as this map is considered for assigning the Khasra number to each piece of land in that village. A Lehkpal prepares the Sharja, while a Patwari is designated to provide the Khasra number and update land records accordingly. A buyer must know that a Khasra number and the plot number need not always be the same. If the plot or piece of land gets subsequently divided, sold, or gifted, then the Khasra number changes accordingly. To better understand the Khasra number of land, where land gets divided, sold or gifted post mutation of the transaction, consider the example below. Suppose for a plot of land, 54 is the assigned Khasra number. The land later gets divided into three parts. So, the three parcels of land will have Khasra numbers allotted as 54/1, 54/2 and 54/3. Also, read – Token money: Meaning, purpose & important things to know Importance & Uses of Khasra Number in Land Records A Khasra number is needed to get rights over a property in a rural area. Through a Khasra number, a prospective buyer can get exhaustive details about a plot over the last 50 years, including details of Plot ownership over the last 50 years Plot area Quality of the soil on the said plot Land cultivation pattern Plot’s geography Number of trees within the vicinity of the plot Leases and mortgages on the plot Any official communication related to the plot Through knowledge of the Khasra number of land, prospective buyers and revenue authorities can prevent land fraud and other unauthorized activities to a great extent in the rural sector in India. Similarly, a Khasra number holds relevance even when taking a home loan , as it gets checked before approval. A Kasra number helps the lender evaluate a prospective buyer’s creditworthiness and their properties. Also, read – Pledge vs hypothecation vs mortgage: Key differences What is a Khata Number? Another key term associated with land records in the rural sector is the Khata number. Now, what is a Khata number? Also known as the Khewat number, it implies joint ownership of a plot or a piece of land. With the Khata number, any person can know the current joint owners of a parcel of land and their total land ownership. Like how the Khasra number works, a Khata number is also not fixed for any plot or piece of land. When any joint owner sells a property, the Khata number gets re-assigned. For example, suppose a husband and wife jointly own a piece of land with the Khata number assigned as 10. They sell it to other individuals with Khata number 7. In that case, the new landowners will have updated Khata number 10 assigned. Also, read – How to Apply for GPRA Accommodation via eSampada and eAwas Difference Between Khasra Number, Khata Number, and Khatauni Number Khasra Number: This refers to the unique identifier allotted to an individual land parcel in rural areas. The Khasra numbe’s meaning lies in its role as a plot-specific record that defines boundaries, size, and location, much like survey numbers in urban areas. Khata Number: The Khata number meaning relates to the landholder’s account in the revenue records. It groups all plots owned jointly or individually and updates with every ownership change, offering a clear picture of total landholdings. Khatauni Number: The Khatauni number difference comes from its focus on cultivation details, recording who cultivates which plots across multiple khasra numbers, along with crop and usage information. Together, these land record numbers simplify verification, and understanding Khasra vs Khata vs Khatauni helps ensure clarity during property checks and lender transactions. In rural regions, it serves as an essential record for verifying land history and ensuring transparency during property transactions. Its relevance extends beyond documentation, as lenders often rely on accurate land records for loan approvals . Providing the correct Khasra for home loan applications helps assess ownership authenticity and reduces the risk of disputes. Understanding Khasra-based land ownership is therefore vital for anyone planning to mortgage agricultural or rural land. Its importance lies in offering clarity, trust, and legal certainty throughout the loan and property assessment process. Also, read – Home Loan Insurance Benefits for New Home Buyers How to get a Khasra Number assigned? A Khasra number can be obtained both online and offline. In India, now most states have adopted digitized land records. As such, the Khasra number can be easily obtained by visiting the official website of the revenue department of the state. Each state would have its land record name and website link. For example, in the State of Karnataka, the land record is called Bhoomi. Likewise, one can also visit the local Tehsildar’s office to obtain these records offline. Wrapping up A Khasra number is a unique identification number allotted to a plot or a piece of land in rural India. Buyers, therefore, must be aware of the Khasra number and its relevance as property owners. Prospective buyers can access all details of a particular property through the Khasra number, both offline and online. Yes, you can obtain the Khasra Number for your land online by visiting the official revenue department website or the land records portal for your state. Is the Khasra number the same across all states in India? No, the Khasra number system can vary by state. Each state has its own unique format, but it serves the same purpose of identifying land parcels in the rural area. What can I do to get the Khasra Number of my Property? To get your Khasra Number, you can check online through state government portals or visit the local tehsil office to check the records. Who prepares Khasra/Khatauni documents? The Khasra/Khatauni documents are created by the Patwari. Why does the government assign the Khasra Number to land parcels? The Khasra Number helps identify, track, and manage land parcels in rural areas, ensuring accurate record-keeping for taxation, development, and legal purposes. What are the details included in Khasra? The Khasra document includes the details of the owner, Khasra Number, area of the land, and information about soil type, crops, and soil testing status. What documents are required to find khasra number? You can find your Khasra details using basic land ownership papers such as the sale deed, previous land tax receipts, or the jamabandi record. These identifiers help you locate and verify the correct land parcel, especially when checking records at local revenue offices or using digital portals that show the khasra number online . Can khasra number help in a home loan approval? Yes, a Khasra number helps a lender confirm land ownership and validate property boundaries during loan assessment. It supports due diligence by ensuring the land parcel is genuine and free from disputes. If you already know how to check the khasra number , it becomes easier to share accurate details with the lender for faster verification. What is khasra number mutation? Khasra number mutation is the official update of land ownership records after a sale, inheritance, or gift. This step is essential for maintaining clear ownership and avoiding disputes during property dealings. meet major expenses like buying a house, funding education, starting a business, and more. How can borrowers ensure they can access funding from lenders when needed? This is where your credit score comes in. A credit score is a number that indicates how likely a person is to pay back a loan and is based on their previous financial and loan repayment history. A higher credit score indicates a better chance of getting loan requests approved and with better terms. The oldest and most popular credit score in India is the TransUnion CIBIL score. This is a three-digit number with a credit score range between 300 and 900. Anything above 700 is considered to be a good credit score, reflecting the borrower’s repayment capacity and creditworthiness. When checking your CIBIL credit score, you may come across a portion that says “written off” in your CIBIL report. This can negatively impact credit scores and hamper your ability to avail yourself of loans . However, a CIBIL write-off can be removed from your report. In this article, we will explore written off meaning in loan and how you can change it. Written Off Meaning in CIBIL: What Does It Indicate? What is written off in CIBIL report? Written off meaning in loan indicates that the borrower has failed to make payments against their outstanding loan for over three months. When an individual cannot repay their loan, the lender can “write off” the borrowed funds. This status on a CIBIL report can adversely affect an individual’s eligibility for loans in the future. Lenders often check a person’s credit history when lending. When they come across a CIBIL written off, it indicates that the borrower has been unable to make repayments against their loans and makes them a defaulter candidate. Additionally, it can severely impact the borrower’s credit score and cause it to drop below the desired level. What Causes a Loan or Credit Card to be Written Off in CIBIL? Once you understand what is written off in CIBIL and its causes, you can take necessary steps to avoid it. Various reasons due to which your loan or credit card might get written off in CIBIL report include: Repeatedly missing monthly instalment payments. Ignoring repayment reminders that your lenders send you. Not settling payments against outstanding loans or credit card dues for more than 3 months. Removal of bad loans by lenders from their active books for accounting purposes while the debt remains legally owed. How to Remove Written-Off Status from CIBIL? When reviewing your CIBIL report, it is essential to examine each aspect carefully. Incorrect information can often lead to a status of “written off” in CIBIL reports, and closed accounts may also be mistakenly marked as “written off”.” Once you have determined that no errors have been made, you must contact your lender to start removing a “written off” status. CIBIL cannot make the change independently, so contacting lenders is the first and most crucial step. You can then proceed with the following steps to remove a written-off status on your CIBIL report: 1. Contact the lender Start by contacting the lender from whom you borrowed the loan and get the exact amount you owe them. 2. Negotiate a repayment plan Once you have reached out, discuss how the outstanding amount can be repaid. You can also negotiate a repayment plan that suits you and the lender. Make sure to settle the total amount. 3. Get a “No Dues Certificate” After the loan has been settled in full, you can request a “No Dues Certificate” from the lender. This is a formal document stating that all dues have been cleared. 4. Inform the credit bureau The lender should then update the credit bureau with the new loan status. 5. Raise a dispute If the lender delays or fails to update the credit bureau, you can directly contact them and dispute the write-off on your report. 6. Provide the necessary documents and follow up You must show supporting documents (such as the “No Dues Certificate”) when raising a dispute. Keep following up with the bureau until the written-off status is removed from your CIBIL report. How Long Does the Written Off Status Stay on Your CIBIL Report? The status of written-off in CIBIL report remains for up to seven years from the date of reporting, even if you repay the outstanding dues during this period. This extended duration significantly impacts your financial credibility and borrowing capacity. During this time, lenders will continue to see this negative mark whenever they review your credit report for loan or credit card applications. Even after you repay the full outstanding amount and obtain a No Dues Certificate from your lender, the account may be marked as ‘settled’ rather than ‘closed,’ which still indicates incomplete repayment. But the good thing is that the impact diminishes over time, especially when you demonstrate responsible credit behaviour by making timely payments on other loans or credit cards. How to Avoid Written-Off Status in CIBIL Report? Getting a CIBIL write-off removed can be a challenging and lengthy process. Rebuilding your credit score can also become difficult. To avoid these problems, there are specific steps an individual can take to prevent a write-off in the first place. This includes: – Assess your ability to repay monthly loan instalments before applying to lenders. – Research different loan options to find the one best suited to your needs. It is easier to apply for and repay loans that have low interest rates and longer repayment tenures. – After applying, make sure to carefully read loan agreements. This can indicate if the lender has any hidden charges or fees that may increase your repayment amount. – Budget your expenses every month and try not to exceed it. – Create a budget and stick to it to control any unnecessary expenses. – In case there is a risk of defaulting on your loan, contact your lender as soon as possible. This can help you uncover solutions that are beneficial to the borrower and lender. How to Improve Your Credit Score After a Write-Off? Late loan payments, settled dues, and “written off” statuses can negatively impact your credit score, making it difficult to avail of loans and other financial necessities in the future. However, individuals can take certain steps to rebuild their credit scores, whether that is a CIBIL rating, Experian credit score , or others. Credit bureaus typically assign credit scores after collecting information about borrowers from the relevant financial institutions or lenders. The parameters that affect your credit score include loan repayment history, the amount owed, credit utilization ratio, the number of loans availed, and the length of your credit history. Making regular full repayments on your credit card, taking out and paying back small loans in full, ensuring your credit utilization ratio is low, and maintaining your repayment history can help rebuild your credit score. List of Common Errors That Can Lead to a Wrong Written Off Status Here are some common errors that can lead to the status of written off in CIBIL report: Incorrect Personal Information: Errors in name, address, age, date of birth, and PAN details. Closed Account Marked as Written-Off: A closed account incorrectly labeled as written-off by the lender. Delay in Balance Updates: Cleared dues not updated on the CIBIL report. Incorrect Days Past Due (DPD): Wrong DPD suggesting delayed payments when payments were made on time. Conclusion CIBIL ratings are crucial in determining an individual’s ability to avail of loans, funding, credit cards, and more. While unforeseen circumstances can negatively impact credit scores, it is important to remember that the score can always be rebuilt. Are you looking to meet your financial goals, improve your credit score, or obtain loans to meet your requirements? The right guidance can help ensure that you do not face unnecessary challenges like CIBIL write-offs along the way. Tata Capital can offer expert guidance, ensuring you achieve your personal and financial goals. FAQs What is written off in CIBIL report? Written off meaning in loan indicates the borrower has failed to settle outstanding loan or credit card dues for over three months. The lender removes the amount from their books as an asset and reports it to CIBIL. Is it possible to remove written off status from CIBIL? Yes, it’s possible. You can clear the outstanding amount by reaching a settlement with the lender, obtain a No Dues Certificate, and then ask for the credit report to be updated accordingly. How long does written off stay in CIBIL report? The written-off status remains on your CIBIL report for up to 7 years from the date of reporting. However, the negative impact on your creditworthiness reduces, particularly when you show responsible credit behaviour. Difference between written off and settled in CIBIL? In CIBIL, “settled” means partial repayment by the borrower upon agreement with the lender, while written off meaning in loan means the lender closed the loan due to non-payment. Can a written off loan affect my future loan eligibility? Yes, written-off in CIBIL remains on your credit report for 7 years. It negatively impacts your credit score, signals high risk to lenders, and reduces your chances of getting future loans. How should I dispute a wrong written off entry? To dispute a wrong written off entry, raise a dispute on the CIBIL portal, submit supporting documents proving timely repayment. Additionally, follow up with both the lender and CIBIL until the incorrect written-off status is corrected. How soon will my CIBIL score recover after paying a written off loan? Paying or settling a written-off account does not erase it from your CIBIL report immediately. The status changes to “settled” and continues to appear on your credit history for up to seven years. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Understanding how to get a CIBIL score in India is simple. Your CIBIL score is based on your credit history. You can establish it by using a credit card, taking a small loan, or using a secured credit product. However, you must make all your payments on time. Checking the CIBIL score is also easy. You can use the official CIBIL website, major banking apps, or financial aggregator websites. They are free to use and provide results instantly. You will need to enter basic details like your name, date of birth, and PAN Card number. If you want to know how to find a CIBIL score in India, you can visit the official CIBIL website, use major banking apps, or financial aggregator websites. A credit score decides your repayment ability and creditworthiness. An individual aims to maintain a score of 700 or above to get easier loan access and better interest rates. However, you might not have a prior CIBIL score if you haven’t availed of any credit yet. But it is necessary to build the score for the future. A good score is required whether you want to apply for a home loan or a credit card. So, how to build a credit score for the first time? This blog takes you through an extensive process of building your credit score for secure loan access in the future. Why does a credit score matter and what is it used for? A credit score is more than securing a credit card or a loan. It also opens up financial opportunities. When you have a good CIBIL history, you qualify for a higher credit limit , lower interest, and purchase your dream home. On the contrary, if you have a poor payment pattern, it reflects as a red flag and reflects on your credit score. Read More – CIBIL score vs. credit score Who are New-to-Credit (NTC) borrowers? New-to-Credit (NTC) borrowers are individuals who have little or no credit history. As a result, they do not yet have a credit score. It is challenging for lenders to evaluate the repayment behavior of such borrowers due to the limited information. Understanding their creditworthiness isn’t easy. The common examples of NTC borrowers include : First-time credit card users People applying for their first loan Young professionals starting their credit journey Individuals who have never used formal credit products If you are wondering how do I establish credit for the first time, you are most likely an NTC borrower. You must use credit responsibly to gradually build a credit history and establish a healthy credit score. How to generate a CIBIL score for the first time? If you are just starting, it can be difficult to build a CIBIL score. In such a case, how do you build trust that your payments will be on time? Here are the most effective ways to build a credit score: Step 1: Get a secured credit card The best way to build your credit score is to get a secured credit card . This is a starting point supported by a cash deposit. The amount of the deposit equals your credit limit. Since this card is issued instead of a collateral or security deposit, you can easily get it. Step 2: Do not apply for multiple cards Applying for multiple credit cards doesn’t help when you are just starting to build a credit score. If you require more than one card, maintain a gap of at least six months. Remember, consistent applications can make you seem loan-hungry. It is best to avoid such practice. Also, it is beneficial to research extensively and apply for a credit card that best matches your requirements. Step 3: Pay your EMI on time A single EMI missed can impact your credit score. To make sure that all bills are paid on time, you can create an auto-debit facility in your account. In case you don’t want to choose an auto-debit option, set a reminder so you can pay the minimum balance on time. This will help ascertain that your EMI is paid without default. Read More – How To Increase Credit Card Limit Step 4: Apply for an unsecured credit card You can use a secured card for the initial six months. This will help get enough data for the bureaus to prepare a credit report. If you are able to create a strong report, the bank will be ready to offer you an unsecured credit card. Switching from a secured to an unsecured comes with additional benefits, including an increase in your credit score. Step 5: Use a Pay Later option Many banks have introduced a Buy Now Pay Later option to improve customer experience. This acts like a credit where you can shop today and pay at a future date. Your repayment pattern is communicated to the credit bureaus, building your CIBIL profile. Make sure you clear the dues on time for a positive score. Step 6: Use your credit responsibly Banks often contact a salaried person for new credit card applications. Remember, it is important to know whether you require that many cards or not. Do not fall prey to the cashback offers and better credit limits. Only apply for a card when you need it. If you start collecting credit cards and spending unnecessarily, it can harm your credit score. Step 7: Avoid applying for multiple credit products at once When you are building your first CIBIL score, you shouldn’t apply for several credit cards or loans at the same time. Every application leads to a hard inquiry on your credit report, which can affect your score negatively. Moreover, if you make multiple applications, lenders may feel that you are heavily dependent on credit. Thus, you must apply for a suitable credit product and use it responsibly to build a positive credit history. Read More – How to Build Credit Score from Zero Step 8: Monitor your credit report regularly By checking your credit report regularly, you can track the progress of your first CIBIL score. You may spot errors, incorrect loan entries, or missed payment records that could affect your score. When you review your report every few months, you understand your credit health and take timely action if any information requires correction or update. Consequently, you can stop any negative impact on your credit score. How to maintain a good credit score? Now, you know how do you establish credit for the first time, but maintaining it is an entirely different thing. When you just start building your credit, here is how you sustain it: Regular payment It is important to clear your dues on time. The bureau keeps a tab on your payment history, making it a significant part of the credit report. Credit utilization ratio Always maintain a low credit card balance. Your credit utilization ratio should always be lower than 30%. Credit utilization ratio = (Outstanding balance / Total credit limit) *100 Credit diversification Maintaining a single credit type isn’t a great way of improving your credit score. Instead, have a mix of credits, including a credit card, a loan installment, and BNPL. This will positively impact your credit history. Monitoring credit report Keep a regular check on the credit score. Identify the inaccuracies, if any, and resolve them to improve the score. The credit bureaus allow you to get a free report annually. Avoid multiple accounts Every credit can directly or indirectly affect your credit score. When you are applying for a new credit card or opening a bank account, be cautious. Any defaults on payment can hinder your CIBIL score. How long does it take to build a credit score in India? When you are new to the credit journey, it usually takes around 3 to 6 months of active credit use to generate your first credit score in India. If you want to know how to generate a CIBIL score as a new user, you can use a credit card or loan responsibly and make all payments on time. The exact timeline for generating your CIBIL score may vary depending on how often lenders report your credit activity to credit bureaus. With consistent, responsible credit behavior, you can build a healthy credit score faster. Read More – How to Increase CIBIL Score From 600 to 750 How to check your CIBIL score and credit report online? The steps to check your CIBIL score and credit report online are as follows: Visit the official website of your preferred credit bureau or a trusted financial platform. Register using your basic details, such as your name, mobile number, and PAN. Complete the identity verification process. Request access to your CIBIL score and credit report. Review the report carefully for your score, loan accounts, repayment history, and any errors. If you check your own credit report regularly, you can track your credit health and identify inaccuracies early. Bottom line Build your credit score from scratch and create a financially sound future for yourself. Implementing the proven strategies can make a significant impact on your credit report. In case you want to apply for an unsecured credit card or learn how to generate a credit score report, Tata Capital is by your side. The finance company helps build and monitor a credit score securely. FAQs How can I get CIBIL for the first time? You can get a CIBIL score by using a secured credit card or using the Buy Now Pay Later payment option. How much time does it take to generate a CIBIL Score? It takes around 3 to 4 months to generate a CIBIL score. How do I build a credit score if I have never taken a loan? If you have never taken a loan and want to build a credit score, you can start with a secured credit card or a small loan. Then, remember to make timely payments and use credit responsibly to build your credit history. What is the minimum CIBIL score you require to get a personal loan? Most lenders require a CIBIL score of 700 or above to approve a personal loan. However, some lenders may approve loans for lower scores with additional conditions. How long does it take to generate a CIBIL score for the first time? It generally takes about 3 to 6 months of active credit usage and reported repayment history to generate your CIBIL score. Can a student apply for a secured credit card in India? Yes, students can submit applications for a secured credit card in India. However, you will need a fixed deposit. Make sure you check the bank’s eligibility requirements and terms before applying. Does checking my own credit score reduce my CIBIL score? No, your CIBIL score doesn’t reduce if you check your own credit score, as it is a soft inquiry. What happens if I miss an EMI payment as a first-time borrower? If you miss an EMI payment as a first-time borrower, it can lower your credit score and remain on your credit report. Moreover, if there are repeated delays, it may affect future loan approvals. Is a CIBIL score of 700 good enough for a home loan? Yes, a CIBIL score of 700 is generally considered good enough for a home loan. It can improve your chances of loan approval and get you more favorable loan terms. Can I get a credit card with no credit history in India? Yes, it is possible to get a credit card with no credit history in India. Many banks offer secured or entry-level credit cards to individuals who do not have any existing credit history. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund As a beginner investor, you’re most likely looking for investment avenues that offer good returns at low risk. If you’re looking to park your funds for the short-term, your top choices are either liquid funds or arbitrage funds. While liquid funds invest in debt securities, arbitrage funds invest across debt and equity and aim to generate returns through arbitrage opportunities in the cash and futures market, thus maintaining fully hedged positions. Even so, both are considered non-volatile investing modes and even offer similar returns. The natural question then – as an investor, which one should you choose? In this article, we review liquid and arbitrage funds and their differences. We also tell you which funds to invest in. What are liquid funds? Categorised as debt funds by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), liquid funds invest in short-term market instruments like commercial papers, government securities and security bills. Although these instruments mature within 91 days, investors can redeem their returns on T+1 basis. This way, liquid funds offer higher liquidity compared to other investment avenues. Besides, the investors benefit from lower interest rate fluctuations given the lesser tenure. What are arbitrage funds? Categorised as hybrid funds, arbitrage funds must have 65% of the fund assets in equities or equity-related securities as per SEBI mandates. Here, the returns are generated from a pricing mismatch between purchases made in the cash market and sales made in the future’s market. For instance, an asset may have a value of Rs. 15 in market A and Rs. 20 in market B. So, if you buy the asset from market A and sell it in market B, you make a profit of Rs. 5. These are your returns. Difference between liquid and arbitrage funds 1. Liquidity: Arbitrage Funds vs Liquid Funds As their name suggests, liquid funds offer better liquidity than other short-term investment avenues. Usually, the redemption amount is disbursed to the investor’s bank account on a T+1 basis or the next working day, provided the transaction is received before the cut-off time. In contrast, redemption occurs on a T+3 basis in the case of arbitrage funds. This makes liquid funds a preferred investment avenue for investors who want high-liquidity investments. 2. Returns: Liquid Funds vs Arbitrage Funds Since liquid funds invest in debt investment instruments that are less volatile than stocks, the returns are more stable and consistent. In contrast, arbitrage funds invest in equity instruments that are known to offer better returns. But instead of being highly volatile like other equity instruments, arbitrage funds have almost no investment risk. This is because these investments hedge risks by buying one instrument and selling them quickly. 3. Exit Load: Liquidity Withdrawal Charges Compared Most Asset Management Companies (AMCs) charge investors an exit fee when they exit or redeem the fund. That said, liquid funds are typically not associated with exit penalties unless investors redeem their funds within seven days of investing. In the case of arbitrage funds, investors must pay fees to exit the fund. Note that these charges are applicable if the investor exits the fund within a few weeks after investing. Also, the period after which exit charges are applicable depends on the asset management company. 4. Risk: Volatility & Market Impact on Both Fund Types Liquid funds, being debt funds, have interest rate and credit risk. This means your returns may get affected due to a rise in interest rates if the issuer loses its financial stability. In contrast, arbitrage funds come with no price fluctuation risk, despite being equity-oriented hybrid funds. This is because these funds are 100% hedged, given the buying and selling of assets occur quickly. 5. Taxation: Liquid Funds vs Arbitrage Funds in India Since the SEBI classifies liquid funds as debt funds, their returns are added to the investor’s taxable income for the financial year. Whether you invest for a short-term or long-term, you must pay taxes according to the tax slab applicable to your overall earnings in a financial year. Arbitrage funds are taxed as equity funds. This means the STCG earned when funds are held for less than a year are taxed at 15%, whereas gains earned after holding funds for over a year are taxed under LTCG. Accordingly, if the gains are above Rs. 1 lakh, the tax is at a rate of 10%. Arbitrage Funds vs Liquid Funds: Which Gives Better Returns? Both investment avenues have their pros and cons. That said, opt for liquid funds if you want to invest in low-risk debt funds, want higher liquidity, and don’t want to pay an exit load on short-term investments that last a few weeks. But if you want to invest in a low-risk, high-return investment avenue, and don’t mind lower liquidity, invest in arbitrage funds. Now, whether you’re looking to invest in liquid or arbitrage funds, you need a reliable investment partner to help you with your journey. If you’re looking for one, turn to Tata Capital Wealth. We allow customers to access their portfolio at their convenience through the Tata Capital Wealth Portal, offer relationship management services, and provide informative and qualitative reports to help you make the right investment decisions. Who Should Invest in Liquid Funds and Arbitrage Funds? Both liquid and arbitrage funds serve short-term investment needs, but they suit different investor profiles. 1. Liquid funds are suitable if you want quick access to your money while earning slightly better returns than a savings account. They work well for emergency funds, surplus cash, or short-term goals lasting a few days to a few months. 2. Arbitrage funds are better suited if you can stay invested for a few months and are looking for relatively higher post-tax returns. They are often preferred by investors in higher tax brackets who want equity-style taxation with controlled risk. 3. Your choice depends on liquidity needs, tax bracket, and investment horizon, rather than just return expectations. Pros & Cons Table: Arbitrage Funds vs Liquid Funds Here’s a side by side comparison of what advantages and limitations each type of fund is associated with: Parameter Liquid Funds Arbitrage Funds Liquidity Very high, usually T+1 redemption Lower, typically T+3 redemption Risk Level Low, subject to interest rate and credit risk Low, but depends on arbitrage opportunities Return Stability Stable and predictable Can vary based on market conditions Exit Load Usually none after a few days May apply for short holding periods Taxation Taxed as per income tax slab Taxed as equity funds Ideal Holding Period Few days to a few months Few months to one year Conclusion Liquid and arbitrage funds are both suitable for short-term investing, but they cater to different priorities. Liquid funds work well when access to funds and stability matter more, while arbitrage funds can be useful when tax efficiency and slightly higher returns are the goal. If you are evaluating these options as part of a broader investment strategy, Tata Capital Wealth can support you with expert guidance. Through personalised advisory services and a convenient digital platform, Tata Capital helps you make informed investment decisions aligned with your financial goals. The main difference lies in where they invest. Liquid funds invest in short-term debt instruments, while arbitrage funds invest in both equity and debt to benefit from price differences between markets. Are arbitrage funds safer or riskier than liquid funds? Both are considered low-risk. Liquid funds face interest rate and credit risk, while arbitrage funds depend on market conditions but remain hedged, which limits volatility. Which is better for short-term parking: liquid or arbitrage fund? Liquid funds are usually better for very short-term parking due to faster liquidity. Arbitrage funds may suit you if you can stay invested slightly longer and want tax efficiency. How are liquid funds and arbitrage funds taxed in India? Liquid fund returns are taxed as per your income tax slab. Arbitrage funds follow equity taxation rules, with short-term and long-term capital gains taxed differently. Can arbitrage funds give negative returns? While rare, arbitrage funds can deliver marginally negative returns in unfavourable market conditions, especially over very short periods when arbitrage opportunities are limited. Why do arbitrage funds sometimes outperform liquid funds? Arbitrage funds can outperform liquid funds due to equity-style taxation and opportunities created by price differences between cash and futures markets, particularly during volatile market phases.
