creditworthiness. Timely repayment of loans results in an improvement in your credit score. On the contrary, delaying loan installment payments can impact your credit score negatively and lead to loan rejections or higher interest rates. Understanding the repayment credit in your bank statement is necessary if you want to enjoy access to credit in the future. Lenders approve new credit or loan requests faster if you have a clean track record. Timely repayment of loans results in building and protecting your credit score. Make sure you track your repayment history to maintain a strong financial profile. Timely loan repayment has a big role to play in building a healthy credit score. If you pay every Equated Monthly Installment (EMI) on time, it helps improve your payment history, which is one of the most important factors used to calculate your credit score . This article explains how timely repayments affect your credit score, how they appear in credit reports and bank statements, and simple tips to maintain a strong repayment record. What does timely repayment of loans result in? There are many long-term benefits of paying your loan EMIs on time. You can build a strong financial profile, which makes borrowing easier in the future. The other benefits of timely repayment of loans are: Improves your credit score by creating a positive repayment history over time. Increases your loan eligibility when you apply for future credit. May help you get lower interest rates on new loans if you have a strong credit profile. Can improve your chances of getting higher loan amounts from lenders. Builds a clean credit history, increasing lender confidence in your ability to repay on time. How does repayment history impact your credit score? Your repayment history has a major impact on your credit score. Lenders send your monthly repayment details to credit bureaus like CIBIL, Experian , Equifax, and CRIF High Mark . Every EMI that you pay on time is recorded as a positive entry. Whereas, if there are any missed or delayed payments, they are reported as negative entries. Repayment history is the most important factor in credit scoring. So, even one missed EMI can noticeably reduce your credit score. What is repayment credit in a bank statement? Repayment credit in a bank statement refers to an entry related to your loan repayment. In most cases, it is actually a debit showing that your EMI amount has been deducted from your account and paid to the lender. The description may vary by bank, such as EMI debit, loan repayment, or NACH debit . However, it does not mean that money has been credited to your account. What is the short-term vs long-term impact of timely repayments? The following descriptions will help you understand the impact of short-term vs long-term timely repayments. Short-term (3-6 months): If you make all your EMIs on time, your credit score may start to stabilize or recover, especially if it was affected by earlier missed payments. Long-term (12+ months): Regular timely repayments build a stronger credit score over time. A long history of on-time payments carries more weight and increases lender confidence. What happens if you miss an EMI? If you miss an EMI, it can hurt your credit score. Similarly, if your payment is delayed, the lender may report it as a Days Past Due (DPD) entry in your credit report. Being 30 days late can noticeably reduce your score. Repeated missed payments may lead to your loan becoming a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) , which seriously damages your credit profile. You may also have to pay a late payment fee. What are the tips to maintain timely loan repayments? Here are some practical tips to help you maintain timely loan repayments: Set up NACH or auto-debit on your salary credit date. Keep enough balance in your account at least one day before the EMI date. Set a reminder three days before your EMI is due. Contact your lender early if you expect a cash-flow problem. Conclusion Timely repayment of loans results in a stronger credit profile and better access to future loans at competitive rates. A repayment credit in a bank statement is an amount credited to your loan account when you make an EMI or loan repayment. It shows that your payment has been received. How long does it take for timely repayments to improve my credit score? Generally, your credit score starts improving within a few months with regular on-time repayments. However, the exact time depends on your overall credit profile. How can I ensure I never miss an EMI? If you don’t want to ever miss an EMI, you must set up auto-debit or standing instructions, keep enough balance in your account, and use reminders to track your EMI due dates. Does prepaying a loan help my credit score? Prepaying a loan does not directly increase your credit score. However, it reduces your debt burden and shows responsible credit management, which can support a healthy credit profile over time. The CIBIL score range in India runs from 300 to 900, and every score within this range reflects a different level of creditworthiness. Your CIBIL score range runs from 300 to 900. In general, the closer your score is to 900, the better your chances of getting a loan approved on favorable terms. If you are a first-time borrower with no credit history, you are not assigned a score of 300. Instead, your credit report is marked NA or NH (No History). This guide explains the CIBIL score range, the maximum CIBIL score, what each score band means, the average score in India, the score lenders usually prefer, and simple ways to improve it. What is a CIBIL score? A CIBIL score is a three-digit number issued by TransUnion CIBIL, one of the four credit bureaus licensed by the RBI in India. It is calculated using your credit history, including repayment behavior, credit utilization, credit mix, account age, and recent loan or credit card inquiries. Apart from TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark also issue credit scores, so your score may vary slightly across different bureaus. CIBIL score range: What each band means? Every score within the CIBIL score range of 300 to 900 reflects a different level of creditworthiness. As a general rule, the higher your credit score is, the more creditworthy you are. CIBIL score range Rating What it means 300 – 549 Poor High credit risk 550 – 649 Fair Some credit concerns 650 – 749 Good Responsible credit behavior 750 – 799 Very good Strong repayment record 800 – 900 Excellent Excellent financial discipline What is the maximum and average CIBIL score in India? The highest CIBIL score in India is 900. However, very few borrowers actually achieve it. In practice, a score of 750 or above is considered excellent and is treated by most lenders as a sign of low credit risk. Although the average CIBIL score in India varies across borrower segments, a score between 700 and 750 is generally viewed as satisfactory. Borrowers in this range usually have a reasonable chance of securing loans. What does my specific CIBIL score mean? A three-digit score tells only part of the story. The real meaning depends on the score band it falls into and how lenders interpret it. Whether you are searching for CIBIL score 763, CIBIL score 764, or any other score within the CIBIL score range, the idea remains the same. You can use specific online tools to enter your score and instantly check its rating, understand what it indicates to lenders, and see the practical steps you can take to maintain or improve it. What if you have no credit history? (NA/NH explained) If you have never taken a loan or used a credit card, your credit report will usually show NA (Not Applicable) or NH (No History) instead of a CIBIL score. This does not mean you have a poor credit profile. However, lenders have limited information to assess your repayment behavior. A first-time borrower can build a credit score by using a credit card responsibly or repaying a small loan on time. What CIBIL score do you need for a personal loan or home loan? While lenders have their own policies, a score of 750 or above is generally preferred for both personal and home loans . But remember, being close to this CIBIL score limit alone does not guarantee approval. Your income, existing EMIs, employment stability, debt-to-income ratio, and other eligibility checks also influence the decision. You can use an online loan eligibility calculator to get a better idea. Also Read – Experian vs CIBIL: Which Credit Score Is Better for You? What are the factors that affect your CIBIL score? The following factors influence your CIBIL score: Repayment history: Your record of repaying loan EMIs and credit card bills. Credit utilization ratio: The ratio of total available credit to that you use. Credit mix: The combination of secured and unsecured loans. Length of credit history: The total age of your credit accounts. Recent hard inquiries: Lenders make an inquiry each time you apply for a loan. How to improve your CIBIL score? Here are a few practical tips that can help you improve your CIBIL score: Pay all your EMIs and credit card bills on time. Keep your credit utilization ratio low. Avoid multiple loan applications within a short window. Do not close old credit card accounts. Maintain a healthy mix of secured and unsecured loans . Check and report for errors (if any). Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Amortization is the process of spreading a cost, typically a loan or an intangible asset, into fixed payments or charges over a set period of time. Understanding the meaning of amortization matters because it directly affects how much you pay in interest versus principal each month. This page explains what amortization is, how a loan amortization schedule works, the principal and interest split, and why this concept matters for borrowers and businesses alike. By the end, you will know exactly how scheduled payments reduce debt over time. Loan amortization refers to paying off a debt through regular, scheduled payments spread across a fixed period, where each installment covers both interest and principal. On the other hand, accounting defines amortization as gradually writing off the cost of an intangible asset over its useful life. The term applies in two related but distinct contexts: loans and accounting. What is amortization? The meaning of amortization comes down to structure: a debt is repaid through fixed, scheduled installments rather than a single lump sum, and each installment is split between interest and principal. To define amortization more formally, in lending, it refers to this repayment structure over the loan term. On the other hand, understanding what amortization in finance is can be very different, since the same word refers to expensing an intangible asset’s cost gradually across its useful life. These two uses share a common thread, since both involve breaking a large cost into smaller portions recognized over time, but they apply to different financial situations. The section below separates the two so there is no confusion going forward. Also Read – What is EMI and how is it calculated? Two meanings of amortization: Loans vs accounting Since the term covers two different financial concepts, it helps to separate them clearly before going further. The table below captures the differences in the two applications of the word: Type What it covers How it works Loan amortization Mortgages, auto loans , personal loans Fixed installments shift from interest-heavy to principal-heavy over time Accounting amortization Intangible assets like patents and software Cost is expensed gradually across the asset’s useful life What is loan amortization? So, what is loan amortization in practical terms? It refers to the schedule by which a loan gets paid off through equal installments over a fixed term. Within each payment, the ratio of interest to principal shifts as the loan progresses. Early installments carry more interest because the outstanding balance is higher at that point. Later installments shift toward principal, since the balance has shrunk and there is less interest to calculate against it. Also Read – Maximum & Minimum Loan Tenure What is a loan amortization schedule? A loan amortization schedule is a table listing every installment due over the loan term. It shows the payment date, the EMI or installment amount, the portion going toward interest, the portion going toward principal, and the remaining balance after each payment. Here is a simplified snippet showing the first three rows of a sample schedule: Payment no. Installment Interest Principal Balance 1 Rs. 500 Rs. 320 Rs. 180 Rs. 47,820 2 Rs. 500 Rs. 317 Rs. 183 Rs. 47,637 3 Rs. 500 Rs. 315 Rs. 185 Rs. 47,452 Principal and interest in a loan amortization schedule The principal amount of amortization refers to the original sum borrowed, which reduces with every payment made. On the other hand, the interest amount of amortization refers to the cost of borrowing, calculated on the outstanding principal balance at that point in time. Interest is highest during early installments and gradually decreases as the principal shrinks. For example, on a Rs. 48,000 loan, the first payment may allocate Rs. 320 to interest and only Rs. 180 to principal, which explains why early payments often feel like they are mostly covering interest. Also Read – Fixed and Floating Interest Rates What is the amortization period? Once you understand the concept, you may be wondering what is the amortization period, and how does it differ from the loan term? The amortization period is the total length of time over which a loan is scheduled to be fully paid off through regular installments. In some cases, this differs from the loan term itself. For instance, a loan may carry a shorter term with a longer amortization period, which then requires refinancing or a balloon payment once the term ends. Why is amortization important? Understanding amortization helps borrowers see exactly how much of each payment reduces their debt versus how much covers interest charges. This clarity supports better prepayment decisions, since borrowers can identify when extra payments save the most on interest costs over the loan term. Also Read – Key Benefits of Prepayment and Partial Payment of Personal Loan Conclusion Whether you are repaying a loan or accounting for an intangible asset, understanding amortization helps you see how a large cost is distributed over time. For borrowers in particular, knowing how principal and interest change across the repayment period makes it easier to estimate borrowing costs, compare loan options, and plan prepayments more confidently. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund The festive season, spanning Navratri, Dussehra, Dhanteras, and Diwali, is India’s biggest spending window, covering home upgrades, vehicles, appliances, travel, and gifting. This is one of the biggest reasons to avail a personal loan in the festive season , as it helps buyers time their purchases around lower rates, faster processing, and dealer discounts. These festive season loan benefits make festive spending more structured than routine borrowing. Festive loan offers are limited-period lending deals, featuring reduced rates, waived fees, or faster disbursal, rolled out during India’s festive months. Why is the festive season a smart time to avail a loan? Lenders compete for festive business, so the reasons to avail a personal loan in the festive season often come down to genuine savings, not marketing. Dealers and builders also run festive deals, lowering the cost of large purchases when paired with financing. The festive season loan benefits typically include the following. Lower interest rates on select products during the offer window Processing fee waivers from banks and NBFCs Faster approval and disbursal timed to festive deadlines Extra discounts from sellers on top of loan savings These festive loan offers rarely last long, so timing the purchase matters. Types of loans you can avail this festive season Festive spending covers more than one category, so the loan should match the purchase. Home loan, for a new home or renovation work Car or two-wheeler loan , bought during dealer offers Consumer durable or personal loan, for appliances or travel Business loan , for MSME owners stocking festive inventory Education loan , for tuition costs falling due this season Apart from these, a low-interest personal loan for the festive season can also cover more specific purposes for borrowers with less conventional festive plans, such as wedding expenses or a family holiday. Benefits of availing a loan during the festive season The core festive season loan benefits go beyond a lower rate on paper: Festive offers reduce both the interest rate and the processing fee. An instant personal loan for festivals can be approved and disbursed within hours. Collateral-free options are widely available for personal and durable purchases. Flexible tenure and EMI choices help repayment fit the monthly budget. A loan preserves savings and investments instead of draining them. Timely repayment through the season builds credit history. What to look for in festive loan offers Not every deal during the festive season is equally good. It’s important to look past the headline rate and check the festive loan offers ‘ effective cost, since fees add to what is actually repaid. Comparing different low-interest personal loans for the festive season may even reveal meaningful savings. Festive season purchases you can finance with a loan Here are some purchases worth making this festive season: Home renovation or a new home purchase timed with Dhanteras A new car or two-wheeler bought during dealer promotions Consumer durables such as a smart TV, AC, or washing machine Gold or jewellery bought on Dhanteras Festive travel, gifting, and wedding-related expenses No-cost EMI vs loan: Which is better for festive shopping? A no-cost EMI for a festive season purchase suits a single product from one retailer, though it’s important to check for hidden fees. A loan suits larger, multi-purpose spending across products and sellers. Factor No-cost EMI Personal or consumer loan Best suited for Single product, single retailer Multiple purchases or larger amounts Hidden costs Possible processing fee Interest and fees disclosed upfront Tenure choice Fixed by the retailer scheme Chosen by the borrower Is it a good idea to take a loan during the festive season? So, is it a good idea to take a loan for Diwali shopping , or maybe some other special occasion? Yes, but only when the purchase is planned, the EMI fits comfortably within budget, and emergency savings stay untouched. Borrowing only what can be repaid without stress keeps festive spending sensible. How to avail a Tata Capital loan this festive season Choosing the right loan starts with matching the product to the festive goal. Log in to the Tata Capital portal or app using a mobile number verified through OTP. Select the preferred loan product, such as personal, consumer durable, or home loan . Enter personal, employment, and banking details as prompted. Upload identity proof, address proof, and recent bank statements. Set up a one-time eMandate for automated EMI payments. Review and accept the electronic loan agreement to complete the process. Conclusion The festive season remains India’s most practical window for planned purchases, and Tata Capital’s festive loan offers make the decision easier to commit to. However, it’s important to remember that these festive season loan benefits hold only when handled responsibly, and rates vary by product and period. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary Net Asset Value (NAV) represents the per-unit value of a mutual fund and is calculated at the end of every business day. It is derived from the fund’s assets, liabilities, and outstanding units, but it does not indicate whether a scheme is cheap or expensive. Understanding how NAV works helps investors know how mutual fund units are priced during purchases and redemptions and avoid common investing misconceptions. Net Asset Value (NAV) is the per-unit value of a mutual fund, calculated by dividing its net assets by the total number of outstanding units. Net Asset Value (NAV) is one of the most important numbers associated with a mutual fund scheme. It tells you what one unit of the fund is worth on a particular day. However, a lower NAV does not mean a fund is cheaper or a better investment. Understanding net asset value’s meaning is essential before investing. This guide explains the net asset value formula, how NAV is calculated, how it works when you buy or redeem units, and what NAV can – and cannot – tell you about a mutual fund. What does net asset value mean? The net asset value meaning is simple: it represents the per-unit value of a mutual fund after accounting for its assets and liabilities. Unlike a stock price, which changes throughout the trading day, a mutual fund’s NAV is calculated and declared once at the end of every business day. What is the net asset value formula? The formula for net asset value calculation is as follows: NAV = (Total Assets – Total Liabilities) / Number of outstanding units Here’s what each of these components means: Component Meaning Total Assets Market value of underlying securities, cash, receivables, etc. Total Liabilities Fund expenses, management fees, and other dues. Outstanding Units Total number of mutual fund units held by all investors combined. How to calculate net asset value – Example Suppose a mutual fund has assets worth Rs. 120 crore, liabilities of Rs. 20 crore, and 10 crore outstanding units. So, the net asset value calculation will involve the following steps: Subtract total liabilities from total assets (120 – 20) = Rs. 100 crore. Divide this figure by the total number of outstanding units (100/10) = 10. Does a low NAV mean a fund is cheap? No. A fund’s NAV has no direct relationship with the returns it can generate. It simply shows the value of one unit on a particular day, not whether the scheme is cheap or expensive. So, a New Fund Offer (NFO) priced at Rs. 10 is not a discount, and ‘more units for your money’ is a sales line, not an advantage. Also Read – PMS vs Mutual Fund NAV vs share price: What’s the difference? Basis Mutual Fund NAV Share Price Meaning The value of one unit of a mutual fund scheme. The price at which a share is trading at a given time. How is it calculated Through a fixed formula. Based on market demand, supply, and numerous other factors. Frequency Declared once after the end of each trading day. Changes constantly during the trading session. Which day’s NAV applies when you buy or sell? The applicable NAV depends on when the fund house receives and realizes your money, not simply when you place the investment request. For purchases and redemptions submitted before the prescribed cut-off time on a business day, the same day’s NAV generally applies, subject to the applicable rules. Requests received after the cut-off, or on a weekend or public holiday, are processed using the NAV of the next business day. Also Read- Types of mutual funds in India What is net asset value of a company? The term NAV net asset value is also used in corporate finance, though its meaning is slightly different from mutual funds. For a company, it refers to the value of total assets minus total liabilities. This measure is commonly used during business valuation, mergers and acquisitions, and in situations such as ESOP planning. It tells you the value of one unit, but it does not indicate whether a fund is cheap or expensive. To make informed investment decisions, compare more than just the NAV. Net Asset Value (NAV) is the value of one mutual fund unit on a particular business day. It is calculated after adjusting the fund's assets and liabilities. What is the formula for net asset value? The formula is: NAV = (Total Assets − Total Liabilities) ÷ Total Outstanding Units. This gives the value of each mutual fund unit. How is NAV calculated? At the end of every business day, the fund values its investments, deducts liabilities, and divides the balance by the total number of units. Is a fund with a lower NAV better? No. A lower NAV does not make a fund cheaper or better. It only represents the value of one unit on that particular day. Is NAV the same as a share price? No. Share prices change throughout the trading day, while mutual fund NAV is calculated once after the market closes on each business day. How often is mutual fund NAV updated? For most mutual funds, NAV is calculated and published once every business day after the market closes and the portfolio is valued. Which day's NAV applies to my SIP installment? The applicable NAV depends on when the fund house receives and realizes your SIP amount, subject to the applicable cut-off rules. Does the expense ratio affect NAV? Yes. Fund expenses are adjusted before the daily NAV is declared, so the expense ratio is already reflected in the published NAV. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund EMI, or Equated Monthly Installment, is a fixed payment method that borrowers choose to repay a loan. Every installment comprises both the principal amount and the interest. A lump sum is a single large payment made all at once. There are no smaller installments made over time. Understanding EMI vs lump sum repayment differences is crucial, as it affects your financial planning. The choice between the two depends on your cash flow, interest rates, and financial goals. EMI and lump sum repayment are two different ways to repay a loan. Each has its own benefits and suitability depending on your financial situation. If you have enough money to pay for a large purchase, should you pay the full amount now or choose EMIs? Interestingly, there is no one-size-fits-all answer to this question. The EMI vs lump sum repayment choice depends on interest costs, your cash needs, and other uses for your money. This article describes and compares both options to help you make a wise decision. What is an EMI payment? An Equated Monthly Installment (EMI) is a fixed monthly payment you make to repay a loan over an agreed tenure. Each EMI includes both the principal amount and the interest. If you have a reducing-balance loan, early EMIs contain more interest, while later EMIs have more principal. You can use an online EMI calculator to estimate your monthly payments without confusion. What is a lump sum payment? A lump sum payment means paying the entire amount in one transaction instead of breaking the payment into smaller ones. Once you pay the full amount, there are no future installments or interest charges. Note that lump sum as a method of payment for mutual fund investments is different from a one-time full payment for a loan or a purchase. What are the EMI vs lump sum repayment key differences? The following table highlights the important differences between EMI vs lump sum repayment: Factor EMI payment Lump sum payment Total cost paid Usually higher because of interest Usually lower Interest outgo Charged at an annual rate None Impact on monthly cash flow Fixed monthly EMIs No monthly payments Effect on emergency savings Helps preserve savings May reduce savings Credit score impact Timely EMIs can improve it No direct impact Flexibility Better if you need liquidity Best if funds are available Processing/foreclosure charges May apply, depending on the loan type None When does a lump sum make more sense? A lump sum payment makes more sense in the following scenarios: You can pay the full amount without using your emergency savings. You already have several EMIs, and another one would increase your monthly financial burden. The EMI interest rate is higher than the returns your money is likely to earn if invested. The EMI includes processing fees or other charges, or the ‘no-cost EMI’ offer is not truly free. Also Read – What is Pre EMI and How to Calculate It When does an EMI make more sense? EMI should be your choice in the following cases: Paying the full amount would reduce your emergency savings. The loan costs less than what your money may earn elsewhere. You need to keep cash available for an upcoming expense. A genuine zero-interest EMI is available with all fees clearly disclosed. What is the catch with ‘No-Cost EMI’? A no-cost EMI has hidden charges, so it is not always completely free. The cost may be covered through a reduced upfront discount, a merchant-funded subsidy, or a processing fee. Depending on the offer structure, GST may also apply to certain charges. Always compare the cash price with the total EMI amount, including all fees, before proceeding. How to decide between the two? A simple checklist EMI and lump sum are both efficient payment methods. If you need to choose one of the two, you can use the checklist given below: Compare the total EMI cost, including interest and all fees, with the cash price. Make sure you still have 3 to 6 months of emergency savings after paying upfront. Compare the EMI interest rate with the return your money could earn elsewhere in an investment. Check whether the new EMI fits comfortably within your monthly income and existing loan commitments. If the EMI has a real interest cost and you have enough savings beyond your emergency fund, paying upfront is usually the cheaper option. Conclusion Choosing between an EMI vs lump sum repayment depends on your budget, savings, and the total cost involved. You must compare the full cost and keep your emergency funds intact before picking the option that best supports your financial goals. The better choice between EMI vs lump sum repayment depends on your finances. EMI is a better option if you want to spread the cost over time without burdening your savings. On the other hand, paying the full amount saves you from future EMIs and interest charges. Does paying in EMIs cost more than paying upfront? Mostly, yes. When you choose the EMI repayment option, you are also liable to pay interest and other charges. This makes the total cost higher than an upfront payment of the full amount. However, if you are eligible for the no-cost EMI, you may not have to pay interest charges. Is no-cost EMI really free? Not always. A no-cost EMI removes interest, but you may still have to pay processing fees or other charges. Carefully check the offer terms for a clear understanding. Does taking an EMI affect my credit score? Yes. If you pay your EMIs on time, it can improve your credit score. Conversely, if you miss or delay payments, your credit score declines. Should I use my savings to avoid an EMI? The idea of using your savings to avoid an EMI depends on your individual financial situation. It isn’t advisable to use all your savings to make a lump sum payment. You must keep money for emergencies. What is the difference between a lump sum payment and a lump sum investment? A lump sum payment means paying the entire amount at one time, such as for buying a product or clearing a loan. A lump sum investment, on the other hand, means investing a large amount in one go, such as in a mutual fund or fixed deposit. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund National Pension Scheme (NPS) and Public Provident Fund (PPF) are both government-backed long-term schemes in India. The choice between mutual funds vs NPS vs PPF, which is better, depends on your risk tolerance, lock-in comfort, and financial goals. While NPS offers market-linked returns based on equity and debt performance, PPF provides fixed, government-guaranteed interest rates. Mutual funds are all market-linked (equity, debt, hybrid). : To decide which is better, NPS or PPF, you need a clear understanding of each investment tool, along with your risk appetite, holding period comfort, and financial objectives. NPS vs PPF vs mutual funds is not just about choosing the investment with the highest returns. PPF is a government-backed savings scheme, NPS is a retirement plan, and mutual funds are market-linked investments. They differ in risk, lock-in, and liquidity. The right choice depends on your financial goal and time horizon. What is PPF? Public Provident Fund (PPF) is a government-backed long-term savings scheme that offers stable, tax-efficient returns without market risk. 15-year lock-in that you can extend in 5-year blocks Maximum investment: Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year Interest and maturity are tax-free under current rules What is NPS? The National Pension System (NPS) is a PFRDA-regulated, market-linked retirement savings scheme designed for long-term retirement planning. Two types of accounts: Tier I: Retirement account, generally locked until age 60 Tier II: Voluntary savings account Under Active Choice, equity exposure is capped as per PFRDA rules. Auto Choice gradually reduces equity with age. At retirement, up to 60% of the corpus can be withdrawn as a tax-free lump sum, while at least 40% must be used to buy an annuity. The annuity income is taxable as per your income tax slab. Where do mutual funds fit in? Mutual funds are SEBI-regulated, market-linked investments that offer flexibility but also carry the highest risk of the three options. No lock-in, except ELSS (3 years). ELSS offers a Section 80C deduction only under the old tax regime. No investment limit or annuity requirement. Returns are not guaranteed. Capital gains are taxed on redemption. As of FY 2026-27, most equity funds attract 20% STCG and 12.5% LTCG above Rs. 1.25 lakh in a financial year. Also Read – Old Tax Regime vs New Tax Regime How are NPS vs PPF vs mutual funds different? A quick comparison The following table offers a quick comparison of NPS vs PPF vs mutual funds. Feature NPS PPF Mutual funds What is it? Retirement savings scheme Government savings scheme Market-linked investment Regulator PFRDA Ministry of Finance SEBI Risk Moderate Very low Low to high Returns Market-linked Government-declared (7.1% p.a. for the July – September 2026 quarter) Depend on market performance Lock-in Till retirement 15 years Usually none (ELSS: 3 years) Liquidity Limited Partial withdrawals allowed Generally high Tax on contribution Old regime: deduction available New regime: Only eligible employer contribution qualifies Old regime: Section 80C benefit New regime: No Section 80C deduction Old regime: Only ELSS qualifies under Section 80C New regime: No Section 80C deduction Tax on maturity Lump sum is largely tax-free; annuity income is taxable Interest and maturity are tax-free Capital gains tax applies as per fund type and tax rules Investment limit Minimum: Rs. 1,000/year Maximum: No limit Minimum: Rs. 500/year Maximum: Rs. 1.5 lakh/year Varies by scheme Tax treatment: What actually survives under the new tax regime? Choosing between NPS vs PPF vs mutual funds based only on tax benefits is no longer advisable under the new tax regime. The key tax differences are shown below. Investment Old regime New regime PPF Section 80 deduction available No deduction (renumbered Section 123); tax-free interest and maturity continue NPS (Self contribution) Deductions under Section 80CCD(1) & 80CCD(1B) No deduction (renumbered Section 124) NPS (Employer contribution) Deduction available Deduction continues (up to 14% of Basic + DA, if conditions are met) Mutual funds No deduction (except ELSS under Section 80C) No deduction NPS vs PPF: Which is better? There is no single best option. The right choice depends on your financial goal, time horizon, risk appetite, and liquidity needs. PPF is suited for capital protection, stable returns, and tax-free maturity. Remember that it requires a 15-year commitment. Go for NPS if your goal is retirement. Ensure you are comfortable with market risk and the annuity requirement, especially if your employer contributes. Consider mutual funds for greater liquidity, but you will have to accept market volatility. You don’t have to choose just one. Many people use a combination of these options to meet different financial goals. Also Read – Where should NRIs invest their money in India Who should consider what? Salaried employee: Consider based on employer NPS contributions. Self-employed person: Study the performance of PPF vs mutual funds based on goals. Risk-averse saver: If you have a 15-year horizon, consider PPF. Need liquidity: Mutual funds generally offer easier access to money than NPS or PPF. Conclusion You must make the mutual funds or NPS or PPF, which is better, choice based on your financial goals, lock-in, risk, and tax benefits under the old/new tax regime. Under the new regime, tax matters less, except for eligible employer NPS contributions. Build Your Wealth with Expert Guidance from Tata Capital! The primary difference between NPS and PPF is the returns. NPS invests in market-linked assets and offers varied returns. PPF is a government-backed savings scheme with fixed interest rates set by the government every quarter. Which is better, NPS or PPF? It depends on your goals. NPS may offer higher long-term returns but carries market risk. On the other hand, PPF is safer and suitable if you prefer stable, guaranteed returns. Can I invest in both NPS and PPF? Yes. You can invest in both schemes at the same time to enjoy the benefits of retirement planning and safe long-term savings. Does NPS or PPF give a tax benefit under the new tax regime? PPF investments qualify for a tax deduction under Section 80C. However, that is not available under the new tax regime. NPS offers a tax deduction only for eligible employer contributions. Which gives higher returns, NPS, PPF, or mutual funds? Mutual funds and NPS can give higher long-term returns as they are market-linked. PPF returns are stable, but generally lower. Can I withdraw from NPS before retirement? Yes. You can make partial withdrawals from NPS before retirement if you meet certain conditions. However, full withdrawal before retirement is allowed only under the rules of the scheme. Is the NPS annuity income taxable? Yes. The pension income you receive from the annuity is generally taxable as per your income tax slab. Are mutual funds safer than PPF? No. PPF is backed by the Government of India, and thus, generally safer than market-linked mutual funds. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A RERA registration number is an important indicator that a real estate project has been registered with the relevant state RERA authority. Checking this number helps you verify project details, approvals, timelines, and the developer’s disclosures before investing. Since every state has its own RERA portal, the verification process is carried out through the respective state website. A simple RERA check can reduce legal risks, improve transparency, and also support a smoother home loan process. A RERA registration number is a unique identification number issued by a state RERA authority to a registered real estate project or agent, confirming compliance with the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. Buying a home is one of the biggest financial decisions you will ever make, and verifying the project’s legal status is just as important as comparing its price or location. Since the introduction of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA), most residential and commercial real estate projects are required to be registered with the respective state RERA authority before they can be marketed or sold. Upon successful registration, every project receives a unique RERA registration number, which serves as proof that it has met the prescribed regulatory requirements. A RERA registration number check can help you confirm whether a project is officially registered and access important details such as approvals, timelines, and the developer’s disclosures. This guide explains what a RERA registration number is, why you should verify it, and how to find the RERA registration number through the relevant state RERA portal. What is a RERA registration number? A RERA registration number is a unique identification number issued by a State Real Estate Regulatory Authority to a registered real estate project. It confirms that the project has been registered under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, and has complied with the required disclosure and regulatory norms. Since RERA is implemented by individual states and union territories, the registration number format, official portal, and search process may differ from one state to another. A RERA number check helps buyers verify key details before buying a property. Why should you check a project’s RERA number? It’s always recommended to carry out a RERA registration number check before buying a property. It helps in several ways: Confirms that the project is registered with the state RERA authority. Reduces the risk of investing in projects with unverified approvals or misleading claims. Gives you access to important disclosures, including approvals, project status, completion timeline, carpet area, and developer information. Helps you track updates and commitments made by the developer on the official RERA portal. Many lenders also perform a RERA number check while assessing home loan applications for under-construction properties. How to find the RERA registration number of a project? Many property buyers often wonder how to find the RERA registration number of a project. You can locate this number in the following places: Project brochures and advertisements : Builders often display the RERA registration numbers in these promotional documents. A builder’s official website : You can also visit the project page on the builder’s official website for a RERA number check. Booking form/sale agreement : These documents also contain a project’s RERA number. However, they are available only after a property’s booking or sale. Signboards and project hoardings : RERA registration numbers are often displayed on signboards and hoardings for a project’s advertisement. State RERA portal : You can also visit your state’s RERA portal to search for a project’s RERA registration number. How to check a RERA registration number online (Step-by-step)? You can complete a RERA registration number check online in a few simple steps: Identify the state in which the project is located. Doing so is essential because RERA is administered by individual states. Go to the official RERA website for that state. Each state or union territory has a different website. Look for options such as “Registered Projects” or “RERA Project Registration Search” on the website. Input the required details, including the project’s name, promoter, and location, among others. Open the project listing page. There, you will find the RERA registration number along with other details, such as registration status, validity, approvals, construction timeline, and promoter details. Also Read – Home Loan Eligibility Criteria How to do a RERA registration verification? You can perform a RERA number check on your state’s RERA portal. Once you locate the project on the state RERA portal using the steps explained above, compare the official details with the builder’s claims. Check the registration validity and expiry date, approved layout plans, carpet area, promised completion timeline, promoter details, pending litigation (if any), and the latest quarterly construction progress reports. A quick comparison can help you spot discrepancies before you invest. State-wise RERA portals for RERA registration verification Since RERA is implemented by individual states and union territories, there is no single national portal for project verification. To complete a RERA project registration search, you need to visit the official RERA website of the state where the project is located. The table below mentions the official RERA authorities and portals for major Indian states: State Official RERA authority Official portal Maharashtra MahaRERA https://maharera.maharashtra.gov.in/ Karnataka Karnataka RERA https://rera.karnataka.gov.in/ Tamil Nadu TNRERA https://rera.tn.gov.in Uttar Pradesh UP RERA https://www.up-rera.in Delhi Delhi RERA https://rera.delhi.gov.in/ Bihar RERA Bihar https://rera.bihar.gov.in/ Haryana HRERA https://haryanarera.gov.in/ Gujarat GUJRERA https://gujrera.gujarat.gov.in/ Telangana Telangana RERA https://rera.telangana.gov.in/ Rajasthan Rajasthan RERA https://rera.rajasthan.gov.in/ Madhya Pradesh MPRERA https://www.rera.mp.gov.in/ West Bengal WBHIRA https://rera.wb.gov.in/ Note: Always verify the latest official RERA portal URL before using it. Government websites may be updated or changed over time. How to check a RERA number on the MahaRERA website (Maharashtra example)? If your property is in Maharashtra, you will need to visit the MahaRERA website for the RERA registration number check. Here are the steps involved: Visit the MahaRERA website < https://maharera.maharashtra.gov.in/ > Click on the “Projects” tab at the top of the Home page. Enter the project name, PIN code, completion date, and district. Hit the “Search” button. Review the project’s registration status, validity, approvals, construction progress, and other details. The process followed by most other state RERA portals is broadly similar, although the layout and search options may differ slightly. What if a project has no RERA number? RERA registration is mandatory for all eligible real estate projects in India. If a project does not have a RERA registration number, it may not be legally permitted to advertise or sell units and could expose buyers to a higher risk of delays, disputes, or other compliance issues. Some lenders may also hesitate to finance these projects through a home loan . However, keep in mind that certain smaller projects may be exempt from RERA registration if they fall below the prescribed thresholds. Is RERA verification necessary for home loans? If you are applying for a home loan for an under-construction property , checking the project’s RERA registration is a smart first step. Most lenders, including Tata Capital, are more comfortable financing projects registered with the relevant state RERA authority. This gives them greater confidence in the project’s legal status. Doing a quick RERA number check beforehand can also help avoid delays during document verification and make the loan approval process much smoother. Conclusion A RERA registration number check is one of the easiest yet most important checks you can make before booking a property. It helps confirm that the project is registered, lets you verify key disclosures, and reduces the chances of unpleasant surprises later. Since every state has its own RERA portal, make sure you verify the project on the relevant official website before proceeding. To check a RERA registration number, first identify the state where the project is located. Then visit that state's official RERA website, open the project search section, and search using the RERA number, project name, promoter's name, or location. The portal will display the registration status and other project details. Where can I find the RERA number of a project? The RERA number is usually mentioned in the builder's brochure, advertisements, official website, booking form, and sale documents. It is also displayed on project hoardings. If you cannot find it, you can search for the project on the official state RERA portal. How do I verify project details using a RERA number? Once you find the project on the state RERA portal, compare the official information with what the builder has shared. Check the registration validity, approved plans, carpet area, completion timeline, promoter details, and construction progress. This simple verification can help you make a better-informed decision. Is the RERA number the same in every state? No. Every state or union territory has its own RERA authority, so the registration number format may differ from one state to another. However, the purpose remains the same—it confirms that the project has been registered with the concerned state RERA authority. How do I search for a RERA-registered project? Visit the official RERA portal for the state where the project is located. Open the project search section and enter the project name, promoter's name, location, or RERA registration number. The search results will show whether the project is registered and provide the related disclosures. What should I do if a project has no RERA number? If a project does not have a RERA number even though registration is required, proceed with caution. Verify the project's status with the concerned state RERA authority before making any payment. Keep in mind that some smaller projects may be exempt from registration under the applicable rules. Is a RERA number required for a home loan? For many under-construction properties, lenders prefer or require projects that are registered with the state RERA authority. A valid RERA registration gives lenders greater confidence about the project's compliance and can make the home loan approval process smoother. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary E-invoicing under GST has become an important compliance requirement for many businesses, including a growing number of MSMEs. Eligible B2B and export invoices must be validated through the Invoice Registration Portal to obtain an IRN and QR code before they are treated as valid. Applicability depends on Aggregate Annual Turnover, while certain sectors continue to remain exempt. Following the e-invoicing process reduces reporting errors, supports faster ITC claims, and helps businesses maintain reliable financial records that can also strengthen their credit profile. GST e-invoicing is a system that electronically validates eligible business invoices through the Invoice Registration Portal by assigning them a unique Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and QR code. A GST invoice is no longer just a document. It can also become a digitally validated record. That is exactly what the GST e-invoice system aims to achieve. Under this framework, eligible businesses must upload their B2B invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP). The portal then generates a unique Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and digitally authenticates the invoice. Introduced in phases, the e-invoice system initially covered large companies but has gradually been extended to many MSMEs as well. As a result, more businesses now need to understand whether the e-invoice applicable rules affect them. This article explains what GST e-invoicing is, who needs to comply, the latest turnover limits, available exemptions, and the steps involved in generating an e-invoice. Keep reading. What is e-invoicing under GST? The e-invoice system under GST is a process through which eligible businesses have their B2B invoices electronically authenticated through the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) managed by the GST Network (GSTN). After validation, the portal assigns a unique Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and generates a QR code that becomes part of the invoice. A common misconception is that the government prepares the GST e-invoice. In reality, businesses continue creating invoices in their own accounting or billing software, such as Tally or similar platforms. The e-invoice system only validates the invoice and records it. This e-invoice GST framework also helps reduce duplicate invoicing, tax evasion, and fraudulent Input Tax Credit (ITC) claims. Understanding key terms: IRN, IRP, and QR code Here are the three key terms related to the e-invoice GST system: IRP (Invoice Registration Portal): The IRP is a government-authorized portal that checks and authenticates eligible invoices. IRN (Invoice Reference Number): The IRN is a unique 64-character hash generated for every valid e-invoice. It helps prevent duplicate invoice reporting. QR Code: After an invoice is authenticated, the IRP also generates a QR code. It contains important invoice details. Also Read – What Is GST on Personal Loan? Who needs to comply with the e-invoicing system? Not every business has to follow the GST e-invoice system. It applies only to businesses whose Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) crosses the limit notified by the government. This turnover is calculated on a PAN basis, meaning the turnover of all GST registrations under the same PAN is added together. E-invoicing mainly applies to B2B and export invoices. The current AATO limit for non-compliance with GST e-invoicing is Rs. 5 crore. Businesses with an annual aggregate turnover exceeding this limit must prepare e-GST invoices and generate IRNs for all eligible invoices. It’s important to note that once your business crosses the GST e-invoice applicable threshold, it becomes mandatory to comply with the system even if your turnover falls below the limit later. E-invoicing limit: Phased rollout history The GST e-invoice applicable threshold has been gradually reduced over the years to bring more businesses under this system. The rollout has happened in phases, as shown in the table below: Effective Date Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) Threshold October 2020 Rs. 500 crore January 2021 Rs. 100 crore April 2021 Rs. 50 crore April 2022 Rs. 20 crore October 2022 Rs. 10 crore August 2023 Rs. 5 crore There have also been reports that the government may further reduce the threshold to Rs. 2 crore, bringing many more MSMEs under the e-invoicing framework. Businesses should keep an eye on the latest notifications issued on the official GST portal. What counts as Aggregate Annual Turnover? The Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) is the combined turnover of all GST registrations (GSTINs) linked to the same PAN. It includes taxable sales, exports, exempt supplies, and inter-state supplies, but excludes GST collected on those transactions. For deciding e-invoicing applicability, the government checks whether your business crossed the prescribed turnover limit in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards, not just the current year. Who is exempt from e-invoicing? Some businesses and transactions are excluded from the GST e-invoice system, even if they meet the AATO threshold. These include: Banks, NBFCs , and insurance companies Goods Transport Agencies (GTAs) Businesses providing passenger transportation services Suppliers of admission tickets to cinemas and multiplexes SEZ units (however, SEZ developers are not exempt) B2C invoices, as e-invoicing is currently mandatory only for eligible B2B transactions and exports Businesses should still check the latest GST notifications, as the list of exemptions may be revised from time to time. Also Read – Advantages of GST for small businesses What documents are covered under e-invoicing? Under the e-invoice GST framework, eligible businesses must generate IRNs for the following documents: B2B tax invoices Credit notes issued for B2B transactions Debit notes issued for B2B transactions Export invoices At present, B2C invoices are generally outside the e-invoicing requirement. However, the government has introduced certain high-value reporting requirements for specific sectors from time to time. It is advisable to check the latest GST notifications for any updates. Also Read – How to calculate GST on a home loan? How to generate an e-invoice on the IRP? Generating a GST e-invoice is simple once your billing software is configured for e-invoicing. Here are the basic steps: Create the invoice in your GST-compliant billing or ERP software. The software automatically converts the invoice into the prescribed JSON format required under the e-invoicing system. Upload the JSON file to the IRP using an API, the offline utility, or other helpful software. The IRP validates the details and generates a unique IRN along with a digitally signed QR code. Share the validated invoice with your buyer/customer. The invoice details are also auto-populated into the relevant GST returns and e-way bills. What are the benefits of e-invoicing for MSMEs? The e-GST invoicing system offers several practical advantages for Micro, Small, and Medium enterprises (MSMEs) in India. These are: Reduces manual errors while preparing and reporting invoices. Makes it easier for buyers to claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) accurately. Helps auto-populate GST returns and e-way bill details, reducing duplicate data entry. Minimizes the risk of fake or duplicate invoices. Improves record-keeping and makes GST compliance more organized. Saves time by streamlining the overall invoicing and reporting process. What are the reporting time limits and penalties? As per the GSTN advisory issued on 5 th November 2024, eligible businesses must upload their GST e-invoices to the IRP within 30 days of issuance. Shorter timelines have also been reported for certain categories. Always verify the latest rule on the official GST portal. If an invoice that requires e-invoicing is issued without a valid IRN, it is treated as invalid under GST rules. This can prevent the buyer from claiming ITC and may also attract monetary penalties and other compliance consequences. How do e-invoicing and GST compliance support access to finance? Maintaining proper e-invoice GST records can do more than help with tax compliance. It also strengthens your business loan application by creating a clear record of sales, turnover, and GST filings. Many lenders, including Tata Capital, consider GST data while assessing eligibility and repayment capacity. Consistent compliance can improve your credibility and make the loan approval process smoother. If you are planning to expand your business, you can also explore Tata Capital’s Business Loan solutions. Conclusion The GST e-invoice system has become a regular compliance requirement for a growing number of MSMEs as the turnover threshold has been reduced over time. Learning whether e-invoice applicable rules cover your business can help you avoid penalties, ensure smooth ITC claims for your customers, and maintain accurate business records. If your turnover is close to the prescribed limit, it is wise to prepare in advance. Since the rules and thresholds may change, always verify the latest updates on the official GST portal. If you need funds to grow your business, you can apply for Tata Capital’s Business Loan. E-invoicing is a system where eligible businesses upload their B2B invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) for validation. The portal generates an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a QR code. The business still creates the invoice in its own accounting software; the government only authenticates it. What is the turnover limit for e-invoicing? The turnover limit for e-invoicing has been reduced in phases over the years. At present, the AATO limit for non-compliance with GST e-invoicing is Rs. 5 crore. Businesses with an annual aggregate turnover exceeding this limit must prepare e-GST invoices and generate IRNs for all eligible invoices. Since the limit may change from time to time, it is best to verify the latest notification on gst.gov.in. Is e-invoicing applicable to my business? E-invoicing applies only if your business crosses the turnover limit prescribed under GST. The limit is checked on a PAN basis by considering all GST registrations linked to that PAN. If your business falls within the notified criteria, eligible B2B and export invoices must be reported through the IRP. Who is exempt from e-invoicing under GST? Certain categories are kept outside the e-invoicing framework even if they meet the turnover criteria. These include banks, NBFCs, insurance companies, Goods Transport Agencies (GTAs), passenger transport service providers, cinema and multiplex ticket suppliers, and SEZ units. The government may revise this list, so checking the latest notification is advisable. Is e-invoicing mandatory for B2C transactions? No. At present, e-invoicing is mainly required for eligible B2B transactions and exports. Businesses generally do not have to generate an IRN for B2C invoices. However, separate QR code requirements or sector-specific rules may apply in some cases, depending on the latest GST notifications. How do I generate an e-invoice on the IRP? The process starts with preparing the invoice in your own accounting or billing software. Once it is ready, the invoice details are sent to the Invoice Registration Portal for validation. If everything is in order, the portal generates the IRN and QR code. The validated invoice can then be shared with your customer. What is an IRN in e-invoicing? IRN stands for Invoice Reference Number. It is a unique number generated by the Invoice Registration Portal after an eligible invoice is successfully validated. The IRN helps identify the invoice within the GST system and prevents the same invoice from being reported more than once. What is the penalty for not generating an e-invoice? If an eligible invoice is issued without a valid IRN, it is treated as non-compliant under GST rules. This may prevent the buyer from claiming Input Tax Credit (ITC) and can also lead to penalties or other action under the GST law. Timely compliance helps avoid such issues. semi-urban areas finance the purchase, construction, extension, or renovation of a house. Eligibility is generally flexible, making it easier for salaried, self-employed, and informal-income earners to apply. The interest rate depends on factors such as income, credit profile, and loan amount, while eligible borrowers may also benefit from government schemes like PMAY-Gramin. Understanding the eligibility criteria, required documents, and application process can help you choose the right home loan with confidence. A rural home loan is a housing loan that helps people in rural and semi-urban areas buy, build, extend, or renovate a home. For many families in villages and small towns, owning a house is still a dream. Arranging funds to buy land and construct a house can often feel out of reach. This is where products such as rural home loans can make a big difference. Also known as gramin home loans, these loans are designed to help people living in rural and semi-urban areas. They provide access to finances for purchasing, building, extending, or improving a home. In many cases, borrowers may also benefit from government initiatives such as PMAY-Gramin. In this blog guide, we have explained in detail what a rural home loan is, its special features, eligibility criteria, required documents, and the application process, among other things. We have also explained how PMAY Gramin Home Loans differ from regular home loans and how rural people can benefit from them. What is a rural home loan? A rural home loan is designed exclusively for people living in rural or semi-urban areas. It helps them access funds to buy, build, or renovate a house in these regions. A rural home loan is also known as a gramin home loan and is designed for both salaried and self-employed individuals. These may include farmers, workers, small business owners, and people with informal sources of income. What are the rural housing loan eligibility criteria? The rural housing loan eligibility criteria are slightly different from those for regular home loans because these loans are designed to meet the needs of rural and gramin households. Although the exact criteria vary from lender to lender, here are the factors that are mainly considered: Age: The applicant must fall within the lender’s prescribed age limit. Residential location: The applicant must be a citizen of India, residing in a rural or semi-urban area. Property location: The property to be purchased must also be in a rural or semi-urban location within the lender’s serviceable area. Employment status: Both salaried and self-employed applicants can apply. These may include farmers and workers with informal income. Credit score: Most lenders prefer applicants with satisfactory credit scores. A few lenders even provide rural home loans to applicants with bad or no credit history. What are the rural home loan interest rates? The rural home loan interest rate varies from one lender to another and typically starts from 7% to 9% per annum. The actual rate is determined using a combination of multiple factors, including the borrower’s CIBIL score , loan amount, repayment tenure, and the overall financial profile. Additionally, borrowers who qualify for PMAY Gramin Home Loans may receive an interest subsidy under the Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS), where applicable. It’s always advisable to compare loan offers from several lenders before making a decision. What is PMAY Gramin Home Loan? The PMAY Gramin Home Loan is linked to the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G). It is a government scheme that aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to eligible rural households. Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries can avail of a home loan at subsidized interest rates for the purchase or construction of a home. The PMAY Gramin Home Loans are provided by banks and authorized housing finance companies, subject to the lender’s eligibility criteria. It is important to note that eligibility under PMAY-G is determined separately from the lender’s loan approval process. Since scheme guidelines change from time to time, applicants must verify the latest eligibility criteria before applying. Also read – Planning to Take a Plot Loan? Some Important Rules You Need to Know What are the documents required for a rural home loan? Applicants are required to submit certain documents to prove that they meet the rural housing loan eligibility criteria . While the exact list may vary across lenders, here’s a common checklist of the documents required: KYC documents such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving License. Address proof , if different from the Aadhaar address. Income proof , such as salary slips, Form 16, or Income Tax Returns (ITR). Alternative income documents for farmers, self-employed individuals, or informal earners, wherever accepted by the lender. Property documents , including title papers, sale agreement, or other ownership-related records. Recent bank statements , as required by the lender. How to apply for a rural/gramin home loan? Eligible applicants can apply for a rural home loan in the following steps: Step 1 – Make sure you meet the lender’s rural housing loan eligibility criteria and the property falls within the lender’s serviceable area. Step 2 – Apply online by visiting the lender’s website or mobile app. Alternatively, there is an option of offline application through the lender’s nearest branch. Step 3 – Submit the required documents. These may include KYC , income, and property papers. Step 4 – Wait for the lender to complete the property and income assessment. Based on this, the lender decides whether to approve your rural home loan application. Step 5 – Receive the loan sanction and disbursal once all checks are successfully completed. Also read – Home loan application process in India What are the benefits of a rural home loan? A rural home loan offers several advantages for individuals and families looking to own or improve a home in rural or semi-urban areas. Helps buy, build, extend, or renovate a home in rural and semi-urban locations. Flexible income assessment for farmers, self-employed individuals, and informal earners. Eligible borrowers may benefit from PMAY assistance or subsidy, wherever applicable. A longer repayment tenure helps keep EMIs more affordable. Tax benefits on home loans may be available under the applicable provisions of the Income Tax Act. Supports better housing and improves long-term financial security for rural households. Also read – Guide for home loan sanction and disbursement process Conclusion A rural or gramin home loan can make the dream of owning a house more achievable for families in rural and semi-urban India. With flexible eligibility, convenient repayment options, and possible support under PMAY-G for eligible applicants, these loans can ease the financial burden of building or buying a home. However, it’s prudent to compare the rural home loan interest rates offered by different lenders and choose the option that best suits your needs. A rural home loan is a housing loan offered to people who want to buy, build, expand, or repair a house in a rural or semi-urban area. It works like a regular home loan, but is designed to meet the needs of borrowers living outside major cities, including farmers and self-employed individuals. What is the eligibility for a rural housing loan? To apply for a rural housing loan, you must generally be an Indian citizen, satisfy the lender's age criteria, and have enough income to repay the loan. The property should also fall within the lender's approved rural or semi-urban locations. The final eligibility may differ from one lender to another. What is the interest rate on a rural home loan? There is no single interest rate for every borrower. The rate depends on factors such as your credit score, income, repayment capacity, loan amount, and tenure. Since lenders may offer different rates, it is always worth comparing a few options before making a decision. What is PMAY-Gramin, and how does it help with a home loan? PMAY-Gramin is a government housing scheme that supports eligible rural families by providing financial assistance to build a permanent house. If the assistance is not enough to cover the full cost, you may also apply for a home loan separately, provided you meet the lender's eligibility conditions. Can self-employed or informal-income earners get a rural home loan? Yes. Many lenders consider applications from self-employed borrowers, farmers, shopkeepers, and people who earn through informal work. If regular salary slips are not available, the lender may accept other income-related documents or use alternative methods to assess your repayment ability. What documents are needed for a gramin home loan? Most lenders ask for identity proof, address proof, PAN, Aadhaar, income documents, bank statements, and property papers. If you do not have formal salary documents, you may be asked to submit other records that help establish your income and financial position. Can I get a rural home loan to construct or renovate a house? Yes. A rural home loan is not limited to buying a ready-made house. Depending on the lender's policy, you can also use it to build a new house, add extra rooms, or renovate and repair an existing home in a rural or semi-urban area. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary A salary advance loan is a short-term borrowing option that helps salaried employees manage unexpected expenses before their next payday. It offers quick approval, minimal documentation, and fast disbursal without requiring any collateral. It is different from an employer’s salary advance, which is given by your employer and adjusted from your next salary. Understanding the eligibility criteria, interest rates, fees, and required documents is crucial before applying. Furthermore, borrowing only what you need and planning repayment carefully can help you use this facility wisely. A salary advance loan is a short-term loan that helps salaried individuals borrow money before their next salary to meet urgent financial needs. Rohit works as an IT professional in a private company. A few days before his salary was due, the plumbing in his house suddenly broke down and needed immediate repairs. The bill was higher than he expected, and the money left in his bank account wasn’t enough to cover the expense. Waiting until payday wasn’t an option. That’s when one of his colleagues suggested taking out a salary advance loan. Also known as an advance salary loan or simply a salary loan, it gives salaried individuals quick access to funds based on their regular monthly income. In this article, we’ll explain how this loan works, who can apply, the eligibility criteria, interest rates, and the steps to get one when you need it. What is a salary advance loan? A salary advance loan is a short-term personal loan designed for salaried employees who need urgent funds before their next paycheque arrives. It allows them to borrow a small amount to manage an urgent expense and repay it within a short period. These loans are typically meant for temporary financial needs rather than long-term borrowing. The primary objective of an advance salary loan is to help you bridge the financial gap between your salary and unexpected expenses without disrupting your regular budget. For example, imagine it’s the 15th of the month, and you suddenly need money for an emergency, but your next salary is still 15 days away. In such a situation, you can opt for a salary loan to cover the shortfall and repay it later in accordance with the lender’s repayment terms. How does an advance salary loan work? An advance salary loan works more or less like a normal personal loan . However, it is designed for smaller borrowing needs and must be repaid within a short tenure. Here’s how the process looks: You apply for a salary advance loan with a lender and submit the required documents. The lender assesses your monthly salary or income to determine your repayment capacity. Based on this, the lender sanctions a short-term loan (often up to 1-3 times your monthly salary). The funds are disbursed to your bank account quickly (sometimes within a few hours). You repay the loan through EMIs or when your next salary arrives. What are the features and benefits of a salary advance loan? An advance salary loan comes with certain unique features that make it suitable for urgent, short-term financial needs. Quick/instant approval and disbursal: Salary loans are often approved and disbursed quickly, sometimes within a few hours. Collateral-free: These loans are collateral-free . It means that you are not required to pledge an asset to qualify for financing. Small-ticket size: Loan amounts are usually smaller. However, they are enough to cover short-term financial needs. Minimal documentation: You are required to submit only a few basic documents, including proof of identity, address, and salary. Short tenures: The loan must be repaid within a short period. It can be for a few months or even your next salary date. Fully digital application: You can apply for a salary advance loan online without visiting a branch even once. The loan is processed and disbursed digitally. What is the difference between a salary advance loan and an employer salary advance? An advance salary loan is very different from an employer’s salary advance. It is offered by a bank or a non-banking financial institution and entails repayment and interest. An employer’s salary advance, on the other hand, is paid by your employer from your next salary. You are not required to repay it to your employer. There are no interest charges as well. Basis Advance Salary Loan Employer’s Advance Salary Provider A bank or NBFC Your employer Source A loan that has to be repaid An advance from your next salary Interest Applicable Not applicable Employer’s Involvement No Yes What are the eligibility criteria for a salary advance loan? To avail of a salary loan, you must meet the following eligibility criteria: You should be aged between 18 and 60 years. You must be a salaried employee with a registered employer. You must fulfill the lender’s minimum monthly income criterion. You should not have changed your company recently. You should have a credit score of 700 or above. It’s important to note that the eligibility criteria might vary from one lender to another. For example, some lenders might even offer advance salary loans to employees with lower credit scores . Whereas some lenders may require a minimum of 2 to 3 years of work experience with the current employer. Hence, you must check your eligibility with a lender before applying. What are the interest rates, charges, and documents for salary loans? Salary loan interest rates may vary from one lender to another. The final rate depends on factors such as your credit score, monthly income, and employment stability. Apart from the interest rate, a lender may levy a one-time processing fee, GST, and stamp duty (as applicable). Other charges might include foreclosure fees, late payment penalties, EMI bounce fees, and loan cancelation charges. The documents required for an advance salary loan might include: KYC documents: Aadhaar card, PAN card, Voter ID, Driving license, or Passport Proof of address (if different from KYC documents): Recent electricity or telephone bills or a rent agreement Proof of income: Latest salary slips or Form 16 Bank statements or a canceled cheque Latest passport-sized photographs How to apply for a salary advance loan online? Applying for a salary loan online is easy and straightforward: Step 1 – Check if you are eligible to apply for a salary advance loan with a lender. Step 2 – Apply online by filling out an application form on the lender’s website or mobile app. Step 3 – Upload the KYC documents , salary slips, and bank statements. Step 4 – Wait for the lender to verify your loan application and provide quick approval. Step 5 – Get the funds disbursed into your bank account. Some lenders provide instant or same-day disbursements based on your income and credit profile. For quick funds, you can check and apply for a Tata Capital Personal Loan. What are the things to keep in mind before taking a salary advance loan? You must keep these points in mind when you apply for an advance salary loan: Borrow only what you need. Make sure the EMI or repayment amount comfortably fits within your next salary and monthly budget. Review the repayment schedule, tenure, and other terms carefully before accepting the loan offer.
