Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Franchising offers one of the most attractive paths to business ownership. But get a proven brand, an established system, and a ready customer base. But even with lower risk than starting from scratch, the upfront franchise fee, setup costs, and working capital requirements can be a significant hurdle for most aspiring franchise owners. That’s where franchise business loans come in. Whether you’re looking to open a quick-service restaurant, a retail outlet, or a service franchise, the right financing can make the difference between getting started and staying stuck. This guide covers everything you need to know – what a franchise loan in India is, who qualifies, what documents you need, interest rates to expect, and how to apply step by step. What is a Franchise Business Loan? A franchise business loan is financing that helps you cover the costs of setting up and running a franchise. This includes the franchise fee paid to the franchisor, interior setup, equipment, stock, and initial working capital. It is not a separate loan product by itself. In most cases, it is a standard business loan applied for to fund a franchise. Franchise loans are generally unsecured, meaning you may not need to pledge collateral. Lenders like Tata Capital consider franchise business loans relatively lower risk because the franchisee is operating under a proven brand with an established business model, making approval more straightforward compared to an independent startup. Why Do You Need a Loan to Open a Franchise? Opening a franchise involves more than just the franchise fee. Most aspiring franchisees underestimate the total capital required, which is why a business loan to start a franchise is often essential. Typical costs you will need to cover include: Franchise fee Store setup and interiors Equipment and machinery Initial inventory Security deposit Working capital buffer A loan to open a franchise ensures you are not stretching personal savings thin from day one. Read More – Starbucks franchise in India Types of Loans to Fund a Franchise There are several options for franchise loans in India: Unsecured Business or Term Loan : This is the fastest route to funding, as no collateral is needed. It is also suitable for most standard franchise setups. Tata Capital Business Loans are a strong fit here. Working Capital Loan : This covers day-to-day operational expenses once the franchise is up and running. Loan Against Property: This is suited for larger franchise investments. It offers higher loan amounts at lower interest rates by pledging property as security. Government-Backed MSME Schemes: Options like Mudra and CGTMSE provide collateral-free franchise loans for eligible small and micro franchise businesses at subsidised rates. Eligibility for a Franchise Business Loan Here is what most lenders look for when you apply for franchise business loans in India: Your age must be between 21 and 65 years at the time of application. You must be an Indian citizen or resident. Existing business owners need 2 to 3 years of operational history. Minimum turnover requirements vary by lender but are generally upwards of ₹10 lakhs. A CIBIL score of 700 or above. A signed or in-principle agreement with a recognised brand strengthens your application considerably when learning how to get a franchise loan. Documents Required for a Franchise Loan Keep these ready before you apply for a business loan for a franchise: KYC and Personal Documents: Aadhaar Card PAN Card Address proof (Aadhaar, Driving Licence, or Passport) Business and Financial Documents: Last 2 years’ ITR Last 6 months’ bank statements GST registration certificate Business plan with projected financials Franchise agreement or letter of intent from the franchisor The franchise agreement is particularly important as many lenders treat it as a key document when evaluating franchise business loans. Franchise Loan Interest Rates and Charges Interest rates on franchise business loans in India depend on your CIBIL score, loan amount, repayment tenure, and the strength of the franchise brand you are partnering with. A well-known franchisor can actually work in your favour with lenders. Loan Type Indicative Interest Rate Processing Fee Unsecured Business Loan 12% – 24% p.a. 1% – 3% of the loan amount Loan Against Property 9% – 15% p.a. 0.5% – 2% of the loan amount Government MSME Schemes 8% – 12% p.a. Minimal or nil All rates are indicative and subject to change. Tata Capital offers competitive rates on franchise loans in India. Use a franchise loan calculator before applying to map your EMI against projected monthly revenue and ensure repayments are manageable. How to Get a Franchise Loan: Step-by-Step? Here is how to get a franchise loan in India: Step 1: Finalise your franchise and get the agreement Choose a recognised brand and secure a signed franchise agreement or letter of intent from the franchisor. This is the foundation of your loan application. Step 2: Estimate your total funding requirement Add up the franchise fee, setup costs, equipment, inventory, security deposit, and working capital buffer to arrive at the exact loan amount you need. Step 3: Check your eligibility Review your CIBIL score, business vintage, and turnover against lender requirements before applying. Step 4: Look at interest rates, processing fees, tenure, and prepayment terms. Do not apply with multiple lenders simultaneously, as it can affect your credit score. Step 5: Apply online with Tata Capital Fill out the application form on Tata Capital’s website with accurate details to avoid processing delays. Step 6: Submit your documents Upload KYC, ITR, bank statements, GST certificate, business plan, and the franchise agreement. Step 7: Await approval and disbursal Once verified, your business loan to start a franchise is typically approved and disbursed within a few working days. Read More – Business Loan to Open Your Coffee Shop Franchise How to Apply for a Franchise Loan with Tata Capital? Applying for franchise business loans with Tata Capital is easy: Visit tatacapital.com and navigate to the Business Loan section. Fill in your basic details like loan amount, business type, and contact information. Upload your KYC, financial documents, and franchise agreement. Get an instant eligibility check and loan offer. Accept the terms and receive disbursal directly to your account. Ready to get started? Apply for a business loan for a franchise with Tata Capital today. Tips to Improve Your Franchise Loan Approval Chances A few practical steps can significantly strengthen your application when figuring out how to get a franchise loan: Choose a recognised franchise brand, as lenders are more confident in established names with a proven track record. Maintain a healthy CIBIL score of 700 or above. Prepare a solid business plan, including revenue projections, break-even timelines, and cost estimates. Keep ITR and bank statements clean to improve credibility. Contribute 20% to 30% of the total cost from your own pocket. This shows commitment and reduces lender risk in franchise loans in India. Conclusion Franchising offers a simple path to business ownership, and financing it is more straightforward than most people expect. With the right preparation, getting approved for franchise business loans in India is well within reach. Whether you are a first-time franchise owner or expanding an existing setup, the right lender makes all the difference. Check your eligibility and explore Tata Capital’s Business Loan options to take your franchise loan in India journey forward today. A franchise business loan is financing used to cover the costs of setting up and running a franchise, including the franchise fee, store setup, equipment, inventory, and working capital. It is not a separate product but a standard business loan applied specifically to fund franchise loans and related expenses. How can I get a loan to start a franchise in India? To get a franchise loan in India, finalise your franchise agreement, estimate total costs, check your CIBIL score, and compare lenders. Apply online with a lender like Tata Capital with your KYC, ITR, bank statements, and franchise agreement. A strong application makes your business loan to start a franchise easier to approve. How much loan can I get for a franchise business? The loan amount for franchise business loans in India varies by lender, your credit profile, and the franchise brand. Unsecured business loans typically go up to a few crores, while secured options offer higher amounts. Your franchise loan in India limit is usually based on turnover, repayment capacity, and total project cost. Can I get a franchise loan without collateral? Yes. Most franchise business loans from NBFCs and lenders like Tata Capital are unsecured, meaning no collateral is required. Government-backed schemes like Mudra and CGTMSE also offer collateral-free options. How to get a franchise loan without security depends largely on your CIBIL score, business profile, and the franchisor's reputation. What documents are required for a franchise loan? To apply for a business loan for a franchise, you typically need your Aadhaar, PAN, address proof, last 2 years' ITR, 6 months' bank statements, GST certificate, a business plan with projections, and the franchise agreement or letter of intent. The franchise agreement is particularly important as it validates your business model. How do I calculate the EMI for a franchise loan? Use a franchise loan calculator available on most lender websites, including Tata Capital. Enter your loan amount, interest rate, and repayment tenure to get your monthly EMI instantly. This helps you plan repayments against projected monthly revenue before committing to a loan and ensures the facility stays affordable. Can a first-time entrepreneur get a franchise loan? course. Whether you have a routine question about your EMI, need an interest certificate for your tax filing, or want to explore your foreclosure options, knowing exactly how to reach your lender quickly makes all the difference. Tata Capital makes this simple by offering multiple support channels like phone, email, WhatsApp, and a self-service customer portal, so you are never left waiting without options. This guide covers each of these channels in detail, including the most important Tata Capital finance customer care numbers, so that you can always find the fastest route to a resolution. Tata Capital Customer Care Numbers For most loan and account queries, a phone is the fastest way to get to a resolution. Tata Capital’s primary customer care number is 1860-267-6060, and you can also write to customercare@tatacapital.com. The helpline is available between 9 AM and 8 PM, except on Sundays and public holidays. Purpose Contact Availability General finance and loan queries 1860 267 6060 9 AM-8 PM (Mon–Sat) Email support customercare@tatacapital.com Business hours Microfinance and rural individual loans 1800 209 9809 Business hours Complaints and escalations 1860 267 6060 9 AM – 8 PM (Mon–Sat) Tata Capital Finance Customer Care Number The main Tata Capital finance customer care number 1860-267-6060 connects you to support for personal loans , business loans , home loans , EMI queries, account statements, and general account management. If your query isn’t resolved at the first level, you can escalate by writing to customercare@tatacapital.com or submitting a complaint through Tata Capital’s grievance page. How to Reach a Customer Care Executive by Phone? Calling the Tata Capital finance customer care number will connect you to an automated IVR system first. Here’s how to navigate it to reach a live executive as quickly as possible: 1. Call the helpline: Dial the Tata Capital finance customer care number listed on tatacapital.com. 2. Select your preferred language: The IVR will offer you a choice of languages at the first prompt. 3. Choose your loan or product type: Select the option that corresponds to your loan from options like personal loan, business loan, home loan, or any other product. 4. Select your query type : Choose from the available options: EMI payment, account statement, foreclosure, loan status, or other queries. 6. Press the option to speak to an executive : Most IVR systems have a dedicated option to be connected to a live customer care executive. If you don’t hear it listed, pressing ‘0’ or ‘*’ usually triggers it. 7. Wait to be connected : Hold times vary depending on the time of day; calling during non-peak hours (early morning or mid-afternoon on weekdays) typically gets you through faster. Tip : Before you call, keep your loan account number and the mobile number registered with Tata Capital ready. The executive will use these to pull up your account quickly, which speeds up the entire interaction. How to Reach Tata Capital via the Customer Portal? If you’d prefer not to call, the Tata Capital customer portal lets you raise service requests, track their status, and request a callback. Here’s how to get there: Go to tatacapital.com and open the official Tata Capital website in your browser. You’ll find the login option in the top navigation bar of the homepage. Select the appropriate portal for your profile. Most individual borrowers will use the Retail Login; sales partners and DSAs use a separate Sales Login. You can sign in using your User ID and password, or log in with your registered mobile number via OTP (see the Login with Mobile Number section below). Once you’re inside your account dashboard, look for the Help, Support, or Service Requests section. Submit your question as a service request, or use the callback option if you’d prefer a Tata Capital executive to reach out to you. Using the Tata Capital portal login to raise a request also gives you a ticket or reference number, which makes it easier to track progress and follow up if needed. Tata Capital Retail Login The Tata Capital retail login is for individual customers, anyone who holds a personal loan, home loan, business loan, or any other retail lending product with Tata Capital. To access it: Go to tatacapital.com and click Login in the top navigation. Select the Retail customer option. Enter your Tata Capital User ID or registered mobile number. Complete the OTP verification or enter your password to access your dashboard. Once you’re logged in, you can view your loan account, download statements, raise service requests, and reach customer support through the portal. Tata Capital Sales Login The Tata Capital sales login is a separate portal for sales partners, channel partners, and Direct Selling Agents (DSAs), not for individual retail borrowers. If you’re a borrower looking to manage your loan account or reach customer support, this login is not the right one for you. Sales partners can access their portal through the Login section on tatacapital.com by selecting the appropriate partner or sales login option. For account-related queries, retail customers should use the Retail Login described above. Login with Mobile Number (OTP) If you don’t remember your Tata Capital User ID or password, Tata Capital login with mobile number is the fastest way to access your account. Here’s how: Go to tatacapital.com and click Login. Select the Retail login option. Choose the ‘Login with Mobile Number’ or OTP option. Enter your registered mobile number and click Send OTP. Enter the OTP received on your phone to access your account. This is the quickest route to the Tata Capital login portal for most customers, and it works as long as you have access to the mobile number you registered with Tata Capital. How to Reach Tata Capital via Email? If your query isn’t urgent and you’d prefer a written record of your query, you can reach Tata Capital customer support by email. When writing in, include your loan account number, your registered mobile number or email address, and a clear description of your query or issue. This helps the support team locate your account and respond accurately without going back and forth. The current customer care email address is customercare@tatacapital.com. Please verify the email address on the site before writing in, as contact details are subject to change. How to Reach Tata Capital via WhatsApp / Chat? Tata Capital also offers support through WhatsApp and a website chat option, which can be a convenient alternative if you want a faster response than email but don’t want to call. The WhatsApp channel typically connects you to a chatbot first, which can handle common queries like account balance, EMI due dates, and payment confirmation without needing a live agent. If your query is more complex, you can request to be escalated to a live executive through the chat itself. The current WhatsApp number is 7506756060 . Verify these details on the site before reaching out, as channels and availability may change. Reasons to Contact a Tata Capital Customer Care Executive Here are some of the most common reasons customers reach out. If any of these apply to you, the contact channels above will get you to the right place: 1. EMI and payment queries: Questions about your upcoming EMI, missed payments, payment confirmation, or auto-debit issues. 2. Account statement or interest certificate: Requesting a loan statement, interest certificate for tax purposes, or repayment schedule. 3. Foreclosure or part-prepayment: Understanding your foreclosure charges, requesting a foreclosure quote, or initiating a part-prepayment. 4. No-Objection Certificate (NOC) : Requesting an NOC after full loan repayment. 5. Portal login or password issues : Trouble accessing your Tata Capital retail login or resetting your credentials. 6. Updating contact details: Changing your registered mobile number, email address, or mailing address 7. Loan status enquiry : Checking the disbursement status of a new loan application 8. Complaints and escalations: Raising a formal complaint or escalating an unresolved issue to a senior team Tips for a Faster Resolution A little preparation before you reach out can cut down the time it takes to resolve your query: 1. Keep your loan account number ready: This is the single most important piece of information the executive will need to pull up your account. 2. Call from your registered mobile number: Many IVR systems can identify you automatically if you call from the number linked to your loan account, which skips the verification step. 3. Note your ticket or request ID: If you raise a request through the Tata Capital portal login, save the reference number so you can track progress and quote it in follow-up calls. 4. Call during non-peak hours: Early mornings (9-11 AM) and mid-afternoons on weekdays tend to have shorter wait times than lunch hours or late afternoons. 5. Use the portal for non-urgent requests: The Tata Capital login portal is well-suited for requests that don’t need an immediate response, and gives you a written record of everything. Conclusion Tata Capital gives you several ways to reach a customer care executive: by phone using the Tata Capital finance customer care number, through the customer portal, via email, or on WhatsApp. For most account and loan queries, the portal is the most convenient starting point since it lets you raise requests, track them, and access your account details in one place. If you need to speak to someone directly, the phone helpline remains the fastest route. How do I talk to a Tata Capital customer care executive? To speak to a live executive, call the Tata Capital finance customer care number listed on tatacapital.com and follow the IVR prompts: select your language, then your loan type, then your query category, and finally choose the option to speak to an executive. If you can't locate the option in the menu, pressing '0' or '*' often connects you directly. How do I log in to the Tata Capital retail portal? To access the Tata Capital retail login, go to tatacapital.com, click Login in the top navigation, and select the Retail customer option. You can sign in using your User ID and password, or choose the mobile number and OTP route if you don't have your credentials handy. What is the Tata Capital sales login? The Tata Capital sales login is a portal for sales partners, channel partners, and DSAs, not for individual retail borrowers. If you're a customer looking to manage your personal or business loan account, you should use the Retail Login instead. How do I log in to Tata Capital with my mobile number? To use Tata Capital login with mobile number, go to tatacapital.com and click Login, then select the Retail option and choose the OTP or mobile number login route. Enter your registered mobile number, click Send OTP, and then enter the code received on your phone to access your account. Can I raise a complaint through the Tata Capital portal? Once you're logged in through the Tata Capital portal login, you can navigate to the Help or Service Requests section and raise a formal complaint or service request directly. You'll receive a ticket reference number that you can use to track the status of your complaint and follow up if needed. Is Tata Capital customer care available 24x7? Availability depends on the channel. The Tata Capital finance customer care number operates during specific business hours. The customer portal, on the other hand, is accessible 24x7 for self-service actions like viewing statements and raising service requests. Many people wonder how to get 1.5 lakh loan support instantly, especially when expenses can’t wait. If you’re thinking, “I need 1.5 lakh rupees urgently, what should I do?” an instant 1.5 lakh loan can help you manage such situations smoothly. Tata Capital offers a convenient option to secure an instant personal loan of 1.5 lakh, making the process quick and stress-free. With an instant loan upto 1.5 lakhs, you can access the required funds quickly and conveniently without dipping into your savings. Understanding the instant 1.5 lakh personal loan An instant personal loan 1.5 lakh provides flexible financial assistance. It is suitable for short-term necessities such as emergency medical bills or house repairs , and it can be paid off over several months to several years. Interest rates differ per lender and credit profile, usually ranging from 10% to 20%. For example, the Equated Monthly Instalment (EMI) at a rate of 15% interest for a period of two years would come to about INR 7,352. However, rates change, which has an impact on EMIs. To properly manage this loan in your budget, consider understanding the repayment terms and affordability as the priority before deciding how to get a 1.5 lakh loan. Also, read – What is Moratorium Period What are the eligibility criteria to get a loan of Rs. 1.5 lakh? To get a small personal loan from Tata Capital, you must fulfil the following eligibility criteria for an instant 1.5 lakh loan : – You must have a minimum salary of Rs. 15,000 – You must have at least 1 year of work experience – Your age must be between 22 and 58 years Meeting these conditions increases your chances of approval for an instant personal loan upto 1.5 lakh . Also, read – What is lien amount Factors affecting your instant 1.5 lakh loan approval Understanding the key 1.5 lakh loan approval factors can help you apply more confidently and improve your chances of securing funds without delays. Lenders review a combination of your financial behaviour, income stability, and application details before approving an instant loan. Here are the major points they consider: 1. Credit score and repayment history Your credit score is one of the strongest indicators of your creditworthiness. A higher score improves your chances of fast approval for instant loan upto 1.5 lakh , while late payments or frequent EMI delays can slow things down. 2. Monthly income and employment stability Lenders assess whether your monthly income is sufficient to handle the new EMI. Steady employment or consistent business income reassures lenders about your repayment capacity when deciding how to get 1.5 lakh loan approved quickly. 3. Debt-to-income ratio If a large portion of your monthly earnings is already tied up in EMIs or credit card payments, lenders may hesitate. Keeping your financial obligations low is one of the most effective quick loan approval tips . 4. Accuracy of your application details Simple errors in your PAN, Aadhaar, or bank details can lead to verification delays. Ensuring accurate documentation is one of the most effective ways to get your instant 1.5 lakh loan approved smoothly. 5. Bank account behaviour Healthy account activity, such as regular credits, minimal cheque bounces, and stable balances, helps lenders trust your financial habits. 6. Existing relationship with the lender If you have an account, card, or previous loan with the lender, your approval process may be smoother. A positive track record can lead to faster decision-making and your instant personal loan 1.5 lakh application may be processed faster. Also, read – What is loan Modification How can you apply for a 1.5 lakh personal loan? You can easily apply for an instant personal loan upto 1.5 lakh with Tata Capital online and offline. Here’s how: 1. Online application process Follow these steps to apply for a small personal loan online: Step 1 – Visit Tata Capital’s official website and navigate to the small personal loans page. Step 2 – Click ‘Apply Now’ and fill in the required details. Step 3 – Upload soft copies of the required documents and click ‘Submit’. That’s it. We’ll verify the information and get back to you in a few minutes. 2. Offline application process If you’re not comfortable applying online, you can also submit your application offline. Here’s how: Step 1 – Visit your nearest Tata Capital branch. Step 2 – Submit the short personal loan application along with the required documents. You can also contact a Tata Capital agent over the phone. We will verify your loan application and documents, and if there are no discrepancies, your instant loan upto 1.5 lakh application will be approved, and our team will guide you for the next steps. Also, read – What is subsidized Loan Calculate your 1.5 lakh loan EMI Before applying for a personal loan, it’s important to understand how much you will pay every month. Your 1.5 lakh loan EMI depends on the interest rate, repayment tenure, and the EMI structure offered by the lender. While a longer tenure reduces your monthly instalment, it increases the total interest paid. A shorter tenure does the opposite: higher EMIs but lower overall interest. To calculate EMI for 1.5 lakh loan accurately, you can use the Tata Capital Personal Loan EMI Calculator . Just enter the loan amount, interest rate, and preferred tenure to get an instant breakdown of your monthly repayment for your instant personal loan upto 1.5 lakh . This tool helps you compare different repayment options and pick one that comfortably fits your income. Using an EMI calculator also gives you a clear picture of your instant loan EMI , helping you plan your budget better and avoid repayment stress. It ensures you choose a loan structure that aligns with your financial goals. Key features & benefits of an instant Rs. 1.5 lakh personal loan An instant personal loan 1.5 lakh withTata Capital is one of the fastest ways to access funds for emergencies or planned expenses. Understanding the key 1.5 lakh personal loan features helps you make a more informed borrowing decision. Here are the major instant personal loan benefits you can enjoy with Tata Capital: 1. Fast digital approval One of the biggest advantages of instant loan options is speed. You can apply online on the Tata Capital website, upload basic details, and get approval within minutes, making it ideal for urgent financial needs. 2. Minimal documentation Instant loans generally require only essential KYC and income proof. Tata Capital has a simple and hassle-free process in place, perfect for urgent needs requiring an instant 1.5 lakh loan . 3. Flexible repayment tenure You can choose a repayment tenure that aligns with your monthly budget. Whether you prefer lower EMIs over a longer period or quicker repayment with a shorter tenure, the flexibility is entirely yours. 4. No collateral needed Our personal loans are unsecured, meaning you don’t have to pledge property or assets. This is one of the key advantages of instant loans at Tata Capital. 5. Direct transfer to your bank account Once approved, the loan amount is disbursed directly into your bank account. 6. Flexible end use Another major instant personal loan benefit is that you can use the funds for almost any purpose, medical expenses, education needs, travel, home repairs, or even consolidating debt. Documents required for instant 1.5 lakh loan At Tata Capital, you enjoy a minimal documentation process, so you only need to provide a few essential papers. These instant loan documents help verify your identity, address, income, and employment details, ensuring faster approval for a personal loan. Here are the key documents for 1.5 lakh loan applications: 1. Photo identity proof A copy of your Voter ID, Passport, driving licence, or Aadhaar card to confirm your identity. 2. Address proof Any valid document such as your Voter ID, Passport, driving licence, or Aadhaar card to verify your residential address. 3. Salary slips Copies of your latest two months’ salary slips to help lenders understand your monthly income. 4. Bank statement A statement of your primary bank account (usually your salary account) for the last three months to review your financial activity. 5. Employment certificate A certificate confirming at least one year of continuous employment with your current organisation. With this minimal documentation , lenders can complete verification quickly, making the instant loan upto 1.5 lakh approval process smooth and hassle-free. Conclusion: Getting your instant 1.5 lakh loan When faced with an urgent financial need, knowing how to get 1.5 lakh loan quickly can make the situation easier to handle. Tata Capital’s Personal Loan can be a reliable solution. We have a quick, hassle-free, and streamlined process that ensures you get access to funds within 24 hours. You can submit your loan application online or offline and manage your financial emergencies with ease. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Today credit cards are everywhere, flooding wallets across the globe. One does not even consider them a novelty item when they swap or tap their cards to pay for their shopping. But credit cards weren’t always plastic cards that made payments with a tap on a POS machine. Credit cards have been around for over 70 years in one form or the other. First introduced as a piece of cardboard, credit cards are now contactless. But ever since their inception, credit cards have transformed the global economy, and India isn’t untouched by them either. In this blog, we will look back at the use of credit cards in India. We will explore how and when they arrived in the country. But before moving forward to the evolution of credit cards in India, let’s trace back their original roots. What is Credit Card A credit card is a payment tool that lets you borrow money from a bank to make purchases and repay it later through a monthly bill. Understanding what is the use of credit card in India is important because it helps you manage expenses, build credit history, and access short-term credit easily. The benefits of using credit card in India include cashback, rewards, discounts, EMI options, and secure payments. To get the best use of credit card in India , you should spend responsibly, pay bills on time, and use card benefits that match your lifestyle and financial goals. Also, read – Outstanding Balance: What It Means and How It Affects You? Types of Credit Cards There are several types of credit cards designed for different spending needs. Common credit card categories include: Credit Cards for First-Time Users: Basic cards with simple features and low annual fees. Good for people who are using a credit card for the first time. Credit Cards for Low-Income Earners: Affordable cards that charge little to no annual fees and offer benefits that suit limited budgets. Travel Credit Cards: These cards give extra benefits while travelling, like airport lounge access, bonus reward points, and special deals with travel brands. Shopping Credit Cards: Made for frequent shoppers, these cards offer rewards or cashback on online and offline shopping and give special discounts. Airline Credit Cards: Launched with airline companies, these cards help you save on flights through air miles, discounts, and travel upgrades. Rewards Credit Cards: They offer reward points on most spends, and extra points on certain categories like dining or groceries. Cashback Credit Cards: Instead of reward points, these cards give direct cashback on eligible purchases, which reduces your monthly bill. Such credit card variants help consumers pick the kind of credit card that fits their financial habits. Also, read – What is the Maximum Credit Limit on a Credit Card in India? Benefits of Credit Cards In case you’re wondering why use credit cards, we’re here to tell you that the benefits of credit card in India start with the primary convenience of “Buy Now and Pay Later.” Not just that, credit card perks range from convenience to rewards. Key advantages of credit cards include interest-free periods, cashback, reward points, and exclusive discounts on travel, dining, and shopping. Many cards come with EMI conversion, making large purchases easier to manage. Additional credit card features often include airport lounge access, insurance cover , and fuel surcharge waivers. Used responsibly, credit card benefits extend to building a strong credit score, improving financial flexibility, and providing secure, traceable payments, making them a valuable tool for everyday spending. Also, read – What are Finance Charges in Credit Cards? Best Ways to Use a Credit Card Smartly The benefits of using credit card in India go beyond convenience. When used properly, it becomes a powerful financial tool. To get the best use of credit card in India , you need to understand what is the use of credit card in India : building credit, earning rewards, and managing payments smoothly. Here are some simple ways to practise smart credit card usage every day: Pay your full bill on time to avoid interest Keep your utilisation below 30% to manage credit card smartly Use rewards, cashback, and offers that match your spending Enable alerts to track expenses and due dates Avoid cash withdrawals and unplanned EMIs Review statements monthly to stay in control Following these credit card usage best practices ensures you not only enjoy rewards but also protect your financial health. When you know how to use credit card wisely and follow the credit card tips listed above, it becomes a safe and effective way to manage money in India. Also, read – 10 Reasons Why Your Credit Card Was Rejected Even with A Good Credit Score Tracing the modern credit card history Modern credit cards have a fascinating story. Like most inventions, it was an individual’s quest to solve a problem once and for all. We can trace back the genesis to the moment in 1949 when a man forgot his wallet at home. In 1949, Frank McNamara, a New York City businessman, was at New York City’s famous restaurant Major’s Cabin Grill. He forgot his wallet at home and couldn’t pay the bill. Luckily, his wife saved him and paid the bill. McNamara determined never to face this embarrassment again, got the idea of a first credit card. He, along with Ralph Schneider, founded the Diner’s Club, the world’s first credit card. The Diner’s Club began with cardboard cards for a few selected men at 27 restaurants. Although Diner’s Club credit cards were elite, they were tailored with cardboard. But then came the era of credit cards as we know them today, and all sorts of plastic credit cards flooded the world. To its credit, American Express introduced the first plastic credit card in 1959, followed by Bank of America, Carte Blanche, Diner’s Club, and other new credit card firms. Then, in 1969, IBM engineer Forrest Parry devised the modern magnetic strip that could be attached to a plastic card. As imprinting got replaced by magnetic strips, credit cards with computer chips are replacing magnetic stripes. Embedded computer chips, known as EMV smart chips, enable encrypted, two-way authentication between a merchant’s credit card terminal and the payment processing network. They created trust and reliability among credit card users. Also, read – What is Credit Appraisal History of use of credit card in India The introduction of credit cards in India was the beginning of a new era which changed the face of the Indian economy completely. Kali Mody was the first businessman from India to introduce the Diners Club credit card in India in 1961, a year after it was initially made available globally. Later, the Central Bank of India issued the first bank credit card in 1980. But Andhra Bank was the one which aroused the public interest in credit cards with its Visa cards. To compete with the growing popularity of Visa cards, Vijaya Bank introduced Mastercard and became the first bank in India to do so. Even back then, it was not easy to qualify for a credit card in India unless your income lies within the annual minimum capacity. But, between 1988 and 1993, against the constraints, multiple PSU banks took the bold step of giving credit cards to many of their selected clients. Also, read – Cash Credit Loan Future of credit cards in India Credit card acceptance in India was initially in the dark shadow, which slowly started to soar over time. People have started showing interest in credit cards as they were offered more benefits than debit cards. Also, the growing financial literacy among the youth is driving this change. Approximately Rs 6 lakh crore was spent in 2018-19 using credit cards in India, which was 30% more than in 2017. However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, credit card transactions fell drastically from March to May 2020. But, as the economy got back on track, credit card usage increased. According to the stats, the use of credit cards in India has been estimated for more than 6.78 lakh ATM transactions and approx. 12.1 crore POS transactions in June 2022. The popularity of credit cards in the mainstream Indian population is gradually increasing. It is predicted to rise continuously by 2.6 million cards between 2023 and 2028. The forecast shows there will be approx. 45.3 million cards in use in 2028. Another reason why the use of credit cards is increasing is the sheer number of issuers in the country. Today, one is not restricted to only banks to get a credit card. Currently, NBFCs are gaining popularity by providing credit on e-commerce and other platforms to customers with perfectly tailored no-cost or low-cost EMI options. Besides, there is a wave of fin-tech startups onboarding younger clients into the credit card ecosystem. They rely on tech and mobile apps to make credit convenient and offer tons of rewards to users. Conclusion A credit card in India has historically been viewed as a debt trap tool due to cultural restrictions and a lack of financial awareness. However, the young generation is firmly committed to altering this paradigm by raising knowledge that they understand the practicality of using a credit card in India. They use their cards for daily purchases, online shopping, and bulk payments. Traditionally, the Indian credit industry was mostly traditional banking oriented. But now, NBFCs are changing the scenario with new innovative products and initiatives, offers, rewards, low interest and processing fees. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund COVID-19 brought in its wake one of the gravest economic crises Indians have ever witnessed. And loan borrowers had to face the worst of it, as they had to manage their EMIs alongside a cash shortage. Many borrowers face such financial pressure due to different emergencies and situations in their lives. Fortunately, the RBI offers a loan restructuring scheme that helps borrowers sail through their EMI payments till they overcome their financial challenges. If you’re a long-time Tata Capital customer with a loan that you’d like to restructure, here is all the information you need. What is loan restructuring? Loan restructuring allows borrowers under financial distress to modify or renegotiate the loan terms, like an EMI moratorium or rescheduling of repayments, with the lender to avoid EMI defaults . If you’re finding it challenging to manage your loan repayments, restructuring your loan might be the way to go. Types of loan restructuring options in India The various types of loan restructuring options in India are: Extension of tenure: Lenders increase your loan repayment period, which lowers the monthly EMI. This is commonly used when there are temporary income issues, but a possibility to repay the loan over a longer tenure. Lowering the interest rate: Lenders may reduce the interest rate to decrease the overall interest cost and monthly burden. This option is usually offered if you have a good repayment history. Reducing the principal amount: In rare cases, lenders may waive a portion of the principal. This is more prominent during severe financial distress or settlement programs , helping borrowers close the loan. Temporary suspension of payments: Banks may offer a moratorium, pausing EMIs for a fixed period. The interest may continue to accrue during this time. Key points and eligibility for loan restructuring With loan restructuring, you can extend your loan tenure for up to two years . The restructuring option is only available for business loan borrowers, micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) , and small businesses. You can only avail of restructuring if you have outstanding loan dues of up to Rs. 50 crore. Any overdue charges will not be restructured. You can’t restructure your loan if you already opted for it under the previous year’s scheme. However, you have the option of extending your loan moratorium period by two years. You can apply for the scheme up to 15th September 2021. Loan restructuring process: Step-by-step guide We, at Tata Capital, offer a seamless restructuring experience for all our existing customers. So, if you have a loan with us, here’s how you can get it restructured. Loan restructuring process for retail loan borrowers Step 1: Head over to our website and click the ‘Login’ option in the top-right corner. Step 2: Select the “Retail Customer Login” option from the drop-down menu. Next, enter your registered phone number/email address/user ID, and enter the correct OTP to log in. Step 3: Select the Customer service > Raise New SR tab. Step 4: Once you’re on the loan restructuring page, follow the instructions prompted on the screen. Step 5: You may need to provide a fresh NACH mandate for EMI repayments on your existing bank account. Documents required for the loan restructuring application The documents you need to submit to initiate the loan restructuring process are: Loan account details: This includes the loan number, sanction letter, and repayment schedule. Income proof: You must provide recent salary slips, bank statements, or business income documents. Proof of financial hardship: You can submit a job loss letter, salary cut notice, or medical bills to prove your financial challenges. Identity and address proof: Submit a valid copy of Aadhaar, PAN, passport, or utility bills. Written request/application: A formal request explaining the reason for restructuring is necessary. Benefits and drawbacks of loan restructuring Loan restructuring has both advantages and disadvantages. The benefits are: Lower financial stress: Restructuring reduces EMIs or pauses payments. This makes repayment easier during income loss or financial difficulty. Prevents loan default: It helps borrowers avoid missed payments. This also helps prevent legal action and recovery proceedings. Protects credit score: It is better to restructure payment on time than to default. Restructuring leaves a minor impact on your credit score. The drawbacks of loan restructuring are: Higher total interest cost: The overall interest paid over the loan period increases when you extend the tenure or opt for a moratorium. Possible impact on credit profile: Restructured loans may be flagged in credit reports, affecting future loan eligibility. Limited eligibility: Lenders do not approve loan restructuring applications for all borrowers. The approval depends on the lender’s policy and the borrower’s repayment history. Impact of loan restructuring on credit score Loan restructuring can have a moderate impact on your credit score . Your credit report may show the loan as “restructured,” which lenders view cautiously. But if you repay EMIs on time after restructuring, your score can improve gradually. Additionally, if you restructure your loan often, it can affect your credit score negatively. It can also affect loan approvals in the future. Tips for a successful loan restructuring process Loan restructuring is beneficial for any borrower experiencing financial challenges. To take more advantage of the facility, here are some vital tips: Contact your lender early: Reach out to the bank as soon as you face financial stress. Explain your situation clearly: Share your reasons for restructuring. You can add documents as proof. Check available options: Understand tenure extension, EMI reduction, or moratorium choices. Maintain repayment discipline: Pay revised EMIs on time to rebuild trust. Assess long-term cost: Review total interest before accepting new terms. Keep records safely: Save approval letters and revised schedules for future reference. Conclusion If you have a loan with Tata Capital, you can apply for loan restructuring to ease your financial burden. Log in to your Tata Capital account today to begin your loan restructuring process. Apply Now FAQs What is loan restructuring, and how does it work? Loan restructuring refers to the process of changing loan terms, such as EMI, tenure, or interest rate. Borrowers must send a formal request to the lender for restructuring. Once the lender approves, the revised loan terms are sent. Who is eligible for loan restructuring in India? Borrowers facing genuine financial stress, such as income loss or business slowdown, are eligible for loan restructuring. Applicants must also have a reasonable repayment record. What documents are required for a loan restructuring application? The common documents to attach to the loan restructuring application include loan details, income proof, identity proof, and bank statements. You also need documents proving your financial hardship. These include a termination letter, a salary cut, or medical certificates. How does loan restructuring impact my credit score? Loan restructuring may slightly affect your credit score. However, timely repayment after restructuring is better than defaults and helps maintain credit health. Are there any fees or charges for availing of loan restructuring? Some banks may charge processing or modification fees, but charges vary by lender and loan type. It is best to check with your lender. Is loan restructuring available for home loans, business loans, and personal loans? Yes, loan restructuring is available for home loans , business loans, and personal loans . You can discuss with your lender regarding its policies. Borrower eligibility also affects loan restructuring approvals. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Direct Selling Agents (DSAs) have become the unsung heroes of the financial world, often playing pivotal roles in bridging the gap between financial institutions and customers. Whether you are seeking a home loan or trying to understand the different loan options available to you, there is a good chance you might encounter a Direct Selling Agent. However, what exactly is their role, and how do they function? In this article, we will delve into the world of DSAs, shedding light on their significance and operations. DSA full form and meaning in banking At its core, a Direct Selling Agent (DSA) is a professional intermediary that represents financial institutions, such as banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) , to promote and sell their products to potential customers. These products can include home loans , personal loans , credit cards , and other financial services. The primary responsibility of a DSA is to identify and interact with potential customers, explain the intricacies of financial products, and facilitate the application and documentation process. In return for their services, DSAs earn a commission based on the product sold or the volume of business generated. Types of Direct Selling Agents (DSAs) Direct Selling Agents can be categorized into three types based on their affiliations and the products they sell: Independent DSAs Independent DSAs may work for several banks and financial institutions. As a result, they have access to a more diversified portfolio of products and can offer customized services to their clients. Bank-associated DSAs These DSAs only represent a particular bank, selling its products to different clients. They may also receive specialized training from the bank. DSA channel partners DSAs can be channel partners, meaning they represent more than one bank. This way, they can depend on more banks to address the unique needs and preferences of their customers. How to become a DSA loan agent: Step-by-step registration process You can register as a DSA loan agent by following the steps below: Step 1: Visit the official website of your preferred bank or NBFC and apply for a DSA agent ID. Step 2: Complete the payment. Step 3: The financial institution will connect with you to verify documents. Step 4: The financial institution’s legal team will analyze your documents, credit history, and score. Step 5: Once satisfied, the financial institution will share the DSA agreement. Sep 6: Sign and submit the DSA agreement. Step 7: You will receive a unique DSA loan agent ID. Direct Selling Agent (DSA) eligibility criteria To apply for a DSA ID, you must fulfill the following eligibility criteria: The applicant must adhere to the bank’s minimum age requirement, which is typically at least 18 years old. All salaried, non-salaried, self-employed professionals, and business owners can apply. The applicant must be an Indian citizen. The applicant must submit documentation as per the bank’s criteria. The applicant must have a high CIBIL score and a strong credit history. While it is not mandatory for the applicant to have a finance or banking degree, they must possess an understanding of the products they have to sell as a DSA loan agent. Documents required for DSA registration Here’s a general list of documents required for DSA registration: Document Purpose Documents to be furnished Identity Proof You might have to share documents such as: Aadhaar Card, PAN card, Voter ID card, Driving License, Passport Address Proof You might have to share documents such as: Aadhaar card, Passport, Voter ID card, Bank statement or passbook, Utility bill, such as electricity or water bill Educational Qualification You might have to share documents such as: School leaving certificate, Graduation certificate, Post-graduation certificate, Professional degree or diploma certificates (if any) Professional Certificates (if any) If you hold any professional certificates, you might be required to furnish copies. Proof of Business (if applicable) You may have to provide documents related to your business, such as a GST registration certificate, partnership deed, shop establishment certificate, etc, in case you are registering as a DSA on behalf of a business. Passport-sized Photographs You might be required to submit a few recent passport-sized photographs for verification of identity and record-keeping. How to apply online for a loan DSA registration? The step-by-step process to apply for a loan DSA registration online is as follows: Step 1: Choose a lender or platform Pick a bank or NBFC, and visit its official website to initiate the DSA registration. Step 2: Fill out the online application form Enter basic details, such as your name, mobile number, email ID, city, etc. Step 3: Upload required documents Upload documents such as Aadhaar card, PAN card, address proof, and business proof, if asked. Step 4: Complete verification The lender will verify your details through a phone call or email. Step 5: Sign the agreement After approval, sign the DSA agreement digitally. Step 6: Get login access Once registered, you will receive login credentials to start sourcing loan customers and earning commission. DSA code: What it means and its importance for agents? A DSA Code is a unique identification number assigned by a bank or NBFC to a DSA. It enables the agent to offer loan products and legally earn commissions. A DSA code is vital for agents due to the following reasons: It proves you are an authorized loan agent. It helps track loan applications and payouts. It builds trust with customers and lenders. It allows access to lender portals and tools. It ensures smooth and timely commission payments. A loan agent must have a DSA code to work and grow professionally. Role and responsibilities of DSA in banking In today’s dynamic financial landscape, home loans have become an essential tool for many aspiring homeowners. With numerous financial institutions offering a myriad of products, making the right choice can be overwhelming. This is where Direct Selling Agents (DSAs) step in, bringing immense value to both financial institutions and potential homeowners. Let’s delve deeper into the multifaceted significance of Direct Selling Agents when it comes to home loans: Expert guidance throughout the process: The intricacies of home loans, with their varied interest rates, terms, and conditions, can be daunting for the uninitiated. Direct Selling Agents demystify these complexities, offering expert guidance at every stage. From understanding the prerequisites of a home loan to navigating post-loan processes, DSAs are invaluable guides. Tailored solutions for every need: Every individual’s financial standing, requirements, and aspirations are unique. DSAs, with their deep understanding of the market and products, can evaluate individual profiles and recommend home loans best suited to their specific needs, ensuring that borrowers are not shoehorned into one-size-fits-all solutions. Efficient documentation and approval: One of the most tedious aspects of securing a home loan is the documentation. Direct Selling Agents streamline this process by helping clients collate the necessary documents, ensuring they are correctly filled out, and liaising with financial institutions for timely approvals. Their involvement can significantly expedite loan sanctioning. Negotiation and better deals: Given their industry knowledge and relationships with financial institutions, DSAs are often in a position to negotiate better terms on behalf of their clients. This could mean a lower interest rate, waiving off certain fees, or securing more flexible repayment terms, all of which can lead to substantial savings for the borrower. Post-loan support: The role of a DSA does not end with loan approval. They often assist with post-loan procedures, whether it is related to disbursement, understanding the loan statements, or even guiding on prepayment and refinancing options. Building long-term relationships: A good DSA aims to build long-term relationships with clients. This ensures that even in the future, should clients have any more financial needs or challenges related to their home loan, they have a trusted advisor to turn to. Market updates and trends: The financial market is ever-evolving, with new products, government policies, and interest rate changes. DSAs keep themselves updated with these shifts. Therefore, clients benefit from timely advice, be it about new loan products that might be more beneficial or government schemes that they can leverage. In essence, Direct Selling Agents for home loans act as a bridge between financial institutions and borrowers. Their expertise, dedication, and personalized approach ensure that the journey of securing a home loan is smooth, efficient, and tailored to the individual’s needs. For anyone looking to navigate the vast sea of home loan options, a DSA can be the compass guiding them to the right destination. DSA in loan products: Scope across different financial products A DSA plays a crucial role in loan products, connecting customers with banks and NBFCs. The agent helps you select the right loan based on your needs and income. The scope of a DSA’s work is wide because agents can offer many types of financial products. These include personal loans, home loans, business loans , car loans , and a loan against property . In some cases, DSAs also help customers with credit cards and insurance . The need for DSAs is increasing with a growing demand for easy and fast loans. They support customers with documentation, application tracking, and approval follow-ups. This means more earning opportunities and a steady income for agents. A DSA enjoys flexible timing, low investment , and long-term growth across different financial products. Skills and qualities required to succeed as a DSA To succeed as a Direct Selling Agent (DSA), you need the right mix of skills and personal qualities. Here’s a look at some of the most demanded skills and qualities: Basic knowledge of loan products and eligibility Good communication to explain loan options clearly Trust-building ability with customers and lenders Patience to handle follow-ups and rejections Time management to handle multiple leads Basic digital skills for online applications Honest and ethical approach to work These skills allow DSAs to earn a steady income and build long-term success. Benefits of DSA for banks and NBFCs It is not just customers who benefit from DSAs; financial institutions, such as Tata Capital , leverage DSAs to: Expand their reach: DSAs extend the reach of financial institutions, tapping into markets and demographics that might be otherwise hard to access. Reduce operational costs: By outsourcing the initial stages of customer acquisition and documentation, financial institutions can achieve significant operational savings. Enhance service quality: DSAs often bring a personalized touch to the services, enhancing overall customer experience and satisfaction. Earning potential and commission structure for DSAs The earning potential for DSAs depends on the number and type of loans they close. DSAs earn commissions from banks or NBFCs for every successful loan disbursal . The commission is typically a percentage of the loan amount and varies by product, such as personal loans, home loans, or business loans. A higher loan value and good performance can lead to better commission rates and a regular income for DSAs. Common mistakes to avoid during DSA registration When you apply for DSA registration, even the smallest of mistakes can cause delays or rejection. Here’s a list of the common mistakes to avoid: Sharing incorrect or incomplete personal details Uploading unclear or wrong documents Not checking eligibility before applying Using an inactive mobile number or email ID Ignoring the terms and conditions of the agreement Applying to unofficial or fake websites If you avoid these mistakes, you can complete your DSA registration quickly and smoothly. Conclusion Direct Selling Agents are more than just intermediaries. They are expert guides, helping navigate the intricate landscape of financial products. Whether you are seeking a loan or any other financial service, a DSA can be your go-to resource, ensuring you get the best solutions tailored to your needs. Moreover, if you are in the market for a financial product, why not leverage the expertise of a DSA? With Tata Capital‘s extensive range of offerings and association with seasoned Direct Selling Agents, your financial aspirations are just a step away. Dive into a seamless financial journey with Tata Capital today! These agents play a critical role in bridging the gap between customers and financial institutions by representing the latter and promoting their products. What are the eligibility criteria to become a Direct Selling Agent (DSA)? Here are the general eligibility criteria for the DSA registration process: The applicant should be at least 18 years of age The applicant can be a salaried, non-salaried individual, a self-employed professional or a business owner. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund The digital revolution has transformed how we conduct financial transactions and access sensitive information. Gone are the days when a minor task required a trip down to the nearest bank; today, you can do almost everything related to banking on your smartphone from the comfort of your home. But as our lives become increasingly intertwined with the digital realm, ensuring the security and privacy of our financial transactions and personal information is paramount. Fortunately, One-Time Passwords (OTPs) have emerged as a sentinel of online security. OTP Use Cases & Examples One-time Passwords are used by businesses who are looking to secure their application against attacks where credentials can be exploited. Here are a few use-cases in which OTPs are generally used: Passwordless Authentication: OTP authentication provides a seamless login experience for users, eliminating the need to remember complicated passwords. It results in more conversions due to the reduction of friction caused by password standards. Multi-Factor Authentication: Nowadays, many web applications require users to enter OTPS after passwords in conjunction to add another layer of security. One-time Passwords are the leading technology in today’s Two-factor Authentication Systems for more secure applications. Phone/Email verification: User verification is an important step in your online relationship with a user. By verifying the identity of the user by phone/email or any other channel, you can reduce spam and fraud on your site while ensuring the user’s security. Account Recovery: Whenever any user forgets the application credentials, they can recover the account by one-time passwords. Payment Confirmation: Financial and banking applications need more security than any other application. That’s why in most financial applications, users need to enter an OTP before confirming any kind of payment transaction. OTP Security Best Practices OTPs are an effective way to enhance security and protect user privacy. Please follow these One-Time Password related best practices: Keep OTPs Confidential : Treat OTPs like passwords. Never share them with anyone, and avoid storing them in easily accessible locations like text messages, email, or notes on your device. Check SMS/emails regularly – to ensure that no OTP is generated without your prior knowledge, regularly check your SMS and emails. Timely update your registered Contact no./Email – Ensure that you regularly update your registered contact information, including your mobile number and email address, in all the relevant platforms where you receive OTPs. This helps prevent OTPs from being sent to someone else in case your contact information changes. Beware of Phishing : Be cautious of phishing attempts that may trick you into entering OTPs on fake websites. Always verify the authenticity of the website or service before entering your OTP. Don’t Auto-Save OTPs: Avoid enabling features that automatically save OTPs in your messaging app or email. This can be a security risk if your phone is lost or stolen. Limited Attempts: Hackers can use brute-force attack tactics to keep attempting until all possible combinations are reached. Hence, ensure you provide only a few attempts of OTP input before changing the code. Update Your Phone OS and Apps: Keep your phone’s operating system and OTP apps up to date. Updates often contain security patches that help protect against vulnerabilities. Secure Your Mobile Device : Use a secure lock screen on your mobile device to prevent unauthorized access. Additionally, consider encrypting your device’s storage. Use Strong, Unique Passwords: OTPs are often sent as a second factor after you’ve entered your regular password. Ensure that your base password is strong and unique for each account. Legal Compliance: Stay updated on data protection and privacy regulations in your region and ensure compliance when implementing OTP solutions, especially in sectors with strict regulatory requirements. To Sum Up In today’s digital landscape, OTP technology is vital in safeguarding financial transactions, sensitive data, and user privacy. MSMEs lay a solid foundation for India’s economic development and are a significant source of innovation and progress. Access to adequate finance is critical for the survival and growth of MSMEs. However, financial institutions restrict their exposure to MSMEs because of the high cost of servicing and the risk of lending without sufficient collateral. Supply chain financing (SCF) plays a crucial role in bridging the financial gap to revitalise MSMEs and provide much-needed liquidity. Through SCF, financiers like Tata Capital provide early payment solutions to MSME sellers by discounting their invoices while enabling buyers to optimise their working capital . Here are some ways in which supply chain financing is bridging the financial gap for MSMEs in India: Overview: Supply Chain Finance in India & Key Market Drivers Supply Chain Finance (SCF) is changing the way businesses manage money and working capital by linking buyers, suppliers, and banks. It allows companies to access funds faster, improving cash flow and reducing delays in payments. This is especially important for India’s Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), which make up over 95% of the country’s industrial units but often face difficulties in getting affordable credit. SCF helps bridge this gap, offering flexible financing options to keep businesses running smoothly. Supply chain finance fintech in India is growing and being used more widely. Broader factors pushing SCF growth include rising digital adoption, stronger support from regulators and the government, and the need for faster payment cycles in trade. These drivers are helping supply chain finance fintech in India become a key tool for business liquidity. Top Supply Chain Finance Companies & Digital Platforms in India (2026) India’s supply chain finance ecosystem is being shaped by digital platforms that connect large buyers, small suppliers, and financial institutions. These supply chain finance companies in India are making working capital access faster, simpler, and more transparent. Some leading options in 2026 include: CashFlo CashFlo focuses on automating accounts payable and enabling supply chain finance. This supply chain finance fintech in India helps large companies manage payments better while allowing suppliers to receive early payments. By connecting buyers, suppliers, and lenders, it improves cash flow across the supply chain. CredAble CredAble offers technology-driven working capital solutions for businesses of all sizes. Its platform supports multiple financing products that help companies manage liquidity efficiently. CredAble aims to simplify trade finance using data and digital tools. FinAGG FinAGG works closely with distributors, retailers, and MSMEs. Its platform is trusted by large corporates and focuses on financing small businesses that form the backbone of India’s supply network. It helps improve credit access at the last mile. Vayana Network Vayana connects corporates and their supply chains directly with banks. It enables easy access to trade finance for both payables and receivables. This supply chain finance company in India also supports compliance needs like e-way bills. Veefin Veefin provides end-to-end supply chain finance technology, designed by banking professionals. Its solutions support onboarding, loan processing, and management, and power SCF programs across public sector banks. Types of Supply Chain Finance Solutions: Invoice Discounting, Factoring, Reverse Factoring & More Supply chain finance in India includes different funding options that help you improve cash flow and manage payments better across the supply chain. These include: Reverse Factoring In this model, a bank or financier pays the supplier early based on the buyer’s approval. The buyer repays the financier later, usually with longer payment terms. Dynamic Discounting Buyers choose to pay suppliers before the due date in return for a small discount. Suppliers get quick cash, while buyers save money on their purchases. Approved Payables Finance (APF) Here, a financial institution provides funds to the buyer, who then uses this money to pay suppliers on time. It helps buyers manage working capital efficiently. Inventory Financing Businesses use their stored goods as security to get financing. This allows them to unlock money tied up in inventory for daily operations or growth. Receivables Purchase (Invoice Discounting or Factoring) Companies sell unpaid invoices to a lender at a discount. This gives immediate cash, while the lender later collects payment from customers. How Do Indian SCF Platforms Work? Step-by-Step Process for MSMEs Supply Chain Finance (SCF) helps MSMEs get paid faster without putting pressure on buyers. It works by allowing suppliers to receive early payment on approved invoices, while buyers get more time to pay. Here’s the complete step-by-step process: Step 1: Buyer Joins an SCF Platform A large buyer signs up with an SCF provider, such as a bank or fintech platform. Step 2: Suppliers are Onboarded MSME suppliers are invited to register on the platform and link their invoices digitally. Step 3: Goods or Services are Delivered The supplier completes the work and raises an invoice for the buyer. Step 4: Invoice is Approved by the Buyer The buyer checks and confirms the invoice amount and payment date. Step 5: Supplier Opts for Early Payment The supplier can choose to wait or request early payment through the platform. Step 6: Financier Releases Funds A bank or lender pays the supplier upfront, usually at a small discount. Step 7: Buyer Repays the Lender Later The buyer settles the amount with the lender on the agreed-upon due date. Timely access to capital Supply chain financing provides early payment solutions to MSMEs and immediately fulfils the demand for working capital. With the onset of technologies and ERP integration, once the SCF line is set up, the fund requirement is fulfilled within a few hours. MSMEs can utilise this money to maintain inventory levels, procure new raw materials, or expand their business operations. Access to affordable means of finance on demand is crucial for MSMEs to conduct uninterrupted business operations. Recurrent source of liquidity The government of India has launched a large number of MSME credit schemes, but they are one-time and non-recurrent access to liquidity. However, to meet daily expenses, MSMEs need to maintain a consistent flow of working capital. Supply chain financing is based on monthly invoices, and it provides MSMEs with an opportunity to have sufficient cash to meet the working capital needs of the businesses periodically. No burden of repayment There is a significant difference in loan payment terms under credit guarantee schemes and supply chain financing. Under credit schemes, the rate of interest is lower. But borrowers need to repay the amount due within the stipulated timeframe. However, it is not the same under supply chain financing. MSMEs have no repayment burden since it’s an advance against invoices due to MSME sellers. Financiers settle the payments by collecting directly from the buyers on the due date. Cost-effective source of funds SCF is an attractive option for MSME sellers as it can access low-cost financing. Lending institutions extend funds based on the buyer’s creditworthiness, supply chain relationship, and the vintage association between the buyer and seller. It is a competitive source of finance compared to traditional forms of financing that promote better collaboration between the buyer and the seller. Buyers with a decent credit rating can negotiate better terms from the seller. In return, it accelerates MSMEs cash flows and strengthens sellers to contribute better in growing the buyer’s business. Benefits for MSMEs: Why Work with Leading SCF Companies? Supply Chain Finance in India offers several advantages that help MSMEs manage daily operations and grow steadily. Better cash flow MSMEs can receive payments faster instead of waiting for long credit periods. This helps them pay salaries, suppliers, and other business expenses on time. Lower borrowing costs SCF allows MSMEs to benefit from the strong credit profile of large buyers. This usually means lower interest rates than regular business loans. Reduced payment risk Since payments are backed by approved invoices and trusted buyers, the risk of delayed or missed payments is much lower. Stronger business credibility Being part of a formal SCF program improves trust with banks, investors, and new business partners. Simple digital access Leading SCF platforms offer easy online onboarding and faster approvals, saving time and effort for small businesses. SCF brings about financial inclusion SCF has existed for decades, but access to real-time data like bank statements, GST, and e-invoices has streamlined the end-to-end process with digital integration and technological advancements. Digitisation has improved the efficiency of the entire process and reduced the cost of supply chain finance in India. With supply chain financing, MSMEs have easy access to finance at a lower cost, reducing their dependence on informal funding sources. It is a straightforward process with minimal documentation and allows borrowers to get funding at better terms from formal financial institutions. Supply chain financing is an efficient financing alternative to meet the working capital needs of MSMEs. By offering easy access to credit, it accelerates the growth and development of MSMEs. Tata Capital Corporate offers several small businesses quick access to capital through its supply chain financing solutions with tie-ups across leading corporate houses in India. Click here to know more about our supply chain financing offerings. Achieve seamless operations with our business solutions! Apply now FAQs What is the meaning of supply chain financing? Supply chain financing is an arrangement where a buyer collaborates with a financial institution to pay suppliers on their behalf. While suppliers may need to join the program, the buyer is responsible for setting up the process. Who should finance the supply chain? In supply chain finance, the buyer takes the lead by involving a financier. The financier pays the supplier immediately, and the buyer repays the financier at a later date. What are the top 10 supply chain finance companies in India? The leading supply chain finance companies in India include KredX, TReDS, Drip Capital, M1xchange, Vayana Network, RXIL, Indifi, Capital Float, Invoice Bazaar, and CashInvoice. These firms offer solutions to enhance liquidity and streamline supply chain operations. What is the difference between supply chain financing and inventory financing? Supply chain financing focuses on strengthening supplier relationships and ensuring supplier cash flow, while inventory financing is specifically designed to fund the purchase and management of inventory. Businesses may use either or both depending on their requirements. What is an example of supply chain financing? An example of supply chain financing is when a retailer partners with a bank to pay its suppliers early, allowing the suppliers to receive their payments without waiting for the retailer’s payment terms to complete. The retailer then repays the bank later. Who are the top supply chain finance companies and fintech platforms in India right now? Leading SCF companies in India include CashFlo, CredAble, FinAGG, Vayana Network, Veefin, and TReDS platforms supported by banks and NBFCs. What specific SCF solutions do these companies provide for MSMEs? They offer invoice discounting, reverse factoring, approved payables finance, inventory financing, and digital working capital solutions for faster payments. How does supply chain finance differ from a typical business loan for MSMEs? SCF is based on approved invoices and buyer credibility, while business loans depend on MSME credit history, collateral, and longer approval processes. Do TReDS platforms help MSMEs access affordable supply chain finance in India? TReDS platforms allow MSMEs to discount invoices online with multiple lenders, ensuring transparent pricing, quicker funding, and lower interest rates. What new technologies are leading the evolution of SCF in India? Technologies like digital platforms, data analytics, API integrations, automation, and AI-based credit assessment are making SCF faster, safer, and more scalable.
