Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund What is the lien amount? The lien amount refers to the specific amount in your bank account that is temporarily frozen or blocked by the bank. This means you’ll see the money in your bank balance, but you won’t be able to use or withdraw it until the lien is removed. A lien is typically placed to hold or block funds in your bank account so that they can be used to repay dues or fulfill certain financial obligations later. In technical terms, a lien refers to the bank’s legal right to hold or reserve funds in your account to secure repayment of dues or settle obligations. This can happen under several scenarios; for example, you have an unpaid loan EMI, a pending credit card payment, or you’ve applied for an Initial Public Offering (IPO). Let’s consider an example to understand the lien amount meaning better. Suppose you have Rs. 1 lakh in your savings account, but your bank places a lien of Rs. 15,000 due to an unpaid credit card bill. Although your bank balance would still be Rs. 1 lakh, your usable balance becomes Rs. 85,000 until you clear the dues or the lien is removed. What is a lien in banking? In banking, a lien means the bank’s legal right to hold or retain funds or assets belonging to a customer to secure a debt or a financial obligation. It prevents the account holder from accessing or withdrawing the marked funds until a specific debt or obligation is cleared. The amount that is placed under a lien is known as the bank lien amount. While the amount remains visible in your account balance, you cannot withdraw or transfer it until the lien is lifted. You must note that a lien in banking differs from an account freeze or block. While a lien is a legal claim on a specific amount in a bank account, a freeze or block refers to a condition wherein the bank puts a complete halt on all transactions in an account. This is usually done in response to issues like suspected fraud or non-compliance with the bank’s directives. You can access the remaining account balance in the case of a lien. However, a freeze makes the entire account inaccessible. Another term that often confuses borrowers is “lien charge”. The lien charge meaning refers to the legal right a lender has over a borrower’s asset or property until the outstanding debt is fully repaid. It helps the lender recover dues if the borrower defaults. Types of liens Now that you know the lien amount meaning, it’s time to discuss the types of liens in banking. Depending on how and why a lien has been created, it can be categorized into any of the following types: Voluntary lien When a lien is created with the borrower’s or account holder’s consent, it is known as a voluntary lien. For example, when you apply for an IPO, you typically authorize your bank to create a lien over the subscription amount in your bank account. Upon receiving allotment, the lien amount is paid to the issuing company. In the case of non-allotment, your bank releases the lien amount. Involuntary lien An involuntary lien is imposed without a borrower’s or an account holder’s consent. This typically happens due to legal or regulatory authorities’ instructions to your bank. For example, if there’s a tax scrutiny on you, the Income Tax Department can instruct your bank to place a lien on your bank account. This type of lien is removed only after you pay your pending taxes (along with the fine, if any). Statutory lien A statutory lien arises from specific laws or banking regulations, with or without the borrower’s consent. It gives the lender a legal claim over the borrower’s asset or property to ensure payment for a debt or obligation. Consensual lien A consensual lien is very similar to the voluntary lien, and the two terms are often used interchangeably. It is created based on a mutual agreement between the two parties. For example, when you apply for a loan against a fixed deposit, your lender instructs your bank to create a consensual lien on your FD until you clear the loan. Why do banks place a lien on your account? There can be several reasons for your bank to place a lien on your account balance. They can be voluntary or involuntary, and typically mean your bank has temporarily restricted access to a portion of your funds. It can be due to a legal penalty being imposed by a regulatory authority or a consensual move for a financial activity. Here are some valid reasons for a lien amount in your bank account: Unpaid loan EMIs One of the most common reasons why banks place liens on their customers’ accounts is missed or delayed EMI payments. The lien amount will help the lender cover the outstanding loan amount if the borrower fails to pay the EMIs even after repeated reminders. Outstanding credit card dues Failing to pay your credit card bills on time can result in your bank placing a lien on a portion of your account balance. This prevents you from using all the funds in your bank account until the dues are cleared. Legal claims Banks may also place a lien on a portion of your account balance if there is a court order resulting in legal claims. It helps in settling legal disputes and ensures compliance with the court’s order. IPO applications When you apply for an IPO through ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount), you instruct your bank to place your bidding amount under lien until the shares are allotted or the refund is processed. Unpaid taxes or regulatory holds Tax authorities, such as the Income Tax Department or the GST (Goods and Services Tax) Department, may instruct your bank to lien-mark funds in your account. In such a case, a lien balance means that it could be used to clear your tax dues. What is a lien on your bank account? A lien on your bank account typically means that a specific portion of your account balance has been temporarily locked by the bank. In other words, your bank has restricted you from withdrawing or using a specific amount until certain conditions are met. So, the next time you are going through your bank statements or mobile banking app, and you suddenly notice a lien amount, you would probably know what it means and why it’s there. Knowing what a lien balance means and how to check a lien in a bank account is crucial, as it helps you identify such holds early and take corrective action. You can either clear pending dues or contact your bank for clarification if you feel the lien is unjustified or unauthorized. How to check the lien balance in your account? Finding a lien amount early helps you avoid payment failures or surprises. There are several ways through which you can check the lien balance in your bank account: Look for SMS or email alerts Most banks send SMS or email alerts to account holders when they create a lien on their accounts. Do check your inbox for any such message or notification informing you about the lien balance in your bank account. Online banking portal You can log in to your online banking portal to check your lien balance. It should be displayed separately under your account balance section. If not, you can go to the “Account Summary” section and click on the “Lien details” or similar option to check your lien amount. Different banking portals may have different interfaces and options. Mobile banking app You can also use your mobile banking app to check the lien balance in your account. The process remains the same as it is for the web portal. Log in to your mobile banking account and tap on the “Account Summary” option under the “My Accounts” section. Your total available balance, along with the lien balance, will be displayed. Account statement Your monthly account statements also reflect your lien amount. Look for an entry that explicitly states “Lien Marked” or “Amount Under Lien”. If you do not have your bank account statement, you can download it from your online banking portal or get it via email by contacting your bank’s customer support team. Branch visit You can even visit the nearest branch of your bank to inquire about the lien balance in your account. A bank representative will fetch the necessary details for you. How to remove a lien from your account? Once you’ve identified a lien in your bank account, it becomes crucial to take steps to remove it. Here’s the step-by-step lien removal process you can follow: 1. Identify the reason First, you must identify the reason why the lien was placed on your account balance. Is it because of a loan default or tax dues, or anything else? Is it voluntary or involuntary? 2. Make the necessary payment(s) If the lien amount is due to a pending loan EMI or credit card dues, clear the necessary payment(s). The bank will automatically remove the lien upon the lender’s instructions. 3. Contact your bank If the lien is still not removed or if there’s a technical glitch, contact your bank’s customer care team to ask how to remove the lien . 4. Submit the required documents Sometimes, your bank may ask you to submit certain documents to remove the lien from the bank account. For example, a loan closure letter, a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the lender, or a lien release letter. 5. Follow up if required Once the bank verifies that the issue has been resolved, it will automatically remove the lien. However, if the lien still appears after seven to ten working days, follow up with your bank. Sometimes, the lien removal process may take more time than expected. For example, when there is an ongoing loan repayment or a pending legal matter. In such a case, be patient and wait for the bank to remove the lien. Conclusion Understanding what is a lien amount and how it affects your bank balance is essential for managing your finances effectively. It is not a penalty but a temporary financial restriction placed by the bank to secure pending dues or legal claims. Review your account statements carefully to identify lien amounts and take prompt measures to remove or resolve them. Yes. You can still earn interest on the lien amount in your bank account. It’s because a lien amount is very much a part of your account balance, just that you won’t be able to use or withdraw it until the lien is removed. Is a lien the same as a bank account freeze? No. A lien is not the same thing as a bank account freeze. A lien means a specific amount in your bank account is temporarily blocked due to pending dues or legal claims, while a freeze refers to a condition wherein the bank puts a complete halt on all transactions in an account. How long can a lien remain on my bank account? A lien typically remains active until the underlying issue, such as unpaid loan EMIs , pending credit card bill payments, or tax dues, is resolved. The bank may take three to seven working days to remove the lien once the issue is resolved or the dues are cleared. Will a lien affect my credit score or loan application? Yes. Liens can impact your credit score negatively and can affect your chances of getting a loan in the future, especially if the lien is due to loan defaults or unpaid dues. However, a temporary lien usually does not impact your credit score directly. Can I request a lien removal without clearing dues? No. It’s usually not possible for a bank to remove a lien before the outstanding dues have been cleared. A lien offers security to the lender against the outstanding loan balance or credit card dues. What documents are required to request lien removal from the bank? The documents required to request a lien removal depend on the underlying issue. For example, if the lien is due to the non-payment of loan EMIs, the required documents may include a loan closure letter, payment receipts, and an NOC from the lender. with financing now. The digital-savvy world has allowed easy access to credit with a simple click and people are no longer as reluctant as they were a few years ago. Diverse types of loans have profited a considerable number of borrowers, and an interest-free loan is one type of loan that is available for you today. However, many are sceptical of this type of borrowing and rarely use it. If you’re among the ones who are doubtful about this type of loan and want to learn more about it, read on! What is an interest-free loan? Also known as a “zero-interest loan,” this is a loan where you are not required to pay any interest. You only have to repay the principal amount. You can either opt for interest-free education loans , interest-free home loans , interest-free car loans , interest-free travel loans , interest-free loans for business, and others from various lenders, or opt for government interest-free loans. Eligibility The eligibility for zero-interest loans varies depending on the lender. The standard eligibility criteria are as follows – You must be over the age of 21 and should not exceed 65. You must have identity proof such as an Aadhaar card, driving license, or pan card. Is it really interest-free? Though it varies according to the lender, an interest-free loan isn’t really free. We’ll tell you how. Firstly, many of these are small-ticket loans, for consumer-durable goods and services such as restaurant bills, technology, jewellery, furnishings, automobiles, and so on. You can simply use any acceptable mode of payment to avail of interest-free personal loans through which your lender lends you money. Many lenders might also demand additional fees in order to supply you with this option. You may be required to pay application costs, prepayments, origination fees, etc. These fees are usually deducted from your loan amount solely, so you’ll have to borrow more than you need. Finally, if you cannot repay the principal amount within the time frame given, you will have to pay penalties and fines. It will add to your overall payment For example, students availing interest-free education loans when failing to pay back their principal amounts, have to pay considerably higher money than availed. In many cases, the burden of their interest-free education loan also falls on their parents. Also,read – How To Pay an Education Loan Without Interest? Different Types of Interest-free Loans Interest-free loans help borrowers meet important expenses without paying extra interest. In India, such loans are usually offered through government schemes, employers, or special promotional offers, often with specific conditions. Some different types of interest-free loans are listed below: Interest-free Education Loans: These help students pay tuition and related costs. They are mostly offered through government or private schemes for students with a weak economical backing. The repayment usually starts after graduation and may require proof of admission or a guarantor. Interest-free Home Loans: These are provided under government or employer schemes for buying, building, or renovating homes. There is a zero-interest benefit, however it is time-limited and depends on timely repayment. No-interest Car Loans: These are promotional offers by car dealers and finance partners for new cars. These usually require a strong credit score. Interest-free Travel Loans: They are offered as “buy now, pay later” options for travel expenses. Fixed repayment schedules apply on them, and defaults attract penalties. Interest-free Personal Loans: They are short-term loans for personal needs like medical expenses or weddings. They may include fees and must be repaid within the offer period to avoid charges. What are the advantages loan without interest? People with interest-free loans have more liberty and more money in their pockets for day-to-day expenses. Instant purchases: You will be able to buy what you need right away. For example, suppose you want to buy a piece of essential household furniture but don’t have the cash to do so right now. You can easily take out an interest-free personal loan and use the funds to meet your immediate needs. Instant approval: Obtaining other forms of loans takes longer than obtaining a no-interest loan. You won’t have to wait weeks for documentation and approval. It is an obvious advantage, especially in certain instances, such as an interest-free home loan or interest-free education loan. You can complete the minimal paperwork requirements and other formalities and get these loans readily. Save money: If used properly, this loan will not only assist you in managing your finances and needs but will also help you save money. For instance, suppose you wish to get a car that is currently at a lower price than the original. You can acquire it with the help of an interest-free car loan and later pay off the principal on time. This will help you save significant money in the long run. What are the disadvantages loan without interest? Instant availability of funds can sound good in the first instance. However, there are risks associated with these types of loans. More financial strain: If you are unable to repay the loan, it will simply add to your overall financial burden, due to which your credit score will be affected negatively. Let’s say, your interest-free loan for business enabled you to commence your business, but you were not able to pay the loan on time. Not only will it affect your future financial requirements, but also affect your credibility. A habit of mismanaged credit: Taking up an interest-free home loan might be regarded as good credit because a home is a necessity. But, taking an interest-free car loan or loans to buy luxury items like jewellery, on the other hand, is not a prudent strategy to manage your finances in the long run. Limited to particular products: Interest-free loans are not available for all types of consumer goods or services. Many of them, including government interest-free loans, have their lists of criteria and categories exclusively for which you can get zero-interest loans. Also,read – Udyogini Scheme: How Women Entrepreneurs Can Benefit What minimum credit score is required to qualify for an interest-free loan? Your credit score is a key factor that determines your eligibility for an interest-free loan. In the case of a zero-interest loan, since the lender is taking on a higher risk of lending funds without interest charges, they typically require a higher credit score. This is because a higher credit score indicates the creditworthiness of the borrower and ensures the lender makes timely repayments. As a result, you must check your credit score before applying for a loan. While the minimum credit score to qualify for an interest-free loan varies between 700 and 900, you must check the lender’s eligibility requirements before applying. To conclude No-interest loans are a viable alternative to other sorts of funding, including interest loans, high-interest credit cards, and other external borrowings. Apart from borrowing from various lending institutions, you can also look into government interest-free loans. However, before opting for this loan, you must carefully assess your needs and affordability.At Tata Capital , we offer interest-free consumer durable loans for 6 to 24 months with minimal documentation. We also approve loans promptly and offer a flexible repayment structure. Reach out to us to get interest-free loans now. Empower Your Business with an Easy Capital Goods Loan! Apply now FAQs 1. What are the eligibility criteria for obtaining an interest-free loan? While the eligibility for a 0-interest personal loan may vary from one lender to another, the standard criteria are as follows- 1. The applicant must be between the age of 21 to 65 years 2. The applicant must have a valid identity proof such as Aadhaar card, PAN card, or driving licence 2. What is the maximum loan amount available under an interest-free loan scheme? The maximum loan amount you can apply for under an interest-free loan scheme varies from one financial institution to another. You must visit the lender’s website and check their loan features to know the maximum loan amount. 3. Are there any hidden charges associated with interest-free loans? An interest-free loan might carry added charges such as processing fees, late payment fees, pre-payment penalties, and so on. It is crucial to carefully read the loan agreement and terms to understand all potential costs involved and clarify with the lender upfront to avoid any hidden charges. Can I get a zero interest loan online for personal use in India? Yes, zero-interest loans for personal use are available online through lenders, retailers, and finance partners, usually for short-term needs and specific purchases. What is the difference between interest free loan and no cost EMI? They both do not charge interest, but no-cost EMIs are usually linked to specific products, while interest-free loans may still include processing or other fees. Are zero interest loans really free of charges or penalties? No. While no interest is charged, lenders may apply processing fees, origination charges, or penalties if repayments are delayed or the tenure is exceeded. Which government schemes offer interest free loans in India? Government interest-free loans are usually offered under specific schemes for education, housing, or particular income groups, subject to eligibility conditions and defined repayment timelines. What is the typical tenure for interest free personal or consumer loans? Interest-free personal or consumer loans are usually short-term, commonly ranging from a few months up to 24 months, depending on the lender and the type of loan. Is a high salary required to qualify for an interest free loan? A high salary is not always required, but lenders usually prefer borrowers with good creditworthiness, stable income, and a strong credit score to reduce repayment risk. However, to streamline the loan process, many lenders now provide easy facilities to track application status for loans, including a bike loan . Wondering how to check your loan status or how to check your bike loan EMI status? Well, different lenders offer different processes and channels to customers to track the loan application status. Nonetheless, certain guidelines remain the same. You can check your two wheeler loan application status with the channels mentioned below. How to Check Two Wheeler Loan Status Online? The easiest way to conduct a bike loan check or check your two wheeler loan status online is via an online feature available on the website of the lender. If you’re confused about how to check the vehicle loan status online? Follow these steps. Step 1: Access Portal Visit the lender’s official website and open the loan application tracking page. Most lenders place this under a “Track My Application” or account login section. Step 2: Input Credentials Enter the details requested, such as your name, date of birth, application or proposal number, and registered mobile number. Use the same details you provided at the time of application. Step 3: Security Check The portal verifies your identity, usually through an OTP sent to your registered mobile number. Enter the OTP to confirm it is you. Step 4: Instant View Once verified, your two wheeler loan application status appears on the screen. You can see the current stage of your application without calling or visiting a branch. Check Bike Loan Status via Customer Care Another way to check your two wheeler loan status is via customer care services provided by the lender. You have two options to contact the customer care services namely email and call. If you choose to call the services, you need to provide the loan application reference number and the registered mobile number to the representative. Once your two wheeler loan check details are verified, you will be able to check your 2-wheeler loan application status within seconds. In case you choose to email the customer care services, you need to mention all the loan application details in the email clearly. You will receive an answer from the lender within 24 hours of the email. • Voice Support Channel: Call the lender’s customer care number and keep your loan application reference number and registered mobile number ready. Once the representative verifies your details, you get your loan status on the same call. • Email Tracking Channel: Write to the lender’s official customer care email with your application details clearly mentioned. Email works well when you need a written record of the response, though replies typically take up to 24 hours. How to Check Two Wheeler Loan Status Offline? You can also track your 2-wheeler loan application status offline. But unlike the online mode, offline mode for a two wheeler loan check can be inconvenient if you have a busy work schedule. Put simply, the offline mode involves a physical visit to your lender’s office and making an inquiry about your loan application status. When you visit the office of the lender, you need to carry a valid ID proof and the reference number which was provided at the time of application. Once all your details are verified, a representative of the lender will help you track the status of your two wheeler loan application status. • Locate Branch: Find the nearest branch of your lender using the branch locator on its website, and visit during working hours. • Required Papers: Carry a valid ID proof and the reference number issued at the time of application. Without these, the branch cannot verify your identity or pull up your application. • Desk Consultation: A representative at the branch verifies your details and shares your application status. You can also ask follow-up questions about pending documents or next steps on the spot. Check Two Wheeler Loan & EMI Using Mobile Number If you’re wondering how to check bike loan status, or how to check bike EMI status, this section helps answer this question. When you apply for a two wheeler loan, you need to provide a mobile number to the lender. The number will be registered with the lender. You can use the mobile number to talk to a customer care representative or track the status of the loan application. The process may involve an OTP authentication process with your registered mobile number before your query is answered. Method 1: The WhatsApp Banking Route (Fastest) Many lenders now offer loan servicing over WhatsApp, making this the quickest way to check your loan and EMI details from your phone. Save the lender’s official WhatsApp number, available on its website. Send a message from your registered mobile number to start the conversation. Select the loan services option from the menu that appears. Complete the OTP verification when prompted. View your loan status, EMI due date, and outstanding balance in the chat. Always confirm the WhatsApp number from the lender’s official website before sharing any loan details. Method 2: The Lender’s Online “Loan Tracker” Portal The loan tracker on the lender’s website gives you a complete view of your application and repayment status. Open the lender’s website and go to the application tracking or customer login page. Enter your registered mobile number. Verify your identity with the OTP sent to that number. Select your loan account to view the application status, EMI schedule, and payment history. Since the portal is linked to your registered mobile number, you can access it even if you have misplaced your application number. Method 3: Missed Call & SMS Banking If you do not have internet access, missed call and SMS services let you check basic loan details from any phone. Find the lender’s designated missed call or SMS number on its official website or loan documents. Give a missed call, or send an SMS in the format specified by the lender, from your registered mobile number. Receive your loan or EMI details via SMS within a few minutes. This method works only from the mobile number registered against your loan, so update your number with the lender if it has changed. How to Download Two Wheeler Loan Statement & NOC Most lenders let you download your loan documents online, making it easy to do a quick bike loan check, bike EMI check, or check bike loan status anytime. Here’s how: Step 1: Visit your lender’s website or mobile app. Step 2: Log in using your registered mobile number and OTP. Step 3: Verify your identity and select your loan account. Step 4: Download the statement or NOC under the documents section to check bike loan status and track bike loan repayment. Ensure information accuracy When checking your loan application status via online portals, email, or SMS, ensure you provide accurate loan information. However, if there are any discrepancies in the loan details, they must also be communicated with the lender immediately. 2. Monitor the status regularly You must take a proactive approach to your loan application and track the status regularly. This will help you promptly address any issues with the lender and ensure a smooth loan process. 3. Keep documentation handy It is important to keep all the loan-related information handy, such as the application form and loan agreement, as they may contain crucial information required to check the loan status. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Imagine making a rewarding career out of your passion for farming, animals, and the environment—one that feeds the entire world and advances agricultural technology at the same time. To fulfil this dream, a Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Agriculture is a great step. However, many find the cost of education to be a barrier. This is where student loans come into play, providing a financial safety net that allows you to concentrate on your studies rather than worrying about the expenses. This will allow you to safeguard your future in the booming agriculture industry and help you finish the degree with ease. What is BSc Agriculture? A Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Agriculture is a four-year program. This degree offers comprehensive learning and training in all fields of agriculture, such as crops, animals, and soils. With this degree, you will be prepared for a range of agricultural careers. You can start your own farms, work for the government, or work in research centres or agribusiness companies. Eligibility criteria for BSc Agriculture and educational Loan You need to complete your Class 12 (or equivalent) with a science background, with subjects like Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. You need a minimum of 50% marks in your 12th-grade exams from a recognised board. To qualify for admission, you have to take entrance exams, such as CUET, ICAR AIEEA, or state-level tests. Cost of a BSc Agriculture Depending on the college or university, the cost of a BSc in agriculture may vary. The fees start at INR 2,520 and go up to INR 12 lakh per year. Selecting a college that provides the highest quality of education is a smart move. Education loan options for BSc Agriculture students An education loan allows you to pursue the course of your choice from a reputed university. There are many advantages to education loans. For instance, you can enjoy some exemptions on tax, flexible modes of payment, and low rates of interest. They stand by you for things like building credit, protecting your future earnings, and paying for different expenses in your life. Further, you will find that most financial institutions offer student loans for a BSc in agriculture. Education loan on agricultural land: How does it work? An education loan on agricultural land is an option some lenders consider when students or parents lack conventional residential or commercial property for collateral. In this case, agricultural land owned by parents or legal guardians may be offered as security, subject to strict conditions. Financial institutions typically assess clear land ownership, updated land records, and whether the land is non-encumbered. Many nationalised financial institutions accept agricultural land only if it has clear title, proper valuation, and is legally mortgageable. However, acceptance varies widely, some lenders restrict its use due to resale limitations and state-specific land laws. For students pursuing farming, agri-science, or allied courses, an education loan for agriculture students may also be available under priority sector lending. These loans often come with relatively lower interest rates and flexible repayment options, especially for courses recognised by ICAR or state agricultural universities. It’s important to note that not all education loans allow agricultural land as collateral, and loan-to-value ratios may be conservative. Documentation, local revenue approvals, and legal scrutiny are more detailed compared to urban property. Features of education loans against agricultural land Using agricultural land as collateral can be a practical option when conventional property is not available. However, this type of funding comes with specific conditions and lender expectations. Below are the key features of education loan for agriculture students to understand before applying: ● An education loan on agricultural land allows students to offer family-owned farmland as collateral when residential property is unavailable. ● Agricultural land must have clear ownership, updated land records, and be free from legal disputes or existing mortgages. ● Most financial institutions require the land to be owned by parents or legal guardians, not the student alone. ● Loan approval depends on state land laws, as some regions restrict mortgaging or transfer of agricultural land. ● Loan-to-value ratios are usually conservative compared to urban property-backed loans. ● Interest rates are generally similar to standard secured education loans, subject to lender policy. ● Longer repayment tenures and moratorium periods are typically available. ● Extensive legal verification and valuation processes apply, leading to slightly longer processing times. States where agricultural land mortgages are allowed Some Indian states permit agricultural land to be mortgaged for education loan for agriculture students, subject to basic documentation and title verification. Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Odisha generally permit financial institutions to accept agricultural land as collateral under their respective land laws. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana also allow such mortgages, provided borrowers submit valid Patta Passbooks and clear Title Deeds. In these states, lenders focus on ownership records, land classification, and whether the land is free from disputes or existing liabilities. While these states are relatively flexible, financial institutions still apply internal risk assessments and may impose conservative valuations. Acceptance ultimately depends on compliance with state regulations and individual lender policies, as all lenders are legally required to follow state-defined land rules when sanctioning education loans against agricultural land. States where agricultural land mortgages are not allowed Certain states either prohibit or significantly restrict the use of agricultural land as collateral for education loan for agriculture students. Punjab, Rajasthan, Bihar, and Karnataka are commonly cited as states where agricultural land mortgages are not permitted or are rarely accepted by lenders due to restrictive land laws. In these regions, agricultural land is often protected to prevent diversion from farming purposes, making it unsuitable for non-agricultural loans like education financing. Restrictions may relate to land ownership rights, transfer limitations, or resale challenges, which increase lender risk. As a result, most financial institutions avoid accepting agricultural land in these states altogether. Even if local laws allow limited use, practical lender policies tend to be cautious, leading to frequent rejections for education loans secured against agricultural land. Education loan eligibility using agricultural land For an abroad education loan secured against agricultural land, financial institutions follow a set of basic eligibility norms to evaluate both financial strength and land ownership. Along with academic requirements, the following conditions are commonly applied: ● At least 50% of the parents’ or spouse’s income should be derived from agriculture or related allied activities. ● A Tehsildar-issued certificate verifying landholding and agricultural income must be submitted and should be no older than 18 months. ● The applicant and co-applicant should have a clean and stable credit history. ● A minimum score of 60% or above in the last completed educational qualification is usually required. ● The collateral must be family-owned agricultural land, clearly defined with 5–7 ft boundary markings and free from legal or ownership disputes. How to apply for an education loan for BSc Agriculture Before selecting a financial institution, consider the loan coverage, interest rate, and payback schedule. You should prepare the necessary documentation before applying for an education loan. Identity verification, academic records, and financial records are a few common documents needed for college loans. The application for an education loan is available through the financial institution’s website or you can visit in person. Please be careful when completing the form and attach all the necessary files. Remember to read the instructions or disclaimers properly. Proceed to submit the loan application, and after your application is accepted, the lender or financial institution will contact you. Step-by-step application process To apply for an education loan for a BSc in Agriculture, you can follow the steps given here: Decide on a lender or a financial institution of your choice. Keep the required documents ready. Visit the lender’s website and access the application form. Read it carefully and fill out the form. Ensure that all details are accurate and up-to-date. Submit the loan application form Career opportunities after BSc Agriculture With a degree in BSc agriculture, there are a lot of job opportunities locally and globally.. You can be an assistant manager, soil quality officer, plant breeder and even a forestry officer. The leading recruiting firms in the field include Big Basket, JK Agri Genetics Limited, and Kaveri Seed Company Ltd. The BSc in agriculture degree is also constantly changing as it implements technology such as drones and genetic engineering. Thus, it is progressive and can be fulfilling. The average salary for those with a BSc in agriculture is around INR 4, ranging from INR 2 lakh to INR 12 lakh per year. Summing up You can take advantage of several opportunities and technological improvements with a BSc in agriculture. It opens doors to making a meaningful impact on food production and environmental sustainability. With the help of an education loan, your financial requirements become much more manageable, allowing you to focus on building your future. As you step into the world of modern agriculture, the right financial plan ensures that nothing stands in the way of your dreams. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Do you dream about starting your own business and becoming a highly respected corporate mogul? Perhaps you want to manage big teams, take on ambitious projects, and work in high-paying jobs. If this is the case, BBA could be the best stepping stone into your dream career. A Bachelor of Business Administration course can help you learn all you need to know about running a successful business. It teaches you essential skills such as marketing, finances, managing human resources, and so much more. When you complete a BBA program, you are a step closer to realising your educational dreams. However, pursuing a BBA degree in India can be expensive. Your financial constraints may disrupt your career plans. In this article, we explore how a BBA education loan can help you achieve your dream career without any financial strain. What is a BBA degree? A Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) is a three-year undergraduate degree program that gives you a foundational understanding of the business management world. It covers all the aspects of running a business such as accounting, finance, marketing, HR, operations management and more. The BBA program offers different specialisations like Marketing, Finance, HRM, Entrepreneurship, and International Business. The Eligibility Criteria for a BBA Program are as follows: – You must have completed your 12th grade with a minimum of 50% marks. – All streams, including science, commerce, and arts, can apply for this course. – Some common entrance exams for this course are the Delhi University Joint Admission Test (DU JAT), the Integrated Program in Management Aptitude Test (IPMAT) and the Symbiosis Entrance Test (SET). Cost of Studying BBA in India In India, the cost of pursuing a BBA program depends on the university you choose and its location. Government colleges may charge tuition fees ranging from Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 1 lakh a year. Private universities may charge between Rs. 1.5 lakh to Rs. 5 lakhs annually. In addition to tuition, you should also consider expenses such as accommodation. You would also have to pay for study materials, books, supplies, transportation, food and other personal expenses. Education Loan for BBA Students Pursuing a BBA program in India can be quite expensive. You need consistent funding at every stage of your education. This is not a possibility for most students. Education loans are the best solution when it comes to securing funds for your studies. An education loan from a reputed financial institution can help cover all your education expenses. These loans come with student-friendly interest rates and flexible repayment terms. With consistent repayments, these loans help you improve your credit score, and they are also eligible for tax deductions. How to Apply for an Education Loan These are the steps to apply for an education loan: 1. Visit the lender’s website and provide your basic information. The lender will then verify your eligibility for an education loan. 2. If you are eligible, the lender will notify you to upload your documents. The documents you need to upload include: – Identity proof – Proof of residence – Academic documents – Financial documents – Collateral documents, if any 3. Now, your documents will be scrutinised, and your loan will be approved if everything is in order. 4. Post approval, you will be required to sign the loan agreement before you can receive the funds. When selecting a lender make sure to read all the terms and conditions of the loan. Select a lender who is well-known and reputable. Final thoughts As a BBA graduate, you will have many opportunities lined up in front of you. From taking charge of the country’s largest corporations to starting your own business venture, you can do anything you set your mind to. However, getting to this point requires adequate financial resources. An education loan for BBA in India can help you secure the necessary funds for your education and focus on gaining the skills you need rather than how to pay for the degree. catches your eye, or that perfect product that works like a charm may all sound like distant dreams. However, a good designer can change the world around us, transforming these dreams into reality. Designers are the driving force behind progress and innovation. They possess unique talents that blend aesthetics and functionality and create solutions for specific problems. If becoming a designer is something you’re passionate about, consider pursuing a Bachelor of Design (BDes). In this article, we discuss how you can finance your BDes education with the help of education loans and pursue your passions without financial constraints. What is a BDes course? A Bachelor of Design (BDes) is an undergraduate degree program that helps you develop your creative and technical skills to excel in various design-related fields. You would gain expertise in fields such as fashion design, product design, interior design, graphic design and more. The eligibility criteria for a BDes program in India include: 1. You should have completed 10+2 or similar examinations from a recognised board. 2. Most universities require a minimum of 50% marks in your qualifying exam. 3. You may need to write entrance exams such as NID DAT, NIFT Entrance Exam, and CEED. Cost of pursuing BDes in India It can be quite expensive to pursue a BDes degree in India with tuition fees ranging between Rs 50,000 and Rs 3,00,000 per annum. You would need to also take into account additional costs such as accommodation, transportation, food, etc. The cost of pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in design would also depend on the specialisation you choose. Some institutes may also require you to create a portfolio, which can add to your expenses. Education loan for BDes An education loan allows you to pursue BDes from prestigious universities and enter valuable programs that might be financially out of reach. With an education loan, you can ensure you receive the best possible education without dipping into your savings. Here’s why you should consider getting an education loan for BDes in design: 1. An education loan results in a more manageable and affordable financial situation. With these loans, you can fund your education without depleting your savings or relying on your family for support. 2. You can focus entirely on your studies without worrying about finances. Use your time in university focused on academics and college extracurricular activities. 3. Time repayments made towards education loans contribute to a positive credit history. This can work out to your benefit later in life when you apply for a credit card, vehicle loan or car loan. 4. Education loan interest repayments are eligible for tax deductions under Section 80E of the Income Tax Act. 5. With the lender and loan offer, you can secure a loan that covers your tuition fees as well as other expenses related to your education, such as accommodation, books, and travel costs. To apply for an education loan online: 1. Visit your lender’s website and fill in your basic information. 2. The lender will now verify your details to determine your eligibility for an education loan. 3. If you are eligible, you will then be asked to upload your documents. Some documents you would need are- identity and address proof, collateral details, course details, and details of the co-applicant. 4. Once your loan has been approved, you will need to sign the loan agreement. After this, the funds will be directly transferred to your bank account. Final thoughts A Bachelor of Design degree allows you to explore a range of creative possibilities and opens doors to many lucrative and interesting career prospects. However, becoming a designer requires adequate financial resources. An education loan can help you finance your B.Des degree and push you towards a life filled with innovation and artistic expression. Want an easy way to finance your design dreams? Tata Capital offers education loans for B.Des students with competitive and affordable interest rates and flexible repayment plans that make your loan affordable and manageable. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund From the highest safety ratings and durability to cutting-edge features, solid performance, and great fuel efficiency, there are many reasons to bring home a Tata car. And if you’re an employee at the Tata Group of companies, you have another attractive reason to go for a Tata car–Tata employee discount on Tata cars. While every employer provides benefits, Tata takes it up a notch with this well-thought-out initiative aimed at appreciating and rewarding the hard work and dedication of the Tata workforce. And it’s not just limited to Tata cars. What is the Tata employee discount on Tata cars? The corporate discount on Tata cars for employees differs based on the model of the car. This discount is subject to change as per the terms set by Tata. Also, not all cars qualify for the discount. 1. Tata Harrier With its robust build and sleek design, the Tata Harrier has a commanding presence on the road. And not just because of its aesthetics but also the powerhouse performance it delivers, thanks to its 2.0L Stellantis-sourced turbo diesel engine. Tata employees have an added incentive to bring home this beast with up to Rs 65,000 corporate discount on Tata cars. 2. Tata Tigor Tigor is where elegance meets efficiency. The car’s smartly designed interiors, coupled with a fuel-efficient 1.2L Revotron engine, allow you to traverse through both city streets and highways in style without compromising on mileage. Available in petrol and iCNG, the petrol variant generates 86 PS at 6000 rpm and 113 Nm of torque at 3300 rpm. It offers a commendable fuel efficiency ranging from 19.28 kmpl for the manual transmission to 19.60 kmpl for the AMT, making it an economical choice for daily commutes. The iCNG variant further ups the efficiency ante with an impressive 26.49 km/kg. Moreover, the Tigor boasts features like rain-sensing wipers and a 7-inch touchscreen, among others. The Tata employee discount on Tata cars for Tigor goes up to Rs 30,000, making the Tigor an even more appealing subcompact sedan. 3. Tata Nexon (Diesel) With its muscular aesthetics combined with stellar performance, it’s crafted for the adventurous at heart. The 1.5L turbocharged Revotorq engine at its core pumps out a hearty 115PS of power at 3750rpm and a substantial 260Nm of torque from 1500-2750rpm. This capability is complemented by its generous ground clearance, making scrapes and bumps a very rare occurrence. For Tata employees, the Nexon becomes an even more attractive proposition if you take into picture the Tata employee discount on Tata cars. Yes, Tata employees can claim an exchange bonus of an additional Rs.15,000 if they choose Nexon. 4. Tata Tiago If it’s zippy performance and compact convenience that you’re looking for, Tata Tiago can provide both in a fuel-efficient package. Nestled under its hood is a 1.2L, 3-cylinder Revotron petrol engine that churns out a spirited 86PS of power and 113Nm of torque. This energetic heart of the car ensures that the car responds to every dip in the peddle. The Tiago is adorned with modern-day features like a 7-inch touchscreen infotainment system and digital driver’s display, which aren’t just bells and whistles but enhance the driving experience substantially. Manoeuvring through tight spots is a breeze, thanks to its compact design, yet the interior is surprisingly spacious, making it a comfortable ride for both the driver and passengers. It offers a fuel efficiency of 20.01 kmpl for the manual transmission and 19.43 kmpl for the AMT version. The best part? With Tata employee discount on Tata cars, you can get Rs. 25,000 off the price tag. Eligibility Criteria for Tata Employee Car Discount The Tata employee discount is meant for current employees of Tata Group companies, including TCS, and is generally extended to immediate family too: spouse, siblings, parents, and children. It falls under Tata Motors’ broader Shop, Share, Smile grouping, the same category that covers vendor and supplier staff and paramilitary and police personnel. You’ll typically need to show valid proof of employment, such as an employee ID, at the time of purchase. The exact discount amount depends on the car model you choose, and as noted above, not every Tata model is covered. Since terms can change and vary by dealership, it’s worth confirming the current eligibility rules and discount amount with your nearest Tata Motors dealer before you buy. Other discounts for Tata employees The benefits of working at Tata Group extend beyond Tata employee discounts on Tata cars. Croma: For TCS employees, Tata offers a Rs. 2,000-3,000 discount on SlingBox HD, SlingBox Turbo, and SlingBox Pro HD. Tanishq: Tata offers a 10% discount on the making charges of all Tanishq products and an additional 2.5% markdown on diamonds. Taj Hotels: Employees at TCS can enjoy lower room tariffs at certain hotels under the Taj Group. Westside: For fashion-forward peeps, Tata offers a 5% flat discount on Westside apparel. Voltas: Lastly, employees at TCS can cut Rs. 2,500-Rs. 4,000 on their next Voltas window or split AC purchase. How to Claim Tata Employee Discount on Cars? Claiming the discount is straightforward. Visit a Tata Motors dealership and let them know you’re a Tata Group employee. You’ll need to carry valid proof of employment, such as your employee ID card or a letter from HR, along with your usual purchase documents. The dealer applies the discount directly to your invoice at the time of booking, so it reduces what you pay upfront rather than something you claim back later. If you’re financing the rest of the purchase, keep your documents required for a New Car Loan ready as well, since the dealer or your lender may ask for them alongside your employment proof. It helps to call ahead and confirm the current discount for your chosen model, since these do change. Tata Employee Discount vs Corporate Car Discount The Tata employee discount is actually one part of a larger picture. Tata Motors runs a broader corporate discount programme, sometimes called Shop, Share, Smile, that groups eligible buyers into tiers: employees of large corporates like SBI, HDFC, Amazon, or Infosys fall into one bracket, government and PSU employees into another, and Tata Group employees, along with vendor, supplier, paramilitary, and police personnel, into their own bracket. Discount amounts can differ across these tiers and across car models. So while every eligible corporate employee gets some form of discount, what a Tata Group employee gets is specific to that bracket, not necessarily the same as what an employee at a different partner company would receive. If you don’t work at Tata Group but still want financing help, Tata Capital’s vehicle loan can support the purchase regardless of which discount tier applies to you. Can You Combine Employee Discount with Car Loan? Yes. The employee discount is applied to the car’s price at the dealership, and financing the remaining amount through a car loan is a separate step, so the two aren’t mutually exclusive. In practice, this means you get the discounted price first, and then finance whatever’s left. Before you finalise anything, it’s worth checking the current car loan interest rate and running the numbers through a car loan EMI calculator , so you know what your monthly outgo looks like on the discounted amount rather than the sticker price. Since discount terms and loan terms both vary, it’s a good idea to confirm with your dealer and your lender that the discount has been applied before the loan amount is calculated, so you’re not financing more than you need to. Summing up As you can see, working at Tata Group isn’t just about being in a big company. The Tata employee discounts on Tata cars, along with discounts on a range of consumer durables, symbolise Tata’s culture of appreciation, making it a great place to work for any professional. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund For some time now, electric vehicles (EV) have been hailed as the future of mobility. Eco-friendly and noise-free, these vehicles present a real and sustainable alternative to petrol-run ones. However, their cost still poses a challenge to widespread adoption, especially in a price-sensitive market like India. Naturally, government-sponsored electric vehicle subsidy programs have become critical to paving the way for EVs in the country. Thanks to the government’s initiatives to promote e-mobility, electric vehicles are becoming more accessible and affordable to the Indian consumer. Individual state EV policies, aimed at increasing affordability even further, provide more impetus to the shift. Government subsidy on electric vehicles Below are the statewise subsidies on electric vehicles as well as the discount on road tax. State Subsidy (Per kWh) Maximum Subsidy Discount on Road Tax Andhra Pradesh Nil Nil 1 Assam ₹10,000 ₹1,50,000 1 Bihar ₹10,000 ₹1,50,000 1 Gujarat ₹10,000 ₹1,50,000 0.5 Karnataka Nil Nil 1 Kerala Nil Nil 0.5 Madhya Pradesh Nil Nil 0.99 Meghalaya ₹4,000 ₹60,000 1 Odisha NA ₹1,00,000 1 Punjab Nil Nil 1 Rajasthan Nil Nil NA Tamil Nadu Nil Nil 1 Telangana Nil Nil 1 Uttar Pradesh Nil Nil 0.75 Maharashtra ₹5,000 ₹2,50,000 1 West Bengal ₹10,000 ₹1,50,000 1 What is a FAME electric vehicle subsidy? FAME, or Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid and) Electric Automobiles in India, is an incentive programme for government subsidy on electric vehicles. The EV incentive programme was presented in 2013 as part of the National Mission on Electric Mobility 2011/National Electric Mobility Mission Plan 2020. The following are the main aspects of the subsidy – The FAME I scheme’s first phase was approved for a two-year period, beginning April 1, 2015. Since then, the EV subsidy programme has been periodically extended. The first phase of FAME was last extended to March 31, 2019. The Demand Incentive Disbursement Mechanism (DIDM) is used in the FAME scheme. The amount of government subsidy on electric vehicles for each vehicle category (pure electric, hybrid, etc.) has already been established based on technology and battery parameters. What is the FAME II (FAME 2) subsidy for electric vehicles? FAME II is the electric vehicle incentive programme’s second phase, which went live on April 1, 2019. Beginning April 2019, the government launched a three-year incentive programme with a budget of Rs. 10,000 crores. The highlights of FAME II are listed below: The FAME II e vehicle subsidy is expected to cover 7,000 e-buses, 5 lakh electric 3-wheelers, 55,000 electric vehicles, and 10 lakh electric two-wheelers. The EV subsidy programme has been extended till March 2024. Increased subsidy for electric vehicles (two-wheelers) is one of the primary attractions of the new FAME II scheme. The incentive for two-wheeler EVs was initially set at Rs. 10,000 per kWh. It has now been increased by 50% to Rs. 15,000 per kWh. Additionally, the e-vehicle subsidy cap has been raised from 20% to 40% of the vehicle’s cost. The subsidy for electric vehicles (four-wheelers) stays unchanged at Rs. 10,000 per kWh. For an electric car, the maximum incentive value is Rs. 1.5 lakhs. FAME II’s Requirements The FAME 2 electric vehicle subsidy is available for electric cars and two-wheelers. While purchasing an EV, you should be aware of the specifics of the subsidies programme. The incentive is available for electric automobiles and SUVs, with ex-factory price being limited to Rs. 15 lakhs. EV four-wheelers that cost more than Rs. 15 lakhs are, therefore, ineligible for the incentive. The system requires a minimum range of 80 kilometers and a top speed of 40 kilometers per hour for battery-powered two-wheelers. The FAME II e vehicle subsidy scheme is available for electric two-wheelers that cost less than Rs. 1.5 lakhs. The following state’s policies do not include a direct subsidy for electric cars and SUVs- Andhra Pradesh Karnataka Madhya Pradesh Punjab Rajasthan Tamil Nadu Telangana Uttarakhand Uttar Pradesh In most states implementing the subsidy policy, the road tax for electric four-wheelers is completely exempted, with the exception of Kerala, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh. In Kerala and Gujarat, buyers are required to pay 50% of the whole road tax amount. In Uttar Pradesh, buyers must pay 70% of the total road tax. In the meantime, registration fees for all kinds of EVs are waived countrywide. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) announced last August that all battery-powered vehicles are exempt from fees for issuing or renewing registration certificates. Top EV-friendly States that Offer Best Incentives to Buyers As every Indian state frames its EV policy in alignment with the FAME subsidy scheme, the incentive or electric car subsidy will vary from state to state. Here are a few states that offer the best EV subsidy to buyers- Gujarat Two-wheeler: Maximum up to Rs. 20,000 Three-wheeler: Benefits up to Rs. 50,000 Four-wheeler: Maximum up to Rs. 1.5 lakh Maharashtra Two-wheeler: Maximum up to Rs. 25,000 Three-wheeler: Benefits up to Rs. 30,000 Four-wheeler: Maximum up to Rs. 2.5 lakh Meghalaya Two-wheeler: Maximum up to Rs. 20,000 Three-wheeler: NA Four-wheeler: Maximum up to Rs. 60,000 Karnataka Besides the FAME EV subsidy, Karnataka doesn’t extend any direct incentives to EV buyers. But it gives electric car subsidy to EV makers. Andhra Pradesh Andhra Pradesh also doesn’t directly offer electric car subsidy to buyers but it offers them an exemption from registration charges and road tax. Telangana Telangana offers EV buyers complete exemption from registration charges and road tax besides the FAME incentive. Tamil Nadu Tamil Nadu offers a 100% road tax waiver and zero registration charges for EV buyers. However, the state government is looking to reconsider its EV policy. Kerala EV buyers in Kerala can get a 50% discount on road tax for the first five years. The state also gives a subsidy to e-rickshaws ranging from 10,000 to 30,000. This subsidy helps reduce the upfront cost of buying environmentally friendly cars. 2. What is the Fame 3 subsidy? FAME 3 is the third phase of the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles scheme in India. It provides enhanced incentives for electric vehicle buyers and supports the development of charging infrastructure to promote EV adoption. 3. What is the tax rebate for EV in India? In India, you can avail a tax rebate of up to ₹1.5 lakh under Section 80EEB for purchasing electric vehicles. This rebate helps lower your overall cost and encourages more people to switch to electric cars and bikes. 4. Are e-rickshaws eligible to receive EV subsidies? If the cost of the e-rickshaw is below ₹5 lakh, you can receive incentives, which is a cost-effective and sustainable choice for your transportation needs. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A car loan or vehicle loan is a sum of money you borrow from the bank to buy a car, while committing to repay it over time with interest. The lender determines the car loan terms after assessing your age, income, credit score, and the vehicle’s price. You can apply for a car loan to buy a new or a used vehicle. If the loan is approved, the lender directly pays the car dealer the remaining price of the vehicle after you have made an upfront down payment. A vehicle loan, meaning money borrowed to buy a car, is a secured loan. The car you are buying is pledged as collateral until you repay the loan with interest. Financial planning is of the utmost importance when acquiring a car so that it becomes as affordable and smooth as possible. Whether you’re eyeing a new or used car, finding a way to divide the cost can significantly ease the burden of a large, one-time payment. Flexible financial options like a car mortgage loan will open avenues to choosing the right fit, and you will probably drive away in a car that best fits your budget and lifestyle. What is a car loan? The best auto loan meaning is a financial agreement whereby a person borrows money to buy a vehicle. The loan would then be used to repay the money borrowed on a lending deal with some interest. Since the car is collateral, the lender will repossess the car if one cannot repay the cash. It is one of the most basic loans for vehicles for people because it enables them to buy their dream car without paying the entire payment upfront. What are its key components? The essential components of a car loan include: Principal: This is the original amount you borrow from the lender to buy a car, whether new or used. Interest rate: This is the percentage charged by the lender on the borrowed amount. A lower interest rate can reduce your monthly EMI and total repayment cost. Loan tenure: This is the period available to repay the loan. If you opt for a longer tenure, it may lower your EMI but can increase the total interest paid. Down payment: This is the amount you pay upfront when purchasing the car. You can reduce the loan amount and monthly EMI by paying a higher down payment. How car loans work? An auto loan meaning is when a person purchases a vehicle and pays for it over time through monthly installments. The lender assesses the buyer’s financial situation and creditworthiness to determine the loan terms, including factors such as the car’s price, interest rate, and the buyer’s credit score, which influence the loan amount and repayment terms. Repayment is usually made in fixed monthly installments, typically ranging up to 84 months. If the borrower makes all payments, they retain full ownership of the vehicle. However, if payments are missed, the lender may repossess the car. What are the advantages of car loans? Derived from car loan meaning and offerings, they provide several advantages: 1. Flexible tenure It provides the flexibility of tenure for repayment. This is up to 84 months. This is helpful because borrowers can spread their EMI payments over a longer tenure, making this manageable and more accessible. 2. Fast processing Most lenders offer streamlined digital processes, so applying for a car loan is quick and hassle-free. After submitting a simple online application and minimal documentation, the borrower can expect the balance to be in their account within a few working days. 3. Customized EMI plans Almost all financiers allow customized EMI payments according to individual needs. This way, the borrower can extend or reduce the loan tenure so that the EMI amount remains comfortable and manageable for repayment in the following month. 4. Competitive interest rates Car loans are offered at very competitive interest rates, making it more affordable to buy a car without overstretching your pocket. You can use online EMI calculators to estimate your monthly payments when borrowing. 5. Instant approval With modern online processes, several auto loan meaning instant approval after verification of the documents. This helps the borrowers gain speedy access to the required funds. This makes the whole loan process smooth and efficient. 6. Maximum loan amount Car loans can offer finance up to Rs. 50 lakhs, allowing you to buy your dream car without any monetary hassle. Such a large amount supports all vehicles, from models for small budgets to expensive cars in luxury categories. What are the eligibility criteria for a car loan/auto loan in India? A car loan is disbursed based on eligibility criteria for different individuals that encompass: 1. Salaried individuals i. Applicants must be between the ages of 21 and 60. ii. A minimum annual income of Rs. 3,00,000 is required. iii. The applicant should have at least one year of work experience. 2. Self-employed individuals i. Applicants should be between 21 and 65 years old. ii. They must be proprietors of their business. iii. The business must have been operational for at least one year. iv. A minimum annual income of Rs. 3 lakhs is required. 3. Self-employed (Others) i. A minimum annual income of Rs. 2 lakhs is necessary. ii. The applicant must maintain an average bank balance (ABB) of at least 0.5 times the loan EMI. What is the car loan application process? Application for a car loan usually involves the following steps: 1. Online application You must go to the lender’s official website to find the car loan meaning and application form. The information in this form includes your name, contact number, work status, and monthly income. Ensure that all information is correct so that it will not be delayed. 2. Upload documents After completing the form, upload all the necessary documents online. The respective documents that a salaried employee or a self-employed individual would provide are as follows: i. Identity proof: PAN card / Aadhaar card ii. Address proof iii. Salary slips and bank statements iv. Income tax returns v. Balance sheet vi. Profit and loss accounts 3. Verification After you apply and submit all the documents, the lender will carry out an in-depth verification process. This will help establish whether the information you provided is correct and whether you qualify for the loan. Most lenders check your credit score, income stability, and employment history. 4. Approval Once your loan application is verified as error-free, a car loan lender will approve your car loan. Most lenders today give instant approvals; you can always check online to see if your approval is already available. 5. Loan disbursal The loan amount is directly credited into your bank account, typically within a few working days of approval. Subsequently, you can purchase the preferred car with the disbursed loan amount and complete the process. Which documents are required for a car loan? The documents you will need to submit for a car loan include: Identity proof: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, passport, or voter ID Address proof: Aadhaar Card, utility bill, passport, or driving license Income proof: Recent salary slips, bank statements, or ITRs Employment/Business proof: Employment details or business documents, if required Car documents: Dealer quotation or proforma invoice Photographs: Recent passport-size photographs Car loan EMI calculation with an example The calculation of car loan EMI depends on the loan amount, interest rate, and loan tenure. Lenders use the standard EMI formula as given below. EMI = [P × R × (1 + R)^N] / [(1 + R)^N – 1] Where P is the principal amount, R is the monthly interest rate, and N is the tenure in months. So, if, for example, you borrow Rs. 5 lakh at an interest rate of 10% per annum for 5 years, your EMI would be approximately Rs. 10,624. The total repayment over 5 years will be Rs. 6.37 lakh, including Rs. 1.37 lakh as interest. What are the types of vehicle loans: New car, used car, and car mortgage loan? Understanding the different loans for vehicles helps you choose the option that fits your needs and budget. Simply put, what is car loan or auto loan meaning? A car or auto loan is a type of financing that helps you purchase or leverage a vehicle by repaying the amount in EMIs. A new car loan is taken to buy a brand-new vehicle. Here, the car acts as collateral, interest rates are usually lower, and repayment tenures are flexible. This option suits buyers looking for predictable vehicle loan details and ownership from day one. A used car loan helps finance pre-owned vehicles. While interest rates may be slightly higher, it’s a practical choice if you want affordability with clear car loan meaning and manageable EMIs. A car mortgage loan is different. A car mortgage loan allows you to pledge an owned vehicle to raise funds for personal or business needs. If you’re wondering what is auto loan versus a mortgage loan, the key difference lies in usage—purchase versus liquidity. Knowing what is auto loan and comparing options ensures smarter financial decisions. What are the car loan interest rates, tenure, & maximum funding in India? Auto loan meaning in India is designed to make vehicle ownership more accessible with flexible terms and structured repayment options. Car loan interest rates generally depend on factors such as the borrower’s credit profile, income stability, and the type of vehicle being financed. Rates may vary across lenders and can be fixed or floating in nature. The tenure of a car loan lasts up to 84 months, allowing borrowers to balance EMI affordability with overall loan cost. Shorter tenures reduce interest outgo, while longer tenures offer lower monthly payments. Maximum funding is typically linked to the vehicle’s on-road price and the borrower’s eligibility. Lenders may finance a significant portion of the cost, with the final amount influenced by income, repayment capacity, and credit history. Reviewing these vehicle loan details helps borrowers choose suitable loan terms. What are the factors affecting car loan interest rates? The various factors affecting car loan interest rates are as follows: Credit score: With a higher credit score , you can get a lower interest rate because it shows responsible credit behavior. Income: A stable and higher income can improve your repayment capacity and may help you secure better rates. Loan amount: The amount you borrow can affect the interest rate offered by the lender. Loan tenure: The time you take to repay the loan affects interest rates. Longer loan tenures may sometimes come with different interest rates and higher total interest costs. Car type: New and used cars may have different interest rates based on their age and value. Lender policies: Banks and NBFCs set rates based on their lending policies and market conditions. What are the common mistakes to avoid when taking a car loan? Borrowers often make some common mistakes while taking a car loan. Make sure you avoid these: Not comparing lenders: Check interest rates, processing fees, and loan terms from different lenders before choosing one. Choosing a long tenure: A longer tenure may reduce your EMI, but it can increase the total interest paid. Ignoring extra charges: Find out about the processing fees, prepayment charges, late payment penalties, and other costs. Borrowing more than you are comfortable with: Pick a loan amount that fits your budget and repayment capacity. Not checking your credit score: Checking your credit score beforehand can help you make a wise financial decision. Missing EMI payments: Pay EMIs on time to avoid penalties and protect your credit score. Conclusion From new car loans to used car loans and refinancing, you can choose loans for vehicles that fit your needs.
