Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund You must have seen that small shop with a long queue of people standing outside holding empty bags and bottles. These are government shops for distributing essential items like food and oil to the public below the poverty line. The main benefit of these Public Distribution System (PDS) shops, commonly known as ‘Ration ki Dukaan’, is that items are provided to the public at a discounted or subsidized price. The Government of India occasionally introduces beneficial schemes designed to improve the well-being of its citizens. These schemes serve multiple purposes, with some focusing on uplifting people economically and others enhancing their overall quality of life. Besides that, the Indian government also extends different subsidies to MSMEs to foster their growth and development. So, in this article, we will explain everything about subsidy, like subsidy meaning, its types and categories, and discuss a few popular business subsidy schemes provided by the Indian government. What is a subsidy? Definition & overview A subsidy is a financial benefit or support that the government gives to institutions or individuals. It can be either a direct or indirect subsidy. Direct subsidy refers to the support given in the form of cash. The indirect subsidy, conversely, refers to the assistance offered through tax cuts or low-interest loans . Loan subsidy’s meaning is to provide the loan at lower interest rates and with other features that help the business grow. And government subsidy is financial assistance the government offers to ease the burden on the recipients and encourage activities in the public interest. Why does the government provide subsidies? Now that you understand what subsidies are, you must learn why the government provides different types of subsidies. The government offers subsidies to help people and businesses afford essential goods and services. Subsidies reduce the cost of items like food, fuel, education, healthcare, and farming inputs. This support is important for poor and middle-income families who may not be able to pay full prices. Subsidies also help farmers by lowering the cost of seeds, fertilizers, and electricity. This support increases food production and keeps food prices stable. Moreover, the government gives subsidies to encourage the growth of essential industries and protect jobs. In some cases, subsidies promote social welfare by improving access to education and health services. This leads to a healthier and more skilled population. In a nutshell, government subsidies support economic development, protect vulnerable groups, and ensure that basic needs are available to everyone at affordable prices. How does a subsidy work? A subsidy reduces the cost burden on producers or consumers, facilitating more accessible products or services. Governments provide subsidies through direct cash payments, tax breaks, or low-interest loans to individuals and businesses to reduce production costs or boost consumer affordability. For businesses, this reduced cost either increases profit margins or allows them to offer goods at lower prices to consumers. By covering part of the cost, subsidies promote industries essential for economic growth or public welfare, fostering broader market participation and competitiveness. Types of subsidies There are broadly six types of subsidies, as explained below. #1. Food subsidy Its main aim is to provide essential food to people below the poverty line. Public Distribution System (PDS) is a government initiative providing essential food items to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households at subsidized rates. These include wheat, rice, sugar, milk, and cooking oil. #2. Export subsidy The government provides export subsidies to encourage small domestic businesses to diversify their customer. One such subsidy scheme is the Merchandise Export from India Scheme. It aims to promote the export of notified goods manufactured in India. #3. Production subsidy A production subsidy allows companies to reduce their production costs. They can increase production value by cutting down their losses and investments. This helps in making products available at a lower price, improving affordability. #4. Subsidies based on industry These subsidies are tailored to meet the needs of the industries they are intended for. They cover various sectors, including transport, health, and agriculture. The government, for example, has launched several transport schemes to make transportation more affordable. It also gives subsidies to help farmers and businesses reduce the initial input cost. This includes providing fertilizer, seeds, power supply, and irrigation facilities at subsidized rates. #5. Tax subsidy This subsidy program grants eligible parties a tax rebate and other benefits. It relieves the financial burden on business owners, allowing them to improve production, extend services, and offer products at a lower price. #6. Employment subsidy These schemes are designed to tackle unemployment. The government offers incentives, such as lower initial investment costs or reduced real estate rates, to organizations to start a company. These measures are aimed at promoting job growth and reducing unemployment. Now that we know what a subsidy is, let’s look at its different categories. Categories of subsidies in India There are two categories of subsidies, namely, social and economic. Depending upon its impact, it falls into either of the two categories. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the two categories. Social Subsidy Economic Subsidy Rural housing Transport Sanitation Industry Water supply Irrigation and food control Healthcare Agriculture Education Industry Women empowerment Communication Common examples of subsidies in India Here are some common examples of subsidies in India: Food subsidy: The government provides rice, wheat, and sugar at low prices through the Public Distribution System (PDS) to help low-income families. Fertilizer subsidy: Farmers get fertilizers at reduced prices, which lowers farming costs and increases crop production. Fuel subsidy: Subsidies on LPG cylinders help households, especially low-income families, afford cooking gas. Electricity subsidy: This scheme reduces the cost of electricity provided to farmers and low-income households. Education subsidy: Scholarships and fee support help students from weaker sections continue their studies. Healthcare subsidy: Government hospitals provide free or low-cost treatment and medicines. Transport subsidy: The recipients of this subsidy scheme include students, senior citizens, and people with disabilities. They get discounted fares on transport facilities. These subsidies support basic needs and reduce inequality. Popular government subsidy schemes in India MSMEs play a crucial role in boosting India’s economy. The subsidy provided by the Indian government supports their growth. A few of them are mentioned below. #1. Credit-linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) This government subsidy loan for business aims to fund technological upgrades in Small-Scale Industries (SSIs). The funds can be used to revamp business production and activities to reduce the cost of creating and providing goods and services. SSI units that get benefits include tiny units, khadi units, village units, and coir industrial units. #2. Marketing Assistance Scheme It is a scheme provided by the Ministry of MSME, inter alia, through the National Small Industries Corporation. It helps MSMEs market their products at exhibitions, trade fairs, and buyer-seller meets. #3. Mahila Coir Yojana This subsidy scheme helps eligible rural women avail of a one-time subsidy of up to 75% of the total cost of the new motorized Ratt or Rs. 7,500, depending upon the case. #4. Amended Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS) The Ministry of Textiles launched ATUFS. It aims to convert existing looms to better technological looms to improve productivity and quality. Some of the beneficiaries of this scheme are the jute, silk, and garment sectors. #5. Technology & Quality Upgradation (TEQUP) Support for MSME Technology & Quality Upgradation (TEQUP) is an initiative by the Ministry of MSME. Its main objective is to make the MSME sector energy efficient and increase competitiveness. #6. Government Subsidy for Small Businesses for Cold Chain The Ministry of Food Production Industries launched this scheme. It provides an integrated cold chain without any break from the farm gate to the buyer. It covers pre-cooling facilities at production sites, mobile cooling units, reefer vans, and value-addition centres. Benefits of subsidies As a subsidy is a social and economic welfare scheme by the government, it has many benefits: #1. Subsidized education helps further contribute to the nation’s GDP, as increased education leads to higher employment. It also leads to an increase in skilled workers. #2. It helps struggling markets by lowering the burdens and providing financial support for future ventures. It’s an indirect means to support the country’s employment and industrial sectors. #3. Subsidies provide incentives and tax benefits to business owners. This leads to increased production and a continuous flow of demand and supply. #4. It helps lower the cost of essential items and makes them affordable for the general public. #5. Besides helping the traditional sectors, such as agriculture sectors, to flourish, subsidies also encourage the advancement of new areas of research and development. Direct vs indirect subsidy: Key differences Direct subsidies involve the actual payment of money to a group or individual. These are often in the form of cash payments, grants, or specific financial support to reduce the recipient’s cost of goods, services, or production. On the other hand, indirect subsidies do not involve direct financial payments. Instead, they include measures such as tax breaks, reduced interest rates, insurance , or rebates that indirectly reduce costs or provide economic benefits to businesses or individuals. Challenges and the future of subsidies in India Here’s a description of the challenges and the future of subsidies in India: High government spending: Subsidies cost a lot of money and increase the burden on the government budget. Leakages and corruption: The benefits do not always reach the right people due to misuse and poor monitoring. Wrong targeting: Some rich people also get subsidies meant for the low-income groups. Dependence on subsidies: Long-term subsidies can reduce self-reliance among people and businesses. Price distortion: Subsidies can lead to waste of resources like electricity, water, and fuel. Need for better delivery: Digital systems like Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) can reduce losses. Focus on the needy: Future subsidies should be limited to those who are deserving and needy. Sustainable approach: The government should balance subsidies with economic growth and development goals. What does ‘subsidy opted’ mean in loans and schemes? In loans and schemes, the term ‘Subsidy Opted’ means that the borrower has chosen to receive financial help from the government. This help reduces the interest rate or cost of the loan. It makes borrowing cheaper, especially for housing, farming, or education, helping people afford loans they might not manage otherwise. Interest subsidy meaning and how it works in India Interest subsidy is a way in which the government helps by reducing the interest you pay on a loan. In India, it is common for home, education, or agriculture loans. The government pays part of the interest directly to the bank, so the borrower pays less. This makes loans affordable, encourages people to invest in homes, studies, or farming, and supports economic growth while reducing financial burden. Conclusion Subsidies play an important role in supporting economic growth and social welfare. They help make essential goods and services affordable, protect vulnerable groups, and promote key sectors like agriculture, education, and healthcare. When planned well and targeted properly, subsidies reduce inequality and contribute to balanced and inclusive development. So, after learning everything about what a subsidy is and its benefits, we understand that subsidies can be a powerful tool for promoting economic growth and improving people’s lives. While it can help keep prices low for consumers and boost production, it provides opportunities for people and MSMEs to start and grow their businesses. The Indian government has launched several subsidy schemes to support small-scale industries in India. A subsidy loan is a type of financial assistance provided by the government to promote the growth of businesses in various sectors. These loans are offered at reduced interest rates, and a portion of the interest rate is subsidised by the government, making the overall cost of the loan more affordable for the borrower. Which is an example of a subsidy? An example of a subsidy is the food subsidy provided to people below the poverty line. It aims at providing essential food to people at subsidised rates to eradicate hunger. The Public Distribution System is a government initiative that provides essential food items, such as wheat, sugar, rice, and cooking oil to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households at a subsidised rate. What do you mean by subsidy? Subsidy is financial assistance provided to support the growth of specific businesses, industries, or individuals. It aims to promote economic and social development by making goods and services more affordable, encouraging production, or supporting the incomes of certain groups. What is the subsidy given by the government? A subsidy is a financial incentive provided by the government to businesses, institutions, or individuals through cash, grants, reduced interest rates, or tax breaks to ease the financial burden on the recipients. It aims to promote social and economic policies in the public’s interest. How many types of subsidies are there in India? A subsidy is broadly categorised into two types- direct and indirect subsidy. Within indirect subsidy, there are six types of subsidies: production subsidy, export subsidy, food subsidy, tax subsidy, employment subsidy, and subsidy based on industry. What is the classification of a subsidy? Subsidy can be classified as direct and indirect. Direct subsidy involves financial transactions between the government and specific recipients, such as cash payments or grants. Meanwhile, indirect subsidy does not involve direct cash transactions but includes measures that reduce the price of goods and services. Indirect subsidies include tax breaks, reduced interest rates, insurance, etc. Is a subsidy available for home loans? Subsidies for home loans are available under schemes like Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna’s credit-linked subsidy scheme. Under this, eligible individuals can apply for a home loan at subsidised interest rates. However, individuals with an annual income of more than Rs. 18 lakhs do not qualify for a PMAY loan. How can farmers benefit from subsidies? Farmers benefit from subsidies through reduced costs for seeds, fertilisers, machinery, and irrigation. Government subsidies help improve productivity, stabilise incomes, and protect farmers from price fluctuations. What subsidy deals with rural employment? The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) provides a subsidy for rural employment. It guarantees 100 days of paid employment per year to adult members of rural households. What is a tax subsidy? A tax subsidy is a government incentive that reduces the tax burden on businesses through tax rebates or reduced tax rates What is a subsidy, and how does it work in India? A subsidy is financial help given by the government to reduce the cost of goods or services. In India, subsidies work by lowering prices or giving direct cash benefits so people can afford food, fuel, education, farming needs, and basic services. What are the different types of subsidies available in India? India offers food subsidies, fertilizer subsidies, fuel subsidies, electricity subsidies, interest subsidies, and export subsidies. These subsidies support poor families, farmers, students, and businesses. They help important sectors grow while reducing inequality and financial burden. Can you give some popular examples of government subsidies? Popular subsidies in India include free or affordable food through PDS, fertilizer subsidy for farmers, LPG gas subsidy for households, electricity subsidy for agriculture, scholarships for students, and low-interest loans under housing and education schemes. What is a subsidy loan? A subsidy loan is a type of financial assistance provided by the government to promote the growth of businesses in various sectors. These loans are offered at reduced interest rates, and a portion of the interest rate is subsidized by the government, making the overall cost of the loan more affordable for the borrower. Which is an example of a subsidy? An example of a subsidy is the food subsidy provided to people below the poverty line. It aims at providing essential food to people at subsidized rates to eradicate hunger. The Public Distribution System is a government initiative that provides essential food items, such as wheat, sugar, rice, and cooking oil, to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households at a subsidized rate. What do you mean by subsidy? Subsidy is financial assistance provided to support the growth of specific businesses, industries, or individuals. It aims to promote economic and social development by making goods and services more affordable, encouraging production, or supporting the incomes of certain groups. What is the subsidy given by the government? A subsidy is a financial incentive provided by the government to businesses, institutions, or individuals through cash, grants, reduced interest rates, or tax breaks to ease the financial burden on the recipients. It aims to promote social and economic policies in the public interest. How many types of subsidies are there in India? A subsidy is broadly categorized into two types: direct and indirect subsidies. Within indirect subsidy, there are six types of subsidies: production subsidy, export subsidy, food subsidy, tax subsidy, employment subsidy, and subsidy based on industry. What is the classification of a subsidy? A subsidy can be classified as direct and indirect. Direct subsidy involves financial transactions between the government and specific recipients, such as cash payments or grants. Meanwhile, indirect subsidy does not involve direct cash transactions but includes measures that reduce the price of goods and services. Indirect subsidies include tax breaks, reduced interest rates, insurance, etc. Is a subsidy available for home loans? Subsidies for home loans are available under schemes like Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana’s credit-linked subsidy scheme. Under this, eligible individuals can apply for a home loan at subsidized interest rates. However, individuals with an annual income of more than Rs. 18 lakhs do not qualify for a PMAY loan. How can farmers benefit from subsidies? Farmers benefit from subsidies through reduced costs for seeds, fertilizers, machinery, and irrigation. Government subsidies help improve productivity, stabilize incomes, and protect farmers from price fluctuations. What subsidy deals with rural employment? The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) provides a subsidy for rural employment. It guarantees 100 days of paid employment per year to adult members of rural households. What is a tax subsidy? A tax subsidy is a government incentive that reduces the tax burden on businesses through tax rebates or reduced tax rates. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Loans have emerged as an essential financial tool in recent years. With careful planning, loans can not only let you indulge in materialistic needs but can also provide financial aid in times of emergencies. However, not everyone can take advantage of loans . Most financial institutions deny loans to individuals with a bad credit score or no sources of income. Desperate for money, these unfortunate souls often end up as victims of cunning loan sharks. In this article, we delve into the depths of this issue, exploring what a loan shark is, how to identify one, and, most importantly, how to stay safe. Loan shark definition: What does loan shark mean in banking & business? A loan shark, also known as a money shark, is someone or a group that engages in predatory lending practices outside the boundaries of the law. Unlike legitimate financial institutions , loan sharks do not follow the regulations set by the RBI. With their local network, loan sharks seek out vulnerable individuals in desperate need of money. Benefiting from their situation, the lenders offer them instant cash even with a poor credit history. However, these loans are provided without any clarity on the loan terms. As a result, the people caught in this trap often get stuck in a vicious cycle of debt , struggling to make payments that don’t seem to dent the original amount they owe. When they fail to repay their debt, these lenders send goons to threaten and extort money by any means necessary. How does loan sharking work? Now that you’ve understood loan sharks’ meaning, it’s time to focus on how they work. A loan shark offers cash without performing any checks on the borrower. So, they may seem like a savior, but their working style is absolutely unsafe. Keep personal belongings as security: A loan shark will take jewelry, property papers, or ID cards and give you money without a legal agreement. Transfer money immediately: A loan shark lends money without background verification. This may seem lucrative, but there is no safety like banks. Collects money frequently: Unlike bank loans that have a monthly installment, loan sharks can ask for small payments often. Most of these payments cover only the high interest, with the actual loan never getting repaid. How to identify a loan shark: Typical loan shark tactics Knowing how to spot a loan shark is essential to safeguard yourself from falling into their traps. Keep an eye out for these red flags in a lender: No official authorization: Legitimate lenders are registered and overseen by financial authorities. However, loan sharks frequently lack the licenses and approvals to function as legitimate lenders. Pushy tactics: Loan sharks might use forceful methods to pressure you into quick decisions. They often make the offer seem lucrative and make you feel like you will lose an excellent opportunity if you don’t agree to their terms immediately. Lack of clarity: Reputable lenders provide transparent documentation that clearly spells out loan terms , interest rates, extra charges, and repayment plans. On the other hand, loan sharks might dodge offering detailed information, leaving borrowers clueless about the actual loan costs. Extremely high interest rates: A major red flag for spotting a loan shark is the excessively high interest rate they impose, often surpassing legal limits by a large margin. These high and recurring interest rates often end up being much larger than the initial borrowed sum. Risks and disadvantages of using a loan shark Loan sharks may seem helpful, but here are the risks and disadvantages you may face in the future: Hidden charges: Since there is no legal agreement, you can be asked to pay any fees at any time. You can’t judge the actual loan cost until it is too late. Harassment: Loan sharks can threaten and intimidate you by sending goons. They can put you under a lot of mental stress. Excessive interest: Loan sharks levy a higher rate of interest, making you repay a lot more than the borrowed amount. Collateral loss: If you fail to repay the loan, loan sharks can seize your assets illegally. How to deal with loan sharks: Risks & safety steps You can steer clear of illegal money sharks by following these tactics: Do your homework: It’s always wise to thoroughly research a lender before taking a loan. Ensure they have the necessary licenses and are regulated by the appropriate financial authorities. Go through the details: Take your time to read and understand all the loan documents before putting your signature on anything. Trustworthy lenders provide clear and easy-to-understand terms and conditions without hurrying you to decide. Compare different options: Don’t hesitate to get loan quotes from several lenders. Comparing interest rates and loan terms can help you spot offers that don’t make sense. Report anything fishy: The government has been taking measures to stop illegal moneylending practices in India. So, if you suspect that a lender is using unfair tactics, report them to the relevant authorities immediately. Why do people turn to loan sharks? Individuals turn to loan sharks when they have urgent financial needs , and banks and formal financial institutions are of no help. Their loan applications are often rejected because of low income, poor credit scores, or no collateral. Loan sharks offer instant cash with minimal paperwork. This may seem convenient during difficult situations. However, what many borrowers don’t understand is the loan shark meaning in business. There are many associated risks and challenges. But since the need for funds is urgent, a lack of financial awareness and delays in bank loan approvals push people toward these illegal lenders. Conclusion Loan sharking has been a concern for ages now. Most people believe that illegal money lending is restricted to rural areas, but that is not the case. With many unlawful money lending apps also emerging recently, more people are prone to being loan-sharking victims than ever before. Hence, it is always advised to take loans from reputed and trusted financial institutions like Tata Capital. With loan transparency, competitive interest rates, and flexible eligibility criteria, Tata Capital ensures your loan process is seamless and safe. Apply for a personal loan today! A loan shark is an unauthorized, illegal moneylender who offers instant loans at very high interest rates. These individuals do not follow any legal or regulatory rules. They use threats or pressure to extort money if you delay repayment. What is the meaning of loan shark in business and finance? A loan shark’s meaning in business and finance is that of an unlicensed lender who imposes unfair terms and charges exorbitant interest. A loan shark also uses illegal or unethical methods of recovering money. Are loan shark loans legal in India? No, loan shark loans aren’t legal in India. These individuals operate without RBI approval, violate state moneylending laws, and do not legally protect borrowers. How can you spot or identify a loan shark? The top signs to identify a loan shark are as follows: Instant cash disbursal Very high interest No written agreement No to minimal documentation requirements Try to push with urgency Offer too good to be true deals What risks are involved in borrowing from a loan shark? Borrowing from a loan shark can lead to debt traps, threats, harassment, violence, and collateral loss. Their illegal money recovery practices can cause severe mental stress. What is the difference between a loan shark and a licensed lender? A loan shark is an illegal, unregistered lender. It charges excessive interest and uses unethical tactics. A licensed lender complies with RBI guidelines, levies standard interest rates, and uses legal recovery methods. Where can I report a loan shark in India? You can report a loan shark to the local police or the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal through their website - www.cybercrime.gov.in - or the helpline 1930. You can also use RBI’s CMS portal or reach out to the Banking Ombudsman. Some of the most common are “deductions” and “exemptions.” Deductions reduce the amount of income that can be taxed, whereas exemptions exclude certain types of income from taxation altogether. Understanding the difference between exemption and deduction is crucial to managing your taxes efficiently. Tax deductions refer to specific investments or expenses that may be deducted from taxable income. Tax exemptions, on the other hand, refer to parts of income that are exempt from taxation to begin with. In this article, we look deeper into what the two terms mean and the primary exemption and deduction differences. Deduction vs exemption: Meaning & key differences It is important to know what differentiates a tax exemption from a deduction. The table below highlights the key differences between deduction and exemption in income tax. Aspect Tax deduction Tax exemption Scope Tax deductions can be applied to varied expenses and investments Exemptions are limited only to specific categories of income Method of application They are deducted from one’s total income before tax calculation They are not included in one’s taxable income at all Impact on income Deductions lower the portion of your income that is subject to tax Exemptions remove certain income types from taxation Objective Their objective is to improve one’s savings, investments, and eligible expenses Their objective is to provide relief for certain income categories Restrictions They are subjected to pre-determined caps based on the deduction They have no tax liability; therefore, no limits Flexibility They are more diverse and flexible They are more uniform and standardized Amount The amount significantly varies based on expenses Exemptions are generally fixed amounts Tax deduction meaning & top examples (India) To understand the difference between exemption and deduction, it is first essential to understand each term. Tax deductions refer to particular expenses and investments deducted from an individual’s taxable income. This lowers their taxable amount, encouraging savings, retirement planning, and other healthy financial practices. For example, Mr. Mehta’s income is Rs. 10 lakhs. He chooses to invest Rs. 1 lakh into a public provident fund. According to section 80C of the Income Tax Act, Rs. 1 lakh is then deducted from Mr. Mehta’s taxable income. Therefore, his taxable income is now only Rs. 9 lakhs. Here are some of the tax deductions available under various sections of the Income Tax Act of 1961. Note that the list is not an exhaustive one. Schemes under Section 80C: Under Section 80C, when individuals invest in a Public Provident Fund (PPF), Equity-Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS), Home Loan Principal Amount Repayments, National Savings Certificate (NSC), Employee Provident Fund (EPF), Pension plans, or Property Stamp Duty and Registration Fees, the amount can be deducted from their taxable income. The limit is up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per annum. Section 80D: Premiums ranging from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 1 lakh paid towards health insurance for individuals and families are tax-deductible. The amount also depends on the insurer’s age. Other deductions are available for the treatment of dependents’ disabilities and for specified diseases. Section 80E: Interest paid on education and homes for first-time home buyers can also be deducted from taxable income. This tax deduction encourages higher education for students whose parents cannot afford the expensive fees. Similarly, the tax deduction on interest payments on a housing loan is provided to encourage investment in domestic real estate. Section 80G: This section enables one to claim tax deductions on contributions to social causes and political parties. The deduction allows the government to support these organizations and social initiatives. Section 80TTA: Section 80TTA provides individuals with a deduction of up to Rs. 10,000 on any income earned through interest on savings made in a financial institution, co-operative society, or post office. Some examples of tax deductions include: Donations: Charitable donations made to registered charities can be deducted from an individual’s taxable income. Educational expenses: In some cases, expenses like tuition fees could be deducted from education-related costs. Medical expenses: Under some circumstances, major dental or medical expenses could also become deductible. Mortgage interest: If an individual has a mortgage on their home, the interest may be deductible. Tax exemption meaning & top examples (India) In some cases, a particular portion of an individual’s income is considered to be tax-free right from its source. These portions are referred to as “tax exemptions.” Tax exemption’s meaning in income tax is that you do not need to spend or invest this portion of your income anywhere to be able to claim the exemption. To understand what an exemption in income tax is, let’s look at some examples: Long-term capital gains: LTCG on Equity mutual funds is typically exempt from taxation. However, it is important to note that there is a limit on this exemption. Up to Rs. 1.25 lakh, LTCGs may be exempt. However, beyond this limit, a tax rate of 12.5% will be implemented. Housing rent allowance: HRA is part of an employee’s salary and is tax-exempt if the employee lives in a rental house. However, it cannot exceed at least one of the following: The rent paid, minus 10% of the taxpayer’s salary; any actual HRA received from the employer; or a portion of their salary (50% for employees in metro cities, and 40% for those not in metro cities). Leave travel allowance: Some employers may also pay employees a Leave Travel Allowance, which is often used for travelling during time off. Taxpayers can claim an exemption on this amount. However, it is important to note that this exemption may only be availed of once every 4 years. Agricultural income: All agricultural income in India is exempt from taxation. This is because agriculture is the only source of income for many in rural India. The country is also entirely dependent on farming for food security. If it were not tax-exempt, food would become too expensive. Lowest income tax slab: An income of Rs. 5 lakhs and below is completely exempt from income tax. This means that if one has an income of Rs. 7 lakhs, Rs. 2 lakhs is taxable income. How to decide: When to use deduction or exemption for tax savings? If you are confused about when it’s right to use tax deductions or exemptions, you must know that the decision is dependent on your income, expenses, and chosen tax regime. Deductions reduce your taxable income, while exemptions exclude certain income from tax. Read on to learn how you can make an informed decision: Learn about the different tax regimes: Under the old tax regime, you can claim many tax deductions and exemptions. But under the new tax regime, the tax rates are lower, and the benefits are fewer. Check your expenses: If you have invested in PPF, ELSS, insurance, or pay home loan interest , deductions may give better savings. Consider your salary structure: Under the old tax regime , allowances like HRA or LTA work as exemptions. Compare both options: Calculate taxes under both old and new regimes before filing. You must choose the option that gives lower tax and suits your financial habits. Section 10, 80C, and HRA: Key tax exemptions and deductions The following tax exemptions and deductions can help reduce taxable income and save on taxes when used properly. Section 10: It covers tax-free income like HRA, LTA, gratuity, and certain allowances, mainly for salaried employees under the old tax regime. HRA refers to house rent allowance. It provides an exemption on rent paid, based on salary, rent amount, and city of residence. Section 80C: It allows you to claim deductions of up to Rs. 1.5 lakh for investments like PPF, ELSS, life insurance, EPF, and tuition fees. New tax regime A new tax regime was introduced in the Budget 2023. As per this regime, the following changes have been made: Various tax deductions and exemptions, such as HRA, LTA, Section 80C, etc., have been done away with. However, the income exempted from income tax has been increased to Rs. 7 lakhs. While one has the option to continue to file taxes under the old tax regime, unless the taxpayer specifies otherwise, the new regime will be the default applicable regime. Taxpayers must choose one of the tax regimes after taking into account the difference between deduction and exemption in income tax as available in the old regime, against those available in the new regime for their income. It is advisable to choose one regime over the other only after calculating the tax payable under each of these regimes. Conclusion While the terms tax deductions and exemptions may appear similar (as both reduce a person’s total tax payable), they are entirely different concepts. Understanding the exemption and deduction differences can help individuals manage their finances more efficiently. Planning ahead for these can not only optimize your tax savings but also help your investment strategy and long-term wealth creation goals. Yes, you can claim both. Deductions and exemptions work together to help reduce your taxable income and overall tax liability within the same financial year. Is it better to have a deduction or an exemption? The choice depends on your situation. Both reduce taxable income differently. Deductions often depend on expenses, while exemptions may relate to your family or income structure. Can exemptions and deductions be carried forward to the next financial year? Carrying forward depends on the specific deduction or exemption and applicable tax rules. Some may be carried forward, while others cannot. What happens if I incorrectly claim a deduction or an exemption? If an individual wrongly files for an exemption or deduction, they may be subjected to interest charges or penalties. To ensure you are accurately claiming tax deductions and exemptions, it is important to consult a professional or utilise reliable tax software platforms. How do changes in tax laws affect deductions and exemptions? Deductions and exemptions can be significantly affected by changes in tax laws. New laws may alter the existing deduction, and exemption amounts or introduce new ones. Staying informed about taxation regulations can help you plan your finances and maximise your savings. What is the main difference between a tax exemption and a deduction in India? A tax exemption removes certain income from being taxed, while a tax deduction reduces your total taxable income after it is calculated. Both help lower taxes, but they work differently. Are tax deductions and exemptions both allowed under the new regime? No, the new tax regime allows very limited deductions and almost no exemptions. Most benefits, such as 80C, HRA, and LTA, are available only under the old tax regime. What are some popular exemptions and deductions Indian taxpayers can claim? Some popular exemptions include HRA and LTA. Similarly, some common deductions include Section 80C investments, Section 80D health insurance, and home loan interest under Section 24. What is an HRA - a tax exemption or deduction? HRA is a tax exemption. It helps to reduce taxable salary if you pay rent. However, you must meet the required conditions under the old tax regime to claim the exemption. How do I choose between using deduction or exemption for tax savings? To choose between deduction and exemption, you must first understand deduction and exemption meaning in income tax. Then, compare the tax under both regimes based on your income and expenses. If you have high investments and allowances, the old regime may help save more taxes. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund The PM Vishwakarma scheme is a testament to the government’s dedication to the welfare of skilled professionals, affirming its commitment to the principles of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ and ‘Skill India.’ By extending accessible financial aid and promoting entrepreneurship among the artisans and craftspeople, this scheme is poised to create a thriving ecosystem that celebrates and preserves India’s diverse artistic traditions while fostering economic growth at the grassroots level. This 3-lakh loan government scheme aims to enable artisans to sustain their traditional crafts and explore avenues for expansion and modernization, thereby contributing to the nation’s economic development. Understanding the PM Vishwakarma Scheme is crucial for artisans, craftspeople, aspiring entrepreneurs, and policymakers to ensure its positive impact on the socio-economic fabric of India. Vishwakarma Scheme: What is PM Vishwakarma Yojana and how does it work? The PM Vishwakarma Loan Scheme is an initiative by the Indian government to provide crucial financial support to artisans, skilled professionals, and entrepreneurs involved in traditional crafts and artistic endeavors. This government loan scheme 2023 encompasses several critical features designed to facilitate the growth and development of this vital sector. Some of the primary components of the 3-lakh loan government scheme include: • Recognition of all Indian artists and craftspeople as Vishwakarma and providing commercial advantages to them • Periodic training in business and industry-related skills to enhance effectiveness • Modernization of manufacturing equipment for improved efficiency, productivity, and product quality • Provision of collateral-free, low-interest loans and interest rate rebates to beneficiaries • Digital empowerment through education and digital transactions • Promotion of Vishwakarma’s goods and increased sales through market involvement Vishwakarma Scheme eligibility: Who can apply for a 3-lakh loan? Below are the Vishwakarma Scheme eligibility criteria: 1. Must be an Indian citizen engaged in traditional crafts, such as pottery, weaving, woodwork, metalwork, and other forms of indigenous artistry 2. Have a valid Aadhaar card and a bank account 3. Age must be between 18 and 35 years 4. Completed at least six months of training in their respective field 5. Must not have defaulted on previous loans or government schemes 6. A viable business plan for the loan amount they are applying for Trades covered under the Vishwakarma Yojana Here are the trades covered under this 3-lakh loan government scheme: 1. Wood-based trades: Carpenters and boat makers. 2. Iron/metal-based/stone-based trades: Armorers, blacksmiths (Lohar), hammer and tool kit makers, locksmiths, sculptors and stone breakers 3. Gold/silver-based trades: Goldsmiths 4. Clay-based trades: Potters 5. Leather-based trades: Cobblers and shoesmiths/footwear artisans 6. Architecture/construction trades: Masons 7. Other trades: Doll and toy makers, barbers, garland makers, washers, tailors, and fishing net makers Documents required for PM Vishwakarma Loan Scheme Below are the documents required to avail of the PM Vishwakarma Loan Scheme: 1. Aadhar card 2. Voter ID card 3. PAN card 4. Domicile certificate 5. Email ID 6. Passport size color photograph 7. Work-related documents 8. Bank account details 9. Income certificate 10. Caste certificate How to apply online for the PM Vishwakarma Loan Scheme To apply online for PM Vishwakarma Yojana, follow these steps: 1. Go to the official website of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme . 2. Create an account if you’re a new user or log in using your existing credentials. 3. Complete the online application form by providing your personal information and contact details. 4. Choose the relevant skill development program or course you wish to apply for. 5. Upload the necessary documents per the specified requirements, including proof of identity and educational certificates. 6. Review and edit your application for any errors or missing information. 7. Finally, submit the application form online. PM Vishwakarma Loan interest rate, amount & repayment details 2026 The PM Vishwakarma Loan Scheme offers collateral-free loans of up to Rs. 3 lakh to eligible beneficiaries. Under the PM Vishwakarma Loan Scheme, the credit is disbursed in two tranches. The first tranche offers a loan of up to Rs. 1 lakh with a repayment period of 18 months. Once the first tranche is repaid, beneficiaries become eligible for the second tranche of up to Rs. 2 lakh, which comes with a longer repayment period of 30 months. The loan is offered at a concessional interest rate of 5% per annum. The remaining interest is supported through an interest subvention of up to 8%. In addition to credit support, beneficiaries also receive an incentive of Rs. 1 per digital transaction, for up to 100 transactions per month. Key features of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme Here are the key features of the PM Vishwakarma scheme: 1. Budget allocation: In the 2023-2024 budget address, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman allocated a substantial sum of Rs. 13,000 crore for the implementation of the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, emphasizing the government’s commitment to supporting the development of the artisan community. 2. Direct benefits and diverse community focus: The 3-lakh loan government scheme is tailored to benefit Vishwakarma workers across various communities. Recognizing the diverse nature of the Vishwakarma community, the program is designed to cater to the specific needs and challenges faced by artisans from different backgrounds and regions. 3. Empowerment through practical training: A vital component of the scheme is providing practical training to artisans and craftsmen, particularly in regions such as Kargil. This training initiative aims to equip them with the necessary skills and knowledge to enhance their craftsmanship, modernize their techniques, and effectively navigate the evolving market demands. 4. Facilitation of loans: The government’s provision of loans ranging from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh, with a contribution of 5% to these loans, serves as a significant financial boost for artisans. This financial aid is instrumental in supporting their businesses, facilitating the acquisition of modern tools and equipment, and promoting overall growth and sustainability within the sector. 5. Employment generation and financial stability: By focusing on creating employment opportunities within the community, the PM Vishwakarma Yojana aims to stimulate economic activity, improve livelihoods, and enhance the financial stability of Vishwakarma workers and their families, thereby fostering a more sustainable and inclusive socio-economic environment. 6. Inclusivity and reach: The comprehensive nature of the scheme ensures that a significant portion of Vishwakarma workers, including millions of traditional tool-using craftsmen and traditional artists, can benefit from the program. Furthermore, the scheme’s outreach extends to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, women, tribals, and other marginalized and disadvantaged groups, promoting inclusivity and equal access to the benefits for all eligible beneficiaries. How to check PM Vishwakarma loan status online & download certificate To download your PM Vishwakarma certificate, log in to the official PM Vishwakarma Loan Yojana portal using your registered mobile number or login credentials. Once the verification process is completed and your application is approved, you will be registered as a “Vishwakarma” on the portal. You can then log in to the portal and download your Vishwakarma Certificate and ID card. To check the loan status under the Vishwakarma Loan Scheme , you can refer to your linked bank account statement or contact your bank branch directly, as loan processing and updates are handled by the bank. Common mistakes to avoid in the PM Vishwakarma Loan application Here are some mistakes you must avoid when you apply for the PM Vishwakarma Loan: 1. Incorrect trade selection : Make sure you select a trade that is covered under the Vishwakarma Loan Scheme, as incorrect trade details can lead to rejection. 2. Multiple applications from the same family : Understand the Vishwakarma Scheme eligibility rules. Only one member per family is eligible, so confirm that your spouse or unmarried children have not applied. 3. Incorrect documents : Submit all required documents correctly to avoid rejection. 4. Skipping training : Complete the mandatory basic training, as it is required to receive the toolkit incentive and the first loan tranche. Conclusion The PM Vishwakarma Scheme is a significant step towards promoting the growth and development of traditional artisans and craftspeople in India. The scheme’s focus on providing financial aid, training, and modernization support will boost the economy and preserve India’s rich artistic traditions. It is given in two tranches, Rs. 1 lakh first and Rs. 2 lakh later, at a concessional interest rate of 5% per annum, with interest subvention support of up to 8%. Who is eligible for the PM Vishwakarma 3 lakh government scheme? Artisans and craftspeople engaged in self-employment in notified traditional trades in the unorganized sector are eligible for the 3-lakh loan government scheme. Additionally, applicants must be at least 18 years old, only one member per family can apply, and no government loan should have been taken out in the last five years. How do I apply online for the PM Vishwakarma scheme? You need to log in to the PM Vishwakarma Loan Portal through a Common Service Centre (CSC). Complete mobile verification and Aadhaar e-KYC. Post that, submit the Artisan Registration Form and register on the Udyam Assist Platform. How can I check PM Vishwakarma loan application status and download my certificate? Log in to the PM Vishwakarma Yojana portal using your registered credentials. Once your application is verified and approved, you can download your Vishwakarma Certificate and ID card. For loan updates, check your bank statement or contact your bank branch. What documents are required for the Vishwakarma loan scheme to apply online? You need an Aadhaar card, a registered mobile number, bank account details, and a ration card for the Vishwakarma loan scheme if you apply online. If you do not have a ration card, you need to submit the Aadhaar cards of all family members. Additionally, applicants without a bank account must first complete bank account opening formalities. collateral. You are typically allowed to borrow between 75% and 95% of your investment value, depending on the lender’s policy. The loan can be taken for different purposes and usually comes with lower interest rates compared to unsecured personal loans. A loan against fixed deposit is a loan you can take by pledging your fixed deposit with the lender while allowing your investment to continue earning interest throughout the tenure. If you have ever wondered, “Can I take a loan against my fixed deposit?”, the answer is yes. A loan against fixed deposit allows you to access funds in times of need without breaking your investment. This guide explains what a loan against a fixed deposit is, how it works, the loan against fixed deposit interest rate, the loan amount you can get, its benefits and disadvantages, and the different types of loans you can avail of against your fixed deposit. What is a loan against fixed deposit and how does it work? A loan against fixed deposit is a secured loan where your fixed deposit acts as collateral with the lender. Instead of breaking your fixed deposit, you pledge it to borrow some percentage of the deposit value. The lender places a lien on your fixed deposit until you repay the outstanding loan amount, while your investment continues to earn interest as per its original terms. You can repay the loan through Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs) or by using the overdraft facility , if available. Once done, the lien is lifted, and you regain full access to your fixed deposit. Learn More – Loan Against Securities What is the loan against fixed deposit interest rate? The loan against fixed deposit interest rate is generally lower than the interest rate charged by unsecured personal loans because your fixed deposit serves as collateral. Most lenders typically charge an interest rate that is 1% to 2% higher than your fixed deposit interest rate, although the exact rate varies across lenders and the type of fixed deposit. For instance, if your fixed deposit earns 5% interest per annum, you can typically obtain a loan at 6% to 7% per annum. Check – Loan Against Securities Interest Rates & Charges Loan amount against fixed deposit: How much can you get? If you are wondering, “ Can I take a loan against my fixed deposit,and how much can I get? “, the loan amount typically depends on the value of your fixed deposit and the lender’s policy. Most banks and financial institutions offer 75% to 90% of the fixed deposit value as the loan amount. Some lenders may also sanction up to 95%, depending on their Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio. These figures are indicative and vary across lenders. However, the loan amount cannot exceed the value of your fixed deposit in any case. What are the benefits of a loan against fixed deposit? A loan against fixed deposit offers several benefits, such as: Lower interest rates compared to unsecured loans. No need to break your investment to access funds. Continued interest earnings on your fixed deposit until it matures. Quick approval and disbursal with minimal documentation and relaxed eligibility criteria. Flexible end use, as the funds can be used for almost any purpose, unlike a car or home loan. Can you take different types of loans against a fixed deposit? Yes. Fixed deposits can help you access different types of loans. However, not every fixed deposit qualifies as collateral. Some common loan options and exclusions include: Personal loan against fixed deposit Education loan against fixed deposit Car loan against fixed deposit Home loan against fixed deposit: Suitable for smaller funding needs. For larger home purchases, a traditional home loan such as Tata Capital Home Loan may be a better option. Loan against tax saver fixed deposit: Not permitted, as tax-saving fixed deposits have a mandatory five-year lock-in period and cannot be pledged as collateral. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A CIBIL score ranges from 300 to 900, with 900 being the highest possible score. While a perfect score is rare, most lenders consider 750 or above to be an excellent credit score. Making timely repayments, maintaining low credit utilization, and responsible borrowing habits are far more important than trying to achieve a perfect 900. The maximum CIBIL score in India is 900, although a score of 750 or above is generally considered excellent for loan eligibility. Your CIBIL score is one of the first things a lender checks when you apply for a loan or credit card. It reflects how responsibly you have managed your credit over the years and plays a key role in loan approval. But have you ever wondered what is the maximum CIBIL score in India and whether it is actually possible to achieve it? This guide explains the highest possible score, what it means, and the habits that can help you get there. What is the maximum CIBIL score in India? The maximum CIBIL score in India is 900. The CIBIL score range typically runs from 300 to 900. A higher score indicates stronger creditworthiness, and vice versa. Note that if a person has never taken a loan or a credit card , their CIBIL score is not 300. Instead, their credit report mentions NA (Not Applicable) or NH (No History). Is a 900 CIBIL score actually possible? While 900 is the maximum score in CIBIL, it is practically impossible to achieve it. A perfect score requires years of flawless repayments, a long credit history, and a healthy mix of credit accounts. And even then, it is not guaranteed. In practice, a score of 750 or above is considered excellent by most lenders. Also Read – How to Increase CIBIL Score From 600 to 750 What CIBIL score do you actually need for a loan? A high CIBIL score certainly helps, but it is not the only factor lenders consider. Your income, existing EMIs, employment stability, and debt-to-income ratio are also assessed before a loan decision is made. So, there is no fixed maximum CIBIL score for loan approval . The table below depicts the CIBIL score ranges and loan approval chances: CIBIL Score Range Loan Approval Chances 300 – 549 Low 550 – 649 Fair, subject to strict checks 650 – 749 Good 750 or above High What affects your CIBIL score? The following factors typically affect your CIBIL score: Repayment history: Your record of paying EMIs and credit card bills on time; this is the single biggest factor. Credit utilization ratio: The percentage of your available credit that you regularly use. Credit mix: The balance between secured loans and unsecured credit in your profile. Length of credit history: The age of your oldest and active credit accounts. Recent hard inquiries: The number of loan or credit card applications made with lenders in a short period. Also Read – How to Build Credit Score from Zero? How to achieve and maintain a high CIBIL score? Instead of trying to achieve a perfect score of 900, you should aim to reach and maintain your CIBIL score above 750. If you are wondering how to achieve maximum CIBIL score, these practical tips can help: Pay all your loan EMIs and credit card bills on time. Keep your credit utilization ratio below 30%. Do not close old credit accounts unnecessarily. Avoid applying for multiple loans or credit cards within a short period. Maintain a balanced mix of secured and unsecured credit. Check your credit report regularly and raise a dispute if you find any errors. There is no fixed timeline for improving a CIBIL score. Credit bureaus update your records only after lenders report them, which is typically done every month. Thus, changes are not immediate. Borrowers with a short credit history may see their scores change differently from those with a long credit history or past defaults. Also Read – Tips to improve CIBIL score after a payment default What are the common myths about the maximum CIBIL score? Myths Facts Checking your CIBIL score lowers it. Self-checks do not affect your score. A high score guarantees loan approval. Lenders look at several other factors too. Closing old credit cards improves your score. It’s the opposite. You need a 900 CIBIL score for the best loan rates. 900 score is practically impossible. A score of 750 or above will do. Taking no loans results in a perfect score. It only shows NA or NH. Conclusion While 900 is the maximum CIBIL score in India, it is practically impossible to achieve. A score of 750 or above is generally enough to be viewed favorably by most lenders. Consistent repayments and disciplined credit usage matter far more than chasing perfection. You can also check your eligibility for a Tata Capital Personal Loan before applying. property deposits, brokerage, travel, and accommodation. While it offers much-needed support, you should consider borrowing only after checking for any available employer relocation allowances. A personal loan for moving is a standard personal loan that helps manage expenses incurred during relocation. Moving to a new city brings several upfront expenses. Funding these entirely from your pocket may strain your finances, especially in a new environment. This is where a personal loan for relocation can help. This article explains the typical cost of relocating, the expenses a personal loan for moving can cover, alternative ways to fund your move, and the key factors to consider before borrowing. What does relocating to a new city actually cost? The cost of moving depends on factors such as the distance, the destination city, family size, and lifestyle. You can get an indicative estimate of common relocation expenses in India from the table below. Expense Indicative cost Rs. * Packers and movers (intercity) 10,000 to 50,000+ Rental security deposit Two to three months’ rent (may be higher in some metros) Brokerage charges Around one month’s rent Travel expenses for family 2,000 to 30,000+ Temporary accommodation 2,000 to 8,000 per night Basic furniture and appliances 30,000 to 1,50,000+ Vehicle transportation 5,000 to 20,000 School admission or transfer costs Varies by school *Indicative costs only. Actual expenses may differ. What is a personal loan for relocation? A personal loan can be used for a variety of purposes. A personal loan for relocation is not a separate financial product; it is a standard unsecured personal loan that can be used to fund moving-related expenses. It is often suitable for relocation because it requires no collateral, has no end-use restriction, and offers quick disbursal. Also Read – What is a Good Credit Score in India? What relocation expenses can a personal loan cover? Depending on your needs, you may use the loan for expenses such as: Packers and movers charges Security deposit and brokerage Travel and temporary stay expenses for your family Furniture and essential household appliances Vehicle transport costs School admission fees for children Initial living expenses until your first salary is credited in the new city Also Read – What is EMI and How Does it Work What are the benefits of using a personal loan to relocate? A personal loan for relocation can reduce the financial pressure of meeting major moving expenses during the initial stages of your transition. Some of its benefits are: Collateral-free borrowing: No need to pledge a hard-earned asset for a one-time expense. Flexible repayment tenure: Spread the relocation cost across affordable Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs). Quick disbursal: Access funds when you need them the most. No end-use restriction : Use a single loan to cover different relocation expenses. Personal loan vs other ways to fund your move Before opting for a personal loan, it is prudent to compare it with other funding options: Funding option Pros Cons Savings No interest cost Can significantly reduce your emergency savings Employer relocation allowance May fully or partially cover relocation expenses Not offered by all employers and may not cover the entire cost Credit card Quick access to funds High revolving interest if not repaid on time Loan against fixed deposit or gold Lower interest rates Requires pledging an asset Personal loan Collateral-free, predictable EMIs, flexible usage Interest, processing fees, and other applicable charges may apply What are the eligibility criteria and documents required? Eligibility varies across lenders but generally depends on factors such as your age, employment, income, work experience, and credit score . Keep your identity, address, income proof, and bank statements ready to facilitate quicker verification. Tip: Apply before changing your salary account or address to avoid verification delays. Also Read – Documents Required for Personal Loan How to apply for a personal loan for relocation? Here’s how you can apply for a personal loan for relocation: Check your eligibility . Decide the loan amount and use an EMI Calculator to estimate your EMI and choose a suitable tenure. Complete the online application form. Submit the required documents. Receive approval and disbursal after successful verification. What should you consider before borrowing for relocation? A personal loan may support you financially in a new city. That said, it is still a monetary commitment. Before borrowing, keep the following points in mind: Check your employer’s relocation benefits before applying, as they may cover part or all of your moving costs. Borrow only the shortfall after using your savings or employer reimbursement. Keep EMIs affordable, especially if you are relocating for a new job and settling into a new city. Factor in the total borrowing cost, including processing fees and other applicable charges, not just the EMI. Understand the impact on your credit profile, especially if you plan to apply for a home loan or another major loan in the near future. Conclusion Relocation costs can run into lakhs. A personal loan for moving lets you spread these expenses over time without pledging any collateral. Before applying, check whether your employer offers relocation assistance and borrow only the amount you need. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary Unsecured loans in India are cash loans that you can secure without any collateral. They do not require pledging a house, car, or any other asset as security. Lenders estimate your loan eligibility based on your credit score, job stability, and monthly income. The different types of unsecured loans include personal loans, credit cards, payday loans, business loans, and lines of credit. Since there is no physical asset to take possession of upon default, the lender’s risk with an unsecured loan is higher. Getting unsecured loans in India is easy, as there is no collateral requirement. You can choose from the different types of unsecured loans based on your needs. Do you need money but don’t want to pledge your property or other assets? That’s where various types of unsecured loans can help. Read on to know more. What is an unsecured loan? An unsecured loan is a collateral-free loan in which approval is based on your credit profile and income. However, with no pledged asset, the lender’s risk increases. As a result, interest rates are higher, and loan amounts are smaller than for secured loans. Read on to learn about the types of unsecured loans in India. What are the types of unsecured loans in India? The following table describes the different types of unsecured loans you can apply for in India: Loan type Typical use Indicative tenure Key feature Personal loan Medical emergencies, expenses for wedding, travel, home renovation, and debt consolidation 1 to 7 years Suited for salaried or self-employed borrowers Credit card Everyday spending, shopping, travel No fixed tenure A revolving credit facility, where you can repay the full amount or minimum due each month Unsecured business loan Inventory, expansion, operating expenses 1 to 5 years Suitable for MSMEs and businesses needing quick working capital Education loan Tuition fees, accommodation, and other education expenses Up to 13 years Loan limits may change as per course, institution, and co-applicant Consumer durable loan Electronics, appliances, gadgets Up to 6 years No-cost EMI may be available through partner merchants Line of credit Short-term cash flow needs Renewable facility Interest to be paid only on the amount used Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) Small online and offline purchases 15 days to 12 months Interest-free credit if repaid on time Secured vs unsecured loans: What are the key differences? Secured and unsecured loans in India are different in the following ways: Parameter Secured loan Unsecured loan Collateral Required Not required Interest rate Lower Slightly higher Loan amount Higher Generally lower Repayment tenure Longer Shorter Approval speed Slower due to asset verification Faster with minimal documentation Credit score dependency Important, but collateral also matters Highly dependent on credit score and income Eligibility Based on collateral value and repayment capacity Based on income, credit history, and repayment capacity Lender risk Lower Higher What happens on default? Lender may seize the pledged asset after due process No asset is pledged, but recovery action, penalties, and credit score damage may follow What are the eligibility criteria and documents required for an unsecured loan? Qualifying for an unsecured loan requires the fulfillment of the following conditions: Age: Usually between 21 and 60 years Minimum income: Rs. 15,000 per month Employment: Salaried or self-employed Credit score: 700+ Existing debt: Within budget and repayment capacity The list of required documents includes: Identity and address proof Income proof (salary slips, ITR, etc.) Recent bank statements What are the advantages and disadvantages of unsecured loans? Unsecured loans in India offer several benefits, but they also have some drawbacks. Advantages Disadvantages No collateral required Higher interest rates Faster processing Good credit score needed Minimal documentation Lower loan amounts No end-use restriction Shorter repayment tenure No risk of losing a pledged asset Missed payments can lower your credit score and lead to recovery proceedings Who should consider an unsecured loan? The best borrower profiles for an unsecured loan are: Salaried professionals with a good credit score and a short-term funding requirement. Small business owners seeking working capital without pledging assets. Borrowers with one-time expenses who do not want to mortgage property. If you can pledge an asset and need a larger loan or longer tenure, a secured loan is usually a more cost-effective option. How to apply for an unsecured loan? The step-by-step process to apply for an unsecured loan in India is as follows: Check your credit score to understand your chances of approval. Compare lenders by looking at the interest rate, processing fee, and the total borrowing cost, not just the EMI. Check your eligibility, including income, employment, age, and other lender-specific requirements. Fill out the personal loan application form online on the lender’s website or app. Upload the required documents with accurate details. Receive the sanction letter and, once approved, the loan amount is disbursed to your account. Conclusion Unsecured loans in India offer a convenient way to borrow funds without pledging assets. However, choosing the right option from the list of unsecured loans is important. Make sure you review the purposes of the different types of unsecured loans, their interest rates, fees, eligibility, and repayment terms before proceeding. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund Summary A loan sanction letter is an official written document issued by a bank or lender, confirming the approval of your loan application. It contains the approved loan amount, interest rate, repayment time, and conditions. However, it is different from the loan contract or the actual loan disbursement. The loan sanction letter also mentions the amount of your estimated monthly payment and its own validity period. You must accept the offer within this timeframe. The letter is proof for buyers and sellers that you have financial backing. Lenders send a loan sanction letter upon loan approval. The loan terms, including loan amount, interest rate, and repayment tenure, are mentioned in this official document. If your loan application is moving ahead with the lender, a loan sanction letter is the first exciting sign. This guide will help you learn the loan sanction letter’s meaning, its contents, format, margin, and why it matters before loan disbursement. What is a loan sanction letter? A loan sanction letter is an official document that banks or NBFCs issue after approving your home loan application , subject to certain terms and conditions. It confirms the lender’s willingness to provide the loan, along with the approved loan amount, interest rate, and tenure. If there are any margin requirements or other special conditions, they will also be mentioned. However, a loan sanction letter is different from the final loan agreement. The latter is a legally binding contract signed before the loan is disbursed. What does a loan sanction letter contain? Your loan sanction letter must contain the following details: Component Description Approved loan amount The total amount the lender has approved to lend to you. Interest rate The rate (fixed or floating) at which interest will apply. Loan tenure The time you have to repay the loan. EMI amount Your estimated monthly payment. Margin money Your required contribution towards the property’s cost. Disbursement schedule When and how the loan amount will be released. Validity period The time within which you must accept the offer. Special conditions Any other conditions that you must fulfill before loan disbursement. What is the loan sanction letter format? The loan sanction letter format is generally standard. It includes the lender’s letterhead, borrower details, approved loan amount, interest rate, tenure, EMI, margin requirement, disbursement terms, validity period, and any special conditions. The letter is usually signed and stamped by the lender. The exact format may vary between banks and NBFCs . What is margin in a loan sanction letter? Margin in a loan sanction letter is the portion of the property’s cost you must pay yourself. Lenders usually finance only a percentage of the property value, so the margin is typically 10% to 25%. A higher margin means a lower Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio and a higher upfront payment. For example, if a property is worth Rs. 50 lakh and the margin is 20%, you pay Rs. 10 lakh, while the lender finances the remaining Rs. 40 lakh. What is the importance of a loan sanction letter in a home loan? You may feel that the loan sanction letter is just a document confirming your loan approval. However, a loan sanction letter is important due to various reasons, such as: It confirms your home loan eligibility and approved loan amount. It helps you negotiate confidently with the seller or builder. It is a key document required before loan disbursement. It locks in the offered interest rate and loan tenure for the validity period of the sanction letter. What to check in your loan sanction letter before accepting? Before accepting your loan sanction letter, you must check the approved loan amount, tenure, interest rate type and reset clause, margin money, EMI amount, processing fee, prepayment or foreclosure terms, and the letter’s validity date. All details must match your understanding. Conclusion A loan sanction letter is an important step in the home loan process. Make sure you read it carefully to understand the approved loan terms. This helps avoid surprises later. Get your home repair loan today and transform your space! Apply now FAQs What is a loan sanction letter? A loan sanction letter, meaning the letter provided by the lender after approving your loan application, confirms the approved loan amount, interest rate, tenure, repayment terms, fees, and other conditions. What is the difference between a loan sanction letter and a loan agreement? A loan sanction letter is an approval in principle that outlines the loan terms. On the other hand, a loan agreement is the final legal contract signed by both parties before disbursement. What does a loan sanction letter contain? A loan sanction letter contains all essential details about the loan you’ve borrowed. If you go through the loan sanction letter format, you will see the approved loan amount, interest rate, loan tenure, EMI details, repayment schedule, processing fees, margin requirement (if applicable), validity period, special conditions, and other terms that must be met before disbursement. What is margin in a loan sanction letter? If you want to know what margin is in a loan sanction letter, it is the portion of the asset’s cost that you must pay from your own savings while the lender finances the remaining. How long is a loan sanction letter valid? A loan sanction letter’s validity is limited, often between 30 and 90 days. It depends on the lender and loan type. Can the bank change the terms after issuing the sanction letter? Yes. In some cases, the lender may revise the terms on the loan sanction letter if your financial situation changes, documents reveal new information, or loan conditions are not met. Is a loan sanction letter the same as loan disbursement? No. A loan sanction letter confirms approval of the loan based on the specified terms and conditions. Loan disbursement, on the other hand, happens later when all verification is completed. A Diwali loan offer is a festive season loan across personal, car, home and business categories, built for quick approval during Dhanteras and Diwali. Festive loan offers across products Here are the four most common loan types you can avail this festive season, each suited to a different kind of spending. Loan type Best for Personal loan A personal loan with Diwali offers suits unrestricted spends such as gifting and appliances. Car loan A car loan offer for Diwali is a cheaper, secured route for a vehicle purchase. Home loan Home loan offers for Diwali cover both a property purchase and renovation work. Business loan A Diwali business loan helps traders stock inventory or manage working capital before the rush Muhurat buying: Financing big Diwali purchases Dhanteras and Diwali are traditionally a muhurat window for buying gold, vehicles and property, so demand spikes sharply. Gold As per RBI guidelines, lenders cannot provide loans for purchasing gold in any form, including gold jewelry, coins, or bullion. A personal loan with Diwali offersis a better fit for such purchases. Vehicle A car loan offer for Diwali can help you secure a vehicle booking during the auspicious, festive season, without draining your savings. Property Home loan offers for Diwali can directly help with property purchases. Home upgrades and renovation for Diwali Many households renovate and buy appliances before Diwali guests arrive. A personal loan suits smaller upgrades, since the funds carry no end-use restriction. For bigger work, a renovation loan or a top-up on an existing Diwali loan spreads the cost over a longer tenure. For families that need to purchase multiple appliances, a personal loan instead of a no-cost EMI may work out cheaper. Diwali gifting and celebration spends Gifting and sweets are recurring expenses, and funding them with debt is rarely wise. However, for a genuinely large one-off expense, a personal loan with Diwali offers can spread the cost into affordable EMIs. Why take a loan during Diwali? Festive expenses arrive all at once, and a Diwali loan spreads that cost without disrupting cash flow. Approvals are quick, which matters when purchases are tied to muhurat dates. Flexible tenure keeps EMIs affordable during a traditionally big-purchase season. Loans can be timed to festive deadlines, so funds are available before Dhanteras and Diwali purchases are due. A fixed EMI schedule makes it easier to plan festive spending alongside regular monthly expenses. Benefits of a Diwali festive loan A Diwali dhamaka loan pairs festive convenience with standard safeguards. Personal and business loans need no collateral. Same-day disbursal is available for eligible applicants once verified. EMIs are flexible, and documentation stays minimal. Interest rates stay competitive with standard personal and business loan pricing. Tenure options range from short to long, based on repayment comfort. Eligibility and how to apply Eligibility for a Diwali loan offer depends on the exact lender, though age, income, employment and credit score are checked across all applications. To apply: Check your eligibility using the online eligibility calculator , based on your age, income, employment type, and credit score. Select the loan product that matches your festive need, and fill in your application with income and employment details. Upload KYC and income documents such as PAN, Aadhaar, and salary slips or ITR, depending on the loan type. Review your Key Facts Statement, which discloses the all-inclusive Annual Percentage Rate (APR), before accepting the offer. Once approved, funds are disbursed to your account, with same-day disbursal available for eligible applicants.
