Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund A personal loan is easily available these days. It is an unsecured loan where one doesn’t have to put up any collateral as security. Nowadays, many banks and financial institutions offer pre-approved personal loans to customers with good credit scores. However, some loans cannot be approved unless a guarantor vouches for the applicant’s repayment capacity. What does a personal loan with a guarantor mean? In a personal loan, a guarantor means a person who proves the authenticity of the borrower. Such a person acts as a witness and provides an assurance of the borrower’s credibility to the lender. The guarantor takes a guarantee on behalf of the borrower to repay the loan with interest if the latter defaults in repayment. In such a scenario, the guarantor is legally bound and liable to repay the loan. Types of loan guarantors When it comes to finding a personal loan with a guarantor , borrowers may rely on different kinds of guarantors: 1. Personal guarantor : A friend or family member who steps in if the borrower cannot repay. This is common for personal, education, or small-business loans. 2. Corporate guarantor : A company that supports the borrower’s application, usually for larger business or commercial loans where added financial strength helps. 3. Self-guarantor : A borrower who secures the loan with their own assets, allowing them to avoid involving anyone else. This works for people with solid credit and adequate resources. 4. Government guarantor : Public agencies that back loans through dedicated schemes, making credit more accessible for students, entrepreneurs, and underserved groups. Eligibility criteria for a loan guarantor The eligibility criteria for a loan co-guarantor will vary by financial institution or lender. In most cases, co- guarantor requirements must fit the following criteria: 1. They must be of legal age 2. They must have a stable monthly income. For example, the income for your guarantor must meet a certain minimum every month. 3. They must have a sufficient credit score and a good credit history. Remember to check the CIBIL score for your guarantor to confirm eligibility. In most cases, co-guarantors for personal loans are friends, family members, spouses, or colleagues. If you require a loan with a guarantor , reach out to Tata Capital’s experts for more information on guarantor eligibility ! Also, read – What Are The Risks Of Being A Personal Loan Guarantor Differences between a guarantor and a co-signer When taking on personal or other types of loans, you may be confused about the difference between a guarantor, a co-applicant or a cosigner . Below, we break down the difference between a guarantor vs. co-signer : – A co-signer is someone who takes on full legal responsibility for a borrower’s debt. If the borrower misses payments or falls behind, the co-signer is immediately on the hook to step in and make things right. – A guarantor plays a similar role, but with one key difference: they’re only required to step in if the borrower completely defaults. Essentially, they are a last resort. While a guarantor isn’t required for personal loans, it can increase chances of approval. It is critical to do your research before signing on as a co-signer vs. a guarantor for personal loans. Why do financial institutions offer personal loans with guarantors only? By offering a personal loan with a guarantor, the lender feels more assured about the repayment of the loan. Here are a few situations when a lender may be compelled to ask for a guarantor: If the borrower is not financially secure enough to repay the loan. If the borrower doesn’t have a stable job and keeps changing jobs frequently. If the borrower’s credit score is not good enough to get a personal loan. If the loan amount is beyond a certain limit. If the lender is not convinced or confident that the borrower will repay the loan. If the borrower already has a number of outstanding loans. In some exceptional cases, a guarantor may be required as it is in accordance with the rules and regulations of the financial institution. Responsibilities of a guarantor for a personal loan Before becoming a guarantor, a person should understand the implications it may have. On becoming a guarantor, the person will become equally liable as the borrower. In the case of a default in payment by the borrower, the lender (bank or financial institution from where the loan was taken) can recover the amount from the guarantor. In such circumstances, the lender can also take legal action against the borrower as well as the guarantor. The guarantor’s monthly income and other assets can also be attached to recover an outstanding loan. This is why most banks have guidelines about guarantors; for example, the guarantor should be in a better financial position than the borrower. On the positive side, if the borrower repays on time, the guarantor’s credit score also increases. However, if the borrower defaults in repayment, the guarantor’s credit score will take a hit, even if the guarantor repays the other loans on time. On becoming a guarantor, an individual’s credit limit is also reduced. Things to keep in mind before becoming a guarantor Here are a few tips that an individual must follow before becoming a guarantor: Ensure that the primary borrower is trustworthy. Check whether the borrower will be able to repay the loan on time. If the guarantor is planning on making a big investment for which they might need a loan in the near future, they should reconsider being a guarantor. Guarantor personal loans impact the guarantor’s credit score as well, which might negatively impact their ability to get other loans in the future. Know why the primary borrower is applying for a loan and assess the risk involved. Ask for a co-guarantor. This way, in case of default in repayment, the entire financial burden will not fall on one guarantor. Read the loan agreement thoroughly and understand it. The guarantor should know what the implications will be if the borrower is critically ill or no more in the future to be financially prepared in such scenarios. Keep checking with the borrower about the progress of their repayment. Also, read – The Role of Co-Applicant in Enhancing Education Loan Eligibility Last words of advice Before signing the loan agreement of a guarantor personal loan, the guarantor should chalk out their contingency plan in case the primary borrower is unable to repay the loan and the burden of repayment falls on the guarantor. Before agreeing to be a guarantor, one should consider factors like the creditworthiness of the primary borrower, their own short-term or long-term financial goals, the borrower’s repayment capacity, the amount of loan etc. Additionally, the guarantor may take precautionary measures by asking the borrower to invest in loan insurance. This will protect the guarantor in case the borrower fails to repay the loan. If you are looking for a personal loan, consider getting an instant personal loan. A personal loan with a guarantor means you’ve borrowed money with someone else—an individual or even a business—who agrees to step in and repay the loan if you’re unable to meet the repayment terms. Who can be a guarantor for a personal loan? Typically, a person must have a stable monthly income, a good credit score with a clean credit history, and be an Indian citizen of legal age. However, the exact eligibility requirements may vary by lending institution. What are the requirements for a personal loan guarantor? Personal loan guarantor requirements vary by lender or financial institution. In most cases, one must be an Indian Citizen, be above the age of 18, have a stable monthly income, and have a good credit history and CIBIL score. What are the risks of being a guarantor for a personal loan? Some risks of being a guarantor for a personal loan include becoming financially responsible for the loan amount if the borrower defaults. Any missed or defaulted payments by the primary borrower can also negatively impact the guarantor’s credit score and overall credit history. How does a guarantor affect my personal loan application? If you are a guarantor on someone’s loan, this may reduce the loan amount you’re eligible for in the future. This is because lenders consider the guaranteed loan as part of your potential financial responsibility. Can a guarantor be removed from a personal loan? In most cases, it is extremely difficult to remove a guarantor from a personal loan. This can generally only be done if the borrower is able to find a new guarantor or pledge some other collateral. There are approximately 6.3 crore MSMEs today, generating turnovers of over Rs. 300 crores. The start-up industry isn’t lagging either. Some 3,000 start-ups are emerging per year and are predicted to create over 2.5 lakh jobs in the coming years. India’s entrepreneurial spirit is undying. However, there’s one roadblock that poses quite the problem: capital shortage. To tackle this head-on, our government has launched numerous projects for funding small-to-medium businesses. So, if you are a business owner looking for funding options, here are the top government schemes for MSME and start-ups you can consider. Latest Government Grant Schemes in 2026 In 2026, the government continues to strengthen support for entrepreneurs with a range of government schemes for business that go beyond traditional credit. Among the key initiatives, the SAMRIDH Scheme offers grants of up to ₹40 lakh to product-focused startups ready to scale, blending funding with mentorship and market access to accelerate growth. The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) remains a major government scheme for startup support. This provides substantial grants to incubators and early-stage innovators in deep tech, AI, and emerging sectors, helping bridge prototype to market. For tech innovators, TIDE 2.0 under the Ministry of Electronics & IT gives focused grant support across robotics, IoT and electronics. Its specialised programmes like the MSME Innovative Scheme fund prototypes and commercialisation with significant seed capital. Even schemes tied with credit support now integrate grant elements that reduce financial burden and fuel innovation. Alongside these, traditional access to a startup loan by government through schemes such as CGTMSE and Mudra continues, ensuring a balanced mix of grants and credit options for businesses nationwide. Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana or MUDRA scheme is a unique credit scheme that offers low-interest business loans to MSMEs and start-ups in the non-corporate and non-farming sectors. Under this government schemes for start-ups and MSMEs, you can avail of three types of loan products: Shishu category – A loan of up to Rs. 50,000 is available for start-ups and small businesses in their initial stages under this category. Kishor category – Mid-aged businesses looking to expand operations can avail up to Rs. 5,00,000 under this category. Tarun category – Under this category, experienced businesses can avail up to Rs. 10,00,000. Tarun Plus – Entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid a previous loan under the Tarun category can borrow above Rs. 10,00,000 and up to Rs. 20,00,000 under this category, introduced to support proven businesses ready to scale further. Raw Material Assistance Scheme for Startups and MSMEs Headed by the NSIC (National Small Industries Corporation) , the Raw Material Assistance programme is a fruitful government scheme for start-ups and MSMEs. It offers financial help through lender guarantees, credit facilitation, and bill discounts. The government takes care of all the paperwork. In turn, businesses get the necessary funds for bulk purchases of raw material and focus solely on manufacturing. 1. Core Benefits Extended Credit: The scheme provides MSMEs with short-term credit for raw material purchases, typically for up to 180 days, so working capital is not tied up in inventory. Economies of Scale: With NSIC support, small units can buy raw materials in bulk and secure the price advantages that usually only large buyers get. Import Assistance: For imported raw materials, NSIC handles the procedural work, including documentation and letters of credit, which saves small units from managing import formalities on their own. No Trading: The assistance is meant for raw materials that go into production. Units cannot use the facility to trade in raw materials. 2. Financial Limits & Credit Support Credit Arrangement: NSIC arranges the credit against security, usually a bank guarantee, and charges interest for the credit period. The unit repays once the production and sales cycle is complete. Maximum Exposure Ceilings: NSIC caps the total assistance per unit based on the security offered and the unit’s scale of operations. The applicable ceiling is confirmed at the time of sanction. 3. Eligibility Criteria Udyam Registration: The applicant must be a registered MSME holding a valid Udyam Registration certificate. Activity Type: The unit must be engaged in manufacturing. The raw material financed must be consumed in the unit’s own production, not resold. Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) The Credit Guarantee Trust Fund for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGT SME) is one of India’s largest start-up funding schemes provided by the Ministry of MSME. Under this scheme, eligible MSMEs and start-ups can obtain a collateral-free loan of up to Rs. 1 crore through the Ministry of MSME and Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI). To know more about this CGT SME business loan eligibility, terms and conditions, etc. Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) The Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) for Technology Upgradation is a government loan scheme for tech start-ups. Here, the Indian Government offers capital to help MSMEs and start-ups upgrade their tech equipment and provides a 15% subsidy for investments of up to Rs. 1 crore. For this, MSMEs/start-ups must get a term loan from a lender through the CLCSS scheme. Udyam Registration and MSME Certification MSMEs are the backbone of any economy, adding not only to the country’s GDP but generating employment in towns, suburbs, and villages. However, registering as an MSME was not always easy for many new business owners. They had to visit local bodies and pay the registration fee before they could be considered a legit MSME. So, many business owners missed out on the benefits of government schemes meant for MSMEs due to the tiresome and confusing registration process. Udyam Registration Certificate is one of the best government schemes for MSMEs in that regard. Udyam fast-tracks registration of MSMEs through the online process. New owners just have to visit the Udyam registration portal, provide their Aadhar card, and they get a permanent MSME registration without paying any fee. The Udyam Certificate also makes it easier for owners to avail of government schemes for MSMEs, like subsidised loans. Startup India Initiative The Start-up India scheme is a trademark scheme of the Indian Government. Its purpose is to provide a healthy ecosystem for business and promote entrepreneurship among the citizens of the country. This government scheme for start-ups provides the following benefits to eligible businesses: Online self-certification compliance for the country’s labour and environmental laws. Under the Start-up India scheme, the Government will not conduct any inspection for 5 years to check compliance with labour laws. However, an assessment may occur if a credible complaint for any violation is approved by at least one level senior to the inspecting officer. In the case of environmental laws, the Government performs random checks. Fast-track application for start-up patents Tax exemption under Section 80 IAC and Section 56 of the Income Tax Act. Easy process for winding up the company in case of bankruptcy. MeitY SAMRIDH Scheme for Startup Acceleration The MeitY SAMRIDH scheme is one of the most important government schemes for start-ups in the country. Many start-ups fail to survive in this competitive business environment due to a lack of funding, low-quality product, and insufficient skill set. So, this scheme helps start-ups with product innovation, business development, and growth. Currently, the MeitY SAMRIDH scheme aims to help at least 300 start-ups bring together the necessary skill set and provide them with investor and customer connections. The scheme also aims to facilitate the expansion of these start-ups overseas. Key Eligibility and Documents for Startup and MSME Funding To access funding under a government scheme for startup or other government schemes for business, meeting the right eligibility criteria and submitting proper documentation is crucial. Whether you’re exploring a startup loan by government or benefits under schemes like PMMY, CGTMSE, or Startup India, a clear understanding of requirements helps streamline your application process and boosts approval chances. T Here’s what you typically need to qualify and apply: 1. Business & Legal Documents Company or firm registration certificate (incl. Udyam/MSME or DPIIT recognition for startups) PAN card and Aadhaar of promoters GST registration (if applicable) 2. Financial & Project Paperwork Bank statements Detailed of business plan Income tax returns or financial projections 3. Scheme-Specific Essentials Proof of eligibility (age, ownership, sector as required) Collateral/security documents if mandated under specific schemes Submitting these accurately can significantly improve your chances of securing government-backed funding. Comparison Table: Best Government Schemes for Startups/MSMEs in India If you are exploring a government scheme for startup funding or evaluating suitable government schemes for business, the table below compares some of the most relevant options available for Indian startups and MSMEs. From a startup loan by government initiatives to subsidy-led and registration-based benefits, these schemes cater to businesses at different growth stages. Government Scheme Beneficiaries Key Benefit Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana Startups and MSMEs Low-interest business loans Raw Material Assistance Startups and MSMEs Credit support or bulk raw material purchase CGT SME Startups and MSMEs Collateral- free loans via SIDBI CLCSS Scheme Tech-based MSMEs 15% subsidy on investments of up to Rs 1 crore Udyam Registration MSMEs Easy MSME registration and scheme access Start-up India Scheme Eligible startups Tax benefits and compliance ease MeitY SAMRIDH Scheme Startups Funding, mentoring and market access Benefits of Registering Under Government Business Schemes Registering under government schemes for businesses can give startups and MSMEs a significant boost. The key benefits include: 1. Financial Support and Easier Credit Access Collateral-Free Loans: Schemes such as CGTMSE allow registered MSMEs to borrow without pledging collateral, as the government guarantees a large share of the loan to the lender. Interest Subsidies: Several central and state schemes subsidise interest costs for registered units, lowering the effective cost of borrowing. MUDRA Loans: Registered small businesses can access MUDRA loans across the Shishu, Kishor, Tarun, and Tarun Plus categories, matched to their stage of growth. 2. Protection Against Delayed Payments Registered MSMEs are protected under the MSMED Act, which requires buyers to pay within 45 days of accepting goods or services. If payment is delayed, the buyer owes compound interest, and the MSME can file a claim through the MSME Samadhaan portal. 3. Tenders and Procurement Preferences Government departments and public sector units must source a fixed share of their purchases from micro and small enterprises. Registered units also receive exemptions from earnest money deposits and tender fees for many public tenders, reducing the cost of bidding. 4. Regulatory and Compliance Relaxations Self-Certification: Recognized startups can self-certify compliance with specified labor and environmental laws, cutting inspection burden in the early years. Patent & IP Benefits: Recognized startups get fast-tracked patent examination and substantial rebates on patent and trademark filing fees, making it cheaper to protect innovations. 5. Subsidies and Tax Incentives Tax Holidays: Eligible DPIIT-recognized startups can claim a 100% deduction of profits for three consecutive years under Section 80-IAC of the Income Tax Act. Technology & Quality Upgrades: Schemes like CLCSS subsidize investments in modern equipment, helping registered MSMEs upgrade technology at a lower net cost. 6. Enhanced Market Reach & Networking Registration opens access to government marketplaces such as the GeM portal, participation in trade fairs and exhibitions at subsidized rates, and connections with incubators and mentorship programs that would otherwise be hard for a small business to reach. Common Mistakes to Avoid When Applying for Startup Schemes When applying for government schemes for business, many startups make avoidable mistakes that can delay approval or affect eligibility. Being mindful of these pitfalls ensures a smoother application process and increases the chances of securing a startup loan by government. Common mistakes to watch out for include: 1. Document & Eligibility Errors Vague Project Descriptions: Applications with generic or unclear project details are hard to evaluate and often rejected. Describe what the business does, what the funds are for, and how they will be used. Incomplete Documentation: A missing registration certificate, bank statement, or ITR can stall the entire application. Prepare the full checklist before applying. Ignoring Scheme Criteria: Each scheme has specific conditions on sector, business age, turnover, or ownership. Applying without checking these wastes time and can affect future applications. Incorrect Financials: Mismatched figures across bank statements, ITRs, and projections raise red flags during scrutiny. Reconcile all numbers before submission. 2. Legal & Compliance Oversights Neglecting Post-Approval Compliance: Most schemes carry reporting and utilisation conditions after funds are sanctioned. Missing these can lead to recovery of benefits or disqualification from future schemes. Missing Commencement Filing: Where a scheme requires proof that the business or project has commenced, a delay in this filing can delay disbursement. False or Exaggerated Information: Inflated turnover, overstated projections, or incorrect ownership details can lead to rejection, blacklisting, and legal consequences. 3. Strategy & Execution Flaws Applying Without Professional Guidance: A chartered accountant or scheme consultant can spot eligibility gaps and documentation issues before submission, which is far cheaper than a rejection. Skipping Market Validation: Funding applications backed by real customer or market evidence are stronger than idea-stage claims. Validate demand before seeking scheme support. Overlooking Tax & Financial Strategy: Scheme benefits interact with your tax position and capital structure. Plan how a subsidy, grant, or loan fits your overall finances instead of treating it as standalone money. Avoiding these errors can help startups navigate government schemes efficiently and access the funding they need. Conclusion Government schemes give startups and MSMEs a genuine head start: cheaper credit, subsidies, procurement access, and compliance relief. The right approach is to register first, through Udyam or DPIIT recognition, then match schemes to your stage of growth and apply with complete, accurate documentation. And when your funding needs go beyond what a scheme covers, a business loan from Tata Capital can bridge the gap with flexible repayment options and minimal documentation. How can a new business apply for a government loan or grant in India? A new business can apply for a government loan or grant in India by researching eligible schemes, preparing a detailed business plan, completing the application online or offline, and submitting the required documents. Is collateral mandatory for startup or MSME government loans? No, collateral is not always mandatory for startup or MSME government loans. Many schemes offer collateral-free funding, especially for small businesses, though some larger loans may require security depending on the lender and scheme. Which sectors or industries are eligible for startup funding schemes? Most startup funding schemes target a wide range of sectors, including technology, manufacturing, healthcare, agriculture, and services. Insurance Medical Insurance Other Insurance Wellness solutions Home Insurance Travel Insurance Investment Mutual Fund If you are researching ways to finance your higher education, you must have come across a term called education loan sanction letter. It is considered to be one of the most important documents of your loan approval process. But what exactly is it? Find out the details in this article. What is an education loan sanction letter? When you apply for a loan , you provide a set of documents along with the application form. The lender examines these documents and decides whether you are approved for the said loan amount and terms. Once approved, the institution sends a document informing you, the borrower, that you have successfully applied and received approval for the loan. This document is the sanction letter. Thus, the sanction letter is an official document informing you that you have been approved for your education loan application . It contains all the necessary information about your loan application, such as the loan amount, your name, loan tenure , interest rate, terms and conditions, etc. After this, the lender sanctions the loan amount, and it reaches your account. This document is only provided after you successfully apply for the loan. Soft inquiries such as contacting the financial institution representatives to understand the loan terms are not considered a loan application. Sometimes universities require proof of financial capability before granting admission to students aspiring to study overseas. Others require a visa permit as well. However, traditionally, financial institutions require proof of admission into a university and student visa to give the sanction letter. In such cases, you can apply for a pre-approved loan sanction letter. Importance & uses of education loan sanction letter for study abroad and Visa When planning to study abroad , securing an education loan is a crucial step. Once approved, the student loan sanction letter or education loan letter serves as an official document confirming the loan amount, terms, and conditions. This letter plays several important roles for students and their visa process. Here’s why it matters: Proof of financial support: Immigration authorities often require evidence of sufficient funds to cover tuition and living expenses. The education loan sanction letter acts as official proof. Visa application requirement: Many countries ask for a student loan sanction letter as part of the visa submission process. Clarity on loan terms: The education loan sanction letter format clearly outlines the loan amount, interest rate, repayment tenure, and other terms, helping students plan finances effectively. University admission formality: Some universities request an education loan sanction letter sample to confirm that the student can pay the course fees before enrolment. Quick processing assurance: Knowing the education loan sanction time helps students schedule admission and visa procedures without delays. A proper education loan letter ensures financial security and smooth processing for studying abroad. Types of sanction letters Once an education loan is approved, lenders issue different education loan letters based on the stage of admission and documentation. Below are the common types of student loan sanction letter you may come across: In-principle sanction letter: Issued early based on basic eligibility. This education loan letter is helpful when admission is in progress and gives an estimate of loan eligibility and education loan sanction time. Pre-approved/Provisional sanction letter: Shared before final admission confirmation. The education loan sanction letter format here is tentative and subject to further verification. Unconditional/Final sanction letter: Issued after all documents are approved. This student loan sanction letter follows a standard education loan sanction letter format and is widely accepted for visa purposes. Conditional sanction letter: Provided with specific conditions to be met. Students often refer to an education loan sanction letter sample to understand such clauses clearly. Pre-Visa sanction letter: Issued to students planning to study abroad, this letter serves as proof of financial support and is commonly used during student visa applications and visa interviews. Each type of education loan letter supports a different stage of your study journey. How to apply for an education loan sanction letter? Once the financial institution approves and sanctions your loan application, you will receive a sanction letter. Here’s how and when you can expect to get it: Step 1: When you submit your loan application form along with all required documents, the lender will review your application. Step 2: Once they approve your application, they will issue a sanction letter outlining the terms and conditions of the loan. Step 3: The lender will send you the sanction letter by post or hand it over to you physically. You can use this sanction letter as proof of funds for your education expenses. Education loan sanction letter format (India) The format of an education loan sanction letter can vary depending on the lender. However, it typically includes the following components: – Addressed to the borrower and co-borrower: The sanction letter is typically addressed to both the borrower and the co-borrower. –Comprehensive loan information: It contains detailed information about the approved loan amount, interest rate, and repayment terms. – Date and validity: The sanction letter is dated, and its validity period is clearly mentioned. However, there are a standard set of documents that most lenders ask for. They are as follows: A correctly filled loan application form. Academic record. Identity proof such as PAN Card, AADHAR card, etc. Proof of address. Proof of admission. Statement of educational expenses such as the tuition fee, hostel fee, cost of accessories for education, and related costs. Income proof of the loan applicant or co-applicant. Bank statement of the loan applicant or the co-applicant. Collateral documents if applicable. Sanction letter issuance After approving your loan application, the lender will issue a sanction letter outlining the approved loan amount, interest rate, repayment schedule, and other terms and conditions. borrowed money. It is the actual cost of borrowing. Depending on the lender’s policies, your credit profile, chosen course and institution, and other factors, the rate of interest on education loans can range from 8% to 15%. The interest rate can be fixed or floating. The calculation of the interest component can be done using the simple or the compound interest method. Most student loans include a grace period while you are studying, but the education loan interest continues to accrue. Education loan interest rate refers to the extra charge you pay to lenders on top of the principal amount you borrow to fund your higher education. Pursuing quality education lays the solid foundation for a successful and financially secure future. However, the rising cost of studying in well-ranked universities and colleges often presents financial challenges. To cover these educational expenses, many students choose education loans . But does an education loan have interest rates and terms that can potentially affect your repayment capacity? To answer this question, let’s start with understanding the meaning of education loan interest rate and how it works. Education loan interest rate refers to the additional percentage charge lenders levy on top of the borrowed money. It generally ranges from 8% to 15% per annum, depending on the lender. This article will take you through the specifics of interest on education loans so you can understand the fine print and, ultimately, make an informed decision. Do education loans have interest rates? Yes, all types of loans feature an interest component. The education loan interest rate is the percentage of the loaned amount the lender charges as the cost of borrowing. This rate is calculated on an annual basis. For example, if you take a loan of Rs. 10 lakh at an interest rate of 12% per annum, you will have to repay an additional Rs. 1.2 lakh in interest along with the original principal amount of Rs. 10 lakh. As shown in the above example, the education loan interest rate directly affects the total amount you repay on an education loan. A higher interest rate results in higher EMIs and a larger total repayment, while a lower interest rate reduces both your monthly installments and the overall cost of the loan. Even a small difference in the interest rate can significantly affect the total amount repaid, especially for long loan tenures. Make sure you compare interest rates across lenders to help you reduce your overall borrowing cost. What are the types of interest rates for education loans & calculation methods? To understand how education loan interest rates work, it is important to answer the question: “Does an education loan have interest rates that can change?” Yes. Education loans can feature either a fixed or a floating interest rate . While floating interest rate changes with shifting market conditions, fixed rates stay constant throughout the tenure of the loan . Since most education loans in India are linked to external benchmark rates, floating interest rates are more commonly offered. Education loan interest rates in India generally range between 8% and 15% per annum. It depends on factors such as the lender’s policies, applicant’s credit profile, loan amount, course, institution, and whether collateral is provided. For example, if you are pursuing a professional course at a reputed institution with collateral, you may qualify for a lower interest rate than your friend who is pursuing a diploma and securing an unsecured loan. The following table highlights the features of fixed and floating interest rates to give you a better understanding. Fixed interest rate Floating interest rate EMI remains the same throughout the tenure EMI or tenure may change when interest rates change Easier to plan monthly repayments Can benefit if market interest rates fall Protects against rising interest rates May become expensive if interest rates increase Usually starts at a slightly higher rate Generally offered at lower initial rates Lenders may calculate education loan interest using simple interest during the moratorium period and switch to compound interest once repayment begins. However, the method depends on the lender’s loan terms. In either case, the calculation will be as follows: Simple interest calculation on education loans Simple interest is calculated on the principal amount of the education loan. It is calculated using this formula: Simple Interest = Principal x interest rate x time period For example, if the loan amount of Rs. 1 lakh is disbursed for a tenure of 3 years at a 10% simple interest rate, the interest calculation will be: Rs. 1 lakh x 10% x 1 year = Rs. 10,000 Year 2 interest = Rs. 1 lakh x 10% x 1 year = Rs. 10,000 Compound interest calculation on education loans Lenders calculate compound interest on the principal amount and the accumulated interest. It is calculated as: Compound interest = Principal x (1 + interest rate/ compounding rate) ^ compounding rate x tenure Say, you’ve taken a loan of Rs. 10 lakh for 2 years with an interest rate of 7%. The calculation will then look like this: 10 lakh* (1 + 0.07/1) ^ 1*2 = Rs. 10,14,049 Thus, your total interest obligation for the loan’s tenure will stand at Rs. 14,049. Simple vs compound: Which calculation method applies to you? Understanding how interest is calculated on loans can help you manage costs and plan repayments better. Education loans may use simple or compound interest, each affecting your education loan interest differently. Basis Simple Interest (SI) Compound Interest (CI) Meaning Interest is calculated only on the principal. Interest is calculated on principal + accumulated interest. Formula SI = P × R × T / 100 CI = P × (1 + R/n)^(n×T) – P Interest growth Linear over time. Exponential over time. EMI impact Results in comparatively lower EMIs and lower total repayment, especially for shorter-duration loans. Leads to higher EMIs or a higher total repayment over the loan tenure, especially for longer-duration loans. Total repayment Lower overall borrowing cost since interest is charged only on the principal Higher overall borrowing cost as interest keeps accumulating on unpaid interest Best suited for Short-term loans or small amounts Long-term loans where growth on interest is manageable Transparency Simple and predictable Complex; requires careful monitoring Example You borrow Rs. 10 lakh at an interest rate of 10% per annum for 5 years. Simple interest is calculated only on the principal of Rs. 10 lakh. It is estimated to be Rs. 1 lakh per year, and Rs. 5 lakh by the end of the tenure. So, total repayment is Rs. 15,00,000. You borrow Rs. 10 lakh at an interest rate of 10% per annum for 5 years. The interest in the first year will be Rs. 1 lakh, which will compound, requiring you to calculate interest on Rs. 11 lakh for the next year. At the end of 5 years, the total interest will be around Rs. 6,10,510, with the total repayment cost reaching Rs. 16,10,510. Knowing this helps manage student loan interest rates efficiently. Fixed vs floating interest rates: Which should you choose? Choosing between fixed and floating interest rates affects both your EMIs and total loan cost. Knowing the difference helps you pick the option that fits your financial comfort. Basis Fixed interest rate Floating interest rate Meaning Interest rate remains constant throughout the loan tenure. Interest rate changes with market benchmarks. EMI stability EMIs remain the same, making budgeting easier. EMIs may rise or fall over time. Risk factor Low risk from interest rate fluctuations. Higher risk due to changing market rates. Initial rate Usually slightly higher initially. Often lower at the start. Benefit during rate cuts No benefit if rates fall. Borrowers benefit directly from rate reductions. Best suited for Those who prefer certainty and fixed budgets. Those comfortable with some uncertainty. Long-term cost Can be higher if rates drop significantly. Can be lower if rates remain stable or decline. Choose fixed for stability; opt for floating if flexibility matters. How do lenders decide your education loan interest rate? Lenders in India use multiple factors to decide your education loan interest rate, and knowing these can help you plan better. To understand how education loan interest works, lenders first evaluate the risk involved in lending to you. Co-applicant’s profile: A co-applicant with a stable income, steady employment, and strong repayment capacity is considered less risky, which can help you get a lower education loan interest rate. Credit score: Your credit score plays a major role in determining the interest rate. 750 and above: Excellent; usually eligible for the most competitive rates. 700 – 749: Good; likely to qualify for favorable rates. 650 – 699: Fair; approval is possible, but the interest rate may be higher. Below 650: It may reduce approval chances or result in a higher education loan interest rate. Academic background: If you are taking admission in a reputed institution or a high-demand course, it can reduce the lender’s risk and improve the interest rate offered. Loan amount: Larger loan amounts may attract slightly higher education loan interest, especially if they are unsecured. Collateral: Collateral-backed loans generally carry lower education loan interest than unsecured loans. Course location: Overseas education loans may have slightly higher interest rates than domestic education loans due to higher lending risk. Loan tenure and moratorium: Longer repayment tenures and extended moratorium periods can increase the total education loan interest payable over the life of the loan. What are the education loan interest rate trends in India? In India, education loan interest rates are influenced by factors such as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) policy rates, lender funding costs, inflation, and market conditions. Most lenders offer floating interest rates, so your rate may increase or decrease during the loan tenure. Currently, education loan interest rates generally range between 8% and 15% per annum, depending on the lender and your profile. The current education loan interest rate trends in India are as follows: Lenders offer floating rates more than fixed rates. If students are admitted to reputed institutions, they often receive lower rates. The interest rates for secured loans are generally lower than unsecured loans. Strong credit profiles and eligible co-applicants can help borrowers qualify for better interest rates. What are the government subsidies and schemes for education? The Government of India offers several schemes to make higher education more affordable. These schemes mainly provide interest subsidies or easier access to education loans for eligible applicants. Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS): It offers interest subsidy during the moratorium period for eligible students from economically weaker sections. PM Vidyalaxmi Scheme: The scheme helps students access education loans through a single application platform, with interest support for eligible borrowers. Dr. Ambedkar Central Sector Scheme: It provides interest subsidy for students from Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) pursuing higher studies abroad. State Government Schemes: Many states also offer education loan subsidies or financial assistance for eligible students. Do student loans have interest payments during the grace period? Unlike other types of loans , education loans feature a grace period – the time between the end of the course and the start of the loan repayment . This means that you don’t need to start paying EMIs immediately but at a later date once you start to earn. A common question while selecting a lender is, “Does an education loan have interest to be paid during the grace period?” Well, there are two types of grace periods offered by different lenders: Grace period with interest payment: Under this option, the borrower needs to pay interest as per the student loan interest rate on the disbursed loan amount, either fully or partially. The principal repayment starts only after the grace period is over. Grace period without interest payment: Here, the borrower is not required to pay any interest during the grace period. The interest keeps accumulating as per the student loan interest rate and gets added to the principal once the grace period ends. Does an education loan have interest-based tax benefits? Apart from helping you move ahead in your career, you have the option of enjoying tax benefits on education loan interest . The interest paid on education loans is eligible for tax deduction under Section 80E of the Income Tax Act. Here is how it works: The tax deduction applies only to interest payments, not to the principal loan amount. Moreover, there is no upper limit on the total interest amount eligible for tax deductions. The tax benefit on education loans is available for up to 8 years from the start of loan repayment or until interest is paid off, whichever is earlier. To claim this deduction, a certificate is required from the lender showing the interest and principal breakup of EMIs. Here’s an example to help you get a better understanding: You have taken an education loan of Rs. 10 lakh for your higher education. The total interest you paid in a year was Rs. 90,000, and the total principal repaid was Rs. 1.2 lakh. Section 80E allows you to claim the interest component for a tax deduction. As a result, you can deduct Rs. 90,000 from your taxable income, provided you are filing the return under the old regime, before calculating the payable taxes. Is interest rate important while comparing lenders? Education loans provide the required financial assistance for higher studies. A common question students ask when exploring different financial institutions is: Are student loan interest rates different across lenders? Understanding whether a financial institution offers lower student loan interest rates can have huge implications on your total repayment burden. In addition to finding student loans with low interest rates, you must ask questions about the prepayment charges, hidden charges, and the total loan amount that can be borrowed. Finally, it is important to note that with longer tenures, your EMIs reduce but the total interest payable increases. If you are confident of securing a well-paying job after the completion of your course, it is better to opt for shorter tenures.
